Mobile-phone studies use call detail records to construct CDR-based social networks and examine calling and texting patterns. Link-centric analysis focuses on user pairs and predicts user relationships, including age. These network-derived features, especially close ties, support payment-default prediction for network services and can outperform geographical-location features.

Dating-market analysis studies heterosexual online dating interactions, local submarkets, sex ratios, age, ethnicity, and racial stratification. Messaging behavior contributes to observed stratification.

Sashimi models corpora through research domains, topics, and time, providing alternatives to traditional topic models and network analysis. Applied to ASCO abstracts from 1995–2017, it detects temporal patterns and thematic transformations in oncology research.

Other applications include sentiment analysis of car-manufacturer web pages and hyperlink networks, tagging topics such as e-mobility and autonomous driving, and localized event detection for public health while accounting for timing, location, weather, and interaction-type confounders.

e023663116a9f1f2a515fd0dd74da5f9c0b1cb81.text:
## Community-Aware Network Inference, Influence, and Epidemic Dynamics

This community focuses on reconstructing and analyzing networks with modular structure, information flow, and contagion. **Network reconstruction** uses multivariate spatiotemporal Hawkes processes and point-process models, including heterogeneous errors and single-edge measurements. It is evaluated on empirical, artificial, and synthetic networks, as well as location-based social-media and violent-gang-crime data, with reconstruction accuracy and motif analysis as outcomes.

**Community structure** distinguishes local influence within communities from global influence across inter-community links. **Modular centrality** extends betweenness, closeness, and eigenvalue centrality to identify influential nodes in modular networks. **InfoRank** uses entropy maximization to estimate accessible information and quantify node-level information asymmetry, outperforming other centrality measures for selecting informative nodes.

Epidemic modeling links these methods to **SIR** and **metapopulation SIR** systems. Synthetic networks support epidemic simulations, while metapopulation models address intra-city propagation, infection prediction, and outbreak simulation. **D2PRI** infers disease-infection networks using power-law and data priors, validated on the Shenzhen clinical report dataset.

Additional applications include two-level community analysis of an SSCI journal system through co-citation patterns, and liability networks, where structural information asymmetry and network structure help quantify contagion risk.

c7dd0967485f6df5602fb3096c88c87e11ca685c.text:
## Graph, Hypergraph, and Temporal Network Analysis

This community focuses on graph and hypergraph representation, generation, centrality, and energy-based analysis.

**Tensor and hypergraph methods.** Hypergraphs can be represented with tensors, including uniform hypergraphs whose hyperedges have equal size. Tensor eigenvector centralities for uniform hypergraphs use Perron–Frobenius theory and are evaluated on hypergraphs derived from n-gram frequencies, Stack Exchange co-tagging, and drug combinations observed in emergency-room visits. Traditional eigenvector centrality is defined through an adjacency matrix and extended to hypergraphs. A tensor-based data model uses tensors to support analysis algorithms while reducing data–program dependence; it models social-network data, supports polystore storage, and uses ETL transformations. Polystores link storage systems used in data warehouses.

**Graph properties and generation.** Hyperedge replacement grammars support graph generation, preserve graph properties and local graph substructures, and are extracted from clique trees. Network patterns are analyzed and modeled through graph generation.

**Energy and centrality.** Graph energy has Randi, Laplacian, and distance variants, correlates with vertex, eigenvector, and betweenness centrality in some network models, and is applied to egocentric networks. Degree, degree centrality, PageRank, and betweenness centrality provide additional graph measures.

**Temporal networks.** Time-varying graphs model transit networks and mobility patterns, using transit feeds implemented in Neo4j. Temporal shortest paths, diameter, density, and centralities analyze dynamics.

74878fd5494d625afa49ff27127b354860014807.text:
## Federated Clinical NLP and Fair Cyberbullying Detection

This community links clinical natural language processing, federated learning, and algorithmic fairness. Two-stage federated NLP applies clinical NLP to clinical notes held in electronic medical record systems across different hospitals or clinics without moving the data. It supports patient representation learning and is evaluated on obesity and comorbidity phenotyping, contributing knowledge progression across the healthcare system toward a learning health system.

Clinical notes also support surgical site infection detection. Clinical NLP performs automatic information extraction, while automated feature generation produces keyword features through sublanguage analysis and supports search-based NLP by augmenting search queries. These features provide a foundation for information extraction systems and are used with machine learning algorithms.

A second focus is cyberbullying detection using Twitter data. Machine learning algorithms detect cyberbullying, while network centrality defines network-position groups for auditing variation in detection performance. Algorithmic bias may affect detection algorithms; algorithmic fairness addresses this issue, and equalized odds post-processes the detector to counter disparity. Heuristics are combined with sublanguage analysis, connecting feature-generation methods across the clinical and social-media applications.

4b463038b551b5d1b7616256341153ef2982fa04.text:
## Recommendation and Research-Network Intelligence

This community links two major themes: recommendation systems and scholarly-network analysis.

A production recommendation engine on the Meta platform operates over a biomedical knowledge base containing more than 27 million articles. It uses customer, product, and trip embeddings as model inputs. Exponential-family embeddings construct product and context representations; product embeddings combine product-name and shopping-pattern information, while customer and trip profiles support customer targeting and next-product recommendation.

Recommendation algorithms use citation networks, text, semantic tags, and co-authorship information to recommend papers and researchers. Their relative algorithm efficiency is evaluated, including implementations on the Meta platform.

The research-network strand models scholarly literature through citation networks, including networks based on the 100 most cited papers. These networks represent research areas, reflect and potentially shape scholarly conversations, and help study research dynamism—growth, decline, and re-emergence. Structural patterns, entropy measures, weak tie theory, and betweenness centrality characterize network structure and multidisciplinarity.

Diversity, supported by a diversity measurement routine, is presented as a strong measure of journal-level interdisciplinarity. Case studies include optical physics and other research areas. A semantic knowledge network, generated and maintained by the Meta platform, connects these data-driven approaches to broader knowledge representation.

598a4f1e7f693fe5f11b7e1cee008616c8d90645.text:
## Dynamic Communities, Social Power, and Structural Change

This community centers on modeling and detecting evolution in dynamic networks and social networks. Stochastic block models represent vertices through latent types and type-dependent edge probabilities; dynamic and seasonal variants extend these structures across time, with seasonal processes driving changing edge-formation probabilities. Seasonal stochastic blockmodeling is defined as a generative process and uses inference procedures to recover normal seasonal behavior for anomaly detection, evaluated on Enron emails and New York City taxi trips.

Dynamic community graph models describe evolving community structure. They define balanced community growth as normal behavior and community merging as abnormal behavior. Topological change detection quantifies graph changes with a graph topology change metric and tests significant structural change using a test statistic. Monte Carlo simulation evaluates these detection methods.

Community detection includes local core member methods, which use relationship closeness and gravity between core and neighboring nodes, while ensemble clustering combines assignments from scalable algorithms to produce dynamic clustering with strong pairwise precision and recall. Dynamic clustering can summarize community evolution in a flowchart.

The social-network portion examines connectivity, centrality, and power. The DeGroot–Friedkin model describes evolving social power; in star topologies, power concentrates in the centre individual. Selective adjustment of interpersonal weights can reduce this dominance under suitable relationship-strength conditions. Web traffic and medical-condition information are additional network-related applications.

8b626e3ce7a6cf07d7ea7fc50a550abc23eedd97.text:
## Network Analysis, Prediction, and Influence

This community connects graph-based centrality, online interaction, and prediction tasks. **PageRank**, a network-centrality measure computed from the **Google matrix**, represents users’ social status, identifies influential users, and forecasts future status. Behavioral motifs improve prediction of future PageRank values. The Google matrix models random-surfer navigation and is constructed from the *English Wikipedia 2017* article network. Its **reduced Google matrix** captures hidden indirect links and is applied to terrorist-network analysis, including relationships and influence among terrorist groups and world countries. PageRank also measures geopolitical sensitivity and country sensitivity to selected banks.

In cybersecurity, **enterprise cyber attack prediction** uses reply-network information. Path structure between user groups is more predictive than user posting statistics, while binary classification determines whether an organization will be attacked on a given day.

A second focus is performance ratings in online speaking communities. The corresponding dataset contains interactions and ratings from six communities. Peer interaction, interaction topologies, and graph signal processing explain rating evolution. Consensus-based prediction and diffusion models use peer ratings and network influence; the prediction model outperforms network-agnostic regression baselines by approximately 23%, while total variation measures rating differences.

Finally, sympathy classification uses regression and deep convolutional neural networks; sympathetic tweets were not found to spread farther.

6fa4231713c53f279f8bab446958ef5ff03ed4f8.text:
### Diffusion, Networks, and Social Influence

This community studies how content spreads through online platforms, social networks, and mobile peer-to-peer systems. Content popularity depends on interest evolution, copying, question-writing style, psycholinguistic factors, search ranking, and platform advertising. Content providers use acceleration strategies—including recommendation lists, re-ranking, seeding, and budget allocation—to promote content; competing strategies are analyzed through differential games and Nash equilibria.

Dissemination models identify interested destinations and not-yet-interested relays. A two-stage strategy combines self-promotion with random gossiping under velocity-constrained mobility, while controlled epidemic and dynamic influence models describe propagation. Minimum weight dynamos study initial node assignments under irreversible simple-majority rules, including rings, tori, and cliques.

Network structure is central: complete, star, balanced, bipartite Turán, and interconnected-star topologies are examined as desired or stable configurations. Centrality affects budget allocation, bridging capital, and awareness advantage, while best-response link alteration can produce stable networks. Social welfare motivates optimal and sustainable social norms, with punishment length and whitewashing affecting outcomes.

A second major theme is crisis information. Hurricane Sandy datasets support disaster detection, sentiment sensing, tweet corroboration, and credibility analysis. Dynamic network inference uses stochastic convex optimization and online media diffusion observations. Information pathways among blogs and social media change during ongoing news events, including the Libyan civil war and Syrian uprising.

5f44414552c2a6b2c20937bbfaeffdfbade214c6.text:
## Community Report: Network Evolution, Bias, and Spatial Platforms

This community centers on how social and evolving networks form, grow, and change. Homophily—similarity by ethnicity, gender, affiliation, age, preferences, and other attributes—shapes friendship formation and social-network evolution, increasing bonding capital while potentially producing fragmentation, popularity asymmetries, and racial bias. Preferential attachment explains growth and scaling behavior, but may emerge from triangle closure or a doubly preferential meeting process rather than act as a direct mechanism. Hidden-tree models, network-evolution models, toy models, and weighted model mixtures study these mechanisms; measurement procedures distinguish preferential attachment from alternatives.

Evolving networks have temporally growing topologies. Dynlocness supports community detection, while temporal graph sketches, equation-free frameworks, and analytical approximations characterize or simulate their dynamics. Network centrality relates network position to bridging capital, awareness advantages, and cyberbullying-detection performance.

A second theme is algorithmic and platform bias. Airbnb is analyzed as a peer-to-peer marketplace using listings and bivariate spatial autocorrelation, revealing centre–periphery relationships with hotels, tourist-attraction effects, tourism pressure in Barcelona, gentrification, offline bias, and racial-bias signals. Gender bias also occurs in named-entity-recognition training datasets; fair classifiers and equalized odds address algorithmic fairness.

159d7ceb310e0e799bc00a5b42b1fc0e8bb32f4d.text:
## Embeddings, Reviews, and Cross-Platform Knowledge

This community connects biomedical and software-language processing with customer-review analytics, Wikipedia traffic, and information retrieval.

**Word embeddings** are trained from PubMed, EHR/clinical notes, Wikipedia, news corpora, and Google News, with GloVe serving as a general-domain comparison. PubMed- and EHR-trained embeddings capture medical-term semantics and produce semantic-similarity results closer to human expert judgments. Embeddings support biomedical NLP and downstream tasks, transfer representation learning, software knowledge extraction, and sentiment classification. On the Amazon Review Dataset, sentiment classes include *happy* and *unhappy*, with neural network classifiers using embeddings as inputs.

For software knowledge extraction, **Sieve** implements cross-platform analysis and transfer representation learning, transferring knowledge from Stack Overflow and Software Engineering Stack Exchange to YouTube. A neural classifier predicts useful query-expansion terms; evaluation on TREC Newswire and Web collections shows improved retrieval performance, robustness, and performance over competitive baselines.

A **review network**, built from customer reviews, measures customer influence through network centrality. The **social promoter score** combines loyalty, ratings, sentiments, and customer centrality, and is compared with Net Promoter Score. Applied to Amazon.com brand reviews, it predicts financial health—operationalized as future sales—more effectively than the baseline.

Wikipedia access data supports **searchshare** and **resistance** analysis: architecture articles tend to attract search traffic but act as traffic dead ends.

ee6af3b344c0e8e4a1defb74b38db4dcfa93523e.text:
## Community Report: Diffusion, Networks, and Social Information Systems

This community studies content diffusion, network structure, and strategic information spreading. Content providers use online platforms such as Vimeo, recommendation lists, re-ranking mechanisms, platform advertising, and acceleration strategies to increase content popularity. Popularity depends on interest evolution, search ranking, question-writing style, psycholinguistic factors, and views per question.

Diffusion is modeled through copying, relays, destination nodes, random gossiping, self-promotion, controlled epidemic models, threshold rules, and dynamic influence propagation. The minimum weight dynamo problem assigns initial node weights so all nodes reach maximum acceptance under an irreversible simple-majority rule, with results for rings, tori, and cliques.

Strategic competition is represented by differential games and Nash equilibria, including budget allocation, multiphase investment, rumor blocking, and competing content providers. Network topology is central: complete graphs, star graphs, bipartite Turán graphs, and interconnected stars are candidate desired topologies for stable networks, while mobility can approximate complete-graph dissemination.

The community also addresses social welfare, optimal social norms, reputation, punishment, whitewashing, and stable matching. Applications include disaster detection and haze management, using social-network sensors and information flow. Datasets cover Hurricane Sandy, online media diffusion, real social networks, and events such as the Libyan civil war and Syrian uprising.

91a5223965b5a70d5a13d415ce7d535034b5e2cd.text:
# Dynamic Networks, Retrieval, and Personalized Prediction

This community connects methods for analyzing evolving networks, inferring structured data, and improving retrieval and personalization.

**Dynamic graph anomaly detection** identifies localized increases in temporal activity within node clusters, including temporal networks and large time-evolving graphs. Hopfield and memory networks combine graph and temporal information, with evaluation on Wikipedia page views and the Enron Email dataset. A distributed implementation supports scalability, and reported precision is good.

**UMHI** addresses unfollow prediction in online social networks. It models temporal attributes from post content and unfollow history, and spatial attributes through social network structure. The Weibo dataset supplies relationship dynamics and user-posted content. Follow and unfollow behavior shape online social-network structure, which also supports viral marketing.

For structured data, **restricted regular expressions with interleaving** are inferred by a polynomial inference algorithm evaluated on large-scale real data and XML corpora. The Relax NG system supports the unconstrained interleaving operator, while Relax NG inference applies this approach to schema inference, improving precision and practicality.

In biomedical applications, relation extraction derives semantic relations among medical concepts from medical documents, improving medical literature retrieval for clinical decision support systems.

Finally, a simple deep personalized recommendation system learns traveler preferences from implicit signals and conditional embeddings. Deep average networks use historical information, listing embeddings encode short-term context, and traveler embeddings feed a conversion prediction model, improving precision and online shopping experience personalization.

8f5748d6d3634fbaf5d4784686a26c431bd04614.text:
## Precision–Recall Methods for Entity and Network Intelligence

This community centers on measuring and improving **precision and recall** across entity resolution, information extraction, classification, event detection, network inference, and citation discovery. Entity-resolution techniques aim for strong precision and recall, while **blocking** improves computational efficiency but trades off duplicate recall; phonetic blocking increases candidate-generation recall.

Key approaches include **active and continuous active learning**, crowdsourcing, predictive coding, and annotation assistance for technology-assisted review and paper screening. **Multi-partite max-weight matching**, heuristic author-name disambiguation, unsupervised string-transformation learning, and query-driven entity resolution address matching, authorship, and consolidation. **Holoclean**, **DMIR**, **MARVE**, **VERSE**, **CBlock**, **AutoBlock**, and **SlimFast** represent systems for data cleaning, retrieval, extraction, and blocking.

The community also covers dynamic social networks, hidden network structure, community profiling, suspicious-group detection, and change-point or emerging-event detection. Methods such as size-agnostic change-point detection, dense-cluster discovery, regularized graph layouts, and semantic visualization support these tasks. Classification uses random forests, gradient boosting, multinomial naïve Bayes, and other machine-learning models. Across applications, precision–recall trade-offs, quality control, real-world datasets, and human–machine or crowd-powered workflows are recurring concerns.

57ecc1c898dc57d6c2ca1ac2c05978ef762b1a57.text:
## Distributed Data Management, Graphs, and Adaptive Processing

This community centers on distributed data management for big-data and graph workloads. MapReduce, implemented by Hadoop and extended by systems such as Manimal, Brace, Meta-MapReduce, MapUpdate, and LIAH, supports graph computation, web-corpus analysis, joins, SGF queries, and wavelet-histogram construction. Its design concerns include mapper/reducer memory, communication cost, reducer size, replication rate, machine count, output correctness, freshness, and limited suitability for fast data. Security, privacy, authentication, interoperability, and GDPR-related challenges are also prominent.

MapReduce workflows use distributed file systems, execution plans, and jobs; Stubby optimizes workflows, while workflow generators support performance evaluation. Generalized hypertree decompositions enable MapReduce query processing, including multiway joins, and probabilistic hitting-set methods provide scalable implementations.

Adaptive indexing targets main-memory column stores and task assignment. LIAH incrementally indexes HDFS blocks through MapReduce map tasks, reducing indexing overhead and improving workload performance as indexes converge; SmartCrowd applies adaptive worker indexing to improve assignment quality.

Graph infrastructure includes external-memory graph generation for small clusters, using shuffle, relabel, redistribute, CSR conversion, MPI, pthreads, and STXXL. Dynamic social networks are modeled through snapshots and time-varying graphs, supporting adaptive collective intelligence and improved individual and collective decision accuracy. Overall, the community links scalable execution, indexing, graph generation, workflow optimization, and responsible data management.

e7e3dc681f348c458faeb5dc721bc432865f9677.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: Prediction, Retrieval, and Dynamic Networks

This community centers on evaluating and improving predictive, retrieval, extraction, and graph-analytics systems. **Precision, recall, and AUC** are dominant metrics: they assess change-point and emerging-event detection, classification, authorship classification, IP identification, recommendation, conversion prediction, citation impact, and health tasks such as Parkinson’s disease detection and drug-recall prediction. The precision–recall trade-off is explicit across systems including **DMIR, Holoclean, VERSE, RIPEX, Core and Peel**, and the seminar user detection framework. Reported results include DMIR’s 1.0 validation and 0.962 testing precision/recall, RIPEX’s high IP-identification precision and recall, and over 99% precision and recall for the 2017 computer science census.

Methods include **random forests, gradient boosting, multinomial Naive Bayes, deep convolutional neural networks, ensemble voting, genetic and memetic algorithms**, and temporal point-process modeling. Graph-focused work covers dynamic social networks, incremental community detection, tensor spectral clustering, graph anomaly detection, graph layouts, alignment, and typed graphlet counting.

Other themes include semantic visualization, analytical queries, approximate functional dependencies, regular-expression extraction, source trustworthiness, recommender systems, cold-start filtering, ad prediction, app-feature extraction, and event forecasting. Datasets span microblog streams, synthetic clickstreams, computer-science papers, census data, and digital traces.

5219ee3a5d9d16370c0ea68c56bb3c44935b6ba3.text:
## Influence, Diffusion, and Network Computation

This community connects influence analysis, network structure, and scalable graph computation. Influence propagation in social networks is modeled by the linear threshold and independent cascade models, with spread measured by the expected number of active nodes at diffusion termination. The general threshold model uses node-specific threshold functions; its KKT conjecture concerns whether local monotonicity and submodularity imply global properties. AD-1 and AD-2 correspond to monotonicity and submodularity, while local-to-global AD-\(k\) results are established for directed acyclic social graphs using continuous extensions of set functions.

An influence-based centrality framework extends degree, harmonic, sphere-of-influence, and group centrality to influence models, characterizing formulations through Bayesian centrality and enabling approximation algorithms. Shapley values assess individual centralities in group influence settings. Dynamic networks are represented by edge-weight updates, supporting tracking of top-\(k\) influential vertices under both diffusion models.

A second theme concerns assortative mixing: global, local, and coefficient-based measures describe similarity or dissimilarity in networks, while multiscale localization analyzes global assortativity.

Finally, SystemML supports large-scale machine learning through linear algebra programs. Fusion-plan optimization selects cost-effective operator-fusion and materialization strategies over operator DAGs, exploits sparsity, and generates code for local and distributed operations.

7c33fb0aedd604e2c11275267c684d62cacda35e.text:
**MapReduce-Centered Big-Data Management and Scalable Analytics**

This community focuses on MapReduce and distributed data management for large-scale processing, graph analysis, web corpora, joins, histograms, and data generation. Hadoop provides a MapReduce platform, while Spark, Hive, Pig, Jaql, Myria, and MRQL Streaming represent related processing systems. MapReduce workflows comprise jobs and execution plans, read and write distributed-file-system data, and are optimized by systems such as Stubby and Manimal. Key concerns include mapper/reducer memory, communication cost, reducer size, replication rate, output correctness and freshness, security and privacy, interoperability, and MapReduce’s limitations for fast data.

The community develops specialized methods: single-round MapReduce supports multiway joins; generalized hypertree decompositions support query processing; MapReduce executes kNN, fuzzy, SGF, and aggregate joins; and exact or approximate wavelet histograms address large datasets. Liah and adaptive indexing piggyback index construction on MapReduce tasks and HDFS blocks, improving workload performance while controlling overhead. MapUpdate extends the model.

Beyond batch processing, external-memory graph generation uses shuffle, relabel, redistribute, MPI, pthreads, and CSR conversion on small clusters. Probabilistic hitting sets guide scalable search, monitoring, influence analysis, and failure detection. Bloom filters, Bloofi, and Flat-Bloofi provide approximate-membership indexing for multidimensional and federated-cloud search.

6f322284be1c21f0e09ce45f8483f71a5379c829.text:
## Dynamic Network Reconstruction and Influential Node Tracking

This community studies two related tasks in changing networks: **dynamic network reconstruction** and **influential node tracking**. Dynamic networks are represented as streams of **edge weight updates**, with **incremental SVD** processing newly changed nodes and edges. Incremental updates accumulate **reconstruction loss**, while **SVD restart** resets this accumulated error when it exceeds a tolerated **maximum error**. Reconstruction quality is evaluated using maximum error.

The **timers** method automatically determines when to restart SVD. It monitors a margin involving reconstruction loss and uses the **SVD minimum loss lower bound** to simplify monitoring. Its time complexity is linear in the number of **local dynamic changes**, and it reduces reconstruction error in dynamic networks.

Influential node tracking identifies either nodes exceeding a user-specified threshold (**threshold influence identification**) or the **top-k influential nodes**. **Sample size determination** selects sample sizes for both identification tasks. The tracking problem is studied under the **linear threshold model** and the **independent cascade model**, and evaluated on five **real network datasets**.

f5356e2aa7ff62dd5520e871b70c5c288ce4c797.text:
## Community Detection and Dynamics in Complex Networks

This community centers on community structure in complex networks, including disjoint, overlapping, dynamic, blind, and core–periphery detection. Methods include DyPerm, Medoc, ENC O D, KromFac’s regularized nonnegative matrix factorization, and ensemble-based approaches. DyPerm incrementally updates affected communities in dynamic networks, optimizes permanence, and is reported 15 times faster than its static counterpart; it is evaluated with NMI on synthetic and real-world networks. Medoc identifies stable communities in dynamic networks, while ENC O D generates vertex feature vectors and combines disjoint-detection solutions. Permanence also identifies candidates for overlapping membership.

Evaluation uses normalized mutual information, precision@10, computational complexity, community-size distributions, partitioning strategies, optimization schemes, and networks with ground-truth structures. Core–periphery detection includes a nonlinear spectral algorithm based on nonlinear Perron–Frobenius theory and relaxed discrete optimization.

The community also covers network dynamics: NDlib supports diffusion simulation, a simulation server, online visualization, and experiments; approximate master-equation lumping clusters similar differential equations and estimates global properties; mean-field approximations analyze dynamics. Applications include Dublin Meetup co-membership networks, knowledge organization and acquisition through network walking agents, Granger-causality learning in multivariate point processes, and blind community detection in partially observable social networks.

a0d32d0e841bf9392b2f86b834324032c6518754.text:
### Graph-Based Anomaly Detection, Learning, and Social Data Mining

This community focuses on detecting anomalous behavior, learning from evolving data, and analyzing social and transactional networks. **Anomaly detection** spans transaction histories, attributed graphs, dense user groups, and dense subtensors. **Spectral anomaly detection**, **ACE**, **Vedar**, and regression-based online detection identify unusual behavior, while **Lookout** explains anomalies in time-evolving graphs by selecting interpretable pair plots with an explanation objective and approximate optimality guarantees. Vedar performs real-time behavior-change detection and is benchmarked against open-source datasets and other systems.

Both **supervised** and **unsupervised learning** support fake-news identification, rumour classification, news-topic classification, spammer detection, enterprise cyber-attack prediction, and money-laundering detection. **Factoid embedding** learns latent user representations across networks despite differing profile attributes and content types. **Self-Taught Hashing** produces binary document codes using supervised and unsupervised components, while graph diffusion convolution improves both supervised and unsupervised tasks.

For streams and dynamic networks, data-stream clustering, frequent-itemset mining, DenseStream, and DenseAlert address evolving data; DenseAlert detects anomalous dense subtensors. Other themes include user identity linkage, profile completion, multiple-membership analysis, and dynamic network reconstruction. Finally, **comparative summarisation** uses maximum mean discrepancy, gradient optimisation, and submodular subset selection to choose representative and distinguishable documents.

52ee2f81977142d99498f29880df2ba2c0d1ddc9.text:
## Community Structure and Dynamic Network Analysis

This community centers on inferring, characterizing, and mining community structure in static and dynamic networks. Statistical inference and statistical techniques use temporal network data, metadata, and node attributes—often treated as ground-truth communities—to study network organization and estimate evolutionary time constants. Synthetic and random networks, including planted communities and Erdős–Rényi networks, provide controlled experiments; real-world networks commonly exhibit power-law degree distributions.

Degree rank estimation uses local algorithms and network sampling to infer node rankings without observing entire networks. Absolute and weighted error evaluate estimation quality, while random and synthetic networks support validation.

For evolving systems, dynamic community detection and dynamic community mining identify communities and their active time intervals. Aggregated graphs can obscure short-lived communities. The filter-and-verify framework, implemented by PHASR, uses spectral bounds to prune suboptimal periods, reducing running time by 55–95% while finding higher-quality communities.

Dynamic network alignment extends static network alignment by optimizing dynamic edge and node conservation. DynaMAGNA++, an extension of MAGNA++, performs this task and is evaluated in computational biology.

Finally, network structure, node attributes, and metadata are interrelated; community characterization supports human interpretation and subsequent processing. Computer simulation and the delayed SIR model examine how structure and delay affect digital-virus spreading.

b5dc9e8d5c2b1e6f5a182c9065e9b8137c8bea2a.text:
## Bibliometric Evaluation and Citation Infrastructure

This community centers on **bibliometrics, scientometrics, and research assessment**, using publication and citation data to evaluate research productivity, performance, quality, and scientific impact. Key indicators include citation counts, total citations, citation rate, h-, g-, k-, c3-, and i3 indices, journal impact factor, journal quality, percentile ranks, citation distributions, and citation impact indicators.

**Web of Science** is the dominant infrastructure: it provides bibliographic records, citation counts, linked references, publication data, journal and subject-category classifications, and the Web of Science Core Collection. Its data support bibliometric analysis, citation analysis, citation-network construction, field delineation, visualization, and assessment of highly cited papers, scientific production, and international collaboration. **Journal Citation Reports** and impact-factor measures rely on Web of Science data.

Comparative systems include **Google Scholar, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, Mendeley, Altmetric.com, PlumX, OpenCitations, Data Citation Index,** and **Google Scholar Metrics**, particularly for citation coverage, alternative metrics, and open citation data. Methods address normalization through field, source, and citation normalization; fractional counting; citation linkage; reference publication year spectroscopy; co-authorship and co-readership visualization; and specialty approximation. Applications include national research assessment, journal rankings, research policy, interdisciplinary research, open access, collaboration networks, and university research evaluation.

29a8c98f203cb0d30943870a883d07e949096f74.text:
## Bibliometrics, Citation Analysis, and Research Evaluation

This community centers on bibliometrics and scientometrics for evaluating research productivity, quality, performance, and impact. It connects citation analysis and bibliometric analysis with research assessment, national research assessment exercises, peer review, journal ranking, university rankings, and individual researcher evaluation.

Web of Science is the dominant data system: it supplies bibliographic, publication, citation, and linked-reference data; organizes analysis through subject categories; supports citation-network construction; and provides records for tools such as CRExplorer. Its coverage includes the Science Citation Index, Social Science Citation Index, Journal Citation Reports, and the Data Citation Index. Google Scholar, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Mendeley, and Altmetric.com are compared or used as complementary sources for citation coverage, readership, bookmarks, and broader attention.

Key indicators include citation counts, h-, g-, k-, j-, c3-, and i3 indices, journal impact factor, citation impact, citation rate, percentile ranks, crown indicators, citation success, and journal quality measures. Methods address field, source, and citation normalization; fractional counting; benchmarking; simulation; network visualization; and visualization methodology. The community also examines citation distributions, highly cited papers, collaboration and co-authorship networks, interdisciplinarity, international collaboration, humanities and hard sciences, and research assessment in contexts including China, the United States, and Italian universities.

c3a0808bb9f6e8d8fcd4fc86f4c52ca3ddd9c8c2.text:
## Community Report: Graph Analytics, Temporal Data, and Efficient Inference

This community focuses on scalable graph analysis across temporal, heterogeneous, and uncertain data. Historical graph data is managed by temporal graph indexes, distributed graph databases, DeltaGraph, and GraphPool, supporting graph evolution analysis, snapshot retrieval, and historical subgraph pattern matching. FROG addresses task scheduling and worker notification to reduce task latency while maintaining task accuracy.

A major theme is structural and probabilistic modeling. Relation-strength-aware clustering uses probabilistic models to cluster heterogeneous objects while accounting for link strengths and user-specified attributes. Nonparametric multi-group membership models combine distance-dependent Indian buffet processes and factorial hidden Markov models to represent group birth, death, evolving memberships, and connectivity for network forecasting. Topological features support classification, while bounded expansion provides a strong notion of sparsity.

The community also studies temporal diffusion and discovery tasks, including diffusion-network sampling, propagation-path inference, information-source localization, BFF, and its relaxed O2BFF variant. Query research covers skyline and aggregate skyline joins, K-MAC product selection, reachability indexing, shortest-distance answering, and ANN search, emphasizing scalability, dimensionality, and query efficiency.

Mercer supports human-in-the-loop intelligence analysis using relationship bundles. Strongly universal string hashing provides high-throughput hashing, experimentally tested on low-power processors. Methods are evaluated on real and synthetic datasets, historical graphs, road graphs, news corpora, and intelligence-community data.

b80bef6bb87d7ffbc2fa9d7fb49dafb9e2f2b6fd.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Graph Analytics, Querying, and Network Inference

This community centers on graph data management, analysis, and evaluation across real, synthetic, historical, road, communication, and news datasets. Experimental evaluation measures degeneracy, hyperbolicity, bounded-expansion statistics, predictive performance, query efficiency, and snapshot retrieval time.

Temporal graph systems include **DeltaGraph**, **GraphPool**, and historical graph stores, which compactly record, store, or retrieve graph histories and snapshots. **Temporal graph analytics**, graph evolution analysis, and spatiotemporal burst tracking operate on these data. Reachability is addressed through classic and *k*-hop reachability tasks, reachability indexes, and the **k-hop reachability index**.

A major query theme is skyline processing: skyline, reverse skyline, aggregate skyline join, and *k*-dominant skyline join queries use batched algorithms, branch-and-bound, iterative algorithms, and efficient heuristics, with scalability studied over relation dimensionality. Query translation methods, universal query languages, and document search engines connect probabilistic translation models with search.

Network learning includes probabilistic models, relation-strength-aware clustering, topological-feature-based classification, graph-based semi-supervised learning, diffusion sampling, propagation-path inference, and missing-link prediction. Nonparametric multi-group membership models combine distance-dependent Indian buffet processes and factorial hidden Markov models for evolving memberships.

Visual analytics systems such as **Tableau** and **VCExplorer** support human-in-the-loop exploration, including loan-guarantee networks, enterprise default risk, and default diffusion paths. Hashing, persistent-memory data structures, and operation pipelining address implementation efficiency.

7d1806ca0f826e7c5a7263dc3cf8b2352a6b00af.text:
## Bibliometrics, Citation Indicators, and Research Evaluation

This community centers on **bibliometrics and scientometrics** for assessing research performance, productivity, quality, impact, and scientific output. Core activities include **citation analysis**, bibliometric analysis, research assessment, national research assessment exercises, journal rankings, benchmarking, and field delineation.

**Web of Science** is the dominant data source: it provides publication records, citation counts, linked references, bibliometric data, subject categories, and citation-network data. Its coverage supports analyses of scientific production, highly cited papers, interdisciplinarity, international collaboration, and field-normalized citation scores. Web of Science data also underpin the **Journal Impact Factor** and comparisons with **Google Scholar**, **Microsoft Academic**, CiteSeerX, and Mendeley.

Key indicators include the **h-index**, g-index, k-index, citation counts, total citations, citation rate, percentile ranks, journal impact factor, citation-impact indicators, Integrated Impact Indicator (i3), downloads, and Mendeley reader counts. **Altmetrics** and systems such as Altmetric.com and PlumX extend measurement beyond citations.

Important methods include citation and source normalization, fractional citation counting, citation matching and linkage, reference publication year spectroscopy, citation-network and co-authorship analysis, network visualization, co-readership visualization, and interdisciplinarity measures. Applications span computer science, mathematics, physics, biomedical research, humanities, climate-change research, universities, research institutions, and international collaboration.

640b93736c1b21277eb6d72826c15b565d2c2bf8.text:
## Open Access, Citation Impact, and Knowledge Networks

This community connects bibliometrics, altmetrics, societal impact, and agent-based models of knowledge acquisition. Web of Science supplies publications, journal data, citation counts, subject categories, and a real-world complex-networks dataset. Citation impact is assessed using Journal Impact Factor and a 2009–2014 citation window; the insufficient citation window is identified as a limitation.

The OA citation advantage focuses on Gold Open Access and proposes two explanations: the early view and selection bias postulates. A longitudinal multidisciplinary analysis tests these postulates and compares OA and non-OA journal impact factors.

Altmetric provides publication-level data, including policy-related documents that mention scientific papers. Annual analysis is recommended for both Web of Science publications with policy-related mentions and the usefulness of altmetric data. Policy-related mentions may indicate societal impact, but should not yet be used for impact measurement until more policy-related sites are tracked.

For knowledge discovery, complex networks provide a structural setting, with information entropy quantifying structural importance. Knowledge acquisition is modeled as agents moving through a knowledge space via a multi-agent random walk. The model incorporates local topology, agent visibility, and agent memory; its walk uses a modified true self-avoiding walk with stochastic flights dependent on visibility fields.

a852c97ead54c1d1bee89f6074a7c46706c8c976.text:
## Research Evaluation, Citation Metrics, and Scalable Data Systems

This community links research evaluation with citation and altmetric indicators. Citation counts, Mendeley readership, and readership counts are related to scientific quality, while Twitter counts are less strongly related and discouraged for evaluation. Altmetrics are contrasted with citations because they capture additional forms of impact; factor analysis and principal component analysis examine their dimensions, including a distinct Twitter dimension. Convergent validity is assessed against REF data, peer assessments, and F1000Prime post-publication reviews. Regression and correlation analyses test relationships among quality, productivity, citations, and research-output indicators. Scientific production is framed through both qualitative quality and quantitative productivity. Field- and time-normalized indicators, including the Mantel–Haenszel quotient (MHQ), address sparse data and institutional units of analysis.

A second theme concerns citation practice: citation theories and conceptual analysis model document selection and the contexts of citing and cited documents.

The community also covers scalable analytics. D4M, D4M.jl, and the D4M–Accumulo connector support database ingest, querying, and analytics pipelines across Julia, MATLAB, and GNU Octave. NoSQL consistency levels govern replication and performance. Finally, ANN Benchmarks compares k-NN and approximate-nearest-neighbor methods for similarity search across standard datasets, parameter settings, and quality–performance trade-offs.

7fc9fef331d8b90722b5d9920d12651a705fe52c.text:
## Social Media Measurement, Privacy, and Malicious Information

This community examines Facebook activity, altmetrics, junk news, and pathogenic social-media accounts (PSM accounts). Facebook is studied as a scholarly-communication medium: a Facebook activity collection gathered shares, reactions, and comments on PLOS ONE articles published from 2015–2017, including activity in both public and private online spaces. Comparing these data with aggregated altmetrics highlights the importance of openness and transparency; the altmetric system collects and aggregates such measures.

A junk news aggregator provides public Facebook content from major US junk news publishers, enabling near-real-time monitoring, transparency into engagement, and media-literacy support. Facebook also assigns advertising interests to users. A browser extension can remove sensitive interests, such as homosexuality, which may be linked to sensitive personal data and associated privacy risks. GDPR, enforced in the European Union, restricts processing of such data under data-protection regulations; homosexuality and the death penalty illustrate the sensitivity of relevant categories.

The community also models malicious information dissemination. PSM accounts differ from regular users in message virality and audience impact, particularly when sharing alternative-news URLs, while generally avoiding mainstream-news URLs. The ISIS-related Twitter dataset provides behavioral evidence, and a Hawkes process quantifies and models PSM influence on information spread.

ce0324e80689983b2dea2f30c0db1b6d16650c08.text:
## Wikipedia, Scientific Structure, and Research Discovery

This community connects three main themes: research-article recommendation, Wikipedia knowledge organization, and ideological diversity in collaborative editing.

A research-article recommendation task links vaccination-related PubMed articles with communication webpages identified through Altmetric. Canonical correlation analysis ranks candidate source articles relative to webpages and augments baseline ranking methods. Performance is measured by median rank, top-1 source-article accuracy, and top-50 source-article accuracy.

Wikipedia is examined through edits, references, tables, and editor activity. The Wikipedia References Dataset draws on Altmetric journal data and Scopus Journal Metrics, classifies articles using all-science journal classifications, and includes Humanities subsets. Research on ideological diversity uses editor surveys, talk-page debates, Wikipedia policies, and Wikipedia edits to connect offline ideological identity with online collaboration. Balanced ideological diversity is associated with stronger team performance and higher article quality, especially for political, social-issues, and science articles; diverse teams also engage in longer, more constructive debates.

TableNet addresses Wikipedia table interlinking through candidate table retrieval and neural table relation classification. It identifies equivalent and subPartOf table relations, using table schemas; retrieval exceeds 88% coverage and alignment classification reaches 90% accuracy.

Additional work studies academic paper structure: headings are analyzed across disciplines for usage prevalence and structural variation, while rhetorical structure concerns how science conveys messages. Humanities articles may avoid headings altogether.

da2763e60dc78051f7f3457552a9d15f5d4688ee.text:
## Bibliometrics, Citation Indicators, and Scholarly Evaluation

This community centers on bibliometrics and research evaluation using citation-based measures for papers, journals, researchers, and scientific fields. Google Scholar provides broad citation coverage, including theses, books, conference papers, and unpublished materials, and supports Google Scholar Metrics, Google Scholar Citations, Publish or Perish, Scholarometer, and other third-party tools. Scopus, Web of Science/WoS Core Collection, Microsoft Academic, and Crossref-related DOI infrastructure provide complementary publication and citation data; Microsoft Academic reports more citations than Scopus overall but fewer than Google Scholar.

Key indicators include raw citation counts, the h-index, g-index, h-alpha, impact factor, journal citedness, field-normalized citations, field-normalized citation scores, citation impact, and second-order indicators. These measures support comparative evaluation, top-cited-paper identification, and assessment of research performance, while being affected by self-citation, reference-list length, citation distributions, field differences, and coauthor credit attribution.

Methods include descriptive statistics, factor and regression analysis, normalization procedures, citation weighting, robust benchmarking, and statistical concordance. Altmetric.com scores and Mendeley reader counts extend evaluation toward readership and non-scholarly impact. The community also addresses open peer review, reproducibility, and research software: JOSS assigns DOIs, improves software quality, and publishes under a Creative Commons license with NumFOCUS and Open Source Initiative affiliations.

a7be288ec8f3318b6f9ce0323257085a8d90c8ae.text:
## Scientometric, Talent-Flow, and Research-Policy Analysis

This community integrates network-based scientometrics, academic policy analysis, job mobility, and scholar identification. A visual scientometric survey uses Web of Science bibliometric data—associated with Thomson Reuters—to examine 1.3 million research papers across 249 subject categories. Network analysis applies centrality, frequency, and citation bursts to identify key journals, subject categories, and universities, including literature on clinical decision support systems. Systematic literature surveys and network visualization tools support this work.

A second theme concerns higher-order networks: construction algorithms represent higher-order interaction data and enable interactive exploration, extending network analysis beyond networks to sequential and diffusion data.

Policy studies examine cash-per-publication reward policies in China, especially Chinese universities. Document analysis of 168 university policy documents from 100 universities covers 1999–2016, including journal eligibility, rewards ranging from $30 to $165,000, and rising average reward amounts.

Job-hop analysis uses public professional profiles and scalable data-science methods, complementing surveys. Work-experience and job-recency metrics relate to hopping propensity, promotion, and demotion, providing insights into talent flow and job- and organization-level competitiveness.

Finally, matching algorithms and rule-based scoring identify scholars with Twitter accounts from bibliometric data. Twitter activity share varies with publication productivity, is stronger in social sciences and humanities, and is lowest in natural sciences.

5e1e34239360e1aa19ba7391c740319550e1e01b.text:
## Bibliometric Evaluation and the H-Index

This community centers on bibliometrics and scientometrics for evaluating research performance, productivity, quality, and impact. Citation analysis uses citation counts, citation distributions, citation impact indicators, journal impact factor, h-, g-, k-, j-, and related indices, as well as percentile ranks and the integrated impact indicator (i3).

The h-index is the dominant theme: it quantifies researcher and journal output from citations, supports author and journal ranking, and reduces sensitivity to extreme citation-distribution tails. However, it is not field normalized, omits parts of the citation record, depends on journal size and time windows, and can disadvantage selective researchers or fail to capture collaborative contributions. Variants and complements include timed, recent, weighted, social, c3, j, and i indices.

Web of Science supplies bibliographic records, citation counts, linked references, subject categories, and citation-network data; its Science Citation Index and Social Science Citation Index are included. It supports bibliometric analysis of scientific production and is compared with Google Scholar for citation coverage. Scopus, Mendeley, InCites, Google Scholar Metrics, Journal Citation Reports, and Data Citation Index represent additional systems for citation, readership, journal, and research assessment.

Key methods include fractional counting, citation and source normalization, field normalization, benchmarking, network visualization, simulation, and bibliometric analysis. Applications include national and institutional assessment, journal ranking, collaboration analysis, interdisciplinary research, and evaluation of Italian university researchers.

fcc6e1c2f3fe5c36d0eccef9cf9e93cd74c34c53.text:
## Bibliometrics, Research Fronts, and Scientific Innovation

This community links bibliometric analysis, scientometric indicators, citation networks, and research diversification. Web of Science (a Thomson Reuters source) and Scopus provide publication and citation data, with journals as analytical units; Web of Science also systematically collected funding acknowledgments from August 2008. Funding studies examine acknowledgment type, database, and language, while recognizing coverage limitations and potential biases and attracting interest from academia and policy makers.

Citation networks, network clustering, and text mining identify research fronts. In HIV/AIDS research, fronts span clinical knowledge, cellular research, and molecular structures and mechanisms, with emergence shaped by technological and epidemiological change. Two molecular fronts relate to drug development. Knowledge translation connects research fronts with biomedical innovation, including translating nanomaterials into pharmaceutical alternatives.

Bibliometric indicators assess scientific output and citation impact. The h-index and Euclidean index measure journal or author impact; the Euclidean index is evaluated against existing indicators for measurement scale and distinctions among analytical units. Research diversification among individual scientists is characterized by extent, intensity, and degree of relatedness: Chemistry leads in extent and relatedness, Industrial and Information Engineering in intensity, while Mathematics and Earth sciences show the lowest extent and intensity/relatedness, respectively.

Spatial scientometrics examines cities: Medicine is highly productive in many cities, Beijing leads output, and high-output cities cluster partly in China. Dental materials research features eleven emerging fronts, including titanium implants, ceramics, composites, and mineral trioxide aggregates.

9f341fabcd83f93f607752e45630c8fd1b65e473.text:
## Open Access, Bibliometrics, and ResearchGate Metrics

This community examines Open Access (OA), citation analysis, linked-reference quality, and institutional research visibility. An OA-labeling methodology systematically combines evidence from diverse sources, including DOAJ, Crossref, OpenDOAR, and ROAR, to distinguish Gold OA (publisher access) from Green OA (repository or archiving routes). Green OA exceeds Gold OA in proportion and growth in most disciplines, while overall free availability is reported at 54.6%. National OA mandates encourage researchers to publish outputs openly.

Web of Science, Google Scholar, and Microsoft Academic support citation and bibliometric analysis. Web of Science and Microsoft Academic linked references show weak-to-nonexistent concordance in the full sample but strong agreement in a restricted sample of publications with fewer than 50 references. Google Scholar measures citations and supplies links to freely available documents, while Microsoft Academic reports fewer citation counts than Google Scholar. Journal Citation Reports 2016 and the Science Citation Index/Social Sciences Citation Index provide citation contexts.

ResearchGate assigns scores to academics and institutions. These scores correlate strongly with Web of Science publication counts and reflect research volume more than visibility, limiting their value for institutional comparison. ResearchGate presence is widespread among PhD-awarding institutions and relates to publication count, while institutional size predicts presence among non-publishing, non-PhD institutions. Citation-orientation analysis studies domestic versus international referencing in natural-sciences papers from 2004, 2009, and 2014.

b7bbbbe03db4214d6e02616404354d5eadb2241a.text:
## Explainable QA and Measuring Interdisciplinarity

This community connects explainable question answering (XQA) with the study and measurement of interdisciplinarity.

Question answering systems, accessed through QA interfaces, provide simplified access to information on the Web, where information pollution occurs. Explainable question answering extends conventional question answering to help alleviate this problem. It provides transparency into the underlying computational model, exposing learning and reasoning steps, information context, interpretation, provenance, and validity. XQA evaluation assesses these systems and their explanatory capabilities.

A second theme concerns interdisciplinarity, characterized as a multidimensional and complex construct. Interdisciplinarity measures are proposed to quantify it and are examined for validity. A systematic review considers how these measures relate to journal subject categories, using information and categories supplied by Web of Science. The measures are used and evaluated in science studies and evaluation studies, with relevance to science policies.

Together, the community links transparent, provenance-aware information access with methodological approaches for evaluating interdisciplinary research.

0301e2e0129a1c403e9a7e6ab3fbf5992abb27fe.text:
# Bibliometrics, Researcher Mobility, and Recommendation

This community centers on bibliometric analysis of computer networking and scholarly impact. Publication counts and article citations, sourced from Crossref, ACM, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar, identify influential authors, institutes, countries, and publication trends in *IEEE Communications Surveys and Tutorials*, *IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking*, SIGCOMM, and INFOCOM. Web of Science and Scopus are compared with Google Scholar for citation coverage; neither indexes American doctoral dissertations.

Researcher evaluation includes the h-index, h-core, K-index, and coauthorship-aware h-alpha and h-alpha-prime indices. The K-index measures citation-network centrality, captures researcher connectedness, and supports scientific-award prediction, including Physics Nobel Prize candidate shortlists. Alpha-authors and alpha-papers identify leading contributors within collaborations.

Dissertation impact assessment uses Google Scholar citation counts extracted by a multistage method from 77,884 American doctoral dissertations accessed through ProQuest. Mendeley reader counts complement citations, particularly for newer dissertations, while Google Scholar counts are useful for older work.

Another theme is researcher mobility: affiliation-address tracking in Web of Science identifies peripatetic researchers publishing in multiple countries. The discussion progresses from brain drain/gain toward brain circulation, with the USA, China, England, and Germany characterized as hubs in the global science system.

Finally, ACM’s Recommender Systems Challenge 2019 includes session-based hotel recommendation from booking sessions, an e-tourism task.

f6e4e06ddbf63d4f954332e6f9ab708a4c4195ca.text:
## Scientific Impact, Mobility, and Sequential Prediction

This community links scientometrics, bibliometric data, and machine-learning methods for studying scientific impact, researcher mobility, collaboration, and recommendation.

Scientific impact is measured through citation count and shaped by the Matthew effect, intrinsic quality, publication aging, and recency. Deep-learning attention mechanisms predict long-term popularity dynamics and interpret these effects. Recurrent neural networks, including long short-term memory networks, predict long-term citation counts using large citation datasets; citation datasets also support popularity-dynamics evaluation.

A scientific mobility framework analyzes institutional affiliation changes, classifying researchers as migrants or travelers and developing mobility indicators from bibliometric data. It incorporates incoming and outgoing mobility, with directionality also applied to country-level mobility. Migrants are associated with higher scientific impact than travelers.

Research collaboration motivates publication-credit methods that account for collaboration benefits. The n-author publication valuation method uses only author count to estimate expected publication value, with axiomatic analysis providing its basis.

For session-based recommendation from anonymous short sessions, recurrent neural networks and heuristic nearest neighbors serve as baselines. A nonparametric context tree supports efficient recommendation, learns static sequential patterns, and adapts to domain changes. Adaptive evaluation simulates continuously arriving new items with limited observations, contrasting with standard static evaluation.

1d31aa8a6e7b6cd2cdae56f23bf0f90d7929a99b.text:
## Biomedical Citation, Translation, and Research Orientation

This community examines how biomedical research connects basic science, clinical research, translational science, and private-sector innovation. A **translational axis** places basic science at one end and clinical medicine at the other. **Controlled vocabulary embeddings**, learned from vocabularies assigned to MEDLINE papers, produce this axis; **appliedness** and **level score** quantify papers’ positions by averaging term locations. A paper-level research orientation indicator measures orientation toward basic or clinical research and has been applied to 5 million biomedical papers.

Citation analysis is another major theme. **Section-based citation counting** uses originating article sections, including introductions and methods, to distinguish context-setting from methodological impact. It has been investigated with DOI-identified citations in PubMed Central open-access articles, although expert judgment is needed for validation. Citation networks incorporate citation context, and direct citations tend to connect papers with similar level scores. Basic-science papers generally receive more citations, while clinical and translational research show lower citation counts, greater citation variance, and fewer highly cited hit works.

**Citation linkage** connects research with life-science, biotechnology, and drug patents. Public research—particularly university research and NIH-funded work—accounts for much patent citation activity and contributes continuously to private-sector inventions.

e768de6408896accee12a09b3ab7362ab1b266b2.text:
## Bibliometrics, Research Evaluation, and Scholarly Decision-Making

This community centers on bibliometrics and scientometrics for research evaluation, academic career advancement, field delineation, and collaboration analysis. Citation count, citation impact, scientific impact, average citations, field-normalized impact, journal impact factor, article influence score, journal quartiles, productivity, and career-wise impact are key metrics. Citation behavior varies by research field, career length, publication year, team size, and journal characteristics.

Google Scholar, Scopus, Dimensions, Semantic Scholar, Microsoft Academic Search, and Google Scholar Profiles provide citation and academic-search data. Comparative analyses examine their coverage, including conference proceedings and peer-reviewed journals. Bibliometric methods include citation analysis, regression analysis, comparative bibliometric analysis, stratified probabilistic sampling, and expert-opinion interviews. Field delineation is evaluated at subject-category, publication, and journal levels, including nanoscience and nanotechnology.

Studies address grant novelty, subsidies, publication support, predatory journals, data-availability statements, open access, and international indexing. Gender inequality, mentorship quality, mentor number and academic age, and university rank are linked to scientific impact and academic careers. Research collaboration is studied through team size and authorship patterns.

A related decision-science cluster examines heuristics, information-greedy procedures, judgment under uncertainty, decision environments, and accuracy–effort trade-offs, including the fast-and-frugal heuristics research program.

5657df19216c140d7049aee1a0d6cad22d24a61a.text:
## Semantic Networks, Scholarly Metrics, and Historical Change

This community examines how research fields evolve through semantic, citation, spatial, and social networks, with particular attention to humanities and historiography.

Semantic networks are constructed from author-declared keywords, full-text themes, or citation relationships. They represent semantic proximity, shared vocabularies, and narratives, and support analysis of temporal and epistemological evolution. An interactive application compares these construction strategies using the *Cybergeo* publication corpus, examining spatial expressions, studied countries, and the spatialised bibliometrics of geographical research.

A second focus is the structure and evolution of history specialisms. Reference-overlap and textual-similarity networks represent relationships among specialisms, while author bibliographic-coupling networks capture scholarly connectivity. Reference-overlap connectivity steadily declines, textual-similarity connectivity remains stable, and author-coupling connectivity declines without increased collaboration. This relates to Fuchs’ theory of scientific change, which predicts growing intellectual and social fragmentation under low mutual dependence and high task uncertainty, although shared vocabularies and narratives may continue integrating scholarship despite weaker citation ties.

The community also evaluates Twitter activity as a scholarly metric. Tweets linking to scholarly documents may provide early indicators of citations and measures of societal impact. Pearson, Spearman, Kendall tau, and distance correlations compare network-derived cluster centroids with a golden-standard event record; Spearman correlations are lower for citation counts across humanities systems.

aca586707c2529808311c5aa69c3282c82331c3e.text:
## Bibliometrics, Citation Impact, and Research Evaluation

This community examines bibliometric evaluation of research performance, outputs, individuals, and research institutions. Citation counts, journal impact factor, immediacy index, and other bibliometric indicators support research evaluation and university rankings, although rankings may suppress disciplinary differences and bibliometricians criticize their use. Government interest in fiscalizing university outputs is related to rankings.

Google Scholar supports bibliometric research by identifying highly cited documents, merging article versions for citation counts, and ranking results by position. Language effects, publication-date handling, and version identification affect the reliability of highly cited-document identification.

The community studies early citations as predictors of long-term scientific impact. Supervised citation prediction models improve when incorporating early citer properties; influential and non-influential early citers are distinguished by publication and citation counts. Influential early citers may reduce long-term impact, potentially through attention stealing, especially when collaboration-network proximity is high. An early citer statistics portal visualizes these patterns.

Co-authorship defines collaboration networks, including single-field, specific cross-field, and non-specific collaboration. Inter-field collaboration characterizes interdisciplinarity and is analyzed for its effect on research-output impact. Advance online publication accelerates article citations and changes journal impact factor and immediacy-index values; studies use the Mann–Whitney U test and journal datasets to examine these effects. DIY and off-the-shelf evaluation approaches are identified as potentially risky or unsuitable.

dbe394ed46154c11d9bda495ecab14bb67ba47c5.text:
## Research Mapping, Open Access, and Social Structure

This community centers on scientometrics and network-based analysis of scientific knowledge. **Citation networks** are used for scientific evaluation, knowledge retrieval, article-importance detection, research-front identification, and tracing historical development through **main path analysis**, **text mining**, and **multi-RPYS**. Citation structures are examined through reference-age distributions, cited and citing environments, author communities, normalization, and network-based models.

**Research fronts** reveal changing areas of knowledge, including HIV/AIDS research on clinical knowledge, molecular mechanisms, cellular processes, drug resistance, virus replication, and related topics. **Cited references** support country comparisons, novelty scores, percentile-based citation indicators, and referenced publication-year spectroscopy.

A second major theme is **Open Access**. Gold and green OA are distinguished, with Crossref, DOAJ, and OpenDOAR supporting OA classification. Pay-to-publish, self-archiving, mandates, funders, subscription journals, and article-processing charges describe routes and policies associated with access and its growth.

**Text mining** supports cognitive-organization studies, research-front discovery, semantic characterization, and the NPD idea-discovery framework, including analysis of crowdsourced ideas. Finally, RFID tracking and mobile-phone communication are used to infer **social structure**, including proximity and displacement relationships in rhesus macaque groups.

b3de34567a492c83bd58b5cc0acf18b8e1736f4c.text:
## Bibliometrics, Open Access, and Networked Social Analysis

This community centers on scholarly communication, citation analysis, and quantitative evaluation. Citation networks support research-front identification, historical main-path analysis, knowledge retrieval, article-importance detection, and scientific evaluation. Text mining complements network analysis by revealing cognitive organization, textual patterns, and paradigmatic fronts; it also powers idea discovery from crowdsourcing applications through semantic characterization and iterative retrieval.

Reference Publication Year Spectroscopy (RPYS) identifies influential cited references, historical roots, and the historical impact of current research, with examples in graphene and solar-cell research. Citation frequency, reference age distributions, percentile-based indicators, productivity, rankings, and quantitative impact measures support scientific evaluation, while citing-side normalization addresses differences in citation propensity.

Open access is divided into gold OA and green OA, with self-archiving associated with accessibility, reader attention, and OA growth. Downloads provide usage-based impact measures, including download share, accumulation time, and paper lifetime.

The community also covers scalable computation: Count-Min Sketch variants, conservative updates, log/tree sketches, and approximate counters address event counting, while parallel triangle counting uses cache-oblivious frameworks. Finally, RFID, mobile-phone communication, purchasing habits, socioeconomic classes, and opinion dynamics connect network methods to social structure; machine learning supports relationship inference, viral-event prediction, and opponent-action anticipation.

241bd4c819546a2a401bbb70826c0aa7d9e3f5b0.text:
## Topic Modeling, Learning, and Text-Based Discovery

This community centers on **topic modeling** and **text mining** for discovering latent themes, structures, and communication patterns in documents, user-written text, social-media posts, course material, forum posts, and literary transcripts. **Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)** is a central method, representing item properties as topic proportions and supporting topical relevance, topic coherence, latent topic discovery, and biomedical hypothesis generation. Related approaches include **dynamic topic modeling**, **online hierarchical Dirichlet processes**, **continuous-time dynamic models**, **labeled LDA**, **separable non-negative matrix factorization**, **full dependence mixture**, and **ET-LDA**.

The community also links topic analysis with **supervised and unsupervised learning**. These paradigms support fake-news identification, rumour classification, news-topic classification, tag-relevance fusion, self-taught hashing, and graph diffusion convolution. Unsupervised methods address factoid embedding, dense-user-group discovery, and network representation, while supervised methods use annotated rumours, social-network features, and mutual-activity features.

Applications include **keyphrase extraction**, **literary-theme identification**, **idea discovery**, **scientific and biomedical exploration**, **web-page recommendation**, and **bisociative information networks**. Systems and frameworks such as **DANE**, **Moliere**, **IDEL**, the **NPD idea discovery framework**, and **hypothesis generation systems** connect extracted topics, embeddings, graphs, and retrieval tasks.

8bc2ca475541aedbe6e62afed485831249b880e8.text:
## Social Network Analysis, User Modeling, and Online Abuse Detection

This community connects user modeling, social-network structure, sentiment, and online-abuse analysis. User modeling represents people with features from access logs, page content, semantic information, mind maps, downloaded or cited articles, and other data sources. Scoring functions support profile evaluation, segmentation, and user-interest inference; embedding-based transaction integration improves these models.

A major theme is cyberbullying and cyberaggression. Detection and prediction use classifiers, linguistic and image content, social-graph features, temporal commenting behavior, and participant vocabulary consistency. A multi-stage detection solution combines an initial predictor, multilevel priority scheduling, and incremental classification to reduce classification time and alert latency, with Vine and Instagram image-comment data used for evaluation. Ask.fm question-answer profiles and its likes network support analysis of cutting behavior and other negative behavior.

The community also covers spam-tweet detection using tweet-inherent features and hand-labeled datasets, alongside competing spammer-detection systems. Sentiment features include valence, arousal, and dominance, supported by sentiment lexicons and SentiStrength.

Finally, bipartite networks connect emotional agents and posts and can be transformed through one-mode or unipartite projections. Neighborhood-based similarity uses entity neighborhoods, unified parametric models, and distributed implementations for large networks.

6cc744349580feb31fc807d77f5b853b17cfd863.text:
## Attention, CQA Routing, and Spam Detection

This community covers attention and influence in online communities, community question answering (CQA), and review spam detection.

The attention work distinguishes **interactional attention** to peers from **informational attention** to content. Users focus on limited sets of peers and topics; peer positions, activity levels, and attentional constraints help refine influence models, while informational attention exhibits focus effects.

For CQA, **cold question routing** addresses questions from newly registered users by finding suitable potential answerers. An **end-to-end routing framework** jointly learns CQA node embeddings, incorporates textual information such as question tags, and leverages heterogeneous graph information. Its embeddings represent graph structural information. The **GAS model**, based on a GCN, integrates homogeneous graphs for global context and heterogeneous graphs for local context, and is deployed at Xianyu.

The review-spam strand uses an anti-spam system operating at Xianyu. A baseline model uses user features, reviewed-item features, and online-review information, while graphs capture local and global review context. Spam review detection compares against this baseline and is performed by the GAS model.
