c672536912eb7041161ae4c7110be498a205e5d9.text:
## Computational Analysis of News, Topics, and Journalists

This community focuses on computational analysis of news articles, their topics, and the relationships expressed through news content. A dataset contains over 500,000 articles linked to 1,000 journalists across 25 news outlets. These articles reflect socioeconomic activities, cultures, human interests, and public concerns, while frequently mentioning cities.

Topic models measure documents’ topical diversity using three elements: topics, words, and documents viewed as collections of words. Hierarchical re-estimation improves topic models at the word, topic, and document levels by combating generality and topic impurity; it outperforms the state of the art on PubMed. Topic models also support dictionary extraction, using co-occurrence data from reference collections.

A computational framework reads large numbers of news articles and extracts semantic relatedness between cities. City co-occurrence—two or more cities appearing in one article—often suggests relatedness, although relatedness varies by topic.

The community also examines media story construction and ideology. Journalists produce news content, and the ideological composition of the accounts they follow reflects their ideological leaning. This social-network composition is associated with the content journalists produce, with a modest correlation between followed accounts’ ideology and journalistic content.

1041402f45f1dffdb6317e3075815fae260aa714.text:
## Community Report: Social Behavior, Content Classification, and User Modeling

This community centers on analyzing social behavior and classifying user-generated content. Cyberbullying is treated as negative behavior related to cyberaggression, victims, instigators, suicidal behavior, and cutting behavior. Detection uses linguistic and image content, social-graph features, temporal commenting behavior, and classifiers trained on labeled Instagram and Vine data. A multi-stage solution combines an initial predictor, multilevel priority scheduler, and incremental classification to reduce classification time and alert latency. Participant vocabulary consistency uses a seed dictionary to discover bullying vocabulary and instigators.

A second theme concerns social-network structure and interaction. Ask.fm question-and-answer profiles and liking networks support analysis of cutting behavior and negative behavior. Bipartite networks connecting emotional agents and posts can be projected into one-mode networks. HNIL combines question embeddings, heterogeneous social-network information, and random-walk learning for question retrieval, addressing lexical gaps in CQA data.

The community also covers sentiment and content classification. Valence, arousal, and dominance features, sentiment lexicons, ANEW, and SentiStrength support television classification and sentiment-strength detection. Spam-tweet detection evaluates inherent tweet features against labeled datasets, while broader spammer systems use historical, network, and user features. User modeling integrates access logs, page content, semantic information, and segmentation for satisfaction prediction.

75d8c5d8ef39c10b6f7f2808684530238963e319.text:
## Community Report: Mobility, Demographics, Networks, and Intelligent Systems

This community connects human mobility, demographic analysis, social relationships, and platform-based urban services. Human mobility is studied through cellular-phone, mobile-network, call-detail, and check-in data, with applications to trajectory analysis, traffic prediction, pandemic spread, opportunistic routing, and spatial interaction. Gravity models, agent-based modeling, mobility mapping, and dynamic graph/network approaches explain movement, distance decay, and population dynamics.

Gender and age support demographic inference, attribute prediction, and relationship characterization. Call frequency and daily regularity vary by gender and age, while homophily scores and node-similarity measures characterize social ties. These themes connect to mobile communication patterns, sexual-market submarkets, and demographic identification from profile images.

Airbnb is examined as a peer-to-peer sharing-economy platform in relation to hotels, tourism pressure, gentrification, municipalities, and spatial distribution in Barcelona. Its customer-service live-chat system is also represented.

Recommendation systems combine customer, product, and trip embeddings with context vectors, semantics-aware autoencoders, and time-dependent item bias. They support food-flavour matching, healthy-alternative suggestions, explanation services, and biomedical knowledge-base applications.

Finally, emotions are analyzed in music, human sounds, news, marketing, urban smellscapes, and viral facets using affective annotation, mixed-effects models, and valence–arousal–dominance representations.

14a42a2a2cca63e0556ba399958b165dd6192d03.text:
## Community Report: Retrieval, Classification, and Summarization

This community centers on methods for organizing, retrieving, classifying, and summarizing text and multimedia content.

**Information retrieval and question answering** include document retrieval over large text collections, legal information retrieval, unseen-query retrieval, and privacy-preserving passage retrieval. Retrieval systems use TF-IDF, weighted word-embedding centroids, relaxed Word Mover’s Distance for reranking, similarity search, relevance feedback, and visual or textual cues. Question answering accepts natural-language questions and uses text matching, word overlap, lexical-morphological modeling, and explainable interfaces.

**Text classification and categorization** use bag-of-words, TF-IDF, k-nearest neighbors and its augmented variant, support vector machines, twin SVMs, multi-label classification, supervised term weighting, and sequential document representations. Applications include biomedical, Arabic, authorship, web-spam, bias, and multi-class classification, evaluated on datasets such as Reuters-21578, PubMed, Twitter streams, and Arabic document corpora.

**Summarization** spans single- and multi-document extractive summarization, automatic and hybrid models, and privacy-preserving multi-document summarization. TF-IDF scores sentences, while ROUGE and ROUGE 2.0 evaluate summary quality through n-gram overlap, with limitations for synonymy and topic coverage.

The community also covers ontology development, citation-context analysis, relation extraction, multimodal event detection, and scalable compressed indexes.

b5bb563574d3fc9e9d8d2cd351db734864b6c9ac.text:
## Community Report: Text Analytics, Summarization, Retrieval, and Scholarly Data

This community centers on methods for representing, classifying, retrieving, and summarizing text and multimedia data.

**Text classification and representation** include text categorization, biomedical and Arabic text classification, authorship attribution, web-spam detection, and bias detection. Core methods include support vector machines, twin support vector machines, k-nearest neighbors and its augmented variant, supervised term weighting, TF-IDF, bag-of-words, explicit semantic analysis, and sequential document representations. Bag-of-words supports TF-IDF features but loses sequential information; semantic and adaptive representations address related limitations, especially for short texts and sparse data.

**Summarization** spans single- and multi-document, extractive, automatic, and privacy-preserving summarization. The hybrid summarization model combines sentence position, aggregate similarity, centroid scoring, and TF-IDF. Multi-document approaches also use hierarchical combination and multi-layered graph models. ROUGE evaluates summarization, while ROUGE 2.0 adds topic- and synonym-aware measures.

**Retrieval and indexing** include document retrieval, unseen-query and live-video-stream retrieval, similarity search, compressed indexes, and privacy-preserving passage retrieval. ONTRAC performs map-matched online trajectory compression and travel-time prediction.

**Scholarly and biomedical analysis** uses MeSH matrices, citation-context analysis, directed citation networks, ontology development, relation extraction, and context-sensitive article ranking. Aggregate-query estimation, clustering, and correlated-heavy-hitter methods address scalable data processing.

915a9f95e420acfbffa0164a7dfdad9371d6cdf2.text:
### Research on Accurate, Explainable Prediction and Ranking

This community spans machine learning for social media, mobility, biomedical text, recommendation, information retrieval, and risk analysis. Accuracy is a central evaluation metric: clickbait detection reaches 93%, personalized clickbait blocking 89%, spam classification exceeds 99% on Facebook and 98% on Twitter, and the correlational artificial neural network reaches 97.57%. Other reported results include 92.1% country-level and 52.8% city-level prediction.

Key methods include supervised machine learning, SVM, k-nearest neighbors, mixture models, matrix factorization, Gaussian mixture models, attention distributions, and hybrid deep learning. K-nearest neighbors supports biomedical text classification, tweet-spam classification, trajectory dissimilarity, and a KNN query interface, while mixture models produce better recommenders than k-NN. Matrix factorization optimizes recommendation accuracy, and NEMF minimizes its accuracy compromise.

BERT and its biomedical variants, BioBERT and ClinicalBERT, provide contextualized representations for question answering, passage and document ranking, and biomedical entity normalization. Clickbait systems combine linguistic, image-based, and location-based features; a browser extension warns readers. Other systems address political slant, radical content, dangerous selfies, tweet geolocation, mobility modeling, transaction risk, and scientific mapping. Explainability, interpretability, calibration, novelty, runtime performance, and earliness complement accuracy in evaluating these systems.

75907273552ec18070bfea6eda6ef52ed071eb4e.text:
## Social Media Analytics, Communities, and Misinformation

This community studies social media as a source of event, community, and behavioral signals. **EviDense** is a graph-based system for high-impact event detection in tweets, producing keyword-based descriptions and fewer duplicate events; mainstream-media news improves its results. Related event-detection methods use geo-tagged tweet streams, spatio-temporal distributions, multi-spatial-scale analysis, and power-law activity patterns associated with short-term unplanned events.

Community analysis includes an event-based sentiment framework that identifies event-related tweets, communities, and influential users, with qualitative and quantitative evaluation. An entropy-based vulnerability measure combines internal and external factors—including inter-community similarity and external node counts—and is sensitivity-tested with Sobol indices on real-world complex networks. Nonuniform timeslicing applies histogram equalization to reduce visual complexity in dynamic graph visualization.

Misinformation research addresses fake-news detection and mitigation using content, network features, social engagements, network types, and online activity signals. Weak supervision uses weak labels, heuristic rules, external knowledge, and unlabelled data to address labeled-data scarcity, including training neural check-worthiness ranking models based on syntactic dependencies.

Other tasks include stance detection, event causality detection, automatic fact checking, and academic-performance prediction. Predictive models use tweets and VK posts, continuous word representations, and reproduce school and university rankings. Evaluation uses precision, F-measure, mean average precision, academic performance, and qualitative or quantitative assessment.

a253d165e4cf357a1917ed7de1b4c14e48b0d3af.text:
### Topic Modeling, Constitutional Analysis, and XML-OLAP

This community combines topic modeling, constitutional research, and complex-data warehousing.

Topic modeling derives statistically linked word groups (“topics”) and encodes legal ideas as associated words. It supports latent data discovery, data mining, and text mining, with applications in political science, software engineering, medical science, and linguistic science. Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) is a popular method, alongside other LDA-based models; topic-modeling tools and datasets support this work. Topic modeling is applied to a corpus of 591 national constitutions.

Constitutional analysis examines cultural inheritance and cultural innovation. A diffusion network represents borrowing relationships among constitutions, including borrowing traced to the US Constitution of 1789. Bounded preferential attachment models constitutional offspring and inheritance distributions. A constitution-making network reveals influential and highly innovative constitutions and displays systematic variation in constitutional lifespan and temporal influence.

The second cluster addresses XML-based warehousing and decision support. An XML data warehouse stores complex data from the web, uses dimensional modeling, and supports data mining and OLAP. Complex data is integrated into an ODS, which represents it as XML documents. XML-OLAP (XOLAP) analyzes XML data through XOLAP operators expressed in an XML algebra. A complex data warehousing methodology addresses complex data and exploits XML as a pivot language.

9bd7ce1c9f643e1ee4d9b81c24aa3e7cced86460.text:
## Learning, Graph Analysis, and Trustworthy Prediction

This community spans machine learning for text, social media, biomedical data, mobility, and network analysis. Clickbait detection and personalized blocking use linguistic, neighborhood, image, and location-based features; reported accuracy reaches 93% for detection and 89% for blocking. Related social-media tasks include spam, radical-content, bot, political-slant, gender, geolocation, and follower-count prediction, with SVM, LDA-incorporated SVM, k-nearest neighbors, and supervised models achieving strong results.

BERT provides contextualized word representations through bidirectional Transformers and supports non-factoid question answering, passage re-ranking, ad hoc ranking, and biomedical entity normalization. BioBERT and ClinicalBERT extend this biomedical classification direction.

Graph-oriented work addresses network alignment, citation-based taxonomy construction, community detection, triangle counting, and influence identification. REGAL outperforms existing alignment methods by 20–30% on average, while direct citation yields a more accurate taxonomy representation than co-citation or bibliographic coupling. TribeFlow and SIDD are associated with improved accuracy in network-related tasks.

Other themes include trajectory dissimilarity and human-mobility modeling, risk analysis and privacy-aware anonymization, fair-user and fraud identification through FairJudge and FairPlay, and approximate query processing with Verdict, which speeds queries while preserving accuracy. Metrics include accuracy, F-score, runtime, speed, fairness, and reliability.

7a8c30ec4af9ffe9790662c9aacfb92c6f6fb733.text:
## Social Media for Event Discovery and News Photo Quality

This community focuses on analyzing social media and multimedia content for real-world event understanding and news-media selection.

An event detection system identifies events represented by sets of social media items, including previously unknown events in archived collections and live streams. Detected events can be automatically summarized. Event-based media retrieval finds media associated with a target event, while event summarization selects relevant, appealing, and representative multimedia content and uses retrieved event-relevant material for concise representations. YouTube is a host and distributor of user-generated social media content.

For news use, the news photo quality framework processes social-media images and supports news photo quality ranking and filtering. It combines a ranking algorithm with a visual spam detection module that filters low-quality media. The ranking algorithm is tuned to rank professional media highly and leverages social features, aesthetic features, and deep-learning semantic features. The framework achieves a retrieval MAP of 64.5% and classification precision of 70%.

033a0e9eb4a048f2f208d651d9ad3fa7cdc7188f.text:
### Social Media Dynamics, Information Integrity, and Political Communication

This community centers on **Twitter** as a social-media and microblogging platform, with connections to Reddit, 4chan, Instagram, Flickr, Sina Weibo/Weibo, and online forums. Twitter supplies tweets, social-media data, user timelines, graph structures, geotagged posts, and election datasets for computational social science.

Major topics include **misinformation, fake news, disinformation, rumors, hate speech, conspiracy theories, and political polarization**. Research examines Russian trolls, social bots, bot accounts, purchased followers, influence campaigns, and the spread of alternative or mainstream news. Political communication includes Hillary Clinton, Donald Trump, Bernie Sanders, the 2016 U.S. presidential election, and the 2018 midterms.

Key tasks and methods include sentiment and stance detection, fake-news and rumor detection, fact checking, bot detection, event detection, location prediction, election-outcome prediction, news-popularity prediction, and crisis response. Analytical approaches include Naive Bayes, classifiers, predictive models, weak supervision, user clustering, unsupervised tri-clustering, Hawkes processes, Bayesian retweet models, diffusion and dynamical activity models, and deep collaborative embeddings.

Retweets, hashtags, user engagement, influence, virality, network features, and content features connect platform activity to news propagation, trending topics, persuasion, and real-world events. Systems such as Hoaxy, Truthy, EMBERS, TwitterTrails, TruTop, Sportsense, and InfluenceTracker support monitoring and analysis.

38202bb0b2494cdf56a1ae69bbd148ed9491de48.text:
## Graph Streams, Triangle Counting, and Latent Network Learning

This community connects streaming graph analytics, incremental maintenance, and graph representation learning.

**Cocos** is a distributed streaming algorithm that processes a graph stream in one pass, estimating both global triangle counts and triangles incident to each node. It produces unbiased estimates, reduces estimation error and processing time versus baselines, and supports anomaly detection through triangle counting.

The **space-time tradeoff approach** maintains triangle counts under single-tuple updates, achieving a space-time product quadratic in input database size and update times as low as the square root of database size. Classical and factorized incremental view maintenance are recovered as special cases, although both require linear-time update maintenance. Its lowest update time is worst-case optimal conditioned on the online matrix-vector multiplication conjecture. The approach also recovers worst-case optimal complexity for non-incremental triangle counting.

**Multi-LENS** is a latent network summarization framework using relational aggregators, relational functions, and low-rank approximations of feature matrices. Its summaries support event detection and anomaly detection, and it derives node embeddings for graph representation learning.

**FI-GRL** is a fast inductive graph representation learning framework using singular value decomposition, random projection, and folding in to represent unseen nodes; it is evaluated for structural hole detection. Related text processing applies SVD and k-means to term-frequency vectors for event detection.

b4b8e20046f87c80081924367f881007a06ffca9.text:
## Graph Mining, Anomaly Detection, and Urban Network Intelligence

This community links scalable graph mining, anomaly detection, representation learning, interactive systems, and urban analytics.

**EagleMine** analyzes node characteristics in large graphs, mining micro-clusters with a water-level tree across resolutions. It summarizes selected clusters using truncated Gaussian distributions, detects overlapping elliptical clusters, and applies statistical hypothesis testing. Its anomaly-detection use cases identify anomalous nodes, outlier groups, users, and bots in Microblog data, with suspiciousness scores.

**ACE** supports unsupervised anomaly detection by compressing information into count arrays and using cache lookups. On KDD-Cup99, it is compared with ELKI, achieving up to a 60× speedup while using under 4 MB of memory.

For graph representation and classification, **Supervised Q Walk** applies Q-learning to generate random walks and is evaluated for single-label and multi-label, multi-class node classification against random-walk embedding learners. The **K-hops Neighborhood Confidence Values Learner** learns confidence values for unlabeled nodes without first learning node embeddings.

Other work models interactive systems, including search engines, by learning group-specific reward functions from user interaction traces, aided by confidence values and evaluated with online metrics. Finally, Twitter data supports event detection, dynamic neighborhood signatures, functional-zone analysis, socioeconomic estimation, and urban policy decision support, while social network distance supports anomaly detection and opinion prediction.

a849efdb02db7e2681866a50b86b07d21697e315.text:
## Social Media as a Sensor for Events, Trends, and Influence

This community centers on Twitter as a large-scale social microblogging and sensing platform, compared with Sina Weibo and connected to Flickr information diffusion. Key topics include real-time and multiscale event detection, event recognition and summarization, trending topics, hashtag life cycles, social sensing, crisis response, and situational awareness. Twitter datasets cover elections—including the 2016 U.S. presidential election—Arabic tweets, movie reviews, Higgs boson messages, and randomly sampled status streams.

Methods include Naive Bayes, convolutional neural networks, DeepWalk, Walklets, distributional semantic models, local variation, graph-based storyline generation, abstractive summarization, Bayesian retweet models, and trend lifecycle analysis. These support tweet classification, popularity and entity-popularity prediction, hashtag forecasting, early high-impact event prediction, related-query suggestion, and mood variation analysis.

The community also studies network structure and interaction through retweets, replies, followers, attention diffusion, social capital, and inequality. Systems such as TrendTop, Sportsense, InfluenceTracker, Australian Crisis Tracker, Pinboard Recommendation System, and BotOrNot operationalize these analyses. A major related theme is platform manipulation: social bots, spambots, fake or purchased followers, political bots, social-botnet infiltration, and information verification. Twitter data is therefore used both to understand real-world events and to assess influence, credibility, and collective behavior.

c9a2e216eb039786e0f5d8de3b25de9f1f70e5ac.text:
## Twitter-Centered Social Media Research

This community centers on Twitter as a social-microblogging system and data source for social media analytics, public opinion, politics, and real-world events. Key applications include event detection and recognition, real-time and multiscale detection, event summarization, rumor and fake-news detection, information verification, crisis response, disaster response, and situational awareness. Hashtags, trending topics, emerging topics, retweets, replies, followers, and hashtag spike trains support trend lifecycle analysis, popularity prediction, mood variation analysis, and social sensing.

Research also examines political communication, including Hillary Clinton, Donald Trump, Bernie Sanders, the 2016 U.S. presidential election, political campaigns, journalists, and public opinion. Bot detection, spam detection, fake followers, social botnets, political bots, and countermeasures address manipulation and misinformation.

Methods include convolutional neural networks, naïve Bayes and other machine-learning classifiers, predictive and activity-prediction models, feature selection, weak supervision, DeepWalk, Walklets, network motifs, unsupervised tri-clustering, Bayesian retweet models, negative sampling, greedy heuristics, distributional semantic models, and graph-based storyline generation. Twitter datasets include Arabic tweets, election data, geo-tagged posts, interaction graphs, and sampled status streams. Related systems include Sina Weibo, Flickr, Pinterest, Myspace, Truetop, BotOrNot, InfluenceTracker, Sportsense, DINFRA, Defender, and the Australian Crisis Tracker.

938883bc15e96eb94caac1f44edbc24686e70d4b.text:
## Community Report: Social Analysis, Recommendation, Graph Generation, and Model Reduction

This community spans four main areas: political and bot analysis, recommendation, graph generation, and epidemic-model reduction.

Political studies use Facebook photographs, image features, and content analysis to predict US senators’ party affiliation and infer political ideology. A similarity network built from privacy-preserving comparisons of senators’ Twitter histories supports party classification. Arabic bot detection uses regression models, while supervised classifiers identify credulous users; English bot-detection tools perform less effectively on Arabic bots, whose behavior includes religious hatred and sectarian rhetoric. The Team QCRI-MIT system addresses SemEval 2019 Task 4 hyperpartisan-news detection using logistic regression, engineered features, bag-of-words representations, readability, and propaganda-analysis features.

Recommendation research evaluates User-kNN, Item-kNN, and BPR-MF on MovieLens and Amazon Movies, using grid search, cross-validation, nDCG, accuracy, novelty, and catalog coverage. A hybrid deep-learning approach performs session-based news recommendation using popularity, recency, and context awareness under temporal evaluation.

Graph-generation systems Multi-MotifGAN and NetGAN are tested on Facebook, Cora, and CiteSeer; Multi-MotifGAN generalizes NetGAN and better reflects motif statistics. An autoencoder-pretrained GCN improves baseline accuracy on citation datasets.

Finally, lumping and counting abstraction reduce epidemic-model state spaces through node partitioning, yielding coarse-grained Markov population models that support approximation techniques.

f5fb6bb190d115d9cd5e3eb0468ce27eae94ea05.text:
## Community Report: Clinical Similarity, Threat Intelligence, and Automated-Tweet Detection

This community connects three application areas: clinical-text understanding, malicious IP identification, and detection of autogenerated tweets.

In the medical domain, **MedSTS** is a Mayo Clinic clinical-corpus resource for **semantic textual similarity (STS)**. Its **MedSTS_ann** subset contains expert-annotated sentence pairs with similarity scores from 0 to 5, and was used to test four STS systems. Clinical STS supports **redundant information detection**, which can reduce cognitive burden and improve clinical decision-making. Natural language processing extracts and consolidates information from clinical text.

For security intelligence, **malicious IP address identification** analyzes approximately 600,000 posts collected from three security forums using a data collection tool. It combines textual information from related posts with latent behavioral features derived through matrix decomposition of user behavior. The approach achieves high classification accuracy and finds up to three times more potentially malicious IP addresses than the VirusTotal blacklist, while requiring only limited keywords rather than sophisticated NLP.

For social-media analysis, **on-the-fly AGT detection** classifies newly downloaded tweets in a simulated Twitter stream. It first applies a text-metadata classifier, then uses a timeline-aware classifier when user history is available. The method detects autogenerated tweets—potentially produced by bots—with reported accuracy of about 98%, evaluated using subject-wise cross-validation.

e73e6accbedd64b0ba45440b46c115ef01f52132.text:
## Semantic Representations, Search, and Scholarly Text Mining

This community centers on representing and analyzing language, documents, queries, and scholarly or biomedical information. Word embeddings—including Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText, and skip-gram—learn low-dimensional semantic representations from sources such as PubMed, EHRs, health-care social media, Google News, and technology-specific corpora. These representations support semantic similarity, term relatedness, contextual preferences, venue representations, and downstream biomedical NLP tasks. Weighted embedding aggregation and centroids construct text representations and support similarity evaluation.

TechNet is a large-scale technology semantic network mined from the U.S. patent database. It establishes semantic relationships between terms and supports relevance assessment, technology search, engineering knowledge discovery, design, innovation, and technical summarization.

Search-focused work models queries and search sessions, computes query–document relevance scores and axiom-related features, predicts important words and next queries, and evaluates query performance. Bag-of-words and modified TF-IDF provide traditional document representations.

The community also covers scholarly and biomedical extraction, including bibliographic reference parsing, protein–protein interaction extraction, clinical named-entity recognition, figure extraction, and personal knowledge-graph population. Deep neural networks, hierarchical attention, BiLSTM-CRF, graph convolution, and distant supervision provide task-specific methods, commonly evaluated with F1 score. Tweet classification applies embeddings and neural models to crisis, health, misinformation, and automated-tweet detection.

d2f601deb7a6c6046b046d60e4ba788d551806fd.text:
## Community Report: Graph-Based Retrieval, Recommendation, and Cognition

This community centers on information retrieval, semantic search, recommendation, and graph representation. Information-retrieval research covers ranking functions, bag-of-words approaches, language-modelling smoothing, typed similarity queries executed by random walks, personalized retrieval, search sessions, and multidimensional relevance judgments. Search data and query logs capture searcher and system behavior, while session-level evaluation assesses personalized retrieval.

Knowledge graphs support electronic textbook platforms, ontology-based modeling, information search, and organization. Continuous knowledge-graph representations—including Gaussian, holographic, and complex embeddings—support entity mention disambiguation, relation inference, and deep question answering. Transitive relations are modeled with order embeddings and assessed through dedicated evaluation protocols.

Graph learning includes Walk-Steered Convolution (WSC), which adapts convolutional neural networks to graphs using Gaussian-encoded random-walk fields. Multi-scale walk fields, graph coarsening, dynamical clustering, and high-level graph semantics extend this approach.

Other applications include cognate detection and prediction through positional or sequential segmentation, smoothing, and graphical error modeling; and e-commerce search, where a simplified ontology framework extracts product classes and query understanding identifies products and brands.

Explainable recommendation spans social and POI recommendation, with user-, item-, model-based, and post-model explanations evaluated through user studies. Finally, mathematical psychology and quantum cognition address order, context effects, and potentially irrational relevance judgments in sequential decision-making.

449e14b5b597e1c26e071306ad1400ab5dce2bb2.text:
## Neural Models for Fielded Ad Hoc Retrieval

This community focuses on neural information retrieval for ad hoc retrieval, evaluated largely on TREC Web Track data. Traditional search engines use term-based approaches that represent queries and documents as bags of words and compute relevance scores from matching terms. BM25F extends this paradigm by exploiting document fields.

PACRR is a neural IR model that captures relevance-matching signals and produces an ultimate relevance score. Co-PACRR extends PACRR with context-aware modeling of local context around matches, using cascade k-max pooling, a shuffling combination layer, and a disambiguation component. It is designed for ad hoc retrieval and its component interactions are examined through ablation analysis.

Field-aware neural ranking consumes document titles, bodies, and incoming anchor text, jointly scoring the document. Masking handles missing field instances, while field-level dropout reduces reliance on any single field. Such neural rankers outperform a learning-to-rank baseline based on hand-crafted features.

DE-PACRR investigates PACRR’s inner workings through layer visualization, intermediate outputs, and weights, advancing model interpretability. DRMM is another neural IR model that captures relevance signals. Latent vector space models and query formulation methods address the vocabulary gap between queries and documents, including differences in complex textual structure.

8660fd93d450e4e67e64bf4f5e70103a06667de5.text:
## Adaptive Detection, Information Extraction, and Representation Learning

This community links methods for detecting events, extracting knowledge, retrieval, and classifying social or textual data. Adaptive event detection uses social media streams as reports from “social sensors,” with concept-drift adaptation overcoming static approaches. The adaptive event detection application demonstrates this through a landslide detector, achieving 0.988 event-detection accuracy versus 0.762 for static approaches, while addressing both weak- and large-signal events.

Information extraction from technical data sheets, including spacecraft-development materials, is enhanced by ontology enrichment. Contron continuously enriches ontologies using Wikidata and WordNet, significantly increasing extracted information.

Retrieval methods combine BM25 or bag-of-words representations for initial rankings with query expansion, pseudo-relevance feedback, WordNet definitions, and document relevance classifiers trained with pseudo-labels for reranking. 

Text classification compares bag-of-words and word embeddings—including Word2Vec, GloVe, and FastText—for user aggression detection; FastText achieves the best weighted F1 among embeddings, while ULMFiT and ELMo are fine-tuned classifiers. FastText tweet vectors can also be clustered with k-means for topic discovery.

Other themes include ELMo-Wikidata fine-grained entity recognition, evaluated on WikiGold’s 112 entity types, and weak/strong balance measures for sign prediction in real-world signed networks.

3c75388b3ad1d9df99be25774cb7fe5fef9f2c8f.text:
## Semantic Retrieval, Representation, and Context-Aware Systems

This community centers on information retrieval, semantic representation, and context-aware prediction across biomedical, scholarly, social-media, and web-service domains.

Word embeddings are a central connective method: trained from PubMed, Google News, health-care social media, or EHR data, they model term relatedness and semantic similarity, support biomedical NLP, sentiment and controversy detection, and represent venues, users’ contextual preferences, and technologies. Weighted word-embedding aggregation constructs text representations, while the Embedded Topic Model uses embeddings to parameterize topic distributions.

Retrieval research includes query–document relevance scoring, textual information retrieval, keyword-based search, and SetRank. SetRank learns permutation-invariant rankings over document or entity sets using stacked multi-head self-attention, modeling inter-entity relationships and entity types; it is evaluated on TREC Genomics and Semantic Scholar query logs and outperforms traditional learning-to-rank and neural IR baselines.

Contextual information supports genre prediction, recommender systems, Twitter sentiment classification, and behavior modeling, with quality of service varying across users, time, and locations. Semantic similarity connects queries, documents, scholarly graphs, and peer-review outcomes.

Web-service research represents, discovers, recommends, composes, and manages services, with quality of service and symbolic reputation guiding selection. TechNet provides a large technology semantic network mined from U.S. patents.

f30146b03b73f73b993ae63243c81c87b47e77fc.text:
## Community Report: Data Quality, Scientific Linked Data, and Personalized Retweet Prediction

This community centers on data quality, truth discovery, scientific datasets, and personalized social-media prediction.

**Holoclean** is a holistic data-repairing framework that unifies qualitative and quantitative repairing. It relies on integrity constraints, external data sources, and statistical properties, and uses probabilistic inference to automatically generate probabilistic programs. It achieves approximately 90% average precision, above 76% recall, and more than twice the average F1 of state-of-the-art methods.

A related **hybrid** truth-discovery method jointly determines the number and values of truths, using conflicting observations to reject incorrect values and allowing multiple valid truths. Hybrid and conservative approaches combine with sampling for quality control and interactive visualization, although sampling introduces sampling error. Data cubes accelerate visualization queries.

**Nanopublications** represent Linked Data granularly with provenance, metadata, and reliable identifiers. Nanopublication datasets support subsets, evolving version histories, and incremental updates that reduce update overhead. They are applied to scientific datasets and citation networks.

**Wikim** performs scientific abstract wikification using metapaths, mention extraction, and entity linking, evaluated on the ACL Anthology Network. TF-IDF supports mention extraction.

Finally, a personalized global classifier, trained with logistic regression on 130,000 tweets from 122 journalists, powers retweet prediction. It uses tweet content, novelty, text similarity, past interactions, network influence, and user-specific features, achieving approximately 0.9 F1.

e8e72ceacc5ac7281a962c23c2efcf25c368f86d.text:
## Summarization, Classification, and Socially Enriched Retrieval

This community centers on automatic text summarization, classification, and resource discovery. Extractive summarization selects sentences, tweets, or other textual units using sentence ranking, sentence position, statistical features, TF-IDF, LexRank, and maximal marginal relevance. Abstractive methods instead fuse source content, while hybrid and joint extractive-compressive models seek more concise summaries. Generic summarization extends to music and speech; LexRank creates music summaries, supported by music descriptors, genre tags, and music information retrieval.

ROUGE is the principal automatic summarization metric, measuring n-gram overlap with human summaries; ROUGE 2.0 updates these measures, although synonymy and topic coverage remain limitations. Fairness is also addressed because summaries may represent groups differently from their input distributions.

Classification applications include resource, rumor, abusive-message, music-genre, and document classification. Term weighting, TF-IDF, LSA, SMTM, LexRank, hybrid screening, and automated classifiers are evaluated through classification accuracy or performance. Systems such as the rumor classification model and automated document classification system report improvements over baselines.

Social tags support resource classification, document search, navigation, retrieval, and alternative browsing, complementing expert and taxonomic categorization. Quantization methods—including vector and product quantization—address compressed indexes, quantization error, and norm error.

7a59b7439fd2c8dea2de3d33bf75428818233634.text:
## Community Report: Graph-Based NLP, Retrieval, and Prediction Systems

This community spans linguistic analysis, information retrieval, data quality, and query optimization.

**SW-IDF** performs unsupervised video tag extraction from time-synchronized comments. It represents comments as a semantic association graph, using dialogue-based and topic-center clustering, graph iteration for comment weighting, and semantic weight combined with IDF. It is evaluated with F1 and MAP.

For **bipolar disorder recognition**, Twitter posts are analyzed using morpheme collocations, syntactic patterns, gender-enriched features, LIWC, TF-IDF, and ELMo; F1 scores exceed 91%. Syntactic patterns are constructed from syntax and word usage and can receive attention through a pattern-attention mechanism.

**Holodetect** is an error-detection framework using few-shot learning and data augmentation. It learns augmentation policies from noisy datasets and clean records, and is evaluated on diverse error datasets using F1, average precision, and average recall.

**Conna** addresses real-time name disambiguation on AMiner through jointly trained, intertwined matching and decision components.

For **ad hoc document ranking**, CEDR combines contextualized representations and BERT’s classification vector with neural ranking architectures, outperforming ranking baselines. BERT and ELMo provide contextual representations, while semantic similarity and table embeddings extend retrieval models for table retrieval, row population, and column population.

Finally, query planning and optimizers use execution-plan costs, feature sets, linear, nonlinear, or nearest-neighbor models to predict query execution time for scheduling and service-level agreements.

139ed393c4ac7c794dda488eecde0122285ebcee.text:
## Summarization, Fair Retrieval, and Efficient Search

This community centers on automatic text summarization, especially extractive, abstractive, and hybrid approaches. Extractive systems select and rank sentences or other textual units using TF-IDF, sentence position, centrality-based relevance, and statistical features. The joint extractive compressive summarization model extends extraction by compressing selected sentences and uses summary-state representations; it reports state-of-the-art results on CNN/DailyMail and Newsroom. Abstractive systems, including dual-attention sequence-to-sequence frameworks and word-graph approaches, generate new text but face faithfulness and fabricated-fact concerns.

Evaluation relies heavily on ROUGE and ROUGE 2.0, alongside faithfulness, summary quality, content coverage, and temporal evaluation. Systems such as MEAD, Opinosis, FRESA, and Microsoft’s summarization system provide comparison points. Applications include microblogs, user-generated content, online news, product descriptions, breaking-news tracking, and evolving stories.

Fairness is a parallel concern: FairSumm and fairness-preserving summarization address unequal representation of socially salient groups and sources. Information retrieval research covers TF-IDF, STF-IDF, relevance models, ranked conjunctive/disjunctive queries, unseen-query retrieval, and compressed indexes. Vector, product, additive, optimized-product, and residual quantization support maximum-inner-product search, with norm and quantization error as evaluation concerns. Related applications include term extraction, ontology development, stock-trend prediction, trading systems, and sequential pattern mining.

d6bcb8a0ff8716dd95a361f700ca7f669df5a514.text:
## Graph-Based Learning, Retrieval, and Robust Prediction

This community connects scalable graph analysis with reliable machine-learning applications. **GSCARF** performs fine-grained clustering by dynamically pruning unnecessary nodes and edges, addressing scalability challenges in massive graphs. Its modularity-clustering basis is affected by the resolution-limit problem, which can hinder reproduction of ground-truth clusters.

For trajectory data, **TrajEDI** provides calibration-aware pairwise dissimilarity. Trajectory dissimilarity supports similarity, diversity, constrained-selection, and nearest-neighbor operations; parameter tuning exposes speed–accuracy trade-offs.

Several systems emphasize uncertainty and selective prediction. A **risk control framework** combines a qualification model—using the probe idea to estimate predictive uncertainty—with a decision model for selective Web QA outputs. It is evaluated on real-world Web QA and academic MRC collections using risk-related metrics rather than traditional EM or F1.

Applications include early fake-news detection, where a proposed early-labeling model uses class-specific text representations, public user profiles, news diffusion speed, and a stopping rule. Tweet spam classification compares neural networks, correlational neural networks, kernel SVM, and k-nearest neighbors; correlated feature selection reduces training time.

Other work covers one-shot invoice document capture, minimizing manual entry; family-tree name suggestion using graphs and ordering functions; and active learning methods that mitigate annotation errors and bias. Evaluation includes accuracy, F1, earliness, reconstruction loss, and running time.

d46153aa1a4e4624bdaca56ef5afb632bb8e658b.text:
## Graph Algorithms, Social Analytics, and Web-Service Systems

This community spans graph optimization, social-network analysis, machine learning, and service-oriented computing. A major theme is computational complexity: minmax server placement, team formation, network-delay minimization, minimum Wiener connectors, task batching, closest truss communities, and contamination clearing are NP-hard; several consistent-tree and adoption decision problems are NP-complete.

Graph methods address coloring, clustering, truss identification, location estimation, and influence. Paired threshold graphs are characterized by vertex-weight inequalities and forbidden induced subgraphs, with a polynomial-time recognition algorithm. Approximation, greedy, minmax, constant-factor, and 3-approximation algorithms target scalable solutions, evaluated using accuracy, efficiency, diameter, density, regret, and related metrics.

Web-service research represents, discovers, recommends, composes, and manages services, including reputation-based organization and service communities. These systems seek improved matchmaking and composition accuracy and efficiency.

Social and textual analytics include clickbait blocking and detection, sentiment and political-slant inference, spam and gender classification, age inference, tweet-origin and home-location estimation, and soccer prediction. Methods include multimodal features, linguistic and neighborhood information, Gaussian mixtures, probabilistic inference, and human–machine hybrids.

Additional systems cover distributed stream processing, online bagging and prequential evaluation, column-oriented storage, browser extensions, and recommender systems. Collaboration, communication, road, Stack Overflow, social-media, and international research datasets support these applications.

e62e3ce33bc6dafa825c79569f4aa9cfe88f5540.text:
## Community Report: Graph Analytics, Relational Learning, and Fair Retrieval

This community spans scalable graph analytics, relational learning, cross-modal retrieval, and marketplace fairness.

For graph analytics, the edge sampling framework supports big-graph analysis and evolving graphs. Its Edge Sample and Discard (ESD) algorithm uses neighborhood information to estimate triangle counts, produces unbiased estimates, and updates them after edge additions or deletions. It is evaluated on real graphs and Barabási–Albert graphs, including accuracy, complexity, and running time. TPA accelerates approximate random walk with restart (RWR) on large and billion-scale graphs using neighbor approximation near the seed and stranger approximation for distant nodes; PageRank supports distant-node estimation.

For relational learning, Datalog represents learned relation definitions from relational databases. Bottom-up and push-based evaluation immediately propagates derived tuples, while Datalog-to-C++ translation is compared with DLV, XSB, and YAP. AutoMode uses database schemas and content to induce language bias with slight runtime overhead.

Cross-modal hashing supports similarity search through compact binary codes. Discrete methods generally improve accuracy over relaxation-based methods; the discrete latent-factor model achieves high accuracy with comparable training time.

FairJudge iteratively estimates user fairness, rating reliability, and product goodness, addresses cold start, and achieved 80% accuracy in fraud identification. It was deployed at Flipkart to report suspected fraudulent users.

bc19600632b65fb4d76810439f4cdebff5c8e04a.text:
## Graph, Social, and Web Intelligence Methods

This community covers methods for improving accuracy and efficiency across graph analytics, social-media analysis, web services, and machine learning.

Graph-oriented work addresses NP-hard and NP-complete optimization problems, graph coloring, community search, closest truss communities, minimum Wiener connectors, and multi-skill or capacitated team formation. Approximation algorithms—including constant-factor, 3-approximation, greedy, minmax, triangle-based coloring, and unified coloring frameworks—are evaluated for solution quality and team-finding accuracy. K-truss identification and maintenance and influential-neighbor algorithms support dense-subgraph analysis.

Social-media research uses Facebook posts, tweets, Stack Overflow, collaboration networks, and real social networks for clickbait detection, sentiment analysis, political slant and gender classification, spam detection, location inference, home-location estimation, and age inference. Content-based, network-based, multimodal, Gaussian-mixture, and graph-based methods are used; clickbait detection reaches 93% accuracy, while personalized clickbait blocking reaches 89%.

Web-service research concerns representation, discovery, recommendation, composition, and matchmaking, supported by web-service datasets and systems. Distributed stream processing, online bagging, prequential evaluation, task batching, column-oriented datastores, and ad-hoc query processing target scalable computation. Privacy and advertising topics include noise allocation, social sensor placement, budgeted and unconstrained social advertising, and quantitative invulnerability assessment.

c4e118a1b221000f5252ea2546157152f6a88b40.text:
**Research Methods for Retrieval, Risk, Dialogue, and Software Migration**

This community spans information retrieval, prediction, and applied decision-support systems. For radical content detection, contextual text and psychological properties models analyze propaganda material using textual, psychological, and behavioral signals; vector embeddings improve on TF-IDF baselines for online-radicalization detection.

SEntNet performs dialogue response selection in task-oriented dialogue systems using source-specific memories of user utterances, system responses, and knowledge-base information. It achieves 91.0% accuracy on Dialog bAbI and 41.2% on DSTC2, outperforming source-unaware recurrent entity networks. Unsupervised context retrieval uses established entities and their contexts, including for out-of-knowledge-base and long-tail entities.

Risk analysis frameworks generate interpretable risk features and train learnable risk models to rank mislabeled entity pairs, evaluated on real data. Feature bit vectors and bitwise hashing replace floating-point representations to accelerate lexical comparison, personalized search, and behavior-based prediction.

Quantum theory models incompatible, interfering relevance dimensions, cognitive state, and decision-making under uncertainty, informing information-retrieval systems. NEMF extends matrix factorisation by optimizing novelty and explainability; user studies assess cognitive state and user-style explanations.

Linkflows formally represents peer-review workflows and comments, while RApIM recommends API mappings for third-party library migration using signatures and documentation, evaluated across eight Java-library migrations.

bb48cc6366a1bacb4f1a303a1fbf3821027b7a6f.text:
## Temporal Networks, Trust Recommendation, and Personal Knowledge Graphs

This community covers three themes.

**Temporal graph analysis:** Independent Temporal Motif items (ITeMs) are edge-disjoint temporal motifs used to summarize and compare temporal networks. Their frequencies form feature vectors that reveal salient network properties and support temporal graph similarity. Importance sampling efficiently estimates ITeM counts, and ITeMs characterize temporal graph structure and evolution. Evaluations use synthetic and real temporal networks, with higher accuracy than other motif-frequency approaches.

**Trust-based recommendation:** Trust networks define user trust compositionally and can integrate social links, while trust-based recommender systems use these networks and trust information to address the cold-start problem. The Multi-faceted Trust Model incorporates additional trust evidence, including public anonymous feedback from user profiles. LOCABAL+ extends the LOCABAL trust-based recommender system using this model, and evaluations on two public item-review datasets show improved accuracy over state-of-the-art systems and Collaborative Filtering. Privacy concerns arise because social-relation data may be perceived as a violation.

**Personal knowledge graphs:** Personal knowledge graph population constructs graphs containing people, personal data, and relationships. Slot filling increases the diversity of populated graphs, and representative set sampling uses the resulting data for downstream applications. However, the task presents data protection, privacy, and fairness challenges, and achieves relatively low overall F1 performance.

38097df37c35f7f85d45e7e301d39ee4f6c2232b.text:
## Data Quality, Retrieval, and Knowledge-Graph Methods

This community spans privacy-preserving data analysis, dataset assessment, information extraction, media coverage, multimodal retrieval, and tourism knowledge graphs.

HDMM is a differentially private method for answering predicate-counting queries over sensitive and high-dimensional databases. It represents query workloads implicitly, optimizes workload answering, and reduces error; statistical agencies and medical institutions use such queries for summary tabulations.

Dataset nutrition labels support data analysis and AI model development by presenting dataset characteristics, detecting issues, and encouraging data-quality and cleaning practices. They use probabilistic and statistical-modeling backends, with a prototype demonstrated on the ProPublica Dollars for Docs dataset. Ground-truth comparison is noted as a limitation.

Technology terminology extraction finds terms in web text, identifies technology-bearing sentences, and classifies terms into semantic labels and AI domains. Its two-stage cascading model combines sentence classification with technology keyword extraction. SWDE uses Doc2Vec and subword embeddings for headline and article representation and supports clickbait detection.

For media analysis, latent representations model selection bias and guide source selection toward diverse, egalitarian, actively covered news. Personalized approaches improve coverage prediction, evaluated on GDELT.

A dual-path neural network combines image modeling and text representations for cross-modal retrieval, using pairwise similarity loss to map modalities into a common semantic space.

The Tyrolean tourism knowledge graph maps Schema.org sources, stores annotated content in a graph database, and supports tourism applications and analysis.

c873c8c8332d1be13d687f461411c038af72c8b7.text:
## Taxonomies, Similarity, and Scalable Data Analysis

This community connects scientific knowledge organization, document similarity, scalable querying, geolocation, and app fraud detection.

For scientific and technical knowledge, topic-level taxonomies are built by clustering documents using direct citation, bibliographic coupling, or co-citation. Direct citation concentrates references more effectively and provides a more accurate taxonomy representation; discipline-level taxonomies based on journal schemas are comparatively inaccurate. Gold standards and reference concentration evaluate taxonomy accuracy.

Word Mover’s Distance (WMD) computes document similarity but has cubic time complexity. Relaxed WMD (RWMD) reduces this to quadratic complexity, while LC-RWMD provides a low-complexity implementation with average linear time on large document sets, GPU mapping, GPU-cluster distribution, and orders-of-magnitude performance improvements.

OLA-RAW performs parallel online aggregation directly over raw data through in-situ processing. Its query-driven bi-level sampling, resource-aware sampling, and memory-resident sample synopsis reduce execution time while supporting SQL querying, data exploration, and continuously estimated results.

Tweet geolocation predicts locations from single tweets, achieving 52.8% city-level and 92.1% country-level accuracy. Finally, FairPlay uses PCF, combining linguistic and behavioral signals to detect malware and search-rank-fraud apps, including fraudulent apps evading Google Bouncer, with over 95% classification accuracy.

0b737d5c6e197590984901a98407f4098e5244bf.text:
## Graph Representation, Private Estimation, and Social Research

This community spans graph analysis, privacy-preserving data streams, and computational social science.

For graph comparison and classification, **NetLSD** produces compact graph signatures related to the Laplacian spectrum, heat kernel, and wave kernel, offering improved expressiveness and computational efficiency. **SGR** performs self-supervised graph representation learning grounded in spectral graph analysis, producing vector representations sensitive to both global and local features and evaluated on large graph collections. These representations support network-type classification, including identifying users from app-switching behavior; temporal motifs and temporal structure extend feature representation to temporal networks. Graph kernels and other representation-based methods provide established comparison approaches.

For streaming data, **Count-Min Sketch** estimates item frequencies in massive streams using sub-linear space and multiple hash functions. Composite hashing and **Mod Sketch** address modular item keys, aiming to improve accuracy and estimation efficiency.

Privacy research focuses on range queries, quantiles, and discrete distribution estimation under local differential privacy and untrusted aggregation. Hierarchical histograms and Haar wavelets provide variance-based accuracy guarantees, while trusted aggregation is a prior setting.

Finally, inferred genealogical networks, built from historical records, enable longitudinal analysis of mating patterns, assortative mating, genetics, digital demography, and computational social science. Editorial and peer-review management uses an efficiency measurement model to assess journal-editing resources.

570d218223e64c92b7ae8bf6634c8a85d52cae8b.text:
## Community Report: Learning, Search, and Prediction from Structured Data

This community covers database learning, scientific table retrieval, company profiling, micro-data estimation, and predictive analysis.

**Verdict**, built on Spark SQL, applies Database Learning to approximate query processing. It learns from past query answers to improve its understanding of the underlying data distribution, producing increasingly faster response times while maintaining the accuracy of existing AQP systems. Maximum entropy supports answer generation, and real-world query traces provide experimental evaluation.

**Scientific table search** uses keyword queries, expanded by target quantity types, to retrieve scientific tables. A probabilistic framework combines structural and semantic information, including table components; TableArXiv supplies queries and relevance judgments. Retrieval is evaluated by accuracy.

**CPCTR** profiles companies from employee perspectives by collaboratively modeling textual employee reviews, salaries, and numerical ratings, learning latent structural patterns. These patterns support opinion analysis and salary prediction, complementing traditional finance reports and SEC filings.

For individual micro-data estimation, locality-sensitive hashing finds support-data subsets similar to aggregated open data; conditional probability selects suitable records. Ensemble classification then classifies the selected support data.

Finally, ratings can be transformed with the discrete Fourier transform into power spectra. A coherence similarity measure derived from these spectra is less sensitive to sparsity and outperforms standard similarity measures. Semi-supervised RNN and ensemble models exploit unlabeled data and achieve reported accuracy improvements.

1613c79936c87fd128f3ebf2d3f2946c8cf41432.text:
## News Recommendation, Multi-Objective Optimization, and Need Elicitation

This community covers news recommender systems, contextual session-based recommendation, and customer-need identification.

**Chameleon** is a deep-learning meta-architecture for news recommendation that implements contextual hybrid session-based recommendation. It uses recurrent neural networks, article content for the item cold-start problem, and user context for user cold start. It models concept drift caused by changing readership interests during breaking events. Chameleon improves recommendation accuracy, novelty, and item coverage, and addresses the session-based news recommendation task. Temporal offline evaluation replays historical clicks and article publication to assess this task.

**MGDRec** applies stochastic multi-gradient descent to multi-objective optimization. Gradient normalization enables objectives with diverse scales to be combined. Its objectives include revenue and recall, while quality product proportion improves alongside accuracy.

**NeedMining** supports customer-need identification and elicitation, evaluating relevant tweets with precision and recall. Need elicitation augments the service-design tool set and provides scalable support for innovation managers.

Key metrics across the community include accuracy, precision, recall, novelty, item coverage, revenue, and quality product proportion.

9f65bef220d4d2127c62612283a240b49ba942a0.text:
## Community Report: Graph Learning, Retrieval, and Risk Detection

This community links graph-based learning with information retrieval, social-media analysis, and clinical decision support.

In retrieval, an information retrieval system models query-term dependence and evaluates TREC queries with user assessments. Term dependence can improve over a bag-of-words baseline for some queries, while search stratagems—including footnote chasing, citation, keyword, author searching, and journal runs—are associated with improved precision. SOWIport provides the SUSS 14–15 and SUSS 16–17 datasets for studying search behavior.

Graph neural networks support relational and multitask learning, including network-centrality estimation through shared vertex embeddings and multilayer-perceptron outputs. They are evaluated on random and real-world graphs, and the Unified Network is a graph neural-network model.

Other graph methods address author disambiguation using local topological similarity and two-step traversal on DBLP, and follower-count manipulation using unsupervised local neighborhoods, user similarity, and deviations between predicted and displayed counts.

Clinical systems include DMIR, which uses a deep convolutional neural network to retrieve whole-brain CT scans from a traumatic-brain-injury cohort, achieving reported validation and test scores near 1.0. Drug–drug-interaction networks, classifiers, and warning systems examine age, polypharmacy, and gender-related risk. Social-media methods use causal inference and action logs for early pathogenic-account detection and harmful-message virality. Metrics include precision, accuracy, recall, specificity, F1, MCC, and retrieval gain.

07a488ffa7903b971adaba9a998db8cf20911575.text:
### SemiGNN for Multi-View Fraud Detection

This community centers on **SemiGNN**, a semi-supervised graph neural network for **financial fraud detection**. SemiGNN uses both labeled and unlabeled data, with user attributes as input features. Unlabeled users can expand the labeled data through social relations.

The method incorporates a **hierarchical attention mechanism** that correlates information from different neighbors and across views in a **multi-view network**. Although user attributes are reported to contribute more than social relations, both provide relevant information to the model.

The community also focuses on representing **higher-order interactions**. **Hypergraphs** model interactions involving more than two nodes and represent group relations, while the **N projected graph** incrementally represents group interactions; its accumulation captures interactions up to *n*-way. In contrast, pairwise abstractions may lose higher-order information. The N projected graph therefore trades off interaction complexity against task accuracy, with higher-order interactions providing increasing benefits as tasks become more challenging.

SemiGNN achieves better accuracy than state-of-the-art methods by combining labeled and unlabeled data, user attributes, social relations, and multi-view network information.

2fa9accdabc496a1f977fd92a40489fa0b83a730.text:
### Graph Methods for Influence, Privacy, and Network Resilience

This community studies graph analysis across real-world, synthetic, random, scale-free, Twitter, mobile social, and adversarial networks. Centrality estimation includes eigenvector and degree centrality, leading-eigenvector spectral algorithms, Sorec’s direct social relation metric and influence spheres, and blind centrality ranking. These methods identify influential users, leaders, and seed nodes for counter-terrorism, covert-network analysis, misinformation prevention, opinion shifting, and network immunization.

Approximation algorithms address hiding leaders and immunization, using combinatorial trace methods; hiding leader is NP-complete under core centrality constraints and relates to densest \(k\)-subgraph. Influence estimation uses hybrid and reverse sampling, influence spheres, and the independent cascade model. Adversarial enhancement methods and AUC measure prediction performance when contagion networks or models are known.

Privacy research covers differential privacy, sum queries, continuous data release, Laplace mechanisms, and randomized perturbation. Temporal correlations, modeled with Markov chains, motivate temporal privacy leakage calculation and resistant release mechanisms. Twitter graphs concerning suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, self-harm, and bullycide are analyzed with Clauset–Newman–Moore grouping, centrality, clustering measures, and Hoaxy for misinformation. Decentralized coloring uses local conflict indices and node diversification, while community detection is evaluated on synthetic and real networks.

7340edcf1fc19d4bfa6aec9c8ce73d9e013c2aba.text:
### Community Report: Network Communities, Learning, and Applied Risk Analysis

This community centers on **community detection** as an unsupervised clustering problem in graphs and networks. It covers hierarchical and fuzzy clustering, community-count estimation with a novel prior, and signed-network detection through decoding, Hamming-distance, bit-flipping, and belief-propagation algorithms. Structural balance and Harary’s theorem connect signed-network clusterability with parity-check constraints. Selective connectors identify multiple communities through subgraphs while tolerating outliers; community detection is also evaluated on real-world datasets and remains limited in parallel and distributed computing.

A second theme is **graph representation learning**. GraphSAGE uses inductive local-neighborhood aggregation and node features to generate embeddings for unseen nodes and graphs. It is evaluated using Reddit post data and protein–protein interaction datasets, contrasting with transductive learning and concerns that node embeddings may be ill-suited for community detection.

The community also addresses **synthetic topology generation**, reproducing degree, clustering-coefficient, hop-length, k-core, and macro-level characteristics of real networks through residual degree attenuation.

Applied network science includes visual analytics for evolving loan-guarantee networks, enterprise default risk, high-default groups, motifs, and default-diffusion paths. Finally, minimum-inefficiency subgraphs and selective connectors are studied in brain, cancer, and food networks.

cf4693e553e520e0c7acbd807c95a8db1b414a32.text:
## Network Representation, Evolution, and Community Detection

This community examines complex-network analysis, network comparison, growth, and evolution, with co-authorship networks as a central application. Network analysis studies measurable network structure, while complex-network analysis supports visualization and interdisciplinary communication. Co-authorship networks illustrate temporal evolution and are used to investigate the academic response to the Chornobyl nuclear power plant accident through bibliographic databases, descriptive statistics, and distributions across scientific fields.

**Network Vector** learns distributed representations of nodes and entire networks by maximizing the predictive likelihood of random-walk paths. It captures global context, embeds networks in a low-dimensional space, and enables network comparison, role discovery, and concept analogy tasks. Network comparison uses structural similarity, derived from cosine similarity, to compare networks and identify inter-cluster edges in sparse graphs.

**Hamuhi Code** performs multi-scale hierarchical community detection, inspired by agglomerative hierarchical clustering. It checks parameterized community definitions, uses structural similarity to compare vertices and clusters, and is evaluated against baseline algorithms on real-world and synthetic benchmark networks.

The **3-Lambda Network Model** is a stochastic model based on average node behavior. Its network generator grows networks through successive interactions and produces characteristics observed in real-world networks. Temporal correlations are noted as potentially invalidating conventional network-analysis results.

5c5502754db2de7c4d0b1de044e14d323d716f4c.text:
## Reddit Communities, Social Behavior, and Community Emergence

This community centers on Reddit and online forums as environments for computational social science, collective thinking, social behavior, user experience, and bullying detection. Reddit provides large-scale activity, post, comment, posting-history, ground-truth, and community datasets, including data shared through the Internet Archive and distributed via Bittorrent. These resources support user history analysis and network analysis, although missing observations create strong risks for both approaches.

A major focus is community emergence: Reddit serves as a testbed for studying how user-created communities develop from existing communities. The community genealogy framework builds community genealogy graphs, representing parent connections and characterizing them with metrics such as number of parents and maximum parent weight. Strong parent connections are associated with future community growth. Structural and dynamic analysis extracts information from the structure and dynamics of Reddit communities, while an academic research survey maps related research directions.

Another topic is online fan communities. The NBA Reddit fan community dataset combines 1.5 million posts and 43 million comments with NBA team-performance statistics. Findings about online fan behavior provide insights for sports management. Reddit communities also support research on community growth, collective thinking, and automatic bullying identification.

731a5d08d906f83aa46b7715921a631af4818766.text:
## Information Extraction, Entity Resolution, and Evaluation

This community covers information extraction (IE), relation extraction, document spanners, and entity resolution. IE includes relation and open information extraction, systems such as information extractors and QA4IE, and applications to legal documents and dynamic legislation networks. QA4IE supports question answering and produces cross-sentence relation triples; its IE benchmark contains two million golden relation triples and uses high-quality human evaluation.

Document spanners formalize extraction over document segments. Split correctness, including black-box extractor variants and split constraints, studies whether extractors behave correctly across segments. Query planning enables parallel evaluation, while incremental evaluation limits re-evaluation to revised segments in dynamic content. Regular spanners are defined using regular expressions and relational algebra.

Entity resolution addresses dirty values through blocking schemes. Skyblocking and active learning identify preferred schemes by approximating a scheme skyline in a multidimensional scheme space, evaluated using PC and PQ, blocking quality, label efficiency, and learning efficiency. Gradual machine learning uses factor-graph inference and evidential certainty to label increasingly difficult instances with less manual labeling; it is competitive with supervised learning and outperforms unsupervised alternatives.

A Siamese convolutional cookie embedding network learns from multimodal user-event sequences for cross-device user matching, identifying cookies belonging to the same person and recovering personalization signals. Relation extraction remains challenged by noisy data, wrong labels, and limited relation types.

89fcfcc16cfe6fd0b2d6891a117a8564e403ab4d.text:
## Network Influence, Epidemic Spread, and Community Analysis

This community studies spreading processes, influential-node detection, and network structure. The SI model analyzes transient epidemic dynamics on arbitrary large networks, including malware propagation when patches are unavailable or infeasible. Closed-form approximations capture SI behavior over time, while reliability theory offers a new interpretation. SI simulations provide rankings evaluated with Kendall’s tau and compared with centrality measures.

Influencer detection uses degree centrality as a local popularity metric and eigenvector centrality as a global metric. Katz and eigenvector centrality are related, and scalable iterative methods approximate both on large networks. Their combination supports Katz–eigenvector community detection. Degree and Katz centrality together capture popularity and similarity through Geometric Potential Gain.

Influence methods include k-shell decomposition and the extended k-shell algorithm, which identifies viral spreaders and can achieve up to 36% greater viral reach with the same number of initial spreaders. These rankings support viral marketing, which seeks maximum reach under a fixed budget.

SIR models simulate epidemic spreading on real-life networks, while vaccination policies—designed with or without knowledge of infected nodes—are evaluated through numerical simulations. Finally, co-citation methodology, degree centrality, and intermediation centrality map relationships among scientific papers. Network communities contextualize viral tweets, positive sentiment, and the Brazilian presidential elections.

abd0c44b92b313dc070c5186606ba6e1585e4ff9.text:
## Community Report: Metadata, Association Mining, and User–Item Intelligence

This community centers on extracting structure from metadata, user activity, and item relationships. **Association rule mining** analyzes metadata, buying patterns, tags, and frequent sets, using support, confidence, confidence boost, and other interestingness measures. Itemset pruning, enhancement, minimal generators, closed and disjunctive closed itemsets, and post-mining or substitution-based pruning address redundancy and pattern explosion. The frequency-confidence framework and an open-source association-mining tool support rule evaluation and parameter-free mining. Resulting rules support metadata recommendation, tennis strategy analysis, and tag consistency.

Metadata is also used in description-driven design, deep regression, cover-song detection, and text similarity. Biological sample metadata is stored in BioSample and Biosamples; field clustering, standardization, and validation address problems affecting biomedical experiments and secondary dataset use.

A second major theme is recommendation and behavioral modeling. Traditional systems rely on IID assumptions for users and items, while non-IID coupling, granular association rules, information granules, continuous cold start, and a PGNN model relationships and changing behavior. Users’ clickstreams, opinions, preferential navigation, attention, and peer positions inform social and collaborative systems.

Audio research includes compressibility-based temporal descriptors, quantized audio features, and cover-song tasks. Organization, repositories, identifiers, and social or tripartite networks provide additional structures for information flow and interaction analysis.

6647a1e891d102ba6ad05aea79dbd2ef6bb81817.text:
## Ranking, Personalization, and Recommendation Systems

This community centers on learning to rank, personalized search, and recommendation quality. Learning-to-rank models include pointwise, pairwise, and listwise approaches such as ListNet and ConvRankNet, with Random Forests and other tree-based models used for ranking. These systems combine standard retrieval features with user and query context, searcher intent, result similarity, popularity, relevance, and temporal signals. Counterfactual inference provides a framework for unbiased learning from biased data, while partial click feedback, soft labels, and removal of harmful training examples support model training.

Neural networks provide complementary methods for ranking, answer selection, relevance estimation, regression, learned indexes, computer vision, and video analytics. Word2vec, GloVe, latent vector spaces, global and local embeddings, and word–entity interactions supply representation features.

LinkedIn is a major application setting, operating personalized search, personalized federated search, LinkedIn Salary, and expertise-search systems. Its professional connections and social-media data support profile disambiguation, topical expert mining, and recommendation features such as People You May Know.

Recommendation quality is evaluated through feature groups, dimensionality reduction, neural feedback relevance models, random forests, and deep recommendation systems.
