Related applications include product search, top-k selection, scholarly venue recommendation, diverse recommendation, profit maximization, and answer selection.

3cdf13326bf7037c86c8c41f7a8c25387e0eb2fd.text:
### Predictive Modeling, Diffusion, and Social Network Analysis

This community centers on prediction accuracy across social, behavioral, geographic, and system-oriented tasks. Applications include influence, protest, disease spread, voter intention, party affiliation, home location, suicide ideation, spam, sentiment, stock trends, and query execution time prediction.

Core predictive methods include logistic regression, decision trees, support vector machines, supervised and ensemble classification, conditional random fields, artificial neural networks, and hierarchical classification. Feature sets may include structural, semantic-field, named-entity, lexical, and event-specific features. Hierarchical classification improves location prediction by predicting broader regions before cities, while structural diversity improves popularity prediction.

Several systems address specialized problems: Attitude Sign Predictor achieves high or near-perfect accuracy; CARP improves prediction accuracy using capsule networks; BoostClean improves absolute accuracy; NetSpam supports spam detection; and TrendLearner addresses prediction tasks over time. Matrix-completion methods use user–item rating matrices and low-rank structure, with accuracy affected by rating volume and skewed distributions.

Information diffusion models explain information adoption, external influence, querying friends, seeding, and parameter fitting, with threshold models serving as simpler comparisons. Multiple Partitioning analyzes multiplex signed voting graphs through layer-wise partitioning and partition-similarity grouping. Other themes include community profiling, latent social-network inference, synthetic data generation, and safely avoiding joins while preserving classifier accuracy.

b5c0d1d250ddaf143f0365395db56ca2d14d7b18.text:
## Community Report: Temporal Structure, Similarity, and Fair Network Decisions

This community centers on temporal networks, higher-order structure, similarity measurement, and computationally difficult decision problems.

Temporal-network research includes temporal motifs, temporal network embeddings, event graphs, temporal network binning, timeline segmentation, and traveling/foremost journey semirings. Event graphs generalize second-order time-unfolded models, expose higher-order topological-temporal structure missed by static or time-aggregated models, and extend to hyper-events. Temporal motifs represent edge ordering and support network feature representations, conversation classification, and temporal-star analysis. Temporal networks also support epidemic source detection and empirical sexual-interaction analysis.

Motif methods include motif clustering, motif correlation clustering, motif covers based on near-cliques, and motif-enhanced meta-paths. Clique percolation uses cliques and clique adjacency in simple graphs, while multiplex clique percolation extends this setting.

Another major thread applies string compressibility, string compression, normalized compression distance, and aligned NCD to temporal audio structure, musical similarity, cover-song identification, similarity-rating prediction, and song-year prediction. Information-theoretic and prediction-based similarity methods compare time series; continuous-valued approaches outperform discrete-valued ones for cover identification.

Fair and connected districting address political and school districting, racial segregation, and plurality voting, but several districting, adoption, subset-selection, consistency-checking, motif-counting, and spread problems are NP-complete or NP-hard.

c469c71d1fea76065e64cd9a50e1e4015114923e.text:
## Learning, Search, Recommendation, and Similarity Methods

This community centers on learning to rank, personalized search, and recommendation. Learning-to-rank systems combine standard search features with user context, query context, searcher intent, and searcher–result similarity; applications include personalized search, static paper ranking, and personalized expertise search. Random forests, tree-based models, ListNet, Stochastic ListNet, latent vector space models, and counterfactual inference provide ranking methods, while temporal ranking models incorporate temporal evidence and crowd signals.

LinkedIn supports personalized expertise and federated search, using profile data and recent activities to infer intent. Expertise scoring targets exploratory queries containing skills. Scholarly venue recommendation models reading behavior and dynamic user interests from academic social networks.

Other work addresses recommendation and prediction: ZoneRec recommends zones for physical businesses using Facebook and urban-planning data, evaluated on Singapore food businesses. String-compressibility descriptors capture temporal structure in quantized audio and support musical similarity, similarity-rating prediction, and song-year prediction. Cover-song identification uses information-theoretic similarity and normalized compression distance, including aligned sequential compression, with Million Song Dataset and jazz-standard benchmarks.

Visualization-aware sampling selects data using a visualization-inspired loss and improves user success. Additional themes include semantic priming, profile disambiguation, hyperlink prediction, social-media inference, epidemic-source identification, and scholarly metrics.

b58063cf5632260b7ae05ab63d9ecb4116193e32.text:
## Community Detection, Structure, and Graph Sampling

This community focuses on community detection and graph clustering in complex networks, where network topology, clustering coefficients, and modularity characterize meso-scale community structure. Methods include modularity maximization, spectral clustering, graph cut methods, stochastic block models, belief propagation, profile and pseudo-likelihood, variational methods, and expert-systems approaches. Dynamic structural similarity can improve detected communities, while node attributes may be lost during network conversion.

Graph models and generators include stochastic blockmodels, BTER, GBTER, and eGBTER. BTER prescribes expected clustering-coefficient distributions; GBTER adds community modeling, while eGBTER captures community structure with satisfactory clustering accuracy. Spectral Graph Forge and ComPAS preserve community structure in generated or sampled graphs. Watts–Strogatz and Barabási–Albert models represent alternative network systems.

Graph sampling aims to preserve structural properties such as clustering coefficients and community structure. Randomized sketching creates reduced graphs for scalable clustering, with correlation-based retrieval inferring full-graph clusters. Uniform random node sampling suits balanced clusters, degree-based sampling unbalanced clusters, and spatial sampling improves cluster balance. Applications and evaluations involve synthetic graphs, real-world networks, US airport and *C. elegans* nervous-system networks, network-category datasets, temporal graphs, social interactions, and other network domains.

a2b22e3fb69462e8fd50dde335ab778d9c585d4a.text:
## Online Social Networks, Cascades, and Network Analysis

This community centers on online social networks (OSNs), their underlying social graphs, and the propagation of information. Information cascades represent spread through social connections; research examines their dynamics, semantics, activation paths, inter-arrival times, bursts, and cascade size. Digg provides a prominent setting, where cascades may reach hundreds of people while affecting only a small fraction of the network. Cascade prediction, quantitative cascade analysis, cascade computation, and rumor prevention are key objectives.

Methods include continuous-time network models, cascade-generating functions, social diffusion and epidemiological models, temporal-based predictors, wavelet transforms, and ultrametric representations. These support prediction of cascading processes, influence, trends, and information propagation. Structural and temporal features, tie strength, edge density, local network structure, and higher-order structure characterize networks and user behavior.

The community also addresses trust, privacy, misinformation, rumors, spammers, fake profiles, catfishing, Sybil attacks, and socialbot threats. Relevant systems and resources include limited-attention alpha centrality, real-time enhanced random sampling, network classification models, incremental community detection, network-aided sentiment detection, Pinterest activity data, Digg follower graphs, Sina Weibo, and real and synthetic social graphs.

9146fb66543dd14fc832655bfee5da28de22c9da.text:
## Twitter-Centered Learning, Polarization, and Disaster Analytics

This community centers on Twitter as a platform for social interaction, news consumption, political discourse, misinformation, and disaster detection, with Facebook providing comparable engagement and human-interaction patterns. Retweet and follower networks, hashtags, activity, topological metrics, and network visualization are used to study polarized discussions, political influence, and follow behavior. Political polarization is measured through cross-partisan retweeting, following patterns, and partisan hashtag use; relative polarization change increased by 10–20% depending on the measure. Misinformation and fake news—including the 2016 U.S. presidential election, the “Twitter bomb,” and Martha Coakley—are addressed through detection and dissemination-tracking tasks, fake-news keywords, URLs, hashtags, and user reactions.

Methods include longitudinal analysis, principal component analysis, factorization machines, ridge and polynomial regression, two-sample t-tests, and low-rank weighted matrix factorization for hashtag recommendation using usage history and hashtag-correlation matrices. In-database learning applies statistical models through relational database theory and query-evaluation algorithms, including retail forecasting applications.

Disaster research links GPS-stamped tweets with fire hotspots, haze events, peatland fires, NASA satellite imagery, and geospatial interdependence. A haze-management analytics tool supports disaster management. Other studies examine demographic inequality, gender identification, university Twitter engagement, and aggregate reputation rankings.

aedcdd9447a8f4618c46cb17f4a8fdba9603fc36.text:
## Temporal Networks, Social Influence, and Causal Inference

This community focuses on modeling social and temporal structure in networks. Temporal networks are represented with event graphs, temporal interaction networks, and macroscale components, while temporal aggregation is avoided to preserve inter-event times and other temporal information. Temporal core decomposition introduces span-cores and maximal span-cores; associated algorithms efficiently compute these dense structures using coreness and temporal spans. Temporal network embedding combines topological and temporal structure, including temporal motifs and inter-event times, to support collective behaviour analysis and conversation classification. These methods are evaluated on digital communication, face-to-face interaction, and other real-world datasets, and relate to epidemic containment over temporal networks.

A second theme is social influence and recommendation. Social relations and homophily motivate social recommendation, while homophily is also treated as a potentially spurious explanation of influence. Characterized social regularization (CSR) models variable influence across friends and products through a universal regularization term, supports explicit and implicit interactions, and outperforms stated social-recommendation baselines.

Opinion dynamics models private and expressed opinions, conformity, discrepancies, and exponential convergence, explaining Asch conformity experiments. Probabilistic causal analysis extracts minimal causal topologies from information propagation traces, using agony-bounded partitioning, to improve influence-spread prediction. Graph-based diffusion inference propagates probability vectors from seed nodes using topological structure, supporting age-group inference and analyses of mobile-operator communication logs.

bb39b6481f9f5b0d661fa3606df632bedec2805f.text:
## Community Detection Across Dynamic, Multimodal, and Urban Networks

This community centers on **community detection** and network clustering: partitioning networks into communities whose definition and scale depend on the resolution parameter. Algorithms are assessed for stability, robustness, causal dynamics, and agreement with ground truth using benchmark graphs, Facebook university networks, and other real-world datasets. The no-free-lunch theorem motivates problem-driven method selection.

Key approaches include spectral and cut-based methods—normalized and sparsest cuts, temporal graph cuts, graph wavelets, and the modulus of families of loops—as well as cooperative and hedonic games using the Myerson value. **HiCode** jointly identifies hidden and dominant community structure. **Community Profiling and Detection (CPD)** combines membership detection with internal content profiles and external diffusion profiles, using scalable inference and outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

The community also covers multimodal settings: OA biclustering mines binary datatables and evaluates bicluster density; n-mode and multiplex graphs support multi-mode communities and overlapping-layer analysis, although n-clique enumeration can be difficult. Dynamic graph signals and processes motivate temporal formulations.

Applications include infection spread modeling, social-network and email analysis, and urban analytics. Mobility networks inferred from over 69 million geo-located tweets delineate anthropographic urban boundaries, complementing administrative boundaries in Great Britain and London. Community interactions are linked to urban infrastructure systems and planning policies.

70bb1e42c8f50bf4376063a08adf648038fb9966.text:
## Community Detection, Vector Search, and Query-Efficient Analytics

This community spans network community detection, vector similarity search, and interactive aggregation.

**Community detection** is studied in social graphs, signed and bipartite networks, hospital-patient discharge networks, and rewired or higher-order networks. Key methods include **modularity maximization**, Louvain, InfoMap, the Memory Algorithm, geometric decomposition, and motif-aware **EdMot**, which constructs a motif-based hypergraph. Modularity measures community strength but has a resolution limit favoring large communities. **GroupSense** identifies interacting user groups using collective sensing and acoustic context. **Dynamical embeddings** and dynamical similarity extend community analysis across temporal scales and uncover functional modules. InfoMap and Louvain support health service area (HSA) delineation, with InfoMap producing low-conductance, high-localization HSAs.

For high-dimensional **similarity search** and maximum inner product search, vector quantization includes product, additive, optimized product, and residual quantization. Quantization error decomposes into norm and direction error, with norm error more influential for inner products; norm-explicit quantization reduces it. Locality-sensitive hashing and approximate nearest-neighbor search support arbitrary dense vectors, with Lucene and Anserini integrations.

**QWLSH** improves cache utilization and query latency through cost models and reduced cache misses. **GeoBlocks** uses query-driven layouts and pre-aggregation for approximate polygon aggregation, enabling sub-second interactive geospatial analytics and adapting to query workloads.

a221f9508109c60cbaa8051cbc901f7550fe5528.text:
## Cascade-Based Community Detection in Spreading Networks

This community centers on community detection in an underlying network, where the goal is to identify highly interconnected nodes. **Cascade-based community detection** infers properties of the underlying network from cascade data, using observed **infection times** of nodes as input. It is addressed through **heuristic approaches**, which are agnostic to both the specific graph structure and the epidemic model.

**Edge weighting** enhances community detection and can draw information from cascade data. The broader spreading context includes **rumor spreading** and **infectious disease spreading**, both of which propagate over the underlying network. An **epidemic model** provides a system associated with these spreading processes, while the heuristic methods remain model-agnostic. Together, these entities connect spreading observations—particularly infection times and cascade data—to methods for discovering communities without requiring a fixed graph structure or epidemic model.

1b0908f289aa66ed46bb56ed3998403175dcee55.text:
## Community Detection Across Multilayer, Temporal, and Attribute-Rich Networks

This community centers on community detection: identifying strongly connected groups and comparing their community structures across network types. Core approaches include modularity optimization, Louvain, InfoMap, hierarchical methods, generative and probabilistic graphical models, belief propagation, node embeddings, and the low-complexity EVA algorithm. Modularity uses the configuration model as a null model, while modularity belief propagation extends optimization to multilayer networks, incorporates a resolution parameter, is implemented in a Python package, and is compared with GenLouvain on synthetic and real-world multilayer networks.

The work addresses multiplex, multilayer, geo-social, temporal, sparse, heterogeneous labeled, linguistic, social, and co-citation networks. Co-located community detection combines spatial closeness and structural tightness, with a near-linear approximation algorithm. EVA targets attribute-aware segmentation, mesoscale topology, and attribute-homophilic clustering. VGraph is a probabilistic generative model that learns community membership.

Evaluation uses modularity, conductance, density measures, NMI, AMI, one-sided AMI, rrNMI, and cNMI, with emphasis on robust measurement and ground-truth recovery. Applications include political analysis of voting data, online-security user behavior and abnormal-community discovery, contagion propagation, opinion dynamics, brain connectomes, and subject identification.

9ba3ccae8347744d48047e127ad0329e86cfe3cf.text:
## Complex-Network Structure, Comparison, and Dynamics

This community examines how complex networks are structured, compared, and analyzed under dynamical processes. Community structure and blockmodelling represent densely connected groups, core-periphery configurations, hierarchical network configurations, and alternative blockmodels. Non-negative matrix factorisation fits blockmodel representations, while alternative discovery uses cannot-link constraints and image-matrix dissimilarity; quality evaluates the resulting models.

Graph and network comparison is surveyed through network similarity methods, with applications in systems biology and pattern recognition. Citation networks support the survey and reveal important papers using centrality measures. Centrality methods also rank influential nodes, with Kendall’s tau comparing rankings and robustness estimation assessing their reliability.

Local information dimension identifies influential spreaders using quasi-local information around a node, bounded by half the maximum shortest distance. Shannon entropy quantifies information in network boxes, while this locality restriction reduces computational complexity. Performance is evaluated on six real-world complex networks and against other rankings.

Networks provide the substrate for susceptible-infected and SIR spreading processes, including an exact networked Markov process and mean-field approximation. Finally, network geometry uses curvature and discrete Ricci flow—originating in smooth-manifold methods—to analyze networks, while structural perturbations can alter community structure and robustness.

ab12a0f852dd5d58052d04c94cb51ee7593882ad.text:
### Community Detection, Network Coarsening, and Low-Resource Classification

This community centers on statistical community detection in complex and large-scale networks. Stochastic block models (SBMs), including degree-corrected and nonparametric variants, provide generative and null-model foundations; likelihood and maximum-likelihood optimization support inference, while hierarchical community structure and edge correlations enable structured network modeling and uncertainty estimates. Spectral graph theory, spectral distance, interlacing theorems, and semi-definite programming provide additional theoretical and optimization tools.

Several methods address overlapping communities. Affiliation graph models and the simpler Jaccard-based affiliation graph model use community-set similarity to represent densely overlapping structures. The partial community merger algorithm (PCMA) detects significantly overlapping, slightly overlapping, and disjoint communities and is applied to Friendster. Node2vec is used for community detection on patent citation networks, with evaluation on real-world datasets using normalized mutual information.

Network summarization focuses on network coarsening for large-scale networks. The spectral preserving coarsening algorithm generates coarsened networks while preserving spectral properties, assessed through spectral measurements and spectral distance.

The community also covers active and semi-supervised learning. Active community detection selects informative nodes and uses constrained semi-definite programming. In sentiment classification, graph embedding, manifold regularization, pre-training, and transfer learning improve low-resource systems, including cross-corpus evaluation. Active learning also supports sentence-level relevance feedback and the AutoTAR continuous active-learning system in TREC 2015 and 2016 total-recall tracks.

a894859309e7df373f6b8e37362290ecc575456a.text:
## Community Detection, Graph Sampling, and Multilayer Consensus

This community centers on **community detection** across weighted, multilayer, attributed, and unweighted networks. Common approaches include label propagation, modularity maximization, clustering ensembles, and methods based on semantic relations. Evaluation may use known ground-truth communities, while extensions address community heterogeneity and email exchange networks.

Several methods improve graph modeling. An edge-weighting scheme uses local topological edge features and regression to assign positive weights for community affinity and negative weights for aversion, producing weighted graphs. The regression model is supervised on artificial graphs using ground-truth communities. Adaptive modularity maximization incorporates these weights and efficiently extracted local features, while addressing—but not eliminating—modularity’s resolution limit.

For multilayer networks, ensemble-based detection produces consensus communities by optimizing multilayer modularity and reconsidering community memberships. Parameter-free graph pruning, based on generative pruning models, removes noisy co-associations and identifies consensus communities without selecting a co-association threshold.

The community also covers scalable and distributed techniques. A closed walk sampler uses random walks and closed-walk counts to estimate the two largest graph eigenvalues on large graphs, including social networks. Eigenvalues relate to viral propagation and network resilience. The 2 choices dynamics provides a metastable, distributed label-propagation algorithm with quasi-linear message complexity.

fe12529e702de20abff39a1b3d01f7ad6355b566.text:
## Community Detection, Hyperbolic Embeddings, and Innovation Networks

This community centers on stochastic block models (SBMs) and extensions for discovering community structure. The SBM represents assortative and disassortative structures, includes the planted partition model as a special case, and samples latent community memberships. Degree-corrected and regularized SBMs address degree variation, observed network data, and robust detection; log-likelihood inference and Markov chain Monte Carlo are used, while regularization reduces inferior local optima. The restricted Boltzmann stochastic block model combines connectivity and node attributes, uses a restricted Boltzmann machine to sample latent memberships, and can extend to overlapping communities and real-world attributed networks.

A second theme is network representation through random walks and heat-based methods. Random walks generate training samples, capture topological and attribute similarity, and traverse latent multiplex hyperbolic space. Heat enables hyperbolic manifold learning and hyperboloid embeddings, with Lorentz distance providing the geometry, although it may violate the triangle inequality.

Generative models produce co-memberships, edge bundles, bridges, and liaison hierarchies, evaluated through information propagation, consensus convergence, and steady-state consensus deviation under noise.

Finally, patents form a co-inventor network for studying inventor communities, knowledge flow, and innovation dynamics. Shared community membership is associated with differences in time to first citation.

2e4b00ec7d1f1a79bba0eead5902abd668572c46.text:
## Dynamic Community Detection in Temporal Networks

This community centers on detecting evolving **community structure** in temporal networks and graphs. **Dynamic community detection** targets mesoscopic partitions that capture large-scale **dynamic community structures**, using data-driven methods and timescales inferred from network dynamics.

A key approach is **continuity-based community description**: communities are computed independently across time slices, then neighboring slices (\(t-1\) and \(t+1\)) are used to reduce noise and distinguish real trends from fluctuations. This is applied to dynamic processes such as the emergence, fusion, splitting, and death of scientific disciplines in a **scientific article network**.

Temporal graphs may instead be represented as **time-sliced networks** or an **aggregated network**. Aggregation enables static community detection but discards most temporal information. A data-driven alternative uses an arbitrary-order Markov chain with community structure; **nonparametric Bayesian inference** selects the simplest explanatory model and identifies relevant timescales directly from temporal interaction data.

The broader literature covers community detection algorithms, their mathematical classifications, algorithm selection, and comparison on benchmark networks. Applications include evolving systems such as **air traffic** and **social organisations**. Wavelet analysis is identified as an emerging subfield in scientific network analysis.

89023d0da42843c701dcc1e4be5ed6e490b4d7d2.text:
## Community Report: Graph Methods for Networks, Data, and Evaluation

This community connects complex-network analysis, linked-data engineering, research assessment, and music applications.

In network science, **von Neumann entropy node centrality** uses spectral eigenvalue distributions to approximate node importance and performs effectively for the optimal spreader problem. It is studied in scale-free and Erdős–Rényi networks, including effects on the giant connected component, robustness, and node failure. **Clustering vulnerability algorithms** formulate vulnerability as an optimization problem—proven NP-complete and potentially non-monotonic—and evaluate clustering disruption using the average clustering coefficient, random geometric graphs, synthetic social networks, and real social-network traces.

For linked data, RDF graphs are published through linked-data portals and described by data models. **ShEx** and **SHACL** support linked-data validation through validation engines and improve data quality; benchmarks generate compliant test structures. Keyword search uses **query graph assembly**, constructing graphs from entity/class vertices and predicate edges. Bipartite-graph-matching best-first search, guided by heuristic lower bounds, solves this NP-complete task.

In research evaluation, ANVUR’s Italian assessment exercise combines bibliometrics and informed peer review in a dual evaluation system, with agreement measured by kappa statistics. Assessment-data and article-sample disclosure issues affect reproducibility and university funding.

Finally, network metrics support music clustering and categorization, including guitar solos, with applications in music didactics and digital music generation.

d4c06e49667f6479e20a261324f0902e1ae31ca0.text:
## Community Detection, Ranking, and Knowledge-Aware Recommendation

This community connects graph analysis with recommendation and preference-learning methods. In complex networks, hierarchical graph clustering reveals multi-scale structure through dendrograms and graph representations, while modularity maximization extracts locally optimal communities. Modularity consensus spaces and semi-supervised label propagation support context-specific classification of latent relationships using pairwise constraints, seed sets, and query sets; performance is compared with random-walk-with-restart methods and evaluated on biological, social, real-world, and simulated datasets.

Recommendation research emphasizes learning to rank, collaborative ranking, and feature-based recommendation. Recommender systems use side information, including user and item features, content-based venue similarity, and location-based venue similarity. Collaborative ranking addresses venue suggestion and sparsity from exact venue matching, focusing on top-ranked lists and diverse recommendations, including on the TREC Contextual Suggestion dataset. CascadeLSB is an online learning-to-rank method under a cascade click model: it learns from partial clicks, explores user tastes, optimizes diverse lists, and has an analyzed regret bound.

Neural ranking models use representation learning and adversarial discriminators for cross-domain regularization, reducing reliance on hand-crafted features and improving held-out-domain precision@1. Discrete factorization machines binarize parameters, minimize quantization loss through discrete optimization, and outperform binarized recommendation models. KB4Rec v1.0 links recommender datasets with Freebase for knowledge-aware evaluation. Mixed-effects models combine social utility with personalized preferences for crowdsourced preference aggregation.

634ad671afc70654ac22cf1d02e146f6d28596fc.text:
## Graph Learning, Social Recommendation, and Scalable Network Analytics

This community connects graph-based machine learning with social, recommendation, and streaming-data applications. Predictive models use student dropout data, dynamic social network data, and users’ posts to support dropout intervention, mental-health prediction, academic-performance prediction, and reconstruction of school and university rankings. Graph convolution, predictive modeling, supervised classifiers, continuous word representations, and social regularization are prominent analytical approaches.

Recommendation research covers online marketplaces, scientific publications, groups, and time-aware or network-based settings. Systems and methods include scientific publication recommender systems, SREC, SEREC, hybrid recommender approaches, user-similarity measures, trust aggregation, least misery, aggregate voting, and network-based recommendation algorithms. These are evaluated through recommendation performance, group satisfaction, and trust metrics, often on real-world datasets.

A second major thread addresses evolving and large-scale graphs. Community discovery methods, community-definition analysis, small-world graphs, Watts–Strogatz graphs, graph generators, bipartite Chung–Lu and bipartite BTER models, and network representations support graph construction and analysis. Influence maximization, influence functions, social diffusion processes, early spreading patterns, and robust or adaptive strategies connect network structure to intervention.

Streaming and data-management methods include bloom filters, stable and biased-sampling variants, reservoir sampling, approximate duplicate detection, stream deduplication, database compaction, and frequent sequence mining. Their evaluation emphasizes false-positive and false-negative rates, convergence, scalability, and real-world datasets.

7f6372c9788f890fff61dd62fb3d1b32f3b5d9ca.text:
## Community Report: Multilayer Structure, Network Dynamics, and Classification

This community centers on methods for analyzing complex, multilayer, multiplex, temporal, and evolving networks.

For multilayer community detection, multislice modularity uses a resolution factor and inter-layer coupling factor. The proposed multilayer modularity instead defines resolution through redundancy-based information and coupling through projection-based information, supporting ordered layers and coupling constraints. It is evaluated on synthetic and real-world multilayer networks, including applications in life sciences, sociology, and digital humanities.

Network classification expands structural feature spaces with first- and second-order subgraph networks constructed from an original network. A network classification model combines these features with original-network features. Handcrafted and kernel-based feature extraction are used; handcrafted features outperform automatically generated features on most network classification datasets.

Topological data analysis maps network nodes into point sets through diffusion processes, producing scale-variant topological information. Neural dynamics on complex networks learns continuous-time dynamics using graph ordinary differential equations and differential deep learning, with optimal control and backpropagation used for training. Applications include node semantic labeling and graph semi-supervised classification.

Temporal analysis uses link stream formalism for IP traffic and MAWI captures. Degree-based outlier detection uses degree over time, including heterogeneous distributions, to detect anomalous events and identify causes of anomalous network activity. The war pact model generates shrinking networks with structural properties resembling real-world trade, war-correlate, and Bitcoin transaction networks.

723d3add05f579068caf4486aaf03494ca47ab16.text:
## Graph Representation Learning for Link Prediction and Network Applications

This community centers on network representation learning: learning low-dimensional node embeddings, edge embeddings, and multiple node representations for homogeneous, attributed, heterogeneous, and professional social networks. These representations support node classification, missing-link prediction, node recommendation, similarity ranking, attribute inference, user profiling, and graph reconstruction.

Link prediction is a major focus, commonly formulated as supervised classification with positive and negative examples. Baselines and signals include common neighbors, link-prediction heuristics, node-similarity measures, network proximity, the Katz index, and modularity-based methods. **DeepLinker** uses links as supervision for deep learning on graphs and produces node-centrality rankings, while **EvalNE** provides evaluation for link-prediction and network-embedding methods. Performance is assessed with link-prediction accuracy, error reduction, and real-world or synthetic datasets.

Key representation systems include **Star2Vec**, which combines strength-aware biased random walks with node-structure expansion for heterogeneous professional networks, and **HSRL**, which uses hierarchical sampling and community-aware compression to preserve local and global topology. **AHINE** applies an adaptive deep model to similarity ranking in points-of-interest networks. **SCAN** learns attribute embeddings for attribute inference and user profiling. Multiple node representations use ego-network decomposition to encode roles across local communities and aid visual analysis. Edge embeddings also support drug-response prediction, while graph-biased temporal point processes model direct and indirect influence using learned embeddings.

9f82047a274e877657990ea7a3ccd6d6c6b16abd.text:
## Streaming, Recommendation, and Robust Network Analytics

This community connects methods for learning from streams, networks, and real-world datasets. Data streams from sensors, Internet Relay Chat, and online banking motivate incremental processing, stream deduplication, approximate duplicate detection, and streaming recommender systems. Bloom-filter variants—including stable, biased-sampling, and reservoir-sampling-based filters—target scalable duplicate detection; the reservoir method improves false-negative rates and convergence over Stable Bloom Filters.

Recommendation research spans online marketplaces, publications, groups, and time-aware systems. Social network data supplies social relevance, user-similarity measures, network structure, and social-status prediction signals. Network-based, hybrid, and time-aware recommendation approaches are evaluated through recommendation performance, with time awareness especially beneficial in fast-aging systems. Group formation uses LM algorithms, AV heuristics, least misery, and aggregate voting.

Graph research covers community discovery, bipartite graph generation, small-world graphs, and graph generators. Community-discovery method selection considers directed edges and multidimensional networks. Bipartite Chung–Lu and bipartite BTER are demonstrated on real-world datasets. The infinity mirror test evaluates graph-generator robustness and exposes implicit or explicit bias and degeneration; robustness also depends on topology and edge placement.

Predictive models address student dropout, meme success, purchasing, sports, and game outcomes, using discovered patterns, early spreading patterns, and predictive coding. Additional themes include SQL progress estimation, frequent sequence mining with varied subsequence constraints, and PAC learnability.

4e3dbe9dacda9e8a9c0f5d297fa99b1331ff4452.text:
## Network Structure, Citation Distributions, and Research Assessment

This community links complex-network modeling with citation-based research evaluation. Degree distributions describe node degree and characterize scale-free networks, often through power laws, preferential attachment, and the Barabási–Albert model. Degree transformations support asymptotic analysis toward log-normal distributions, with Berry–Esseen estimates providing convergence rates; log-normal approximations further describe degree-distribution tails.

The Chinese venture capital network is analyzed using degree and clustering-coefficient distributions. Its network dynamics model incorporates relational and structural embeddedness and partner-selection mechanisms, while a random graph model provides a baseline controlling for network scale, growth, investment frequency, and syndication tendency. The network includes an elite clique, measured with the E-I index, which forms the center of a small-world network. EVOCUT generalizes the Barabási–Albert model and models complex-network evolution.

A second theme concerns citation distributions and research assessment. Normal publications exhibit a lognormal citation distribution, enabling probability calculations and estimates of highly cited papers. Double rank analysis relates local rank position to world rank position and supports research assessment through the double-rank property. Percentile-based double rank analysis uses world percentiles and publication counts to estimate highly cited paper likelihood, offering a robust research assessment method for institutions and countries.

Finally, scientific breakthroughs are treated as rare events supporting global progress of knowledge; probability and expected frequency estimate their likelihood and occurrence rate.

00e6dff76c1540c34ef01ea22ccdf393a500df64.text:
## Community Report: Networks, Social Q&A, and Cross-Domain Learning

This community centers on network representation, model selection, community discovery, and predictive tasks on social and information networks. Network model selection uses task-neighborhood functions and robust criteria to choose interpretable representations for attributed-network inference and other predictive tasks, improving task performance across online user-activity datasets. Community-discovery methods are organized by features such as directed edges and multidimensionality.

A major theme is cross-domain network learning. DIME combines meta-proximity scores, broad learning, and an aligned autoencoder to learn user embeddings from diverse links and attributes. HGANE applies hierarchical graph attention to collective link prediction in directed aligned networks, predicting both intra-network social links and inter-network anchor links.

Another cluster concerns semantic retrieval and question answering. Quora, Stack Exchange, CQA datasets, and Siri support question retrieval and semantically similar-content applications. Semantic flow graphs, question embeddings, clustering, and social information address lexical gaps and equivalent-question retrieval. Quora studies anonymous questions, including topical mixing, personality traits, response time, user equality, information exposure, and connection establishment.

The community also covers graph metrics and dynamics: distance sum and generalized distance sum address independence, dominance preservation, and accessibility vulnerability; connected random graph generation uses property-conditioned sampling; and social-interaction models examine connectedness, belief dynamics, diffusion, long-term bonds, and message spreading. OCWA and homomorphic-cover methods address semantic equivalence and incomplete-database semantics.

e1a7e72a2ad6fa342a795d8477bf1b4b7bb130d1.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Similarity, Search, Communities, and Skyline Queries

This community covers methods for network analysis, search, conversation, visualization, and skyline querying.

**Similarity and community organization:** In-network node similarity uses network neighborhoods and extends proximity-based similarity. A unified parametric model instantiates four neighborhood-based similarity measures, with neighborhood matching controlling similarity meaning and matching specificity at a computational-cost trade-off. ACM mines application-aware communities around concerned attributes: feature subspaces are expanded and evaluated through subspace fitness, while cohesive network-backbone regions provide community seeds. ACM is assessed on synthetic datasets and real-world networks.

**Search and interaction systems:** Query auto completion is a search-system feature implemented by a query completion engine that aggregates multiple engines. User information improves recommendations, and engine aggregation increases recommendation diversity. A bandit setting optimizes the mixture of engines, which outperforms a single engine. Content-based and social-graph-based conversation models use user information and location to support personalized interactions.

**Visualization:** InfiniViz uses result-refinement querying with progressive bin refinement, reducing cognitive and computational cost while minimizing information loss. It is evaluated on real and benchmark datasets.

**Skyline querying:** KSJQ extends k-dominant skyline queries to joined relations and aggregated skyline preferences. Base-relation preprocessing reduces processing time versus joining before skyline computation; experiments use real and synthetic datasets.

359bcacb6bbc923faf4fa9c87685dfbd80148bdd.text:
## Community Report: Dynamic Networks, Retrieval, and Influence

This community connects social-network analysis, dynamic networks, information retrieval, and influence maximization.

**HellRank** is a distributed centrality measure for bipartite social networks. Using local information and Hellinger distance between nodes on the same side, it identifies central and behaviorally representative users without centralized topology knowledge. Its rankings are evaluated with Spearman and Kendall rank correlations, and it is tested on real-world networks. Centrality estimation and central node identification are key applications.

For dynamic social networks, snapshot models support change-point detection, including a three-step approach evaluated on synthetic, real-world, and road-network datasets (California, Pennsylvania, and Texas). This approach improves detection quality and achieves up to 9× speedup. Social network analysis also addresses strongly connected social groups, while control theory and social dynamics models provide foundations for multi-agent systems and influence processes.

The retrieval strand uses **polyrepresentation**, combining information-object, work-task, user-background, ideal-answer, and information-needs representations to improve retrieval accuracy. Subjective logic models this combination through belief and uncertainty, using retrieval-dataset evidence to predict suitable representations before retrieval.

Finally, adaptive seeding strategies use the dynamic independent cascade model to select users for influence maximization. Greedy adaptive seeding has a provable performance guarantee; heuristic methods improve scalability and are evaluated on synthetic power-law and real-world networks.

2c40c91c1c8708c7c2e3f2c3a9ef97bd4a7bead0.text:
## Heterogeneous Network Representation and Expert Finding

This community links network representation with expert finding in heterogeneous bibliographic networks. **UNRA** is presented as a universal network-representation approach for heterogeneous information networks, addressing the common focus of existing methods on homogeneous information networks. It maps different node types into a continuous **common vector space** and is built on a **mutually updated neural language module**. This module captures relationships among homogeneous nodes and correlations between nodes and their content. UNRA is evaluated for node representation and network visualization.

**Expert finding** is studied within heterogeneous bibliographic networks and uses textual content analysis to rank candidates and authority ranking to estimate their authority. The authority-ranking method uses network structure in heterogeneous information networks and ranks objects through typed interactions. It is integrated into an expert finding framework, which is evaluated on a bibliographical dataset supporting both general and specific queries.

Together, the concepts connect heterogeneous network structure, content-based analysis, authority estimation, and representation learning for expert-finding systems.

e2381c44914a8beede9f5f255040fff75d27a3a9.text:
## Graph Learning, Higher-Order Structure, and Temporal Multilayer Ranking

This community covers network embeddings, graph learning, relation extraction, diffusion, and centrality in multilayer and higher-order networks.

**Embedding methods** learn low-dimensional node representations for node classification and link prediction. Improved DeepWalk-based embeddings jointly model shared and layer-specific information across multilayer networks, supporting classification, link prediction, and community detection while producing highly modular structures. Enhanced network embeddings exploit edge labels to preserve relations and network structure, with evaluation on multilabel node classification.

**Graph neural methods** include graph convolutional networks using localized spectral convolutions, and motif convolutional networks, which generalize earlier approaches. Motif models use weighted multihop motif adjacency matrices to capture higher-order neighborhoods and achieve strong semi-supervised node-classification results, addressing the inability of standard graph convolutions to capture higher-order interactions.

**Relation extraction** combines bidirectional LSTMs, attention, capsule networks, and dynamic routing for multiple entity pairs within multi-instance, multilabel learning.

**Temporal multilayer nonlinear HITS** extends HITS to weighted directed temporal multilayer networks. Based on a multi-homogeneous order-preserving map and the Perron eigenvector, it computes node, layer, and temporal centrality vectors via power iteration.

**Other applications** include BLAG, a bandit model that learns forwarding ability while limiting information loss, and efficient heuristics evaluated on synthetic and real datasets. Benchmarks assess performance and whether institutional differences are meaningful.

f1f5c3e76eca7533616d82c294f0564c029d47b5.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Social Media Analysis, Bots, and User Modeling

This community centers on computational analysis of Twitter and other microblogging social networks. Major tasks include location prediction—using tweet content, context, and network information to infer home, tweet, mentioned, or semantic locations—and point-of-interest recommendation. User modeling includes interest inference, profile construction and enhancement, profile representation, and profile evaluation.

A prominent theme is detecting automated and malicious activity. Unsupervised spam-campaign detection identifies botnets and bot accounts, which may use shortened URLs and duplicate content; detection protocols, REST APIs, social honeypots, and malicious-bot databases support collection and filtering. Real-time user-type classification categorizes organization/individual and male/female users, including workforce-diversity applications.

Political research examines Russian trolls, foreign influence operations, bot activity, election datasets, narrative propagation, and conservative or liberal amplification. Network causal inference estimates causal influence from exposure-related outcome differences while accounting for propagation, graph sampling, and estimation bounds.

Gab is studied as a Twitter alternative using 22 million posts, with attention to hate speech, alt-right users, conspiracy theorists, and trolls. Other applications analyze public-library communication and themes in over 19,000 tweets, genetic-testing discourse and digital health, scholarly communication and altmetrics, and music information retrieval.

276da15651662e1fc810eef9ec1383aaa13ca663.text:
## Graph-Based Recommendation, Identity Linkage, and Table Understanding

This community spans sequential recommendation, graph-based user modeling, and table structure recognition. Sequential recommendation includes Markov chains, recurrent models, autoregressive training, data augmentation, and top-k evaluation. COSRec encodes purchase histories as three-way tensors, uses 2D convolutions for sequential features, and aggregates high-order interactions to model pairwise relationships. A memory-augmented graph neural network uses shared memory and bilinear functions to capture short- and long-term interests, long-range dependencies, and item co-occurrence patterns.

Latent-variable and variational methods model evolving user states and session-based recommendation. They use posterior distributions, reparameterization, the Bouchard bound for softmax, and variational autoencoder or variational expectation-maximization approaches. GFedRec uses an encoder-decoder framework to reconstruct masked items from past and future context while avoiding data leakage. Style injection and style-conditioned recommendations apply conditional VAEs and style transfer to diversify recommendations; the latter reports a 12% NDCG@20 improvement over a VAE baseline.

Graph neural network frameworks combine local neighborhood and global community structure from user social graphs for user identity linkage, alongside profile data and network proximity. Community detection uses label propagation and strongly connected components on test networks.

For tables, GraphTSR predicts cell relations from table cells, while SciTSR provides labeled structures extracted from scientific-paper PDFs; HTML, ASCII, spanning cells, and table cells are also addressed.

c00547f352609c51dcbb5456a4086776edab2adf.text:
## Community Report: Network Structure, Attributes, and Multiview Prediction

This community studies how network structure and node attributes interact, and how their combined information supports analysis and prediction.

The **generalized clustering measure** extends clustering coefficient \(C_3\) from triples to cliques and node groups of arbitrary size. It has analytic formulae for three-, four-, and five-node cases, established theoretical properties, fast runtime on U.S. airline networks, and documented limitations.

The **attribute connectivity alignment test** evaluates whether node attributes align with network structure. It uses label propagation and node sampling, computes empirical p-values, and is evaluated on synthetic networks and a CyTOF network containing single-cell subpopulations and associated cell markers.

The **multiplicative attribute graph (MAG)** models network structure as shaped by node attributes; the homogeneous binary MAG is its corresponding variant.

For wellness prediction, **NetCare** uses social network structure and is evaluated on longitudinal NetHealth data from University of Notre Dame students. It predicts stress, happiness, positive attitude, and self-assessed health, improving over baseline models.

Finally, the **multi-entry neural network (MENET)** combines textual, network, and metadata features through multiview learning. It provides a Twitter user-geolocation method, integrating user-generated content with network-based and content-based information.

5be4f61b1a8aaf597acbe7381114332ce2c88049.text:
## JNET for User and Content Modeling

This community centers on **JNET**, a system for **user representation learning** and content-oriented applications. JNET uses **joint network embedding** to model social connections and **topic embedding** to model text content, placing users and topics in a **shared latent space**. Its architecture is implemented through a **probabilistic generative framework**.

The learned representations support **content recommendation**, including **expert finding** as an example application. JNET is evaluated using **StackOverflow discussion posts**, where expert finding is applied to users and discussions, and using **Yelp reviews**. Together, these datasets provide settings for assessing how jointly modeled social and textual information can support recommendation and user-focused tasks.

0ec8d86d491efe4dd3829839d4fa5f6601b57c9c.text:
## Graph Methods, Reproducibility, and Robust Network Systems

This community links graph structure analysis with reliable computational workflows and network applications. **Network motifs** are treated as higher-order connectivity patterns: motif-based controversy detection, information-theoretic motif analysis, higher-order motif features, and temporal five-node motif counts use them to characterize diffusion, spreading, and dominant structures. A variational principle formulates dominant-motif identification as an optimization problem.

**Reproducibility** is connected to workflows, versioned data and services, computational context, and open-source software. Workflow provenance traces and provenance services capture execution information, while the CPK ontology and annotated CPK dataset support workflow representation. Open-source systems also support digital-preservation repositories, standards, protocols, and preservation strategies.

The community studies **trust and social networks** through trust aggregation, multi-faceted trust models, trust-aware neighbourhoods, collaborative filtering, and regular equivalence. These methods connect trust networks with recommendation and robustness under threats.

**Robustness** is examined in transportation networks, trust metrics, progress estimators, and graph topologies. Watts–Strogatz and unsupervised small-world graphs are compared with random and power-law graphs. Collaboration, friendship, mobility, communication, and real-world interaction networks provide application settings, supported by sampling, graph reconstruction, path-query, clustering-vulnerability, and human-mobility methods.

8c290000bec829590fe132823a45ba881d584b7b.text:
## Predictive Analytics, Reviews, and Social Systems

This community centers on prediction accuracy across social, commercial, and data-management applications. Logistic regression, support vector machines, decision trees, machine-learning classifiers, generalized additive models, and artificial neural networks support tasks including suicide-ideation, market-trend, protest, demographic, interaction, and social-property prediction. Feature selection, event-specific features, weighted path entropy (WPE), localforecasting, and CARP improve predictive performance; working-profile prediction reports 87% accuracy, while Twitter sentiment reaches 97.87% for upward market trends.

A major theme is review analysis. Yelp reviews support positive/negative and five-star classification, using review text, ratings, and user data. CARP uses capsule networks, viewpoints, aspects, logic units, and routing by bi-agreement to analyze sentiment across seven real-world datasets. Deception research measures prevalence across Expedia, Hotels.com, Orbitz, Priceline, and TripAdvisor, with deception classifiers and generative deception models.

Reputation links ratings, past contributions, ranking algorithms, Yelp businesses, and Groupon merchants. Groupon and daily-deals research examines pricing schemes, merchant reputation, and the Groupon effect.

Database-oriented work addresses query planning, execution-time prediction, cost-based optimization, distributed dataflow, and safely avoiding KFK joins. Classifiers remain robust when joins or dimension tables are discarded, while distributed gradient descent optimizes logistic-regression and SVM models.

329155082ba90bbac632187db78b5beb3f1cb654.text:
## Scholarly Identity Disambiguation and Specialty-Based Reviewer Support

This community centers on **author name disambiguation** and **bibliometric specialty approximation**. Disambiguation is evaluated with labeled datasets, including DBLP, using pairwise precision, recall, and F1, particularly for large ambiguous name blocks. Features include title words and coauthor names, while random forest, naive Bayes, and logistic regression serve as classifiers. Imbalanced training data is examined through positive-to-negative training ratios: naive Bayes and logistic regression perform optimally at 1:1, whereas random-forest improvement saturates around 1:10–1:15. DBLP is a digital library using a hybrid approach that combines algorithmic disambiguation with manual error correction.

Specialty approximation associates publication records with research specialties using fields such as authors, references, title, and source. It supports peer identification, research policy, and research management. Bibliometric specialty approximation uses key sources, including references, to generate reviewer suggestions. These suggestions support reviewer assignment for senior research fellowship applications, showed no indication of mismatched scientific focus, and received a normal reviewer acceptance rate. The work is grounded in scholarly communication and research disciplines.

e4eb076c6f0223c38fbf867a4d19f02a70bc2a5a.text:
## Community Report: Graph-Based Recommendation, Hyper-Relational Learning, and Structure Discovery

This community centers on graph representation learning, recommendation, and structure discovery.

For recommendation, **GhostLink** is an unsupervised probabilistic graphical model that uses timestamps and review content to learn latent influence networks from BeerAdvocate, RateBeer, Amazon, and related review-community data. It supports influential-user detection and separates latent preferences from influenced preferences, improving item recommendation. A **hybrid model** combines graph-embedding methods and individual embeddings, outperforming individual baselines under standard metrics and supporting a hybrid social recommendation system. **Rule-guided neural recommendation** mines inductive rules from item-centric knowledge graphs to infer multi-hop item associations, provide human-readable explanations, and improve cold-start generalization. Factorization and regression trees use latent profiles and user-generated reviews to support explainable recommendation; user studies evaluate acceptance and practical value.

For hyper-relational learning, **Bregman hyperlink regression** predicts tuple hyperlink weights through a learned symmetric similarity function based on Bregman divergence. It generalizes graph embedding when tuple order is two and Poisson regression when order is one, with stochastic optimization and generalized minibatch sampling enabling efficient learning.

For structure discovery, **AutoFD** formulates functional-dependency discovery as sparse regression, including on noisy datasets, and outperforms existing FD discovery methods.

Finally, **NIPEN** learns low-dimensional latent manifolds and variables from legislative bill texts, revealing legislators’ ideal points and trust-network structure for voting prediction.

bc7624669cce1e0c1ff17ec02a38166aacbfc23a.text:
## Location, Reviews, Mobility, and Recommendation Research

This community centers on data-driven analysis of human behavior, geographic activity, and online platforms. Location-based social networks—including Foursquare—provide check-in and mobility data for spatio-temporal behavior modeling, venue suggestion, check-in prediction, and personalized or spatial item recommendation. GeoSAGE addresses user–item sparsity by combining personal interests, crowd preferences, spatial co-occurrence, content, and a spatial pyramid.

Reviews and reputation form another major theme. Yelp and Groupon datasets support analysis of merchant reputation, ratings, daily deals, and the “Groupon effect.” Deception prevalence is studied across Yelp and travel-review communities, using generative models and deception classifiers; Yelp reviews also raise questions about biased or fake reviews and observer effects.

Methods for movement and transitions include HypTrails, which uses Markov chains, informative Dirichlet priors, Bayes factors, and roulette-based prior elicitation to compare hypotheses about human trails. Mobility analysis also uses mobile-phone data from Côte d’Ivoire and Portugal to examine developing countries and social segregation.

Additional topics include accessibility computation from origins to destinations via public transport and quad-trees; collective perception extraction by topic and geography; mixture models optimized with EM for voting, product recommendation, and push-message open-rate prediction; and entity search and ranking evaluated with graded relevance measures. ORCID is examined for researcher coverage, web identities, and scholarly orphans.

fba729da80aeed6185587b8e37dac1f95d314247.text:
## Twitter Sentiment for FTSE 100 Prediction

This community focuses on using the **Twitter sentiment score (TSS)** to predict future stock-market trends, particularly the future price and trend of the **FTSE 100**. **Lexicon-based sentiment analysis** is used to compute sentiment scores from Twitter text.

The prediction task employs several methods. **Logistic regression** and **linear discriminant analysis** classify future market trends, while **polynomial regression** is applied in the TSS modeling analysis. The proposed **baseline correlation** criterion is associated with the Twitter sentiment score and enables prediction without historical sentiment or market data.

Reported performance includes **97.87% accuracy** for predicting upward market trends using the Twitter sentiment score. The baseline correlation achieves **67.22% prediction accuracy** while reducing computation. Overall, the entities describe a sentiment-driven approach to FTSE 100 forecasting, combining Twitter-derived metrics, regression and classification methods, and correlation-based evaluation.

a778d37dac4fb65dc28e99df32765953649e9577.text:
## Disinformation Detection in Multi-Layer Diffusion Networks

This community focuses on detecting disinformation versus mainstream news, while considering political bias across different news sources. The key method is logistic regression, used to classify news and evaluated with AUROC, reaching performance of up to 94%.

The approach uses multi-layer representations of Twitter diffusion networks. These network layers support computation of global network features, which quantify different aspects of the news sharing process. Together, the diffusion-network representations and global features provide information for the classification task, while political bias is incorporated as a consideration when distinguishing disinformation from mainstream news.

f91483b68ba9b6b8e4ab8a46f4ffe18e1ef6a650.text:
## Community Report: Social Platforms, Data Systems, and Applied Learning

This community spans social-media analysis, probabilistic databases, recommendation, multimodal retrieval, and domain-specific NLP.

**Gab** is a major topic: studies analyze millions of posts and conversation threads to discover topics, examine cascade behavior, and measure hate-speech diffusion. Gab is characterized by limited moderation, broad protection of hate speech, and strong ties to alt-right, conspiratorial, and trolling communities.

**Probabilistic databases** address incomplete and imprecise data using possible-worlds representations, semirings, semimodules, and probabilistic Datalog semantics. They support aggregate and non-aggregate query answering, query-probability computation, and approximation of result-value distributions.

Recommendation research focuses on recommendation quality, trust dynamics, and user acceptance. Random forests, schema-level patterns, neural feedback relevance models, and genetic-algorithm-inspired hybridization are evaluated against baselines, including in zone recommendation for physical businesses using Facebook and urban-planning data.

Other methods support fine-grained cross-media retrieval through classification, center, and ranking constraints; political-bias prediction from speeches, manifestos, and media texts; and two-stage federated clinical NLP for obesity and comorbidity phenotyping without moving clinical notes between institutions. TexT enables semi-automatic transcription, word spotting, and annotation of archival handwritten documents.

fbce2d515787ffaaea2994f0424d47581f42d9e5.text:
## Recommender Systems, Collaborative Filtering, and Bias Mitigation

This community centers on recommender systems that address information overload by modeling user preferences, interaction histories, and item content. Collaborative filtering and matrix factorization are core approaches, commonly framing recommendation as matrix completion over rating matrices and learning low-rank structure. Extensions include deep neural networks for nonlinear user–item relationships, hierarchical bi-level maximum-margin matrix factorization, Wasserstein CF for cold-start items, and NAS, which applies neural and social-behavioral attention to model friends’ preferences and social latent effects.

Efficiency is another focus. Compositional coding combines binary codes, real-valued vectors, sparse weights, and integer-weight approximation to improve recommendation efficiency while maintaining accuracy; binary hashing represents collaborative filtering in Hamming space. Recommendation algorithms are evaluated using recommendation accuracy, calibration, diversity, and group average popularity.

The community emphasizes popularity and exposure bias: popular items can suppress long-tail items and disadvantage low-mainstream users. Exposure bias depends on prior exposure and can reduce diversity over iterations. Debiasing and calibration approaches assess differences across user groups, including LastFM’s low-, medium-, and high-mainstream users. Social recommendation uses friends’ selections under sparse preferences. Additional work covers HINT for similarity and transition matrices over tweet–news datasets, comparative-text clustering and knowledge transfer, and applications in music, movies, e-commerce, online platforms, and vacation rentals.

10618a02eba8185510fe72e4d26d7ec30c6676d2.text:
## Structure-Aware and Automated Learning over Relational Data

This community focuses on machine learning over relational databases, including database table joining, feature discovery, data transformations, and predictive analytics. Relational structure is represented through functional dependencies, key–foreign key dependencies, KFK joins, and FD-induced patterns.

**AC/DC** provides structure-aware learning over relational databases, using functional dependencies and sparse tensors for relational analytics. It supports training and evaluation with principal component analysis, ridge linear regression, and polynomial regression, and is benchmarked against MADlib, LibFM, and TensorFlow.

**One Button Machine** automates feature engineering and feature discovery, automatically joins database tables, applies advanced data transformations, and reduces data exploration time. Evaluated in Kaggle competitions, it improved prediction accuracy and outperformed a state-of-the-art system in Kaggle leaderboard ranking.

Another theme is **avoiding joins safely**: decision trees, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, and linear classifiers were evaluated for robustness when KFK joins were avoided. High-capacity classifiers retained prediction accuracy.

The applications include voter intention prediction from Facebook likes in a multiparty context. Studies report that parsimonious digital traces, including a single Facebook Like, can provide predictive information comparable to broader datasets or hundreds of heterogeneous Likes, with machine-learning classifiers exceeding earlier multiparty-study accuracies of approximately 60–70%.

3b25404d40e059d4af9ed7980e6c519d2d0bac4d.text:
## Graph-Based Prediction Across Transactions, Networks, and Online Behavior

This community centers on graph-based prediction in three areas: illicit transaction detection, evolving social networks, and mental-health-related advertising analysis.

For anti-money-laundering, the Elliptic Data Set represents Bitcoin transactions as a time-series transaction graph with directed payment-flow edges. Illicit transaction classification evaluates Random Forest, Multilayer Perceptron, Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Logistic Regression methods; Random Forest achieves an AUC of 0.92 and outperforms evaluated graph methods. A graph visualization prototype supports temporal inspection of illicit activity, analysis, and model explainability.

GCN-GAN addresses temporal link prediction and network dynamics prediction in weighted dynamic networks. It combines GCNs for local topology, Long Short-Term Memory for evolving features, and a Generative Adversarial Network to generate the next weighted network snapshot while addressing edge-weight sparsity and range variation.

RGNet uses GUVec global user embeddings and Einstein field equations to model online discussions as relativistic gravitational systems. It predicts temporal engagement and discussion growth, while also supporting non-temporal engagement prediction. Its reported scores are Micro F1 0.72 and AUC 0.62; a Newtonian gravity model provides a baseline.

Other applications include friendship prediction from hashtag profiles using bipartite graph embeddings, and anxious-depression prediction from real-time tweets, user posting patterns, anxiety-related lexicons, and five-tuple feature vectors.

05b37e383f1a1dfc425ca5d9e217ab6b7e485289.text:
### Signed-Network Opinion Dynamics and Polarization

This community centers on opinion dynamics, signed networks, polarization, and echo chambers. Opinion-dynamics research models opinion evolution, consensus, divergence, and neutralization in networks containing positive and negative relationships. Key approaches include the DeGroot model, Friedkin–Johnsen model, voter and generalized voter models, consensus models, stochastic multi-agent models, boomerang-effect models, and agent-based opinion-formation models. Markov chains, graph Laplacians, mean-field methods, and multidimensional Fokker–Planck equations support analysis of individual and population-level evolution. Stubborn agents and zealots represent fixed opinions, while biased assimilation, confirmation bias, selective exposure, and repulsive interactions help explain polarization.

Structural balance theory connects signed networks—representing friendship/trust and enmity/distrust—to polarized communities and opinion outcomes. Frustration index, line index of balance, Stirling-based indices, spectral goodness of fit, and structural-balance visualization measure imbalance and polarization. Signed graph attention and convolutional networks, signed social-network induction, edge-sign inference, network inference, and partitioning address signed-network analysis.

Echo chambers arise from like-minded interaction, selective exposure, commenting patterns, and content-promotion algorithms; they can reinforce polarization, radicalization, and misinformation cascades. Recommendation methods, including opposing-view and contrarian-content recommendation, are studied as possible interventions, while system transparency and telephoning may reduce polarization.

9ac0666a173f1f5ff29c1b69c3a796afb8b90ddb.text:
## Recommender Systems: Methods, Challenges, and Evaluation

This community centers on recommender systems that address information overload through personalized recommendation, ranking, top‑N recommendation, rating prediction, and item recommendation. Systems commonly learn from explicit ratings or implicit user–item interactions, modeling user preferences, interests, and representations.

Collaborative filtering—including user-based, item-based, neural, quaternion, and large-scale variants—uses interaction patterns and matrix factorization or matrix completion. Content-based filtering uses item content, while hybrid recommender systems combine collaborative, content, and side information such as product attributes, reviews, aesthetic features, and sentiment. Deep learning, representation learning, autoencoders, metric learning, ensemble learning, and deep reinforcement learning support richer user and item embeddings. Specialized systems and methods include RippleNet, Neural Graph Collaborative Filtering, VBPR, Bayesian Personalized Ranking, recurrent Poisson factorization, and sequential recommender systems using temporal dynamics or Markov chains.

Key challenges include data sparsity and noise, cold-start and item cold-start problems, popularity bias, bias disparity, and limited feedback. Cross-domain recommendation and transfer learning address sparse or unfamiliar settings. Evaluation includes offline evaluation on MovieLens, MovieLens 1M, public, and dense recommender datasets, using RMSE, ratings, click-through rate, recommendation accuracy, performance, and diversity—highlighting the diversity–accuracy dilemma.

9cf01ab260096681d4574f5939d1dc7ed13b8b50.text:
## Social Media, Political Influence, and Stance Analysis

This community centers on social media as a setting for sentiment analysis, stance detection, political polarization, and manipulation. Stance detection infers a viewpoint toward a topic or entity and classifies it as supportive or opposing; it is distinct from sentiment polarity, although positive or negative language may express stance.

Political activity is examined through bots and automated accounts, which operate on social media and can enable manipulation and deception. Bot operations were studied around the 2016 U.S. presidential election, the 2017 French presidential election, and the 2018 U.S. midterms, including an election-tweets dataset. The Cambridge Analytica scandal connects political issues, data privacy, the Zuckerberg hearing in the U.S. Congress, and English- and Spanish-language reactions; cross-language analysis revealed cultural differences in privacy perspectives.

The 2018 Turkish election Twitter datasets analyze pro- and anti-Recep Tayyip Erdogan polarization, including disagreement about refugees and agreement about terrorism under Turkey’s new presidential system. Separate word-embedding models compare political leaders, issues, and lifestyle choices in embedding space.

Methods include text mining, meaning extraction, word embeddings, and evidence-based systematic mapping. Arabic sentiment-analysis research, mapped across 51 primary studies, emphasizes solution research alongside validation and evaluation, with publications increasing annually since 2015.

ebb6413bd9a6c31a47c0fb5fe872cb307791da60.text:
## Query Structure, Uncertainty, and Repair in Databases

This community centers on conjunctive and join queries evaluated over databases, often represented by query hypergraphs. Structural properties—including treewidth, hypertree width, generalized and fractional hypertree width, semantic acyclicity, and query decomposition—guide tractability, output-size bounds, and worst-case optimality. AGM bounds, polymatroid linear programs, NPRR, Leapfrog Triejoin, and worst-case optimal parallel algorithms address efficient query evaluation under communication-round and per-processor-load constraints, including skewed data.

A second theme is inconsistent, uncertain, and probabilistic data. CERTAINTY(Q) asks whether every repair satisfies a query, with complexity ranging from P to coNP-complete for specified self-join-free Boolean conjunctive queries. Repairs, constrained repairs, transaction repair, functional dependencies, equality-generating dependencies, and tuple-generating dependencies connect integrity constraints to database correction and serializable updates. Probabilistic databases support conditioning on observations, hypothesis management, and probabilistic query evaluation; UpsilonDB provides hypothesis analytics using U-relational data.

Ontology-mediated queries and separability study tractable query answering under logical theories and dependencies. Functorial and adjoint data-migration functors, FQL, and category theory connect schemas, queries, and database migration. Systems and methods such as PANDA, DeepDive, CADO, ICG-Datalog, quasi-succinct indexes, and parallel query processing operationalize these ideas.

7cbc0527048046f4934bd0d223ed7e4f5674cd51.text:
## Community Report: Uncertainty, Dependencies, and Data-Driven Systems

This community centers on managing uncertain, incomplete, and probabilistic data through formal dependencies, hypothesis systems, and scalable data-processing methods. Functional dependencies support web-based data imputation, dependency-graph modeling, aggregate queries, causal reasoning, and optimal subset repair. They extend to ontology, equality-generating, conditional, and differential dependencies, with separability providing tractable query answering for theories involving TGDs and EGDs.
