Probabilistic databases represent uncertain data and support conditioning on observations, joint-distribution recovery, and hypothesis management. **Upsilon-DB** uses U-relational hypothesis databases and a design-by-synthesis pipeline for predictive analytics, while **PaleoDeepDive** produces probabilistic databases from scientific and palaeontological data. These systems connect uncertain observations with scientific-hypothesis synthesis and prediction.

The community also addresses practical data acquisition and analysis. **ArchiveSpark** enables distributed web-archive processing, corpus construction, metadata indexing, and dataset derivation. Web search supports fact finding, information gathering, journalism studies, and imputation through keyword generation and value extraction.

Spatial crowdsourcing focuses on task assignment among workers, including distance-based or binary utility and online heuristics. Related work studies automated and guided team formation, faultline minimization, and organizational coordination. Markov-chain models support keyword-relationship discovery, sequential prediction, web navigation, and order inference, while causal-inference frameworks use structural equations and observational data.

8b8e8f4e196022bc13cea0c6fcc0d9d3d1907eae.text:
## Relational Data Management, Learning, and Query Processing

This community centers on methods for exploiting relational structure in data management and machine learning. Functional dependencies provide schema-related information, support dependency-graph models, causal reasoning, data imputation, aggregate queries, design-theoretic synthesis, and optimal subset repair. Related concepts include equality-generating, tuple-generating, conditional, and ontology functional dependencies.

AC/DC performs structure-aware learning over relational databases by decomposing optimization into aggregates over joins and using sparse and factorized computation. It supports factorization machines and principal component analysis, and is benchmarked against libFM and TensorFlow. Factorization machines also support knowledge tracing, incorporating student, item, attempt, knowledge-component, and linked-data features.

Query processing is represented by LevelHeaded, an in-memory architecture for business-intelligence and linear-algebra queries using worst-case-optimal joins. It is evaluated against systems including LogicBlox, MonetDB, Hyper, and Intel MKL. Leapfrog Triejoin, NPRR, and factorized computation likewise address efficient join or aggregate processing.

The community also covers uncertainty and curation: probabilistic databases represent uncertain data, while web-based data imputation combines functional dependencies, keyword generation, web search, and value extraction. Category theory, functorial semantics, algebraic data integration, declarative languages, and database mapping systems provide formal foundations for schemas, instances, mappings, and relational learning.

3e1902bc832a931059b86bb3e4dcd10664a9952e.text:
## Query Evaluation, Conjunctive Queries, and Structural Tractability

This community centers on query evaluation and answering, especially conjunctive queries, unions of conjunctive queries, ontology-mediated queries, and queries over databases, graphs, probabilistic data, and incomplete information. Core theoretical concerns include NP-completeness, undecidability, data complexity, polynomial-time tractability, and enumeration with polynomial delay or constant delay.

Query structure is analyzed through hypergraphs and query graphs, using treewidth, fractional hypertree width, submodular width, dependency weighted count, free-connexity, semantic acyclicity, and hypergraph or simplicial decompositions. These measures explain tractable evaluation, compressed results, and efficient enumeration. ICG-Datalog supports linear-time evaluation on bounded-treewidth structures and captures conjunctive queries with bounded-width simplicial decompositions; CFG-Datalog supports query evaluation in related settings.

Other methods include query decomposition, reduction rules, color coding, linear programming, factorized representations, data factorisation, duplicate elimination, and enumeration algorithms. Document spanners, regular spanners, regex formulas, and information extraction languages address structured extraction. Existential rules, guarded and warded TGDs, description logics, and OBDA constraints support ontology-mediated answering and knowledge-base construction. Systems and tools include MVDB, FDB, PiWD, DeepDive, LARA, Mizar, Coq, and parallel query processing frameworks.

1cf9c66d30af223d20565778550139b040f7599b.text:
## Community Report: Query Evaluation and Structural Complexity

This community centers on query evaluation, especially conjunctive queries, unions of conjunctive queries, positive relational algebra, and probabilistic query evaluation over relational and probabilistic data. Query structure is modeled with query hypergraphs and analyzed using treewidth, hypertree width, fractional hypertree width, generalized hypertree width, submodular width, and dependency weighted count.

A major theme is tractability through decomposition and structural restrictions. Query decomposition, hypergraph decompositions, simplicial decompositions, semantic acyclicity, free connexity, and bounded treewidth support efficient evaluation, enumeration, or compressed results. ICG-Datalog provides linear-time evaluation on bounded-treewidth structures and captures conjunctive queries with bounded-width simplicial decompositions; CFG-Datalog and alternating automata support other evaluation approaches. Fixed-parameter tractability and parameterized complexity describe additional guarantees, while W[1]-hardness marks limits.

The community also studies query answering under inequalities, negation, existential rules, ontology mediation, constraints, and model checking. Parallel query processing addresses one-round algorithms, per-processor load, and data skew.

Related systems and methods include factorised databases and factorized representations, MVDB, FDB, PiWD, StreetX, quasi-succinct indexes, and offline compilation. XML and XPath evaluation, RDF data, data exchange, model counting, and probabilistic methods broaden the application scope.

7ac4320b80dc1910b17b401b09961234420499ff.text:
## Query Complexity, Databases, and Structural Decomposition

This community centers on conjunctive and join queries evaluated over databases, including probabilistic and uncertain data. Query hypergraphs and hypergraph decompositions expose structural properties such as treewidth, fractional/generalized hypertree width, submodular width, semantic acyclicity, and free-connexity. These measures guide query decomposition, join algorithms, ranked enumeration, compressed results, and tractable evaluation.

A major theme is output and communication complexity: AGM and GLVV bounds, worst-case size bounds, query-result size, data skew, per-processor load, communication rounds, and one-round or worst-case-optimal parallel algorithms. Leapfrog Triejoin, NPRR, SIMD methods, and parallel query processing support these goals.

Constraints—including functional and equality-generating dependencies, keys, tuple-generating dependencies, and integrity constraints—shape query answering, database design, and repair. Transaction repair and constrained repair address inconsistent databases, while `CERTAINTY(Q)` studies whether every repair satisfies a conjunctive query, with P, FO, and coNP-complete cases.

The community also covers ontology-mediated query answering through existential rules, nonrecursive Datalog rewriting, and related Datalog formalisms. Probabilistic query evaluation studies conjunctive queries over probabilistic databases, while PANDA supports aggregate queries with functional dependencies. Category-theoretic and functorial data migration connects schema transformation with query replacement.

14da03b18776bb92bbc164e40f66bc239127af93.text:
## Community Report: Context-Aware Recommendation, Networks, and Uncertainty

This community centers on recommendation and search systems, network analysis, collective attention, and data-driven decision support.

Recommendation research includes a production **recommendation engine** deployed on a meta platform. It uses customer, product, and trip embeddings, matches food to flavour profiles, supports healthy-alternative recommendation, and provides explanations. Related food recommenders support meal, recipe, diet, ingredient-substitution, and healthy-food recommendation, using flavour profiles, health factors, recipe ratings, and online recipe collections. A context-aware embedding model improves product search by modeling both short- and long-term context, outperforming word-based relevance-feedback and context-aware models. Product search also includes multi-page search and purchase-history personalization.

Network and information research models collective attention, media attention and disregard, opinion propagation, and communication. The multiplex media network, based on 129 countries over 212 days, reveals skewed, hierarchical, and asymmetric relationships, including regional attention blocks. Collective attention relates to perceived credibility, polarization, concentration, and uncertainty; unsubstantiated claims can attract sustained attention.

Methods include graph signal processing, convolution, z-transforms, spectral representation, multifractal analysis, Granger causality, diffusion models, dynamic relation embeddings, heterogeneous edge embeddings, and Gaussian fuzzy sets. Other applications address cost subsidization for service adoption, clinical productivity using EHR data and VPU, and e-commerce knowledge graphs.

290c278baf047fb849fd4f32125dd564d5984cdb.text:
## Community Report: Adoption, Search, Data Mining, and Digital Services

This community spans methods and systems for adoption dynamics, search, streaming analytics, healthcare, and digital libraries.

**Adoption and diffusion:** Diffusion models explain service adoption and web-service life-cycle stages, informing investment decisions. Network externalities and heterogeneous user–service affinity create near-zero and near-one adoption equilibria. Cost subsidization addresses this chicken-and-egg problem, estimating minimum subsidy, duration, aggregate cost, and time to a target adoption; two-target subsidies maintain users with positive net utility.

**Search and similarity:** Diversified top-*k* search uses Div-A*, Div-DP, and Div-Cut. A framework applies sufficient/necessary stopping conditions and solves current diversification through A*, dynamic programming, or cut points. Streaming similarity self-joins handle unbounded streams with time-dependent similarity, minibatches, and an L2 index. SparseDTW computes optimal dynamic-time-warping distance.

**Popularity and prediction:** Phoenix-R, based on the minimum description length principle, predicts future popularity and is evaluated by RMSE. Ensemble learning predicts vaccination uptake using registry data and web-search frequencies.

**Mining and verification:** Serial episode discovery mines event sequences. Uncertain frequent-itemset mining may be outsourced to a service provider, with integrity verification ensuring result correctness.

**Clinical and digital infrastructure:** A clinical productivity system uses EHR data and VPU metrics, improving care quality and consistency. Fedora-based repository infrastructure supports interoperable web-based digital libraries, diverse digital collections, and an open-source release, through University of Virginia–Cornell collaboration.

270eda0dfa686e56628f222abbe9105b9d0878de.text:
## Community Report: Networks, Adoption, Retrieval, and Structured Analysis

This community links methods for analyzing social, information, and service networks with systems for retrieval, document processing, and event analysis.

Longitudinal analysis studies document samples, university-ranking systems (ARWU and QS Global University Rankings), genealogical networks, mating patterns, mood, and trolling exposure over time. RFID tracking and mobile-phone communication infer social structure, including consumption-based socioeconomic stratification and opinion evolution among networked agents. Genealogical networks are computationally inferred from historical records and support digital demography and genetics.

Service adoption is addressed through cost subsidization and diffusion models. Subsidies target adoption equilibria, minimum subsidy and duration, aggregate cost, and time to target adoption, while diffusion models characterize web-service life cycles and inform investment decisions.

Information retrieval emphasizes multi-stage systems with candidate generation, filtering, preliminary ranking, and reranking, balancing efficiency and effectiveness. Dynamic parameter prediction uses classifier cascades and pre-retrieval features to tune retrieval depth and approximate evaluation thresholds. Quality scores compare filtering with full evaluation.

Document structuring and text segmentation organize unordered documents into sections, using Hough transform, TextRank, and Universal Sentence Encoder. Multimodal quality recognition combines image and text feature extractors through Siamese networks. Finally, DancingLines analyzes cross-platform event popularity using time-series alignment and trend metrics on real-world datasets.

3756ad45851510500f40a958929fb1c0cf47140e.text:
## Community Report: Search, Adoption, Analytics, and Digital Systems

This community connects methods for search, recommendation, temporal analysis, and service adoption with applied clinical, repository, and data-mining systems.

Diversified top-k search uses similarity to balance relevance and result diversity. Its framework employs `sufficient()` and `necessary()` stopping conditions, while Div Search Current, Div A*, Div DP, and Div Cut provide solution methods evaluated on Enwiki and Reuters. Topical user profiling supports search, navigation, personalization, and recommendation paths; topical generalization uses the Wikipedia category graph to add broader labels.

Streaming similarity self-join addresses continuously arriving unbounded streams using minibatches, streaming algorithms, L2 indexing, and time-dependent similarity. SparseDTW, WDTW-CD, dynamic time warping, and piecewise linear recursion support time-series comparison.

Adoption research models network externalities, heterogeneous service affinity, and subscription costs. Cost subsidization targets equilibrium adoption, minimum subsidy, duration, aggregate cost, and time to target adoption. Diffusion models connect service life cycles with investment decisions.

Popularity studies use Phoenix-R and the minimum description length principle for future prediction, evaluated by RMSE, while ensemble learning combines behavioral, clinical, registry, and search-frequency signals.

Applications include clinical productivity decision support using EHR data and VPU, associated with care-quality and consistency improvements; Fedora-based interoperable digital libraries; uncertain frequent-itemset mining; serial episode discovery; and news community classification under concept drift.

8132a6dd6cc156a33631087817b8e657a44ee253.text:
## Recommendation, Explainability, and Adaptive Learning Systems

This community centers on recommender systems and recommendation quality, with matrix factorization, neural collaborative filtering, and deep neural networks as core approaches. These methods learn from implicit feedback, user/item features, and user–item interaction functions; matrix factorization models interactions through latent representations and can incorporate social or sequential information. Neural collaborative filtering extends this with multilayer perceptrons for nonlinear interactions.

Sparse and cold-start sequential recommendation is addressed by SPMC, which uses socially aware personalized Markov chains, recent activity sequences, and social relationships. Consumed item packs support user-based CIP-U, item-based CIP-I, and embedding-based DeepCIP recommenders, all of which support incremental updates and achieve competitive recommendation quality. DeepCIP uses word embeddings, while DeepCoNN and TransNets learn representations from review text; TransNets adds a target user–item-pair latent layer regularized toward review representations.

Explainable and entity-based recommendation uses Personalized PageRank to jointly rank items and knowledge-graph entities, producing explanations even when review text is unavailable. EB-SeqGANs connect energy functions with maximum-entropy imitation learning.

The community also covers multistakeholder recommendation, incorporating stakeholder interests into algorithms and evaluation. EASE-ML addresses automatic model selection and resource allocation in shared multi-tenant clusters using multi-armed bandits and Bayesian optimization to reduce regret, with evaluations including image-classification workloads and synthetic data.

fdb54f1d44c5d405a0f18abf65fdf58d0f2bd534.text:
### Data Integration, Metadata, and Association-Rule Mining

This community connects dataset discovery, metadata management, heterogeneous-data integration, and association-rule mining.

Association-rule mining analyzes metadata values and evaluates rules using support and confidence. Redundancy and pattern explosion motivate maximal non-redundant mining, post-mining pruning, subsumption, and substitution-based processes that reduce rule sets without information loss. Frequent and closed itemsets, minimal generators, equivalence classes, and disjunctive search spaces support compact representations; generalized association rules extend rules with disjunction and negation. These methods are applied to spatio-temporal tennis-ball trajectories for strategy analysis and player-performance improvement, and power recommendations in metadata systems.

Metadata recommendation is integrated with the CEDAR Workbench for metadata authoring and real-time recommendations. It uses ontology terms and association-rule mining and was evaluated on NCBI BioSample and EBI BioSamples metadata. Biological sample metadata supports biomedical experiments, but inconsistent fields, weak validation, and anomalies hinder standardization, search, and secondary dataset use.

Termite and Termite Join reduce integration effort across heterogeneous, unstructured, and differently schematized databases by learning embeddings and identifying related concepts. Categorical Query Language and CQL data migrations implement functorial data migration for integrating the Open Quantum Materials Database and supporting safer data sharing.

Dataset search/retrieval includes Google Dataset Search, entity-centric and tabular search, while sensor and business data integration supports IoT, Industry 4.0, manufacturing simulation, and ad hoc business queries.

b02ec71217906663d37ceaec2a71b65ecb3c84c7.text:
## Knowledge Bases, Association Mining, and Information Retrieval

This community connects knowledge-base analysis with association-rule mining, ranked retrieval, and information-theoretic evaluation. Knowledge bases support entity linking, knowledge extraction, inference rules, relationship explanation, and KB question answering; REX uses a knowledge base to explain entity connections, while CorText and Visone analyze and animate its historical development. Digital repositories maintain such evolving knowledge structures.

Association-rule mining enumerates and evaluates rules derived from frequent sets. Itemset pruning, itemset enhancement, post-mining pruning, and maximal non-redundant rule mining address pattern explosion and redundancy. Confidence, support, confidence boost, interestingness, and statistical significance assess rule quality, while type I and II errors highlight risks in rule search and evaluation. The frequency-confidence framework and open-source association mining tools support this process, including recommendation systems and buying-pattern analysis.

Ranking functions order results by relevance in ranked and vertical retrieval, using weighted scoring and criterion weights. Semantic matching, query embeddings, and document coherence further characterize relevance. Entropy and Shannon information provide efficiency, quality, novelty, and similarity measures; entropy-based analysis evaluates document coherence and user sessions at multiple levels. Together, these methods support information exploration, recommendation, and structured explanation.

28181f62b9b457cabbb03b1ecf0c081de2046f50.text:
## Network Embedding, Structural Identity, and Link Prediction

This community centers on network embedding and node representation learning: assigning graph nodes low-dimensional representations for downstream node classification, link prediction, and recommendation. Methods preserve network or graph structure, high-order proximity, node content, labels, or other properties.

Matrix factorization provides a unifying embedding perspective, integrating structural information, node content, label information, and high-order proximities. It also supports item recommendation and multi-label classification; recommender systems commonly evaluate it with RMSE, while movie-rating prediction uses iterative matrix factorization and the Koren integrated model.

Random-walk and sampling approaches include skip-gram with negative sampling, vertex-context sampling, and sequential vertex-to-context graphs for efficient or scalable training. Weighted network embedding uses weighted vertex-edge sampling and is evaluated on word similarity search. SNE represents signed networks with signed-type vectors and is compared with unsigned embedding models.

Structural identity is emphasized by struc2vec, which uses hierarchical similarities and multilayer graphs, and by LASAGNE, which uses local Approximate Personalized PageRank distributions for locality- and structure-aware embeddings. Link prediction estimates future links on benchmark and real-world network datasets, using neighborhood, friendship-maintenance, cross-link, and similarity features; top-k distance similarity, Adamic-Adar similarity, and supervised or unsupervised methods are evaluated by link-prediction accuracy.

783b38f2d36b7922aee8dbba5deed02eb091fd78.text:
## GraphRAG Research Community: Rules, Relevance, and Knowledge Exploration

This community centers on extracting, organizing, and evaluating knowledge from relational data, documents, and user activity.

**Association rule mining** enumerates rules from itemsets and frequent sets, using support and confidence. Itemset pruning, enhancement, and rule blocking reduce search space and redundancy, while confidence boost produces smaller, crisper rule sets. Statistical significance and type I/type II error analysis address false discoveries. The frequency-confidence framework and open-source association mining tools support evaluation and parameter-free mining.

**Knowledge bases** provide infrastructure for inference, knowledge extraction, relationship explanation, and question answering. REX uses a knowledge base to rank entity-relationship explanations with interestingness measures and delta-based computation.

**Information-theoretic methods** use entropy, Shannon information, and configurational information to assess efficiency, quality, document coherence, novelty, topic drift, and user similarity.

**TIMEMACHINE** generates knowledge-base timelines using web co-occurrence statistics, temporal and content diversity, submodular optimization, and performance guarantees.

For search and recommendation, semantic matching learns query and advertisement embeddings, supports advanced matching, and is evaluated through online and editorial relevance and incremental revenue. Ranking functions, blending, TF-IDF, and document coherence organize retrieval.

The community also includes process mining, event-log analysis, mobility systems, interactive knowledge maps, and graph-based detection of self-censorship.

5403b9816f5d8b2e57a217a80bab51e96182db11.text:
## Multimodal Retrieval, Document Processing, and Graph-Based Recommendation

This community connects nearest-neighbor search, multimodal retrieval, document understanding, social recommendation, and dynamic graph analysis.

**Multimodal retrieval** uses common or joint embedding spaces to compare text, images, audio, video, and learned track or artist representations. FGCrossNet learns fine-grained text, image, and audio features using classification, center, and ranking constraints; its benchmark includes bird subcategories, video, and audio. Canonical correlation analysis (CCA), including a neural CCA layer, learns correlated query and item projections and supports cross-modality and research-article recommendation. Applications include text-to-image, audio-to-sheet-music, and zero-shot retrieval.

**Nearest-neighbor methods** support retrieval and graph construction through spatial indexes, tree-like structures, multilayer Voronoi diagrams, approximate k-nearest-neighbor graphs, and ranking metrics. Graph hierarchies organize partitions into supergraphs or graph trees with sublinear tracing.

**Document systems** combine Hough-transform text segmentation, binarization, OCR, word spotting, and annotation for historical handwritten documents. TexT supports semi-automatic transcription and archival manuscript search.

**Social and graph applications** include interactive news recommendation using user-dependent interaction graphs, G-CNNs, attention-based LSTMs, and concentration features; Vent data supports emotion and temporal analysis. Dynamic graph anomaly detection combines Hopfield and memory networks for evolving networks.

b240aa4ff1ca6ea263278dee0effe80ec7d0a633.text:
## Community Report: Data-Driven Networks, Innovation, and Optimization

This community connects social-network diffusion, emotion analysis, scientific innovation, and operational decision-making.

In social networks, information and products spread through social connections. Multi-cascade influence maximization studies launching one cascade alongside existing cascades under the Independent Multi Cascade Model, using activation functions, heuristic seed selection, and data-dependent approximation ratios guided by upper and lower bounds. Its approximation hardness is established under the Exponential Time Hypothesis and a stated quasi-polynomial-time assumption. Product diffusion is modeled through linear update dynamics, product externalities, and competitive contagion.

The Vent dataset contains user posts and social connections, supporting emotion taxonomies, hierarchical emotion categories, temporal activity analysis, emotion networks, and affective landscapes. The Game of Thrones kills dataset supports kill networks and machine-learning-based kill prediction.

Machine learning and text analysis detect scientific innovation and measure scientific novelty. Research on the diversity innovation paradox links diversity with innovation while showing unequal adoption, recognition, and academic-career outcomes for gender and racial minorities; the doctoral-recipient dataset tracks these careers.

Finally, data mining and business analytics use operational data for data-driven decisions in container-terminal planning and management. Database management systems use cost-based query optimizers, plan enumeration, and cardinality estimation for analytic workloads.

e7216b2a9c7c54ef0c701f931ff7c538f064c697.text:
## Social Media Popularity and Scientific Impact

This community connects social-media analytics with scientometrics and research-impact measurement.

For **post popularity prediction**, a **dual attention model** uses image and caption information, while incorporating user environment and user-specific posting patterns. **Explicit attention** models image–caption pairs, and **implicit attention** models the user environment. An **Instagram post dataset**, collected from Instagram, supports prediction of popularity measured through **likes**; statistical analysis identifies image and caption factors influencing likes.

The community also examines emotion and performance. **Tweets** from microblogging sites contain fan reactions to a **cricket tournament**. **Emotion extraction**, supported by data mining, derives **fan emotions** from these tweets. **Correlation analysis** studies relationships between fan emotions and **player performance**, as well as download and citation statistics. Player performance is reported to influence **stock market performance**; brands sponsor tournament matches and endorse studied players.

In scientometrics—part of the **science of science** and encompassing **bibliometric analysis**—statistical analysis is applied to scientific publication data. **Europhysics Letters** provides a case study with download and citation statistics. Download statistics reflect publication popularity, while citation statistics indicate **academic impact**.

beeb0a43518253da42fb43509f32b7e7c849c0d4.text:
## Social Media Misinformation, Extremism, and Information Diffusion

This community centers on how online social networks—especially Twitter, Instagram, and YouTube—spread, classify, and counter misinformation, fake news, rumors, and extremist content.

Twitter provides datasets for studying the 2016 U.S. presidential election, fake-news links, Russian trolls, state-sponsored accounts, ISIS-related content, image activity, diplomacy, medical research, and local attitudes toward immigration. Causal modeling examines fake news’ influence on the election, while information-flow networks identify influential spreaders. Misinformation and fake news are closely related; rumor blocking seeks to limit their spread by launching positive cascades.

The **SemiPSM** framework detects pathogenic social-media accounts using semi-supervised causal inference, manifold regularization, and cascade information. A context-aware computational approach analyzes extremist content using religion as context. Related work examines online radicalization, alt-right activity, bots, Russian trolls, and information warfare.

YouTube recommendation analysis finds that the algorithm favors cable and mainstream news over independent channels, while discouraging radicalized-content recommendations. Hashtag research studies social signals, temporal patterns, semantic displacement, and large Instagram datasets. Automated text classification of *Fridays for Future* comments finds group cohesion and emotional attachment more common than solidarity.

Additional methods include knowledge-graph embeddings and a unified framework supporting inductive and transductive learning on attributed multiplex heterogeneous networks.

383a087567a4a71cb1ff8f4839983d65dda021ae.text:
## Social Media Dynamics, Collective Action, and Trust

This community examines online social networks—especially Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, Instagram, Google+, and 4chan—and how users, professional accounts, and spammers create, share, and evaluate content. Cross-posting activity, site-specific profile norms, profile-name reuse, and correlated identities across platforms are recurring themes.

Research analyzes popularity evolution, fame, audience engagement, voting behavior, upvoting and downvoting, retweet cascades, trending topics, and content propagation. Reddit popularity is measured through votes and comments, while temporal clustering identifies distinct popularity trajectories. Studies also examine mainstream and alternative news, including the spread of content from Reddit and 4chan to Twitter, alt-right communities, Gamergate, and election discussions involving Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump.

Key methods include measurement studies, crawling, clustering analysis, statistical machine learning, and measurement-based analysis. A Spatial Dirichlet Hawkes Process models streaming spatiotemporal data, estimates tweet locations, and discovers activity patterns in geolocated posts. A computational framework supports an open-source event detection tool and analyzes peaceful and violent collective action across time and geography.

Trust and safety topics include fake followers, link fraud, malicious content, abusive behavior, cyberbullying, hate, suspension mechanisms, and fraud multimodality. Other work studies political profiling, demographic bias, sentiment, selfies, and contrarian content recommendation using user and content polarity plus recommendation acceptance probability.

fa78d0c5fbb7c3197aa1fa83627f3931d4eb36db.text:
## Behance Analysis and Selfie-Based Sleep Prediction

This community links quantitative analysis of Behance, an online creative community for creative professionals, with research on sleep-condition prediction and demographic identification.

The Behance study examines factors attracting appreciations and followers to artworks. It considers gender, grayscale colors, and creative-professional activity: male users are associated with more appreciations and followers, while grayscale artworks receive fewer appreciations. Behance enables creative professionals to maintain relationships and showcase their artworks.

The selfie-based sleep condition prediction method uses facial cues from selfies to predict an individual’s sleep condition. It predicts sleep-deprived fatigue rate as an indirect measure, with sleep deprivation reflected by fatigue. Fatigue percentages are reported as higher for females than males, highest among the 0–20 age group, and highest among Caucasians, followed by Asians and African Americans.

Automatic demographic identification identifies subjects’ gender, age, and race, connecting these demographic concepts to differences in sleep-deprived fatigue rates. Overall, the community brings together social-media artwork analysis, demographic identification, and indirect sleep-condition assessment.

b66dc0c31a3f7a39eaeadd847160779cf35c7366.text:
## Association Mining, Metadata, and Personalized Graph Analysis

This community centers on association-rule mining and its evaluation. Rules are derived from frequent sets and itemsets, with itemset pruning, enhancement, and post-mining pruning addressing pattern explosion and redundancy. Support, confidence, confidence boost, statistical significance, and interestingness measures rank or filter rules; false-discovery rates and Type I/II errors highlight risks in rule search. Maximal non-redundant rule mining, irredundant rule bases, rule blocking, and substitution-based reduction seek compact rule sets. Applications include buying-pattern analysis, tennis-strategy analysis, and metadata recommendation. The open-source association-mining tool implements confidence boost, while the frequency-confidence framework provides traditional evaluation.

A second theme is biological-sample metadata. Biosample datasets store metadata whose fields and values may lack standardization, validation, and principled schemas; field clustering, metadata standardization, and schema methods support reuse. The metadata recommendation system uses association mining and was evaluated with NCBI Biosample metadata; Alexandria is associated with IBM Research.

Recommendation and user modeling address users and items through non-IID coupling, personalized attention, entity or playlist embeddings, and graph-based systems such as A-PGNN. These connect user behavior, reviews, clickstreams, opinions, and repositories to recommendation, cold-start, and social-network extraction tasks.

f3fb2358fb16d51e322031edb347cf907a742613.text:
## Recommendation Systems: Collaborative, Hybrid, and Knowledge-Aware Methods

This community centers on recommendation systems built from user–item interactions, collaborative filtering, and matrix factorization. Collaborative filtering uses implicit or explicit feedback for rating prediction and top-*N* recommendation, but faces cold users, non-profiled playlists, and infrequent songs. Matrix factorization provides a low-rank basis, while Regularized Multi-Embedding (RME) incorporates user and item embeddings for cold-start recommendation, improving Recall@5, NDCG@5/NDCG@20, and MAP@10.

Neural Personalized Embedding models personal preference and improves cold-user recommendation. RHC-PMF, RV-PMF, and RHCV-PMF combine ratings, helpfulness, centrality, views, and other implicit or explicit signals. User reliability and semi-supervised learning support personalized task recommendation and task matching.

Music recommender systems address playlist continuation through collaborative filtering, content-based recommendation, and hybrid playlist continuation models trained on labeled playlist-song pairs, including rare or unseen songs. Photo recommendation combines collaborative filtering with aesthetic features and deep style-transfer embeddings across 500px, Unsplash, and Adobe Behance.

Other applications include social, video-game, teammate, political-campaigning, and personalized task recommendation. Knowledge-base representation learning, heterogeneous entity embeddings, graph-based recommenders, and graph-query recommendation connect structured knowledge and item relationships to personalization and explanation. Evaluation uses MovieLens, Amazon reviews, Spotify playlists, and metrics such as Recall, NDCG, and MAP.

725aaf14fb48d4f4e8012e0d842e114067b63f2c.text:
## Data Marketplaces, Acquisition, and Sentiment-Aware Language Learning

This community connects data monetization and machine-learning infrastructure with language-processing tasks.

The proposed **data marketplace** targets monetization in the **Web of Data**, where commercial data has not broadly transitioned and traditional advertising is considered unsuitable. It serves **data providers** and **data customers**, with **FedMark** as a prototype and **DANCE** providing data-acquisition services. DANCE constructs a two-layer join graph during offline processing and uses Markov chain Monte Carlo for heuristic search. Acquisition is constrained by **data quality** and **budget**, while optimizing join informativeness and attribute correlation.

**Model-based pricing** prices machine-learning model instances rather than raw data. It supports seller revenue maximization, affordability, low runtime cost, and formal resistance to arbitrage; noise injection provides a concrete realization. The marketplace uses this framework to incentivize providers and enable customers to buy data transparently.

A second theme concerns language and representation learning. **ERMES** performs cross-lingual sentiment classification, transferring sentiment knowledge from English to label-scarce, imbalanced target languages. It uses emoji prediction to learn sentiment-aware representations and achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets. Entity embeddings, generated by a computer processor and stored in a feature registry, support multiple models and address redundancy and model decay.

Finally, extractive and abstractive summarization address information overload, using statistical and sentiment features to reduce redundancy and improve content coverage.

1b0a609853cef984ba02f24ac2e51e982ca42370.text:
## Online Social Networks: Propagation, Trust, and Privacy

This community examines online social networks and social media as systems for interaction, knowledge acquisition, influence, and information propagation. Facebook, Reddit, YouTube, Digg, 4chan, and related datasets support studies of friendship graphs, comments, likes, popularity, political discourse, and collective debates.

A major theme is the spread and evaluation of misinformation, fake news, rumors, disinformation, conspiracy news, junk news, and false information. Methods and systems include fact checking, information credibility evaluation (ICE), Hoaxy, Truthy, sentiment and opinion mining, argumentation mining, topic extraction, and network-aided sentiment detection. Cascade dynamics are analyzed through cascade size, viral cascades, cascade-generating functions, Hawkes processes, stochastic diffusion models, and cascade prediction.

The community also studies influence, persuasion, selective exposure, confirmation bias, echo chambers, polarized communities, partisan sharing, and opinion influence campaigns. Social bots, Russian trolls, Sybil accounts, and like farms motivate Sybil account detectors, SybilFence, reputation manipulation analysis, and suspicious-link detection.

Privacy is addressed through privacy settings, privacy preferences, privacy-aware data partitioning, policy negotiation, and cross-network account matching. Structural diversity, node embeddings, community identification, temporal analysis, and sampling methods support analysis of large-scale social networks and their evolving content.

2b8f5598c565bc506545efffb4161cfe27f0d245.text:
## Online Social Networks: Information, Influence, and Privacy

This community centers on online social networks and social media systems—including Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, Digg, 4chan, and social bots—as environments for interaction, information consumption, and propagation. Key topics include misinformation, fake news, rumors, conspiracy theories, hate speech, media bias, echo chambers, polarized communities, selective exposure, and partisan or mixed sharing.

Information propagation is studied through viral cascades, cascade size, cascade dynamics, popularity, influence, and cascade prediction. Methods include stochastic diffusion models, cascade generating functions, quantitative cascade analysis, limited-attention alpha centrality, influence prediction, and influence-backbone analysis. Structural diversity, structural homophily, and common neighborhood signatures examine how network structure relates to links and diffusion.

Sentiment analysis and opinion mining address positive and negative sentiment, opinion polarity, majority sentiment detection, political discourse, and persuasion. Network-aided sentiment detection and collaborated opinion mining combine textual content with network structure; fact checking and information credibility evaluation address false information.

Facebook is especially prominent: studies examine comments, video and scientific-news consumption, conspiracy and fake news, echo chambers, structural diversity, like farms, influence bots, and data leakage. Datasets include Facebook profiles and friendship graphs, YouTube videos, Reddit networks, Digg follower graphs, customer reviews, and geolocalized call records. Privacy settings, privacy-aware data partitioning, privacy-policy negotiation, and security protocols address information protection, while SybilFences and Sybil-account detectors study platform abuse.

626941528137f1e65218e2bdd4e015b4900b2559.text:
## XML Data Management, Schema Mappings, and Query Evaluation

This community spans XML warehousing, data exchange, query answering, and compressed indexing.

XML data warehouses use dimensional modeling, multidimensional XML data, complex hierarchies, join indexes, and query-performance optimization for decision-support XQuery. The XWeB benchmark generates scalable warehouses, extends support for complex hierarchies, and evaluates summarizability processing. XOLAP algebra provides a framework for analytical XQuery and performance optimization, while native XML DBMSs offer management with limited performance.

Schema mapping connects source and target schemas through source-to-target constraints, GAV/GLAV dependencies, target constraints, EGDs, and weakly acyclic target TGDs. ABD mappings induce ABD semantics, supporting results for solution existence, solution checking, UCQ evaluation, and certain-answer evaluation. Data exchange addresses inference-based semantics, exchange repairs, weak acyclicity, and constrained target schemas. SPARQL2XQuery accesses XML datasets and uses XS2OWL to map OWL ontologies and XML Schemas.

Query research covers UCQ enumeration, polynomial or fixed-parameter tractable delay, consistent answers, XR-certain answers, stable models, and disjunctive logic programs.

Compression research targets XML and inverted indexes using grammar/DAG compression, run-length and gap encoding, universal indexes, and SIMD algorithms such as GroupSimple, GroupScheme, Group-AFOR, and Group-PFor, evaluated on TREC and Wikipedia datasets for speed and space.

d002b5f23c7f4b9fee41bc5c0276490d4c3ef605.text:
## Distributed Clustering and Privacy Amplification

This community focuses on distributed density-based clustering and privacy amplification in distributed systems.

**Distributed density-based clustering** operates on distributed data, which may be heterogeneous. It considers the shapes of local clusters and provides a distributed approach to density-based clustering while reducing communication overhead. Local clusters have potentially relevant shapes, making shape-aware clustering important across distributed settings.

The community also examines **privacy amplification methods**. These methods amplify privacy, require only a limited number of local operations, and achieve privacy amplification with moderate communication overhead. This is significant because data exchange causes communication overhead in distributed systems.

Privacy amplification may improve security and privacy in systems based on **locally trusted relations**, while distributed systems may themselves rely on such relations. Overall, the entities connect two complementary concerns: efficient clustering of distributed and heterogeneous data, and privacy-preserving processing with limited local computation and controlled communication.

94db9d7598695a3a1ced43b302cf4c75a73823be.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: Question Answering, Anomaly Detection, and Cultural Analysis

This community covers three major research areas.

**Question answering over RDF** is addressed by a metasystem that reuses six existing question-answering systems. It uses question features as classification inputs and is evaluated on QALD-6. Machine learning supports its construction, and the metasystem outperforms the best single system by 14% in F-measure. DBpedia, extracted from Wikipedia, provides the basis for an entity-search test collection.

**Anomaly and breach detection** focus on log data, TCP dumps, and evolving tensor streams. DenseAlert incrementally detects anomalous dense subtensors and guarantees a lower bound on maintained density, while DenseStream incrementally maintains and updates dense subtensors faster than batch algorithms. Retweet events form an evolving tensor stream. Graph analysis, supported by graph databases and combined with time-series databases, detects breaches and affected components in simulated and real-world logs. Attack profiles, derived from adapted kill-chain mechanisms, support detection of simulated attacks and advanced persistent threats.

**Wikipedia analysis** examines world literature, multilingual language versions, and an implicit literary canon. The Observatory of World Literature investigates representation and bias, while DBpedia data supports writer identification and evaluation of identification methods.

dac3dd09c75329975afc86faed27a630034210e4.text:
## Community Report: XML Data Management, Graph Security, and Dynamic Networks

This community centers on XML and multi-model data management. UDBMS is envisioned as a unified platform supporting semi-structured, graph, NoSQL, and flexible-schema data, with unified query processing, indexing, and cross-model transaction guarantees. VIP2P disseminates XML documents through a structured DHT, using distributed materialized XML views and both subscription and snapshot query modes.

XML query research covers exact and preference queries, evaluation plans, XPath, and schema inference. Unranked data tree automata, enriched with epsilon transitions, capture vertical XPath and provide XPath satisfiability procedures with decidable emptiness. XML warehouses address complex hierarchies, summarizability, dimensional modeling, query optimization, and join indexes; XWeb provides scalable benchmark data. Grammar and dictionary-based compression, including GraphZip and Lempel–Ziv methods, exploit repetitive XML or graph structure.

A second major theme is graph security and evolution. Sybil identities threaten e-communities, consensus, and governance through social-edge solicitation and active attacks. Trust graphs, conductance-based expansion, negative feedback, and Sybil-resilient defenses limit corrupt identities. Byzantine agreement applies when the Byzantine fraction is below one third.

Dynamic-network work includes snapshots, link prediction, embeddings, and time-aware gradient attacks that rewire links to hide target links. Transaction networks connect to multilayer patent networks, while Trans2Vec extracts address features.

b80d479e53a0df7d11cf6006e44fe23ff7354ed0.text:
## XML Data Integration, Warehousing, and Compressed Indexing

This community connects XML data management across schema mapping, data exchange, analytics, warehousing, and indexing.

Schema mapping links source and target schemas through source-to-target constraints, GAV/GLAV dependencies, target TGDs, and EGDs. Annotated bidirectional dependencies (ABDs) induce ABD semantics, supporting solution-existence, solution-checking, UCQ, and certain-answer evaluation. Inference-based semantics addresses certain-answer anomalies, while XR-certain answers relate to stable models. Weak acyclicity provides decidability-related results. SPARQL2XQuery translates SPARQL into XQuery over XML datasets, using XS2OWL to map XML Schemas and OWL ontologies.

XML data warehouses and XWeB support scalable warehousing, complex hierarchies, multidimensional XML data, and summarizability processing. XOLAP algebra extends XQuery for analytical and OLAP queries, including a pattern-tree-based rollup operator. Query optimization uses join indexes and XML materialized-view selection; native XML DBMS support remains limited in performance.

A second theme is compact indexing and compression. Universal indexes compress inverted indexes and differential lists using gap or run-length encoding. SIMD methods such as Simple, Scheme, AFOR, PFD, and S4-BP128-D4 target fast integer compression, with S4-BP128-D4 decoding at as little as 0.7 CPU cycles per integer. Grammar, DAG, Lempel–Ziv, and run-length compression address repetitive XML and versioned document collections, while compressed self-indexes trade indexing speed for integrated storage.

4108a8495d6cb18a5e34b502bd6fc96eabe47473.text:
## Query Evaluation, Graph Paths, and Scalable Relational Systems

This community studies query evaluation across probabilistic databases, graph databases, document spanners, and relational or linear-algebraic systems. Conjunctive queries, unions of conjunctive queries (UCQs), and navigational queries are central: conjunctive-query evaluation has NP-completeness and W[1]-hardness lower bounds, while UCQs can achieve polynomial or fixed-parameter tractable delay when query size or atom count is bounded.

Probabilistic query evaluation over binary-signature probabilistic instances can be viewed as probabilistic graph homomorphism or constraint-satisfaction problems. Combined-complexity analyses use d-DNNF lineage compilation, η-acyclic lineages, and graded DAGs; the X-property characterizes tractable constraint-satisfaction cases.

Context-free path querying uses context-free grammars and can reduce evaluation to matrix transitive closure, with relational query and single-path semantics. Matrix multiplication supports this computation and also represents join-and-aggregation tasks.

Regex formulas connect document spanners, relational algebra, and conjunctive queries, but even acyclic and γ-acyclic queries remain hard; exponentially many tuples can lead to NP-completeness.

LARA unifies relational and linear algebra operations. LARADB implements LARA operators as range iterators in Apache Accumulo, a Google BigTable implementation, and can outperform native MapReduce integration for smaller-scale matrix multiplication.

dd16908e5f7c11e460489509ac0853ba7dc3b86a.text:
**Community Report: Utility Mining, Stream Processing, Privacy, and Decision Support**

This community spans efficient pattern mining, data-stream systems, privacy-preserving linkage, diagnostic support, and feedback-driven decision making.

ProUM is a projection-based method for discovering high-utility sequential patterns in time-ordered sequence data. It generates utility arrays, uses sequence-extension utility as a pruning bound, and applies pruning strategies to reduce memory usage and execution time, achieving strong scalability. Utility mining also addresses itemset-based data.

BriskStream is an in-memory stream-processing system for shared-memory multicore architectures. It introduces RLAS, an execution-plan optimization paradigm that uses NUMA distance, heuristics, and branch-and-bound strategies to optimize producer–consumer operator placement. BriskStream improves scalability and throughput over distributed stream-processing systems.

Proof of Execution is a consensus protocol implemented in ResilientDB. It combines speculative execution and out-of-order processing to reduce Byzantine-fault-tolerance costs and client latency, achieving up to 86% higher throughput than existing protocols.

Privacy-preserving record linkage integrates masked sensitive information; its multiparty extension uses incremental clustering and record clusters, evaluating linkage quality and scalability, including healthcare applications.

Diagnostic systems use historic cases, clinical guidelines, biomedical literature, physician observations, and heuristics. Related work models sequential decision making through utility maximization, feedback, exploration, and exploitation to anticipate follower preferences in Twitter and Reddit data.

9b3de642e8f0e6e91f34d77fb09e0891e6509011.text:
## Graph Analytics for Sampling, Streaming, and Anomaly Detection

This community centers on scalable analysis of static, evolving, and streaming graphs. **Network sampling** includes node, edge, topology-based, randomized, and graph-induction methods, supporting network exploration, expansion, and analysis of static or continuously changing graphs. **Wedge sampling** provides fast, accurate estimates of clustering coefficients, triadic measures, and uniform or directed triangle counts, with probabilistic error estimates and time–accuracy tradeoffs.

For graph streams, **frugal streaming** offers one-memory and two-memory algorithms for low-memory quantile estimation, including multi-group streams and HTTP traces. **Neighborhood-aware graph sampling** targets label-density estimation in NoSQL graph databases, providing unbiased estimators and convergence guarantees.

A second major theme is anomaly detection. **StreamSpot**, spectral anomaly detection, regression-based online detection, AMEN, DenseAlert, and the self-feeding process address real-time, attributed-graph, or dense-subtensor anomalies. Corrupted observations can reduce detection performance, while observation fusion can recover it. Applications include smart-meter consumption, anomalous product reviews, and rating manipulation, where binomial regression identifies reviewers deviating from majority opinion.

**Apache Spark** supports distributed processing for evolving graphs and implements systems such as Portal, Parallel MLPCD, and Parallel ALID. Portal additionally enables scalable, temporal, exploratory querying through alternative physical representations and partitioning strategies.

ec6dfbcba6f296012a16324d59a0051caae3b394.text:
## Graph Analytics, Route Querying, and Temporal Motifs

This community covers graph modeling, network analysis, route querying, and motif counting.

**Graph operator modeling** uses graph similarity—especially degree-distribution-based similarity—to model multiple graph operators from input graphs rather than repeatedly executing them. It achieves high modeling accuracy and major speedups over brute-force execution, with evaluations on real-world, synthetic, and other graph datasets. Synthetic graphs imitate real-world networks, including power-law degree distributions.

For sequenced route querying, **StarKOSR** extends routes using an A*-style search and heuristic estimates of remaining cost, while **PruningKOSR** prunes route extensions using dominance relationships. Both solve top-k optimal sequenced route querying, ranking routes by total cost; hop labeling can improve the efficiency of both methods and supports shortest-path querying.

A **sampling framework**, layered over exact counting algorithms, enables fast, memory-efficient approximate frequency estimation, achieving one-to-two-orders-of-magnitude speedups across datasets. It estimates counts of **temporal motifs**, which extend motifs with temporal edge ordering, including temporal star motifs. Temporal star-motif counting is NP-complete.

The **Venmo** peer-to-peer payment network provides a case study of offline social interaction through financial transactions. Its analysis examines structure and evolution using connectivity, density, degree distributions, and clustering coefficient; the giant component eventually contains 99.9% of nodes, and the clustering coefficient reaches 0.2.

6562a4d15517c3e2d1e8818e105964772c84a163.text:
## Graph Analytics for Evolving, Streaming, and Sampled Networks

This community focuses on scalable analysis of static, evolving, and streaming graphs, emphasizing network sampling, anomaly detection, clustering, and change-point detection.

Sampling methods include node, edge, randomized, topology-based, neighborhood-aware, and graph-induction approaches. Wedge sampling provides fast, probabilistic estimates of clustering coefficients, triangles, and other triadic measures, with time–accuracy tradeoffs. Neighborhood-aware graph sampling offers unbiased, convergent estimates of node and edge label densities in live networks, offline datasets, and NoSQL graph databases. Frugal streaming supplies one- and two-memory algorithms for quantile estimation under strict per-group memory limits.

For anomaly detection, StreamSpot processes heterogeneous graph streams edge by edge for advanced persistent-threat detection, while spectral anomaly detection, regression-based online detection, AMEN, and normality-based neighborhood analysis address anomalous behavior and attributed graphs. Applications include smart-meter consumption and opinion-spam or rating-deviation detection.

Evolving-graph analysis is supported by Portal, which provides temporal selection, exploratory querying, physical representations, and partitioning strategies. Apache Spark supplies distributed processing, including Spark Streaming and Lambda-based systems. Change-point detection combines generalized hierarchical random graph models with Bayesian hypothesis tests, while equation-free and coarse-graining frameworks study evolving-network dynamics and structurally dense subgroups.

da3edb108ec24776b56323264b85d818c8c52dee.text:
## Graph Inference, Consistency, and Distributed Social Systems

This community connects network inference, graph structure analysis, distributed community detection, recommendation, and replicated data consistency.

**Network inference** recovers unknown or weighted-undirected topologies from grouped data and snapshots of consensus dynamics, including under uncertain parameters. The hub model assumes each observed group has a leader and is demonstrated on congressional senators, literary characters, and North American flora. D2PRI infers disease-infection networks using data and power-law priors. Additive and multiplicative risk models efficiently predict cascade length, duration, and activation risk.

**Graph analysis and social applications** include StructMatrix, which combines structure detection with adjacency-matrix visualization and relationship features for large Wikipedia and DBLP graphs. LoCEC classifies user relationships and communities through parallel processing on the WeChat network. Distributed community detection uses 2 Choices Dynamics for dynamic random graphs and social opportunistic networks; Sarve applies this modeling to conference-session recommendation.

**Consistency and replication** span strong, eventual, and bounded consistency. MDCC provides strong consistency through optimistic commits without a master, while DConssandra trades consistency against latency using staged replication and user-specified bounds. Spinnaker combines key-range partitioning, three-way replication, Paxos, and a transactional get-put API. Improve3C addresses consistency repair; CRDT sets, adaptive consistency, and delivery guarantees connect consistency with determinism and exactly-once processing. Skyline and aggregate skyline joins support multi-criteria querying.

0d3dc8007c3d8257396568602b022871ef746ec7.text:
## Distributed Data, Graph Analytics, and Consistency

This community centers on scalable database systems, graph analytics, replication, and adaptive performance management. Apache Accumulo provides distributed NoSQL storage, scalable warehousing, real-time ingestion, responsive querying, and server-side sparse matrix multiplication through the D4M 2.0 schema. Graphulo builds graph analytics from matrix primitives, while Vertica, GraphLab, Distributed GraphLab, Giraph, and GraphLab PowerGraph support iterative, vertex-centric, relational, and neighborhood-based graph analysis.

Several systems address multi-model and heterogeneous data. UDBMS proposes unified models, indexes, query processing, and cross-model transaction guarantees for semi-structured and NoSQL data. RDF graph alignment uses graph bisimulation to reconcile entity identity, blank nodes, and ontology evolution across evolving curated datasets.

Consistency and fault tolerance are major concerns. MDCC provides strong consistency with optimistic commits across data centers, while adaptive consistency, partial quorum replication, probabilistic bounded staleness, asynchronous replication, and CRDT-based methods explore relaxed guarantees. Distributed GraphLab combines consistency with pipelined locking and versioning; Shark offers fault-tolerant, column-oriented, in-memory analytics with dynamic replanning.

Performance management includes RITA’s Binary Integer Program for divergent index designs, online workload monitoring, load balancing, and elastic reconfiguration. H2O uses resource availability and unused workstation capacity for autonomic placement and planning, while topology discovery reconstructs sparse network structure using shortest- and second-shortest-path measurements.

13f6888061b0807a1b71460128c75a5d08a7be48.text:
### Community Report: Distributed Data, Graph Analytics, and Adaptive Database Systems

This community centers on distributed databases, graph analytics, replication, consistency, and workload-aware optimization.

Apache Accumulo is a distributed NoSQL and relaxed-consistency system supporting scalable warehousing, real-time ingestion, responsive querying, and server-side sparse matrix multiplication. Graphulo builds graph analytics on these matrix primitives. Graph analytics also includes iterative, graph-relational, one-hop neighborhood, and node-similarity workloads, evaluated with systems such as Vertica, Giraph, GraphLab/PowerGraph, and GraphBLAS.

Several systems address scalable analytics: Shark combines MapReduce-like execution, distributed memory, column-oriented in-memory storage, and dynamic mid-query replanning for complex SQL analytics and fault-tolerant recovery. H2O uses resource availability and unused workstation capacity for autonomic placement and query planning. UDBMS provides unified query processing, indexing, flexible schemas, and cross-model transaction guarantees for semi-structured and NoSQL data.

Replication research spans strong and eventual consistency. MDCC provides strong consistency through optimistic commit without a master, while supporting data-center outages. Methods include partial quorum replication, asynchronous and delta replication, probabilistically bounded staleness, adaptive consistency, and staged replication.

RITA performs online workload monitoring and binary-integer-program index tuning, generating divergent designs for load balancing and replica failures. Additional analytical themes include query-plan optimization, graph embedding, topology discovery, and edit-distance methods for comparing strings, data values, and graph-related structures.

cd245e57c2d3001389fdd2ce9331103653e1c01d.text:
## Community Report: Consistency, Graph Communities, and Social Analytics

This community centers on distributed data consistency and replication. MDCC uses an optimistic commit protocol to provide strong consistency without a master or partitioning, while sustaining data-center outages; it offers throughput and latency similar to eventually consistent quorum protocols. Spinnaker combines key-based range partitioning, three-way replication, a transactional get-put API, and Paxos, with read performance comparable to eventually consistent stores. DConssandra uses staged replication and user-specified latency bounds to trade replica consistency for access latency. Related work covers CRDT sets, partial quorum replication, probabilistically bounded staleness, delta replication, and delivery guarantees including exactly-once semantics.

A second theme is distributed and dynamic community detection. Distributed protocols recover planted partitions in sparse, disconnected dynamic graphs under a probability-ratio condition and logarithmic time. Two-choices dynamics supports detection in dynamic random graphs and social opportunistic networks. LoCEC classifies real-world relationship types using community classification and parallel processing on WeChat data.

Graph analysis and interaction applications include StructMatrix for large-scale adjacency-matrix visualization and structure detection on Wikipedia and DBLP graphs; SARVE recommends conference presentation sessions using participant characteristics and Pearson correlation; and social-cue field experiments examine effects on ad clicks, advertised connections, and ad performance. Skyline methods address multi-criteria decisions, including dynamic, join, aggregate, and k-dominance queries.

5e679a717d90cbbb4738abb12b0c9e5dbe36083d.text:
## Recommendation, Privacy, and Scalable Sequential Modeling

This community covers point-of-interest (POI) recommendation, location-privacy preference recommendation, shared-account cross-domain sequential recommendation, and candidate retrieval.

For POI recommendation in location-based social networks, geographical information and check-in data support personalization, although check-in data are often sparse. Logistic matrix factorization (LGMF) fuses a local geographical model using users’ geographic profiles, main activity regions, and location popularity. Carefully tuned matrix factorization is a strong baseline and can outperform reported newly proposed methods; standardized benchmarks and extensive baseline tuning are emphasized.

Location-privacy preference recommendation predicts whether users may release location information at particular places and times, supporting privacy decisions. Integrated privacy datasets evaluate accuracy, while local differential privacy provides a formal guarantee. Preference Mover’s Distance, an Earth Mover’s Distance–based user distance, remains effective with sparse data.

IDSR is an end-to-end sequential recommender that mines dynamic intents from behavior sequences and uses an intent-aware diversity-promoting loss, improving recommendation diversity and achieving comparable or superior accuracy. In shared-account cross-domain sequential recommendation, ψ-Net variants (Net I and Net II) construct role-specific and cross-domain representations and are evaluated with MRR on simulated Amazon and Smart TV datasets.

Finally, Synthonet represents users with retrieval keys; similarity search and actor-critic learning support efficient candidate retrieval, addressing the scalability challenge of deep-learning recommenders.

43b96bb332505e2afc43161bc2b7ea7b001aedc0.text:
## Recommender Systems: Methods, Challenges, and Evaluation

This community centers on recommender systems and the recommendation task, including personalized, top‑N, ranking, rating prediction, session-based, sequential, social, cross-domain, POI, and online-advertising recommendation. Systems learn from explicit ratings, implicit feedback, user–item interactions, preferences, behavior, and side information such as item content and social relations.

Collaborative filtering remains foundational, especially matrix factorization, matrix completion, user- and item-based methods, Bayesian personalized ranking, collaborative ranking, latent-factor models, and negative sampling. Content-based filtering, hybrid recommender systems, ensemble learning, metric learning, and representation learning combine behavioral and content signals. Deep learning methods include recurrent neural networks, attention mechanisms, autoencoders and variational autoencoders, graph neural networks, neural graph collaborative filtering, transfer learning, and deep reinforcement learning. Markov chains and recurrent Poisson factorization address sequential or temporal dynamics; hyperbolic space and item/user embeddings support representation learning.

Major challenges are data sparsity, cold-start and item-cold-start problems, popularity bias, information overload, noise, and bias disparity. Explainable recommendation addresses explainability, while diversity and novelty complement accuracy. Offline evaluation uses ratings, NDCG, recommendation performance and quality, diversity, novelty, and cross-validation. MovieLens, Last.fm, Epinions, Amazon, Netflix, and benchmark datasets support evaluation of systems such as Conet, DRR, IARN, Seer, and WebAPIRec.

0cb63973d4a50e951cf710e1e0ed70e045a7db5d.text:
## Recommender Systems, Fairness, and Social Influence

This community centers on personalized and sequential recommender systems, including movie recommender systems, recommendation engines, and big-data architectures for heterogeneous data. Systems use item content, user profiles, collective behavior, social networking information, and social influence to generate recommendation lists and explanation services.

GATE is a personalized-recommendation method addressing sparse implicit feedback and heterogeneous data. Its neural gating structure combines word-level attention over item text, neighbor-level attention over item neighborhoods, binary ratings, and fused hidden representations. A semantics-aware autoencoder builds user profiles and supports a recommendation engine.

Fairness is represented by bias disparity, provider-side fairness, provider diversification, and provider coverage. FAR re-ranks recommendation lists while balancing ranking quality with provider fairness and personalized user tolerance. Re-ranking algorithms reduce bias disparity, though recommender systems may amplify data bias; synthetic and real-world data support evaluation. Ranking algorithms are assessed using out-of-sample accuracy, while recommendation effectiveness and user satisfaction measure outcomes. Explanation services may improve satisfaction, and A/B testing validates results.

Reinforcement learning, including Deep Q Networks, supports recommendation and learns interview-question sequences. Social influence methods detect peer effects from observational data and predict event-cascade trajectories, evaluated on Higgs boson rumors spreading through Twitter and U.S. legislation co-sponsorship cascades over shared campaign-donor networks.

7d620805786c6516de9a53a354fc48569b67efa6.text:
## Sequential Recommendation, Rating Prediction, and Research Impact

This community centers on recommender systems that model user behavior, preferences, item popularity, intent, and consumption trends over time. Sequential recommendation uses behavioral and context sequences, including product-category information, with seq2seq translation architectures. RNS is a neural sequential recommender combining hierarchical attention-over-attention with aspect-aware user and item representations to capture long-term preferences and short-term patterns.

Sequential skip prediction models skips within music-listening sessions using acoustic features, interaction logs, track embeddings, and encoder–decoder or Multi-RNN architectures. Multi-RNN encodes the first half of a session, predicts skips in the second half, and achieves mean average accuracy of 0.641 and first-skip accuracy of 0.807.

Rating prediction includes collaborative filtering and low-rank matrix completion over user–item rating matrices. Related methods include TMF, FARP, and IFWMF; FARP targets tail users and items. Skewed rating distributions and item cold start affect accuracy. Hybrid, content-based, ontology-based, and review-semantic systems provide alternatives or improvements, while synthetic feedback loops combine recommenders with virtual users.

Additional methods learn metric-based user and item representations, jointly exploit textual contents and item co-clicks, and encode product-category relations. Finally, long-term impact prediction uses early citations and journal impact factor to support research performance assessment, with accuracy varying by discipline.

c8f412b31dc5b9e8952ca12d4dddde60e5bf7b0e.text:
## Sequential Recommendation, Mobility, and Social Relationship Modeling

This community centers on sequential recommendation, user representation learning, and mobile-phone-based relationship characterization. In sequential recommendation, Markov chains perform well on extremely sparse datasets, while recurrent neural networks (RNNs) process consumed item embeddings to model users and predict next points of interest (POIs). RNNs generally suit denser, more complex datasets.

SASRec uses self-attention to predict the next item from relatively few historical actions, combining long-term semantic modeling with Markov-like local-history behavior. It is reported as an order of magnitude more efficient than comparable CNN- and RNN-based models, and attention visualizations expose relevant activity patterns. Item embeddings, often created with skip-gram with negative sampling (a Word2Vec variant), support semantically rich user representations; in contrast, item co-occurrence and Word2Vec recommenders typically lack effective user representations. These representations support future-song prediction but may also enable recovery of private information when combined with external data.

For next-POI recommendation, STLSTM, an LSTM variant, models spatio-temporal intervals between check-ins. Its time and distance gates regulate short- and long-term interest updates, while coupled input and forget gates reduce parameters and improve efficiency.

The mobile phone call dataset links users’ age, gender, and billing locality to relationship characterization. Egocentric network rank helps distinguish intimate from casual relationships: intimate ties show higher call frequency and daily regularity, with patterns varying by gender and age.

df21e390f4d480d130ded5b953a2d639e22f5bca.text:
## Neural Sequence Modeling and Recommendation

This community centers on neural methods for sequential prediction, recommendation, classification, and retrieval. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs), LSTMs, bidirectional LSTMs, hierarchical RNNs, and augmented RNNs model session sequences, user behavior, musical-taste evolution, customer purchase sequences, and long-term dependencies. They support session-based, sequential, next-item, next-POI, and next-station recommendation, including systems such as CARL, Multi-RNN, and the augmented recurrent neural network.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) complement sequence models by extracting local patterns from text, images, audio, and user-profile metadata. They support text and sentiment classification, search-term detection, image and recipe retrieval, and relevance classification. Hybrid deep learning networks combine CNN and RNN components; DeepInf incorporates network structure and features into CNNs.

Attention and self-attention mechanisms enhance sequence modeling, recommendation, and churn prediction. Graph-oriented approaches include graph neural networks, memory-augmented GNNs, SR-GNN, SEMIGNN, and heterogeneous-network methods, particularly for session graphs and recommendation. Transformers, encoder–decoder architectures, sequence-to-sequence models, and models such as SASRec and Seq2Slate extend attention-based sequential learning.

The community also covers authorship attribution, clickbait and spam detection, forecasting, semantic tagging, question answering, and retrieval. Evaluation uses metrics including mean reciprocal rank, mean average accuracy, and area under the curve.

ba6cc1cac1b43076586370f69caa648f3efae203.text:
## Sequential Recommendation, Ranking, and Graph Analysis

This community centers on sequential recommendation and user-behavior modeling. Recurrent neural networks, self-attentive networks, Markov and hidden Markov models, and sequence-to-sequence architectures support next-item, next-POI, session, and sequential-skip prediction. Contextual information is incorporated through context-aware recommender systems, CA RNN’s adaptive context-specific input and transition matrices, and temporal or geolocation features. SASRec, HCRNN, and memory-augmented graph neural networks represent notable recommendation methods and systems.

A second theme is ranking and classification. Production ranking systems, information-filtering algorithms, ranking-based methods, and probabilistic multi-aspect criteria address result ordering, user ranking, and cross-device matching. Binary classification is applied to biomedical articles, comparative summarization, and matching, with agent-based models and guided self-organization among the methods.

Graph analysis focuses on directed and undirected graphs, communities, hierarchy detection, and graph mixtures. Graphlets, graphlet degree sampling, ERGM Graphlets, and the ERGM package support structural analysis using local topologies, nodal attributes, and topological measures. Community characterization and interpretation methods address multi-resolution communities, permanence maximization, and detectability thresholds.

Additional topics include contextual Twitter sentiment classification, topic detection and automatic article-topic assignment, hidden-database crawling, privacy inference attacks, and fast hashing methods such as recursive, cyclic-polynomial, and randomized Karp–Rabin hashing.

3578002f07e6eb3e281ca842d5f69c767f1c63e4.text:
### Community Report: Recommender Systems and Personalized Ranking

This community centers on recommender systems that address information overload by selecting and ranking items for users. Core tasks include recommendation, top-*n* and top-*k* item recommendation, rating prediction, personalized and collaborative ranking, click-through-rate prediction, and item recommendation.

Collaborative filtering—user-based, item-based, neural, and cross-domain—learns from user–item interactions, ratings, explicit or implicit feedback, and sparse user behavior data. Matrix factorization, latent factor models, matrix completion, Bayesian personalized ranking, Bayesian Poisson factorization, and hybrid matrix factorization model user preferences and low-rank structure.
