Deep learning, attention mechanisms, word embeddings, item embeddings, topic models, and distributed representations incorporate content and side information such as product attributes, reviews, and taxonomies.

Important challenges include sparsity, user and item cold starts, continuous cold start, popularity bias, and the diversity–accuracy dilemma. Hybrid, social, context-aware, news, product, and cross-domain recommendation extend the basic setting; social recommendation uses social relations and dynamics.

Evaluation emphasizes recommendation accuracy, predictive accuracy, RMSE, mean reciprocal rank, click-through rate, ratings, novelty, diversity, and user experience. MovieLens, Netflix, online reviews, product reviews, clinical notes, scholarly literature, and Behance are representative datasets. Systems and methods such as CARL, ORFEL, NCDRec, SARVE, VBPR, SocRecM, ATTSUM, IARN, LES, and SIBRank illustrate specialized approaches.

015f66f1e0a1f6bd1095e3c5fe54c81cb2970844.text:
## Community Report: Networks, Ranking, Science, and Privacy

This community centers on graph-based analysis, ranking, classification, and scientific research behavior. Graphlets characterize local topologies and provide sufficient statistics for exponential family random graph models; graphlet degree sampling and ERGM graphlets support network characterization. Sequence-based network representation incorporates topological measures and nodal attributes to represent dynamic attributed networks and identify emerging sequential patterns. Community characterization methods apply these ideas to dynamic complex and scientific collaboration networks, while agony, iterated agony, permanence maximization, and multi-resolution local communities address hierarchy detection and the resolution limit.

Ranking connects information-filtering algorithms, result sets, partial orders, ranking-based methods, and cross-device matching. Classification includes binary and biomedical article classification, guided self-organization, agent-based models, and contextual recurrent neural networks (CA-RNNs), which use adaptive context-specific input and transition matrices for behavior modeling.

A major scientific-information strand covers automatic article topic assignment, topic detection, research landscapes, topic mobility, and topic-selection strategies evaluated by research potential, success, efficiency, and diversity. H-index prediction uses researcher authority and the ArnetMiner dataset; an R-based model reports an R² of 0.92.

Online advertising includes parked domains, Google AdWords, the Google Display Network, targeted advertising, visitor-intent extraction, and privacy-aware advertising. Privacy inference attacks expose personal information in profiles, motivating mitigation. Hashing methods address fast n-gram hashing, with pairwise independence central to several constructions.

6253cb8b9025482083351c686180efa560850351.text:
## Compact Embeddings for Recommender Systems

Recommender systems represent sparse categorical features with embedding vectors stored in embedding tables. For large-vocabulary features, these tables grow linearly with vocabulary size and increase overall model size, creating a need for more compact representations.

Differentiable product quantization supports learning compact embeddings and has been generalized to recommendation problems. Multi granular quantized embeddings learn compact embeddings for sparse features and specifically target large-vocabulary sparse features, especially infrequent items. They are designed to handle the power-law data distribution common in recommender systems.

The resulting compact embeddings can reduce model size to approximately 20% of the original, addressing the scaling cost of embedding tables while retaining a representation for sparse categorical features.

9cbf162838409e043290dc64b8d5d95b41f3f854.text:
## Recommender Systems, Engagement, and Scalable Personalization

This community centers on recommender systems for e-commerce, music, video, and online services. Core approaches include collaborative filtering, content-based recommendation, matrix factorization, random walk with restart, and ranking. These systems commonly learn from implicit feedback and user–item relationships, while explicit ratings, side information, node content, labels, and network structure can improve models or address cold-start problems. Item popularity is both a ranking heuristic and a source of non-uniform weighting for missing data.

Matrix-factorization methods include alternating least squares, implicit matrix factorization, and EALS, which efficiently handles variably weighted missing data. Incremental updates support newly arriving feedback. SimDex accelerates serving by indexing matrix-factorization predictions for exact top-*k* recommendation, falling back to blocked matrix multiplication when indexing is not beneficial.

Other work addresses track similarity using collaborative-filtering signals, implicit matrix factorization, and side information, evaluated on the SoundCloud dataset with an open-source implementation. Video recommendation emphasizes engagement—watch time, average percentage watched, and relative engagement—rather than views alone, while distinguishing engagement from popularity.

Dense recommender datasets complement sparse industry-scale data and enable studies of preference diversity, consistency, scale acuity, anchoring bias, and counterfactual learning. The community also covers multi-stakeholder recommendation, preference elicitation, bandit comparisons, reproducibility, and research challenges.

9c1fe1cd53495d148634c631a95040a1b29719c2.text:
### Recommendation, Graph Learning, and Price-Aware Prediction

This community covers recommender systems based on collaborative filtering, graph learning, session modeling, and price awareness. Matrix factorization is a widely used recommendation strategy that models user–item interactions and commonly underpins collaborative filtering. Collaborative filtering also includes recent graph-neural-network approaches.

**Multi GCCF** is a collaborative-filtering method that learns user and item embeddings from a user–item interaction graph, while integrating proximal information through separate user–user and item–item graphs. It is evaluated on four public recommendation benchmarks.

The community also addresses session-based prediction. Last-click-out prediction focuses on predicting the final action in a session-based interaction, including the task emphasized by the RecSys Challenge 2019. Polinks submitted a solution to this challenge, and one reported mean reciprocal rank score is 0.60277. Ensemble learning is used for last-click-out prediction and comprises session-aware learning, which is implemented with recurrent neural networks.

Price-aware recommendation targets user purchase-intention prediction by learning price-aware user representations. It models item price as a factor in price awareness, with item categories modulating how users perceive and respond to price. Graph convolutional networks are used in this price-aware recommendation setting, and price awareness improves modeling of user preference.

c8bb463dc1cada778792ca153b555aa7baf2bc33.text:
## Recommendation, Ranking, and Learning Systems

This community centers on recommender systems that generate personalized item rankings while addressing information overload, data sparsity, and cold-start users or items. Matrix factorization learns user and item representations from the user–item matrix, commonly using dot products. Bayesian Personalized Ranking (BPR) applies pairwise learning with negative sampling; its variants include HyperBPR, which learns embeddings in hyperbolic space, View-Enhanced Sampling, which uses viewed items as intermediate feedback to purchases, and Adversarial Personalized Ranking, which applies adversarial training to improve generalization. Metric factorization instead measures user–item closeness with Euclidean distance and supports rating estimation and personalized ranking.

Deep learning and neural collaborative filtering extend representation learning, using user and item embeddings and additional content or interaction signals. DeepPage applies deep reinforcement learning to page-wise recommendation, using real-time feedback to arrange complementary items in a two-dimensional display. Hybrid music recommenders combine techniques to support large catalogs and discovery of non-popular music.

The community also includes reinforcement-learning approaches to join-order enumeration. ReJoin uses deep reinforcement learning and artificial neural networks with the PostgreSQL optimizer, evaluated by plan quality and join-enumeration efficiency. Related evaluation measures include MAE, RMSE, correlation coefficient, and relative improvement.

311fd6e3fecea87f3d41067d71551170718da7f5.text:
### Recommender Systems: Methods, Tasks, and Challenges

This community centers on recommender systems that address information overload by learning user preferences and ranking or predicting items. Core tasks include recommendation, rating prediction, top‑N recommendation, personalized and collaborative ranking, product and news recommendation, and scholarly information recommendation.

Collaborative filtering—including user- and item-based methods—uses explicit or implicit feedback, ratings, user–item matrices, and interaction data. Matrix factorization, latent factor models, matrix completion, Bayesian personalized ranking, Bayesian Poisson factorization, hybrid matrix factorization, and factorization-based topic models model preferences and sparse behavior. Deep learning, distributed representations, word and item embeddings, topic models, and semantic keyword extraction incorporate content and interactions; hybrid methods and side information use item metadata, product attributes, and review text.

The community also studies social recommendation and diffusion methods, including mass diffusion, heat conduction, balanced diffusion, and similarity preferential diffusion, linking recommendations with social relations, contagion, information cascades, and user activities. Specialized systems include news, product, scholarly, and online catalog recommenders.

Key challenges are sparsity, cold-start users and items, temporal dynamics, and the accuracy–diversity tradeoff. Evaluation includes recommendation accuracy, ratings, RMSE, diversity, novelty, user experience, and impact. MovieLens, Netflix, product reviews, and scholarly literature serve as data sources.

b744aab3db34e6393b412e05dbefc728fe147a5f.text:
## Recommender Systems, Streaming, and Applied Prediction

This community centers on recommender systems that learn long-term user preferences and generate personalized ranked lists. Matrix completion, latent factor models, non-negative matrix factorization, convex clustering, and other recommendation algorithms support recommendation tasks, while sequence-aware systems use ordered user–item interaction logs to model behavioral patterns and evaluate alternative algorithmic solutions through benchmarking.

A major theme is robustness: shilling attacks, including fraudulent reviews, affect algorithm performance and different users. Shilling-attack analysis quantifies these effects in real-world scenarios, using datasets such as RARD and RARD II. RARD II extends RARD with recommendation logs and implicit-rating matrices, supports MR DLIB, and includes JabRef as an additional service partner.

The community also covers conversational recommendation. Dialog systems and recommender research support personalized conversational sales agents, which use long-term preferences and optimize a per-session utility function for e-commerce companies. Recommendation systems target improved user experience, vendor revenues, conversion rate, and expected revenue.

Applications include mobile and web recommendation, music streaming, e-commerce, and digital libraries. A separate data-infrastructure line supports drug repurposing through chemical ontologies, molecular ontological labels, compound–target databases, compound similarity, non-negative matrix factorization, and NOIR-DR.

Finally, Facebook Live exemplifies live social broadcasting: mobile-produced streams connect broadcasters and viewers, generate social engagement, and raise Internet-infrastructure and network-burden concerns.

3df7e0a74534eb8aa3b5221efadc9484c71a82c2.text:
## Recommendation, Bias, and Efficient Representation Learning

This community centers on recommender systems and recommendation algorithms for online marketplaces, music streaming, personalized playlists, and scholarly or product recommendations. Core tasks include top‑k item recommendation, long-tail recommendation, temporal and whole-chain recommendations, and online inference.

A major theme is popularity bias: systems favor popular items, underrepresent long-tail items, reduce coverage, and may create bias disparity or diverge from user expectations. Fairness, ranking quality, coverage, catalog coverage, and long-tail coverage are key evaluation concerns. Temporal xQuAD addresses omissions over time, while normalized representations target popularity bias.

Methods span neighborhood-, model-, trust-aware, and collaborative filtering, often using implicit feedback and user–item bipartite graphs. J‑NCF jointly performs deep feature learning and nonlinear interaction modeling. Collaborative metric learning uses uniform or two-stage negative sampling, attention neural networks, and triplet-based objectives. Multimodal attentive metric learning and product embeddings support preference prediction and product recommendation.

Representation learning is also used for binary and cross-modal retrieval: UCH couples outer- and inner-cycle networks with a generative adversarial mechanism to learn common representations and hash codes. Binarized collaborative filtering uses knowledge distillation and stochastic penalties for efficient binary representations.

Temporal systems model session graphs and time slices. DeepChain applies multi-agent and model-based reinforcement learning. Evaluation uses MovieLens 100K/1M, Amazon Movies, movie and benchmark datasets, with offline, online, automatic, and human evaluation.

710efb094c8e7d59301237347b05741ef739d5d0.text:
## Recommendation Systems: Collaborative, Neural, and Session-Based Methods

This community centers on recommender systems that address recommendation, ranking, top-*N* recommendation, candidate generation, and click-through-rate prediction while mitigating information overload. Collaborative filtering learns from user–item relationships and interaction data, but faces sparsity, data sparsity, cold start, and user-privacy risks. Federated learning offers a privacy-preserving implementation, while set-level ratings can supplement individual item ratings.

Neural approaches include neural collaborative filtering, ConvNCF, autoencoders, graph neural networks, and neural graph collaborative filtering. These methods exploit user–item graphs, embedding propagation, and high- or low-order feature interactions. Quaternion collaborative filtering uses quaternion algebra and Hamilton products for representation learning. MKR, cross-compress units, KNI, IPNN, FGCNN, and MatchZoo support knowledge-enhanced, feature-interaction, or text-matching recommendation.

Session-based recommendation operates without long-term preference profiles, modeling behavioral sequences, item transitions, and session graphs. SR-GNN and nearest-neighbor methods are evaluated on session-based recommendation datasets; hierarchical frameworks address item, session, and feature-level coupling.

Causal recommendation and causal embeddings connect recommendations to business objectives and incremental treatment effect. TagRec, tag-based systems, and curiosity-aware recommendation extend application scope. MovieLens, multi-aspect review ratings, interaction graphs, and in-house datasets support evaluation using hit ratio, diversity, surprise level, and business-related measures.

a3cf75adbb1e0567ab89b1d079f251293ff7f2ef.text:
## PageRank, Google-Matrix Spectra, and Network Ranking

This community centers on PageRank and related ranking methods for web, social, citation, Wikipedia, university, vocabulary, and other directed networks. PageRank evaluates node importance from link structure, using a memoryless random-navigation model and a damping factor; it is fundamental to Google Search and is compared with citation ranking, author impact, and paper importance.

The Google matrix provides the mathematical foundation: its dominant eigenvector yields the PageRank vector, while eigenvalues, eigenvectors, eigenstates, spectral density, and the core part determine convergence and stability. Arnoldi methods and spectral analysis study these properties, including relaxation times and spectrum gaps. The matrix is also constructed from Ulam networks and coarse-grained Perron–Frobenius operators.

CheiRank complements PageRank by analyzing information-flow organization, with PageRank–CheiRank planes applied to university, Wikipedia, and Linux networks. Variants include Weighted PageRank, Dynamic PageRank, evolving or time-dependent teleportation, TotalRank, 2DRank, and endorsement-based ranking.

Applications span Wikipedia language editions and historical figures, Twitter networks, author co-citation and citation networks, integer-divisor networks, and the World Wide Web. Related work studies hyperlink categories, linking patterns, geographic information, social ranking, graph sampling, recommendation, knowledge fusion, and community or activity-pattern discovery.

4b3748ad964242b8c5161b95441411560994352c.text:
## Cross-Domain, Graph-Based Recommendation and Learning

This community centers on recommender systems, especially personalized and Top-N recommendation, cross-domain collaborative filtering, explainability, and cold-start/data-sparsity challenges. Matrix factorization learns latent user factors and embeddings from interactions, using ALS or BPR, while EigenRec builds low-dimensional inter-item proximity models and includes PureSVD. GrafC2T2 encodes content, temporal, and trust information in graphs; knowledge graphs support personalization, interpretability, news recommendation, and cold-start mitigation.

Neural approaches include NeuCDCF, a wide-and-deep cross-domain model for nonlinear user–item relationships, and ADC, which uses adaptive deep learning, cross-domain loss, and gradient-based loss balancing. ACdn transfers aesthetic preferences through an aesthetic network and cross-connections. AKGE extracts high-order subgraphs and applies attentive graph neural networks to user–item recommendation. RecWalk uses graph walks and sequential decision processes to produce meaningful user-to-item paths.

Applications include local music and long-tail artist recommendation, hotel search, food and healthy-alternative recommendation, news understanding and personalization, and video summarization through keyframe extraction. Evaluation uses MAP, hit ratio, ADC, and standard or long-tail recommendation accuracy across datasets such as Epinions, Ciao, Million Playlist, and news-reading data. Neo separately applies deep neural networks to adaptive query-plan optimization, learning from existing and commercial optimizers while handling data patterns and estimation errors.

37f5da609e8ac7f2ecbcfc3ed05a0fc2bd5e7dd6.text:
## Collaborative Filtering, Representation Learning, and Adaptive Recommendation

This community centers on collaborative filtering (CF) for top-N recommendation and personalization. CF infers user preferences from user–item interaction data and explicit ratings, commonly using matrix factorization and latent user/item vectors. However, it faces privacy risks, cold-start users, popularity bias, and weak coverage of long-tail items.

Algorithm selection is framed as a recommendation problem: CF4CF uses subsampling landmarkers and benchmark datasets, while CF2Vec applies graph2vec to derive distributed representations of CF data. Its performance is competitive with handcrafted metafeatures and comparable to or better than metalearning approaches.

Content- and attribute-aware methods extend CF with item/user attributes, rating attributes, reviews, and unstructured text. AARM combines ratings with synonymous and similar review aspects through a neural attention network. LCMR uses memory networks, combining local memories for content information with centralized memories for interaction data; it is evaluated using hit ratio and NDCG.

Cross-domain CF transfers rating preferences to address cold-start users. Cross-Domain Latent Feature Mapping learns user latent mappings with neighborhood-based gradient boosting trees and is evaluated on Amazon transaction data.

A generic re-ranking framework personalizes existing algorithms, improving coverage and novelty while promoting suitable long-tail items. Related measures include predictive performance, model effectiveness, ratings, and NDCG.

eb1a8b5ff7cb81034a9b2d8a8a9c7c1639d98056.text:
## PageRank, Google Matrices, and Network Ranking

This community centers on PageRank and its spectral foundations for ranking nodes in web, social, citation, Wikipedia, and other information networks. PageRank evaluates web-page importance from linking pages, uses random navigation and teleportation, and is computed as an eigenvector of the Google matrix. The damping factor or Google parameter alpha affects ranking and decay.

The Google matrix represents random-surfer navigation and is analyzed through eigenvalues, eigenvectors, spectra, eigenstates, and invariant core parts; the Arnoldi method supports eigenvalue analysis. These ideas extend to Wikipedia language editions, Twitter networks, vocabulary networks, university web networks, integer-divisor networks, and Ulam networks generated from coarse-grained Perron–Frobenius operators.

Related ranking methods include Weighted PageRank, Dynamic PageRank, Evolving Teleportation PageRank, TotalRank, 2DRank, Alpha Centrality, and CheiRank. CheiRank and the PageRank–CheiRank plane distinguish information-flow organization. PageRank is also applied to author co-citation and citation networks, paper importance, academic prestige, historical figures, social status forecasting, and node-importance estimation.

The community additionally covers sampling and graph analysis, including graph signal sampling, two-stage adaptive sampling, mixture sampling, optimal weighting, struc2vec, and structural-context analysis.

d4acc35f67dedd4a886a9104b39cd229abdd0c76.text:
## Search, Ranking, and Personalized Recommendation

This community centers on evaluating and improving search and recommendation systems through relevance, user behavior, and ranking methods. Search engines and retrieval systems produce search results, query suggestions, and related searches; ranking functions combine term weights or attribute values, while specialized functions support vertical and video search.

A major theme is bias-aware learning to rank. Click data and impression signals contain position and selection bias. Unbiased and counterfactual learning-to-rank methods use observation or propensity estimation, instrumental variables, historical interactions, and intervention data to correct these effects and optimize additive rank metrics. Related methods include GUBM, click models, Deep PropDCG, SVM PropDCG, and propensity-weighted ranking SVM.

Evaluation uses relevance judgments, test collections, graded relevance measures, discounted cumulative gain, diversity metrics, rank-similarity measures, and quality scores. Visual features, metadata, and page-layout signals support webpage-quality analysis and relevance ranking, including in the Vitor dataset.

The community also covers mobile and personalized recommendation systems. Randomized field experiments report increased podcast streams and aggregate diversity, but reduced individual-level diversity. Search-task hierarchies, task extraction, and satisfaction prediction support task personalization, while music datasets and skip-prediction tasks model listening behavior.

b4ea93167af2e6335f3297625a9e0e325fe0dc01.text:
## Wikipedia, NLP, and Social-Media Analysis

This community centers on Wikipedia as a knowledge platform, dataset, and research testbed. Wikipedia articles, revision histories, editing data, server logs, and multilingual editions support entity linking, semantic content classification, article recommendation, vandalism detection, quality evaluation, trivia mining, and edit-activity analysis. Systems such as TagMe link text fragments to Wikipedia pages, while entity trivia extraction and automatic trivia fact extraction mine relevant facts. Wikipedia is also connected to Wikidata, YAGO, Freebase, and related knowledge-representation efforts.

A second theme is mathematical knowledge: mathematical formulae are treated as first-class objects in contrast to ordinary Wikipedia pages. The NIST Digital Repository of Mathematical Formulae, NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, Mathoid, special LaTeX macros, and computer algebra systems address formula representation and retrieval, requiring adaptations to natural-language-processing methods.

The community also studies social-media dynamics using Twitter data, hashtags, timelines, server logs, Epinions, Slashdot, and Wikipedia. Methods include temporal point processes, dynamical and coevolving models, lag analysis, clustering, network synchronization, and signed-network mining. Applications include content and meme diffusion, disaster monitoring, vaccine sentiment, health-sentiment spread, political disaffection, electoral prediction, and user engagement. Related systems analyze hashtag entities, conversations, recommendations, and emerging events.

2e7cab7049e88d2aa63fcf047e1fcd575af49cb1.text:
## Social Media, Information Diets, and Event Analysis

This community centers on Twitter and other social-media systems as sources of large-scale data for news, politics, emergencies, finance, health, and public discourse. Twitter supports news sharing, journalism, campaigning, hashtag adoption, personalized recommendations, and analysis of collective mood, while social bots operate across Twitter, Weibo, and social media to influence opinion making, propaganda distribution, and election results. Human control and human interaction are considered in regulating bot capabilities.

Key methods include bursty topic detection and event classification for identifying financial and political events affecting stock-market volatility, using tweet polarity and high-frequency Greek and Spanish market data. Microblog retrieval extracts tweets describing needs or available aid during emergencies; Credbank and Pheme provide crowdsourced or journalistic accuracy assessments. Spambot research benchmarks detection techniques, human discrimination, and collective behavior analysis.

Information-diet characterization models the topical distribution of information items, including news organizations’ focused diets and personalized recommendations intended to reduce topical imbalance. Joint non-negative matrix factorization learns a liberal–conservative ideology space from content consumption. Deep learning and neural information-retrieval models support related analysis. Datasets span elections, Zika, bird flu, Rio+20, controversial topics, and stock markets, linking online behavior to news audiences, demographics, voting outcomes, and cultural or biological cycles.

adf7b1f75ddf1560e6681181461e05e3a0487a94.text:
## Contextual and Sequential Recommendation Systems

This community centers on recommendation, user modeling, and prediction from reviews, interactions, transaction sequences, and context.

**CARL** performs context-aware joint user–item representation learning for rating prediction. It combines review-based and interaction-based features through dynamic linear fusion, uses attention to identify informative context terms and review features, and applies factorization machines to model higher-order feature interactions. Reviews provide scoring information, while user–item interactions contribute complementary features. Rating prediction accuracy is the evaluation metric.

The **Neural Attentive Recommendation Machine** addresses session-based recommendation in e-commerce scenarios where user profiles are unavailable. Its hybrid encoder models sequential behavior and uses attention to capture the user’s main purpose. These are combined into a unified session representation for joint item/session representation learning and bi-linear candidate matching, with notable gains on long sessions and evaluation on two benchmark datasets.

**TransRec** embeds items in a transition space and models users as translation vectors for large-scale sequential prediction and next-item recommendation, including third-order interactions.

Embedding-based transaction integration combines multifaceted transaction data with auxiliary relational tables, improving user modeling and demographic prediction from purchase history, including gender and marital status. Context-aware venue recommendation uses scoring functions over user context, venue content, and reviews, evaluated on the TREC Contextual Suggestion Track.

b2bfd0cce323b9d78e70312a3fa26fd44466fdf2.text:
## Wikipedia, Entity Linking, and Social-Media Knowledge Systems

This community centers on Wikipedia as a knowledge platform, dataset, and source for downstream analysis. Wikipedia articles, revision histories, server logs, biographies, and multilingual editions support studies of article creation, editing activity, collaboration, concept relatedness, social movements, lag relative to news, and electoral prediction. Wikidata, Freebase, YAGO, and knowledge-base systems extend Wikipedia’s structured representation.

Entity linking is a major theme. TAGME performs fast annotation of short and long texts, addressing synonymy and polysemy by linking fragments to Wikipedia pages. Related systems include context-aware hashtag entity linking, semantic content classification, trivia extraction, article recommendation, and semantic full-text search. These methods support retrieval, annotation, quality evaluation, and knowledge discovery, including long-tail entities and trivia facts.

Natural language processing connects textual analysis with social media and specialized domains. It supports topic identification, trending-topic detection, sentiment analysis, n-gram statistics, and mathematics-aware processing. Mathoid, MathML, the NIST repositories, and a mathematics-aware part-of-speech tagger treat mathematical formulae as specialized objects.

Twitter and other social-network datasets enable analysis of hashtags, content and meme diffusion, user engagement, peer influence, political disaffection, health and vaccine sentiment, and electoral outcomes. Dynamical and coevolving models, clustering, network mining, and lag analysis relate online activity to events, news, and collective behavior.

63b9e2c75abe724dd45a9eea13e487483030f4f9.text:
## Provenance, Reproducible Science, Retrieval, and Personalization

This community connects reproducible computational science with provenance-aware data and workflow management. Reproducibility concerns computational scientific experiments, versioned workflows, data, services, and computational context. **ReproWD**, multi-seed evaluation, and hyperparameter evaluation support more reliable reproduction, while workflow provenance traces and provenance services capture execution and specification information. Systems including **CRISTAL**, **Curator**, **ProvDB**, and the provenance capture and visualization system support provenance management, traceability, attribution, and visualization interaction.

Scientific datasets combine scientific metadata, lineage, annotations, permissions, and data reuse. **Integrated metadata management**, **Data Atlas**, **Fluidinfo**, and the **VIMMP marketplace** support dataset publication, indexing, retrieval, and access, including clinical and neuroimaging data. Workflow systems and ontologies—including **CPK**, **EMMO**, and marketplace-level ontologies—structure computational analyses and data discovery.

A second theme is personalized and conversational recommendation. Mobile recommender systems and podcast recommendations use consumption histories; randomized field experiments assess effects on streams, diversity, editor engagement, and revenues. Understanding assessment uses tests and interviews to identify expertise and deficiencies and recommend topics or learning materials. Neural models, retrieval models, snippet taxonomies, and Google Web Search address app representation, search, and result presentation. Database evolution is treated through co-existing schemas, synchronization, and bidirectional transformation.

9883c88f8b33c5cb4d154e12080dfb90554958db.text:
## Social Networks, Mobility, Semantics, and Community Evolution

This community centers on social network analysis, social groups, and the dynamics of information and communities across online and mobile environments. Social network analysis identifies strongly connected groups, influential bloggers, collaboration structures, and relationships in coauthorship, learning communities, health, software repositories, and mobile networks.

Group evolution discovery and social group evolution address change identification and the formation, persistence, and transformation of groups. Methods include GED, integrated group evolution methods combining network analysis with text mining, group extraction, and network metrics. Evaluation considers flexibility, ease of implementation, user importance, and community quality.

Information spreading is modeled in mobile networks using information-spreading models, epidemic models, interactive Markov chains, mean-field theory, flooding time, and mobile conductance. Large-scale simulation and datasets such as Renren support validation and prediction.

Semantic analysis supports question answering, thematic analysis, spam detection, and analysis of blog content. Semantic visualization and navigation organizes a semantic information space through precise, connotative, and thematic search. Tumblr and blogosphere datasets support crawling, blog recommendation, thematic analysis, and hate-promoting blogger detection.

Mobile and socially aware networking connects mobility models, opportunistic and delay-tolerant networks, routing, forwarding, data dissemination, incentives, and mobile social sensing. Recommendation systems further combine hybrid, social, sensor-based, and proactive approaches for mobile multimedia and smart communities.

58a1fe12256daafe032e93e1887e3b1b841cc012.text:
## Network and Graph Representation Learning

This community centers on learning low-dimensional node and graph representations from network topology, structure, and attributes, and applying them to downstream tasks. Network representation learning preserves topology and supports node classification, clustering, link prediction, and classification. Classical approaches include DeepWalk, node2vec, LINE, HARP, FastRP, and weighted matrix factorization; HARP improves LINE through hierarchical initialization, while FastRP uses very sparse random projection and iterative computation for scalable embeddings.

Graph representation learning and graph embedding preserve low- and high-order proximity, often using cosine or Euclidean similarity. GCN supports semisupervised node classification with node features, and hierarchical GNNs and differentiable pooling address graph-level representation learning, although pooling may discard information. DAOR is a parameter-free graph embedding approach with competitive link-prediction and node-classification results.

Attributed network embedding integrates topology with node attributes. Attri2vec learns a latent attribute subspace through a network-guided transformation and supports embeddings for new nodes. Polysemous embedding represents multiple node facets with separate vectors and association degrees.

Applications include link prediction—especially in bipartite and out-of-sample settings—event attendance prediction, node clustering, vital-node identification, community vulnerability analysis, network visualization, and recommender systems. BINE specializes in bipartite networks, while Network Lens, multimodal information extraction, and multi-stream feature learning connect representations with richer node and document information.

03221eab53a5bd7ebc57811f576a18075774240a.text:
## Link Prediction in Evolving Social and Technological Networks

This community centers on **link prediction**, the inference of hidden, missing, future, or dissolving links from observable networks. It supports **network evolution analysis**, community partitioning, open-source project recommendation, and node-attribute inference.

Major approaches include **network representation learning**, network embeddings, vertex embeddings, singular value decomposition, edge representations, and **community-enhanced network representation learning**. Structural and topological methods use common neighbors, shortest paths, Katz scores, local degree, topological similarity, neighborhood features, and random walk with restart. Heuristic methods, horn clauses, motif features, weighted path entropy, and neural approaches provide alternative predictors. The **infinite multiple membership relational model**, **LMMG**, **microscopic evolution framework**, **HyperMap**, SMLP, and MEGAN are among the specialized models and systems evaluated for prediction.

The community also connects prediction with **homophily**, social attributes, negative interactions, triadic or triangle closure, preferential attachment, geographic distance, and distance decay. These concepts inform friendship formation, social ties, and network growth. Related tasks include community analysis, multiple-membership analysis, dynamic network analysis, and network summarization. Evaluation uses social, technological, criminal, GitHub, Internet, and other real-world network datasets, supported by systems such as EvalNE and Mandolin.

a54276ff28f8e87dd0d959a3160c09d24747755b.text:
## Social Networks, Spreading, Semantics, and Recommendation

This community centers on social network analysis, including coauthorship networks, social groups, mobile networks, learning communities, hate-promoting communities, and web-based communities. It studies interaction structures, influential users, community dynamics, collaboration, and dynamic team formation. An integrated group evolution method combines social network analysis with text mining.

Information spreading is examined in mobile networks through spreading models, gossip mechanisms, random and smart spreading, epidemic models, and gossip algorithms. Flooding time and mobile conductance measure spreading performance, while large-scale network simulation validates analyses. Semantic analysis supports question answering, thematic analysis, category mapping, CQA spam detection, and analysis of blog activity; it also questions epidemic interpretations of cascades.

Socially aware networking addresses opportunistic, delay-tolerant, and ad hoc networks through routing, forwarding, data dissemination, and incentive mechanisms. Mobile multimedia recommendation systems target overload on mobile devices and can use proactive, sensor-based, hybrid, and socially informed approaches.

Factorization machines support knowledge tracing by estimating student knowledge, handling multiple knowledge components and attempt counts, and encompassing established factor models. App-based FM and LOD-enabled features—including property-object lists and PageRank scores—improve recommendation performance. Tumblr, mobile social networks, app usage data, and blogosphere datasets support these studies.

525d1deaee8ae023b7d46300f78b0c16b85b885a.text:
## Graph Representation, Heterogeneous Networks, and Inference

This community centers on network and node representation learning: network embedding produces low-dimensional node representations for homogeneous, heterogeneous, homogeneous-subnetwork, and bipartite settings. These representations support node classification, clustering, link prediction, network alignment, visualization, and recommendation. Language-modeling ideas motivate methods such as heterogeneous SkipGram and SAC2Vec; SAC2Vec also integrates node content through a multilayer graph.

CARL targets heterogeneous networks by jointly optimizing heterogeneous SkipGram and deep semantic encoding, with an online update module for incoming nodes. It improves relevance search and link prediction relative to state-of-the-art baselines. GPSP uses space projection and is evaluated for clustering and node classification.

A second theme is heterogeneous information networks, including higher-order interactions and network motifs. MoCHIN supports user-guided clustering using an accelerated inference algorithm and applies to arbitrary motif forms. Stratified meta structures and commuting matrices underpin SMSS similarity measurement.

The community also covers signed networks: signed graph convolutional networks use balance theory for representation learning and link-sign prediction, extending approaches primarily developed for unsigned networks. Non-backtracking centrality and its biased random walks are compared with maximal-entropy random walks and support hitting-time analysis. Finally, HornConcerto mines Horn clauses in large knowledge graphs using fact-based confidence scores, while CARL and HornConcerto address link prediction and inference from observable networks.

b9d837bfc2a36bc75089443e6d19d9294c01c58e.text:
## Social Network Evolution, Communities, and Link Inference

This community centers on social-network evolution, link formation, and community structure. **Link prediction** infers hidden or missing links, forecasts new links and link dissolution, and supports community partitioning, social-network evolution, and open-source project recommendation. It is formulated through neighborhood graphs and inference, and uses network representation learning, random walk with restart, the LMMG model, HyperMap, and community-enhanced representation learning. Evaluation involves real-world, technological, face-to-face, and dynamic network datasets, including Facebook, GitHub, and other social-network corpora.

**Homophily**, heterophily, social attributes, geographic distance, and distance decay explain friendship formation and network evolution. Homophily is observed in demographic and preference-related attributes, produces local clustering, and affects complex contagion, popularity capital, and node-attribute inference. Facebook datasets from Laguna and Batangas show age-based homophily; the OpenStack ecosystem did not show the expected same-firm tendency.

**Preferential attachment** is modeled as a structural dynamic and may emerge from triangle closure or a doubly preferential meeting process. It is used in network-growth and social-network models, alongside Chung–Lu, transitive Chung–Lu, hidden-tree, city-level, and demographic structural network-generation methods. Community analysis uses internal and external dominating sets, internal/external slopes, spatial measures, and province boundaries. GraphVis supports interactive graph mining.

86c02f6205fa40dcac353b441eb981e072d1e9c9.text:
## Graph Models, Prediction, and Network Reconstruction

This community focuses on graph modeling, network generation, and prediction tasks. **Dyadic independence models** capture local network information, including degree, while also incorporating global constraints such as clustering coefficient and assortativity. They can efficiently generate random networks with properties similar to observed networks and are evaluated for competitiveness in link prediction and network reconstruction.

**Matrix block approximation** is used to construct approximative dyadic independence models. These models also approximate non-trivial **exponential random graphs** while enforcing edge independence. An associated **approximative framework** supports fitting such exponential random graphs.

**Link prediction** is evaluated on real-world datasets and extends to **hyperedge prediction** in hypergraphs. Hyperedge prediction is experimentally evaluated on 15 real-world datasets and serves as a canonical task for evaluating graph models. **Adaptive ranking algorithms** are likewise tested on real-world datasets.

Overall, the entities connect local and global network constraints with graph-model approximation, random network generation, and empirical evaluation through link, hyperedge, and reconstruction prediction.

cdc1f3544095b6ed9dbe2bce9665e17f0de19d62.text:
### ExEm for Expert Embeddings and Recommendation

This community centers on **ExEm**, a graph embedding method for analyzing collaborative networks of experts. ExEm applies **dominating set theory** to identify dominating experts, then constructs **random walks** beginning at these experts and traversing the collaborative network. The walks are stored as sequences and supplied to a **Skip-gram** neural network.

**Word2vec** and **fastText** are used to train the Skip-gram network, enabling ExEm to produce low-dimensional **expert embeddings**. These embeddings support expertise modeling and an **expert recommendation system**.

ExEm is evaluated through **link prediction** and **multi-label classification**. Link prediction is facilitated by graph embedding and provides an evaluation setting for ExEm. Overall, the relationships connect dominating-set-based expert selection, network random walks, Skip-gram training, and embedding generation to expert recommendation and predictive evaluation.

99b3ecd75e4ad5fd1054721e46005cdcc24da3e2.text:
## Graph Representation Learning for Bipartite and Dynamic Data

This community centers on graph representation learning for link prediction, particularly in bipartite networks and n-ary relational data. The link-prediction setting assumes node attributes are unavailable, relying instead on topological features and learned graph features. Applications include master data management, risk assessment, fraud detection, and anti-money laundering.

Key methods include Graph Autoencoder and Linear Graph Autoencoder baselines. The Linear Graph Autoencoder uses the graph adjacency matrix to learn vector-space representations of nodes and supports both link prediction and node clustering. A 2-hop-path approach forms predicted adjacency matrices by multiplying reconstructed and normalized training adjacency matrices; it is evaluated on bipartite datasets.

dyngraph2vec extends representation learning to dynamic graphs, learning temporal transitions and representations of evolving networks through a deep architecture composed of dense and recurrent layers. Earlier methods largely focus on static networks. A link prediction dataset containing relational-data subgraphs addresses limitations involving temporal information, while also supporting evaluation of unseen-link prediction.

Toy datasets support experiments on network dynamics and are created using stochastic block models. Overall, the community connects adjacency-based reconstruction, topological reasoning, and temporal modeling for relational-network analysis.

573218fc5200d10990e54a348fa910ca1c524bda.text:
## Graph Ranking, Recommendation, and Dynamic Multilayer Networks

This community centers on graph-based ranking, recommendation, link prediction, and network evolution.

**BiRank** provides iterative vertex ranking on bipartite graphs, using query vectors and a smoothing regularization function. It extends to generic *n*-partite graphs and forms the basis of **TriRank** for tripartite ranking. Applications include personalized item recommendation and item popularity prediction, with evaluation on synthetic and real-world datasets.

**PERS** supports explainable recommendation by modeling user–aspect or location–aspect relations in bipartite graphs. It uses user reviews, extracted aspects, sentiment, and deep neural networks to model review–aspect correlations. It also employs a bipartite core-based and ranking-based method.

Random-walk methods support ranking and link prediction. Random Walk with Restart uses a common restart probability, while Random Walk with Extended Restart assigns node-specific probabilities. **SURE** learns these probabilities, improving ranking and link-prediction accuracy.

Generative models represent multilayer networks, overlapping communities, user-preference sequences, and layer interdependence, with expectation-maximization for latent-variable inference. They are applied to South Indian villager support and malaria genetic substring networks.

A dynamic network model uses persistent links, node-specific dynamic fitnesses, and Markov dynamics to forecast links, including in the e-MID interbank market. It captures preferential trading and lending, while accounting for time-varying topology.

3666b57da087baf33cd8fd06df423f9d410aa4bc.text:
## Graph Learning for Dynamic, Signed, and Attributed Networks

This community centers on graph-based link prediction, node representation, and classification across dynamic, signed, multiplex, and attributed networks. Link prediction uses network topology, content information, structural feature vectors, heuristic methods, and graph embedding methods to model changing user–item relationships and incomplete graphs. Graph embeddings also support node classification, clustering, reconstruction, and graph visualization.

SINE is an attributed network-embedding method that learns low-dimensional node representations from incomplete graphs. It separately models node–context and node–attribute relationships, mitigates missing links and attributes, scales to millions of nodes and edges, and uses online stochastic gradient descent. It is evaluated for link prediction, node classification, and node clustering. DynGEM uses deep autoencoders to embed evolving graph snapshots, improving stability over time; it is evaluated for anomaly detection, reconstruction, and visualization.

Signed multiplex link prediction is addressed by SMLP, which leverages negative relationship layers and mutual information across network layers. Positive and negative interactions jointly improve classification performance, while signed graph Laplacian methods and diffuse-interface methods incorporate these signals.

Deeplink combines structural and content information through structural feature learning and outperformed structural and hybrid approaches on IRBlogs and Telegram. Content-based filtering uses descriptors and collaborative domain knowledge for feature weighting, including cold-start items. The community also examines systematic bias, filter bubbles, and algorithmic fairness: heuristic predictors are more biased than graph embeddings.

8c5b7e6adcf4ce12f1e32a9b31497efff09fe066.text:
## Centrality, Influence, and User-Behavior Graph Analytics

This community centers on graph-based importance, prediction, and strategic network analysis. PageRank is related to Bonacich centrality and incorporates sentence position and semantic-role information; its semantic-role-aware variant ranks key phrases, uses lexical features, is evaluated on scientific articles, and outperforms state-of-the-art baseline approaches. PageRank also supports pairwise link prediction, including triangle formation, while diffusion-based methods improve consistency under standard link-prediction evaluation.

A centrality maximization game models network formation through strategic placement of out-links. Nodes use centrality as utility, and Nash equilibria include 2-cliques for one out-link and ring or Butterfly networks for two. Best-response dynamics and local best responses support this analysis.

Competitive influence maximization treats budget allocation and seed selection as a game among competing parties. Influential nodes receive discrete budgets, while payoff estimation and a best-response oracle improve efficiency.

Other applications include home-location estimation from social relationships and user centrality, with hub and authority users posing difficulties. HITS identifies authority or celebrity users; hub users follow many celebrities, and higher HITS scores correlate with weaker same-home-location tendencies.

Unsupervised joint representation learning embeds posted content and follower networks to detect anomalous dense groups and troll-like behavior, evaluated on 2019 Canadian elections tweets. PageRank also assesses bank-country interactions, identifying Industrial and Commercial Bank of China as highest by assets.

d64adf68ce3c1c4486e295744986c9c7f07c6330.text:
## Research Community: Language, Social Identity, and Text Generation

This community covers neural language analysis, social-identity inference, automatic title generation, and influence prediction.

A convolutional neural network performs search-term detection on a hospital and clinic query set, analyzing speech-query transcriptions and detecting origin and destination search terms. It learns image embeddings and calculates character-level embeddings, and is compared with Levenshtein-distance word matching.

DTATG is an automatic title-generation system. It extracts central sentences, converts them into dependency trees, and applies a Dependency Tree Compression Model to remove branches. A trimmed sentence that passes a title test becomes a title candidate; DTATG selects the highest-ranked candidate. Its generated titles achieve higher F1 scores than previous methods.

Name embeddings are learned from 57 million contact lists by exploiting homophily in communication patterns. They encode ethnicity and nationality and serve as representations for a nationality classifier. The classifier performs fine-grained classification across 39 groups, achieves an F1 score of 0.795, is evaluated against Ethnea, and is applied to Twitter celebrity followers.

A neural clickbait detection engine uses image embeddings for clickbait detection and achieves an F1 score of 65.37%, exceeding the 55.21% benchmark. Separately, a machine-learning model predicts high-PageRank users, with PageRank defining influence and an F1 score of 0.942.

f16a415926f49fcf78e40b668364bc538759e4b7.text:
## Graph-Based Prediction, Data Quality, and Platform Analysis

This community links graph learning, data cleaning, social-media analysis, and technology-network research. **Link prediction** uses network embeddings and singular value decomposition, and is evaluated with precision, AUC, and the Katz metric on benchmark datasets and cross-domain patent networks. Node-similarity distributions—especially common-neighbor similarity—are derived with generating functions for Erdős–Rényi, small-world, and scale-free networks; theoretical AUC follows from similarities of connected and unconnected pairs. Embeddings also support semi-supervised node classification and generic clustering.

For data quality, **pattern-driven data cleaning** preserves frequent patterns, expresses declarative repairs, and computes them with a linear-time repair algorithm. Integrity constraints support data repair algorithms, while repair quality is assessed using precision and recall. Related-set discovery and data integration/cleaning use **SilkMoth**, which creates set signatures, prunes candidates through signature selection, and verifies remaining pairs using maximum matching over bipartite graphs.

Machine-learning classifiers support clickbait and abuser detection, platform identification, and online-social-media post classification, using linguistic, image-related, profile-description, and profile-image features. Random forest and multinomial naïve Bayes perform well; reported results include AUC 0.92, classifier AUC 0.8, precision 0.819, and recall 0.966. Policy-citation prediction combines classification models with online attention to forecast citations of research output in public-policy documents. Patent citations model knowledge flows and spillovers across 29 technological domains in dynamic technology networks.

440c0a52d564c004c3ad3e38beaad53af049333e.text:
## PageRank, Google Matrices, and Network Ranking

This community centers on PageRank and related ranking methods for directed, weighted, and large-scale networks. PageRank evaluates web-page importance from hyperlink structure, under a random-navigation model with teleportation and a damping factor; it is fundamental to Google search and is applied to Wikipedia, Twitter, coauthorship, citation, patent, banking, and other information networks. It also represents social status, academic reputation, paper importance, and institutional prestige.

The Google matrix provides the mathematical foundation: its dominant eigenvector yields the PageRank vector, while spectral analysis examines eigenvalues, eigenstates, convergence, and the matrix’s core part. Google matrices are constructed for Wikipedia language editions, Twitter, integer-divisor and Ulam networks, and from Perron–Frobenius operators or clickstream and pageview data.

CheiRank, derived from the Google matrix, complements PageRank by characterizing information-flow organization; the PageRank–CheiRank plane combines both dimensions. Reduced Google matrix methods focus on selected network structure. Variants include personalized, weighted, dynamic, evolving-teleportation, seeded, and task-specific PageRank, as well as HITS–PageRank mixtures, AuthorRank, PaperRank, and TotalRank. These methods support localization, forecasting, community and hyperlink analysis, and ranking in web and social systems.

c89450abb24cd10cdc3ba590482d50fa7774aff5.text:
## Community Report: Graph Learning, Influence, and Sequential Prediction

This community covers methods for network influence, recommendation, embeddings, rumor detection, and robust graph analysis.

For influence propagation and seed selection, Basic-Selector uses predicted mobility and iterative greedy selection, while the more efficient Fast-Selector exploits geographical interdependencies and achieves higher coverage with a slight sacrifice relative to Basic-Selector. Aurora addresses PageRank auditing by using gradients to identify influential graph elements and demonstrates linear scalability. Related approximation algorithms extend random reverse-reachable sets. Convex relaxation supports malicious-node removal while accounting for network connectivity and trading off false positives and false negatives; it outperforms structure-ignoring and state-of-the-art related baselines.

Multi-view network embedding is represented by MVN2Vec, which models collaboration and preservation and improves embedding quality. The multiplex diffusion model uses MCMC inference for latent structure and node parameters.

In rumor detection, Credible Early Detection (CED) models reposts as sequences to identify rumor candidates earlier, reducing prediction time span by more than 85% and outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.

Sequential recommendation includes Caser, which applies convolutional filters for local sequential features and general preferences, outperforming state-of-the-art methods. Alternating Linear Bandits combines alternating least squares for online matrix-factorization recommendation. CMTRF combines monotonic rating-scale transformations with matrix-factorization regression to address heterogeneous rater behavior and population-specific preferences.

eb2d15ce3ebb9ec741fb78e83e249ab24a2ba5ed.text:
## PageRank, Google Matrices, and Network Influence

This community centers on **PageRank**, a ranking method for directed networks that evaluates nodes from their incoming links and underpins Google Search. It uses a random-navigation model, teleportation, and a damping factor; variants include **weighted**, **dynamic**, **evolving-teleportation**, **personalized**, and parameter-free **TotalRank** approaches. PageRank is applied to web pages, large-scale graphs, Wikipedia language editions, Twitter, citation and author co-citation networks, patents, academic reputation, social status, historical figures, and bank or country influence.

The **Google matrix** represents network navigation and yields the PageRank vector through its dominant eigenvector. Its spectrum, eigenstates, core part, and convergence can be studied with methods such as Arnoldi analysis and Perron–Frobenius operators. The **reduced Google matrix** focuses this analysis on selected network structure. **CheiRank**, derived from the Google matrix, complements PageRank by distinguishing information-flow organization; both form the PageRank–CheiRank plane.

**Personalized PageRank** visits or samples nodes in directed networks and is approximated using Monte Carlo, mean-field analysis, and distributed or parallel frameworks. It also supports PowerWalk. Overall, the community connects spectral methods, graph models, web information, citations, and social influence.

623931db74fe2b0d4d9d74b8558e404d597723f1.text:
## Language, Trustworthiness, and Scholarly Analysis

This community connects analysis of AI conference manuscripts, user trustworthiness, microblog content, and bibliographic data.

For peer review outcome prediction, manuscript text is examined through lexical and psycholinguistic analysis, including word usage, frequency, age of acquisition, and abstractness. Semantic analysis is applied to full manuscripts, while pairwise semantic similarity measures word-content overlap. Accepted manuscripts show greater similarity, greater use of scientific and AI jargon, and more words related to machine learning and neural networks. They also score lower on two readability indicators. In contrast, words related to logic and symbolic processing and knowledge-based systems are negatively associated with acceptance.

Machine learning and semantic analysis serve as modules for user trustworthiness prediction, including domain-based trustworthiness across different time periods. Machine learning is also used to classify microblog posts expressing customer needs and supports sentiment analysis of user-generated content. E-mobility tweets are an evaluated microblog dataset.

Quantitative bibliographic analysis constructs and explores large digital bibliographical datasets, including citation networks. Knowledge-based systems and neural networks represent relevant systems, while scientific and AI jargon, domain-based trustworthiness, and logic and symbolic processing are key concepts.

4674880bb04d7f809243d198aa2aed50848cc8a8.text:
## Network Dynamics, Multiplex Structure, and Semantic Navigation

This community covers network analysis across higher-order, multiplex, temporal, and semantic settings. Hypergraphs represent interactions among more than two nodes; hypergraph clustering uses correlation-clustering objectives, minimum cuts for two labels, and approximation algorithms based on linear-programming relaxations for multiple labels. It supports edge-label community detection and is demonstrated on temporal data.

Multiplex networks couple layers through interlayer adjacency matrices and coupling strength. Link persistence and correlations among hyperbolic node coordinates explain edge overlap and enable trans-layer link prediction, mutual navigation, and multiplex embeddings. Geometric multiplex models and tunable eigenvector centralities extend these analyses. Supracentrality matrices define joint, marginal, and conditional supracentralities through their dominant eigenvectors, with singular perturbation theory analyzing weak and strong coupling. Applications include European airline transportation and mathematician graduation and hiring.

HopRank models navigation within k-hop neighborhoods, using clickstream-derived transition matrices. It connects human navigation in semantic networks, PageRank teleportation, and ontology exploration interfaces, with BioPortal providing biomedical-ontology clickstream evidence.

More broadly, the networks dataset links stochastic and deterministic dynamics, adaptive networks, contagion, opinion models, waves, and coupled oscillators. Semantic structure influences teleportation, while temporal networks represent changing entities or interactions.

8d0ba6d11025fcec72b830b8b9a62b0f9035fd5a.text:
## Citation-Based Research Evaluation and Classification

This community centers on bibliometric methods for assessing research impact, academic prestige, institutional reputation, and technology importance. PageRank is applied to citation networks among universities, producing measures of academic reputation and institutional prestige that correlate strongly with ARWU Subject Rankings. Related variants include PaperRank, which measures paper impact using weighted, time-ordered citation descendants, and AuthorRank, which evaluates authors while accounting for citing authors’ impact. Both are applied to bibliographic records in INSPIRE, a dataset covering fundamental physics.

Citation counting is refined through individual citations that distribute credit among co-authors, while Citation Coins offer a closed-market mechanism intended to eliminate self-citations and circular citations. PageRank is also used for patent scoring to support technology-management decisions.

A major classification theme is the algorithmically constructed classification system (ACCS), which builds paper-based fields from citation relations. ACCS identifies and clusters work on overall water splitting, evaluates discriminatory power, and compares its clusters and citation averages with INSPEC classification and journal-based Web of Science subject categories. These averages support publication-impact analysis. More broadly, bibliometric data provide quantitative evidence for academic prestige, especially across research institutions, while university rankings evaluate institutional excellence.

52f3eeca5393cc45553cfed900b02da7a7cb22e6.text:
## Semantic Extraction, Similarity, Diffusion, and Social Systems

This community spans text understanding, retrieval, similarity search, information diffusion, and social or organizational analysis.

**Semantic extraction and retrieval** include Gextext, which extracts latent relationships and disease networks from unstructured literature using correlation thresholding and text embeddings. It infers Diseasome graphs and organizes drug names and stroke phenotypes by shared properties. Semantic analysis supports entity extraction, category mapping, semantic question answering, and CQA spam detection, while content-based retrieval supports image feature extraction, simplification, query execution, and operational search.

**Similarity search** focuses on exact and randomized set similarity joins evaluated with Jaccard similarity. Bitmap filters use bitwise operations and similarity upper bounds to accelerate PPJoin, AdaptJoin, and GroupJoin. Prefix filtering, high-dimensional sketching, and robustness to missing rare tokens support faster approximate or exact joins.

**Diffusion and sentiment** connect epidemic models, self-exciting processes, Hawkes point processes, and generalized stochastic SIR models to citation cascades, research-idea diffusion, and online information diffusion. Positive messages spread more slowly but reach larger audiences, while positive exposure can predict later negative sentiment.

**Social and organizational systems** study friendship, team performance, fan behavior, team formation, faultline minimization, mobility, and conflict prediction. Friendship relates to individual and team performance, socializing, and publishing activity, while social-media and CQA systems analyze campaigns, public opinion, and spam.

17dfaa56d229970fcd65cfdf4bec2690a7d81aff.text:
# Retrieval, Crisis Analytics, and Multimodal Knowledge Extraction

This community connects information retrieval, social-media analytics, disaster response, and biomedical knowledge extraction.

**Retrieval and query expansion.** Query expansion supports internet search, information filtering, personalized social-document retrieval, cross-language retrieval, multimedia retrieval, and patent searching for prior art. Word embeddings, centroid-based expansion, professional crowdsourcing from patent examiners, expert-specified expansions, query weighting, and query ranking are compared across technical areas. A time-aware retrieval model mines temporal evidence from external collections and re-ranks results, improving precision on TREC microblog collections.

**Social-media event detection.** Power-law distributions characterize political Twitter mentions, retweets, and event-related tweet time series. Basic verification uses spatiotemporal distributions without content, while advanced verification adds semantic analysis and improves event-detection precision and recall. Multi-spatial-scale detection uses geo-tagged tweet streams, whose regional activity shows self-similarity. Tweet classification uses GloVe, crisis word vectors, and attention-based BLSTM-CNN models, supporting rescue prioritization.

**Disaster imagery and multimodality.** Flood image datasets with expert annotations support flooded-area determination, inundation-depth estimation, and water-pollution assessment. Content-based image retrieval and relevance feedback select images for flood-impact analysis and provide volunteered geographic information. Interactive multimodal learning uses multimodal embeddings for social-media search and exploration.

**Biomedical extraction.** Gextext performs unsupervised disease-network extraction from PubMed abstracts, benchmarking against GloVe and inferring diseasome graphs. Disease proximity relates to geodesic distance and gene-profile similarity.

3cd869ed1850f8f99b9d02c0931f8bc6f92f3270.text:
## Social Media Analysis, Elections, and Topic Discovery

This community centers on Twitter-based analysis of political events, information diffusion, and content classification. Election studies use Twitter data for outcome prediction, manipulation analysis, voter fraud and suppression detection, and election-interference detection. Datasets include the 2016 U.S. presidential election, 2018 U.S. midterms, and 2019 Argentine elections; prediction is compared with traditional polling and includes Alberto Fernandez and Mauricio Macri. Troll accounts and foreign-interference datasets document misinformation campaigns, while interaction graphs quantify account influence. Population bias and political-ideology inference are identified as confounders.

Methods for diffusion and influence include graph analysis, network theory, two-mode networks, and retweet-activity visualization. RTbust applies unsupervised feature extraction to the 10-million-retweet dataset to detect social bots, achieving an F1 score of 0.87. Impact is characterized through reach, hot streaks, temporal clustering, buildup and falloff, and changes in user networks and content.

A second theme is topic discovery and tracing. LDA, labeled LDA, and hierarchical Dirichlet process LDA support latent-topic discovery, forum-post classification, and mapping posts to lectures and readings in Coursera courses. Query optimization uses maximum set coverage to retrieve topical tweets through the Twitter Search API, targeting high recall and improved F1 over the firehose. Sub-event detection supports retrospective crisis analysis of Hurricane Harvey and the 2015 Nepal earthquake.

20b024fd8a91f4cf8e5fda2f9e10d1a3e45ee3be.text:
## Coordinated Influence and Twitter Diffusion

This community examines influence campaigns, coordination networks, and information diffusion on Twitter. A network-based framework constructs coordination networks from behavioral traces shared among accounts, enabling the identification of coordinated Twitter accounts. Such networks are studied in influence-campaign case studies involving the U.S. elections, Hong Kong protests, the Syrian civil war, and cryptocurrencies.

A separate focus is diffusion prediction for Twitter events. Events are classified as either informative or trending, whose diffusion processes and governing user features differ significantly. Random forests select features for prediction, while Bayesian logistic regression learns and predicts information diffusion. The resulting model achieves 93% accuracy for informative events and 86% for trending events.

Together, the work connects behavioral and network-based detection of coordinated activity with predictive modeling of how information spreads across distinct types of Twitter events.

48ad8083f5fcab9da7efb35f56504320ef039385.text:
## Multimodal Retrieval and Actionable Disaster Information on Twitter

This community links multimodal representation learning with disaster-related Twitter analysis. A deep multimodal convolutional recurrent network learns vision and language representations end-to-end from the Twitter Image Tweet Dataset and is evaluated on MS-COCO. Using hinge-based triplet ranking, it distinguishes matching from mismatching image–text pairs and infers image-text similarity. These representations support cross-modal retrieval in a shared visual-textual embedding space, enabling images to be matched with sentences.

A second theme is disaster hashtag identification and actionable information filtering. The Disaster Hashtag Dataset contains annotated disaster-related tweets from Twitter, with hashtags indicating actionable information; associated resources are available on GitHub. Long Short-Term Memory models address disaster hashtag identification, evaluated with F1 score and reaching 92.22%. Actionable hashtags support filtering tweets for actionable disaster-response information. Multi-task learning provides a framework for LSTM models and improves ADR extraction performance by 7.2% in F1 score.

Twitter also supplies datasets involving sexual-harassment stories and news diffusion cascades from the United States and Italy, connecting social-media content, information diffusion, and applied crisis-response analysis.

f61991c2169e213ac0af7287bf7b2561a0c7b56e.text:
## Social Media, Crises, Influence, and Analytics

This community centers on Twitter and related platforms as sources for social-media analysis, crisis response, news dissemination, political activity, and market prediction. Twitter provides textual and imagery content, tweets, hashtags, trending topics, and datasets such as CrisisMMD, multimodal disaster data, attack datasets, and the Russian troll Twitter dataset. CrisisMMD supports crisis response and management through annotated natural-disaster data; processed social-media information supports situational awareness for humanitarian organizations.

State-sponsored trolls—including Russian and Iranian actors linked to the Internet Research Agency—use Twitter for online political campaigns, disinformation warfare, and news dissemination. Hawkes processes quantify influence and model news spread across Twitter, Gab, and 4chan/pol. Russian trolls were more influential overall, although Iranian trolls were more influential on /pol/. Gab’s 22-million-post dataset supports research on hate-speech diffusion.

News research examines Western and Arab media coverage of the Beirut and Paris attacks, including coverage and sympathy bias. Trust Scores in Social Media and multiple regression analysis connect news-organization trustworthiness, Twitter use, quantity of tweets, and audience engagement.

Other applications include an adaptive, sentiment-based short-term stock-trading system evaluated against the DJTATO index and optimal trading results. Finally, Twitter supports hashtag activism such as #ILookLikeAnEngineer, addressing gender and engineering diversity in the STEM workforce.

1226a183df1444043d57adc1cbb5bb111d23066b.text:
## Twitter Research: Polarization, Bots, Diffusion, and User Interests

This community centers on Twitter-based social media mining and analysis, including sentiment, user influence, tweeting behaviour, message virality, and communication across geographical regions. Political studies examine polarization, ideology, news sources, and entertainment preferences, with datasets from the 2016 U.S. election, Brexit referendum, 2018 Turkish elections, French presidential election, Brett Kavanaugh nomination, and debate events. The Turkish election work analyzes 108 million tweets, Erdogan’s reelection, and the shift from a parliamentary to presidential system.

A major theme is misinformation and manipulation. Hoaxy supports large-scale analysis of misinformation and fact-checking; social bots pollute content, spread misinformation, and initiate retweet cascades. Bot detection uses lexical diversity, machine-learning classifiers, BotOrNot, diffusion networks, k-core decomposition, and centrality-based disruption. Russian troll-account datasets connect state-sponsored manipulation with election and Brexit-related retweet amplification.

Other work models latent diffusion structure and identifies implicit, multidimensional topic preferences using a multi-topic preference model and mixed Gaussian model. Twitter data also supports spam and botnet detection, software-related tweet identification, adverse-drug-reaction surveillance, opioid relapse prediction, and alcohol-interest analysis. The #ilooklikeanengineer campaign illustrates connective action, gender-diversity advocacy, and event-, media-, industry-, and personality-driven triggers.

f1f0d1d1dc72ac5ae6c4aeaedd510212c9816a90.text:
## Twitter Networks, Influence, and Information Diffusion

This community centers on Twitter as a social networking service and research data source, accessed through the Twitter Standard API and network sampling. Studies examine users, follow networks, communities, roles, topical communities, hashtags, and public discussion topics using complex network analysis, exploratory and topical analysis, network embeddings, spatial analysis, and tweet representation.

A major theme is influence: follower numbers, user importance metrics, relevance, coverage, reach, engagement, and activity help identify influential accounts and predict election outcomes, including the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. Network sampling retrieves influential accounts, while hashtag-based methods support election analysis and comparisons with author keywords.

Another theme is information diffusion. Social contagion, peer influence, network cascades, hashtag cascades, node adoption thresholds, and threshold intervals describe how information spreads. The opacity problem means cascades may reveal threshold intervals rather than point estimates. Rumor detection and classification address misinformation propagation using two-step classification, novel features, feature grouping, and mixed- and single-rumor datasets.

The community also studies verification, anomalous and extreme tweeters, topic diversity, social neighborhoods, and within-group interactions. Applications include disaster communication and flood prevention using Hurricane Harvey, hurricanes Irene and Sandy, tornadoes, and other U.S. disaster datasets; political imagery and state-sponsored information warfare involving Russian troll accounts; and “Why I Didn’t Report” reasons using supervised analysis.

18b1f82f2eca533fdc6bf607f67a1b44828c4e6a.text:
## Data Quality, Adaptive Sensing, and Public-Health Analytics

This community links machine learning, data cleaning, interdisciplinary science, social sensing, and immunization policy.
