In scientific-paper analysis, a collection of more than 1.2 million papers spanning computer science, mathematics, and physics is used to study citation patterns and interdisciplinary research, including increased citations from mathematics and physics to computer science.

Data quality is a central theme. CleanML benchmarks how cleaning affects downstream machine-learning models, using statistical hypothesis testing and the Benjamini–Yekutieli procedure to control false discoveries. MLClean provides a unified framework integrating preprocessing and joint data cleaning with machine learning, and supports fairer models. In-processing and post-processing methods also improve training and trained models.

The ASSED system combines machine learning with physical and annotated sensors for adaptive social-sensor filtering, dynamic filter selection, and physical-event detection. It addresses concept drift and supports landslide detection, achieving 0.988 accuracy after four years without expert intervention, compared with 0.762 for static classifiers.

Twitter data support bot and automated-account classification, while also providing spatial and demographic information for vaccination and disease-risk estimation. Vector-borne disease risk assessment, validated on the 2016 Florida Zika outbreak, identifies neighborhood-level disease-importation risk to guide targeted public-health intervention. Political communication, vaccine hesitancy, public disorientation, MMR coverage, and Italian immunization policy connect these methods to vaccination outcomes.

e8cce281e5c0ff3aa4b946713ddd1458c9a2e6f3.text:
## Machine Learning, NLP, and Applied Information Systems

This community centers on machine learning and natural language processing, including their relationship to artificial intelligence, data science, knowledge organization systems, and web knowledge extraction. Machine learning supports location, employment-status, popularity, trustworthiness, hate-speech, abuse, rumor, and like-farm detection, as well as computational advertising and article-hashtag ranking. Timeline-based features, lexical and morphological modeling, tree-based models, deep learning architectures, sequence-to-sequence models, multi-label classification, and string similarity are recurring methods; F-measure, precision, recall, gold standards, and similarity metrics support evaluation.

NLP is adapted to informal language, neologisms, Persian, mathematical formulae, legal documents, biomedical concepts, keyphrase extraction, and article similarity. Mathematical information retrieval includes semantic retrieval, vector-space representations, mathematical notation, Mathoid, computer algebra systems, format conversion, and dataset-reference detection.

Social-media research uses Twitter data, microblog posts, the Harvey Twitter Corpus, and Twitter Explorer for agenda setting, political discussion, socioeconomic estimation, disease risk, trending topics, and abuse analysis. Other application areas include plagiarism and paraphrase detection, news recommendation, question answering, and music representation using Spotify datasets, playlists, songs, and artist, album, and track information. Frugal streaming and one-/two-memory algorithms address streaming data, while interactive network visualization and spatial analysis support exploration.

2e203b2ee6d262b79c5e3e62ab87cedffc23516d.text:
## Social Media, Elections, Rumors, and Mobility

This community links social-media analysis with election prediction, rumor detection, opinion polarization, and mobility mapping. Election polls from news outlets were evaluated for accuracy and bias in the 2016 U.S. presidential election, using election results as the reference. Social media was investigated as an alternative prediction source: Twitter data supports sentiment analysis, election prediction, sentiment-drift analysis, and demographic-bias quantification. Sentiment drift can reflect changes over time and correlate with real-world events.

Rumor detection identifies rumor tweets by matching them with verified rumor articles, providing insight into rumor behavior in American politics. Online text streams—including social media and news streams—represent public discourse. Retweet behavior is central to polarization analysis in online communities: retweets are often treated as endorsements, but out-of-context quotes and retweet latency can reveal or obscure antagonism between groups and produce misleading interpretations.

A separate mobility mapping methodology uses open big data, Twitter data, origin-destination surveys, configurable spatial boundaries, and census districts to study mobility patterns in public and social-interaction spaces. The Concepcion metropolitan area is its study setting, including movement toward and the impact of public spaces.

67d2d5ca86afdbdbe7ca1c9b69685a213ca1556a.text:
## Machine Learning, NLP, and Social-Data Analysis

This community centers on machine learning and natural language processing (NLP), positioned within artificial intelligence and data science. NLP supports argumentation mining, abuse detection, article similarity, place-name harvesting, biomedical concept extraction, and full-text similarity search. Machine learning complements string similarity and NLP, enabling web knowledge extraction, user-trustworthiness prediction, employment-status prediction, table recognition, and question-answering metasystems. The F-measure is a recurring evaluation metric; one question-answering metasystem outperforms its best single system by 14% F-measure.

Twitter data and microblog posts form a major application area. NLP and machine learning analyze political discussion, agenda setting, trending topics, customer needs, electoral outcomes, demographic bias, disease risk, and mobility patterns. Twitter Explorer supports exploration, while MP HCNN is evaluated on Twitter data. Mobility mapping uses Twitter data to infer functional zones and socioeconomic statistics.

Other themes include recommendation and behavioral analysis, including personalized news recommendation, online dating recommendation, popularity prediction, browsing behavior, shopping patterns, and user recommendations. Information and scholarly systems address plagiarism detection, paraphrase plagiarism, dataset-reference detection, mathematical formulae, and semantic retrieval, with systems such as NewsDeps, LES, Mathoid, and NIST digital libraries.

2d91de2773f3fdfe2493c48a14960fc41cf35784.text:
## Search and Ranking Bias in Political Queries

This community focuses on bias in search results, distinguishing between **data bias** and **ranking bias**. Input data can generate data bias, while the ranking system can generate ranking bias. Both forms contribute to overall search bias.

A **bias quantification framework** measures bias arising from two sources: the input data and the ranking system. The framework is applied to a dataset of **politics-related queries**, providing a way to assess bias in politically relevant search results.

The community also connects search bias to **public opinion**: bias in top-ranked results can shape how people perceive issues and potentially influence public opinion. Overall, the relationships describe a pipeline in which input data and ranking-system behavior create distinct biases, these biases produce biased search results, and a quantification framework evaluates them in the context of political queries.

2eca570da068d3c2df7264617814a148eee8b4ac.text:
## Machine Learning, Reasoning, Visualization, and Computing Careers

This community connects machine learning and artificial intelligence with natural language processing, sentiment/opinion mining, and argumentation mining. Historical tweets support language and sentiment analysis; web scraping can collect arbitrary date ranges and bypass Twitter API restrictions, while the Twitter API has a three-week chronological-query limit. Machine learning also supports opinion trend inference from hashtag co-occurrence signals, including inferred support for Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump, using statistical physics of complex networks.

The Vadalog knowledge graph management system integrates with Jupyter and supports data wrangling, expressive logical reasoning, probabilistic reasoning, and complex reasoning for advanced knowledge graphs. Argumentation mining can exploit social-web data, multiple sources, and background knowledge.

Another theme concerns large graph visualization. Topological similarity and graph kernels estimate layout appearance and aesthetic metrics more efficiently than computing layouts, while matching human perceptual similarity. User studies using eye tracking assess this perception.

Finally, R3 analyzes career trajectories and models temporal transitions and employer retention across academia, industry, and government, including post-PhD computing careers. Computing research encompasses artificial intelligence, network security, and hardware design.

078e4cf571a6175b8c90481dcde985c7bcb17c0a.text:
## Community Report: Retrieval, Ranking, Diversity, and Applied Modeling

This community centers on information retrieval, especially ad hoc retrieval, document ranking, relevance assessment, and social media search. Retrieval models and neural rankers use click logs or relevance judgments, while HINT combines local matching and global decision layers to aggregate relevance signals across granularities. MP-HCNN ranks short social media posts using hierarchical convolutional layers and pooling-based similarity measurement, integrating character-, word-, and phrase-level evidence.

Query expansion uses pseudo-relevance feedback, locally trained embedding learning, concept hierarchies, latent semantic spaces, and sequence-to-sequence neural networks. A query expansion engine is trained and tested on open datasets and keyword-extracted training data. Content-based recommendation and playlist continuation are framed through ad hoc retrieval.

Web2Text improves retrieval through boilerplate removal and sequence labeling, achieving strong CleanEval results and improving ClueWeb12 retrieval. EXS applies adapted LIME posthoc explanations to clarify neural-ranker results, query intent, and document relevance.

The community also evaluates retrieval-system diversity. Rank-Biased Utility extends Rank-Biased Precision, accounts for user effort, and is studied with diversity metrics and diversification campaigns. A constraint-based axiomatic framework analyzes metric suitability.

Finally, composite compartmental models extend SIR models to multiple pathogens, using Twitter-derived seasonal influenza-like-illness time series, epidemiological data, and overcomplete dictionaries.

345b8e6bce1e362c7af81e5387df979efc125b66.text:
## Social Platforms, Popularity, Expertise, and Network Risk

This community centers on online social networks and platforms—especially Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn, Google+, Myspace, ResearchGate, and Venmo—and their users, profiles, ties, interactions, and content. Facebook supports friendship, link recommendation, news consumption, public tagging, reactions, comments, advertising interests, and political profiling; YouTube supports video sharing, comments, engagement, popularity, monetization, and cross-cultural consumption.

A major theme is modeling content popularity and dissemination. Video popularity prediction, popularity dynamics, video longevity, view count, likes, comments, and video engagement are studied using diffusion models, collective diffusion models, copying processes, agent-based models, temporal text network models, and the infectious-recovery SIR model. YouTube video datasets, popular-video listings, and engagement graphs support this work.

Other methods address ranking, search, and expertise: fairness-aware ranking, personalized search and federated search, expertise ranking, topical expert mining, link and hyperlink prediction, and personalized posting schedules. ResearchGate scores and research-quality indices connect professional networks to expertise discovery.

The community also examines privacy, abuse, manipulation, and misinformation through attribute-inference and friendship-identification attacks, profile-cloning detection, fake engagement, like farms, junk-news aggregators, malicious pages, and online radicalization. Network structure is analyzed with configuration models, multiplex approaches, connected components, clique distributions, robustness, and attack strategies, including weak and strong ties, cultural convergence, and gender inequality.

0529e04985beabb44d58cf8a53c440b62ed7b234.text:
## Retrieval Evaluation and Interpretable Ranking

This community focuses on evaluating, interpreting, and improving information-retrieval and ranking systems. **Document ranking** uses textual features, while retrieval-model interpretability explains how and why documents are ranked for queries. Intent modeling interprets ranker behavior through **query intent**, explaining both query intent and document relevance; it is evaluated on the **ClueWeb test collection**. A simpler retrieval model approximates text-based and neural ranking models, including **DRMM**, and its closed-form notation enables interpretation-accuracy measurement.

The community also covers learned **query expansion**, trained with Q-learning and applied with a simpler retrieval model to estimate an underlying ranker’s behavior. OpenAI Gym provides a Q-learning environment, while Pyndri supports applications involving learned query expansion.

Evaluation relies on **TREC Eval**, **PyTREC Eval**, and Python interfaces, with PyTREC Eval combined with Pyndri and OpenAI Gym. Metrics include **NDCG**, **RankDCG**, CTR, and bounce rate. RankDCG satisfies proposed ranking-evaluation criteria and has a public package.

Finally, cost-sensitive weighting learns semantic representations for tail pairs, improves ad retrieval in the Bing Sponsored Search setting, raises CTR, reduces bounce rate, and is evaluated on Amazon product recommendation data.

43605b0ca298d9e92046bcba70b5fd42947546b5.text:
### Social Platforms, Popularity, Expertise, and Trust

This community centers on online social networks and platforms—especially Facebook, YouTube, Google+, LinkedIn, ResearchGate, and online video services—as sources of behavioral records, profiles, messages, comments, likes, shares, and social-media content. Facebook research covers friendship structure, weak and strong ties, cross-network account matching, link recommendation, news and scientific-news consumption, political advertising, radicalization, malicious pages, like farms, and reputation manipulation. YouTube research emphasizes video popularity, engagement, comments, views, video longevity, cultural consumption, spam, clickbait, and recommendation.

Key analytical methods include agent-based, social-network, temporal-text, collective-diffusion, infectious-recovery (SIR), structural-user-choice, behavioral-analysis, statistical-analysis, and iterative-ranking models. Systems and datasets such as the YouTube Video Dataset, Facebook Profile Dataset, Pushshift Telegram Dataset, malicious Facebook pages, and ResearchGate Q&A posts support prediction and classification.

A second major theme is expertise and reputation: topical expert mining, personalized expertise search, expertise ranking, scientist ranking, ResearchGate scores, and research-quality indices. Privacy and security work addresses attribute-inference and friendship-identification attacks, privacy leakage, profile cloning, abuse, and enterprise cyber-attack prediction. Fairness-aware ranking, gender analysis, gender inequality, and female-authored research examine discrimination in platform and scholarly ecosystems.

955cc1627a91675528c6699003c5aa9873ba6cab.text:
## Social, Group, and Food Recommendation Research

This community links recommendation, social networking, and personalized interaction systems. Food recommender systems recommend cooking inspiration, restaurant meals, and supermarket products, with potential to promote healthy eating while facing design challenges. Food recommendation also includes individual and group settings.

Social graphs and social networking services provide user-user connections and social profiles for friend and group recommendation. Psychometrics enriches friend recommendation through personality traits and extended social profiles, including demographic information and smartphone sensor data. Distributed social networking services address development without central knowledge of the social graph, while cross-site linking supports service integration and user attraction on platforms such as Medium.

Cross-domain social recommendation connects information and social domains through bridge users. Neural social collaborative ranking integrates social connections and user-item interactions, propagating bridge-user embeddings to non-bridge users and evaluating performance on real-world datasets.

Probabilistic neighborhood-based recommendation estimates preferences with a probabilistic graphical model, treating similarity as an unobserved factor and formulating estimation as posterior maximization. Its multilayer extension learns feature-based similarity descriptors and achieves accurate preference estimation.

An axiomatic approach analyzes group recommendation and ranking systems. Although axioms specify desired requirements, an impossibility result shows that mutual satisfaction may be unreachable. Related systems include random-walk, trust-based, and social-choice approaches. Finally, Soc2Seq generates textual replies using social graphs, content preferences, and conversational style.

4794494661eb749868daa1e6a8a909a125e4611e.text:
## Community Report: Recommender Systems, Social Networks, and Responsible Data Management

This community connects recommendation research with social-network analysis, food applications, data management, and algorithmic responsibility.

Recommendation topics include multi-stakeholder, group, reciprocal, online-marketplace, online-dating, recipe, diet, ingredient-substitution, and healthy-food recommendation. Food recommender systems use user signals and datasets to support meals, recipes, menus, supermarket products, restaurant meals, cooking inspiration, and healthier eating. Group recommendation is treated as a specialization of food recommendation and as a component of multi-stakeholder systems. Collaborative filtering models user taste and attractiveness to recommend initial or reciprocal contacts, while random-walk systems provide group recommendations.

Axiomatic approaches analyze tie-strength and centrality measures, group-recommendation requirements, trust-based systems, social choice, and projective maps. Related network methods include influence-based centrality, harmonic and Bayesian centrality, effective resistance, graph symmetrization, Laplacian matrices, sampling, degree anonymization, and locally trained embeddings. These support studies of social status, interpersonal influence, user similarity, flaming, and signed networks.

Data-management themes include data lakes, cloud databases, big-data processing, state management, database security, range queries, and algebraic integration. GDPR, privacy, individual rights, causal algorithmic fairness, responsibility by design, and automated-decision law frame responsible data use. Evaluation relies on datasets, empirical studies, recipe ratings, and Kendall’s tau divergence.

b41f5a5a4ae3dcb5be3c371896e220579305136e.text:
# Influence, Diversity, Evolution, and Network Dynamics

This community centers on influence maximization: selecting a seed set of \(k\) nodes to maximize expected influence spread or the number of aware users. Extensions address targeted influence maximization, audience diversification across communities, and seed diversification using seed diversity and monotone submodular diversity functions over categorical or numerical attributes. Aditum solves diversity-sensitive targeted influence maximization under the triggering diffusion model, reverse influence sampling, and provides a \((1-1/e-\epsilon)\)-approximation. Seed diversification also uses non-monotonic submodular maximization with a \(1/e-\epsilon\) guarantee; economic objectives include perfect substitutes, perfect complements, and Cobb–Douglas utilities.

For incomplete networks, the seed-and-observe query model, probe-and-seed algorithm, and edge queries support discovery and influence estimation with almost tight approximation guarantees. Reinforcement-learning agents learn network-discovery policies and improve influence spread by 10–36%; transferable policies are evaluated across four social-network domains.

Evolving influence maximization (EIM) alternates seed selection with knowledge learning in temporally growing networks, using a bandit-based framework to learn changing influence probabilities.

A related opinion-formation strand combines agent-based modeling, attitude-change and group-behavior theories, evolutionary game theory, credibility, recipient characteristics, and situational factors. Finally, path-anomaly detection analyzes variable-length temporal paths, including chronological-order anomalies, within graph-constrained networks.

39ceedc061eee3a89fb0e4a7ecc76aa8a00639ef.text:
## Tie Strength, Social Networks, and Targeted Recommendation

This community focuses on estimating **tie strength**—the interaction strength between entities in **online social networks**—and applying it to ranking, marketing, and recommendation. **Tie strength estimation** supports **targeted marketing**, improves recommendation reliability, and enhances the **ranking of dominant entities**.

The network context includes **Facebook** and **Digg**. Facebook categorizes users into **advertiser interest categories** based on music interests, while music genres provide a basis for inferring those interests. Targeted marketing can also be implemented through a **decision support system**.

Methodologically, the community includes **partial differential equations (PDEs)**, particularly **reaction-diffusion equations**. These models use **cyber distances**, such as friendship hops, and are validated with datasets collected from Digg. Overall, the relationships connect social-network interaction modeling with tie-strength estimation, PDE-based techniques, advertiser categorization, recommendation, and marketing-oriented decision support.

e1779eba5f63bae0e58c5a735c8c1dd9f2f6ff2f.text:
## Social Networks, Influence, Privacy, and Political Information

This community examines online social networks as systems shaped by user behavior, social structure, information and communication technologies, and third-party applications accessing user data. It distinguishes endogenous influence, arising from network structure and user state, from exogenous influence, arising externally. Influence source disentanglement uses activation cascades—including simulated and Facebook political-survey cascades—to classify user activation and identify influential user groups.

False information forms a major theme: it spreads across the Web and social networks, can weaponize information in campaigns, manipulate public opinion, and affect elections. The false information ecosystem covers perception, propagation, detection, and containment, including political false information that may spread faster and farther.

Computational politics applies computational methods to election-campaign persuasion, political affiliation analysis, political debates, and participation. Social surveys and free-response text classification support public-opinion analysis, while opinion mining addresses user stance.

Methods for network analysis include network shrinkage estimation, James–Stein estimators, adaptive single-pass sampling, and unbiased higher-order dependency estimation for streaming networks, aiming to reduce estimation error. User dynamics are modeled with networked oscillation models and differential equations incorporating Laplacian matrices.

Privacy and governance include geo-location inference with graph convolutional neural networks on geo-tagged tweets, attribute generalization, relation-based access control, predicate calculus, and answer set programming. These address privacy preferences, access conditions, privacy protection, and stance-profiling implications.

59291d43065cd4ab219ba3a027e5ddb08afeb9d8.text:
## Provenance, Reproducibility, and Data-Intensive Research

This community centers on reproducibility, provenance, metadata, and scalable analysis of scientific and web data. Reproducibility concerns validating and reusing computational experiments, supported by versioned workflows, data provenance, computational context, multi-seed evaluation, and hyperparameter evaluation. **ReproWD** facilitates reproducibility, while **CRISTAL** captures and manages provenance, supports provenance tracking, and orchestrates large-scale analyses, including in the N4U project.

Workflows produce provenance traces through workflow engines and provenance services. Provenance supports dataset identity and lineage, traceability in data publication, clinical analysis, visualization interaction, and fine-grained analysis of output origins. Scientific datasets are described by scientific metadata, annotated by users, and generated by scientific codes and large-scale simulations. Integrated metadata management and systems such as **Fluidinfo** support dataset publication and metadata management. Dataset version control supports branching, merging, and difference operations on large datasets.

The community also addresses aggregate-query analysis and provenance: value-level annotation captures provenance where tuple-level annotation is inadequate, while unknown-data-impact estimation studies aggregate queries. Scalable exploration uses **Zenvisage**, transparent autoscaling, and 2D partitioning. Semi-supervised methods—including **PACE**, **RELP**, and Gaussian Random Markov models—support video longevity, tagging, classification, and other prediction tasks. Video popularity prediction combines hosting APIs, search and browsing logs, embeds, links, and web traces.

4773fa92f399374c3e6c634665226c62d1011a22.text:
### Graph Analytics, Sampling, and Networked Recommendation Systems

This community centers on scalable graph analysis, network structure, and recommendation applications.

**Graph sampling and estimation** include egocentric subgraph frequency estimation, random-walk sampling, closed-walk samplers, probability sampling, and labeled or unlabeled neighbor estimators. These methods estimate graph size, graphlet and subgraph frequencies, clique distributions, and maximal-clique prevalence, using safety margins, exact counting, or approximate greedy algorithms. Frequent subgraph mining, subgraph discovery, clique discovery, and subgraph isomorphism address pattern analysis.

**Network structure and resilience** cover multigroup and core–periphery networks, bridging or redundant interconnections, coordination, structural stability, network efficiency, and formation dynamics. Resilience is assessed with invulnerability indices, graph eigenvalues, scenario analysis, and attacking/target-network models.

**Recommendation and social systems** include domain adaptation for logged data and biased policies, cross-network node classification, group recommendation, random-walk recommendation, and axiomatic analysis of tie strength and elite size. ORFEL detects defamation, illegitimate promotion, and fraud in user–product bipartite graphs, using asynchronous vertex-centric processing and reporting high detection rates and speedups.

**Scalable graph computing and visualization** feature BatchLayout, ForceAtlas2, OpenOrd, minibatch processing, cache blocking, and force approximation. Other themes include patent retrieval, knowledge extraction, graph embeddings, query routing, and GPU-oriented execution.

7b22f27dbcffbe9a66b10109fb4f17e2740ab996.text:
## Provenance, Reproducible Data, and Scalable Analysis

This community centers on managing scientific datasets, metadata, provenance, and reproducible workflows. Scientific codes generate large datasets, while integrated metadata management stores metadata within datasets and supports extreme-scale science, including plasma physics and neuroscience. Provenance services capture workflow specifications and execution traces, enabling traceability, introspection, and reproducibility of experiments.

Key systems include CRISTAL, adapted for workflow and provenance tracking and used in the N4U project; ProvDB, which manages metadata across collaborative data-science workflows; ReproWD, which supports reproducibility; and Data Atlas, which indexes and provides parameterized access to clinical and neuroimaging datasets. Dataset version control, implemented through DataHub, supports branching, merging, and differencing of large datasets.

The community also studies provenance for aggregate queries. Value-level annotation addresses limitations of tuple-level annotation, while unknown-data-impact estimation and sensitivity analysis examine how query results and rankings change. Zenvisage supports exploration of large datasets, and 2D partitioning improves processing.

Learning applications include video popularity prediction, video longevity estimation, and personalized image tagging, using semi-supervised methods such as PACE and Gaussian Random Markov models. Security-related work examines location authentication, proximity graphs, Sybil devices, and virtual vehicles.

3c0b321f53b0e9d2515f121496861d66c4cc0cef.text:
## Facebook Advertising, User Data, and Junk News

This community focuses on Facebook as a major online advertising platform, ranking second to Google by advertising revenue. Facebook delivers ads and other information through the newsfeed; ads constitute 10–15% of received information, while users see a median of 70 ads weekly from 12 advertisers. Large-scale ad exposure analysis uses the Facebook Ad Exposure Dataset, containing more than 7 million ads from approximately 140,000 advertisers.

The community also examines targeting and profiling. Only up to 22.76% of assigned interests relate to received ads, a pattern described as overprofiling. Statistical analysis of personal-information and wall-activities datasets supports behavioral analysis, including gender-based information-revealing behavior. Facebook user profiles provide the underlying personal and wall-activity data.

IMCrawler, based on iMacros, uses web data extraction to crawl Facebook user profiles and addresses limitations of social-network APIs. 

Junk news, including conspiracy theories, targets military personnel with claims about military affairs and national security. Veterans and military personnel share relatively little junk news, while users interested in the political right distribute substantial amounts. Military and veteran pages interact with political-conspiracy subgroups on Facebook, and current and former military personnel interact with conspiracy subgroups on Twitter.

f4adc26a078f4c35810a24cfc191ce4f9c4e2c9d.text:
### Community Report: Learning Schemas and Querying Distributed Data

This community connects formal schema learning, query languages, and Web-scale query execution.

**Schema learning and verification** focus on disjunctive multiplicity schemas, including their disjunction-free restriction. These schemas retain much of the expressiveness of document type definitions and support schema satisfiability, tree membership, containment, implication, and twig-query satisfiability analysis. Learning algorithms use positive and negative examples to produce minimal schemas, with soundness, completeness, polynomial question and time complexity, and learnability as central criteria. Positive-only learning also applies to simple path and path-subsumption-free tree queries.

**Query learning and logic** include qhorn queries, quantified Horn expressions, query matching, and verification from user responses. QSQN evaluates queries over Horn knowledge bases using bounded term depth, depth-first search, and tail-recursion elimination, with fixed-bound polynomial data complexity.

**Linked-data querying** includes LDQL and link-traversal-based execution over the Web of Linked Data and RDF documents. Formal semantics and abstract execution models address soundness and completeness, while syntactic conditions identify feasible complete execution. Triple Pattern Fragments reduce server load but increase network and client-side load.

Other themes include a flexible RDF change framework with a change ontology, sensitivity analysis of rankings and query results, big-array I/O optimization, and algorithmic systematic-review convergence.

54b8ca9464751664bc2bcfc2e20996e3e799b805.text:
## Social Platforms, Political Advertising, and Business Networks

This community connects Facebook- and Google-based platforms with political advertising, online communities, and business partnership discovery.

Facebook provides group-based social networking, including question-answer interactions, and contains a Facebook group dataset with approximately 280 million user reactions. User opinions expressed through content interactions support a business similarity model, which captures virtual relationships among businesses. Business community detection identifies related business communities, while business outlier detection finds non-obvious relationships within them. These outliers may reveal strategic business partnerships. A partnership recommendation service applies this similarity-based approach to recommend potential partnerships.

The community also examines political communication and polarization. Content interactions can produce echo chambers, reinforcing confirmation bias, polarization, and misinformation cascades. Among co-commenters, lexical convergence may indicate emerging collective identities; among opposing users, it may reflect development of a common vocabulary that enables dialogue.

Facebook and Google created political ad archives to improve political advertising transparency. Political advertising generated billions of impressions and more than $300 million in spending. However, archive limitations enabled deception and bypassing. Quasi for-profit media companies created deceptive online communities for political messaging, aided by lower regulatory requirements on online platforms.

4df95e74a535e13e552a94144b20059c10855d3b.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Retrieval, Multimodal Embeddings, and Network Prediction

This community centers on representation learning and retrieval across heterogeneous data. **Recurrent Binary Embedding (RBE)** learns compact binary representations with residual vectors, enabling bit-wise similarity computation, near-lossless top-*k* neighbor selection, and exhaustive retrieval over more than a billion candidates. Integrated into a multi-GPU retrieval system, it outperformed a production retrieval system on paid-search data.

For multilingual scholarly discovery, **HRLHG** learns interpretable publication representations from heterogeneous graphs and multilingual repositories. Its supervised hierarchical random walk combines local task-independent and global task-specific information in a joint low-dimensional embedding space for cross-language citation recommendation and neighborhood discovery.

Cross-modality retrieval uses shared embedding spaces and **canonical correlation analysis (CCA)**. A CCA neural layer combines analytically computed projections with pairwise ranking loss, supporting text-to-image, audio-to-sheet-music, and zero-shot retrieval, with nearest-neighbor search.

The community also studies network structure and prediction. Simplicial closure, tie strength, and edge density indicate higher-order organization; higher-order link prediction emphasizes local information and requires less long-range information than pairwise prediction. Temporal evolution is examined across 19 higher-order interaction datasets.

Finally, same-user account prediction on Facebook datasets frames multiple-account detection, achieving reported AUCs of 0.952 and 0.877. Scholarly impact analysis uses Altmetrics, Mendeley, Lattes, and GetLattesData for Brazilian researchers.

e991f1bdbb7eabe9690b6ad95a5d3583ba178d20.text:
## COVID-19 Advertising, Misinformation, and Public Discourse

This community examines coronavirus advertisements as a resource for quality control in public health communication and public discourse. The advertisements incorporate COVID-19 into their messaging and agendas and include several instances of possible misinformation, including bioweapons conspiracy theories.

Facebook enables the rapid spread of misleading, false, or agenda-driven information. The Facebook Ads Library is used to examine advertisements on Facebook and was the source for discovering and collecting the coronavirus advertisements dataset. Related Facebook user data contains nearly 725,000 social relations and data from more than 5,000 social media users.

The broader context is the COVID-19 infodemic: COVID-19 prompted concerns about an infodemic of fake news, and the World Health Organization warned of a possible infodemic. Together, these entities connect advertising analysis, misinformation, social media users, social relations, and public health communication.

a0d9aa38501ef4726d1537a7ddc5fef82a6ac126.text:
## Search, Recommendation, and AI-Assisted Scholarly Evaluation

This community links exploratory search research, music-event recommendation, and manuscript classification. A user study in a social science digital library examined exploratory search activities through eye tracking and gaze metrics. Keyword search was most frequent, while author searching and reference/citation browsing supported related-work discovery. Tree graph representations, including combined session trees, visualized search patterns and attention to document metadata through dwell time and fixations.

The Music Event Graph supports local music event recommendation using genre tags and artist-related information. Artist similarity is modeled with latent semantic analysis and social tags; importantly, even long-tail artists with small digital footprints may be represented. A user study evaluated the feasibility of this recommendation system.

The AI-assisted article classification system uses academic articles and author–editor interactions to support editorial decision-making. Machine-learning classifiers assess article classification, manuscript quality, and journal scope. Manuscript-quality estimation uses author and affiliation reputation, similarity to accepted papers, and keyword-search features; similarity is computed against an accepted-papers dataset. Journal editors are the organizational users of this system.

215c813b29e4a073b5c8ed839b94293e97cf7464.text:
## Community Report: Fair, Private, and Efficient Social-Media Intelligence

This community spans multimedia retrieval, social-media recommendation, fairness, privacy, and popularity modeling.

For heterogeneous multimedia data, multimodal hashing represents image-text and video-tag pairs as binary codes. The MCR method applies regularization to sigmoid outputs to reduce hashing-bit correlation, enabling fast XOR-based comparisons and shorter retrieval time for multimodal retrieval.

HIPIE uses YouTube video metadata and historical popularity series with a Hawkes Intensity Process to explain and predict video popularity. It supports viral-video identification, virality reasoning, and online-promotion response estimation.

Several works study Facebook’s News Feed. A reproducible measurement methodology parameterizes and validates an analytical model using time-to-live counters to model publisher visibility and occupancy. Measurements reveal visibility and occupancy bias, especially at the top of the feed; what-if analysis motivates a fairness-based News Feed design.

Fairness also concerns text summarization and representations. FairSumm generates high-quality summaries while reducing unequal group or source representation. A privacy adversarial framework removes private-attribute leakage, improving fairness while examining recommender-performance trade-offs.

AbuSniff analyzes Facebook friends and activity to identify perceived strangers and abusive friends, recommending protective actions such as unfriending or restricting access. Questionnaires, supervised learning, mutual-activity features, and multinational user studies evaluate acceptance and perceived protection.

Finally, 3Layers provides context-aware tag recommendations, compared with a popularity baseline; semantic cues affect acceptance differently in collaborative-tagging and individual-tagging settings.

360c3ba6d9e86b49e5d23a37f00fce1ef99d61f4.text:
## Screenshot Mining, User Inference, and Event Prediction

This community links screenshot-based information extraction with behavioral, demographic, and event forecasting.

A **smartphone screenshot** collection is organized as a **screenshot repository**. **Image preprocessing**, implemented with **OpenCV-based modules**, prepares images for **optical character recognition** and metadata extraction. An LSTM-based release of **Tesseract OCR** achieves 74% character-level accuracy. The processed repository supports **image retrieval** through a dedicated **vertical search engine** and can inform behavioral studies and **just-in-time health interventions**.

The community also addresses **demographic data inference** and **working profile prediction**. **Generalized additive models** use co-variables and **spatio-temporal entropy**, which captures user mobility behavior and mobility regularity, to infer demographic characteristics and improve the personalization and accuracy of mobile services. Working profile prediction achieves 87% accuracy.

For forecasting, machine-learning algorithms and **Twitter analytics** support **protest prediction**, validated on U.S. airport protests using event-specific features. **ARIMA**, **LSTM**, and **Hawkes Process** are evaluated for growth potential prediction; ARIMA achieves higher prediction accuracy than both LSTM and Hawkes Process.

ed04005ff5046988e2aedc084345d20a0bd6e076.text:
## Community Report: Learning from Social, Textual, and Network Data

This community centers on prediction, community discovery, topic modeling, and social/mobile sensing. Prediction accuracy is a major evaluation theme: parsimonious digital traces can match or exceed broader datasets; structural diversity improves popularity prediction; and hierarchical classification improves location prediction by moving from broad regions to cities. Reported systems and tasks include Frappe, smartphones, Android, iOS, home-location identification, working-profile prediction (87%), and page-suitability prediction (91%).

Hierarchical clustering supports core-community detection, compact-community construction, city-state identification, moving-point clustering, and brain-network analysis. It uses approaches including LexDFS, synchronization similarity, network-distance bounds, and linear-time algorithms. Community structures are compared through structure similarity, community transitivity, and hub dominance; language models and LDA are evaluated for preserving such structures, while multilayer community detection targets communities across network layers.

LDA and related unsupervised topic-modeling methods identify topic categories, support semantic mining, and analyze long or short texts, including question-answer pairs and policy records. Topic modeling also supports similar-question ranking and dengue outbreak detection, with seasonal regeneration for epidemic changes.

The community further connects citation behavior, social-link and property prediction, popularity trends, retrieval pipelines, and mobile-phone sensing. Methods include neural recommendation, supervised and ensemble classification, incremental and two-step learning, k-NN retrieval, and mixed-method validation.

3fc5511555e2edf8528521992920b3c12b21f444.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: Efficient Web, ML, and Multimedia Systems

This community centers on performance-enhancing systems for web browsing, machine-learning workflows, dynamic networks, and image search.

**SpeedReader** extends browser **reader mode** by applying **document tree translation** within the rendering pipeline before page rendering. Its page suitability prediction reaches **91% accuracy**, while transformed pages provide up to **84% bandwidth reduction** and **27× speedup**. By removing commonly recognized trackers and reducing tracker interactions and third-party requests, it improves privacy.

The **human-in-the-loop ML system**, preliminarily implemented as **Helix**, accelerates ML workflow development and iterative experimentation through change tracking, responsive feedback, introspection and debugging, background execution, and automation. Helix achieves speedups of up to **10×**.

For evolving networks, **GC-LSTM** combines a graph convolution network—which learns node structure from network snapshots—with an LSTM for temporal modeling. It performs end-to-end dynamic link prediction, including added and removed links, and is evaluated for key-link prediction, prediction accuracy, and error rate. Dynamic prediction is contrasted with static link prediction.

For image search, **Text2Vis** maps textual queries into a visual feature space using bag-of-words regressors and deep recurrent models capturing word order. The space uses **ResNet-152** pool5 or **AlexNet** fc6–fc7 features; these models are trained on ILSVRC12 and Places, respectively. Caption generation provides an alternative image-indexing strategy.

720e8dec86f7af6481afa63c7610808dba4fed12.text:
# Sentiment, Network Prediction, and Behavioral Structure

This community links three research themes.

**CARP** is a capsule-network-based sentiment architecture for user reviews. It extracts user viewpoints and item aspects, combines them into informative logic units, and infers associated sentiments. Its routing mechanism is **routing by bi-agreement**, and it substantially improves prediction accuracy across seven real-world datasets.

**Interaction prediction** concerns missing retweet, reply, and quote interactions, including those in a month-long Greek-speaking Twitter interaction dataset that also contains follow interactions. Higher-dimensional triads help predict interactions among highly active users, while in-degree and out-degree are important for less active users. User profiles and time locality affect predictive performance.

**Effective transitions** use isospectral matrix reductions to approximate eventual transition probabilities in biased random walks. The method predicts links in weighted, unweighted, directed, and undirected networks; its approximation often improves accuracy and has lower temporal complexity.

A music-streaming study uses large-scale user behavioral data to predict musical structure from acoustic content, rather than customary hand-labeled data. Skip events identify when listeners stop songs, and their timing correlates with musical structure; skipping distributions are independent of user cohort.

Finally, analysis of San Francisco urban park visits finds increased sentiment and reduced negativity, especially in greener regional parks. Nature contact is associated with mood and subjective well-being, while negation-word use decreases during visits.

a9ec62f6c1611b76a8a5f8a50ab25a9b57e481e9.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Streaming Analytics and Local Community Discovery

This community covers three connected areas: temporally evolving data, local graph analysis, and scalable aggregation.

**Temporally biased sampling (T-TBS and R-TBS)** adapts supervised-model training to evolving streams while retaining older data beyond a sliding window, improving robustness. R-TBS uses fractional samples and maximizes sample-size stability while bounding sample size; unlike T-TBS, it supports unknown time-varying arrival rates. Spark evaluates the approach, which also supports online model management through periodic retraining.

**Local graph partitioning and community search** analyze rich graphs using network structure, attribute data, and side information. AttriPart is a scalable attribute-aware partitioning method and an application of localforecasting for predicting local community evolution. It reportedly produces partitions up to 1.6 times denser and runs approximately 43 times faster than PageRank-Nibble. Single-community search identifies a target community using random node weights, with target nodes receiving higher weights on average; a variant of the method of moments supports this task. Overlapping community detection uses superior seed-set selection based on centrality measures, evaluated with intra- and inter-cluster density and runtime.

**Moments Sketch** provides compact, mergeable summaries for sample moments and high-cardinality aggregation queries, including quantile estimation over sub-populations and time windows. Method-of-moments and maximum-entropy approaches perform quantile estimation. Druid, MacroBase, and Spark use these summaries, while Cascade further improves threshold-query time.

3ef0195a4102c5f9005e32562447ff3cd16cef02.text:
## Multimodal Retrieval, Music Classification, and Cold-Start Recommendation

This community covers deep-learning methods for question answering, music genre classification, multimodal learning, and recommendation systems.

For end-to-end question answering, answer selection is a key stage. Convolutional neural networks are evaluated on TRECQA and compared with IDF-weighted word overlap, a strong baseline. Standard retrieval metrics and manual user evaluation assess effectiveness and answer quality.

Music information retrieval includes genre classification. A hierarchical attention network classifies intact song lyrics using word, line, segment, and song layers. Evaluated on the 117 Genre and 20 Genre datasets, it outperforms non-neural and simpler neural models and visualizes important words and lines. Lyrics-based classification uses song lyrics alone. Multi-label genre classification, supported by MUMU, extends single-label classification to fine-grained labels by combining audio, text reviews, and cover-image features through multimodal learning and feature embeddings.

In recommendation systems, latent factor models face the item cold-start problem. A model-based cold-start latent factor prediction method uses a convolutional neural network to process item descriptions and extract visual signals of item attractiveness, training against usage-derived latent factors. It learns text and image representations and outperforms baseline estimators. MUMU contains album audio, reviews, and cover images, enabling multimodal feature combination.

de4711faa34760a65ee6c0b36cc69f6b02d7f59e.text:
## CNN-Based Text Classification and String Similarity

This community centers on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for Persian sentiment analysis and approximate string similarity search.

The CNN is described as a feedforward artificial neural network that applies convolutional processing to Persian text. It classifies sentiment in binary and five-class settings, with the five classes representing different levels of sentiment intensity. The model is evaluated on three Persian social media datasets, using area under the curve, and outperforms traditional machine-learning methods.

A related system, CNN ED, generates string embeddings with a convolutional neural network. It embeds edit distance into vector representations and approximates that distance using Euclidean distance. During training, CNN ED uses triplet loss together with approximation error. This approach enables fast approximate string similarity search and achieves higher efficiency than baseline embeddings. It also outperforms CGK and GRU embeddings.

Overall, the relationships connect CNN architectures to both Persian sentiment-classification tasks and efficient representations for edit-distance-based string search.

9bd03f16c50431cf4b8aafd246470149977ed790.text:
## Community Report: Social Networks, Content, and Hierarchical Analysis

This community links graph clustering, social-network analysis, content modeling, and applied prediction.

**Network methods.** Hierarchical clustering addresses core community detection, uses LexDFS and synchronization similarity, and produces compact communities across multiple scales. It also clusters moving points across snapshots and brain structural connectivity networks using network-distance bounds. Admissible clustering methods are characterized by value and transformation axioms, with universal upper and lower bounds. Randomized shortest paths connect shortest-path, random-walk, and current-flow methods through Boltzmann path distributions; RSP betweenness centrality is a related metric.

**Social prediction and roles.** Prediction accuracy is evaluated for home-location identification, social and individual property prediction, and popularity prediction. Home location uses gazetteers, tweeting behavior, and a travel prediction classifier. User roles capture influence strength and cooperativeness and help analyze strongly connected groups. Bluetooth Low Energy, custom applications, smartphones, Android, and iOS support social-connectivity mapping and mobile sensing.

**Content and questions.** LDA, unigram, and bigram language models represent topics, preserve community structures, and support social-link prediction; finer content granularity performs better. Topic modelling and topic-distribution regression support similar-question ranking on collaborative question-answering platforms and archives.

**Applications.** Other themes include dengue outbreak detection, biomedical ontology engineering, citation and non-citation, content quality, social voting, and ranking algorithms.

47fe59c4133e8451dfbbb66bbc18500cce359fc4.text:
## Event Popularity, Recommendation, and Response Prediction

This community covers event-trend analysis, text-based recommendation, and user response prediction.

**DancingLines** is designed for cross-platform event popularity analysis and is evaluated on real-world event datasets sourced from social network and search engine platforms. It uses **TF-SW**, which performs event popularity quantification and leverages TextRank and Word2Vec, and **WDTW-CD**, an adaptation of dynamic time warping for event-popularity time-series alignment. DancingLines proposes event popularity trend metrics.

The recommendation strand includes a text content-based recommender system developed as part of the **Agnes** application. It recommends college events and groups, represents text-described items as feature vectors, and creates user models from user-provided keywords. These keywords are expanded into weighted lists of near-synonyms, while modified TF-IDF generates item feature vectors. Modified TF-IDF was evaluated against Word2Vec and GloVe; Word2Vec learns distributed representations from occurrence statistics.

The prediction strand targets rare user responses using sparse categorical features, whose limited positive examples make prediction difficult. Neural feature embedding learns representations from users’ web history and improves prediction accuracy. User response prediction is essential for ad targeting and is performed in real-time bidding systems.

2e774e4ade52142c52353dd9eb3210c1031c2078.text:
## Declarative Ingestion, Credibility, and Distributed Learning

This community centers on scalable data ingestion, credibility-based rumor classification, multimodal learning, and crowdsourced decisions.

**Ingestion systems:** IngestBase uses declarative ingestion plans and languages, an optimizer, and a distributed fault-tolerant runtime engine. It supports ingestion-aware data access, Spark and Hadoop MapReduce post-processing, and reports low ingestion overhead. Its optimizer applies pipelining and operator reordering. Strider optimizes logical query plans according to stream state, using Kafka and Spark, while targeting high availability, fault tolerance, acceptable latency, and high throughput—up to 3.1 million triples per second on a nine-machine cluster.

**Credibility and rumor classification:** A convolutional neural network uses tweet text and user-profile metadata to estimate low-level tweet credibility, outperforming baselines. Aggregating these predictions yields event credibility, which improves time-series rumor classification, especially in early phases. Weighted majority voting also optimizes classification performance; reject options are useful, whereas quantized confidence reporting does not improve performance.

**Multimodal and ranking methods:** A two-branch deep neural network represents audio and lyrics; CNNs process audio, while Doc2Vec and fully connected layers process lyrics. CNN-based neural reranking is studied within a Lucene-integrated multi-stage ranking architecture.

**Crowdsourcing and distributed models:** Crowd workers complete binary microtasks, with aggregation producing M-ary decisions through weighted voting. Local clustering results from individual nodes are aggregated into global models.

e9d60199c3aab1a4721effd7b2ffda1774bf5a62.text:
## Neural Methods for Text, Sequence, and Prediction Tasks

This community centers on neural modeling for text classification, semantic matching, retrieval, recommendation, and forecasting. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) extract local n-gram, short-distance, visual, audio, and feature-generation patterns. They support text classification, binary and five-class sentiment classification, Persian text analysis, search-term detection, question-answer semantic matching, and relevance classification for penetrance and prevalence. CNNs also combine with LSTMs in hybrid models such as LSTM-CNN.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs), including long short-term memory (LSTM), weighted RNN, multi-RNN, and augmented RNN systems, model sequence structure and long-term dependencies. Applications include DeepParaphrase, recurrent recommendation, session-based sequential skip prediction, music personalization and next-station prediction, customer purchase sequences, citation-count prediction, and deep landscape bid forecasting. Recurrent models use article embeddings, song metadata, user interaction features, and dynamic user behavior.

Text classification is evaluated with Reuters-21578 and public Twitter data and can use neural or non-neural methods, including support vector machines and naive Bayes variants. Related systems and methods include weakly supervised neural classification, semantic tagging, relation extraction, query expansion, similarity search, and cross-modal information retrieval.

cdc72994f5bdf6dd8302ce416639b80e09494859.text:
### Fine-Grained Cross-Media Retrieval and FGCrossNet

This community centers on **fine-grained cross-media retrieval**, which addresses limitations of coarse-grained retrieval by returning exact results at the subcategory level. Its evaluation resource is the **Fine Grained Cross Media Retrieval Benchmark**, which contains 200 fine-grained Bird subcategories and supports image, video, text, and audio media.

**FGCrossNet** is a deep model proposed for this retrieval task. It jointly learns representations for images, videos, text, and audio. Its video processing differs from image processing because video requires handling multiple frames, whereas a single image can convey information from one frame.

FGCrossNet uses three constraints to improve fine-grained representations: a **classification constraint** for learning discriminative features, a **center constraint** to compact features within the same subcategory, and a **ranking constraint** to encourage sparse features across different subcategories. Together, the benchmark and model connect multimodal data—including Bird imagery and associated media—to methods for precise cross-media retrieval.

407c00eac44b296ed910a6e7fbe30ee98c2569eb.text:
## Neural, Graph, and Text-Mining Methods

This community centers on neural methods for classification, semantic matching, relation extraction, prediction, and social-network analysis.

**DeepInf** predicts individual users’ social influence using graph neural and attention networks, user-specific features, and each user’s local network. It is evaluated on Weibo, Digg, and the Open Academic Graph, and incorporates network structures into convolutional architectures.

For question answering, **aNMM** performs attention-based semantic matching and short-answer ranking with a question attention network and value-shared weighting, using TREC QA data. Convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory methods support semantic matching and open-domain question answering, including a softmax classifier. The **LSTM-CNN** method performs cross-sentence n-ary relation extraction, uses word and positional embeddings, and outperforms CNN-LSTM, which serves as a baseline.

Text classification includes vector-space representations, word vectors, neural and non-neural methods, automated content labeling, and multiclass classification. **AE1-WELM** combines word vectors with cost-sensitive weighted extreme learning and AdaBoost M1 for balanced and imbalanced classification, improving weighted-ELM accuracy.

Finally, LSTM-based growth-potential prediction estimates future technology-cluster growth from patent citation networks. Nested stochastic block models support citation-network clustering, while MAPE and direction accuracy evaluate predictions.

44d3b3741e9a068f93454d01d7a15bc7daac6332.text:
## Graph Analytics, Spatial Querying, and Privacy-Preserving Graph Systems

This community centers on scalable graph analysis, graph databases, and methods for understanding large, dynamic, social, and spatial graphs. Graph databases store graph structures and large sparse relational datasets, support graph algorithms, and increasingly require very high update rates. Algebraic property graphs provide a mathematically rigorous bridge between graph database models and graph algebra.

A major focus is efficient computation. SNAP provides more than 140 graph algorithms, while graph analysis supports distance queries, diffusion-cascade analysis, and breach detection. Systems and methods such as SpeedReader, parallel toolkits, bimodal block processing, and motif-counting algorithms target substantial speedups. StructMatrix addresses visual inspection of large-scale graph structures.

Spatial querying and prefetching form another theme. SCOUT uses structure following and an approximate graph model to prefetch data for interactive spatial queries, achieving 71–92% prefetching accuracy and 4–15× speedup. Range-query research combines spatial data structures, Monte Carlo integration, hierarchical histograms, and local differential privacy, including untrusted aggregation settings.

The community also covers graph structure and privacy: synthetic and real graph benchmarks, degree-distribution models, community partitions, centrality, subgraph frequencies, anonymization, and social-graph classification. Methods including HyperBPR, ERMES, TCMS, and link-prediction-enhanced community detection are evaluated on benchmark datasets.

cddabe8fa2d5cec8477de0dc90d25646f59bae92.text:
## Document and Hypergraph Representation Learning

This community focuses on network representation learning for document and hypergraph data, especially node classification.

The regularized linear embedding method produces document representations for linked documents. It initializes representations through word vector averaging in a pretrained word embedding space, then uses pairwise document similarities to adjust them. Linked documents can be represented as citation networks, where citation structure encodes network proximity. The method is evaluated on node classification.

For high-order relationships, hypergraphs represent connections through hyperedges of variable sizes. The line hypergraph convolution network supports node classification on hypergraphs by constructing the line graph of a hypergraph and applying graph convolution to it. It is evaluated on multiple real-world network datasets.

More generally, network representation learning supports node classification and can model high-order relationships with hypergraphs. Graph convolution networks provide a semi-supervised approach to node classification by aggregating neighborhood attributes, while the line hypergraph convolution network applies this graph-convolution principle to hypergraph-derived line graphs.

2b65bc78821abb817e54156d2fa2df89673f2adc.text:
## Graph Analytics, Scalable Systems, and Structural Methods

This community spans graph storage, analysis, visualization, querying, and social-network modeling. Graph databases provide storage, topology analysis, graph structures, and algorithm execution, while graph algebra remains a commonly missing standard. SNAP supports large-network analysis with compact in-memory representations and more than 140 algorithms; M-Flash uses bimodal block processing for billion-scale computation and eigensolvers, and supports both flexible programming and real-graph evaluation. Highways on Disk reduces I/O for directed weighted graphs through auxiliary edges.

Distance querying is a major theme. Geometric Distance Oracle combines hyperbolic cores and spanning trees for scalable approximate distances, while Gate Graph uses gate vertices to recover non-local shortest paths. Related work includes dynamic reachability, interval labeling, and node, point-to-point, and single-source distance queries.

Community and structure analysis includes RLS heuristics for densest-subgraph optimization, parallel community-quality computation, StructMatrix visualization and structure detection, and SCOUT’s structure-aware spatial prefetching, which achieves 71–92% accuracy and 4–15× speedup. Social-graph research addresses influence, centrality, anonymization, generative models, and subgraph frequencies. Datasets include synthetic, real, Wikipedia, DBLP, Stanford, neuroscience, medicine, biology, and billion-scale graphs. TCMS applies term-class relevance with B-tree indexing for logarithmic testing.

dbbf3bfde48a6a6cc2d9cc72db82b781e33467d3.text:
## Networks, Citation Dynamics, and Reviewer Bias

This community examines how scientific knowledge and professional relationships develop through citation and co-authorship networks, and how these networks shape peer review.

In a *Strategic Management Journal* scholarly community, citation and co-authorship networks are modeled using non-parametric preferential attachment functions. Both networks show rising total competitiveness: receiving new citations or developing new collaborations becomes harder over time. Their average attachment exponents are 0.29 and 0.30, respectively. Citation dynamics combine preferential attachment—the “rich get richer” phenomenon—with author fitness, producing a related “fit get richer” phenomenon in which estimated author fitness influences new citations and co-authorships.

Main path analysis and intermediacy trace the historical development of scientific knowledge. Intermediacy identifies publications connecting older work to newer work and differs from main path analysis in its treatment of path length.

The peer-review component uses neuroscience manuscript reviews: 7,981 manuscripts submitted to PLOS ONE, where reviewers were instructed to assess scientific validity alone. Yet reviewer bias was associated with co-authorship proximity: validity ratings increased by approximately 0.11 points per step of network proximity. Substantive disagreements between schools of thought may underlie biased judgments. Reviewer recusal alone may not eliminate bias; recruiting reviewers from diverse professional networks may reduce it.

ed34bd6ae6e35ac3607fd46c118c8cce102c5fe3.text:
## Topic Modeling, Dynamic Analysis, and Online Systems

This community centers on **topic modeling** and text mining for discovering latent themes, communication patterns, and topic structure in large document and social-media collections. **Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)** is a central method, extended through labeled and hierarchical variants, topical-relevance scoring, collapsed Gibbs sampling, and user-defined topic evaluation. The **embedded topic model (ETM)** represents topics with embeddings and uses amortized variational inference, outperforming LDA while handling large, heavy-tailed vocabularies.

Dynamic modeling is represented by **CLDA**, which partitions corpora into local time-based segments, applies LDA, and uses parallel execution; it has been evaluated on NIPS papers, computer-science abstracts, and PubMed data. Related continuous-time and online hierarchical models address evolving topics, while topic quality can be assessed using perplexity and coherence.

Applications include literary-theme identification, forum and hashtag analysis, medical and constitutional corpora, crowdsourced ideas, and product-relationship networks. Systems such as **Peacock** support large-scale LDA, while **Macross** combines metapath2vec representations with location, time, and text for urban-dynamics modeling. The community also connects topic analysis with recommendation, conversation modeling, streaming systems, and contextual multi-armed bandits for online optimization.

9253bd28af3eb488867f47129fddb4035998a0c8.text:
## Information Cascades, Overexposure, and Online Extremism

This community connects information cascades, social influence, and information contagion across social and information networks. Cascade prediction is an established task, while theoretical models examine audience effects, irrelevant-content filtering, and overexposure. Overexposure—and similarly indiscriminate word-of-mouth recommendations or over-promotion—can produce negative reputational effects, especially when audiences are unreceptive.

Theoretical modeling also yields an optimal marketing strategy, found by a polynomial-time algorithm and shown to outperform natural baseline strategies. Content selection and irrelevant-content filtering jointly shape the quality of users’ content streams.

A second focus is online extremism. Extremist content spreads through highly infectious information cascades, with information contagion describing the epidemic-like spread of online extremist propaganda. Propaganda effectiveness measures adoption of extremist content in the general population. ISIS produces and disseminates such content, and an ISIS supporter user dataset contains 25,000 users manually verified as associated with ISIS online propaganda.

Dynamical activity connectivity maps analyze activity and connections in this dataset, using network structure and temporal activity patterns to investigate the dynamics of social influence and its role in spreading information through supporter networks.

199822eeaca57428fa8a3ed3c04154a3a0013800.text:
## Misinformation, News Propagation, and Detection

This community examines how fake news, misinformation, and disinformation spread through social media and online systems. Social bots and bot accounts amplify low-credibility content, target high-follower users, and contribute to viral diffusion; humans also reshare bot-posted false news. Propagation studies compare trusted, suspicious, clickbait, conspiracy, and disinformation sources by volume, speed, distribution, demographics, direct retweets, and reaction behavior. Disinformation diffusion is highly unequal, while lower-income and less-educated users share more from disinformation sources.

Key detection work includes fake news detection, stance classification, and identification of fraudulent profiles and content polluters. FNC-1 provides a shared stance task, while its F1-based evaluation metric may favor majority classes and alter top-system rankings. A feature-rich stacked LSTM performs strongly, particularly on minority classes. Fine-grained reaction models annotate reaction tweets, and bot identification metrics distinguish bot and non-bot behavior.

A bias-aware news recommendation system uses article clustering and bias scoring to recommend more balanced content, addressing political polarization and personalized news-feed distribution. Automated news-story identification applies network clustering to 61,864 articles, producing story clusters representing linked coverage, including UK news media. These systems support detection and prevention of malicious online manipulation, while content polluters remain a challenge for real-time event prediction and election forecasting.

a34f77fd308842a0b632bbfe2f4084a2d7d1afb1.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Structure Inference

This community studies contagion-driven decision-making and network analysis. **Adaptive influence maximization** selects seeds iteratively under full-adoption or myopic feedback to maximize the expected number of adopters under a seed budget. Its **adaptive greedy algorithm** achieves tight \(1-1/e\) guarantees for submodular influence maximization and under the independent cascade and linear threshold models; for submodular cascades, it approximates the optimal non-adaptive seed choice. Compared with the non-adaptive greedy algorithm, its advantage is characterized by the **greedy adaptivity gap** and can be unbounded under full-adoption feedback. A risk-free adaptive greedy variant is never worse than non-adaptive greedy.

A second theme is **network structure inference** from information cascades and contagion observations, including epidemics and misinformation propagation. Bayesian network structure inference samples compatible networks, producing a network distribution for uncertainty quantification and edge marginal probabilities; the independent cascade model demonstrates this approach.

Graph and node representations encode structural signatures, learned through reward schemes. Information cascades form temporal cascade networks and may saturate or expire under diffusion inhibition.

Finally, sparse seeding concerns strategic competition: firms offering substitutable products choose seeding strategies in a duopoly game, where Nash equilibria may arise and targeting key individuals seeks greater market share.

3398ac4006c4c5c0f0ec207207d4d2a6c613214b.text:
### Research Impact, Diversity, and Scholarly Information Needs

This community centers on measuring scientific impact, research quality, and researcher ranking. Citations connect research papers to cited works, propagate knowledge, and support quality assessment; paper citations and yearly citation counts serve as impact proxies. The h-index characterizes impact and ranks researchers, while h-index and e-index sequences assess impact across time and yearly impact, addressing limitations such as ignored excess citations. Altmetrics seek impacts beyond traditional citations, using data collection and tools such as Google Books and the Ngram Viewer.

Diversity is linked to scientific impact: ethnic, gender, affiliation, and disciplinary diversity are evaluated, with ethnic diversity showing the strongest correlation and reported paper and scientist impact gains. Coarsened exact matching compares ethnically diverse papers and scientists with matched controls, while randomized baseline models establish homophily in ethnic, gender, and affiliation collaboration.

Patent citations indicate technological impact and correlate positively with paper citations, but lag paper citations by a median of six years and exhibit distinct temporal patterns. A comparative study analyzes citation patterns in 919,000 biomedical papers cited by U.S. patents.

Scientific fame is studied through influential physicists, scientific articles, and global digitized books accessed via Google Books. Domain taxonomies and taxonomy hierarchies support research-scope analysis, data-analysis experimentation, quality assessment, and researcher ranking. Social science researchers’ information needs include literature, research data, measurement instruments, software, data analysis, networking, and illustrative material.

cac8cecd852915f15eb6dae84e4b371cd4d30ef9.text:
## Community Report: Behavioral Analytics, Temporal Data, and Recommendation

This community centers on mining user behavior, evaluating information quality, and searching or curating temporal and social data.

**User behavior and profiles:** Web usage mining analyzes web logs and web log data for pattern discovery, pattern analysis, forecasting, customer profiling, personalized services, and adaptive websites. User profiles capture listening habits, topical interests, and visitor clusters, supporting search personalization and profile embeddings. Behavior is evaluated through engagement, retention, contributions, privacy preferences, and answer quality. Digital badges and first-time badges encourage desirable actions.

**Evaluation and similarity:** Offline testing, online testing, and multi-armed bandit testing generate evaluation metrics. Answer quality uses answer length, code lines, external hyperlinks, and acceptance. Similarity measures include RMSS, deep meta-structure methods, scoring functions, and meta-path-based approaches. HMTT enhances text similarity using tags.

**Social and multimedia systems:** Tencent Weibo and its dataset support macro- and micro-level behavioral analysis, including forwarding, topic preferences, and original-message sharing. Last.fm data supports analysis of tags, songs, genres, song co-occurrence, similarity, and popularity.

**Temporal archives and curation:** Web archives support temporal search and historical analysis. Tempas provides archive search, while sub-collection extraction creates topic- or event-focused collections. Mimir supports probabilistic query processing over a deterministic database engine. Tags, metadata reconciliation, semantic metadata layers, and temporal indexing enable discovery and reuse.

58094b540adcbb6069c99cd4f052cda3f91beafb.text:
## Community Report: Topic Models, Cluster Labelling, and Process Abstraction

This community centers on text mining, topic modeling, clustering, and process mining.

For knowledge-intensive business services (KIBS), topic modeling analyzes Twitter posts to identify themes, user intent, and representative top words; sentiment analysis examines entrepreneurship-related content. The seed-guided multi-label topic model (SMTM) supports dataless and multi-label text classification using seed words, category topics, and explicit category sparsity. Spike-and-slab and weak-smoothing priors model sparsity, while seed-guided biased GPU sampling performs inference. Classification accuracy evaluates SMTM. Topic similarity compares user documents with topics from the BBC News dataset, while attention factors select prominent tweets and popularity ratings relate top words to potentially popularity-increasing topics.

A K-Fold ensemble strategy, an ensemble-learning method, uses structured initialization and annotated text corpora to improve topic-model accuracy and reduce instability; stability assessment measures this variation.

For event data, process mining and process discovery generate process models from event logs. Local process models and common subsequences support unsupervised event abstraction, which groups low-level events into higher-level activities and improves model discovery; fitness evaluates process-model quality.
