Finally, clustering organizes KIBS posts and journal articles. Mutual-information-based cluster labelling uses normalized mutual information to rank topical terms, while lexical fingerprints support cluster comparison and visualization.

356c9ec2de38d79a9684cf45edc2d54a482773ca.text:
## Scalable Clustering, Graph Analysis, and Privacy

This community centers on scalable analysis of large, heterogeneous graphs and datasets. Clustering is a major theme, including K-means, DBSCAN, density-based and distributed clustering, memetic and genetic algorithms, canonical PSO-based K-means, fuzzy and partitioning approaches, and graph-modularity methods. These methods support entity resolution, outlier detection, cultural-boundary analysis, and clustering-quality evaluation.

Scalability is emphasized for distributed spatial clustering, distributed spatial indexes, temporal graph indexing, spatial query processing, large-graph analysis, and large scientific datasets. Related tasks include top-k spatial-textual cluster queries, reachability queries, time-based path queries, network partitioning, and index construction.

Bipartite graphs provide representations for user–aspect, word–document, actor–movie, and other relations. One-mode projection compresses these graphs, while modularity and BiRank analyze their structure.

The community also addresses privacy and data protection. Transaction anonymization, k-anonymity, generalization, re-identification, and optimal TP-aware anonymization balance privacy thresholds against information loss. Policy specification and enforcement and access-control policies support privacy governance.

Applications span laboratory information management, IoT and location-based services, political-violence and transaction networks, patent applications, telephone-call networks, ETL logs, and social or human-interaction networks.

0ef93e330038de77d5933d1ba6c2c4d1b9b2225f.text:
## Scalable Clustering, Spatial Mining, and Graph Analysis

This community centers on clustering and its scalable application to large, heterogeneous data. Methods include K-means, DBSCAN, CNNI, canonical PSO-based K-means, graph modularity, memetic algorithms, and density-based clustering. Clustering quality depends on parameter selection and can be evaluated through clustering indices, modularity, and validity measures.

Distributed spatial clustering partitions data across sites, generates local models or patterns, and aggregates them into global models with dynamically determined cluster counts. A distributed spatial clustering algorithm, based on K-means and an elaborated aggregation phase, targets very large spatial datasets while maintaining high-quality results. Scalable density-based distributed clustering instead clusters local representatives at a global server and trades clustering quality against transmission cost.

Spatial data mining also supports top-k spatial-textual cluster queries. These rank clusters by location proximity and keyword relevance, apply density thresholds, and accelerate processing using gridded posting lists, fast range queries, object skipping, and early stopping.

The community further covers graph clustering, community detection, partitioning, and visualization, including temporal graphs, bipartite and multilayer networks, and political-violence or patent-application networks. Applications include laboratory information management for scientific data, entity resolution, outlier detection, transaction anonymization, and scalable analytics over logs and IoT streams.

2d0668bf3e62c9c13e7c620c8594f62d80452cca.text:
## Community Report: Temporal Web, Social Data, and Interactive Curation

This community centers on mining and searching temporal web and social data. Web usage mining analyzes web logs for pattern discovery, pattern analysis, forecasting, resource annotation, user-behavior extraction, and personalized or adaptive services. User behavior is modeled with computational mechanics, echo state networks, and self-feedback, and evaluated through engagement, retention, contributions, privacy preference, and perceived answer quality. Tencent Weibo supports macro- and micro-level behavioral analysis, including forwarding behavior and topic preferences.

Web archives and Tempas address temporal search through temporal indexing, popularity ranking, and query recommendations, while sub-collection extraction supports focused archive analysis. Delicious and social-bookmarking data provide timestamped bookmarks and popularity evidence for identifying important websites. Tag reconciliation and semantic metadata layers address synonymy and ambiguity and connect tags across open-data portals.

On-demand curation systems such as Mimir communicate uncertainty through annotated result cursors and interactive interfaces. Related systems support historical research: an interactive Norfolk directory links historical entities to newspaper mentions and census information, while newspaper access tools serve digitized collections.

Other methods target recommendation and evaluation. Last.fm data captures songs and listening histories for mixtape, song similarity, and popularity analysis. Meta song evaluation uses online chord databases and pseudo annotations. HMTT applies multigranularity topics to short-text hashing. SVM-based citation methods use systematic-review data, statistical grouping, and ensemble algorithms.

2e8733f2dd6a2c9d42c7fa6b435d975894ca2ed7.text:
## Community Report: Research Data, Retrieval, and Graph-Based Learning

This community spans scientific research infrastructure, information extraction, search, recommendation, and network analytics.

A major theme is **bibliographic and document processing**. Bibliographic reference parsing compares tools such as GROBID, CERMINE, ParsCit, Anystyle Parser, Biblio, and others using F1-score; retraining improves several parsers. OCR++ extracts structural information, bibliographies, and public-dataset links, exporting TEI documents. WebSMatch supports public-data integration, metadata extraction, source integration, refinement, and visualization.

**Search and personalization** address user intent and interaction. Two-stage approaches detect intent presence and then tag utterances, including open intents and transcription errors. Conversational systems, gatedlongrec, dynamic ranking, mobile search, and interaction-based embeddings use feedback, recency, frequency, and ranking behavior to improve relevance. Tripartite vector representations jointly model jobs, skills, titles, and resumes, improving relevancy.

The community also covers **research communication and reproducibility**, including software citation, software credit, research software, open science, academic data sharing, Jupyter notebooks, and open peer review.

Finally, **graph and machine-learning methods** support directed graph embedding, semi-supervised node classification, fraud and illicit-transaction detection, anti-money-laundering, misinformation classification, crowd-risk warning, and propagation analysis. F1-score and related evaluation measures are recurring metrics.

cb16b01aa34bd3a5c602f8ddefddc5f4d77d635a.text:
## Graphs, Communities, and Data-Centric Analysis

This community spans graph data management, temporal-network analysis, online communities, privacy, business processes, and financial prediction.

**UDBMS** is envisioned as a multi-model data-management platform supporting graph and semi-structured data, NoSQL, unified schemas, query processing, indexing, and cross-model transaction guarantees. Graph models represent entity profiles and provenance descriptions, while object-centric behavioral constraint models extend data models with behavioral perspectives.

For temporal graphs, **Temporal Neighbourhood Aggregation (TNA)** uses recurrent variational graph convolution, hierarchical recurrence, and variational sampling to predict future links and subsequent graph states. **Temporal graph cuts** analyze multiplex graphs and dynamic graph signals. **STWalk** learns temporal-node representations, whereas aggregated networks discard much temporal information.

Online communities generate published user content and discussion, evolve over time, and may develop intercommunity conflict. Reputation systems support consumer protection, distinguish honest and cheating participants, and aim to reduce scam losses. **LinkMirage** anonymizes links while preserving community structure, supporting privacy-preserving reputation and Sybil defenses; Facebook data is used to evaluate de-anonymization attacks.

Outlier detection examines ETL execution logs, temporal graphs, reciprocal-edge prediction, and provenance summaries, including clustering-based and contextual methods. In finance, coupled matrix and tensor factorization jointly predicts correlated stocks using events and investor sentiment; public sentiment is related to stock movements, the DJIA, and used-car prices.

992c306550c4e609ede4617e6d49e14528e9465a.text:
## Graph Signal Processing, Network Roles, and Scholarly Discovery

This community connects graph-based signal processing with network analysis and information retrieval. **Discrete signal processing on graphs** extends filters, convolution, and the z-transform to graph signals, supporting spectral representations, linear prediction, blog classification, weather-station data compression, and customer-behavior prediction. **Graph shift operators**, including the normalized graph Laplacian, define graph-frequency domains and support distributed graph-filter design. ARMA graph filters provide distributed, temporally adaptive alternatives to FIR filters, while localized spectral analysis, sparse frequency representations, and graph-based short-time Fourier analysis address graph and time-varying signals.

A second theme is **role discovery**. Roles are characterized through structural, regular, or stochastic equivalence, flow patterns, and feature representations. Role discovery combines graph-based, feature-based, and hybrid methods, with role-feature construction and assignment supported by network measures.

The community also covers **knowledge discovery from scientific documents and information networks**. Entitymetrics highlights important knowledge units and builds entity-entity citation networks. GV-Index uses publication-year variance and research-area growth for scientist-network visualization. Paper-to-reviewer matching uses learning, integer programming, suitability scores, and matching frameworks to optimize reviewer assignments.

Additional methods include MFNG network generation, PCA-based dimensionality reduction, convex/nonconvex rank relaxation, and Faster SAX for accelerated time-series search.

e48163e309b111e92b9119d98432fd959e08698b.text:
## Community Report: Network Embeddings, Expert Ranking, and Plant-Science Knowledge

This community centers on network representation learning, knowledge discovery, and domain ontologies. Network embedding produces low-dimensional node vector representations and distributed network representations. Methods include DeepWalk, node2vec, LINE, GraRep, HOPE, RandNE, BoostNE, and ProGLe.

ProGLe is a fast, scalable embedding method that constructs a sparse proximity matrix, applies sparse matrix decomposition, and uses spectral analysis to incorporate local and global information through network propagation patterns. It is experimentally compared with DeepWalk, node2vec, LINE, GraRep, and HOPE. RandNE uses Gaussian random projection and iterative projection to preserve high-order proximity without explicitly computing high-order proximities; it supports distributed computation, dynamic network updating, billion-scale networks, and network-reconstruction evaluation. BoostNE learns multi-level embeddings from coarse to fine while avoiding a global low-rank assumption and uses a strategy analogous to gradient boosting.

Expert finding is addressed through ranking, deep-learning, matrix-factorization, and gradient-boosting-tree models. Ranking models jointly consider document–entity relatedness, document timeliness, and temporal relations among entities, evaluated on a new dataset; deep-learning models outperform other categories. Ensemble learning and multimodal matching tasks support comparison.

The plant science ontology, developed using Prot G, models Arabidopsis thaliana and represents genomic and phenomic data, supporting automated reasoning and knowledge discovery.

62f296e7d53994f692bbab97345265511eefe271.text:
## Signed Networks, Opinion Dynamics, and Polarization

This community centers on how opinions evolve, separate, or reach consensus in social networks, especially when relationships include positive and negative links. Opinion-dynamics models include DeGroot averaging, Friedkin–Johnsen, voter and generalized voter models, stochastic multi-agent models, and agent-based or spatial approaches. They examine consensus, divergence, polarization, neutralization, stubborn agents and zealots, heterogeneous thresholds, limited interaction, and influencing strategies.

Signed networks provide the structural foundation: structural balance theory, balance dynamics, signed graph Laplacians, signed network partitioning, and signed link analysis characterize friendship, trust, enmity, and distrust. Frustration index, line index of balance, partial balance, and structural balance visualization measure or display imbalance and polarization; exact frustration-index computation uses binary linear programming models and Gurobi.

A related information-environment cluster studies echo chambers, filter bubbles, information segregation, selective exposure, confirmation bias, biased assimilation, media bias, and partisan sharing. These mechanisms connect recommendation and content-promotion systems to user polarization, misinformation cascades, and viewpoint discovery. Systems and datasets include signed graphs, social-media and Facebook networks, blogs, blog-citation networks, Memetracker, and news outlets. Applications include controversy detection, contrarian or opposing-view recommendation, meme propagation, diversity maximization, epidemic containment, and network dismantling.

72912ec30583b10c8e4f7953a558e3f5a188021d.text:
### Graph Signal Processing, Network Analysis, and Knowledge Discovery

This community links graph-based signal processing with dimensionality reduction, information-network analysis, and knowledge discovery. Graph signals are indexed by graph nodes and modeled as outputs of network processes. Discrete signal processing on graphs extends filters, convolution, and the z-transform to graph data, supports spectral representations and linear prediction, and processes irregular weather-station data. ARMA graph filters provide robust, distributed graph-domain filtering and are contrasted with FIR filters, including for time-varying signals. Localized spectral analysis, graph short-time Fourier transforms, and sparse frequency representations address graph-frequency structure.

Dimensionality reduction includes principal component analysis, symbolic aggregate approximation, sketching, and compressed representations for high-dimensional sparse data and time-series databases. PCA analyzes measures such as degree and strength, produces spectral templates and representative points, and computes metrics such as the GV index and media PCA score.

Graphs support relational queries, evolving-network modeling, and network-based analysis. Information networks connect scientific documents and entities, enabling knowledge discovery, entity importance analysis, and network analytic tasks. Related applications include astronomy literature, scientific documents, and social or communication networks.

Finally, convex relaxation makes combinatorial optimization and rank minimization tractable, using the nuclear norm; it can outperform structure-ignoring and state-of-the-art related approaches.

44f223b0eecdf3440f6ebcf7e5cf981119b3905a.text:
### Community Report: Influence, Communities, and Diffusion in Social Networks

This community centers on social-network structure, influence optimization, viewpoint discovery, and infectious-disease diffusion.

For marketing, **influence maximization with general marketing strategies** optimizes a marketing strategy mix under budget or partitioned-budget constraints. **Reverse influence sampling** and the **scalable RIS algorithm** provide scalable solutions, with stated \((1-1/e-\epsilon)\) and \((1/2-\epsilon)\) approximations; Monte Carlo hill climbing is a slower baseline. **Coupon allocation** selects seed users to maximize expected cascades and is formulated as approximate submodular maximization under partition-matroid and knapsack constraints, with approximation ratios approaching \(1-1/e\).

A second theme is structural analysis. **Social tie strength inference** uses network topology and strong triadic closure, while tie-strength optimization employs linear relaxations to infer fine-grained strengths and limited STC violations. **Overlapping communities** involve multi-membership vertices, challenging community boundaries; f-cores and community networks represent this structure. Graph partitioning uses social interactions to identify communities and discover viewpoints, including those surrounding Brexit, media bias, and filter bubbles.

Finally, disease studies compare direct and indirect transmission. The SPDT model uses synthetic social contact networks and identifies hidden spreaders, while network-based diffusion models capture co-located transmission. Indirect transmission can substantially enhance infectious-disease emergence.

890a3caa31f52a4aa306f3acd613972bb15c890a.text:
## Community Report: Demographic, Mobility, and Network Dynamics

This community centers on how network topology and connectivity shape social behavior, infrastructure, and spreading processes. Network topology influences group performance, resource allocation, meme propagation, game equilibrium, and power-grid stability, while user-arrival patterns can generate different topological properties. Graph sampling, graph generation, spectral views, and projection/backboning methods analyze or construct networks; active search and selective harvesting depend on topology.

Demographic attributes—including gender, age, race/ethnicity, and socioeconomic class—are used to explain homophily, relationship characterization, switching behavior, mobility, and communication patterns. Automatic demographic identification, demographic inference, and demographic attribute prediction recover attributes such as gender from available data. Age relates to connectivity through kin and non-kin ties, while gender differences appear in call frequency, daily regularity, fatigue, and economic recovery time. FetLife and its European member network provide examples involving identity, sexual-market interactions, and network structure.

Human mobility is studied using check-ins, cellular-phone, bank-card, ATM, and other digital traces. Trajectory analysis, gravity models, and hybrid mobility models connect movement to spatial interaction, transportation, traffic prediction, and pandemic spread. Mobility also informs opportunistic routing and information diffusion.

Meme creation, sharing, and propagation are modeled through retweet graphs, comparative independent cascade, creator/consumer models, dynamic message passing, and spreading-process control. Smart grids, power networks, communication networks, scientific repositories, and geospatial interfaces provide application settings.

048572efb6cab89bb1d179bbff78ef85b2a9e1b5.text:
## Community Report: Networks, Mobility, Demographics, and Diffusion

This community studies how network structure, human behavior, and demographic attributes shape communication, mobility, resilience, and information spread. Network topology affects group performance, optimal resource allocation, meme propagation, game equilibrium, and power-grid stability; user arrival curves and patterns can themselves shape topology. Graph sampling, graph generation, exponential random graph models, multiplicative attribute graphs, and spherical feature graph models support network analysis and synthesis. The spherical feature graph model represents features on a hypersphere using von Mises–Fisher distributions while avoiding graph degeneracy.

Human mobility is examined through check-in, cellular-phone, digital-mobility, and trajectory data. Race/ethnicity, gender, age, wealth, socioeconomic class, friends, and social context relate to movement, commuting, spatial interaction, pandemic spread, traffic prediction, and information diffusion. Age-specific small worlds distinguish kin and non-kin ties and may influence diffusion across generations.

Demographic inference and attribute prediction target age and gender, with homophily scores measuring demographic similarity. Privacy-preserving profile matching is addressed by “message in a sealed bottle,” a decentralized multi-hop smartphone system that establishes secure channels using preference profiles.

Diffusion research covers meme creation, sharing, consumer decisions, retweet graphs, and propagation control. Power and smart-grid studies connect communication networks, topology, stability, blackout prevention, and resource allocation. Hurricane Odile provides a setting for measuring economic recovery time.

d1199a4d40bfc0adc4bbc900c23bb0277999bd44.text:
## Community Report: Intent, Retrieval, and Transferable Graph Recommenders

This community covers four connected themes: user-intent understanding, efficient retrieval, graph-based recommendation, and patent analysis.

GEN Encoder maps search queries into distributed intent representations, using Bing click logs and implicit feedback as weak supervision. It is evaluated on query-intent similarity and paraphrase tasks, helping address sparse tail traffic. Approximate nearest-neighbor search efficiently compares GEN encodings to prior queries, while locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) supports sublinear query complexity and improved processing of high-dimensional image data. These methods underpin image retrieval and real-time nearest-neighbor query processing.

Open intent discovery extends intent classification to unseen intents. A two-stage bidirectional-LSTM/conditional-random-field system first detects intent presence, then tags intents, with adversarial training improving cross-domain robustness. A crowdsourced dataset of 25,000 utterances supports evaluation.

Graph neural networks support recommendation and matrix completion. IGMC constructs local subgraphs from rating matrices without side information and transfers rating prediction across datasets, including Douban. MCNE uses binary masks, conditional embeddings, Bayesian Personalized Ranking, compression, and pre-learned node features to model multiple behaviors. RECSYS-DAN uses adversarial loss for domain-indistinguishable representations, addressing imbalance and cold-start recommendation across Amazon data.

Finally, patent retrieval supports analysis, valuation, litigation, and licensing. Interactive tools provide cognitive assistance, but web-search methods require domain adaptation for patent documents.

85dee531fcd105752f625ef82b6a2fb7a205b9b1.text:
## Session Recommendation, Feature Selection, and Contextual Advertising

This community centers on recommendation and advertising systems under sparse, high-dimensional data. Session-based recommendation predicts the next item and top-N results, addressing cold starts by modeling recent sessions, current-session interests, and inter-session behavior. Recurrent neural networks, including dwell-time-aware RNNs, use visited items and item dwell time as signals of user interest; recurrent latent variable networks model stochastic latent variables, infer their posterior distributions from observed data, and capture complex temporal dynamics.

For top-N recommendation, CODAE is a trust-aware recommender that learns high-order correlations from rating and trust data. It fuses hidden layers from separate stacked denoising autoencoders through correlative regulation and improves recommendation performance on public datasets. Embedded feature selection exploits high-dimensional side information by learning nonnegative, sparse feature weights, solved efficiently with augmented Lagrange multiplier and alternating direction methods. Sparsity and low-rank structure help address data sparsity affecting rating, trust, and cold-user preference information.

A second theme is CTR prediction for contextual advertising and advertisement serving. Linear regression and extracted features support CTR prediction, while publisher context determines displayed advertisements. Improved serving is intended to increase advertising revenue.

c1d34a36bca2303fae3957d283c243d570fbd2d5.text:
## Recommendation, Feedback, and Graph Matching

This community covers personalized recommender systems and graph matching. Collaborative filtering infers user preferences from collective information and explicit feedback, supporting personalized recommendations on Amazon and Netflix and evaluation on MovieLens. Recommender systems also use side information about items, while user preferences may be collected from previously visited locations. Mass diffusion is used in recommendation algorithms.

The work examines recommendation quality through diversity and novelty. COSRA combines the cosine index and resource allocation index, is evaluated on RYM, Netflix, and MovieLens, and improves diversity and novelty. A recommender influence metric measures system influence across the full user–item rating matrix and is evaluated on real-world and synthetic datasets. Because recommendations can create feedback loops through user acceptance, feedback loop deconvolution recovers intrinsic preference ratings and identifies affected items.

A second theme is matching users or nodes across bipartite or correlated graphs. Percolation-based graph matching uses seed vertex pairs, while community labels and community degree vectors provide side information, particularly when seed counts are small or networks are weakly correlated. The two-threshold percolation algorithm handles imperfect initial matching, and the basic percolation algorithm is adapted for graphs with community structure. Amazon and Netflix represent consumer–product bipartite-network applications.

e3b1560685ae8894bb389cf546ac68c4c3ae902a.text:
## Graph-Based Retrieval, Detection, and Fact Validation

This community spans knowledge-base retrieval, triple scoring, vandalism detection, and graph-based search.

For **Wikidata vandalism detection**, the WSDM Cup 2017 task required near-real-time predictions and recast detection as an online-learning problem. Participant software was evaluated on TIRA; the best approach achieved **0.947 ROC AUC** and **0.458 PR AUC**. Wikidata is treated as a knowledge base containing triples.

**Entity retrieval** improves search using entity types organized in a type taxonomy, including hierarchical type information. Retrieval models combine type-based and term-based similarity, while taxonomy choice and specificity affect usefulness.

The **CatSeAR triple scorer**, developed by the CatSeAR team for the WSDM Cup triple scoring challenge, performs triple scoring and hybrid fact validation. It combines answers from three sources with a linear regression classifier and achieved **79.58% accuracy2**. Triple scores represent information relevance.

Graph search research addresses **rumor source detection** under untruthful answers. Simple batch querying and interactive directed querying use estimation algorithms, diffusion snapshots, and social-network topologies to improve detection probability.

**Active search** and selective harvesting choose labeled nodes under a query budget, using topology and node attributes. Selective harvesting restricts candidates to neighbors, but the tunnel vision effect can bias classifiers; diversification balances exploration and exploitation.

Finally, **DANE** embeds dynamic attributed networks, maintaining fresh online embeddings through offline consensus embeddings and matrix perturbation theory updates.

6a54607ab6ec4c9f648f1b6e290b81122be05306.text:
## Graph Mining, Reliable Ranking, and Emoji Embeddings

This community covers data mining tasks and methods for heterogeneous, noisy, and social-media data. Classification and clustering are major data-mining operations, supporting downstream network-embedding applications. Missing, inconsistent, and conflicting data can affect classification, clustering, and regression, motivating experimental comparisons and attention to research validity.

For heterogeneous information networks, meta-paths compute user–item similarity but may be numerous. Meta-path reduction selects smaller subsets while preserving semantics. SPMR performs this reduction without supervision and evaluates subsets for maximal semantic preservation; prior methods use supervised information.

Collaborative recommendation is represented by GRank and ReGRank. GRank uses graph-based ranking but may rely on unreliable paths and neglect path-type semantics. ReGRank provides reliable recommendation paths aligned with path semantics and unifies or adapts graph-, neighborhood-, user-, preference-, and representative-based collaborative ranking. Similarity and neighborhood principles guide path consistency. GRank models user priorities in a heterogeneous information network.

QANet performs query-based anomaly detection in heterogeneous networks, uses tensor decomposition, is evaluated on synthetic networks generated by a network-generation model, and outperforms existing anomaly-detection methods.

Another focus is emoji analysis. A network built from 147 million emoji tweets models co-occurrence patterns. Network embedding learns low-dimensional emoji vectors, which support emoji-similarity experiments, emotion identification, and sentiment analysis.

Crowd-powered data mining addresses machine-hard sentiment analysis and image classification, with clustering and classification also included; quality, cost, and latency control are fundamental.

ed7fcd67f8a97fd0fb2c7104397c2539c6e4902f.text:
## Knowledge Graphs, Query Interoperability, and Explainable Prediction

This community spans knowledge-graph modeling, semantic querying, recommendation, provenance, and biomedical prediction. RDF and property graphs are principal data models: RDF is a W3C standard queried with SPARQL, while property graphs support Gremlin traversal. OWL ontologies, Shape Expressions, schemas, entity classes, aliases, and identifiers support consistent representation of named entities and resources.

Gremlinator translates a subset of SPARQL SELECT queries into Gremlin traversals, enabling interoperability across graph data-management systems and graph-pattern matching. QR2 provides query reranking over a web database through arbitrary ranking functions and a public search interface. Semantic layers and RDF graphs represent document metadata and semantic information, supporting structured queries, archived-document ranking, and search-query processing.

RippleNet propagates user preferences over knowledge-graph links and is evaluated for movie, book, and news recommendation, addressing limitations of embedding- and path-based methods. Generalized vector space models combine named entities or keywords and are tested on the TREC dataset.

Graph segmentation and summarization operate on property graphs for provenance analysis; summaries preserve path constraints, while provenance graphs use property graphs and Cypher. Finally, multi-relational knowledge-graph completion supports polypharmacy side-effect prediction, generating interpretable hypotheses for wet-lab validation using drugs, combinations, and protein targets.

1ed9ed18be011e50bb76791b60ee86bc8e384c54.text:
# Graph-Based, Cross-Modal, and Noisy-Text Retrieval

This community covers efficient retrieval across modalities, graph indexing, and historical-document search.

Cross-modal hashing methods, including fusion supervised deep cross-modal hashing and fusion hash networks, learn unified binary codes from paired samples. They embed pairwise similarity and classification information, preserve semantic consistency, and use modality-specific hash networks to encode out-of-sample queries. Binary codes support Hamming-distance comparison and probability-based indexing, which selects bits for index codes and constructs inverted index tables to improve indexing accuracy and real-time efficiency. Benchmark datasets evaluate ranking accuracy.

Approximate k-nearest-neighbor graphs support large-scale nearest-neighbor search. Graph merging includes peer merge for parallel computation and joint merge for incorporating raw data into existing graphs. Joint merge enables incremental and hierarchical graph construction, producing graph hierarchies for open-set indexing.

For historical document search driven by mass digitization, OCR-generated noisy text is represented with word vectors and projected with queries into a common vector space. A noisy-text search system ranks candidates using a nearest-neighbor metric and is evaluated on typewritten German WWII documents.

Additional methods include sparse Gaussian Markov random-field learning through pseudo-likelihood, Besag auto-normal parameterization, and sparse inverse covariance estimation. Query-invariant listwise context modeling applies domain generalization to reduce inter-query variability and improve generalization to unseen queries.

80f656458b1db30ffbee014e83132e5307c49903.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Secure Search, Graph Queries, and Social Analysis

This community spans scientific information retrieval, graph querying, privacy-preserving search, and social-network analysis.

**LRSE** is a searchable-encryption scheme integrating machine learning for lightweight ranked search over encrypted cloud data. It combines local and global representations, improved secure kNN, privacy protection, low system cost, and state-of-the-art search quality, evaluated on benchmark datasets. Semantic relations connect keywords from scientific articles to context extraction, article classification, and a semantic search engine supporting meaningful browsing and scientific information retrieval.

**Generalized Graph Query** supports graph pattern matching over generalized graphs and multi-relational data. Through dynamic query construction, it expresses relational and non-relational restrictions and supports bottom-up discovery.

For social analysis, a machine-learning framework for **social network mental disorder detection** uses social network data, multi-source learning, and an SNMD-based tensor model. It is evaluated with an online-social-network user study and does not rely on self-reported factors.

Communication-pattern research applies topic modeling and perplexity to the Hurricane Sandy Twitter dataset, identifying user concerns across warning, response, and recovery storm phases. Keywords also support targeted information spreading and hashtagging, relevant to crisis communication.

Finally, the **NIPS 2016 review process** produced review data used in an ordinal-ranking experiment comparing ordinal and cardinal rankings, evaluating process soundness and proposing monitoring metrics.

680aa9e2a37695b62ed825042fbfa15566ed5bc0.text:
## Hashing, Similarity Search, and Efficient Data Systems

This community centers on efficient retrieval and similarity computation, especially cross-modal hashing. Cross-modal hashing generates compact binary hash codes for searching heterogeneous multimedia, image-text pairs, and other modalities. UCH provides an unsupervised approach using coupled inner- and outer-cycle networks, a generative adversarial mechanism, and a learned common representation. Deep cross-modal hashing, asymmetric correlation quantization hashing, composite correlation quantization, and fusion-supervised deep cross-modal hashing target retrieval effectiveness and efficiency; unified hash codes and modality-specific hash networks support cross-modal queries.

A second theme is set and similarity search. Bitmap filters use XOR, population count, and similarity upper bounds to accelerate PPJoin, AdaptJoin, and GroupJoin. BinSketch estimates Jaccard similarity, while BayesLSH and BayesLSH Lite provide locality-sensitive hashing approaches. Binary hash joins, multiway hash joins, and three-way joins emphasize substantial speedups over cascaded or CPU-based joins.

Systems research addresses iterative and browser workloads: Helix reuses or recomputes intermediate results, while SpeedReader translates document trees, removes trackers, reduces bandwidth, and improves privacy. Graph convolutional networks model transaction graphs and ranking information, supporting applications including illicit transaction classification, mixing-service detection, and customer identification.

b79c278bf233d890e24b4e8af3201bebae445134.text:
## Multimodal Retrieval, Neural Optimization, and Data Search

This community spans cross-modal retrieval, information retrieval, query optimization, classification, and recommendation.

**Cross-modal hashing** addresses efficient retrieval across image-text modalities. Deep cross-modal hashing combines feature learning with hash-code optimization, while DCHUC jointly learns unified hash codes and hashing functions for unseen queries. JCCH forms semantic hashcode clusters and reduces the heterogeneity gap; CMUL connects triplet and classification-based unary losses with linear complexity. These methods are evaluated on benchmark and public datasets, improving retrieval accuracy and achieving state-of-the-art cross-modal retrieval.

**Deep reinforcement learning** is applied to join query optimization through the Fully Observed Optimizer, which avoids exhaustive join-order enumeration and is faster than dynamic-programming approaches. Actor–critic training, PPO, pointer networks, ensemble learning, and equal-size k-means reduce or guide the action space. Related work includes IRGAN, whose PPO-based objective improves convergence in its generator–discriminator minimax game.

**Dataset on Demand (DOD)** searches databases, data lakes, and cloud storage, using 4C to classify compatible, contained, complementary, and contradictory views and reduce the view choice space.

**HILAP** formulates hierarchical text classification as a Markov decision process, learning label-assignment policies with neural encoders and improving Macro-F1 over flat classifiers. Neural hybrid recommendation supports item prediction and rating prediction, while pointer networks solve combinatorial keyword recommendation from landing pages and search logs.

0f3b491d3f87e75fa8597286b9ac1aa9634fb117.text:
## Graph Mining Across Heterogeneous Networks

This community centers on data mining, clustering, similarity measurement, and predictive modeling for heterogeneous information networks (HINs). HIN analysis uses meta-paths and meta-structures to represent relations, assess path-based relevance, embed nodes, predict neighbor distributions, and support investment-exclusion and adverse-media prediction. DMSS provides a deep-meta-structure-based similarity measure, while CNNI and RMSS introduce alternative similarity approaches. Reduced meta-paths aim to preserve semantics and improve mining effectiveness despite relation-type imbalance.

Clustering connects these representations to hidden-information discovery, entity resolution, cultural boundaries, signed-network balance, and efficient joint personalized PageRank estimation. Methods include k-means, DBSCAN, fuzzy and partitioning clustering, canonical PSO-based k-means, and relation-strength-aware approaches. StreamSpot applies clustering to anomaly detection; other work addresses spambots, opinion spam, and network change points.

The community also covers recommender systems and applied prediction. Hybrid recommenders support patient–doctor matchmaking, family-doctor recommendations, and patient trust, while deep-learning recommenders address broader recommendation tasks. Applications include breast-cancer diagnosis and prognosis, student-dropout management, ESG compliance, business analytics, company embeddings, and social-media behavioral analysis using digital DNA and social fingerprinting.

930b4bfed04af6a3c6dd877c0f3658d91bfbe340.text:
## Recommendation, Cold Start, and Compensation Analytics

This community centers on recommendation systems and LinkedIn’s statistical compensation platform. Collaborative filtering uses anonymized user-interaction logs and supports personalized recommendation, but performs poorly in cold-start settings. Hybrid recommender systems combine collaborative filtering with other techniques, including data-mining methods, to address cold start, changing user context and evolving tastes. They are evaluated with accuracy metrics, often on movie datasets, and face cross-domain recommendation challenges.

A retrieval-based product recommendation system uses a joint product embedding optimized for retrieval and evaluated on product shopping data, including cross-category and cold-start settings. Text embedding maps textual descriptions into a latent feature space, while joint text embedding learns text representations end-to-end, incorporates unsupervised text embedding, and can use user interactions to learn representations. Joint product embeddings fuse modality-specific embeddings from product images and textual descriptions through late fusion; a modular architecture supports separate modality training. Personalized recommendation can also be framed as personalized text ranking.

For collaborative filtering, self-organizing maps identify similar users, followed by k-means clustering; this helps mitigate scalability problems. Separately, LinkedIn Salary, launched and operated by LinkedIn, provides compensation insights and supports salary transparency. Its deployed statistical modeling system uses Bayesian hierarchical smoothing and is evaluated with de-identified compensation data collected from LinkedIn users.

e97ac0141644ffdd778077cc1d8c0f7ba7f3ce67.text:
## Community Report: Language, Music, Patents, and Procedural Knowledge

This community connects natural language processing, information retrieval, and representation learning across several applications.

**Sentiment and conversational analysis** includes sentiment analysis for Persian web content, enterprise information extraction, and smart management. CommentsRadar is an entity-centric search engine that aggregates articles and associated user comments, extracts named entities linked to knowledge-base entries, and mines temporal trends. ScenarioSA provides 2,214 manually labeled, two-speaker, multi-turn conversations for interactive sentiment analysis, modeling affective states and sentimental evolution.

**Music representation and recommendation** centers on playlists composed of ordered songs. Sequence-to-sequence models encode playlists as sentences and learn fixed-length playlist representations; playlist embeddings support playlist discovery and are evaluated for music recommendation. Artist, album, and track information form factual metadata, while genres are semantic labels and potential supervision for music representation learning. Pandora and Apple Music provide cloud-based playlist services.

**Patent and knowledge discovery** uses NLP, feature extraction, document comparison, and full-text similarity search to compare patent applications with existing patents, automate prior-art search, and assess inventiveness and result quality. Literature-based knowledge discovery uses bibliometrics and temporal keyword co-occurrence networks. Finally, creative procedural knowledge is formalized through a CPK ontology and extraction pipeline, supported by annotated workflows, goals, commands, and actions from online design tutorials.

088af37cf33ae00fab8014aabe5b7d43c7928a0c.text:
## Community Report: Data Mining, Diversity, and Networked Intelligence

This community connects data mining applications, graph learning, recommendation diversity, agent-based information sharing, and career analytics.

Data mining supports breast-cancer diagnosis and prognosis, student-dropout management, educational data mining, time-series clustering, scientific-publication analysis, and container-terminal operations. CASP-DM and CRISP-DM address process development, while statistical modeling systems and specialized spatial indexes accelerate mining.

Diversity is modeled through variety, balance, and disparity. xQuAD, determinantal point processes (DPPs), hybrid recommendation algorithms, and diffusion-like recommendation address recommendation-list or bundle diversity. The bundle generation network combines DPP-based quality/diversity decomposition, feature-aware softmax, and masked beam search, and is evaluated on co-purchase and online-bundle datasets. New, relative, and DIV diversity indicators measure variety, while design-idea ranking maximizes diversity.

Agents collaborate through knowledge diffusion, information sharing, network walking, and face-to-face interaction under noisy observations and limited learning horizons. A unified framework supports inductive and transductive learning and integrates heterogeneous network data.

GraphSAGE performs inductive representation learning through local-neighborhood aggregation, using node features to classify unseen nodes and generalize across unseen graphs. LinkedIn Salary uses company transitions and statistical modeling to provide salary, compensation, and transparency insights.

63bd48b37657fdd3208ee2e679561baad4cf5eb6.text:
## Data Mining Across Health, Education, Search, and Optimization

This community centers on data mining and its applications in sequential pattern mining, healthcare, education, information retrieval, and social or spatiotemporal analysis.

Sequential pattern mining extracts frequent subsequences from sequence databases using sequential pattern models and algorithms such as PrefixSpan and CSPADE. Constraint programming supports this task through global constraints, generic constraint solvers, and regular-expression mining, and is reported as more flexible and efficient than A* search and mixed integer programming. Mixed integer programming provides stochastic optimality guarantees and is evaluated for index deployment ordering.

Healthcare applications include breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis, drug recall prediction, and clinical decision support. Search-query spikes and state-level query-volume attributes help predict FDA and medium-risk prescription-drug recalls, achieving approximately 0.791 AUC and sixfold lift at 5% for one-day-ahead prediction.

Educational data mining uses student data for performance prediction, dropout management, and institutional improvement. Information retrieval systems support event extraction, relationship extraction, thematic mapping, and seizure-event tracking; the graph-based bibliographic information retrieval system addresses research-paper and mathematical-knowledge retrieval. Tweets Miner mines Twitter microblogs for stock-market analysis.

Database-oriented methods include dynamic physiological partitioning, which redistributes data across shared-nothing clusters while supporting migration and query-runtime evaluation, and spatial indexes that accelerate mining and similar-object search. A semi-automated peer-review system uses a semi-supervised human-assisted classifier to reduce traditional review bias and incompleteness.

7455e3647e317a54f86cdaf0c5dba839d4334f5e.text:
## Community Report: Data Mining, Retrieval, and Applied Prediction

This community centers on **data mining** and its applications in health, education, enterprise decision support, and scientific-publication analysis. Key tasks include breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis, drug recall prediction, student performance prediction and dropout management, stock trend prediction, time-series clustering, sequential pattern mining, event extraction, and object classification.

Several systems support these applications. **Information retrieval systems**, including the **graph-based bibliographic information retrieval system**, process TREC queries, exploit query-term dependence, and support event extraction and event mapping. The **tweets miner** addresses mining of Twitter microblogs, while the **semi-automated peer review system** relates to research-paper assessment.

Important methods include named entity and relationship extraction, clustering algorithms, constraint programming, mixed integer programming, local search, stochastic blockmodels, hybrid attention networks, recurrent binary embeddings, and state-space models. Sequential pattern mining uses projected databases, frequent subsequences, and generic constraint solvers, with applications to web-user and DNA-sequence analysis.

Database infrastructure is another major theme: layered uniform grids, hierarchical binary space partitioning, and sampled flat Voronoi tessellations accelerate search and mining. Dynamic physiological partitioning redistributes data across shared-nothing clusters while managing migration, query runtime, node utilization, and energy constraints.

Evaluation uses AUC/MAUC, ROC curves, error rate, lift at 5, dropout rate, and query runtime.

b0d1af7fc03cdd296842f6d28afd09a30ce1d63a.text:
## Community Report: Rumor Detection, Knowledge Retrieval, and Research Intelligence

This community connects machine learning, natural language processing, and artificial intelligence with rumor detection, misinformation classification, knowledge-graph retrieval, and scientific research support.

Rumor research focuses on early detection and debunking, particularly health-related rumors. Neural models learn hidden representations from rumor-related tweets, while rumor classification models combine low- and high-level features. Propagation features describe content-propagation cascades but are less useful during early rumor phases. Classification accuracy improves within the first 10 hours, and one model exceeds 90% accuracy on a curated rumor dataset. Misinformation studies compare conspiracy theories with scientific news and fact-checked content, using sources including the World Health Organization and Snopes.

AqquCN is a question-answering system that combines web-corpus and knowledge-graph evidence. It uses convolutional networks and latent-variable query interpretation for entity ranking and entity-set retrieval, evaluated with F1 and mean average precision on TREC and public query workloads. Language models support rhetorical-relation-aware document relevance estimation, where discourse links such as contrast, cause, and explanation improve retrieval effectiveness.

QT2S applies machine learning and NLP to fine-grained geographic grounding of tweets, supporting disaster response and real-time traffic monitoring. CASP-DM extends CRISP-DM with context handling, model reuse, and enhanced process outputs. A digital encyclopedia organizes correct, up-to-date scientific results and solved problems through personalized interfaces intended to improve research efficiency.

d6aa815da399bfbd7f35ddc125527e303d986661.text:
## Community Report: Trustworthy Social Data, Graph Privacy, and Reproducible Research

This community links machine learning with social-media analysis, entity resolution, privacy, information design, and scientific reproducibility.

Social-media research addresses fake news and rumors: platforms can spread falsified content, while linguistic and content analysis, social context, datasets, and machine learning support rumor detection and debunking. Interpretable machine learning and transparent news-feed algorithms are proposed to mitigate fake-news propagation. Influencer marketing uses quantitative and qualitative information—engagement rate, community size, reach, audience value, demographic attributes, natural text, images, and video—to evaluate influencers; an influencer dataset covers five platforms and 713,824 influencers.

Entity-resolution methods include blocking, filtering, hybrid techniques, schema-agnostic blocking, block processing, and random-forest classification using source trustworthiness. ReLiC performs entity profiling and profile completion, using authoritative sources and selection criteria, and outperforms COMET experimentally.

Graph anonymization protects real graph datasets, while graph de-anonymization exploits their structural properties; the DK series provides anonymity models evaluated against such attacks, with machine learning enabling attack techniques.

Information design studies electricity consumption, prosocial behavior, and resource sharing through quantized and privacy-aware feedback, mean-field equilibria, and fixed-point equations.

Finally, reproducibility frameworks implement FAIR principles—findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability—supporting computational experiments, with ecological niche modeling as a case study.

a9db1fa65856b71cedb82a7976c4274633ffc463.text:
## Community Report: Machine Learning, Document Intelligence, and Social Analytics

This community connects machine learning, scalable data processing, and decision-support systems. The **corpus conversion service** supports document ingestion at scale through microservices, document conversion, and custom model training on document collections. It converts documents into structured formats, while PDFs, bitmap images, and complex tables remain challenging inputs; conversion quality reaches approximately 99% precision and recall.

**DANA** provides hardware-accelerated in-database machine learning, integrating with PostgreSQL and outperforming multi-threaded MADlib. It automatically generates and configures FPGA accelerators, uses the Striders hardware structure and database catalog information, and expresses user-defined functions through a Python embedded DSL. DANA achieves an average 11.3× end-to-end speedup over MADlib.

Social media analytics platforms use machine learning to identify topic pathways, tourism aspects, sentiment, and deeper emotional feedback, presenting insights through visualization tools for business decision making. Content-polluter and fake-profile detection use tweet-based methods, network data, real-time streams, and fake-user data, including applications to civil-unrest prediction.

Finally, **VizRec** improves visual recommendation systems, controls misleading recommendations, and applies classical statistical testing, VC dimension, statistical significance, and statistical learning theory.

b110aa193d21f2301e6ae1fec941ab75be844cca.text:
## Machine Learning, Web Archives, and Social Data Systems

This community centers on **machine learning**, spanning entity matching, web knowledge extraction, table recognition, employment-status prediction, genealogy data mining, computational advertising, and social-media analysis. Machine learning is combined with **string similarity**, dissimilarity spaces, relevance feedback, graph operator modeling, and timeline-based features; applications include detecting like-farm accounts, identifying leadership roles, and analyzing informal social relationships.

A major strand concerns **technology-assisted review** and autonomous continuous active learning. These methods extend Cormack and Grossman continuous active learning, use relevance feedback, and are evaluated on legal datasets, Reuters RCV1, TREC 6, and the TREC 2002 filtering collection.

Another strand addresses **web archiving and temporal retrieval**. The Wayback Machine, web archives, Heritrix, Memento, timemaps, datetime negotiation, and web archive interfaces support access to archived pages and revisions. Crawling methods include deferred representation discovery, two-tiered crawling, and sliding-target policies; archived-page timestamping involves cryptographic hashes and repeatability requirements.

The community also studies **social networks and cooperation**, using visualization, clustering, centrality analysis, and geographic aggregation to examine online communities, leadership, and evolving cooperation. Finally, cloud infrastructure supports scientific workflows, provenance capture, and resource re-provisioning, while parallel dataflow systems address scalable processing.

3da4689fbdcd38706a5e61a3cc24bc29bc618f40.text:
## Web Archives, Learning, and Scalable Data Analysis

This community connects web archiving, machine learning, and data-intensive social and scientific analysis. The Wayback Machine and Internet Archive support archived-page access, with DIP, Slide, Dive, and Skim describing human or robotic access patterns. The Web Archive API exposes content and structural metadata, inlinks, and outlinks. Memento and its MediaWiki extension support datetime negotiation and correct revision retrieval.

Archiving research addresses temporal drift, archival quality, inconsistency windows, and deferred representations. Deferred Representation Discovery and Crawling uses PhantomJS and an adapted Hypercube model to capture client-side embedded resources, though it is slower than Heritrix. EPOW improves crawling through parallelization and scheduling, while two-tiered crawling and sliding or sticky target policies manage archive access.

Machine learning supports entity matching, relevance feedback, web knowledge extraction, table recognition, computational advertising, employment-status prediction, and detection of like-farm accounts using timeline features. Autonomous Continuous Active Learning applies relevance feedback to technology-assisted review and is evaluated on legal, Reuters, and TREC datasets. Scalable entity matching runs generic algorithms across small data neighborhoods.

Other strands analyze informal social networks, cooperation, leadership, and online communities, and apply genealogy data mining to population dynamics. Cloud-aware provenance, workflow repeatability, and resource re-provisioning connect cloud infrastructure with reproducible scientific workflows.

793eb4b2a9c8ad554f837390c80b689d6e604090.text:
## Community Report: Social Diffusion, Search, Healthcare NLP, and Data Systems

This community spans four major themes.

**Social-media diffusion and misinformation:** Gab datasets (22–34 million posts, millions of conversation cascades) support topic discovery, cascade analysis, hate-speech diffusion, and study of alt-right, conspiracy, troll, and news communities. Rumor spreading is modeled with susceptible–infected, Bass, upgraded Bass, and Pólya’s urn models. Tasks include rumor-source detection and latent infected-node identification, using MAP estimation, infection betweenness, cascade patterns, and cascade accuracy. Blockchain-based sequential algorithms and information-exchange contracts aim to limit rapid spreading.

**Search and querying:** Search-by-ideal-candidates generates transparent queries and dynamically refreshes ranking. Query generation, labeling, learned SQL embeddings, workload sampling, database-agnostic management, and security auditing support multi-tenant database systems. Simple batch and directional interactive querying address query budgets and potentially untruthful answers.

**Healthcare NLP:** Two-stage federated NLP uses distributed clinical notes without moving data, supporting patient representation learning, obesity and comorbidity phenotyping, and healthcare-system knowledge progression. Clinical NLP, automated feature generation, sublanguage analysis, and information extraction also support surgical-site infection detection and electronic medical records.

**Navigation and recommendation:** Human-navigation simulation models spatial cognition, k-hop preferences, and path properties, informed by BioPortal clickstreams and human experiments. ZoneRec applies machine learning to Facebook business and urban-planning data to recommend zones for Singapore food businesses, evaluating feature groups and temporal generalization.

470e7191d5044b6af5a84267a5d451ae64c9d787.text:
### Web Search, Retrieval Evaluation, and Recommendation

This community centers on web information retrieval and the evaluation of search engines, including Google, Bing, Yahoo, and Microsoft systems. Search engines receive queries, produce search results and snippets, and are assessed through offline and online evaluation using relevance judgments, relevance labels, query logs, and datasets such as TREC ad hoc data, scientific abstracts, and the Bing drug query dataset.

Key effectiveness measures include MAP, nDCG, graded relevance measures, correct answer rate, quality score, and preference identification ratio. The literature addresses evaluation bias, assessor disagreement, rank similarity, and frameworks for meta-evaluation and retrieval effectiveness evaluation.

Core retrieval methods include automatic and feedback query expansion, RM3, association- and distribution-based term selection, combined term selection, statistical stemming, semantic mapping, query segmentation, on-the-fly query decomposition, and document expansion by query prediction. Ranking approaches include machine-learned ranking, pairwise and supervised learning to rank, dynamic ranking, centroid-based rank fusion, and multi-stage retrieval with filtering and candidate-generation stages.

Related systems support web crawling, web archive search, hidden-web discovery, information cards, aspect computation, and web-based data imputation. Recommendation systems connect filtering and ranking with user interaction, navigation behavior, personalization, marketing, and evaluation bias.

89b1b1f1a8897907f506ea8f3419bf3c475eed57.text:
## Community Report: Diffusion, Search, and Recommendation Models

This community links three themes in online information systems.

**Hate speech diffusion:** Hate speech occurs on online social media and is generated by hateful users, while non-hateful users provide a comparison group. Hateful users show distinctive diffusion dynamics, greater outreach, higher popularity, and more cohesive profiles and networks. Hate and non-hate speech datasets support analysis of semantic relations, including texts containing “women,” “white,” and “black.” Epidemic models and stochastic SIR approaches study online information diffusion, while Hawkes point processes, HawkesN, and extended Hawkes models represent self-exciting activity, finite populations, and cascade-size distributions.

**Entity-oriented search:** Entity-oriented search addresses information needs through direct answers and service interaction. Search intents are categorized into entity intent categories. Query refiners are studied by entity type and query annotation; over half seek service interaction, while more than a quarter seek knowledge-base information. Popularity and recency affect item-entity linking.

**Recommendation and semantics:** Item-based collaborative filtering learns item similarity using cosine similarity, Pearson coefficient, historical item profiles, and recommendation-aware objectives. NAIS adds an attention network and improves on FISM, with evaluations on public benchmarks. Knowledge-aware recommender systems connect items to knowledge-base entities. Quantum semantic correlations use quantum geometry to study similar meaning and semantic relations, compared with cosine similarity.

7a6c6858a93d03951179430a2cc0a405f297bd09.text:
## Community Report: Bias, Cascades, Archives, and Recommendation

This community connects research on online platforms, network behavior, information retrieval, named-entity recognition, and product recommendation.

**Gab** is studied through its posts and a dataset of approximately 34 million posts, 3.7 million cascading conversation threads, and nearly 300,000 users. Research examines hate speech, anti-Semitism, language use, topic discovery, topic evolution, and five cascading patterns. Echo-chamber patterns precede the most viral cascades, while susceptible-infected and Bass models predict cascade evolution with up to 84% accuracy. The Pittsburgh synagogue shooting and shooters’ posts provide a related case involving Gab users and anti-Semitism.

**Bias and networks** are examined in Airbnb and co-authorship settings. Airbnb shows gender and racial-bias signals, homophily, heterophily, avoidance, offline bias, and links to gentrification. Network statistical analysis measures these behaviors. The NKOS co-authorship network, built from the NKOS bibliography, studies gender differences, institutional proximity, and geographic proximity.

**Named-entity recognition** is evaluated for gender bias using U.S. Census baby names and training datasets: male names are recognized more often as PERSON entities than female names.

**Archives and retrieval** include Memento infrastructure, its aggregator, web archives, federated search, and caching. Cache systems reduce response time and achieve 70–80% human-service hit rates.

Finally, the bundle generation network uses encoder-decoder modeling, feature-aware softmax, DPPs, and masked beam search for personalized product bundles, improving diversity and response time.

74c44e48797d39fe5245940cbb382fdcf6bc7b7a.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: Semantic Retrieval, Taxonomies, and Online Ranking

This community centers on information retrieval and recommendation, especially vocabulary or term mismatch, query expansion, entity relatedness, and conceptual indexing. Word embeddings support concept embeddings, which produce concept vectors for estimating inter-concept similarity and improving indexing. Query expansion combines word embeddings, pseudo-relevance feedback, gradient search augmentation, and embedding-based methods; pseudo-relevance feedback plus gradient search augmentation performs best overall and improves a TF-IDF retrieval system. Semantic hashing is another retrieval method.

Topic taxonomy construction is addressed by TaxoGen, which recursively constructs taxonomies using term embeddings, local embedding, hierarchical clustering, and adaptive spherical clustering. The resulting taxonomy organizes semantically coherent term clusters and supports recommendation, information filtering, and web search.

Recommendation methods include GemRank, which factorizes user–item information from a user–item matrix and performs well across data densities, and the knowledge-aware path recurrent network. The latter composes entity and relation semantics into path representations, models sequential dependencies, and uses weighted pooling for explainability; it supports preference prediction and cold-start recommendation and outperforms collaborative knowledge-base embedding and neural factorization machine baselines.

Online ranker evaluation is modeled as a K-armed dueling bandit problem using interleaved pairwise comparisons. MergedTS applies divide-and-conquer and Thompson sampling under a Condorcet assumption, reducing suboptimal comparisons and evaluated by regret and time complexity.

a682e33ea8ad957ab503cf892bc564bbaaa04edb.text:
## Mobility, Retrieval, Speech, and Sequential Prediction

This community covers machine-learning methods for human mobility, information retrieval, hate-speech detection, music representation, and sequential recommendation.

Human mobility prediction uses current and historical user trajectories, fine-grained on-device behavioral data, and multi-modal learning to support location-based services. Tasks include next-venue and trip-destination prediction, with performance affected by prediction-target granularity. Human mobility modeling surveys and data-driven frameworks analyze real-world mobility datasets, quantify mobility meta-attributes, select prediction algorithms, and apply rigorous validation. Recurrent and Markov models are frequently used.

For sequential skip prediction, recurrent neural networks—including the weighted **W RNN**—model user interaction features, serialized text semantic information, and song metadata. W RNN uses word vectors and weighted text-representation vectors, and is evaluated by loss, recall, and F1; one recurrent model achieves 0.648 mean average accuracy. Ensemble models combine recurrent or deep-learning architectures and improve recommendation performance. The WSDM Cup 2019 task was won by ekffar, whose implementation was open-sourced on GitHub.

Information retrieval uses deep-learning systems such as **Duet** and **Conv-KNRM** on wikIR59k, Robust04, and ClueWeb09, though these methods require substantial annotated data. Hate-speech detection uses multilingual, human-annotated tweet datasets—including personal attacks and journalism-related accounts—and benefits from ensembles. Mel spectrogram configurations trade frequency and time resolution, evaluated with Million Song Dataset and MagnaTagATune.

67cb211418129b2eb3c1c02fffe544774376f18b.text:
## Web Search, Retrieval, and Evaluation

This community centers on web information retrieval, major search engines, and methods for measuring and improving retrieval effectiveness. Google, Yahoo, Bing, Microsoft, and other search engines produce search results and search engine results pages; Google and Bing show high agreement in top results, while Google outperforms Bing in reported retrieval effectiveness and achieves a 95.3% correct-answer rate for navigational queries.

Evaluation relies on relevance judgments, relevance labels, query logs, scientific abstracts, snippets, and datasets such as TREC ad hoc data, WT10G, and the Bing drug query dataset. Metrics and frameworks include MAP, NDCG, quality score, rank similarity measures, maximized effectiveness difference (MED), offline evaluation, weighted offline evaluation, and retrieval-effectiveness and meta-evaluation frameworks. These address assessor disagreement, evaluation bias, partial judgments, and efficiency–effectiveness tradeoffs.

Query processing is another major theme: automatic and feedback query expansion, RM3, BO1, local context analysis, association- and distribution-based term selection, statistical stemming, query segmentation, semantic mapping, and on-the-fly query decomposition. Combined term selection can improve effectiveness.

Systems also cover machine-learned and supervised ranking, dynamic ranking, candidate generation, filtering, and result reranking. Web crawlers support indexing, data extraction, accessibility and vulnerability checking, while web-based imputation and hidden-data extraction exploit search results. Recommendation systems connect ranking and filtering with user interaction and evaluation bias.

8992618b92ef5da4868363cfa15130ebc1ec90d3.text:
## Ranking, Linked Data, and Question Exploration

This community centers on information retrieval and learning to rank for web search and e-commerce search. Traditional learning-to-rank methods require relevance judgments, while online learning-to-rank learns from user interactions and faces a speed–quality tradeoff between rapid learning and optimal rankings. Click rate, order rate, revenue, and add-to-cart ratio provide feedback signals; among evaluated objectives, order rate is reported as the most robust. Popularity- and relevance-based features must be combined under query-attribute sparsity. SIM-MGD accelerates convergence and improves user experience, while C-MGD preserves MGD convergence while addressing speed.

A second theme is recommendation with Linked Open Data (LOD). Factorization Machines support top-N recommendation using lightweight LOD-enabled features, including property-object lists and PageRank scores; KNN-item and BPRMF serve as baselines, while subject-property lists decrease performance. LOD features may also be obtained through a public SPARQL endpoint. Freebase supplies billions of RDF triples for information retrieval and knowledge-based question answering, with parsing supported by open-source Unix-like tools.

The community also studies crowdsourced exploration of growing, networked question sets. Worker allocation balances discovering new questions with answering current ones, maintains crowd-answer confidence, enables unbounded exploration, and reduces growth bias. Indri, implemented in C++, exposes search through Luandri; Luandri interfaces with Torch models written in Lua.

8443c3a93ac74839c5f80d6e9cb155ca526578d2.text:
## Community Report: Recommender Systems, News Understanding, and Online Evaluation

This community centers on personalized recommendation and its measurement in production settings. **MR DLib**, built on the **Living Lab**, delivers scholarly article recommendations through systems including **Sowiport** and **JabRef**; it delivered 94 million recommendations and supports online A/B evaluation. **Click-through rate (CTR)** is a central engagement metric, used to assess immediate personalized news recommendation, recommendation engines, and advertising. Methods such as **context-aware deep models**, **contextual rankers**, **FLEN**, and **privileged-features distillation** improve CTR, while **algorithmic ad rewriting** targets higher CTR and valence in medical and preventative-health advertising. **Zorro** estimates CTR without access to proprietary advertiser models.

The community also addresses evaluation methodology: **A/B testing**, **multi-armed bandit testing**, offline/online testing, and metrics such as conversion rate, dwell time, and Pearson correlation. 

For news understanding, **Story Forest** performs online document clustering, identifies events, and incrementally builds story trees over Chinese news data. **LDA**, topic extraction, and concept-taxonomy methods organize long and short texts, user queries, and click logs. Compact retrieval is supported by **recurrent binary embedding**, enabling bit-wise similarity and billion-item-scale exhaustive retrieval.

a9291cba45e281430469106339c8e0815039a19b.text:
## Semantic Web Visibility and Session-Based Search

This community connects semantic annotation deployment in tourism with intelligent search and query suggestion. Semantic annotations, created according to the schema.org vocabulary, contribute to semantic structured data. The Semantify It platform supports annotation file creation and publication and enables website integration without programming. It served the deployment effort beginning with Tourismusverband Mayrhofen Hippach, addressing touristic service providers in Tyrol. These annotations improve online visibility, reduce providers’ dependency on online travel agencies, help search engines understand web content, and enable intelligent applications. Semantic structured data is also relied upon by search engines, chatbots, and intelligent personal assistants.

The second topic is session search, where queries evolve through query reformulation and reflect a dynamic information need. Session-based query suggestion uses session context to infer the next query and scores candidate queries. A sequence-to-sequence model captures session context, incorporating query-aware attention and a copy mechanism that lets the decoder copy source words. An extended relevance model is driven by users’ query reformulation decisions, estimates how search behavior affects those decisions, and significantly improves session search performance. Vocabulary selection is addressed by Semantify It, linking semantic-data creation with practical deployment.

cd85124e2ba2a05be8cbbfe918bad9ba8e1c4fbb.text:
## Social Networks: Influence, Diffusion, and Structural Analysis

This community centers on social networks modeled as nodes and relationships, including directed, multiplex, time-dependent, and small-world structures. Core topics include information spread, rumor dissemination, viral marketing, social advertising, peer effects, opinion dynamics, social cohesion, communities, hierarchy, and network stability.

Influence-oriented tasks select or minimize seed users, maximize coverage, allocate coupons, and optimize revenue or sponsored advertising. Methods include heuristics, local greedy algorithms, scalable seed-set algorithms, monotone submodular maximization, distributed algorithms, and polynomial-time approaches. General threshold, DeGroot–Friedkin, Friedkin–Johnsen, polar opinion, and other temporal models describe diffusion, social power, adoption, and competing opinions.

Network analysis uses centrality, degree, outdegree, harmonic centrality, shortest distance, graph diameter, tie strength, structural cohesion, navigability, and spread width or speed. Network embedding—including content-enhanced CENE—supports node classification, role identification, profile matching, and cross-network identity resolution. Systems and datasets such as Friendster, Wi-Fi access logs, EverQuest2, fitness status updates, and cell-phone call networks support empirical evaluation. Applications extend to internet advertising, trust networks, product visibility, market segmentation, and user retention.

06972a956ca54aace034728279db4fe96005dc47.text:
## Information Retrieval: Ranking, Expansion, and Evaluation

This community centers on information retrieval systems for document collections, search engines, digital libraries, and scholarly information systems. Core tasks include ad hoc and web document retrieval, document ranking, question answering, expert finding, entity linking, semantic matching, and exploratory or recency search.

Ranking research spans traditional retrieval models such as BM25, TF-IDF, vector-space and language models, as well as learning-to-rank, online and unbiased learning-to-rank, re-ranking, and ranking pipelines. Neural approaches use deep neural networks, LSTMs, neural embeddings, and neural rankers to address contextual dependencies, semantic matching, and vocabulary mismatch. PACRR, CO-PACRR, MatchPyramid, ANMM, and other neural systems represent this direction.

Query expansion and reformulation are prominent methods, including relevance feedback, pseudo-relevance feedback, automatic and structural expansion, combination-based expansion, and polyrepresentation. Candidate generation and semantic or text matching support these pipelines.

Evaluation relies on relevance assessment and judgments, TREC collections and test collections, click data, and training data. Key measures include mean average precision, average precision, NDCG, retrieval effectiveness, retrieval performance, retrieval quality, ranking robustness, user experience, and evaluation reliability. Position bias motivates counterfactual risk minimization, counterfactual learning-to-rank, propensity-weighted ranking SVM, and related unbiased methods. Elasticsearch provides an applied retrieval platform.

aec72295646656838527a960cc16455bc479b8c8.text:
## Community Report: Social, Web, Geospatial, and Causal Data Mining

This community centers on mining online, social, geographic, and health data to discover patterns, predict behavior, and assess change.

**Web and social-media analysis** includes web usage mining of web logs for pattern discovery, forecasting, customer profiling, personalized services, and adaptive websites. HITS and a HITS–PageRank mixture model forecast hit counts, identify authority users, and analyze access statistics. Tumblr is studied as a hybrid microblogging, blogging, and social-networking platform, including reblogging patterns and blog recommendation. Friendship prediction exploits overlapping users, hashtag profiles, composite social networks, and hierarchical Bayesian models.

**Group and mobility analysis** addresses social group evolution and change identification.
