GED and SGCI identify evolution events and stable groups, with evaluation based on flexibility, implementation ease, and user importance. Geo-spatiotemporal pattern discovery explores propagation and influential patterns, while home-location estimation uses social networks, centrality analysis, and iterative location propagation. Seed-driven extraction improves data yield and request efficiency through search-radius optimization and recursive clustering.

**Causal, health, and behavioral modeling** includes causal inference from observational and EHR data, controlling confounding under strong ignorability and using matching, survival-based testing, and bootstrap difference-in-differences. TARS/TBP model purchase periodicity and recurrency, while deep learning uses headline and article-body features and their semantic relation.

482d71f8ff35a7b8682df87be0077bae46df7618.text:
## Social Networks, Influence, and Graph Analytics

This community centers on social networks modeled as graphs of actors, nodes, and relationships, including directed, temporal, multiplex, and semantic-multiplex structures. It studies information flow, rumor dissemination, viral marketing, peer effects, social cohesion, collective behavior, and small-world navigability.

A major theme is influence maximization: seed selection supports viral marketing, social item maximization, maximum coverage, and incentivized social advertising. Static and temporal approaches rank candidate seeds, with outdegree often outperforming other time-dependent measures. Monotone submodular maximization, partition-matroid and submodular-knapsack constraints, scalable seed-set algorithms, local greedy methods, and polynomial-time algorithms address these optimization problems.

Other work models consumer response and advertising through click models, multinomial and mixed multinomial logit methods, product visibility, social cues, attractiveness, and externalities. Social Item Graphs capture influence and item propagation.

Graph analytics covers node classification, role identification, profile matching, cross-network identity resolution, expertise testing, and network embedding, including CENE, GCHMMs, and Kohonen self-organizing maps. Structural analysis uses centrality, harmonic centrality, graph diameter, tie strength, cohesion, membership dimension, and metric tree likeness. Systems and datasets include web search engines, internet advertising, Wi-Fi access logs, click logs, EverQuest2, Fitness Status Updates, and DPBench.

57127dc818107f64932f7b13d2f27a3198f22ecf.text:
## Semantic Web, RDF, and Linked Data Systems

This community centers on RDF as the W3C-standard graph data model underlying Linked Data, Linked Open Data, and Semantic Web applications. RDF graphs represent subject–predicate–object relationships and support bibliographic data, scientific results, metadata, table extraction, and open-data publishing. Nanopublications and micropublications use RDF to represent research results.

SPARQL is the principal language for querying RDF datasets and SPARQL endpoints. Research addresses SPARQL query processing, basic graph patterns, query evaluation, linked-data querying, ontology-mediated query answering, and query workloads such as real-world query corpora and “streaks.” Extensions and related systems include Gremlinator, CPSPARQL, and Sage; performance is compared across systems including OpenLink Virtuoso, 4Store, and JenaTDB. RDF graph engines and methods include query graph assembly, OptBitMat, RDF views, and distributed RDF data management.

Ontologies, OWL, RDFS, SKOS, and Shape Expressions provide semantics, schemas, annotations, and constraints for heterogeneous data integration. Related concerns include RDF constraints, class completeness, ontology summarization, and semantic annotation. Data quality and provenance are recurring themes, supported by Luzzu, nanopublication provenance models, computational provenance, and provenance summarization.

The community also covers semantic and keyword search, information access, dataset interlinking, RDF instance matching, and search over large or streaming data.

2b780c83d6dbd7ba700c1e638e91aeab049dd9bb.text:
### Information Retrieval and Neural Ranking

This community centers on information retrieval, especially document retrieval, ad hoc retrieval, document ranking, and complex answer retrieval. Digital libraries, search engines, Elasticsearch, online public access catalogs, and retrieval services provide application settings, while TREC collections and related datasets support evaluation.

A major theme is ranking. Traditional approaches include BM25, vector space and language models, Dirichlet belief networks, retrieval models, ranking functions, relevance feedback, pseudo-relevance feedback, and query expansion or reformulation. These address vocabulary mismatch, term similarity, and weak or ambiguous queries through candidate generation, document expansion, and query prediction.

Deep neural networks support neural ranking models and rankers, including PACRR, CO-PACRR, MatchPyramid, Match Tensor, DeepCAS, and multi-task neural ranking. Curriculum learning, supervised and online learning to rank, hand-crafted features, and training data support ranking pipelines. Interpretability is addressed through LIME, DeepSHAP, retrieval-model interpretability, and calibration.

Evaluation emphasizes retrieval effectiveness, retrieval performance, retrieval quality, average precision, user experience, and evaluation reliability. Human annotators, relevance assessment, user studies, query logs, and TREC benchmarks connect system performance with user-centered assessment. Related applications include expert finding, literature review, exploratory search, search-session segmentation, recommendation, and scientific information retrieval.

4f54648c634e24ef6b1a932e89486733968bd766.text:
### Structured Query Analysis and Graph Database Interfaces

This community covers structured-query systems, graph databases, and interactive query interfaces. **Precision interfaces** analyze how structured queries change by examining input query logs; they support both **SQL** and **SPARQL**, analyze fewer than 75,000 queries in under 12 minutes, and generate interactive interfaces and interaction designs intended to improve existing interfaces.

**Knowledge bases** and **ontologies** provide external knowledge for constructing structured queries, while knowledge bases also support the construction of entity representations. **Query expansion** uses knowledge bases to expand queries.

**Graph database systems** store and process heterogeneous network-like datasets, but lack established standards for both data models and query languages. Vendors support **SQL** as an existing standard language and are working toward query-language standardization. SQL also provides a framework for implementing privacy constructs, while SPARQL is used to express and execute structured queries.

Interactive interfaces are tailored to user tasks. Examples range from **Google Finance**, a simple interactive interface, to **Tableau**, a complex visual exploration interface. Tableau’s salient interaction components are derived from **OLAP queries**.

f26d349c02d53869d5a42a067e4371c5a34d43c2.text:
## Information Retrieval, Scholarly Search, and Recommendation

This community centers on **information retrieval** for web, scholarly, scientific, and digital-library settings. Core tasks include ad hoc retrieval, entity retrieval, expert finding, relevance prediction, topical relevance assessment, literature review, and top-*k* retrieval. Digital libraries and scholarly information systems provide important environments, while recommendation systems address expert, author, journal, movie, and scientific-paper recommendation.

Retrieval models include the **vector space model**, language models, BM25, ranking functions, and neural ranking models. Neural information retrieval uses representation learning, neural embeddings, long short-term memory, PACRR, MatchPyramid, and related models. Query expansion is supported by pseudo-relevance feedback, structural and concept-based expansion, combination-based expansion, term dependencies, WordNet, and query-term co-occurrence. Re-ranking, online learning to rank, click models, user click feedback, and propensity-weighted ranking SVM support interactive and personalized search.

Key systems include **Mr. DLib**, the scientific paper recommender and retrieval framework, search-term and author-name recommenders, Arabic information retrieval systems, service-enhanced retrieval systems, and document browsers. Evaluation uses TREC collections, the iSearch test collection, user-query data, relevance assessments, average precision, retrieval quality and performance, Fleiss’ kappa, and Krippendorff’s alpha.

afcdca342524d6e229636c7772c8fd5725e36cb5.text:
## Graph Systems, Literature Exploration, and Similarity Methods

This community connects graph databases, graph processing, and scientific-literature exploration. RedisGraph, developed by Redis Labs as a Redis module, adds graph-database functionality and represents connected data through adjacency and sparse matrices. It employs GraphBLAS for optimized sparse-matrix operations and supports graph processing; benchmarks report improved performance.

Property graphs are stored and processed in graph databases such as Neo4j. Their schemas involve data-definition languages, schema validation, and schema evolution: validation is enforced through homomorphisms, while evolution is represented by graph rewriting. Neo4j 3.5 provides partial schema support, and high-level query primitives accommodate flexible schemas. Cypher inspires proposed schema-DDL syntax.

GrapAL, built on Neo4j, queries the Semantic Scholar literature graph through a simple query language. It supports scientific-literature exploration, expert finding, peer-reviewer identification, citation-based metrics, and discovery of indirect biomedical connections.

Short-text topic modeling is represented by the open-source STTM library, integrating methods based on Dirichlet multinomial mixtures, global word co-occurrences, and self-aggregation. Performance is evaluated across datasets and tasks.

Spatial search strategies define spatial similarity computation using area of overlap or Hausdorff distance. A prototype evaluates their effects on performance and user relevance ratings; Hausdorff distance yields slightly better ratings, while both perform similarly in one evaluation. Spectral embedding uses adjacency and Laplacian matrices to map networks into latent spaces.

14dd437facefa2fc9901120ac276b6354089e12a.text:
### Online Recommendation, Retrieval, and Evaluation

This community connects information retrieval, recommendation, and online experimentation. In scholarly recommendation, **Mr. DLib** uses **JabRef** and the **Living Lab API** to deliver article recommendations through the Living Lab, an online evaluation environment. The Living Lab delivered 1,826,643 recommendations and supports online A/B testing.

**Meta-learning** addresses algorithm selection for ad hoc retrieval and scholarly recommendations. A meta-learner predicts how to combine retrieval methods, using axiom-related features derived from queries and top-ranked documents. Gradient boosting machines and generalized linear models serve as meta-learning models, producing overall relevance scores. The multilingual retrieval system performs cross-language ad hoc retrieval for Arabic, Chinese Mandarin, and Spanish, using English collections and sometimes target-language examples.

Recommendation applications include e-commerce personalization, product search, job recommendation, similar-job recommendation, and homepage personalization. Embedding methods use user interaction, recency, and frequency; frequency-recency embeddings perform best for homepage personalization, while recency-based embeddings perform best for similar jobs.

Evaluation spans offline testing, online testing, A/B testing, and multi-armed bandit testing. Bandits reduce exploration cost and have been implemented in production. Metrics include click-through, conversion, buy-through, click-buy rate, dwell time, F1, relevance, and customer interaction measures.

**Privileged-features distillation** improves click-through and conversion prediction by transferring training-only information from a teacher to a serving-time student model.

cfbf4d50577b8d1e6375652bd50adf069db9676c.text:
## Information Retrieval, Query Expansion, and Scholarly Search

This community centers on information retrieval for digital libraries, scholarly information systems, web documents, news, and recommendation services. Retrieval models include the vector space model, BM25, language models, the Polya urn document language model, ranking functions, representation learning, neural embeddings, and long short-term memory methods. Inverted files support search infrastructure.

Query expansion is a major theme: pseudo-relevance feedback, WordNet and thesaurus terms, co-occurrence and co-word analysis, concept-based, structural, combination-based, and collective evolutionary concept-distance expansion improve retrieval performance and quality. Search-term, discipline-specific, author-name, and journal-name recommenders support query formulation, while entity suggestion and entity retrieval extend results with relevant entities. Polyrepresentation motivates adding topical author names.

Systems include scientific paper recommender and retrieval frameworks, service-enhanced retrieval, Arabic information retrieval, academic digital libraries, retrieval services, and search-term recommendation services. Expert finding and expert recommendation connect retrieval with author centrality and bibliometric-enhanced retrieval.

Evaluation uses TREC collections, the iSearch test collection, student relevance assessments, average precision, retrieval-quality and performance measures, and inter-assessor reliability metrics such as Fleiss’ kappa and Krippendorff’s alpha. Topic-based retrieval, re-ranking, adaptive navigation, user click feedback, and relevance prediction address user-centered search.

2086ca082ce415a18ff7209d023d4a4df0b9bac1.text:
## Deep Meta-Structure Similarity and Biomedical Dataset Retrieval

This community focuses on similarity, ranking, clustering, and recommendation in heterogeneous information networks (HINs). Traditional similarity metrics depend on user-specified meta-paths or meta-structures, which may be numerous in HINs and sensitive in clustering.

DMSS is a deep meta-structure-based similarity measure. It decomposes deep meta-structures into deep meta-paths, combines their commuting matrices through local and global weighting strategies, and produces a final commuting matrix. RMSS is based on recurrent meta-structures, which decompose into recurrent meta-paths and recurrent meta-trees. DMSS outperforms state-of-the-art metrics for clustering, while RMSS outperforms existing metrics on ranking and clustering. Similarity measures are also applied to product recommendation and multi-relational recommender systems.

The community also covers Personalized PageRank (PPR) estimation. Bidirectional-PPR for one source-target pair is extended to joint PPR estimation for many pairs; clustering and distributed computation reduce its complexity and execution time.

A ranking pipeline combines similarity measurement, query expansion, and dataset categorization. It was evaluated on a dataset retrieval corpus and the 2016 BioCADDIE Dataset Retrieval Challenge. Query expansion improved baseline InfAP by up to 5.0% and InfNDCG by up to 3.4%; the pipeline achieved the highest InfAP score and could enhance biomedical dataset management systems.

d0ce6750a3285f72c2243534e0769c41be40eb79.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Declarative Analytics, Expert Search, and Industry 4.0

This community connects three themes: data-science systems, semantic expert finding, and data-stream processing for Industry 4.0.

**SystemDS** supports the full data-science lifecycle through declarative languages and frameworks, including data integration, cleaning and preparation, distributed and federated machine learning, debugging, and model serving. Its design draws on Apache SystemML. Declarative frameworks use execution engines capable of centralized or distributed execution, programming models, and optimization techniques.

**WiSer** is a semantic search and expert-finding system. It integrates the Wikipedia knowledge graph, links publication text to Wikipedia entities, and builds author expertise profiles. Structural embeddings, language modeling, semantic relatedness, and random walks support profile-centric scoring and expert ranking. WiSer is applied to the University of Pisa research community, technology transfer, and HTAP applications. Its transaction design uses PROMISE, read-set embedding, serialization sequence numbers, and coordinator-free aggregation constraints to preserve availability while targeting consistency.

**Certus** is an entity-linking system using a graph model for entity profiles and provenance descriptions, with support for multiplicity. Its architecture includes indexing and physical storage models evaluated with HBase and Postgres.

Finally, Industry 4.0 and the Internet of Things motivate data-stream processing systems and technologies, although streaming frameworks face implementation obstacles identified through site inspections and industry findings.

53eab8690fe426660726f9fa7f2c356a7ec46a03.text:
## Urban Dynamics and Social-Media Timing

This community covers urban dynamics modeling, heterogeneous information networks, and social-media posting optimization. **Macross** constructs a heterogeneous information network from aggregated spatial and temporal information and applies a **metapath2vec-based** approach to jointly model location, time, and text information. Metapath2vec learns representations for locations, times, and frequent words. Evaluated on geo-tagged social media posts, Macross outperforms competing models on activity recovery and activity classification. Geographic topic models are identified as previous approaches to urban dynamics modeling.

The community also includes **Bhin2vec**, which embeds nodes in heterogeneous information networks while addressing relation type imbalance. It splits the skip-gram loss into relation-specific task losses and uses a task-aware random-walk strategy. This strategy generates samples according to relative training ratios across tasks.

For Facebook pages, optimal posting time is derived considering information type and location, implemented through posting schedules, and intended to maximize content visibility. Posting schedules apply to individual pages or groups of similar pages. The Facebook Pages dataset contains approximately 10 million audience reactions, which serve as an outcome measure for content visibility; audience reactions are influenced by posting time. Temporal analysis examines daily, weekly, and monthly patterns, while information spread is reflected in content visibility.

3d6975532872486959db7120e4519b368a7c664a.text:
## Influence Maximization in Social Networks

This community centers on **influence maximization**: selecting a limited **seed set** or seed users to maximize expected **influence spread**, information dissemination, product awareness, or adoption through network diffusion. It is commonly formulated as **submodular maximization** under a budget constraint, where greedy algorithms provide approximation guarantees, ratios, or factors.

The main diffusion models are the **independent cascade**, **linear threshold**, contagion, triggering, and discrete-time Markov-chain models. Influence spread can be estimated using **Monte Carlo simulation**, mean-field approximation, reverse influence sampling, and methods such as **IMM**, **SSA**, **TIM**, **IRIE**, and **QuickIM**.

Extensions address deadlines (**time-critical influence maximization** and Proteus IM), sequential observation and uncertainty (**adaptive influence maximization**, adaptive seeding), targeted users, multiplex networks, two-phase seed selection and activation, and competing or interacting entities. Other objectives include revenue, profit, coupon allocation, multiple-product adoption, diversity of exposure, audience or seed diversification, and influence limitation.

The community also studies influence disparity, adversarial settings, network structure, intrinsic nodal activation, and economic utilities such as perfect substitutes, perfect complements, and Cobb–Douglas. Related analysis includes social centrality, influential-node tracking, community partitioning, and influence-source disentanglement.

e31a8c24d0ce85aa3786e7064fbf27d0bfda0bcf.text:
## Social Graphs, Retrieval, and Network Resilience

This community centers on social and heterogeneous information networks, with applications in recommendation, search, prediction, mobility, and network security. Social graphs support social recommendations, collaborative retrieval, cultural-interest propagation, consumer-choice analysis, and socially informed routing; they also provide the basis for node and edge betweenness analysis.

Data sparsity is a recurring challenge in collaborative retrieval, friendship prediction, rating, and trust data. Social collaborative retrieval, latent collaborative retrieval, and ILCR use social information and query–user–item tensors, while factor models, semi-supervised algorithms, weak social connections, and hierarchical Bayesian models mitigate sparse observations. Friendship prediction further exploits overlapping users and composite social networks.

Heterogeneous information networks support network mining, neighbor-distribution prediction, recommender systems, anomaly detection, and entity ranking. Relevant methods include meta-path similarity, BHIN2VEC, Macross, weighted heterogeneous networks, and relation-type handling. Search research includes projection graphs, social search, entity search, multi-faceted ranking, snippet scoring, and local top-k queries, evaluated with mean average precision, perplexity, and query response time.

A second major theme is network robustness. Cyber and physical networks are modeled as interdependent systems subject to targeted or random attacks, failure propagation, cascading failures, and network takeover. Network disintegration is assessed using giant-component size and betweenness, while fixed-point analysis, self-healing, and evolution models address resilience. Road-network work studies shortest-path queries, path costs, and travel time.

ff4290490bd466234221d669447f3c33872906ec.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: ESG, Adverse Media, and Heterogeneous Networks

This community connects financial text analysis, ESG compliance, risk management, and cyber defense. Sentence-level sentiment analysis examines financial news, using distributed text representations, multi-instance learning, and context preservation to transfer information from document-level analysis. Evaluated on a manually labeled dataset, it achieves predictive accuracy of up to 69.90% and supports financial decision-making.

For ESG compliance prediction, an investment exclusion list prediction model uses negative news exclusion list data and heterogeneous information networks (HINs) containing information about listed firms and annual reports. These models predict firms likely to enter exclusion lists, supporting risk management and socially responsible investment. Adverse media prediction models learn from adverse media coverage data to predict future coverage and enable surveillance of powerful institutions, while also supporting risk management and socially responsible investment. HIN information substantially improves predictive accuracy over methods without network information.

The community also highlights HEER, which performs comprehensive transcription of heterogeneous information networks through edge representations and learned heterogeneous metrics. HEER is evaluated via edge reconstruction on two large-scale real-world datasets. Cyber attack prediction supports cyber defense and risk management, while reliable protection is required for information systems infrastructure.

fd1bfaf818b9cb4cc7c5199f173da2501f047951.text:
## Ontologies, Emergency Management, and Scholarly Networks

This community centers on ontology-based knowledge representation, ontology summarization, emergency management, and scholarly network analysis. An **ontology** provides a framework for publishing, sharing, and reusing data in the Semantic Web, supports heterogeneous information integration, and includes data and schema layers. **Ontology understanding** supports ontology engineering and ontology learning, while **ontology summarization** produces abridged ontology summaries through various summarization methods and measures.

The **EMPATHI ontology** conceptualizes emergency management and planning, models hazard crises, represents core concepts and relations, and supports integration of heterogeneous information. Situational awareness draws on social media content, satellite imagery, and local sensor data, and is critical for emergency management and planning.

**Korona** performs scholarly community discovery using graph partition, supports scholarly network prediction, and applies semantic similarity measures. It uncovers co-authorship networks and predicts such networks using the **Pure dataset**, which contains research data collected from the University of Bristol. These networks are analyzed with academic information. The **scholarly knowledge graph** contains Semantic Web scholarly data, with semantic similarity determining relatedness among its entities.

85f3821998ee6ced1b5a1abfb5553367a10486a1.text:
## Community Report: Social Graph Mining, Recommendation, and Community Analysis

This community centers on graph-based analysis of social and heterogeneous information networks, spanning recommendation, classification, spam detection, graph exploration, and community detection.

**LCGR** and **LLGR** extend discrete choice models with, respectively, latent-class and local logistic graph regularization. Both incorporate social relationships, target large-scale social-media applications, and are evaluated on synthetic and real-world datasets. LCGR models preference discrepancies across social groups using latent classes and MCEM, while LLGR uses ADMM. **SEREC** addresses social recommendation through social exposure, social regularization, and social boosting; causal-process-based recommendation models user exposure before rating prediction.

For review spam, **NetSpam** treats review data as heterogeneous information networks and maps spam detection to classification. It uses behavioral and linguistic features from reviews and users, with evaluations on Yelp and Amazon datasets; review-behavioral features perform particularly well. Entropy-based features support fraud classification and are evaluated on ground-truth Twitter data.

Community analysis includes **MEDOC** and **ENDISCO** for disjoint, overlapping, or fuzzy detection, with runtime and accuracy comparisons; ENDisCo also explores core-periphery structure. **VCExplorer** combines graph exploration, visualization, aggregation, and summarization, using hub-based HA graphs and consolidated information across subgraphs. Path-based relevance methods model cross-meta-path synergy probabilistically for heterogeneous networks.

c24f91a5c79dca52f3d5f4726207c64beb48da85.text:
## Community Report: Social Signals, Emergency Response, and Adaptive Prediction

This community connects research on disaster response, economic resilience, collective emotion, information propagation, search, and email behavior.

For disasters, **sentiment sensing** and collective emotional-response patterns support detection and localization of natural and man-made disasters. Natural disasters can produce pulses in collective emotion, studied through Japanese blog articles, questionnaire surveys, and **collective emotion extraction**. Emotion exhibits weekly, seasonal, and longer periodic cycles, with long-term memory and power-law autocorrelation decay.

Economic resilience is measured through **economic recovery time**: the return of bank-card payments and ATM withdrawals to baseline. Hurricane Odile in Baja California Sur provides a case study linking recovery, income level, and pre-disaster food and gasoline expenditure.

Emergency-operation-center monitoring uses an **alert-based ranking system**, workload bounds, and Pareto-optimal top-k selection to prioritize social-media requests. **Investigative simulation** extends dual graph simulation with categorical labels, partial-match pruning, and ranking.

Information propagation is modeled using temporal scaling, information attractiveness, and individual interactions. The temporal propagation model reduces prediction error from 6.7% to 2.6%.

Other systems address query auto-completion through aggregated engine mixtures optimized in a bandit setting, and personalized conversation through content and social-graph models. Enterprise-email studies combine logs, interviews, and deferral classifiers to explain unread marking, flagging, workload, and sender importance. **HomeGuard** extracts domestic-violence victim situations in Bangladesh and supports help provision using NGO case studies.

610bd6180e48b0014e4ce2ad6d40d563415074b0.text:
## Community Report: Disambiguation, Networks, Disasters, and Digital Intelligence

This community connects methods for resolving entities, analyzing networks, aggregating cultural metadata, and supporting crisis response.

**Author name disambiguation** addresses homonyms, name variation, imbalanced training data, and ambiguous name blocks. Automated systems use linkage functions, coauthor names, coreferring-author classifiers, ethnicity-sensitive features, and agglomerative clustering. Triangulation on labeled datasets evaluates pairwise precision, recall, and F1.

**Graph and clustering research** includes YASCA, a seed-centric method for local community identification and global graph partitioning. Ensemble clustering combines network partitions and supports dynamic clustering. Spectral methods use a hypergraph generalization of the non-backtracking Hashimoto matrix, with comparisons to Bayesian belief propagation and planted generative models; localized eigenvectors can undermine standard spectral partitioning. Hub networks study authorities, isolated eigenvalues, and localized eigenvectors.

**Digital Public Library of America** aggregates cultural-heritage metadata through an ingestion system, remediation, enhancement, aggregation infrastructure, and partner networks.

**Crisis and social analysis** covers natural-disaster emergency response, including Hurricane Odile and economic recovery time relative to baseline activity. Temporal correlations connect fire hotspots with tweet activity. Investigative simulation extends dual simulation with categorical labels, partial-match pruning, and top-k ranking. Collective-emotion extraction from online text examines periodic cycles, long-term memory, and tension. Other applications include email-deferral classification, domestic-violence extraction, and entity-centric organization of tweets.

566f4e062cd79df0730475384c5d872eb354f2ff.text:
## Community Report: Search, IoT, Security, and Political Information

This community links information retrieval, user behavior, and diversity-oriented search. Target app selection identifies which mobile apps should receive a query, using crowdsourced search queries, user behavior, retrieval models, and high-dimensional app representations. A unified mobile search framework, motivated by Apple Siri and Google Assistant, integrates this task; neural models outperform retrieval baselines. Term mouse fixations and fixation time infer topical user interests from viewed documents, titles, keywords, and search sessions collected in a domain-specific digital library.

Diversity maximization addresses filter bubbles and is formulated as a quadratic knapsack problem. Greedy heuristics followed by randomized local search improve solution quality and efficiency, while polynomial non-approximable algorithms are also associated with the formulation.

Internet of Things search engines (IoTSEs) are classified into eight functional groups through a structured study of a corpus containing over 200 works. IoT research emphasizes public perception, challenges, cybersecurity, and security issues affecting IoT devices. An AI-based threat intelligence system uses open-source information to help security analysts address poisoning attacks.

Finally, social media supports information dissemination, political communication, and rapid mapping after natural disasters through a WebGIS interface. Invocation graphs and embedded graphs model ideological domain interactions, including asymmetric linkage patterns, across the political spectrum before the US presidential election.

9b72663dbaaaa648e70d9ff4e38751126860672a.text:
### Dynamic Topic Modeling, Social Media, and Scholarly Change

This community centers on topic modeling for unstructured documents, tweets, course material, forum posts, biomedical abstracts, and scientific literature. Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) is a core method: it represents documents or items through topic proportions, discovers latent topics, and supports topic coherence evaluation. Extensions include labeled LDA, hierarchical Dirichlet process LDA, embedded topic models, DocNADE, ET-LDA, and CLDA.

A major theme is temporal and dynamic analysis. CLDA decomposes large corpora into local time segments and uses parallel execution; it was applied to NIPS papers, computer-science abstracts, and PubMed data. Dynamic topic modeling and related continuous-time models track changing topic structures. Topic modeling also supports event segmentation, topic comparison, and analysis of literary themes and cultural-scale collections.

Tweets provide a central social-media application. Twitter’s Firehose and Streaming API supply data for sentiment analysis, topic discovery, event causality detection, and real-time search or prediction. Tweet churn, bursting hashtags, and hashtag lifecycles motivate prediction of burst occurrence, timing, duration, and fading.

The community also addresses scholarly communication and preservation. Citation profiles are categorized by peak and monotonic patterns; dynamic growth models reproduce these profiles, whereas preferential attachment models do not. Public web archives preserve linked resources but reattach only about 12% of orphaned annotations, while archived resources may disappear.

d4118ccc01674adc6006f802084c94fc4261ae2e.text:
## Social Graph Retrieval, Network Resilience, and Query Processing

This community centers on using social graphs for recommendation, retrieval, consumer choice, cultural-interest propagation, and peer-to-peer routing. Data sparsity is a recurring challenge: collaborative retrieval uses social information, weak connections, factor models, semi-supervised learning, hierarchical Bayesian models, and multiple learned random variables. Latent Collaborative Retrieval models query-aware recommendation with a factorized model optimized by BPR; related systems include social collaborative retrieval, ILCR, and TSI-WR, which combines topic information, weak connections, and a factor-graph framework.

Friendship prediction exploits overlapping users and composite social networks, while neighbor-distribution prediction uses evolution factor models, neighbor-distribution vectors, and label-evolution matrices. Q&A hashtags such as #lazyweb and #twoogle are studied through hashtag-log analysis and helpful-tweeter communities.

A second major theme is resilience. Cascading failures, targeted and random attacks, failure propagation, network takeover, and self-healing are examined in cyber-physical, cyber, and physical networks. Factor graphs and message passing support fixed-point and healing analyses.

Query and data-management methods include ADiT for distributed top-k queries, group-based path processing, shortest/path queries, multi-objective sampling, multidimensional histograms, and projection graphs for P2P overlays and betweenness analysis. Mobility studies connect path-cost estimation with travel time and trajectory or mobile-phone datasets.

1a1ffca8a651d8e0eae2ba531ab1fb73092261e9.text:
### Community Report: Networks, Prediction, and Retrieval

This community spans graph analysis, temporal dynamics, recommendation, and information retrieval.

For Wikipedia, revision networks represent editor activity sequences and induced editor triads. Motif analysis and motif subgraph ratio profiles compare articles and characterize controversial versus non-controversial articles. Wikipedia mathematician networks, extracted from 2013, 2017, and 2018 snapshots, support centrality analysis, with comparisons to MacTutor and Imperial College London survey results.

UrbanRhythm extracts urban dynamics from human mobility data, using staying, leaving, and arriving attributes, the Saak transform, mobility distribution features, and motif analysis. Urban dynamics include city states, short-term regularity, and long-term periodicity. Coarse-grained state detection combines graph distance and hierarchical clustering to infer school, weekday/weekend, and functional-connectivity states.

Non-backtracking spectral methods provide graph comparison metrics and embeddings, including comparisons involving biological networks and Watts–Strogatz graphs. Brazilian court decision prediction uses a working prototype evaluated on 4,043 Brazilian court cases to predict case outcomes and decision unanimity, despite legal-system complexity and high litigation rates.

Recommendation systems include a social explorative attention network that attends to higher-order friends, supports personalization, and seeks recommendation equality, measured by the Gini coefficient. Featured-snippet studies examine Polish Google results, Wikipedia, paragraph presentation, ranking position, and retrieval methodology; Google Assistant and Home Assistant can read such snippets aloud.

0f128681dad2b618227998ab895c7399ecd7f20a.text:
## Neural Ranking and Retrieval Research

This community centers on information retrieval, document ranking, learning to rank, ad hoc retrieval, and complex answer retrieval. Traditional approaches include BM25, handcrafted IR features, and local relevance matching; BM25 serves as an unsupervised baseline and weak-supervision signal, while neural methods can outperform it according to MAP.

Neural ranking models use deep learning, neural term embeddings, word embeddings, language representations, and query-document similarity vectors. They support pointwise and pairwise ranking, require large-scale training data, and learn from raw text. Weak supervision synthesizes training data and can pre-train supervised neural ranking models.

Key systems include Match-Tensor, which models local relevance matching and global topicality and is evaluated on social media documents; Word-Entity Duet and Attr-Duet, which use knowledge-graph information, cross-space word/entity interactions, and attention to reduce noisy entities; and SemAuto, which uses autoencoding and semantic features from knowledge graphs.

End-to-end architectures combine lexical and temporal signals, using bidirectional LSTMs and kernel density estimation for social media stream search. Contextualized dictionaries support document retrieval using manually compiled reference documents and key-term extraction.

Evaluation and datasets include TREC, TREC Web Track, TREC Complex Answer Retrieval, ClueWeb, Robust, training data, and social media documents. A related strand examines data retrieval, observational research data, user behavior, and cross-disciplinary analytical frameworks.

4185c22387b6b83291a6ceefafb4969c6f428894.text:
## Dynamic Topics, Real-Time Social Data, and Resource Preservation

This community links topic modeling, temporal analysis, Twitter search, citation dynamics, and web archiving.

Topic modeling methods include LDA, static finite models, CLDA, ET-LDA, continuous-time dynamic topic models, and online hierarchical Dirichlet processes. CLDA partitions large corpora into local time segments, applies LDA in parallel, and was evaluated on NIPS papers, computer-science abstracts, and PubMed. ET-LDA combines topic modeling with event segmentation through a joint Bayesian model. Peacock provides distributed, hierarchical LDA learning with topic de-duplication for industrial-scale applications; topic coherence supports model evaluation.

Twitter-focused work studies changing term distributions, tweet and query churn, real-time search, public sentiment, and event-related discussion. The Twitter Firehose and Streaming API supply data, while real-time Twitter search relies on in-memory indexes. Dynamic postings allocation addresses the “Goldilocks” trade-off between query speed and memory utilization. Bursting-hashtag research predicts occurrence, timing, duration, and fading.

Other strands model scientific citation profiles: dynamic growth models reproduce observed profiles, while preferential attachment models fail to explain them. Studies of shared resources measure archival coverage and loss: about 20% are archived after one year and 41% after two and a half years, while losses reach 11% and 27%, respectively. Public archives reattach about 12% of orphaned annotations.

88df551822a343a4beb366790b853cc97ce49400.text:
## Reproducible Research and Robust Neural Evaluation

This community centers on reproducibility, data availability, and computational preservation in research. Reproducibility is supported by open-source software, available raw experimental data, and explicit computational context; changes in the computational environment can otherwise affect results. Raw data—such as that produced and used in experimental fracture mechanics—may be difficult to retrieve through an institutional email address or corresponding author. Publication data requirements and long-term data availability address this problem, while Dataverse and Zenodo can deposit data and provide DOIs, making raw data citable. ORCID and ResearcherID provide corresponding authors with persistent identifiers independent of institutional email.

For neural models, evaluation includes comparison with neural baselines, incorporation of low-resource and noisy collections, and assessment using an evaluation metric. Multi-seed evaluation varies random seeds across model initialization and data sampling. Hyperparameter evaluation tests nearby configurations within an epsilon-distance neighborhood. Both methods are proposed to improve reproducibility; hyperparameter evaluation varies hyperparameters.

The encapsulator preserves computational context in a time capsule and provides a self-contained environment, approximating an executable paper. This environment enables end users to validate findings and conduct new research, linking preserved computational conditions with practical reuse.

a8f0e19f7da0d0f43252bb624901b860e8a82d6b.text:
## Causal Analysis of Badges and Web Activity

This community centers on causal inference for user behavior and cybersecurity monitoring using web data. A causal inference framework estimates the effects of first-time badges on a popular Q&A website, including whether badges change behavior according to users’ action utility. It incorporates survival-based hypothesis testing to control for utility heterogeneity and bootstrap difference-in-differences estimation to account for random behavioral fluctuations over time. Digital badges, including badges awarded after a first action, aim to encourage desirable user actions; user sessions represent trajectories and intent and group web traffic from the same location and date.

The framework supports causal analysis of observational data when controlled experiments—the gold standard—are infeasible. It relies on the strong ignorability assumption, requiring treatment and outcome to be conditionally independent given observed covariates. Observational data may consist of multiple base relations joined into a study population; conditional independences in those relations help infer independences in the joined relation, with graphical models representing this structure.

Google Analytics collects and aggregates web traffic and archives it for web activity monitoring and cybersecurity forensics. Web traffic supports rule-based anomaly detection and predictive modeling for cybersecurity monitoring, including understanding threats from malicious cyber actors.

46f932a42d3b89598f095c8fdb27c69ef1ca72a6.text:
## Community Report: Interactive Retrieval, Vision, and Data-Driven Analysis

This community connects information retrieval, computer vision, and interactive user-centered systems. Content-based image retrieval uses color and dominant color descriptors, color quantization, Earth Mover’s Distance, and optimal color composition distance; linear-time approximate Earth Mover’s Distance supports efficient large-scale retrieval. Flood image datasets evaluate retrieval alongside flooded-area determination, inundation-depth estimation, water-pollution assessment, and distractor images.

Interactive retrieval emphasizes user feedback, human-in-the-loop retrieval, gradient interleaving, and ranking refinement. Seeker adapts results in real time and is evaluated through human-in-the-loop experiments. Query and interest modeling uses term mouse fixations, fixation time, viewed documents, document titles, and keywords to infer topical user interests.

Real-time search addresses changing query and tweet distributions, query churn, in-memory indexes, and the Seeker system. Dynamic postings allocation manages memory and query-speed trade-offs, including the “Goldilocks problem.” Approximate IC and OD filters evaluate spatial predicates.

Computer-vision research spans object detection and tracking, neuromorphic vision, scattering transforms, and converted MNIST and Caltech101 datasets. Finally, linguistic analysis and crowdsourced data support automatic toxic-behavior detection in League of Legends, including transitions from typical to toxic players, tribunals, and player warnings.

db8794fdc471f93bc3dcd9127401ad1e21220819.text:
## Knowledge Graphs for Scholarly Processing, Question Answering, and Recommendation

This community centers on knowledge graphs as infrastructure for machine-actionable scholarly communication. The Open Research Knowledge Graph uses crowdsourcing and multimodal knowledge acquisition to collect machine-readable research contribution descriptions, while knowledge graph infrastructure supports scholarly knowledge acquisition, processing, storage, and access. SchenQL and SQL query bibliographic metadata; mixed collection calculus, nested relational calculus, query normalization, rewrite rules, and the conservativity theorem address queries under set, bag, and mixed semantics.

A second theme is question answering. Convex handles incomplete conversational questions by using conversation context and question completion, and is evaluated on ConvQuestions. Quest answers complex questions directly from textual sources by constructing a noisy quasi-knowledge graph, adding semantic alignments, applying similarity joins, and using Group Steiner Trees. Knowledge-graph question answering is also limited by incompleteness and staleness.

Recommendation methods use knowledge-graph connectivity, semantic features, and reasoning paths. RippleNet, KGCN, GraphSW, PGPR, and MoHINRec support personalized or explainable recommendation. GraphSW applies stage-wise training and is evaluated on Last.FM, LFM-1b, Amazon-book, and Yelp datasets; MoHINRec uses motif-enhanced meta-path similarities. Comprehensive Personalized Ranking uses a Bayesian treatment and CPR optimization criterion. Link formation studies relate personalized and global degree, with personalized out-degree stronger than in-degree in directed networks.

c7ddf246f127ccd035ce0b15dc49a53aa38bd346.text:
## Social Network Alignment and Opinion Dynamics

This community links scalable social network alignment with mathematical models of opinion evolution.

**SHNA** addresses heterogeneous social network alignment, a combinatorial optimization problem challenged by an extremely large search space and network heterogeneity. Its two-stage model uses synergistic graph partitioning and intra-/inter-network meta diagrams to partition networks into sub-networks, prune unmatched pairs, and shrink the search space. Anchor links then establish correspondences between matched sub-networks. SHNA is evaluated on the *real world aligned social networks* dataset.

**DNA** aligns dynamic social networks using deep neural architectures. It models local user dynamics, including friending evolvement, while preserving global consistency with neighboring representations. DNA produces dual embeddings, extracts identity embeddings, maps them into a common subspace across networks, and uses an alternating algorithm for optimization.

The community also models **opinion dynamics**: correlated subjects, endogenous individual opinion evolution, and repulsive interactions—potentially caused by adversarial attitudes—are formulated through a mean-field multidimensional Fokker–Planck equation. This equation characterizes population-level evolution, derives steady-state opinion distributions dependent on personality and social interactions, and provides stability conditions. Dynamic social networks represent evolving social interactions, while social communities influence collective belief dynamics.

155a4c2254205012db1c4551ddc3aeaa42ff4820.text:
## Community Report: Formula Conversion, Legal Retrieval, and Fraud De-anonymization

This community spans mathematical information retrieval, legal information retrieval, and online search-rank fraud.

In mathematical information retrieval, the **mathematical format conversion benchmark** evaluates conversion of mathematical formulae between representation formats using task-specific **conversion evaluation metrics** and an extensively curated **gold standard**. The gold standard links formula components to **Wikidata**, is generated from online legal repositories, and can train **formula concept discovery** methods. **Context-aware formula conversion** incorporates textual context, while semantic enrichment and contextual information aim to reduce conversion errors. Formulae are also used in computer algebra systems.

For legal information retrieval, **deep learning**, document vector embeddings, and semantic similarity measures support retrieval in the legal domain. **Vector space representation** generates document representations through two mechanisms; an **ensemble model** combines them, representing legal case documents in different vector spaces.

The fraud-related systems address search-rank fraud posted through online systems and crowdsourcing sites. The **Upwork search rank fraud dataset** contains collected examples. **Dolos** performs fraud de-anonymization, identifying suspicious reviewer groups and fraud apps on Google Play. It uses **MCDense** to uncover fraudster-controlled account communities, stylometry to attribute groups to crowdsourcing-site profiles, and deep learning for fraudster attribution—targeting the human masterminds behind the fraud.

3a1fa464970b681166f7d5d80db92df624fdb41f.text:
## Learned Databases, Querying, and Game Analytics

This community centers on data-driven methods for databases, query processing, and applied analytics. Cardinality estimation supports query optimization: deep learning and containment-based cardinality estimation reduce estimation error relative to PostgreSQL, provide estimates to the PostgreSQL optimizer, and improve query plans. Containment rates measure overlap between SQL-query results; CRN represents query pairs and can estimate these rates. DeepDB proposes data-driven learned DBMS functionality, while workload-driven approaches train machine-learning models from representative query observations. Data-driven models learn directly from data, support query answering, and generalize better to unseen queries.

DeePSpace is an engine for approximate geospatial query processing over geospatial data, supporting bounded-precision results, flexible aggregation queries, and small required query state. A temporal data model uses K-relations and snapshot semantics, evaluating queries at each snapshot, and is implemented as database middleware competitive with native implementations.

Other systems query financial tables and PDF tables using SQL-like querying, table-type classification, nearest-row search, and text matching. Neural ranking models use curriculum learning, whose pacing functions move from easy to difficult instances and improve retrieval effectiveness by up to 2 percent.

Game analytics includes a competition using NCSOFT’s Blade & Soul logs for churn prediction and churn-timing prediction, where highly ranked participants used deep learning, tree boosting, and linear regression.

985223c1f539ea1a70ab2b52bef4746af1b82055.text:
## Context-Aware Recommendation and Inclusive Credit

This community connects context-aware recommendation with data-driven credit and lending applications.

In the television domain, **joint context content embeddings** is a deep learning-based method proposed for context-aware recommendation. It maps content and contextual settings into a **shared latent space**, learning joint latent representations of viewing situations and content. Built on **deep metric learning**, it uses **n-pairs loss** (including a relaxed variant) as a training objective and is evaluated on television recommendation datasets. More broadly, deep learning supports representation learning and models question–text interactions.

A separate strand addresses credit scoring and financial inclusion. **Feature engineering** constructs features from user data and can improve credit-scoring performance. User data can also be used to construct **pseudo-social networks** for identifying similar people; these are analyzed through complex network analysis combined with representation learning. **Smartphone-based microlending** uses credit scoring and is proposed as a means to enhance financial inclusion and potentially financial wellbeing. Credit-scoring methods, including those using call-detail records, are constrained by ethical and privacy regulations to avoid unfair discrimination.

302f4fc12df3d8f271b7411b6605af8d519cc71e.text:
## Failure-Aware Approximate Querying and Video Analytics

This community connects distributed, statistical, and approximate query processing with video-monitoring workloads. Distributed query processing shards data across nodes and supports interactive analytics, but stragglers, resource contention, and node failures can slow or disrupt execution.

**Failure-aware approximate query answering** addresses failed and straggling nodes, producing approximate answers with confidence bounds. It supports aggregate queries involving joins, grouping, `HAVING` clauses, some nested subqueries, and spatial constraints. The method exploits co-hash partitioning properties and is experimentally evaluated on the TPC-H dataset.

Approximate filters accelerate video monitoring queries over video streams by avoiding costly object-detection operations. They evaluate predicates involving spatial relationships and include OD filters, which adapt principles from object detection, and IC filters. Video streams support declarative queries, while deep learning enables advances in frame classification and object detection.

Overall, the community relates approximate filtering and statistical query processing to efficient aggregate and interactive analytics, particularly when distributed systems face failures, stragglers, or resource contention.

b40b51aa064c63367be492b01208150757a4825a.text:
## Social Networks, Group Dynamics, and Personalized Prediction

This community centers on **social network analysis**, including retweet, mention, Facebook friendship, email, student, co-membership, mobility, and learning networks. These networks support analysis of communication, relationships, isolated students, knowledge propagation, delinquent behavior, academic performance, and electric-vehicle adoption.

A major theme is **group formation and evolution**. Group evolution discovery and social group evolution identify evolution events, stable groups, and changes using **GED**, **SGCI**, and an integrated group-evolution method combining network analysis with text mining. These approaches are evaluated for flexibility, ease of implementation, and user importance, using datasets such as email-based networks and the Polish blogosphere. Group formation also supports group recommendations, optimizing satisfaction through least-misery algorithms and aggregate-voting heuristics.

The community includes systems for network dynamics and experimentation: **NDlib** provides diffusion simulation, a simulation server, and online visualization. **Meetup** and group-meeting data support studies of changing group composition and community perception.

Personalization methods include **TARS/TBP** for periodic and recurring purchase behavior, ordinal Boltzmann machines for co-occurrence and ordinal preferences, and a deep forgetful novelty-seeking model for next-action prediction using movie genres, forgetfulness, and novelty propensity.

f039badb0fb8d9bb914bb98b2569f9e4c983cb28.text:
## Community Report: Neural Ranking, Research Metadata, and Trade Recommendation

This community centers on deep learning, neural networks, and recommendation systems. Neural ranking models apply neural networks to relevance estimation, learn from raw text, and reduce reliance on hand-crafted features. They are evaluated on benchmark tasks alongside non-neural linear ranking, heuristic, graph-based, nearest-neighbor, Markov-chain, and factorization methods. Deep learning can surpass Markov-chain and factorization approaches, although heuristic methods may outperform some deep-learning recommenders.

Recommendation systems use exporting-countries data from the international trade network to identify products that countries could produce or export. Country fitness supports simulations of changes in export diversification, with potential benefits for national competitiveness, especially in developing countries. LorentzFM performs recommendation and click-through-rate prediction, learns feature interactions, and reduces parameter counts by 20–80%. DeepFM, xDeepFM, and Deep Cross provide comparison methods for recommendation and CTR prediction.

A second theme is metadata classification by research discipline. This is formulated as multi-label classification, using neural networks, multilayer perceptrons, tree-based models, and research-data metadata compiled into training and evaluation sets. It supports scientometric research and analysis of interdisciplinarity. An LSTM performs dynamic supervised link prediction using temporal citation counts, temporal keyword importance, and genealogical relations; keyword communities are constructed from those relations. Reported F1-macro scores are 0.755 for LSTM and 0.760 for multilayer perceptron.

4ce2077d10d43c1b30b4e20d18a9a1d699d26892.text:
## Query Semantics, Cardinality Estimation, and Social-System Security

This community connects database theory, query optimization, and social tagging-system analysis.

For query optimization, MSCN is a deep-learning method for cardinality estimation. It represents relational query plans, uses set semantics and true cardinalities, captures join-crossing correlations, and is evaluated on a real-world dataset. Cardinality estimation supports query optimization, alongside deep reinforcement learning, which learns query-state representations. A state transition function combines the current state with a query operation, while subqueries represent query states.

A second theme concerns positive relational algebra over order-incomplete databases. Partially ordered relations support possible- and certain-answer problems, which are respectively NP-complete and coNP-complete. Query evaluation studies aggregates and duplicate elimination, including its complexity under bag semantics. The U-semiring extends SQL semiring semantics, supports unbounded summation, set/bag semantics, duplicate elimination, integrity constraints, and SQL query-equivalence reasoning. It enables formal verification, including verification of query-rewrite rules, and can be implemented in Coq.

The security and social-media strand studies profile-injection attacks against social tagging and tag-based recommender systems, including overload and piggyback attacks. Support vector machines and naïve Bayes filters are evaluated as countermeasures, while deep learning is evaluated using synthetic spam data generated from del.icio.us. eWOM classification and causal analysis link Twitter topics, dessert mentions, access concerns, and sales using sales data and LiNGAM.

1fc3590b76de13e811082ae9749d2f8ea477b002.text:
## Networks, Bias, Lyrics, and Infrastructure

This community links social network analysis, student networks, media, and road-network vulnerability.

**Social networks and education:** Social network analysis examines retweet and mention networks, including interactions among world leaders, and uses centrality to identify prominent leaders. In student social networks, it studies group formation, friendships, academic performance, knowledge propagation, isolated students, and delinquent behaviors. Expanding students’ networks is associated with holistic development, while network findings can inform inclusive learning and educational methods.

**Bias and media:** Movie social networks are built by fusing IMDb movie data with movie dialogue subtitles and supported by an open code framework. Social network methods and data science investigate gender bias in on-screen roles. Gender and racial bias are also studied in song lyrics using WEAT and distributed representation methods.

**Lyrics analysis:** Song lyrics analysis covers more than half a million songs across five decades. Lyrics style is characterized by length, repetitiveness, speed, vocabulary, and readability.

**Road networks:** Discrete Ricci curvature analyzes road networks through network intrinsic geometry and measures vulnerability, identifying key road sections and fragile elements while tracking vulnerability evolution over time. It is compared with centrality and complex network statistics, whereas node-based methods focus on connections and contribute to the node paradox.

912f4f0d7fcecccf4ab60c1c1b15ac04dd0329bf.text:
## Graph Query Processing, Matching, and Incremental Graph Analytics

This community centers on efficient **query processing** over graph and property-graph data. It covers graph query languages and systems including **Gremlin**, the Gremlin Graph Traversal Machine, Apache AsterixDB, and generalized graph query systems. Gremlin serves as both a traversal machine and language, supporting OLTP graph databases, OLAP graph processors, and property-graph traversal.

A major topic is **graph pattern matching**: graph queries map to relational join computations, while graph simulation and triple simulation reduce matching complexity. Structural constraints and capacity bounds support applications such as top-k team formation. Graph database views store precalculated matches and improve query performance.

The community also emphasizes **incremental query processing** and **incremental view maintenance**. Linview, IncNRC+, delta-query derivation, generalized discrimination networks, and incremental graph pattern matching maintain materialized or graph views under updates, avoiding costly full re-evaluation. Matrix factorizations can make maintenance cheaper.

Performance concerns include indexing, join-order selection, query-optimization heuristics, LSM trees, tuple compaction, parallelism, and search-space expansion. Shrinkwrap improves over oblivious query processing, while Pique acts during processing and improves answer quality. Data enrichment, ingestion, graph-stream summarization, and closed-world semantics further affect whether graph data can be queried effectively.

495ab8e220bb1174658ea83a1d4effcc8e79c7b8.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Data, Queries, and Recommendation Systems

This community centers on differential privacy and privacy preservation for sensitive databases, data publishing, statistical studies, and query answering. Differential privacy uses random noise and privacy mechanisms, with epsilon, privacy budgets, and privacy loss controlling privacy guarantees and utility. Approximate and dynamic differential privacy address relaxed definitions and temporally correlated location data; location perturbation, private spatial decompositions, and the planar isotropic mechanism support spatial privacy.

Key methods include hierarchical decomposition, constrained inference, sensitivity hulls, the low-rank, recursive, Shapley value, bivariate Laplacian, and small-count mechanisms. Systems such as the privacy engine, DPClean, PrivTree, PrivBasis, PrivThr, and PrivThrem operationalize private querying, workflow tuning, spatial processing, or mining. Applications include frequent itemset and graph-pattern mining, subgraph counting, count queries, and non-interactive data publication.

The community also addresses efficient and accurate data access. BlinkDB, dynamic sample selection, top-k retrieval, and approximation target response time, while stale-view cleaning improves aggregate query accuracy and maintenance efficiency for materialized views.

Recommendation algorithms, including model-based and trust-aware approaches, use content, semantic tags, and co-authorship; privacy protection can reduce utility. Diversification systems and OptSelect connect recommendation quality with response-time efficiency. Graph anonymization, node differential privacy, and edge perturbation protect network structure and social links.

6176396c779ebb64180cab25edcd961fb5eb4a5f.text:
## Scalable Network Embedding, Compression, and Transaction Analysis

This community centers on efficient network embedding for network mining, similarity search, classification, and temporal link prediction. Embedding maps nodes into continuous vector spaces: DeepWalk and node2vec use random walks, while Trans2vec incorporates transaction amounts and extracts address features for one-class SVM phishing detection on Ethereum transaction networks. T-edge models temporal weighted multidigraphs using time-dependent walks and edge multiplicity, outperforming baseline embeddings.

Scalability is addressed through compression and compact representations. NECL compresses graphs before embedding and improves DeepWalk and node2vec embedding time by 23–57% without reducing classification accuracy. NetSMF uses sparse matrix factorization and spectral sparsification as a scalable alternative to dense matrix factorization, with bounded spectral approximation error and high embedding efficiency and effectiveness. MCNE-T reduces memory cost, while BinaryNE learns sparse binary node codes with a three-layer neural network, modeling context and attribute relations through online stochastic-gradient learning. Multi-hot compact embeddings also reduce memory cost using shared basis vectors, enabling fast bit-wise similarity search.

IDEALEM provides lossy compression based on statistical similarity, spectral reconstruction analysis, stationarity modes, and min/max checks for significant patterns. Hybrid screening combines machine and crowd classifiers to reduce screening cost while balancing accuracy, evaluated on datasets including Cora, Wiki, DBLP, and transaction data.

95483fccc04b3e9c7dd075fa6c0b1374146e13a2.text:
## Temporal, High-Order, and Social Network Analysis

This community centers on analyzing evolving and high-order networks, especially temporal networks with timestamped links, temporal motifs, event graphs, temporal strong components, and dynamic community structures. Event graphs provide second-order time-unfolded representations that expose higher-order temporal structure and properties missed by static or time-aggregated models; related methods include temporal binning, timeline segmentation, traveling semirings, and temporal network structure tracking.

High-order networks generalize pairwise relationships through weighted hypergraphs and simplicial-complex filtrations. Network distance metrics and persistent homology—producing barcodes—compare such structures, distinguish weighted pairwise networks, and analyze dynamical systems and engineering coauthorship networks.

A second theme is document and repository organization. Nonnegative matrix factorization, max-correntropy NMF, supervised topic modeling, semantic similarity, vector-based models, RI-k trees, Louvain detection, and topic overlay/science overlay mapping support document clustering, topic identification, and repository clustering. Git, DataHub, and World of Code support dataset version control, shared-commit analysis, and collaboration over data.

The community also studies diffusion and prediction: minimum-weight dynamos under irreversible majority rules, epidemic source detection and containment, threshold contagion, SIS epidemics, and predictive analysis of social dynamics. Applications include face-to-face and sexual-interaction networks, WhatsApp conversations, Behance and digital art, legislative texts, online news, exchange rates, and web visualization sites.

93947914506072cbedf4872df0d6e25a194ea5b0.text:
### Privacy, Utility, and Efficient Data Systems

This community centers on differential privacy and privacy-preserving data analysis. Differential privacy protects sensitive databases, data publishing, statistical query processing, recommendation algorithms, and frequent graph pattern mining by bounding privacy loss, typically through noise addition. Key mechanisms include the Laplacian, bivariate Laplacian, planar isotropic, low-rank, recursive, small-count, and sensitivity-hull approaches; approximate and dynamic differential privacy extend the framework to relaxed guarantees and temporally correlated location data.

Spatial privacy is addressed through private spatial decompositions using quadtrees, kd-trees, and privately selected splitting points. PrivTree applies hierarchical decomposition to histogram construction over spatial and sequence data, avoiding a predefined splitting-depth threshold while improving utility. Location perturbation and differential privacy support location privacy protection.

Graph privacy includes node and edge differential privacy, graph anonymization, and private mining of mobile-phone-call and web-click graphs. Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling and neighboring-pattern counting support private frequent graph pattern mining.

The community also studies the privacy–utility–accuracy tradeoff, including query accuracy, data distortion, sensitivity, and privacy budgets. Separate systems improve data access efficiency: stale view cleaning estimates aggregate queries more accurately and efficiently than full view maintenance, while BlinkDB and dynamic sample selection target response-time requirements. Diversification methods such as OptSelect and xQuAD address efficient top-k retrieval.

e9c215b10891b24980c3d9fdc93d245b6f818964.text:
## Network Optimization, Influence, and Opinion Dynamics

This community studies optimization and dynamics on social, road, and multilayer networks. **Influence maximization** supports viral marketing by selecting budget-constrained seed nodes, but is NP-hard. Conventional greedy algorithms use marginal gains and achieve a \(1-1/e\) approximation; SSA and IMM provide approximately \(1-1/e-\epsilon\) guarantees, while hop-based algorithms offer theoretical guarantees, efficiency, and evaluation on real OSN datasets. Monte Carlo simulation is accurate but slow and unscalable, motivating sampling reduction in TIPTOP and estimation-and-refinement methods that accelerate oracle calls. Cost-aware target viral marketing is approximately solved by TIPTOP, which uses integer programming.

**Node discoverability optimization** creates budgeted incoming edges. Greedy and dynamic-programming methods provide near-optimal or exact baselines, while estimation and refinement scales better. **Diversified coherent core search** finds \(k\) d-coherent cores in multilayer graphs, maximizing covered vertices through greedy and search algorithms.

For trajectory-aware facility location, **TOPS** places service sites on road networks under cost and capacity constraints. **NetClus** uses multi-resolution clustering, supports dynamic mobility updates, and is evaluated on urban trajectory datasets.

Finally, **opinion dynamics** uses Markov chains, stochastic multi-agent models, peer assembly, and birth-death chains to model collective and polar opinions, with relevance to viral marketing and political strategy design.

0364bb6ed5776e6c1102866ecd54074913374363.text:
## Information Retrieval, Ranking Robustness, and Equilibrium

This community spans document, text, Web, snippet, and item-recommendation retrieval, with emphasis on effectiveness, robustness, and strategic behavior. Deep learning architectures operate solely over query and candidate text and support document and snippet retrieval. They demonstrated retrieval effectiveness, including top or near-top performance achieved by AUEB systems submitted to BioASQ 6, Task 6b Phase A.

Ranking robustness concerns the stability of rankings under adversarial document manipulation. Document authors use such manipulation to compete for higher rankings in Web retrieval, potentially reducing robustness and producing unwarranted effects on retrieval effectiveness. Ranking robustness is analyzed through ranking-function variance and empirically evaluated for RankSVM and LambdaMART. The community conjectures that lower ranking-function variance increases robustness. For linear ranking functions, regularization is applied and greater regularization increases robustness.

Document retrieval and query reformulation are studied jointly. Query reformulation produces refined queries with respect to document relevance estimation and acts as one player in a two-player strategic game; relevance estimation is the retrieval modeler’s objective. A normal-form representation is used to derive equilibrium theory, reached when both players are best responses. Equilibrium algorithms improve performance in text retrieval and item recommendation.

fc75ad67f32dbb0ea3ea50416506c67d2dd21e9c.text:
## Graph and Stream Processing: Scale, Sampling, and Guarantees

This community combines network analysis, temporal sampling, graph community detection, and distributed processing.

For **network scale selection**, networks are projected into metric spaces, where metric trees support efficient search. Spectral clustering identifies informative scales and learns parameters for the **Joint SBM**, outperforming greedy and gradient-descent alternatives. Higher-scale representations reduce entropy rate and degeneracy, increase global network efficiency, and improve determinism relative to microscale representations. Joint SBM models heterogeneous, non-aligned graphs, exploiting cross-graph information to estimate shared communities and outperform separate SBMs.

For evolving data streams, **temporally biased sampling** adapts supervised-model training using decay functions and unequal-probability sampling while retaining some older data beyond sliding windows. T-TBS is a simple scheme; reservoir-based R-TBS supports unknown, time-varying arrival rates and stabilizes sample size. These methods enable periodic retraining and online model management, with Spark-based distributed evaluation.

The distributed systems work includes **SP Join**, a MapReduce/Spark framework for metric-space similarity joins. Its cost model guides data partitioning and quality-guided splitting mitigates skew.

Finally, formal **delivery guarantees** connect exactly-once processing with consistency and determinism. Lightweight determinism enables exactly-once delivery with minimal overhead, unlike conventional techniques and industrial solutions that incur significant overhead.

3ccdc891c15bc79efb5e81501f2cec46bed8912f.text:
## Recommender Systems, Graph Projections, and Knowledge Discovery

This community connects research-paper recommendation, graph-based modeling, and literature knowledge discovery. A recommender system builds user models from mind maps and recommends research papers; Docear integrates it into mind-mapping and reference-management software. Its mind-map-based modeling is compared with models based on users’ downloaded or cited articles, using offline evaluation and a user study. Online evaluation uses 430,893 displayed recommendations and 4,700 users, measuring click-through rate; the approach achieves 7.20%, nearly twice the best baseline.

User–item relationships can be represented as bipartite graphs, whose one-mode projections produce projected networks. Unweighted and weighted projections are studied through connectedness, topological properties, cliques, and maximum edge weight. These properties support influencing-node selection for viral marketing in online social networks. Actor–movie relationships provide another bipartite-graph example through an online movie database.

Astronomy literature is processed with computational linguistics and text-based similarity search to find related articles. An astronomy similarity search tool recommends papers similar to an input paper and is compared with recommender systems.

Mandolin supports knowledge discovery on RDF datasets through rule mining, grounding, inference, referenced-graph imports, and similarity relationships among literals, with results comparable to statistical relational learning algorithms.

21f2bbf047d3c1e25700075e8bba2eb0c71d7c7c.text:
## Knowledge Graphs, Question Answering, and Web Archives

This community centers on knowledge bases and information access. Knowledge bases contain triples, inference rules, and set-valued predicates; they support entity retrieval, named entity linking, relationship explanation, dialogue, recommendation, and question answering. Completeness and correctness are important evaluation concerns, while negative statements address limitations of traditional positive-only knowledge bases.

Question answering takes natural-language questions and connects to knowledge bases, conversational search, and table search. Systems and frameworks include QA4IE, QnAMaker, and Dr Tux. Information extraction is supported by ontologies, ontology enrichment, authority files, Markov Logic Networks, and technical data sheets, with IE Benchmark providing evaluation.

A second major theme is temporal web access. Web archives preserve Web history and archived resources but have temporal and presentation complexities. Tempas supports archive search, while sub-collection extraction, federated search, and temporal search enable focused investigation. Mementos, manifests, and fixity blocks support archive dissemination and verification.

SPARQL endpoints provide access to Linked Open Data and historical events data. SPARQL federation frameworks, federated querying, and query optimization coordinate multiple endpoints; SPARQL 1.1 Update defines update behavior.
