The historical events dataset additionally offers a Linked Data interface, DBpedia links, and a timeline application.

86d9d51c0a639e66e6da1087447e160ec5842e7f.text:
## Social Networks, Diffusion, and Structural Analysis

This community centers on **social networks** as structures of actors, friendship links, communities, and temporal or multiplex connections. Major topics include **information spread**, **social contagion**, peer influence, social cohesion, structural diversity, network segregation, assortativity, and mixing patterns. Models include threshold, susceptible–infected–recovered, DeGroot–Friedkin, co-contagion, composite compartmental, and information-diffusion models, addressing adoption, opinions, health sentiment, and information cascades.

A second focus is influence and resource optimization: **viral marketing**, seeding and scheduling of seeds, competitive influence maximization, maximum coverage, optimal budget allocation, and protection resource allocation. Convex optimization, linear programming, heuristics, polynomial-time algorithms, and evolutionary frameworks support these tasks.

Structural methods include clique, truss, \(k\)-shell decomposition, community identification, overlapping communities, centrality maximization, graph signal processing, Gromov hyperbolicity, and metric tree likeness. Inference and privacy topics cover latent social-network and diffusion-network inference, topology inference, cross-network identity resolution, profile matching, secure multiparty computation, and \(k\)-structural-diversity anonymization.

Named systems and datasets include **TrendNets, TIPAS, HyperMap, Finding Nemo, HRLHG, LDBC SNB, Wi‑Fi access logs, cascade data,** and **synthetic population datasets**.

6faaef000b3473a520ce287ffe340b38f7f6824d.text:
## Community Report: Uncertainty, RDF Streams, and Social-Network Behavior

This community connects three themes: uncertainty-aware complex event recognition, Semantic Web/RDF stream processing, and online social-network behavior and trust.

Complex event recognition handles incomplete or erroneous data streams and imperfect event patterns. Automata, probabilistic graphical models, probabilistic models, and first-order logic are used under uncertainty, while Petri nets and grammars are less frequently used. Uncertainty-aware techniques generally have lower performance than deterministic approaches.

In the Semantic Web, RDF is the default data model for Linked Data, and RDF graphs support Semantic Web applications. RDF stream processing extends evaluation from static graphs to dynamic streams and supports real-time Internet-of-Things data. C-SPARQL is an RDF Stream Processing engine, while PRSP is a plugin-based framework using SPARQL and distributed SPARQL engines. PRSP is evaluated with YABench for performance and correctness and maintains high performance.

eLinda explores Linked Data and RDF graphs through exploration paths, including class, property, subclass, and object distributions, visualized with bar charts; URI nodes can be expanded.

Online social networks—including LinkedIn, WeChat, and MySpace—are studied for trust, access limitations, and behavioral dynamics. Three-valued subjective logic, grounded in the Dirichlet categorical distribution, computes trust in arbitrary graphs and is implemented by AssessTrust. It is validated on Advogato and Pretty Good Privacy datasets. WeChat users’ release behavior follows power-law and anti-memory patterns.

785e84f880c1e3eeed52cbe325ca44eaf16dd6c0.text:
### Similarity, Hashing, and Multimodal Graph Retrieval

This community focuses on efficient similarity search, representation learning, and retrieval across high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and multimodal data. Similarity search supports time-series mining, image annotation, pattern matching, and knowledge-network analysis; systems such as DISA and algorithms including Forward Backward Similarity and R-PathSim address efficient search. Query relaxation, result diversification, relevance measures, and representation independence improve retrieval robustness and usefulness.

A major theme is compact binary representation. Unsupervised learning, semantic representation learning, vector quantization, and binarization produce binary codes that enable Hamming-space nearest-neighbor search and fast XOR comparison. Self-Taught Hashing, semantic hashing, Deep Cross Modal Hashing, Composite Correlation Quantization, composite quantizers, and modality-specific hash networks target scalable or cross-modal retrieval while addressing quantization error and hashing-bit correlation.

Cross-modal retrieval connects audio, visual, image, and other modalities through joint audio-visual embeddings, cross-modal feature learning, and probability-based indexing, with recall@k evaluating performance. Deep neural networks support these embeddings, ranking, short-text matching, recommendation, and conversation-mode learning, while Torch provides a deep-learning system.

Graph-oriented work models similarity in heterogeneous networks using typed graphlets and structural/content information. The community also includes unsupervised data-stream clustering for evolving streams and noisy-data learning.

a8e5d1b0853d62391f2ef7a1b94e3c2e619e886d.text:
## Big Data Quality, Ingestion, Similarity, and Inclusive Credit Scoring

This community covers Big Data quality, scalable ingestion, similarity sketching, community detection, ranking, and alternative-data credit scoring.

Research on **data quality** examines how quality affects knowledge extracted from Big Data. A **hierarchical framework** organizes quality dimensions, while assessment methods consider **batch, stream, and hybrid processing**; a systematic literature review surveys methods adopted by the Big Data community.

The **ingestion framework**, built on **Apache AsterixDB**, supports data ingestion at scale, adaptive responses to changing reference data, and enrichment for complex analytical queries. Enrichment may use reference data and machine-learning operations, although it cannot always be completed during ingestion preprocessing. Performance is evaluated under varied workloads.

**Binsketch** performs dimensionality reduction for high-dimensional sparse data and estimates Jaccard, cosine, inner-product, and Hamming similarities, with mean squared error evaluation. It is also assessed for ranking performance. Production ranking systems use machine-learning models and require real-time response.

**Inclusive community detection** incorporates low-degree users into larger communities, reducing community-assignment bias and outperforming existing approaches on Jaccard similarity.

Finally, call-detail records construct call networks for social network analytics. Propagated influence scores and calling-behavior features support credit scoring alongside credit/debit account information. Models are evaluated by profit measures, with profit-based feature selection, and the approach has implications for financial inclusion.

6181f8e6316049abb50f2432140159ecb3095ed0.text:
## Community Report: Hashing for Multimodal Retrieval and Related Learning Systems

The community centers on efficient retrieval across heterogeneous modalities, especially cross-modal, multimodal, and image retrieval. Cross-modal hashing represents images, text, and other multimedia data with compact binary or unified hash codes, enabling fast search in Hamming space, reduced storage cost, and nearest-neighbor retrieval. Methods include deep cross-modal hashing, deep discrete supervised hashing, discrete latent factor model-based hashing, joint cluster cross-modal hashing (JCCH), DCHUC, UCH, semi-supervised multimodal hashing, fusion supervised deep cross-modal hashing, asymmetric correlation quantization hashing, composite correlation quantization, and multi-head asymmetric hashing.

Deep methods use feature learning, deep convolutional neural networks, multimodal convolutional recurrent networks, triplet loss, unary loss, quantization loss, semantic consistency, and label information. Discrete optimization, relaxation-based continuous methods, dimensionality reduction, and query-adaptive bit weighting or hash-code ranking address learning and search efficiency. Image retrieval is evaluated with mAP; related systems use hash tables, probability-based indexing, top-k retrieval, and instance-search pipelines.

Other represented topics include feature extraction and text classification, music classification/tagging using datasets such as Music Tagging Dataset and Serial Speakers, and optimal control of neural dynamics on complex networks using Pontryagin’s maximum principle and forward-backward sweeps.

4fb4c01773caac85c5c63ae2a7956662d32948a9.text:
# Entity Resolution, Data Privacy, and Value Attribution

This community spans three themes: scalable entity resolution, privacy-preserving data processing, and cooperative-game-based contribution analysis.

Entity resolution identifies descriptions of the same real-world entity across databases, knowledge bases, and the Web of Data, improving data quality and analytics. MinoanER uses token-based entity similarity and composite blocking to address Web entity descriptions’ variety, volume, and veracity, performing especially well on high-variety knowledge bases. Entity indexing and massively parallel matching support Big Data settings.

A second theme concerns social-network data collection and analysis. Anonymization, fuzzification, and a probabilistic privacy-preservation model protect sensitive information and limit data reconstruction, while consent and GDPR-compliant processing address regulatory requirements.

The third theme uses Shapley and Myerson values to quantify tuple or user contributions. Shapley-based coalition games support query answering, including conjunctive and aggregate queries, fair compensation, and movie-rating analysis. Factorized representations and factorized databases rewrite query-answer computations as linear programs, expressible in Math GNU Prog or AMPL. Myerson values extend contribution analysis to graph-restricted games over communication networks; exact computation requires connected coalitions, while permutation or connected-coalition Monte Carlo sampling and hybrid algorithms provide approximations. Additional work covers column-type prediction in Web tables using lexical matching or deep models exploiting contextual, table-locality, and inter-column semantics.

e15aa1898c1cd78a8fee3b418dbd56364210fa15.text:
## Similarity, Retrieval, and Mining Across Complex Data

This community centers on similarity search, graph analytics, and multimodal retrieval. Similarity search supports image annotation, pattern matching, similarity query processing, and knowledge-network analysis. It uses query relaxation and result diversification to balance recall and result quality; GenGreedy, GenCluster, and CB2S diversify relaxed candidates. Forward Backward Similarity and R PathSim provide efficient or representation-robust search, while HeteSim measures relatedness among heterogeneous objects through path-constrained, semi-metric relationships. Locally biased graph algorithms discover local structure in large data graphs under locality constraints, supported by algorithmic and statistical theory.

A major thread is hashing for efficient retrieval. Cross-modal hashing and deep cross-modal hashing retrieve across text and image modalities, with deep methods integrating feature learning and end-to-end learning. Composite Correlation Quantization preserves intra-modal similarity and inter-modal correlation through learned mappings and composite quantizers. Self-Taught Hashing uses unsupervised learning, Binarized Laplacian Eigenmaps, and linear SVMs to produce binary codes.

Other topics include data-stream mining and clustering for continuously arriving, evolving data; long-term preservation of temporal data; political-bias prediction from media reports, speeches, and manifestos; and community-endorsement prediction from online discussion response structures.

7231a6fb2f6d41882dec09b9c794d60f07b70e8d.text:
## Community Report: Meta-Learning, Trust, and Information Retrieval

This community centers on recommender systems, bibliographic parsing, and clinical information retrieval.

**Recommendation systems:** Meta learning supports recommendation algorithm selection, including micro-, mid-, and global-level meta learners. The meta-learning recommender system selects algorithms for individual user–item pairs and is evaluated on MovieLens 100K/1M using RMSE, F1, and click-through rate; it underperforms a single-best SVD++ model on RMSE. Recommender systems also support literature recommendation, including patient-specific clinical literature recommendation, and report recommendation accuracy and a 7.20% click-through rate. Trust-based collaborative filtering uses trust networks, explicit trust scores, implicit trust relationships, similarity matrices, and regular equivalence; it improves recommendation accuracy and is evaluated on Epinions.

**Cross-domain and sparse-data methods:** D2D-TM addresses multi-domain recommendation and cross-selling using user interaction histories, homogeneous/divergent features, and latent features learned through a VAE-GAN-CC network with cycle-consistency weight sharing. Multi-domain recommendation and trust-based filtering address cold-start problems, while probabilistic tag–keyword mapping, dimensionality reduction, and user-tag prediction address sparse location-preference data.

**Parsing and retrieval:** ParsRec uses meta-learning for parser selection in bibliographic reference parsing, evaluated on 105,000 chemistry references. It outperforms GROBID on F1 and reduces false-positive and false-negative rates. Clinical decision support combines neural representation learning, distant supervision from MIMIC-III, and retrieval models, improving clinical information retrieval effectiveness.

923bd8a220830e841f57ce282fc1131615271bb7.text:
## NLP, Search Behavior, and Political/Emergency Analysis

This community connects natural language processing (NLP), question answering, search interaction modeling, and analysis of political and emergency communications.

**Dr Tux** is a Python-implemented question-answering system for Ubuntu users. It uses AskUbuntu questions, NLTK, and CoreNLP, selecting the most similar question through question-similarity matching and assessed by manual evaluation. Question-answering models additionally use BM25 and word overlap features.

The **GUBM** models grid-based user browsing behavior using interaction features from search engine result pages and commercial image-search logs. It is trained through unsupervised learning and evaluated with behavior-prediction perplexity. Image search induces behavior distinct from general Web search, complicating standard click models. Interaction behavior provides implicit relevance feedback and is also studied using laboratory user-study data.

NLP analyzes the Facebook Ads dataset, released by the U.S. House Intelligence Committee, identifying textual and semantic features related to ad effectiveness. Ads were clustered into political campaigns associated with labeled parties; campaign patterns suggested an intent to sow political division. The ads were allegedly purchased by the Russian government and linked to suspected foreign influence in the 2016 U.S. presidential election. Less-positive sentiment was associated with more effective ads.

**Savitr** performs unsupervised location extraction from microblog text, including sparsely geo-tagged content, displays results on a map-based interface, and achieves an F-score of 0.79 for emergency monitoring.

b7e6af7ebc6ee2ec71a31872090e90b6878bb208.text:
### Classification, Summarization, and Graph-Based Knowledge Extraction

This community links evaluation-driven classification, feature engineering, summarization, crowdsourcing, music information retrieval, and graph extraction.

Text-classification work uses feature extraction, selection, term weighting, term clustering, dimensionality reduction, and contextual factor selection. Word- and character-level features support multiclass text classification, abuse detection, follower-loss detection, and automated document classification. Reported measures include classification accuracy, classification performance, response latency, and cost–accuracy trade-offs. Hybrid screening algorithms, catch22, and hctsa select compact feature sets, while rumor systems combine time-series and credibility features; one rumor classification model exceeds 90% accuracy.

Summarization methods include LexRank, Grasshopper, LSA, MMR, support-sets-based centrality, relative-entropy minimization, and generic summarization. They produce representative, concise, and diverse summaries of music datasets and support music summarization within music information retrieval, including evaluation with a Fado genre classifier.

Crowdsourcing addresses binary microtasks and answer aggregation. Expert cores, weighted majority voting, reject options, and quantized confidence reporting are used to improve classification while modeling worker reliability.

Gextext extracts latent relationships from unstructured literature through correlation thresholding, learning disease networks from Wikipedia, PubMed, and stroke corpora, and inferring Diseasome graphs. Community detection includes spectral modularity maximization, global detection, and locally biased approaches.

f86bd7dda104cd5bd56a91b522d9cc004e2d05bc.text:
## Information Retrieval, Recommendation, and Bibliometric Search

This community centers on information retrieval, including text matching, clustering, recommendation, academic search, and text-based question answering. Deep neural networks and natural language processing support relevance prediction and question-answering models; Word2Vec, Sentence2Vec, and Paragraph2Vec are evaluated as deep-learning approaches for relevance prediction, which produces relevance scores. BM25 provides a comparison point, while Indri is an indexing framework used by the information-retrieval community.

MatchPyramid formulates recommendation as text matching, representing users and items through review texts and predicting ratings. Its MatchPyramid recommender system is evaluated on the Amazon Review Dataset, including AZ-CSJ and AZ-MOV, and achieves relative improvements over DeepCoNN and TransNets; DeepCoNN is itself extended by TransNets. User reviews may help alleviate the cold-start problem.

Bibliometrics enhances information retrieval and academic search through bibliometric information. The Bibliometric Enhanced Information Retrieval workshop series addresses academic-search issues and is held at ECIR and in conjunction with JCDL and SIGIR.

Other applications include product-search relevance prediction in e-commerce and business-process management. Clustering groups cases by process-flow characteristics, followed by influence analysis that identifies correlated business areas; business areas also affect process-execution details.

6e8ce7f07c7ed548970424c3400d086448d111e3.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Query Processing and Spatial Analytics

This community centers on differential privacy for statistical databases, query answering, and data release. It addresses aggregate, count, predicate, linear, and range queries, balancing privacy loss with data utility, query accuracy, response time, and information loss.

Key methods include random noise, Laplace/Laplacian and bivariate Laplacian mechanisms, the matrix mechanism, HDMM, hierarchical decomposition, private spatial decompositions, PrivTree, PrivThr, sensitivity hulls, constrained inference, and workload-adaptive mechanisms. Differential privacy is also applied to temporal correlations, continuous data release, location privacy, spatial data structures, and anonymized or non-interactive publication. Local differential privacy supports range queries in untrusted aggregation settings.

The community studies query workloads as matrices whose spectral properties characterize difficulty, with QWLSh supporting efficient workload processing. Ektelo provides a framework for differentially private computation, while DPClean applies privacy during workflow tuning. Other systems and methods address spatial and multidimensional analytics, including single-node multidimensional stores, spatial data warehouses, R-trees, SAR trees, and approximate algorithms.

Applications include decision support, business intelligence, online analytical processing, mobile sensing, smartphone and trajectory data, and social-media privacy. Related work covers provenance for aggregate queries, prediction models, privacy-preserving publishing, and inferential privacy, including individual attribute inference and auxiliary information.

3d0813504856143d0335163f40ab9d692d17e81f.text:
## Unbiased Ranking, Bandit Feedback, and Bias-Aware Systems

This community centers on reducing bias in recommender and search systems, especially position and examination bias arising from implicit user feedback. Unbiased learning to rank (ULTR) encompasses counterfactual and online learning-to-rank approaches. Counterfactual learning uses historical interactions, explicit user models, inverse propensity score (IPS) weighting, and theoretical guarantees; position-based models estimate examination bias, while contextual position-based models condition it on query- and user-related context. Instrumental-variable methods and randomization provide alternative ways to estimate or remove bias.

Online learning-to-rank learns from implicit feedback without an explicit user model. Document Space Gradient Projection improves gradient estimation by projecting updates onto the examined-document feature space, reducing variance and improving ranking performance for linear ranking models.

The community also covers learning from bandit feedback. Counterfactual risk minimization and off-policy estimators support policy performance estimation, while RecoGym, built on OpenAI Gym, simulates recommender environments for comparing bandit algorithms. Recommender-system logs enable reward prediction, argmax recommendation selection, exploration, and error adjustment, although adjustment can violate conditionality and likelihood principles.

Applications include dream-job recommendation, search engines, and ArXiv intervention harvesting. Broader themes address biased data collection, professional gender bias, privacy in Cambridge Analytica tweets, and webpage change-notification systems.

e6e46f19d6122485173ce595d651d6e964d5e847.text:
## Recommendation and Multimodal Search Methods

This community covers Top-N and cross-domain recommendation, multimodal representation learning, and large-scale multi-view visual search.

For recommendation, CIGAR performs candidate generation, preference-preserving binary embedding, and real-valued re-ranking, reducing query time by orders of magnitude and improving Top-N accuracy. Correlative denoising autoencoders learn robust representations from sparse user ratings using shared parameters and regularization; they support Top-N recommendation and are evaluated with MAP. DDTCDR addresses cross-domain recommendation through dual learning, latent orthogonal mapping that preserves user relations, and autoencoder-based feature extraction. It is evaluated on a three-domain movie, book, and music dataset and outperforms classical transfer learning. Multimodal IRIS combines multimodal feature learning, an Interest-Related Network, item-similarity recommendation, and knowledge sharing across modalities, improving interpretability. Autoencoders also pretrain node embeddings, reducing parameters in graph convolution layers.

For visual search, query-adaptive hash-code ranking builds multiple hash tables for joint multi-view search, exploiting complementary view information. Query-adaptive bitwise weighting uses hash-function quality and complementarity to reduce quantization loss, while query-specific rank fusion combines hash-table results through graph diffusion. Hamming distance supports hash-based nearest-neighbor ranking. ViTOR uses transfer learning from a pretrained image-classification model and synthetic saliency heat maps generated from webpage snapshots; the ViTOR dataset includes ClueWeb12 webpages, TREC Web Track queries, and relevance judgments.

4cfa13bd07d6de0fdbbd72cc3da4c5501525112d.text:
## Scalable Distributed Data and Graph Processing

This community centers on scalable distributed computing, with MapReduce as a major organizing method. Hadoop provides an implementation platform, while Spark, Hive, Pig, and distributed data-management systems support big-data processing. MapReduce enables wavelet-histogram construction, kNN and multiway joins, fuzzy joins, web-corpus analysis, graph processing, and large-scale crawling, but incurs mapper-to-reducer communication costs. Join algorithms, generalized hypertree decompositions, parallel query plans, operator reordering, and learned cost models target more efficient query execution.

Graph analytics is another major theme. Wedge sampling approximates clustering coefficients, triangle counts, triadic measures, and budgeted top-k maximum inner-product search, offering practical time–accuracy tradeoffs. External-memory graph generation uses shuffle, relabel, redistribute, MPI, and CSR conversion to create large graphs on small clusters. Systems such as AGL, Deltagraph, historical graph stores, temporal graph indexes, and distributed spatial indexes address scalable graph, spatial, and temporal workloads.

The community also covers adaptive and persistent indexing, including database cracking, stochastic cracking, Bloofi, and NV-tree approaches. Scalability is evaluated through communication cost, replication rate, overhead, and query-processing behavior. Finally, blockchain systems such as ResilientDB and methods including cross-blockchain transactions and Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus connect distributed data processing with transaction integrity and untrusted infrastructure.

a5937367c94cfba03829bad134babbe5b83f7679.text:
## Community Report: Data, Web, Graph, and Recommendation Systems

This community links data cleaning, web data management, graph analysis, semantic search, and recommendation.

Data cleaning includes error detection, data repairing, semantic type detection, matching, and similarity joins. It may be performed offline or integrated with exploratory analysis, with frameworks such as **MLClean** supporting unified cleaning. Similarity and join-size estimation support data-cleaning applications, query handling, and query-plan generation, including d-ary and similarity self-joins.

Web systems address crawling, extraction, and archive processing. Web crawlers collect application data, crawling statistics, and accessibility or vulnerability information. **ArchiveSpark** enables distributed web-archive processing, metadata-indexed queries, research-corpus construction, and derivation of smaller datasets. Semantic mapping improves hidden-data extraction and explains disagreements through query provenance.

Semantic query expansion enriches searches using place partonomies, concept expansion, and embedding-based document similarity, evaluated with DCG@K. Scholarly venue recommendation models reading behavior and dynamic user interests, while neural and personalized recommender systems use behavioral signals.

Graph methods include the generalized stochastic block model for discovering overlapping groups and bridge vertices, and geometric distance oracles that approximate shortest-path distances using hyperbolic structure and spanning trees. Precomputed summaries and tree-contraction methods introduce approximation error. Further topics include migration analysis, synthetic clickstreams, and web accessibility.

7e300b7b71d92ea2e3090e39066275c704bde62c.text:
### RDF, SPARQL, and the Semantic Web Graph Ecosystem

This community centers on RDF graph data, ontologies, and Semantic Web infrastructure. RDF is a W3C-standard graph data model and the default model for Linked Data and Linked Open Data deployments. It supports data integration across heterogeneous sources, open-data publishing, bibliographic data, scientific metadata, nanopublications, and micropublications.

SPARQL is the principal graph query language for RDF and is executed through SPARQL endpoints. Research addresses SPARQL query formulation and processing, basic graph patterns, optional and negation operators, updates, query workloads, and real-world query corpora. SPARQL-to-SQL and relational-query translation connect RDF querying with database systems, while systems such as PhD Store and Gremlinator support query execution or translation. RDF graph search, graph joins, source selection, dynamic record clustering, and query execution plans target performance; execution time, memory consumption, and performance improvement are key metrics.

Ontologies provide the semantic framework for publishing, sharing, reusing, and integrating data. OWL and RDFS support ontology-based representation and reasoning, although strict SPARQL does not account for their semantics. Shape Expressions (ShEx), RDF constraints, and SHACL-related approaches describe graph structure. Provenance, metadata, semantic annotations, interlinking, and dataset quality further support reliable Linked Data and knowledge organization.

3af9635015be7495ad740668f7a6ffe6c7f85084.text:
## RDF, SPARQL, and Linked Data for Semantic Web Integration

This community centers on RDF, RDF graphs, ontologies, and the Semantic Web as foundations for representing, integrating, and publishing heterogeneous data. RDF is the W3C graph-structured data model underlying Linked Data and Linked Open Data, including datasets such as DBpedia, bibliographic data, metadata, and scientific results represented as nanopublications or micropublications.

SPARQL is the principal graph query language for RDF. Research addresses SPARQL query processing, endpoint execution, SPARQL-to-SQL and relational query translation, source selection, view-based query rewriting, optionality, negation, correlation, substitution, and distributed Linked Data querying. RDF graph search, query execution plans, RDF stream processing, and systems such as PhD Store, Fedra, CPSPARQL, PSPARQL, and OptBitMat extend or optimize this ecosystem. Gremlin and Cypher represent related graph-query approaches.

Ontologies, OWL/OWL 2, RDFS, SKOS, and ontology-based data access provide semantics, reasoning, interoperability, and structured representation. Shape Expressions (ShEx) and RDF constraints support validation and schema description.

The community also emphasizes provenance and quality: Luzzu, provenance-aware nanopublications, semantic annotations, research objects, data-quality metrics, and quality assessment support trustworthy data integration and scholarly communication. Dataset interlinking, author disambiguation, semantic search, and Linked Data deployment connect these methods to practical Web and research applications.

d34781b6c4c6ce6a5ca8453155069f84247ee97f.text:
## Wikipedia, Temporal Behavior, and Knowledge Quality

This community centers on Wikipedia and related knowledge repositories, including Wikidata, Stack Overflow, question-and-answer websites, search engines, and recommendation engines. A large-scale user survey, matched with server-log activity, develops a taxonomy of Wikipedia use cases organized by reader motivations, desired knowledge depth, and prior topic knowledge. These findings support improvements to Wikipedia’s user experience and content recommendation.

Temporal point-process modeling links user behavior in digital traces to source trustworthiness and information reliability, despite noisy user evaluations. Convex optimization learns parameters from historical evaluations, while interdependent multidimensional temporal point processes—fit with variational EM—model continuous user participation, content effects, peer influence, badges, and gamification. They improve user-behavior prediction and predict evaluation events, using Wikipedia and Stack Overflow data.

A related semantic-annotation approach combines text-based methods with temporal correlation from Wikipedia edit histories and page-view logs, especially during trending-topic burst periods. Applied to trending Twitter topics and mapped to Wikipedia entities, it improves annotation performance by 17–28%.

The community also addresses vandalism. Machine classifiers use contextual edit features and editor characteristics to detect vandalism in Wikipedia and Wikidata, achieving an 89% catch rate and reducing patroller workload by 98%. Wikidata’s structured-knowledge-base setting requires feature engineering distinct from text-based wikis.

8663029761be9c5fd02446dec2b1608068925697.text:
## Retrieval, Question Answering, and Query Evaluation

This community connects information retrieval, medical question answering, document querying, and approximate pattern matching.

For retrieval, Deep Contextualized Term Weighting (DeepCT) maps BERT contextual representations to context-aware term weights, addressing weaknesses of term frequency. DeepCT indexes and weighted queries support first-stage passage retrieval through ordinary inverted indexes; deep neural ranking models are generally reserved for later stages because of computational cost. Passage re-ranking, passage-length constraints, and large passages are central to non-factoid question answering.

QRefine uses a character-enriched Seq2Seq model to transform ill-formed questions into well-formed ones, improving answer retrieval. Pentagon participates in the MediQA question answering shared task, using task-specific pretrained models, language inference, and question entailment to filter and re-rank medical answers. It reports a mean reciprocal rank of 0.9622 and Spearman’s rho of 0.338.

A second line studies regex formulas and regular document spanners over text documents. Relational algebra supports joins, differences, and black-box extractors; positive relational algebra can be evaluated with polynomial delay, while difference and schemaless natural joins can be intractable. Automaton compilation enables constrained evaluation.

Finally, COBS combines inverted-index and Bloom-filter characteristics in a compact bit-sliced signature index for k-mers and q-grams, supporting approximate pattern matching over 100,000 microbial DNA samples and outperforming Mantis.

5982c70bca1d508f4d5f60a041e997191d82a1c3.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Queries and Scalable Spatial Search

This community connects differential privacy, data publishing, query answering, and utility preservation. Differential privacy protects databases, sensitive attributes, and users by controlling privacy loss through noise addition, including Laplace, matrix, bivariate Laplacian, and planar isotropic mechanisms. It supports statistical, count, aggregate, correlated, continuous-release, and spatial queries, as well as non-interactive data publication. Systems and methods include Ektelo, HDMM, DPClean, PrivTree, PrivThr, PrivThrem, private spatial decompositions, constrained inference, and sensitivity hulls.

Utility and accuracy are assessed through data utility, query accuracy, query response time, partition quality, privacy loss, and regret ratio. Workload-aware approaches include workload embeddings, query workloads, workload-adaptive mechanisms, and the matrix mechanism. Range queries use local differential privacy, differentially private counting, hierarchical histograms, and Haar wavelets, including spatial-region counting.

A second major theme is nearest-neighbor retrieval and graph construction. KD-trees, R-trees, Vor-trees, spatial indexes, graph hierarchies, and multilayer Voronoi diagrams accelerate nearest-neighbor and k-nearest-neighbor search. Related tasks include approximate and online k-nearest-neighbor graph construction, k-NN graph merging, geographic information retrieval, interactive spatial queries, and geo-social group queries. The community also covers data warehouses, materialized views, query optimization, utility mining, anonymization, and privacy leakage.

9b5aef920dd60584cc9f95aab62a9fd9513f929c.text:
## Graph Mining, Privacy, and Personal Knowledge Extraction

This community covers graph structure discovery, privacy-preserving mining, and knowledge extraction from notifications.

**Local community detection** uses conductance objectives, generative network models, and local approximation of unobserved network structure. Stochastic block models provide a probabilistic basis, with approximations applied to two variants; methods are evaluated on real datasets and compared with state-of-the-art algorithms.

**Hierarchical graph clustering** uses agglomerative clustering and node-pair sampling. Sampling induces a cluster distance with the reducibility property, enabling nearest-neighbor-chain acceleration. The resulting dendrogram reveals multi-scale graph structure and is evaluated on real datasets.

**Subgraph discovery** includes pattern and clique discovery. **Nuri** is a general system that uses prioritized subgraph expansion and pruning to find the *k* most relevant subgraphs under user criteria. It is benchmarked for pattern mining and subgraph isomorphism and outperforms a distributed alternative for clique discovery.

**Utility mining** supports market basket, click-stream, medical, and bioinformatics analysis. Privacy-preserving utility mining combines utility maximization with privacy-preserving data mining to protect sensitive private information.

Finally, a personal knowledge extraction system processes approximately 120 million smartphone push notifications. Notification templates and template semantics support query translation and extraction of knowledge facts, which populate a personal knowledge base while privacy preservation is supported by uploading only non-personal templates.

2b40b1e2070aafe05f0665fb146c78cc4597497f.text:
## Community Report: Personalized Retrieval, Recommendation, and Representation Learning

This community centers on retrieval and recommendation systems, especially e-commerce sponsored search, multi-behavior personalization, and query understanding. Personalized ad retrieval frameworks combine ad matching, cost-sensitive weighting, hierarchical signal–key–ad modeling, and multi-stage architectures. Taobao deploys behavior sequence transformers, SDM, and personalized attractive selling-point prediction; SDM fuses short-term sessions with long-term behaviors through gated fusion. NMTR and MCNE model multiple user behaviors using multi-task learning, conditional representations, binary masking, and Bayesian Personalized Ranking.

Neural methods also support search and generation. Neural machine translation performs search-query translation and generates retrieval keywords, while generative retrieval addresses vocabulary and corpus issues. Workload embeddings represent SQL text or optimized query plans for query recommendation, summarization, index selection, expensive-query identification, and query-reuse prediction.

Code retrieval, summarization, and generation are jointly addressed in end-to-end and multi-task architectures, evaluated with BLEU. Pentagon applies task-specific pretrained models, language inference, and question entailment to filter and rerank medical answers in the MediQA shared task, achieving MRR 0.9622 and Spearman’s rho 0.338.

Evaluation spans MRR, CTR, AUC-ROC, BLEU, Kendall’s tau, Spearman’s rho, bounce rate, and commercial metrics. Recipe retrieval, trivia extraction, mathematical-symbol representations, and citation-network analysis form additional application areas.

2aa5859e22078cd613120ec7f9f3ee06c470dd37.text:
## Big Data Integration, Querying, and Learning

This community centers on managing and analyzing large, heterogeneous data across relational, semi-structured, array, graph, NoSQL, and polystore environments. Big data challenges traditional RDBMSs through storage, computation, scalability, and costly aggregate queries, motivating specialized storage engines, array processing, big-data models, and systems such as SciDB, D4M, Accumulo, MongoDB, and TigerGraph.

Querying is a major theme. SQL remains a core declarative language, extended through recursion, windowed aggregates, semantic layers, and SPARQL-to-SQL translation. Datalog and Datalog+ support bottom-up evaluation, optimization, explanation, migration, and reasoning with existential rules; VadaLog, PUG, FactorBase, and related systems apply these ideas. Query answering includes conjunctive queries, ontology-mediated queries, probabilistic data, sum queries, and weakly sticky Datalog+, with description logics and termination analyses addressing decidability and tractability.

Polystore systems such as BigDAWG provide unified access to diverse databases through middleware and “islands.” Data integration also involves schema mapping, evolution, provenance, citation, data quality, and migration.

The community further connects relational learning and classification—including incremental and multitask learning—with graph datasets and applications such as recommendation, fraud detection, and dropout prediction. Semantic and natural-language interfaces include DBPAL and SQL query synthesis.

5e8fc0669ea21f3fbaec23fe198eb29f744167e4.text:
## Neural Search, Recommendation, and Health-Text Mining

This community covers neural methods for search, recommendation, and biomedical text analysis.

**AHNQS** performs query suggestion using an attention mechanism, combining session-level and user-level neural networks to model short- and long-term search histories. Evaluated on the AOL query log, it outperforms RNN-based baselines, improving MRR@10 by up to 21.86% and Recall@10 by up to 22.99%.

**Action conditional sequence modeling** extends recurrent neural networks for next-item prediction through recommendation-action and state-action fusion modules, with evaluation on real-world large-scale datasets. Encoder–decoder and sequence-to-sequence models support fashion ensemble completion, predicting complementary fashion items; the Apriori algorithm is a competitive baseline, and top-1 accuracy is used for evaluation.

**PHRecSys** is a content-based article recommendation system that enriches article representations with phrase-level features, improving click and view prediction. Attention mechanisms also improve ranking and model interpretability by focusing on meaningful text spans.

For biomedical text, recurrent and attention-based models address ADR mention extraction and adverse drug event detection. Multi-task learning uses the latter as an auxiliary task, improving F1 by 7.2%; adaptive boosting LSTMs with attention form an ensemble neural network, while feedback-based active learning improves F1 and AUC using oversampling.

**Maester** performs relatedness detection for agreement-aware search, using investigative questions and agreement levels, keyword-entity matching, and gradient boosting trees.

bee7d9ae52a27bba83a741e05bade3952ab96098.text:
## Graph Analytics, Approximation, and Data-Driven Systems

This community connects graph mining, approximate computation, recommendation, and data management. Densest subgraph discovery is a fundamental graph-mining task, with exact and approximation algorithms supporting graph-, clique-, and pattern-based density definitions. Approximate computation includes query and data approximation: random sampling and sample-based joins use uniform samples to reduce output size, while approximation is applied to graph pattern matching, trajectory compression, dense-subgraph computation, shortest-path distances, and network anomaly detection. These methods support more efficient big-data analytics.

Graph modeling uses graph grammars, including vertex replacement grammars and KT grammars. KT grammars encode frequent substructures, are extracted using the Minimum Description Length heuristic, and are evaluated on real-world and synthetic datasets. Gremlin provides a common graph-computing platform spanning OLTP graph databases and OLAP graph processors; its integrated graph algebra consolidates graph algebra operators and supports graph pattern matching.

The community also covers learning-based systems. Learned indexes use learned models as alternatives to traditional index structures and are compared with B-trees and baseline implementations. NMTR applies multi-task learning to multi-behavior recommendation, modeling cascading behaviors and sparse users. Hybrid neural networks address heterogeneous structures and item ranking. UIC formulates utility-driven adoption as social welfare maximization, approximated by a greedy allocation algorithm implemented in BundleGRD. Answer aggregation combines crowd responses through majority voting or expert-core methods based on worker reliability.

be0e18520d497b0da6e9d8a1812c619b9c37c084.text:
## Methods and Systems for Social, Scholarly, and Historical Data

This community links machine learning, data management, crowdsourcing, and digital humanities. Supervised learning and classifiers support rumour judgement, crowdsourced decision prediction, migrant churn, group evolution, censorship, spammer, and toxic-behavior detection. Multi-task learning improves tweet-level rumour classification, including rumours from the 2011 England riots, while social, temporal, spatial, linguistic, and behavioral features provide inputs. Collective judgement estimation is evaluated on tweets about seven rumours and relates community belief to ground truth.

OCR research uses diplomatic transcriptions and historical documents as ground truth. Mixed OCR models achieve character accuracy above 90%; semi-automatic improvement uses a small number of corrected lines, while confidence and lexicality metrics correlate with true accuracy. Ocropus and individual or mixed OCR models support this work.

LaBurst detects bursts and key moments in social streams, including sports events and earthquakes. Toxic-player studies connect behavioral transitions, reports, tribunals, and automatic detection.

PIQL provides privacy-aware query languages, bounded key/value operations, scale independence, and SLO-compliance prediction. AsterixDB offers scalable NoSQL data management, partitioned LSM storage, feeds, and transactions.

Other themes include open knowledge bases, crowdsourced geospatial data, information spaces, knowledge maps, academic data sharing, reputation economies, science maps, and linking open data.

6094f8b64ce9080f2fc8f68ae66342b33c081ec8.text:
## Online Optimization, Personalized Advertising, and Language Systems

This community connects online decision-making, personalized sponsored search, and language technologies.

**Contextual multi-armed bandits** support online optimization and online learning for tailored web experiences. They use engineered context and bandit-arm features, while addressing decision constraints, optimization-health monitoring, productization challenges, and theoretical regret bounds. Offline evaluation is also applied to bandit systems.

**Personalized attractive selling-point prediction** predicts product selling-point keywords for individual users using surrogate explicit feedback. Framed as a sponsored-search problem, it enables ad-title manipulation and improves revenue per thousand impressions by 2%, with a merchant opt-out rate below 4%. Multi-task learning improves this prediction, using a relevance-based auxiliary task as regularization.

**Neural machine translation (NMT)** performs search-query translation for cross-lingual information retrieval. It is trained on sentence-level parallel data and evaluated on an Italian-English query-document dataset, where the multi-task approach achieves a 16% improvement over a strong NMT baseline. The NMT model is described as unaware of retrieval-corpus vocabulary distribution.

**DBPal** implements a natural-language interface to databases using NMT. It outperforms existing rule-based NLIDBs and achieves comparable performance to deep-neural-network NLIDBs. Feature engineering also supports wide-deep learning and data-management tasks.

91ddad29e6a352056d43a7e3806f89c606d52586.text:
## Community Report: Social Judgement, OCR, and Scalable Knowledge Systems

This community connects machine learning, crowdsourcing, document digitization, and data-management systems.

**Social and collective judgement** are studied through supervised learning, classifiers, and domain adaptation. Rumour research uses tweets—including the 2011 England riots and seven-rumour datasets—to predict individual judgements and estimate community belief, with collective judgements correlated against ground truth. Related work models crowdsourced decisions, group evolution in evolving social networks, and spammer detection; a two-mode labelled hidden Markov model outperforms supervised learning for the latter.

**Toxicity and online behaviour** are examined through linguistic analysis of League of Legends crowdsourced cases. The Tribunal evaluates reports, while automatic toxic-behaviour detection and player-warning tasks model transitions from typical to toxic players.

**OCR improvement** uses diplomatic transcriptions as ground truth. Mixed OCR models, mixed models, and semi- or fully automatic improvement achieve character accuracy above 90%; confidence and lexicality metrics correlate with true accuracy.

**Scalable information infrastructure** includes AsterixDB, a full-function big-data system with NoSQL data modelling, partitioned LSM storage, feeds, transactions, and a scalable runtime. PIQL provides query-level operation bounds, scale independence, SLO compliance prediction, and privacy-policy authoring and enforcement.

Knowledge maps and science maps support information search and interdisciplinary collaboration, while open knowledge bases emphasize geospatial quality and crowdsourced data.

a620c8cfa3a5de1a3be6dcf5168109c45bab4604.text:
## Community Report: Scientific Search, Figure Mining, and Graph-Based Methods

This community connects research-paper infrastructure, figure extraction, inverse scattering, and graph-path optimization.

**Scholarly search and visualization.** TIB ArXiv extends ArXiv Sanity Preserver with a unified backend, text-based search, enhanced search and ranking, paper visualization, programming interfaces, and a user interface. ArXiv offers programming interfaces and an alternative search portal, while ArXiv Sanity Preserver is an open-source framework.

**Figure extraction.** DeepFigures uses a deep neural network for end-to-end figure detection and extraction from rasterized PDFs, and is deployed in Semantic Scholar across 13 million scientific documents. Induced figure labels, generated through distant supervision and supplemented by ArXiv and PubMed, train the model and achieve 96.8% average precision.

**Inverse scattering.** DeepNIS is a deep-neural-network methodology for nonlinear electromagnetic inverse scattering involving EM wavefields and potentially high-contrast objects. Its cascaded complex-valued residual CNN modules connect DNN architecture with an iterative inverse scattering method. It learns a general EM inverse scattering model, outperforming conventional methods, and is evaluated by image quality and computational time.

**Graph and learning methods.** Randomized optimal transport extends the bag-of-paths framework using free-energy minimization, Gibbs–Boltzmann distributions, and hitting or non-hitting paths. These path measures relate to resistance and shortest-path distances. Multi-task learning enables joint classification and translation while learning a user-sensitive ensemble function, including illegal-comment classification on the Kaggle Toxic Comment Dataset.

12eaee08530fcc055c47da3a3ea2f93811a47f40.text:
# Contextual Ranking, Web Archives, and Sequential Pattern Mining

This community connects BERT-based representation learning with biomedical entity normalization, candidate ranking, and recommendation. BERT uses bidirectional Transformers to pre-train contextualized word representations and supports sentence-pair classification. BioBERT and ClinicalBERT adapt this approach for biomedical and clinical text mining. BERT-based ranking performs biomedical entity normalization, addressing term variation through fine-tuned models.

Candidate ranking selects candidates suitable for a job description—approximated by past job experience—and uses archival quality as a ranking feature. In web archives, URI lookup returns binary responses, while recommendation augments lookup by filtering candidate URIs to archived pages and ranking recommended content.

A second theme concerns next-basket recommendation and high-utility sequential pattern mining. IERT, inspired by BERT, pre-trains item representations conditioned on transaction contexts, producing contextualized item embeddings that capture sequential user behavior. It is proposed for next-basket recommendation, where existing methods use static item representations. High-utility sequential patterns, applicable to market basket analysis, are discovered through high-utility sequential pattern mining, a knowledge-discovery task.

HUSP-ULL is evaluated on real-life datasets, including Ta Feng. It uses a lexicographic sequence tree and utility linked list; pruning strategies reduce its search space using tight utility upper bounds.

b269ce160097a127f01dcc8b4ec1a6d9cb1ba975.text:
## Community Report: Social Influence, Research Trends, and Explainable Data Integration

This community links methods for social-network analysis, diffusion, recommendation, research-trend discovery, and cross-dataset explanation.

**Explain3D** explains disagreements between semantically similar queries over disjoint datasets. It uses semantic mapping and query provenance to identify causes of result differences, formalizes optimal explanations, and improves efficiency with a smart partitioning optimizer. Synthetic and real-world data evaluate it, in contrast to traditional record-linkage and schema-matching approaches.

Social influence research addresses influence detection, event cascades, recommendation, and contagion. Discriminative ranking identifies likely sources of cascade events and is evaluated on U.S. House legislation co-sponsorship and Higgs boson rumors spreading through Twitter. Homophily is treated as a confound that can be mistaken for influence. Interaction-Aware Diffusion (IAD) models contagion adoption under interacting contents and sentiment interactions, using Weibo for evaluation.

Network formation studies connect homophily, triadic closure, friendship formation, and social bots. A randomized field experiment finds that displaying shared attributes reduces informational friction, updates perceived similarity, and increases friend requests, especially when similarities are surprising.

TrendNets maps research trends from dynamic co-word networks using sparse matrix decomposition and convex optimization, separating stationary from bursty topics. It is evaluated on a 16-year conference-paper collection.

Finally, set-level rating models address systematic under- and over-rating and improve item-level rating prediction.

1f12ecb5394dcb5e598c007cfa1d197a5a3fa8c7.text:
## Opinion Intervention and Temporal Event Discovery

This community connects network opinion dynamics with temporal event discovery. In the DeGroot–Friedkin model, susceptibility interventions modify agents’ susceptibility to persuasion and define opinion maximization or minimization, measured by the sum of opinions. Opinion maximization targets agents under a budget constraint; the budgeted objective is NP-hard and not submodular, motivating heuristic optimization evaluated on a Twitter network with real opinion estimates. Without a budget constraint, an optimal target set can be found in polynomial time.

Multiphase investment strategies optimize opinion influence across phases: a phase’s final opinions become initial biases in the next, while myopic investment provides a baseline. Two-phase strategies are characterized through Nash equilibria, and optimal budget allocation between two phases is polynomial-time computable. Simulations show that stronger initial-bias effects require greater first-phase investment.

For temporal networks, event discovery segments timelines into non-overlapping intervals and models events as dense subgraphs, maximizing total density across intervals. Dynamic densest subgraph discovery and approximate dynamic programming support a fast approximation algorithm. A node-coverage formulation encourages covering more nodes and is NP-hard even on static graphs; submodularity enables greedy approximation there, with the greedy approach extended from static to temporal networks.

289a59816642aae303c05cb45442a35b46c9e973.text:
## Community Report: Diffusion, Cooperation, and Data-Centric Systems

This community centers on information, product, and idea diffusion in social and technical networks. Multidimensional marked Hawkes processes and temporal point-process models address product adoption, recurrent product usage, competing products, cascade diffusion, and latent diffusion-network inference, evaluated on URL-shortening and music-streaming datasets.

Seeding research studies budget allocation, sparse seeding, and scheduling which node to seed over time. Scheduling heuristics improve product adoption rates by 29%–94% and outperform existing methods in empirical simulations. Nash equilibria, differential games, community-membership games, and best-response link alteration strategies connect competition, cooperation, network topology, and stable or efficient communities. Social welfare maximization and optimal social norms address incentives, punishment length, whitewashing, and sustainable cooperation.

Image-virality work links virality scores and dynamics to visual and relative attributes. Document-classification methods, including Bi-LSTM, process legal documents for relevant tagging and case allocation. Idea-relation characterization uses document corpora, pairwise cooccurrence, and prevalence correlation.

Systems include DeepPage for real-time-feedback page recommendation and complementary-item display, and cloud-aware provenance for reproducible workflow execution, virtual-machine configuration, and resource re-provisioning. Event-evolution tracking analyzes social-post streams and incrementally detects event birth, growth, decay, merging, and splitting. Open-source and proprietary technology development are also contrasted.

e0ba8078df5517d304a31a631e27f899b3ef1f51.text:
## Community Report: Temporal Archives, Social Metadata, and Process Discovery

This community connects methods for making large, heterogeneous collections searchable, interpretable, and analyzable.

**Web archives** are treated as temporal collections supporting web-archive search, temporal search, analysis, and focused sub-collection extraction. Systems such as **Tempas**, **Plus**, and surrogate-based interfaces support collection understanding, graph-query processing, and access to archived resources. Surrogates—including social cards and browser thumbnails—summarize collections.

**Social tagging systems** such as **BibSonomy**, **Delicious**, and **Last.fm** create folksonomies through collaborative annotation. Tags support document navigation, exploratory search, resource classification, and popularity-driven browsing. **Tag reconciliation** and semantic metadata layers address synonymy, ambiguity, incoherence, and relations across portals. Recommender methods include verbal and semantic tag recommendation, query recommendations, and time-aware lurker ranking.

**Process mining** analyzes event logs for process discovery, variants, exceptions, and machine learning. Local process model mining supports sequence, concurrency, choice, and loops; process models are evaluated with fitness. Business-process datasets include personal loan and overdraft processes.

For digitized historical documents, **corpus conversion services**, OCR models, document parsing, and machine-learning classification convert PDFs and bitmaps into structured representations at scale. Diplomatic transcriptions provide ground truth, while character confidence, lexicality, and error-rate metrics assess OCR quality.

Finally, protected accounts and surrogate nodes address sensitive graphs by balancing connectivity, utility, and topology opacity.

7eec5c321cd04b5f3f72cc6d362249ee82ad1418.text:
# Graph Sampling, Network Inference, and Applied Analysis

This community centers on methods for estimating and analyzing large, sampled, and dynamic graphs. **Egocentric subgraph frequency estimation** combines probability or random-walk samples of egocentric networks with exact subgraph counting to estimate relative frequencies, including large maximal cliques. Related clique-size and composition analyses use labeled or unlabeled neighbor estimators and are applied to Facebook users, college and country friendship graphs.

Sampling methods also support unbiased graphlet and graph-size estimation. SafetyMargin corrects random-walk estimators, while IE exploits induced edges. Coarse-grained topology estimation uses design-based inference, induced-subgraph sampling, and star sampling to estimate category sizes and inter-category connection probabilities in weighted category graphs.

Another major topic is graph optimization: approximate greedy algorithms use sample materialization to achieve near-optimal guarantees, while randomized methods address betweenness centrality, total hitting time, hit coverage, and network control. Graph signal reconstruction recovers bandlimited signals through sparse injection, graph filtering, and time-domain interpolation, with perfect reconstruction as a criterion.

Applications include mobile social networks built from call and text activity, project-success analysis of software projects, academic referral and usage analysis, and misinformation interaction studies. Privacy-aware learning includes ActiveClean and the functional mechanism, which perturbs objective functions for accurate regression under differential privacy.

967c411d45a63223042970f446545588e37a8f7b.text:
## Graph Sampling, Inference, and Network Applications

This community centers on estimating graph structure and analyzing social and software networks. Sampling methods include probability, uniform, independence, link-trace, induced-subgraph, star, and random-walk sampling. Random walks support unbiased estimators, graph-size and graphlet estimation, safety-margin corrections, and approximate greedy algorithms. Egocentric subgraph frequency estimation extends these ideas to egocentric networks, maximal cliques, and relative subgraph frequencies, while labeled and unlabeled neighbor estimators measure clique-size distributions.

Coarse-grained topology estimation uses design-based inference, sampled nodes, and neighbor category information to estimate category sizes and inter-category connection probabilities in weighted category graphs. IE, combined with SafetyMargin, estimates graph size using induced edges.

Other methods address optimization, privacy, and signals. Functional mechanism perturbs objective functions for privacy-preserving optimization and accurate regression; ActiveClean trains convex-loss models and is evaluated on UCI Adult, UCI EEG, Dollars for Docs, and WorldBank data. Graph signal reconstruction uses bandlimited signals, sparse signal injection, graph filters, and time-domain interpolation, with perfect reconstruction and network control as goals.

Applications include mobile social networks built from call and text-message activity, Facebook clique and misinformation analyses, project success analysis using team structure and external developer activity, academic referral analysis using PeerJ data, and bibliometric author contribution estimation through linear regression.

96145a8614d1df64a6a8fb216ada3ef2e8ed7dff.text:
### Scalable, Distributed, and Privacy-Aware Data Systems

This community centers on scalability in large-scale data processing, graph analytics, spatial computation, and distributed systems. MapReduce supports scalable processing across computer clusters, including wavelet-histogram construction, web-corpus analysis, kNN and fuzzy joins, and multiway joins. Its costs and behavior are assessed through communication cost, reducer size, replication rate, and the number of machines. Manimal, Brace, MapUpdate, and Somabit extend or exploit MapReduce-style processing.

Spatial analytics includes distributed spatial clustering, density-based and variance-based clustering, distributed spatial indexes, reachability queries, and top-k spatial-textual cluster queries. These methods emphasize clustering quality, near-linear query scaling, and operation across servers and cores. Join algorithms include optimized, repartition-based, multiway equijoin, and kNN join techniques.

Graph research covers graph neural networks, graph convolution, message passing, temporal graph indexing, approximate query processing, and scalable graph machine learning through systems such as AGL. Other systems address scalable entity matching, record linkage, recommender systems, and online social networks.

Privacy and security form a parallel theme: privacy-aware data partitioning, secure MapReduce protocols, search interfaces, database-as-a-service, and policy specification aim to limit disclosure and protect computation, including in untrusted infrastructures.

09e7bb12d65f606a258d824fd5b32b74dbbbf1ef.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Data Quality, Privacy, Search, and Network Inference

This community centers on extracting, integrating, searching, and analyzing heterogeneous data. **Truth discovery** and **data fusion** identify true values from conflicting source observations, while accommodating multiple truths and false claims from unstructured-data extraction. Related methods include belief structured matrix factorization, probabilistic graphical models, hybrid models, source-reliability and reputation algorithms, and posterior sampling.

**Privacy** is addressed through synthetic data, privacy-aware data partitioning, obfuscation, distributed online social networks, and privacy-focused search interfaces. Synthetic data protects privacy while mimicking real or microdata distributions and provides evaluation settings for truth-discovery algorithms, entity resolution, network-structure recovery, spectral partitioning, ecological link prediction, and latent self-exciting point-process models. These methods are also tested on real-world and real data.

A second major theme is **similarity search**, including high-dimensional and approximate search, Euclidean distance, query relaxation, text hashing, bit-wise comparison, and Forward Backward Similarity. Result diversification and diversification frameworks reduce similarity among returned results. Systems and methods also support schema matching, semantic type detection, entity consolidation, visual content analysis, product search, and network analysis using models such as mixed-membership stochastic blockmodels, matched bipartite block models, and spectral partitioning.

d6bb546eb2bc0f49cc186866df100840e4a8024b.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Dynamic Retrieval, Ecological Networks, and Reproducible AI

This community connects three themes: explainable product search, ecological link prediction, and reproducible AI research.

For product search, a dynamic relation embedding model builds a dynamic knowledge graph from multi-relational product data, search-session context, and changing user–item search and purchase behavior. It ranks products in a latent space and supports explainable retrieval through logic inference and entity soft matching.

Ecological network link prediction addresses imperfect detection using a framework formulated as maximum-likelihood identification. The framework incorporates a Poisson N-mixture model and probabilistic nonnegative matrix factorization, and is solved with a scalable convergence-guaranteed optimization algorithm. It is validated on real-world ecological networks and synthetic data, complementing matrix-completion collaborative filtering, which does not address ecological challenges.

A related graph-signal line studies blind community detection in unobserved time-varying networks. Signals are produced by filtering white noise; spectral partitioning recovers latent stochastic blockmodel communities and has consistency guarantees.

Finally, AI paper repositories are examined in an explorative study of over 1,700 repositories. Missing documentation, maintenance, and difficult runtime configuration reduce code quality, reproducibility, and code reuse, contributing to the academia–industry gap. Curated synthetic datasets, derived from minimally perturbed real data, support privacy, bias correction, diversity, collaboration, and protection of disadvantaged groups.

0a8b2a990c2928e7ad5faa532f9bb92f51de83d4.text:
## Research Assessment, Novelty, and University Data Governance

This community links bibliometric research assessment with university data stewardship and online ranking analysis. Comparative bibliometric analysis and international research benchmarking use citation and publication analysis across scientific disciplines, often relying on total citations and total publications. These indicators can create distortions when disciplinary differences and scientific fertility are ignored. The VQR 2004–2010 assessed Italian universities and professors; its “new productives”—previously unproductive professors who later became productive—are studied through publication output and same-university co-authorship. Unusually high exclusive co-authorship may indicate gift authorship. Assessment criteria and PBRF systems can also encourage opportunistic behavior.

A major methodological theme is research novelty. Temporal embedding learning derives semantic change from scientific literature to construct a novelty metric measuring topic novelty. Panel data analysis, including work on MEDLINE/PubMed, examines whether novelty predicts future publication growth; effects on literature growth may persist for over ten years.

Another theme concerns CWTS Leiden Ranking systems. Website experiments and visitor activity analysis examine visitor countries, pages, and attention to ranking indicators.

Finally, universities accumulate grey data and exploit it for learning analytics, requiring data governance and stewardship. Privacy, cyber risk, open-access requirements, HIPAA, FERPA, and PII protections frame tensions between transparency, accountability, and responsible data use.

9a24396088c6b61c08816791463dca69613e2ea4.text:
## Cloud Databases, Recovery, Privacy, and Modularity

This community connects cloud computing and Database-as-a-Service with elasticity, scalability, availability, and pay-as-you-go usage, while highlighting data privacy and database security as adoption concerns. Cloud databases use security mechanisms, and database outsourcing is performed through Database-as-a-Service.

Searchable encryption enables efficient retrieval over encrypted cloud data. LRSE provides lightweight, efficient multi-keyword ranked and top-k search using word2vec embeddings trained on English Wikipedia, an improved secure kNN method, and a Dual Embedding Space Model that substitutes the traditional Vector Space Model. It operates under a known background model.

Database systems provide transactions, stored procedures, and declarative querying. Stored procedures colocate application code with the database but may reduce modularity through tightly coupled application and data-tier code. Actor database systems combine actor-based data tiers with database features; actor abstraction encapsulates state, supports modularity, and enables scalability reasoning. Their use is illustrated by a smart supermarket application, while modularity-based approaches apply modularity to community detection.

Recovery research addresses media failure and system unavailability. Instant restore, incrementally implemented on ARIES, restores data segments on demand and permits read/write access during restoration, reducing repair time to seconds and post-failure transaction latency below one second. Single-pass restore further decreases repair time and increases restore bandwidth. ARIES provides the traditional foundation for logging and recovery.

4d771319bbea9a953cca7b984cf78027f3c82316.text:
## Graph Learning, Prediction, and Social-Data Analytics

This community spans graph-based machine learning, social-network analysis, information retrieval, and data systems, with extensive evaluation on real-world datasets such as CiteSeer, Cora, temporal data, access logs, and the Facebook ad exposure dataset.

Predictive modeling includes student-dropout and academic-performance prediction, meme-success detection, purchase prediction, and ranking reproduction from social-media posts. Dynamic-network models outperform static and non-network alternatives, while feature selection improves inference efficiency. Classification covers spreading behavior, fraud, node classification, and incremental maintenance; LLGR and LCGR add graph regularization, latent classes, and social relationships.

Neural methods support user and item preference prediction, collaborative ranking, operator embeddings, and explainable recommendation. DirectRanker is neural-network based, while SemNet uses historical states to predict developments in quantum physics. Matrix factorization, mixed-effects models, spectral algorithms, and maximum-entropy models provide additional predictive and estimation techniques.

Graph tasks include community extraction, group formation, influence maximization, graph matching, correlation clustering, haplotype assembly, and hidden-database crawling. Systems and methods such as adaptive and non-adaptive BC approximation, percolation-based matching, Multi-MotifGAN, and view-driven deduplication address scalability and structure.

TagMe focuses on efficient, accurate annotation of short and long texts, resolving synonymy and polysemy on the fly. Visual analytics, query-performance prediction, and network-based quality indicators connect analytical methods to practical data infrastructure.

e858d34a2b4a8a8cb8ffe88e9c5e2da6a2e5f469.text:
### Relational, Graph, and Matrix Query Processing

This community connects relational algebra, graph computation, matrix languages, and polystore systems. Relational algebra underlies SQL and operates on relations, which are multisets of tuples; associative arrays provide a common mathematical formulation linking SQL, NoSQL, NewSQL, and polystores. Relational joins are central, with database query optimizers addressing join-size estimation and join-execution planning. Join-project plans use intermediate projections, fractional edge cover numbers, and maximum hypergraph density to characterize worst- and average-case behavior.

MATLANG expresses matrix operations through relational algebra using arithmetic, grouping, and summation. Its extensions MATLANG+inv and MATLANG+eigen add matrix inversion and eigen operations. Whereas MATLANG without inversion cannot compute transitive closure, MATLANG+inv can compute it for directed graphs; the evaluation problem for MATLANG+eigen is complete for ∃R.

GRFusion integrates graph-relational queries into a relational engine, treating graphs as first-class citizens and using SQL to define them. Implemented in VoltDB, an open-source in-memory relational DBMS, GRFusion’s query engine executes graph operators and cross-data-model query plans containing relational and graph operators. It reports up to four orders of magnitude query-time speedup over state-of-the-art approaches.

eca871d3c1b3c25b0d9702ebdea8624fe43b9642.text:
## Community Report: Scalable Graph Analytics, Dependency Discovery, and Network Systems

This community spans scalable graph processing, heterogeneous-network representation learning, data-dependency discovery, recommender systems, and supercomputer visualization.

A typed graphlet counting framework counts typed graphlets—small induced typed subgraphs of heterogeneous networks—and is evaluated by runtime, space efficiency, parallel speedup, and scalability. Heterogeneous networks encompass homogeneous, bipartite, k-partite, and signed graphs; bipartite stream graphs extend bipartite concepts.

Node similarity modeling combines automatic path discovery with deep content embedding. Continuous and supervised reinforcement learning explore useful paths, while semi-supervised joint learning integrates path exploration and content embedding. Supervised reinforcement learning is jointly trained with unsupervised deep embedding, which supports inductive learning across the network.

A scalable hyperbolic recommender system uses hyperbolic geometry, a novel hyperbolic model, and the Einstein midpoint to implement asymmetric recommendation. It is evaluated on complex-network datasets and reportedly outperforms Euclidean models while scaling to millions of users and hundreds of thousands of items.

Maimon performs approximate dependency discovery, mining multivalued dependencies and reconstructing acyclic schemes; information theory defines approximation. Multivalued dependencies are noise-sensitive and contrast with functional dependencies.

Finally, Accumulo, D4M, Unity, and a 3D visualization platform support monitoring and management of Lincoln Laboratory supercomputer systems, with scalability as a key concern.

039ee012972cf54c8b4213e8d8e65e977a5f7552.text:
# Graph Methods for Temporal, Multimodal, and Document Understanding

This community brings together graph formalisms, graph learning, and structured-information systems. **Stream graphs** provide a formalism for temporal network modeling and generalize classical graph concepts; weighted stream graphs add node or link weights, while directed stream graphs add link directions. Transitivity and clustering coefficient are defined for stream graphs, and network transitivity helps explain common-neighbor methods.

**SWAG** is a graph convolutional network algorithm that combines efficient random walks with graph convolutions, adapts GraphSAGE to weighted graphs, and is trained on the weighted Target product graph. Random walks and feature diffusion can generate community-based and role-based embeddings.

For food understanding, a recipe retrieval system uses meal images as queries and is trained and evaluated on **Recipe1M**, which pairs images with raw recipe text. Attention-based recipe text encoding focuses on meal-specific preparation steps to address intra- and inter-class variability. Self-attention processes raw recipe text and can remove the need for upstream instruction sentence embeddings. Retrieved recipes provide input for nutrient content estimation.

For document analysis, word box graph representations model invoice pages using trainable textual and positional features. Table detection and extraction is reformulated as text box labeling, with a neural network model evaluated on an invoice documents dataset containing pro forma invoices and debit notes.

3feec130c6ddb6d8579fece6e13e39c1a2d6cd53.text:
## Database Repair, Query Answering, and Causality
