This community centers on maintaining data quality and answering queries over imperfect relational databases. **Integrity constraints**, matching dependencies, and functionality constraints support **data cleaning**, error detection, duplicate resolution, and repair. Methods include consistency-based, abductive, and model-based diagnosis; database repairs, tuple-based repairs, active integrity constraints, revision programming, and repair validation. Systems and approaches include **BoostClean**, grounded database repairs, answer-set programs, and relational matching dependencies.

A second theme is **query answering and rewriting**. Datalog, Datalog+/–, existential and guarded rules, description logics, and OWL 2 reasoners provide logical foundations. Materialisation, chase algorithms, semi-naive fixpoints, Magic Sets, and incremental maintenance support efficient computation, while sticky and weakly sticky Datalog+/– enable rewriting-based answering. Query rewriting also supports semantic query optimization, ontological query compilation, resolved answers, and query latency management.

The community studies **query-answer and database causality**, relating tuples and tuple-based repairs to causes, view updates, answer-set programs, and model-based diagnosis. It further examines entailment, decidability, computational complexity, chase termination, necessary answers, secrecy views, uncertainty management, and clean or resolved answers.

17eca1ebf2f5c8529b37e26dd0b5d1b6293b421e.text:
## Community Report: Data Quality, Causality, and Distributed Data Systems

This community centers on managing unreliable, complex, and distributed data. **Data cleaning** includes data repairing, duplicate resolution through matching dependencies, pattern-driven methods, and interactive systems such as **ActiveClean** and **MLClean**. Integrity constraints, denial constraints, and active integrity constraints support integrity checking, diagnosis, and repair validation.

A major theme connects **database repairs** with **query-answer causality**. Tuple-based repairs, grounded database repair, model-based diagnosis, answer-set programs, and view updates provide methods for identifying database tuples that cause query answers or violations. Repairs also support uncertainty management and are studied through rationality postulates and repair semantics.

The community also addresses efficient data processing. **Join size estimation**, including similarity join and streaming similarity self-join estimation, supports query-plan generation and data-cleaning applications. Methods target estimation accuracy, estimator error, and streaming settings.

Another cluster concerns **blockchain systems**, including Ethereum, Hyperledger Fabric, private, permissioned, and permissionless blockchains. Smart contracts enable protocol enforcement and data-management frameworks, while systems such as **BlockBench** benchmark contract workloads. These studies relate blockchain performance and interoperability to database capabilities.

Graph-oriented work covers graph signal reconstruction, homophily estimation, infection-source identification, motif analysis, recommendation, and diversified top-k search.

9dfe3a47dc187f87f216ee0688c19e8c9021e991.text:
## Query Answering, Causality, and Consistent Data

This community connects database query answering with causality, repairs, diagnosis, and rule-based reasoning. Query answering is formulated as an entailment problem over databases and Datalog+/− theories, including existential rules, disjunction, and weakly sticky, sticky, and weakly acyclic fragments. Description logics provide decidable query answering, while guardedness and other acyclicity notions establish decidability and chase termination boundaries. Query rewriting supports semantic query optimization, compiles ontological queries into equivalent first-order queries, and can retrieve resolved answers in tractable cases.

Query-answer causality and QA causality study causes and responsibility for query answers, including under integrity constraints and views. They connect to consistency-based and model-based diagnosis, answer-set programs, database repairs, hitting sets, and vertex covers. View-conditioned causality extends this perspective to views and updates.

Data quality is addressed through integrity constraints, matching dependencies, entity-resolution policies, active integrity constraints, revision programming, and repair semantics. These methods transform dirty instances into clean or minimally resolved instances, with repairs modeled using fixpoints and uncertainty management.

Additional systems and methods cover secret answers and secrecy views, query stability and computability, distinct-value estimation, collaborative graph analysis, recommendation, and verification of dynamic processes.

ff545a4cf4357c64fc1365c8d0f0364153a6a6b4.text:
## Integrity, Causality, and Blockchain Data Management

This community centers on inconsistent databases, integrity constraints, repairs, and query-answer causality. Database repairs address violations of denial constraints using active integrity constraints, fixpoint operators, grounded repairs, repair programs, and repair semantics. Tuple-based repairs connect directly to causes of query answers, while consistency-based and model-based diagnosis provide explanations, responsibility values, hitting-set, and vertex-cover formulations. Matching dependencies, revision programming, qualitative data repairing, and uncertainty management extend this repair-oriented perspective.

Datalog supports bottom-up and push-based evaluation, stratified programs, data migration, explanation generation, and translation to C++. Related systems and frameworks include DLV, PUG, Dynamite, and a declarative statistical modeling framework. Provenance abstraction, graph-based provenance models, and provenance questions address explanation and query analysis.

A second major theme is blockchain data management. Blockchain systems such as Ethereum and Hyperledger Fabric support decentralized applications and smart contracts. Private, permissioned, permissionless, and interoperable blockchains use mechanisms including private channels, access control, and concurrency control. Blockbench benchmarks smart-contract workloads, while systems such as BlockLite, ModelHub, and global asset management systems represent supporting data-management infrastructure. User-generated content and geospatial extraction provide application-oriented data sources.

7bf25c8a0f60789b58864d63a182f6ad70ec8e0b.text:
## Blockchain Interoperability, Execution, and Distributed Analysis

This community covers blockchain systems, their performance, and interoperability. General-purpose systems such as Ethereum and Hyperledger Fabric support decentralized applications and smart contracts; Ethereum provides a Turing-complete smart-contract machine. Permissionless blockchains use peer-to-peer cryptocurrency systems, while permissioned blockchains support asset management and registration. Blocklite emulates public blockchains, including proof-of-work, peer-to-peer networking, hash-based immutability, and preprocessing, through an accessible programming interface.

Smart-contract execution addresses concurrent execution using optimistic concurrency control (OCC), batching, and deterministic replay. Miner nodes execute contract batches and produce schedule logs, which validators replay; graph partitioning reduces replay communication costs. Blockchain systems must also operate despite Byzantine nodes, and consensus protocols can be customized through programming interfaces.

Interoperable blockchains aim to connect siloed systems, but cross-chain communication, general cross-chain transactions, access control, and requirements beyond data standardization remain open problems.

Other research concerns distributed dependency discovery, where algorithms share six processing primitives and use search-space pruning and communication-optimized implementations, especially in shared-nothing architectures. XML schema learning performs inference over XML documents and restricted regular-expression subclasses; SOIRE and iSOIRE use single-occurrence regular expressions, automata, maximum independent sets, and support interleaving.

Finally, multi-feature rumor blocking uses multi-layer diffusion models, with Multi-Sampling and Revised-IMM providing solution methods evaluated on real datasets.

6875cb22542c1716a939a815f7fba226ec2d0f58.text:
## Ranked Enumeration, Evaluation Protocols, and Robust Datasets

This community studies ranked enumeration of top-*k* answers to conjunctive queries in relational databases. A ranking function orders results; decomposable or compatible ranking functions enable partial score aggregation and efficient enumeration. Query decomposition and query structure, together with database instances, influence output-sensitive complexity. Priority-queue algorithms target near-optimal or asymptotically optimal enumeration delay, including after updates, while light-heavy thresholds control delay, preprocessing cost, and maintenance cost.

Preprocessing is a central trade-off: preprocessing time and partial computation can reduce enumeration delay, and different preprocessing choices complicate algorithm comparisons. A proposed preprocessing protocol-selection method supports more transparent result sharing. Static evaluation considers hierarchical queries without updates, whereas dynamic evaluation handles single-tuple inserts and deletes, with update time and enumeration delay as key metrics; factorization width characterizes query structure.

The community also addresses evaluation of recommender algorithms on public datasets, which are often heavily preprocessed. An embarrassingly shallow autoencoder, defined as a linear model for sparse data, uses a training objective with a closed-form solution and achieves high ranking accuracy. Evaluation protocols and dataset robustness are important for making comparisons across studies reliable and transparent.

5ff761a869e143ee247d487ff2f4605836068079.text:
## Scalable Graph, Bitmap, and Data-Processing Systems

This community centers on scalable algorithms and systems for large and heterogeneous data. Spectral link prediction algorithms, based on spectral embedding and using a k-closest-pairs algorithm, are compared with standard link-prediction algorithms that compute similarity metrics on vertex pairs. Their runtime and performance are evaluated on large networks, with scalability improving as dataset size increases.

Transactional frequent subgraph mining is represented by DIMSpan, which mines string-labeled directed multigraphs on distributed in-memory dataflow systems such as Apache Spark and Apache Flink. DIMSpan uses pruning and other optimization techniques to improve runtime and network-traffic efficiency, demonstrating scalability on large graph collections.

Bitmap processing is another major theme. Compressed bitmap indexes, including Roaring bitmaps implemented by CRoaring, support union, intersection, difference, and symmetric-difference operations. Vectorized algorithms compute these operations between arrays using SIMD instructions. Apache Spark, Elasticsearch, and Oracle use Roaring or compressed bitmap indexes to accelerate processing and queries.

Frequent itemset mining includes Apriori, Eclat, and FP-Growth. Generated datasets vary in frequent-item density and maximum transaction size; these factors affect performance, with Eclat and FP-Growth handling increases better than Apriori.

Additional topics include push-based bottom-up evaluation for Datalog and deductive databases, and OpenGeoBase, a spatio-temporal NoSQL database supporting IoT and evaluated with an intelligent transport-system dataset.

aaf2a7feeb6c590905395e81f690b5e5c7924f8b.text:
## Database and Stream-Processing Performance

This community centers on evaluating and improving database, stream-processing, and distributed-system performance, especially **throughput, latency, execution time, memory consumption, and storage cost**. Query optimization is a major theme: PostgreSQL uses a linear disk-I/O cost model, while query optimizers, sampling-based query re-optimization, cardinality estimation, query merging, operator reordering, and memory-I/O cost models address query-plan quality. Sampling-based re-optimization can catch large errors made by PostgreSQL.

Stream-processing systems emphasize efficient, low-latency execution. **TStream** supports stateful stream processing with transactional state management, asynchronous state transactions, operation-chain execution, dual-mode scheduling, and dynamic restructuring on multicore machines. It achieves high throughput with limited latency penalties. Other systems, including **Bleach, MacroBase, StreamBox HBM, Strider, Pyxis, DGCC, Elasticutor, Minos, and ChainifyDB**, report strong throughput or latency improvements. RDF stream-processing systems such as **PRSP** and Strider are evaluated using throughput and latency.

The community also covers transaction correctness and scalability, including concurrency control, snapshot isolation, serializability, distributed transactions, fault tolerance, data replication, and shared-nothing architectures. Spark, Hadoop, Hive, Shark, and PostgreSQL provide comparison or deployment contexts for large-scale analytics.

3e076ff3ac636696eef437f7796a2e1f994256c8.text:
## Query Evaluation, Enumeration, and Natural-Language Aggregation

This community connects tractable query evaluation with enumeration and information extraction. For conjunctive queries and unions of conjunctive queries, it studies combined and enumeration complexity, fixed-parameter tractability, self joins, and free-connexity. Free-connexity characterizes tractable enumeration for several query classes, including some unions containing—even consisting entirely of—intractable conjunctive queries. Closed-form formulas compute expected conjunctive-query cardinalities over RDF data.

A second strand develops CFG-Datalog and related automata methods. CFG-Datalog captures conjunctive queries with suitable simplicial decompositions, guarded negation fragment queries of bounded CQ-rank, and two-way regular path queries. Query evaluation translates CFG-Datalog to alternating two-way automata, whose semantics use cycluits; bounded treewidth enables efficient evaluation, including bilinear-time evaluation and fixed-parameter tractability. Stratified negation is supported.

A third strand concerns document spanners and enumeration. Sequential and extended variable-set automata extract mappings from input documents. Circuit-based enumeration structures support dynamic node relabelings, with logarithmic relabeling time, linear preprocessing, and linear answer delay or constant delay enumeration.

Finally, NLAQ maps natural-language queries to RDF aggregate queries. Query-intention understanding identifies aggregations, uses an extended paraphrase dictionary to propose semantic mappings, and filters them with predicate-type adjacency sets. Aggregate translation plans produce query plans, and NLAQ is evaluated on QALD.

6ae1493554c17300efdce30d358144b5c6ad6c15.text:
## Graph-Based Influence, Learning, and Social Data Systems

This community centers on influence optimization in social-network graphs. Influence maximization selects seed nodes to maximize expected influence spread under stochastic propagation; its variants include lattice influence maximization, time-critical optimization with deadlines, and seed minimization, the dual problem of reaching a target audience with few seeds. Marketing strategy mix assigns seed activation probabilities, while IMM-VSN and IMM-PRR provide lattice algorithms, with IMM-VSN faster at equal spread and suited to independent strategy activations. ASTI addresses adaptive seed minimization with approximation guarantees and expected running-time bounds.

Fairness is a major concern: influence disparity may affect socially salient groups, and time-critical optimization defines group-fairness constraints. Online learning estimates diffusion using node-level feedback and achieves cumulative expected regret of order O(1/√T).

Other work studies social learning and opinion dynamics, including non-Bayesian models, French DeGroot dynamics, imperfect or biased private signals, and conservative, radical, or negative signal structures. Agents update belief reports from private and neighboring beliefs.

Data systems include seed-driven extraction across geo-social sources, using search-radius optimization and recursive clustering to improve yield and request efficiency. Heterogeneous edge embeddings support friend recommendation in multi-graphs, evaluated on Hike. RE query processing uses sublinear indexes and parallel processing for regular-expression path queries. False-news datasets support characterization, detection, classification, and mitigation.

1f47b89f3e17779b516f5e4a9f09aba15c33fa34.text:
## Urban Networks, Ranking, Mobility, and Social Signals

This community spans computational analysis of urban life, digital platforms, graphs, rankings, and affect. Mobility research uses mobile network data, activity patterns, census districts, public spaces, and Uber-related movement to characterize human movement, floating populations, urban lifestyles, and city structure. Functional clustering groups neighborhoods by activity timelines, while matrix factor analysis extracts salient mobility patterns. Airbnb, Uber, ride sharing services, taxis, and delivery markets connect sharing-economy platforms with supply–demand matching, tourism pressure, gentrification, municipal regulation, and changing demand and offerings.

Graph research develops graphlet counting, centrality algorithms, time-varying and temporal representations, graph generative models, and the X Kronecker product graph model. Variance representations and approximate query processing address sampling and numerical precision, including catastrophic cancellation and floating-point loss.

Ranking research evaluates rankers through online evaluation, interleaving, dueling bandits, multi-dueling bandits, and human judgment. Fairness methods—including FairSumm, fairness-aware recommendation, and optimization frameworks—target unequal representation and protected-group disadvantage in ranked outputs.

Other themes include virality and message propagation, with spread metrics and viral facets; emotion analysis in marketing, news, music, and human sounds; and urban smellscapes studied through smell-tagging methodologies, sound dictionaries, georeferenced pictures, and perceptions of public spaces.

39dc574998d06d71814efb8289e51443234fdd99.text:
### Visual Features and Hybrid Indexing for Web Retrieval

This community focuses on using visual and spatial information to improve relevance ranking in ad hoc web retrieval. Web page snapshots provide both query-independent raw layout information and query-dependent layouts rendered with matched query words. A human-inspired visual perception model extracts visual features from these snapshots and jointly learns them with human-crafted features end-to-end.

Visual features support extraction of page-quality and structural visual signals, enable efficient online acquisition through extended inverted indexing, and improve relevance-ranking performance. Hybrid index structures evaluate both visual and spatial features, and are assessed for performance and result accuracy against baseline indexes. The baseline methods extend a visual LSH structure and a spatial R*-tree, combining alternative indexing approaches for comparison.

Evaluation uses benchmark problems, including those provided by OpenRuleBench, a benchmark suite for rule engines and deductive databases. Thus, the community connects page-layout analysis, learned visual representations, spatial and hybrid indexing, and benchmark-based evaluation.

08ad363c49d844c2b1622d3509a21931dd1ffd32.text:
## Performance, Streaming, and Data-System Engineering

This community focuses on evaluating and improving database and stream-processing performance, especially throughput, latency, scalability, and workload behavior. RDF stream processing systems are assessed using throughput and latency; systems such as PRSP, Strider, StreamBox HBM, MacroBase, and TStream report high processing rates, while Bleach emphasizes high throughput and low latency.

TStream is a central example of multicore stateful stream processing. It combines transactional state management, asynchronous state transactions, operation-chain execution, concurrent state access, dual-mode scheduling, and dynamic restructuring. Evaluated on a 40-core machine and across four applications, it supports skewed and multi-partition workloads while maintaining state-of-the-art processing latency.

Database performance is compared across PostgreSQL, MySQL, Neo, RedisGraph, and other systems. PostgreSQL provides comparison results, implements a linear disk-I/O cost model, supports in-database analytics through MADlib, and hosts TSPDB. Its architecture has also been modified through comprehensive alteration schemes, with centralized logging identified as a source of transaction-latency variance.

The community also covers distributed transactions, replication, hardware heterogeneity, skewed requests, and workload-sensitive benchmarking. Systems including ChainifyDB, DGCC, Minos, Pyxis, Orthrus, and Elasticutor target higher throughput or reduced latency, while IoT and agricultural data streams motivate practical monitoring and analytics applications.

791a77e4e5cee46dd291fb28202db49b02617292.text:
## Community Report: Versioned Data, Linkage, and Analytical Querying

This community centers on three themes: versioned data systems, spatio-temporal entity linkage, and typed analytical querying.

**Forkbase** is a system for multi-version data that supports forkable applications and two variants of fork semantics. It integrates data versioning, provides efficient storage for blockchain applications, and demonstrates collaborative-analytics and wiki-engine applications. Blockchain applications may require tamper evidence. Forkbase introduces a novel index structure that efficiently identifies and eliminates duplicate content.

**ST-Link** implements a linkage model for matching spatio-temporal usage records belonging to the same real-world entity across services. Based on k-l diversity, it uses spatial and temporal filtering to reduce the matching space and sequential scans to avoid random disk access. It scales to large datasets, including records generated by location-enhanced services.

**Typed linear algebra** provides a unified representation and analytical-querying framework with strong type checking. LA diagrams express queries as paths, which the LA operator kernel extracts and executes; TPC-H supplies benchmark queries for evaluation.

Performance studies compare Forkbase with PostgreSQL and MySQL, evaluate typed linear algebra and ST-Link, and report advantages over keyword-based approaches for term-based similarity search and related-document search.

79e669fcffb8529911b3f1f97385a26c94a770f8.text:
## Information Retrieval, Interpretability, and Literary Search

This community spans information retrieval, online learning to rank, neural retrieval, and computational literary analysis. Ranking models support retrieval and are constructed with machine-learning and probabilistic methods. Online learning-to-rank methods include Dueling Bandit Gradient Descent (DBGD) and Pairwise Differentiable Gradient Descent (PDGD); PDGD substantially outperforms DBGD under ideal and worst-case conditions, challenging the applicability of DBGD’s theoretical bounds.

Neural IR re-ranking supports ad hoc search, but effectiveness and performance involve trade-offs. Query latency depends on encoding models, network architecture, and hardware acceleration. Trie-based pruning, self-normalized training, and mixed online/offline serving reduce inference or serving latency. LET’S MEASURE extends OSIRRC with performance measurement, including runtime.

Interpretability research examines neural retrieval models through DeepSHAP, which adapts DeepLIFT and estimates feature importance using Shapley values. Its explanations are compared with LIME and require a suitable reference input document. Beam search, simple trees, and explanation interfaces address faithfulness and human or algorithmic interpretability.

For literary computing, the Literary Theme Ontology supplies shared terminology and definitions for literary themes, supporting theme identification, media annotation, computational searching, and large literary corpora. Corpus indexing enables searching these collections, complementing close reading, literary theory, collaborative analysis, and algorithmic analysis.

Other work studies search behaviour and task relevance through log analysis, diary studies, and Android-app-based user studies. CMN NMF discovers stub communities from overlapping users and social relevance, with extensions based on user similarity.

6e3fcbeacc4bec0d25f062aeb04926a285844d8f.text:
## Distributed Social Networks and Social-Media Analytics

This community focuses on distributed online social networks (DOSNs) as alternatives to centralized OSN applications, addressing scalability and security concerns through decentralization and peer-to-peer (P2P) architectures. P2P networks support DOSN implementations including LifeSocial.KOM, Safebook, and PeerSoN. LifeSocial.KOM later evolved into LibreSocial, a fully functional DOSN that addresses the challenges of operating a completely decentralized social network.

Somabit is a system designed to scale across varying data volumes. It develops a distributed algorithm, uses big data technology, and applies MapReduce for distributed processing. Its analysis of social media data employs sentiment analysis, supporting knowledge discovery and contributing data sources for market analytics. Scalability is associated with MapReduce, Somabit, distributed algorithms, and DOSNs: MapReduce supports scalable processing, while Somabit and its distributed algorithm are designed to scale to any data volume.

3e3bdcb9c0f7f8cf507a6d52455359906b33f34f.text:
## Urban Networks, Mobility, Diffusion, and Ranking

This community links computational network analysis with urban sensing, human mobility, online diffusion, and ranking. **Chatty Maps** uses geo-referenced pictures and an urban sound dictionary to map perceived urban characteristics in London and Barcelona, while urban smellscape research connects odors, emotions, and restorative experiences. Aggregated mobile network data and mobile phone records reveal human activity, movement, temporal activity patterns, and floating populations; a visualization tool presents such data for London.

Diffusion research examines virality, message propagation, wording, emotions, and viral facets. Valence–arousal–dominance configurations help model emotional and viral effects, while spread metrics operationalize news virality. Related systems include online marketing and Pokémon Go, whose natural-experiment analysis found increased floating populations and pedestrian traffic.

Urban platform studies cover Airbnb demand and supply, municipal regulation, Uber, UberX, yellow taxis, ride-sharing, and taxi/delivery markets, emphasizing supply–demand matching and online/offline algorithms.

Ranking research addresses human judgment, flexible and classical statistical ranking models, generalized random utility models, fairness, and protected-group disadvantage. Interleaving and multi-dueling bandits support online ranker evaluation.

Graph methods include parallel graphlet counting, centrality measures such as time and k-path centrality, Kronecker product graph models, mixture models, and latent-state representations for large-scale and time-varying networks. Interlocking directorates are used to study national, transnational, and city-level organization of the global corporate elite.

07db828994f848184121b237b91cd7c95a9cf3e6.text:
## Community Report: Graph Analytics, Research Discovery, and Data Systems

This community connects graph structural similarity, community detection, knowledge graphs, crawling, and data management.

Structural similarity in graph data is measured using cosine, Dice, and Jaccard similarity, generalized edge clustering coefficients, automorphism groups, and maximal-clique-preserving mappings. These methods support knowledge discovery and network community detection. The SCORE method addresses community detection, while SCORE+ improves SCORE and shows significant gains on the polbooks, Simmons, and Caltech network datasets.

Knowledge graphs, including DBpedia and adaptive similarity networks, support knowledge discovery, knowledge-graph question answering, paper ranking, and paper recommendation. Etymo facilitates artificial-intelligence research through paper search, a graphical interface, and an adaptive similarity-based network of papers that learns from user feedback. AI research papers are a target dataset for search.

Source is an unsupervised social-media crawler that learns from page structure, builds sitemaps and navigation tables, and applies crawling policies to improve efficiency and focus on user-created content.

BigDatalog provides scalable, high-performance graph analytics on multicore systems and Apache Spark, outperforming GraphX implementations. Visual data management research, including DeepLens, combines dataflow query processing with deep-learning models, data-source semantics, query workloads, and automated physical design.

QA pipelines connect components whose performance is assessed through micro-evaluation, including collective failure cases, on DBpedia.

ce7b39dbcf5c79e200074d4944321861af2114ea.text:
## Graph Processing, Ranking, and Constraint-Aware Systems

This community covers scalable graph processing, graph-stream mining, anomaly explanation, rank-aware databases, and spatio-temporal access control.

**Lookout** explains anomalous behavior in time-evolving graphs by selecting a small number of pair plots under an explanation objective. It produces succinct, visually interpretable explanations for human analysts, scales linearly with graph edges, and offers approximation with optimality guarantees. It is evaluated on Enron email and DBLP coauthorship data and explains ground-truth anomalies in the LBNL computer network.

**GraphZip** is a scalable graph-stream-mining method inspired by Lempel–Ziv and dictionary-based compression. Using minimum description length, it discovers maximally compressing, interesting patterns in real-world and artificially generated graphs.

**StreetX** implements spatio-temporal access control over multiple arbitrary spatial regions and time windows using an abstract constraint language. Its prototype was tested on 10 million records; it resolves constraint conflicts automatically and jointly optimizes access control and query evaluation.

Other work studies graph-processing practice through an online survey of computations and software, emphasizing scalability, visualization, large graphs, and diverse graph entities.

The rank-aware database line defines ranked relations over totally ordered score structures, including ordinal containment, ordinal equivalence, and infimum aggregation. Relational calculus and Gödel logic preserve behavior under ordinal transformations, including top-k query results.

1701680436831a3e4727d5f4bfa05a1d60a5b00e.text:
## Approximate Graph Analytics and Music Information Systems

This community covers two related areas: scalable graph querying and computational music analysis.

For graph analytics, GRASP provides a solution for graph approximate query processing and creates GRASP summaries. These summaries support node group minimization and can be explored through a visualization plug-in. The framework addresses label-constrained reachability queries, including their aggregate form, counting label-constrained reachability queries. Graph DBMSs provide capabilities for evaluating these queries, while graph approximate query processing offers controllable error estimation and combines visualization with approximate analytics. Scalability is experimentally evaluated for GRASP. The work also concerns distributed databases, digital libraries, and an information-flow framework that organizes information in digital libraries, builds on an earlier information-flow approach, incorporates ontologies, and extends to first-order logic.

The music strand addresses genre classification, pattern extraction, and artist disambiguation. A music genre classifier uses a MIDI corpus containing over 40,000 genre-annotated files; genre-specific patterns represent pieces for classifier training and evaluation. Repeating-pattern identification extracts patterns from symbolically encoded music using pattern-extraction algorithms. For artist analysis, metric learning learns artist embeddings directly from audio, uses a new negative-sampling method incorporating music genre as side information, and supports unknown-artist clustering and audio-only artist disambiguation. An alternative approach learns embeddings using artist classifiers.

5c8cfc1b362e715ce1d84adcda57d86cab90857d.text:
## Fides: Auditable Transactions on Untrusted Infrastructure

This community centers on **Fides**, an auditable data management system designed to reside completely on **untrusted infrastructure**, such as third-party servers. Fides uses **TFCommit** to manage transactions and employs **tamper-resistant logs**, supported by cryptographic techniques, to detect malicious failures.

**TFCommit** is an atomic commitment protocol that executes transactions across multiple servers in an untrusted environment. It avoids the need for expensive **Byzantine replication**, providing an alternative approach to transaction coordination under potentially unreliable infrastructure.

The main themes are trustworthy and auditable data management, transaction atomicity, malicious-failure detection, and operation across external servers. Fides’s experimental evaluation demonstrates **scalability** and relatively low **overhead**, highlighting performance considerations alongside its security and auditing mechanisms.

690e5c58d0ad6cb09149a6aac78393171422d86b.text:
## Blockchain Interoperability, Consensus, and Provenance

This community centers on blockchain systems, cross-blockchain interoperability, and provenance management.

**Cross-blockchain transactions (CBT)** enable transactions across multiple blockchains and must preserve ACID properties. CBT is a distributed commit protocol that extends two-phase commit, uses heartbeat mechanisms to ensure liveness, and provides a graphical interface for monitoring transaction status. Distributed commit protocols target scalable transaction processing, while CBT demonstrates high, linear scalability and low overhead. Reliance on a centralized component is described as incompatible with practical scalability.

**GeoBFT** is a geo-scale Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus protocol implemented in the ResilientDB blockchain and database fabric. It supports consensus across geographically distributed replicas through topology-aware grouping and local consensus parallelization. Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus maintains common state despite faulty or malicious replicas and is also used by resilient database systems.

The provenance theme includes Why Provenance and Why Not Provenance. Provenance summarization addresses the large size and usability challenges of Why Not Provenance, producing approximate summaries that balance completeness, informativeness, and conciseness. Provenance patterns encode provenance concisely, while sampling techniques improve scalability during provenance capture and summarization. Blockchain is additionally linked to disinformation mitigation.

f2a8b4b175b99b3d7ddf7d34544e96069a8b7256.text:
## Company Profiling from Employee Perspectives

This community centers on **company profiling**, using employee-generated information alongside traditional financial sources. **Online employment services** provide employee ratings and textual comments, while **employee reviews** offer textual evidence for profiling. Traditional sources include **finance reports** and **SEC filings**.

The key method is **CPCTR**, a company profiling approach based on **collaborative topic regression**. CPCTR jointly models textual employee reviews and salary information to learn **latent structural patterns** of companies. These patterns support two related tasks: **opinion analysis**, by helping identify positive and negative opinions, and **salary prediction**, through latent variables that influence salaries.

Overall, the community links employee reviews, salaries, and financial reporting within a unified framework for learning company profiles and analyzing organizational opinions and compensation.

ca68e4d5b5b70712ddf0ca9cf79770647b169800.text:
## Scalable Streaming, Parsing, and Event Analytics

This community focuses on high-throughput stream processing, memory systems, parsing, and process mining. TStream is a shared-memory multicore stream-processing system with transactional state management, asynchronous state transaction processing, batched state accesses, and an operation-chain execution model. Evaluated on a 40-core machine, it improves throughput and scalability with limited latency penalty, particularly for stateful and windowed operations.

StreamBox HBM is a stream-analytics engine for hybrid memory combining DDR4 and HBM DRAM. It uses HBM-resident key-pointer arrays and sequential-access sorting for grouping, achieving 110 million records per second and 238 GB/s memory bandwidth on all 64 cores of Intel Knights Landing.

AOMG provides workload-driven approximate quantiles over temporal windows. It uses subwindow summaries, frequent-value summarization, tail-value retention, and compression, achieving less than 5% relative value error.

ParPaRaw performs massively parallel finite-state-machine parsing of delimiter-separated data on GPUs, supporting bulk loading, in-situ querying, and stream processing. It exploits PCIe full-duplex transfers, reaching 14.2 GB/s parsing throughput.

The community also covers benchmarking Apache Flink and Apache Storm using open-world, online-gaming-inspired workloads; streaming telemetry quantiles; and process mining with Prom 6, including discovery, conformance checking, and machine learning on event data. Dataframes and columnar storage are proposed to improve scalability.

f46011573d4310800e5f9c7f4fde3274bb89ed2e.text:
### Scalable Local Community Detection with LOCEC

This community centers on **LOCEC**, a method for local community detection. LOCEC uses a two-phase process: it first applies **local community detection**, followed by **community classification**. The method addresses sparsity in both **relationship features** and **relationship labels**, highlighting challenges in representing and classifying network relationships.

LOCEC supports large-scale processing through **parallel and distributed processing**. It is evaluated on the real-world **WeChat network**, a social network associated with the **WeChat** platform. Thus, the community links a scalable detection and classification method with relationship-oriented metrics and labels, distributed execution, and evaluation on a social-network dataset.

6b514a58daa498c9c544376bbd6cc814a37785e5.text:
## Community Report: Network Structure, Dynamics, and Measurement

This community studies complex networks, their statistical structure, and the flows and interactions they represent in social, biological, transportation, mobility, and information systems. Power-law distributions, scaling exponents, lognormal distributions, degree heterogeneity, hubs, and high-degree nodes are recurring themes. Studies address power-law verification, fitting, binning effects, and background models, while noting that stochastic Kronecker graph models may fail to generate power-law or lognormal distributions and may produce many isolated vertices.

Key network-generation systems include the domi-join model, which uses join operations and dominating sets, and enhanced stochastic Kronecker models for massive graph generation and the Graph500 benchmark. Directed-network methods include reduced Google matrices for hidden-link discovery and influence analysis, middleman robustness, edge-balance ratios, and measurement frameworks using link-, node-, and cascade-based estimators. Sampling bias is addressed through approximate importance sampling.

Community-detection methods identify cohesive, overlapping, two-mode, and hierarchically nested communities while accounting for edge direction. Network-flow research models memory, maps flows, and examines intermediary substitutability. Applications include friendship and voting networks, political leaders, terrorist networks, global mobility, tourism, humanitarian and development efforts, and event-related Twitter activity.

c16e5b079b960e459cbff42569280f41ddb424c7.text:
## Graph-Based Ranking, Diffusion, and Social Data Analytics

This community connects network diffusion, recommendation, ranking, and social-media-based detection.

**Contextual centrality** models diffusion processes while incorporating structural positions, nodal contributions, cascade payoff, diffusion rate, and diffusion period. It can approximate eigenvector centrality when diffusion is prolonged and the product of diffusion rate and largest eigenvalue exceeds one. Its adoption predictions are evaluated on microfinance adoption in Indian villages and weather insurance in Chinese villages. Homophily, often associated with friendship, links network structure to cascade payoff, particularly when \(p \times \lambda_1 < 1\).

**Recommendation systems** use ranking, user similarity, and user congruity. Friendship and social relations inform similarity, while ratings and comments indicate agreement; incorporating congruity improves recommendation performance. **Seq2slate**, a recurrent sequence-to-sequence method, performs slate optimization by selecting and ordering items while accounting for item interactions, and is evaluated on ranking benchmarks using average precision and Kendall’s tau.

The community also covers **ADR mention extraction**, where recurrent neural networks and co-training process 0.1M tweets for adverse drug reaction surveillance. Finally, a mathematical optimization framework integrates network structure information with content modeling to support human trafficking detection, using social media platforms and social sensors and evaluated on a human trafficking dataset.

bcc90bb07f142a74c7e51a553918f2dbf4883f5c.text:
## Community Report: Dynamic Recommendation, Graph Analytics, and Bias

This community centers on recommender systems, personalization, and graph-based modeling. Popularity bias gives popular items disproportionate exposure, affects user groups differently, and may contribute to miscalibration; greater popularity-bias amplification tends to produce greater miscalibration relative to true user preferences. Time-aware personalized popularity addresses temporal dynamics by combining global popularity with local popularity among user neighbors, and achieves competitive result accuracy against model-based collaborative approaches. Item popularity is also reported as a strong accuracy baseline.

Several systems address recommendation dynamics and sparse data. A dynamic graph attention network models changing user behavior and context-dependent social influence, dynamically inferring influencers from current interests. RELINE embeds multiple relational graphs into a shared latent space using network embeddings, capturing geographical proximity, temporal influence, and user preference dynamics, and is evaluated for cold-start effectiveness. A user-profile feature-based approach uses feature scores derived from user-item interactions and is evaluated on MovieLens 100K.

DBRec combines latent group discovery and hierarchical modeling to learn compact user and item representations. Deep likelihood models estimate selectivity in relational tables by approximating joint distributions without independence assumptions, using Monte Carlo integration for wildcard and range queries. Public-private graph research applies incremental k-truss discovery, with node and edge insertion strategies evaluated on real-world datasets. A human-centric data economy compensates users contributing data to online streaming services.

f75911f888e87bfeaed861fca40d11f0ab2695a4.text:
## Directed Networks, Flows, and Large-Scale Network Modeling

This community centers on directed and complex networks, their structure, measurement, and dynamics. Directed networks represent friendship networks and support edge selection, in-degree analysis, balance measurement, sampling, and middleman analysis. Middleman power and robustness concern intermediaries that broker network flows, while node contestability addresses whether such intermediaries can be substituted.

Community analysis includes a method for cohesive and two-mode communities that accounts for edge direction, overlap, and hierarchical nesting. A measurement framework combines link-tracing sampling with link-, node-, and cascade-based estimators, outperforming BFS and random-walk sampling on link-based characteristics. Approximate importance sampling corrects sampling bias through reweighting.

Power-law and lognormal distributions are used to characterize in-degree, interactivity time, social sensors, and edge-balance profiles; binning can make lognormal data appear power-law-like. The domi-join model studies scale-free, edge-bound growing networks using dominating sets and join operations.

Stochastic Kronecker graph models support massive graph generation and the Graph500 benchmark, though they may produce isolated vertices and fail to generate power-law or lognormal distributions. Network flows model the movement of ideas, information, and activity in social and biological systems. Mobility applications include Twitter-based global mobility estimates and base-station traffic influence ranking.

23a0d6b4112247a20087ed84ed84b20eee7a5e49.text:
## Social Security, Misinformation, and Distributed Consistency

This community focuses on detecting malicious accounts, containing misinformation, and securing information exchange in online social networks. Fake profiles include compromised profiles, cloned profiles, and online bots, often established by cyber criminals; cyber laws aim to mitigate these threats.

Spambot detection distinguishes social spambots from genuine accounts using social fingerprinting, similarity measures, digital DNA sequences, and DNA analysis techniques. Digital DNA encodes account behavior as character sequences, while behavioral modeling captures account lifetimes. Both supervised and unsupervised detection are supported.

Misinformation containment addresses rumor spreading through competing campaigns and multi-cascade diffusion with cascade priority. Blockchain-based sequential algorithms, built on blockchain technology and using virtual information credits, are intended to avoid rapid, intense rumor spread; simulation and experimental evaluation assess their effectiveness. Blockchain is also embedded in trusted social networks, which employ decentralized contracts and motivate trust networks. Secure information exchange contracts protect peer-to-peer exchanges.

A separate systems theme concerns data consistency. A data consistency simulation tool models workloads and database behavior, measures consistency, and detects violations under network partition. The CAP theorem describes consistency tradeoffs, while ACID represents stronger guarantees. Misinformation containment also has conditional inapproximability results based on NP and DTIME assumptions, limiting certain polynomial-time approximation guarantees.

17938c8ce80259a92b3e29642da9852952f84f92.text:
## Fake Health News Detection and Explainable Recommendation

This community centers on **fake health news detection**, motivated by the threat fake health news poses to **public health**. The **FakeHealth** dataset supports this task with rich **news content**, news reviews containing detailed explanations, social engagement data, and a user-user social network. More generally, fake news detection uses news content and abundant social engagements as evidence, while explainability is required for health-specific detection methods. Exploratory analysis examines FakeHealth’s characteristics and validates its quality.

A second theme is **recommendation**, including recommender systems for resources with limited capacity. An **autoencoder-based recommender system** uses an autoencoder for representation learning. An **explainable recommendation system** likewise uses an autoencoder and explains predictions through a neighborhood-based explanation style, supporting explainable recommendations and potentially influencing user trust.

The community also covers **relationship classification**, which maps user relationships to predefined real-world social connection types and supports recommendation applications and social advertising. Overall, the entities connect dataset-based health misinformation research with representation learning, explainable recommendation, social-network analysis, and trust-aware recommender systems.

b8b74327c4442142e51a2e04d5e9250bfcd7fde3.text:
## Community Report: Scalable Influence and Trust in Social Graphs

This community studies social-network influence, graph representation, trust, and data-quality systems.

**Influence maximization** selects *k* influential seeds for viral marketing in online social networks and multiplexes. QuickIM delivers state-of-the-art result quality while running one to three orders of magnitude faster, using one to two orders of magnitude less memory, and achieving the \(\Omega(n)\) space lower bound; its performance is independent of influence probabilities. EasyIM is an exception to its memory advantage. In multiplexes, overlapping users connect layers with heterogeneous diffusion models. ISF provides a \(1-1/e\) approximation, while KSN runs computations in parallel using a single-layer \(\alpha\)-approximation algorithm. Multi-round influence maximization supports non-adaptive and adaptive settings: cross-round and within-round greedy methods address the former, while adaptive algorithms approximate the adaptive optimum. Reverse influence sampling enables near-linear running time.

**Graph embedding** is represented by GEMSEC, which jointly learns node clusters and embeddings, minimizes negative log likelihood, and uses clustering constraints that improve representation quality.

**Trust and safety** include a Social IoT trust model with trustor, trustee, evaluation, transfer, transitivity, and updates, validated experimentally. Social-network honeypots use artificial profiles for malicious-activity detection. ProfileGen creates realistic professional profiles from education and employment records. A risk model uses human labels to prioritize risky machine-labeled instances, improving entity-resolution quality under fixed human cost.

8aa0100190b6f29730c495e587d8fb236d53a64e.text:
## Crowdsourcing, Trust, and Stream-Based Knowledge Systems

This community centers on crowdsourcing as a social machine and human–machine network, leveraging the wisdom of crowds and information workers for search, annotation, literature review, paper screening, dictionary access, mathematical practice, and jury selection. Amazon Mechanical Turk, crowdsourcing platforms, QurK, and phased crowdsourcing support these workflows, while contribution quality, answer correctness, and audience skepticism provide evaluation measures.

Trust is a second major theme. Trust models, three-valued subjective logic, weighted links, and trustable paths support participant recruitment, social IoT interaction, and trustworthy crowds. The trust-based recruitment framework uses multi-hop friendship relations, a suggestion component, and trustable paths to select participants; jury-selection research addresses altruistic and paid users through exact, greedy, and bounding algorithms.

Stream systems emphasize complex event processing, real-time and persistent streams, event-pattern detection, adaptive query processing, load shedding, and workload balancing. Crowdsourced stream processing and the CSP design framework combine human workers with stream computation.

Other topics include content-based retrieval and raster image indexing; scholarly infrastructure using DOI, Crossref API, ResourceSync, and article ingest; and network analysis through TwitterTrails, retweet networks, generalized two-mode cores, and trustable paths. Mathematical practice connects MathOverflow, symbolic computation, crowdsourced collaboration, and the production of mathematical knowledge.

e8fda9b47460bed0418ab80e7d10fc2ef1674f87.text:
### Crowdsourcing, Trust, and Adaptive Data Systems

This community centers on human–machine collaboration, crowdsourcing, and systems that combine human judgment with computational processing. Crowdsourcing is framed as a social machine that leverages the wisdom of crowds, including through Amazon Mechanical Turk, information workers, and participatory agents. Applications include mathematical practice and knowledge production, jury selection, dictionary accessibility, motion-capture annotation, social-media classification, and crowdsourced stream processing.

Trust is central to recruiting and evaluating contributors. A trust-based recruitment framework uses multi-hop friendship relations, trustable paths, weighted links, and a suggestion component to select trustworthy participants. Jury selection addresses altruistic and paid users through exact and greedy algorithms, with bounding techniques reducing jury-error calculations. Contribution quality, answer correctness, and individual or jury error rates support quality assurance.

Stream-processing systems address event-pattern detection, classification, and load shedding. The CSP design framework and AIDR combine crowdsourcing with stream processing, achieving higher classification accuracy than pure stream processing while reducing manual effort. Query processing also includes adaptive, hybrid, and cost-based optimization.

Other themes include information retrieval and scholarly infrastructure. Adaptive distributional ranking detects collection-specific term distributions and is evaluated on TREC. Content-based retrieval uses feature extraction, synthesis, semantic labeling, and query execution. Big scholarly data platforms support scholarly-resource management, while CrossRef, ResourceSync, and HTTP response headers enable preservation automation. Twittertrails analyzes rumor propagation, refutation, burst activity, networks, and audience skepticism.

a51bd990a2eccf8410b4414ebf937049a15ea4a8.text:
## Wikipedia, Knowledge Bases, and Networked Knowledge

This community centers on Wikipedia and related knowledge infrastructures. Wikipedia is treated as a large general-purpose knowledge base, collective memory, social sensor, and site of large-scale collaboration. Its multilingual editions—including English, Chinese, German, and Russian—support studies of browsing behavior, multilingualism, article access, editing, literature, and reader motivations.

A major theme is structured knowledge and entity-oriented retrieval. Wikidata provides nationality and occupation attributes, supports vandalism detection, and is monitored alongside Wikipedia. Knowledge bases contain triples, inference rules, set-valued predicates, and query-oriented representations; they support entity retrieval, relationship explanation, dialogue, recommendation, and knowledge-base question answering. Completeness and correctness are explicit evaluation metrics, while negative statements remain underrepresented.

The community also examines Wikipedia’s social and information networks: hyperlink, revision, co-occurrence, norm, user-interest, mathematician, and biographical networks. Methods include motif analysis, centrality, lag analysis, fuzzy matching, neural attention, linear models, and spatial-preferred-attachment models. Systems such as GalaxySearch, REX, Wikipedia Live Monitor, article recommendation systems, and semantic content classifiers operationalize these ideas.

Applications include vandalism and Tor-edit monitoring, article-quality evaluation, related-topic navigation, entity-oriented search, event detection, geopolitical and mobility analysis, rumor spreading, and electoral analysis using page views.

a2c04963b0b6f6d0a918ee8a39402a1f9defc2bd.text:
### Wikipedia-Centered Knowledge, Retrieval, and Collaboration

This community centers on Wikipedia and Wikidata as collaborative knowledge infrastructures. Wikipedia contains multilingual articles, tables, biographies, categories, discussion threads, revision histories, SQL/XML dumps, server logs, and access data; Wikidata provides a structured, collaborative knowledge base with person records and bibliographic links to Scholia. Both support real-time edit monitoring and vandalism detection.

Major research topics include information retrieval, semantic representation, and recommendation. Word2vec, GloVe, fastText, skip-gram, local/global embeddings, singular value decomposition, and generic or document-specific language models support semantic modeling. Systems and tasks include GalaxySearch, entity trivia extraction, article recommendation, related-topic navigation, sub-article matching, namespace discovery, table matching, Tablenet, and table interlinking.

The community also studies collaboration and social structure through revision networks, user-interest networks, semantic networks, motif analysis, induced triads, norm networks, and biographical social networks. Trust models, trust-based recruitment, contribution blocking, and Wikidata vandalism detection address reliability and governance.

Multilingual editions—including English, Chinese, German, and Russian Wikipedia—enable comparison of editing and browsing behavior, content diffusion, multilingualism, and cultural perspectives. Wikipedia data additionally supports research on emerging entities, collective memory, mobility, elections, news lag, social sensors, and online information seeking.

e4d96acb0213198ef3e6cbf26924937a0f4a2862.text:
## Keyword Extraction and Cyber Threat Event Analysis

This community links text information extraction, keyword extraction, title construction, and cyber threat event analysis.

For cyber threat event detection, unsupervised machine learning identifies novel events—previously non-extant events—and developing events related to previously detected events. Detected events are ranked using importance scores, with detection error rate as an evaluation metric. Keywords and named entities contribute to event importance scoring, while user influence weights noun phrases.

Text information extraction extracts informative tweet terms characterized as keywords or named entities for event detection. Keyword extraction includes a supervised keyword extraction model trained with graph-based features derived from graph-of-text representations.

A title construction system supports semi-automatic title construction from scientific abstracts. It extracts and recommends keywords, which are hypothesized as candidates for constructing titles and are evaluated by comparison with title words. The system achieves 82% macro-averaged precision.

d22ce243f8b8209c23a9c8fff07523f4e5b4b91c.text:
### Interactive Recommendation and Explainable Knowledge-Graph Fact Checking

This community connects two themes: interactive recommendation and knowledge-graph-based fact checking.

The query-based interactive recommender system transforms feedback-based recommendation into a retrieval task. It generates personalized questions from an automatically constructed query pool, using user feedback to improve recommendations. Query recommendation retrieves candidate queries and ranks them with an adapted attention GRU. The system was deployed on the Taobao App homepage, evaluated through offline and online experiments on Taobao, and released with the Taobao dataset. Online A/B testing supports evaluation.

The fact-checking theme evaluates claims using knowledge graphs, including DBpedia, and models checking as probabilistic inference. This enables efficient claim labeling and interpretable explanations. Explainable fact checking uses reference information from knowledge graphs to produce explanations for decisions. GReASE is a generative model for relevance search that learns hidden, user-defined relevance semantics and uses graph-based patterns and manually defined meta paths. Meta paths characterize relationships between query and answer entities; answer entities are constrained by their properties. GReASE advances expressiveness and effectiveness.

Selective data cleaning supports fact checking by choosing numerical quantities to clean. It optimizes non-linear objectives such as minimizing uncertainty or maximizing surprise, using optimization algorithms. Data fishing can bias selective fact checking, while data errors contribute to uncertainty in claims.

65e4b77b2ac26daef20c7922822a9d9dcd014889.text:
## Community Report: Precision–Recall Methods Across Entity, Graph, and Multimedia Tasks

This community centers on evaluating and improving precision, recall, false positives, false negatives, workload, and computational cost across information-processing tasks.

Entity resolution is a major theme, including incremental resolution from linked documents, query-driven and multiple-source resolution, candidate generation and pruning, blocking schemes, and heuristic author-name disambiguation. Locality-sensitive hashing methods—including BayesLSH, FastCoveringLSH, LSH-S, and unsupervised triplet hashing—support similarity estimation and candidate retrieval; BayesLSH provides probabilistic recall guarantees. Multi-partite max-weight matching improves matching precision and recall by exploiting multiple sources. Active learning, transfer learning, distance-metric learning, and bootstrapping address labeling and similarity learning.

Other work covers change-point, emerging-event, and sub-story detection; size-agnostic change-point detection is assessed using precision and recall on streams. Network-structure inference uses degree-corrected stochastic block models, dense-cluster discovery, and core-and-peel methods, with precision and recall evaluated on network datasets.

Multimedia and recommendation topics include image retrieval/classification, ontology-driven visual concept detection, music tagging/classification, content-based recommendation, and app-installation prediction. Quality-control frameworks enforce precision/recall requirements, while approximate algorithms, query-driven methods, candidate triage, and adaptive pruning manage query workload and computational cost.

ff870d9db1609dab5b2f6142d815556861b063b0.text:
## Recommendation, Retrieval, and Adaptive Learning

This community spans recommendation, search, and cross-modal retrieval, addressing information overload and information seeking. Recommendation systems model user–item interactions, perform rating prediction, personalized ranking, and explanation generation. The explainable recommender system uses a neural network to combine rating-score prediction with explanatory words and achieves lower RMSE than traditional methods; feature engineering improves rating prediction.

NeuRec is a neural-network recommendation model integrating nonlinear transformations with latent factors. Its user-based and item-based variants focus on corresponding aspects of the interaction matrix and are evaluated for personalized ranking.

Deep reinforcement learning supports recommendation, search, and online advertising. The DRR framework models recommendation as sequential decision making, explicitly represents interactions through a state-representation module, adapts dynamically, and optimizes long-term rewards. It uses an actor–critic scheme and real-time feedback, with offline and online evaluation. Hyperparameter optimization across recommendation datasets considers negative sampling distribution, number of epochs, subsampling parameter, and window size.

Cross-modal retrieval learns joint audio–visual embeddings in a common feature space, projecting audio and visual features for cross-modal search. Nearest-neighbor search over learned track embeddings supports retrieval, evaluated by Recall@K on a YouTube-8M subset. Self-supervised learning uses the dataset’s large-scale video data.

fc8d600d6f92489611a658e5f264d4706494d734.text:
## Community Report: Graph Analytics, Prediction, and Reproducible Systems

This community spans graph analytics, fraud detection, user modeling, recommendation, and repository forecasting.

**TigerGraph** provides GSQL for SQL-compatible and NoSQL programming, expresses iterative graph algorithms in bulk-synchronous-processing terms, and supports massively parallel query and analytics computation. Benchmarks demonstrate strong scale-up and scale-out performance.

For suspicious entity group detection, **SliceNDice** efficiently extracts groups using a suspiciousness metric based on abnormal synchronicity across multiple graph views. This multi-view graph-mining approach represents attribute similarity and supports applications including payment fraud, false-information, and Sybil-account detection. SliceNDice was evaluated on Snapchat’s advertiser ecosystem, where it produced real fraud-ring discoveries.

**ClusChurn**, developed and evaluated on anonymous Snapchat data, clusters new users using platform activities and ego-network structures, identifies interpretable user types, and predicts churn in a real-time data analysis pipeline. Attention mechanisms model activity correlations, while LSTM sequence modeling is used for churn and cross-repository forecasting; ARIMA has higher accuracy for some time-series predictions.

On GitHub, repository popularity prediction forecasts fork and watch events. GitHub also provides benchmark data and a laboratory for studying diffusion of innovation.

Finally, **DeepRec** is a Python/TensorFlow, GPL-licensed, extensible deep-learning recommender system supporting rating prediction. Publicly shared systems and data sharing address reproducibility.

96ad7b2942fde2b9a28becf88805b3666e15338e.text:
### Diversity, Recommendation, and Adversarial Attacks

This community examines how **recommendation systems**, particularly in **news services**, shape information selection, user behavior, and diversity. Redundant recommendations can create **filter bubbles**, while strengthening users’ most-interesting categories may reduce diversity. An **article selection model** studies behavioral changes and is verified against **target data**, with **non-recommendation** serving as a comparison condition.

Diversity is analyzed through three components: **variety**, **balance**, and **disparity**, and is linked to **interdisciplinarity**, **knowledge diffusion**, and **knowledge integration**. **Rao–Stirling diversity** measures interdisciplinarity, combines variety and balance, and decomposes into disparity; its unresolved combination of variety and balance motivates **dual concept diversity**. The **new diversity indicator**, **relative variety**, and **DIV diversity indicator** operationalize these components independently. DIV diversity further distinguishes interdisciplinary knowledge integration and knowledge diffusion in citing patterns. The **Gini coefficient** indicates balance but not variety.

The community also studies **adversarial recommendation attacks**. An **adversarial fake user generator** creates fake profiles designed to resemble real users and match their rating distributions. A **repeated general-sum game** models the recommendation system and fake-user generator as opposing players. **Attack intent** can target **top-K recommendation quality**, while machine-learned adversarial attacks provide the methodological basis.

71197b182386f7561789c02b3788dadf75359b7b.text:
## Entity Resolution, Similarity Search, and Evaluation

This community centers on entity resolution, similarity search, and methods for evaluating retrieval and matching quality. Entity resolution identifies and merges records representing the same real-world entity. Its workflows use blocking and blocking schemes for candidate generation, followed by weighted bipartite or multipartite maximum-weight matching. Query-driven and incremental entity resolution support resolution in response to queries or linked documents, while transfer learning, active learning, and crowd workers address labeling and cost–quality trade-offs. Multiple-source resolution exploits cross-source information.

Locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) supports efficient candidate generation, near-neighbor reporting, and all-pairs similarity search with sublinear query time. BayesLSH and BayesLSH Lite provide probabilistic similarity estimation or candidate pruning; LSH hash tables, LSH-SS, FastCoveringLSH, and distance filtering address search efficiency and false negatives. Query workload, query time, computational cost, and shuffling cost are recurring concerns.

Precision, recall, false positives, and false negatives quantify system behavior and their trade-offs. These metrics evaluate schema reconciliation, authorship classification, recommendation, event and sub-story detection, network inference, image and concept detection, and urban deprivation classification. Bayes networks achieve higher precision and recall than approximate functional dependencies for query reformulation, while discriminative information retrieval and concept augmentation improve recall.

6887c483dade29056aa6083f309cf101efb78f79.text:
## Community Report: Reinforcement Learning, Advertising, and Constraint-Aware Modeling

This community centers on intelligent recommendation and online advertising, alongside constraint-based data quality and improved text classification.

For product recommendation, **UCB-RS** enhances the upper confidence bound algorithm for non-stationary multi-armed bandits and large state spaces. It reportedly outperforms epsilon-greedy, UCB1, and EXP3, and is used within recommendation systems. Online advertising applies reinforcement learning to determine ad selection, interpolation, and placement. A **deep Q-network** jointly makes these decisions, while advertising strategies balance advertising revenue with user experience. Two-time-scale reinforcement learning is proposed for non-convex influence optimization and is compared with stochastic-gradient-descent schemes; an additional algorithm addresses dimensionality challenges.

A second theme concerns classification and data validation. **Correlation-adjusted naïve Bayes** improves accuracy over traditional naïve Bayes, incorporates class correlation through a correlation factor, and is evaluated on real-world data. It addresses text classification, where naïve Bayes estimators are widely used but perform poorly on small training datasets; paragraph vectors and sparse representations are also associated with classification.

The **Coded** system performs data-error detection using statistical constraints. Domain knowledge can be expressed through logical or statistical constraints, including denial constraints and functional dependencies, enforcing statistical independence or dependence and supporting downstream statistical modeling.

dd3b61ede7b8a71a4871f3250662b471c7b970ee.text:
## Community Report: Contextual Recommendation, Privacy, and Counterfactual Search

This community links recommendation, information seeking, and privacy-preserving personalization.

**Recommendation and visual information seeking:** The content-based image recommendation system uses visual cues and bookmarks, and is evaluated on WikiArt and a Pinterest image collection. It supports image recommendation during information seeking, where visual cues provide information scent under the information scent model and information foraging theory. NAIRS is an interpretable neural recommendation system using a self-attention network; attention weights represent the importance of interacted items and produce user profiles. Personalized recommendation also uses latent factor models, tree-structured regularization, user profiles, and inferred sensitive attributes.

**Contextual and behavioral modeling:** A context-aware embedding model for product search models short- and long-term context and outperforms word-based context-aware models using commercial search logs. Short-term context captures current hidden intent and improves promotion on later result pages. Implicit feedback, including clicks and other behavioral signals, supports re-ranking and personalization but is confounded by presentation bias.

**Causal search evaluation:** Propensity estimation uses intervention data harvested from historic feedback logs. Position-based models provide consistent estimates, while the extremum estimator is evaluated in ArXiv Full-text Search and Google Drive Search. Counterfactual learning-to-rank addresses presentation bias given observation propensities.

**Narrative and privacy:** Character-network extraction and analysis support summarization, role detection, retrieval, and recommendation over fictional works. Aegis provides multifaceted privacy by preserving public persona attributes while obfuscating sensitive ones through topic, hashtag, and post suggestions.

716a6c1989d1f337f75f79abed4b6b178fbfa7dc.text:
## Community Report: Semantic Search, Web Annotation, and Visual Graph Analytics

This community connects semantic data publishing, search evaluation, scientific knowledge modeling, and graph-based analysis. Schema.org provides vocabulary, types, and subsets for structured web data, semantic annotations, and scalable publishing. These annotations support online visibility for touristic service providers, intelligent applications, executable scientific papers, and content commons; Semantify It supports their creation and distribution.

Web annotation research includes Hypothes.is, the Open Annotation data model, annotation-target archiving, and reconstruction or retrieval against archived web-resource versions. Search-engine studies compare Google, Yahoo, Bing, and other production systems using retrieval-effectiveness tests, relevance judgments, correct-answer rates, result descriptions, and agreement in top results. Google and Bing show high agreement, while Google reports a 95.3% navigational correct-answer rate versus Bing’s 76.6%. Search aspects, query operators, neural networks, and flexible operator embeddings support retrieval and preference prediction.

SemNet builds semantic networks from 750,000 scientific papers, representing physical concepts and predicting quantum-physics research trends. Visual analytics and VDMS provide human-in-the-loop exploration of large visual datasets and metadata graphs, including financial-risk networks. Temporal graph indexing and adaptive labeling address reachability and time-based graph queries. Blocking and view-driven deduplication support scalable data cleaning, including Yahoo’s movies and restaurants datasets.

166000395682eec8ae7b1ff2c88f8d444d0fd36b.text:
## Anna: Elastic, Policy-Driven Cloud Storage

Anna is an extension of a distributed key-value store into an elastic, multi-tier cloud storage service. It organizes storage into vertical tiers with different cost–performance tradeoffs and provides horizontal elasticity, adding or removing nodes in response to load dynamics. A policy engine coordinates these mechanisms and balances service-level objectives, including latency, fault tolerance, and cost.

Anna uses multi-master selective replication, targeting hot keys. Together, these methods support configurable management of storage behavior across changing workloads.

The associated deployment architecture provides modeling capability without significant latency impact and executes a neural network model. It is deployed in a real-world production search system, where the modular solution supports productionization and can realize recent gains from neural networks.

88002f484b1b6f339ddbe9ebefb0ed409a8e757d.text:
### Community Report: Retrieval, Incomplete Data, and Dynamic Networks

This community spans information retrieval, multimedia analysis, database theory, and epidemic-network modeling.

Image retrieval uses nearest-neighbor query processing, global image descriptors, and compact hashing methods, including extremely low-bit, multi-head asymmetric, and deep discrete supervised hashing. An instance-search system evaluates performance with mAP; multi-head asymmetric hashing reaches 94.4% mAP with 8-bit codes. Unsupervised triplet hashing produces 32–256-bit binary hashes using stacked restricted Boltzmann machines and triplet networks.

Text retrieval includes SS4MCT statistical stemming, affix and infix detection, and unsupervised formation matching for morphologically complex, multilingual text, including English–Persian CLIR. Named entities are represented through aliases, entity classes, identifiers, and generalized vector-space models. Smartphone screenshots are preprocessed, OCR-processed with Tesseract, and indexed for text extraction and health-intervention studies.

Other work addresses music classification and tagging with deep convolutional neural networks, while label noise affects tag performance. Incomplete-database research studies counting completions and valuations for self-join-free conjunctive queries, Codd tables, and approximation complexity.

Network research models direct and indirect interactions through SPDT and synthetic graph models, supporting epidemic forecasting. OJC performs source localization under partial observations using candidate selection and Jordan covers. Layered networks and Kalman prediction reduce error, while cascade reconstruction uses Steiner-tree sampling.

cf499345b9b11110e4f4abd880a9d083ee977585.text:
## Session-Based Recommendation and Evaluation

This community centers on session-based recommendation, next-item prediction, and the relationship between offline and online recommender-system evaluation. Session-based recommendation models item interactions as session graphs and predicts the next item from sequences of user–item interactions.

**Neta** is proposed for session-based recommendation. It uses neighborhood retrieval to retrieve similar sessions and capture collaborative information, while guided attention extracts collaborative representations. Neta also incorporates a time-aware mechanism to model temporal recency and uses co-attention to weight complementary collaborative representations. Co-attention additionally determines representation importance for next-item prediction.

Offline evaluation traditionally uses next-item prediction and aims to reliably estimate online performance; its results serve as a proxy for online evaluation. Bandit feedback can improve this process: it includes shown recommendations and whether users clicked them, enabling offline estimates that more accurately reflect online performance. In contrast, online evaluation measures the effect of recommending an item as a causal intervention.
