Network structures include core-periphery and star networks, while incomplete information can produce persistent hub-and-spokes or connected networks.

Information-sharing research examines anonymity, bias, user equality, exposure, and connection establishment. Anonymity grids, distance sums, and generalized distance sums provide analytical tools. Social signals increase information spread likelihood and propagation speed; originality, retention, and production coefficients measure sharing behavior.

Knowledge diffusion is modeled through multilayer diffusion, event-based, and generative information-sharing methods. Knowledge diaspora analysis traces research-interest flows: physics and medicine mainly act as sources, while material science, chemical engineering, immunology, microbiology, and environmental science act as sinks.

Scholarly infrastructure includes AMiner-integrated unified frameworks, CWTS classification, direct citation analysis, and breakthrough-paper detection using micro-clusters, CSS rankings, citation filtering, and diffusion. MOOC datasets and forum activities support performance prediction, competence development, and social-learning studies.

c1ddf3a2bd767d0129f07d1a764121723c3cc8fd.text:
## GraphRAG Community: Research Communication, Mobile Retrieval, and Graph Learning

This community connects the evolution of research communication with mobile information retrieval, practice diffusion, and graph-embedding evaluation.

**Research communication and arXiv:** arXiv is a preprint repository where researchers share publication-ready articles before formal peer review. Its growth reflects collaboration and data-sharing practices, and it has a notable place in Web history. “Modern arXiv” proposes a substantially different future version based on new technologies, which have also eased document creation and dissemination.

**Mobile information retrieval:** This area searches document collections and uses test collections, relevance judgments, user studies, and user-log analysis to study mobile information needs and usage. Mobile devices, context awareness, adaptive user interfaces, and query reformulation support retrieval on mobile platforms.

**Practice diffusion and collaboration:** Practices spread through collaboration and mentorship. Syntactic signatures track practices in large document collections, while an inheritance graph represents their transfer. Its structure helps predict collaboration longevity and assess practice fitness.

**Graph learning and classification:** Classification is evaluated on the arXiv, DBLP, BlogCatalog, and CiteSeer graph datasets. HARP learns low-dimensional node embeddings, compresses input graphs, and improves DeepWalk, LINE, and node2vec through hierarchical initialization, with gains measured by Macro F1. Tweet-count classification achieved the best area under the ROC curve; feature groups were also evaluated using ROC curves.

988465adb7e471e760b9d4a273cdc6c6f90245a8.text:
## Community Report: Scholarly Networks, Disambiguation, and Scientific Text Mining

This community centers on computer-science literature analysis through publication, citation, collaboration, and author networks. DBLP, CiteSeerX, Web of Science collections, scientific-literature corpora, and specialized biomedical, food-and-agriculture, high-energy-physics, and Enron datasets support evaluation and network construction.

A major theme is author name disambiguation: homonym and synonym problems are addressed through publication clustering, agglomerative clustering, linkage functions, coreferring-author classifiers, predefined features, and automated systems. Deep neural networks enable automatic feature learning and achieve a reported 0.69% prediction error on Vietnamese author names. DBLP supplies gold-standard records and real-world collaboration data.

Network methods include citation linkage, co-authorship and co-citation analysis, bibliographic coupling, citation-network topic models, author-topic models, multidimensional ranking, rank aggregation, and expertise estimation. These methods support academic ranking, subdiscipline identification, knowledge-network construction, and visualization.

Text-focused work covers denoising full texts for keyphrase indexing and biomedical relation or protein-interaction extraction. Maui indexes original, denoised, and noisy text against gold standards, using readability and information-rich content. Parallel markup links presentation and content MathML for search indexing.

Additional topics include co-readership visualization, scientific writing patterns, mathematical representation, Sleeping Beauties and patent citations, information propagation, and the evolution of research areas.

7af2a4cbcf9c6e84edda51a15d98cf5bf71d4d84.text:
## Scholarly Literature Mining, Networks, and Disambiguation

This community connects computer-science literature analysis with author identification, text processing, visualization, and scientific networks. **Author name disambiguation** addresses homonyms, name variants, imbalanced training data, and ambiguous name blocks through publication clustering, linkage functions, coauthor-name features, agglomerative clustering, coreferring-author classifiers, hybrid approaches, and deep neural networks. DBLP, CiteSeerX, and labeled datasets support evaluation using gold standards and pairwise F1; automated and general disambiguation systems are key outputs.

**Text denoising** extracts information-rich, readable sentences from full text and supports keyphrase indexing, biomedical relation extraction, and protein-interaction sentence extraction. Maui indexes full and denoised text, with performance compared against gold standards.

Citation and collaboration research uses citation graphs, citation relations, coauthorship, bibliographic coupling, co-citation analysis, citation-network topic models, and multidimensional network ranking. DBLP supplies publication and author data for computer-science knowledge and collaboration networks. Co-readership visualization complements citation-based visualization and is assessed through qualitative comparison and expert interviews.

Other themes include mathematical representation through Presentation and Content MathML, scienceography across mathematics and computer science, figure extraction with DeepFigures, and scientific-literature datasets used to study novelty, propagation, and figure types.

531a8879ac500a4a022e1b2047ce9828f9656dc0.text:
## Community Report: Query Recommendation, Provenance, Privacy, and Rumor Containment

This community spans graph querying, provenance, private data analysis, string similarity, and rumor containment.

**TRQuery** is an embedding-based framework for SPARQL query recommendation over RDF data, evaluated on YAGO. It combines embedding scores with edit distance and uses approximate subgraph matching, compared with whole-graph matching through a vector-space score model. Its experiments demonstrate strong efficiency and effectiveness; structural edit distance provides a recommendation baseline.

**PUG** answers provenance questions, including queries with negation, using a graph-based provenance model that supports reverse reasoning and encodes diverse provenance models. It takes Datalog queries as input, and generated Datalog programs compute explanations. Datalog systems support semi-naive fixpoint evaluation and Magic Sets.

**Ektelo** supports efficient, reusable implementations of privacy algorithms for linear counting queries. Its algorithms compose operators belonging to a small number of operator classes, and it has been used to design state-of-the-art algorithms.

**MinJoin** is a randomized method for edit similarity joins: it uses string partitioning and local minimum hash values to find string pairs within threshold \(k\) edit distance.

Finally, the **RC model** formulates rumor containment as constrained optimization. Rumor-containing strategies are evaluated under a budget using a rumor-truth mixed spreading model, with effectiveness as the objective and cost also quantified through computer experiments.

b9b836dbbeed20ef424a03b2b254c0e8499066c0.text:
## Efficient Approximation, Querying, and Learning Systems

This community centers on computational efficiency, scalable querying, and information acquisition. Efficiency is measured through models involving seven variables, including in-flow and delay efficiency, and is linked to discoverability and editorial-resource costs. Approximation algorithms address optimization problems such as tie-strength optimization, densest subgraph discovery, minimum-inefficiency subgraphs, and cascade inference, often under low query-latency constraints.

Query rewriting supports partitioning transformations, provenance factorization, structured web queries, hierarchical preference paths, and compilation of ontological queries into equivalent first-order queries. HypDB rewrites biased queries into unbiased ones, while generative retrieval can skip rewriting. EAGR is designed to minimize query latency.

TAGME provides fast, effective annotation for short texts and long documents, resolving synonymy and polysemy. Schema research examines disjunctive multiplicity schemas, satisfiability, containment, implication, and twig-query properties. Such schemas are learnable from positive examples, whereas inclusion of negative examples affects learnability. Learning algorithms target soundness, completeness, minimality, polynomial time, and polynomial question complexity.

Other themes include computational frameworks for collective-action analysis, semantic relatedness, correlation and hypergraph clustering, and efficient information acquisition. QS QN evaluates queries over Horn knowledge bases using bounded term depth and strategies such as depth-first search and tail-recursion elimination.

1961064c02c9bd4bbce40ae8b87c503b611cc334.text:
## Approximate Data Systems and Behavioral Modeling

This community centers on scalable, interactive, and uncertainty-aware data analysis. **Probabilistic databases** use semiring and semimodule representations, support aggregate and non-aggregate query answering, and give meaning to probabilistic Datalog semantics. Systems such as **Sprout** and **Mimir** query probabilistic data; Mimir extends a deterministic database engine with lenses, JDBC integration, uncertainty-annotated result cursors, and an analyst GUI.

**Query rewriting** compiles ontological queries into first-order queries, factors provenance, and transforms biased queries into unbiased ones. Approximation algorithms address low-latency optimization, consistent trees, cascade inference, and tie-strength optimization. **GeoBlocks** uses query-driven layouts and pre-aggregation for approximate geospatial aggregation, while **Starling** uses cloud functions and object stores to provide interactive latency, lower cost, and straggler mitigation. **Focus** enables low-cost, after-the-fact video querying by selectively applying expensive CNNs.

The community also covers streaming and online analytics, including cooperative scans, online aggregation, predictive buffer management, and failure-aware approximate query answering, evaluated in part with TPC-H.

A second theme is computational social science: agent-based modeling, Markov and higher-order Markov models, innovation diffusion, social-network generation, keyword relationships, web navigation, dating markets, email conversations, bias detection, and social tie-strength inference. These methods model heterogeneous interactions, transitions, cascades, and behavioral uncertainty.

5f4744f04355449d31d846498fb2d3545009783a.text:
## Community Report: Network Structure, Influence, Discovery, and Online Detection

This community covers four themes: network generation and sampling, influence propagation, order-dependency discovery, and streaming anomaly detection.

Network studies compare stochastic block and 2K models, random networks, and preferential-attachment variants. The triangle generalized preferential attachment (TGPA) model produces higher-order clustering and power-law degree and eigenvalue spectra, while standard preferential attachment typically lacks higher-order clustering. Sampling methods—including forest fire and depth-first sampling—may distort observed degree distributions, although power-law eigenvalue spectra can persist with partial observation. Stochastic block and 2K models face tradeoffs between diameter and clustering, with goodness-of-fit depending on the social-network domain.

Competitive influence models use averaging-based propagation and seeded voters to study candidate success in elections; percolation thresholds are validated by simulation and real-world networks.

OCDDISCOVER and FASTOD address order-dependency discovery, extending functional dependencies. OCDDISCOVER uses pruning rules, but these may remove legitimate dependencies; its completeness claim is disputed. FASTOD’s set-based canonical form is central to a rebuttal.

K-truss minimization is NP-hard and uses edge deletion, pruning rules, and upper-bound strategies to identify critical connections. Finally, VEDAR performs single-pass, real-time behavior-change anomaly detection, benchmarked against Numenta HTM and Twitter ADVec SH ESD, supporting high-availability systems. Online image hashing uses Hadamard matrices, Sylvester construction, locality-sensitive hashing, and ensemble learning.

2450729cd43351316a693e79586d24aaaa594ef6.text:
## Community Report: Temporal Networks, Innovation, and Knowledge Organization

This community connects temporal-network analysis, scientometrics, document clustering, and biomedical innovation.

Temporal networks are modeled as discrete-time systems with timestamped links, temporal motifs, event graphs, interlayer adjacency matrices, and temporal strong components. Methods such as temporal aggregation alternatives, subnetwork extraction, temporal core decomposition, and temporal network structure tracking reveal evolving frequency patterns and macroscale structure in digital communication, face-to-face interaction, air traffic, and article-spread data. Temporal networks also support spread-network reconstruction and event-stream analysis.

Innovation research examines demand and supply perspectives, technological capabilities, and selection mechanisms across invention, innovation, imitation, and clinical or translational stages. Knowledge translation links molecular entities, nanomaterials, and biomedical research to pharmaceutical alternatives, using literature network analysis, computer-assisted content analysis, and scientometric mapping. Medical cases include cervical cancer, Ebola hemorrhagic fever, RNA interference, and drug discovery.

Document clustering uses nonnegative matrix factorization, max-correntropy NMF, supervised topic modeling, semantic similarity, vector-based models, and RI k-trees. NMF connects to latent-factor analysis and frequency-pattern extraction. Namespace discovery applies clustering to Java source code and organizes results with MSC and PACS.

Algorithmic historiography uses multidimensional scaling and HistCite to reconstruct intellectual lineages. Mutual redundancy links information measures with reflexive communication, the triple helix, and sociological theories.

3b6964e881443fd9fbde318dbcc99f84c1ec01a8.text:
### Mapping Innovation, Knowledge, and Evolving Research Networks

This community links scientometric analysis with medical innovation and knowledge translation. The innovation process is studied through demand and supply perspectives, technological capabilities, selection mechanisms, and literature-network analysis. Medical innovation is illustrated through human papillomavirus, RNA interference, and magnetic-resonance-imaging case studies. Knowledge translation follows the movement of molecular entities and nanomaterials toward pharmaceutical alternatives, including drug discovery and translational, preclinical, and clinical stages; cervical cancer and Ebola hemorrhagic fever provide demand-of-knowledge perspectives.

A second theme is document organization and semantic analysis. Document clustering uses nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF), supervised topic modeling, vector-based similarity, and semantic similarity measures based on topic maps. Max correntropy NMF learns semantic feature spaces, maximizes correntropy, and is evaluated on Reuters21578 and TDT2. RI-k trees address large-scale, changing collections and sparse document vectors, improving cluster quality over K-trees. Namespace discovery applies clustering to Java source code and organizes namespaces with MSC, PACS, and the ACM classification system.

Bibliometric mapping uses multidimensional scaling, VOS, and spring-embedded algorithms to represent funded research networks, EINS, and innovation dynamics. Algorithmic historiography reconstructs intellectual lineages using HistCite and multidimensional scaling. Temporal-network methods track evolving structures, extract significant subnetworks, and transform frequency patterns into networks revealing structural change.

69ad351f892383ccc3683eeca3bab1a45aa16449.text:
## Network Dynamics, Motifs, and Spectral Analysis

This community covers three connected themes: network modeling, temporal structure, and percolation.

Graphons provide nonparametric methods for estimating massive, dense, and sparse networks, including missing-link estimation and centrality under uncertainty. Network abstraction represents sequential data as smaller summary networks, while binary-image mappings and vertex reordering support network-structure visualization. Social-media mining applies these ideas to social networks.

Temporal-network research studies timestamped links, induced temporal motifs, motif frequencies, and pathways. Motif-counting algorithms are analyzed for runtime complexity and achieve 1.3×–56.5× speedups over a baseline. Multi-order graphical models combine higher-order Markov chains, capture pathways and temporal characteristics, and use graphical-model selection for Markov-order detection.

Percolation analysis compares adjacency and standard non-backtracking matrices with high-order, particularly second-order, non-backtracking matrices. Spectral radii and their reciprocals provide threshold bounds; the second-order matrix yields a tighter lower bound and is evaluated on 42 real networks. Above the percolation threshold, a giant component emerges.

Finally, the DeGroot–Friedkin model describes evolving social power and self-appraisals during sequential opinion discussions. Constant topology produces exponential convergence to an equilibrium, while periodic topology yields periodic solutions. Under arbitrary topology variation, doubly stochastic and irreducible interaction matrices yield a unique non-trivial equilibrium.

dbc9b8837177c815a5abe78df4aeb8d7454221e8.text:
## Community Report: Social Networks, Communities, and Graph Analysis

This community centers on modeling, mining, and evaluating social and interaction networks. Tie strength is a major theme: it measures connectedness, decays after interaction, relates to dispersion and mean tie strength, and is modeled over continuous time through diffusion and convection dynamics. These measures connect to higher-order structure and edge density.

Social search uses local information, direct friendships, social streams, and recursive incentives to reach distant targets, with applications including vessel routing and Q&A hashtags. Trend prediction combines temporal-based predictors, recent or cumulative degree, unsupervised clustering, and social diffusion models to identify patterns likely to spread globally.

Community analysis includes social circles, ego networks, political affiliation, cross-party interaction, and partisan structure, illustrated by Wikipedia and politically active Twitter users. User participation is addressed through badge systems, reward mechanisms, and referral contests, while antisocial behavior and sockpuppetry motivate early identification and classification using posting, linguistic, and network features.

The community also covers graph algorithms and infrastructure: AdaWave performs parameter-free clustering on noisy, high-dimensional data; randomized and approximate methods support clique counting and target finding; sampling and indexing address #P-hard s-t reliability estimation; and Swarm adaptively rebalances distributed spatial streams. Datasets include Breadcrumbs, real and synthetic social graphs, social streams, and friends-and-family networks.

676cae691fdeebf7abfbe11de1b15488af7da668.text:
## Influence, Social Recommendation, and Multimodal Retrieval

This community connects social influence, recommendation, election control, diffusion, fairness, and cross-modal retrieval.

Social influence underlies social recommendation and election control, but homophily may be a spurious cause mistaken for influence. DASO is a deep adversarial social-recommendation framework using bidirectional mappings between item and social domains, adversarial learning, and user representation learning. DSCF is a deep social collaborative-filtering system that incorporates distant neighbors and explicitly models neighbors’ item opinions. Deep neural networks combine user–item interactions with social-network information and process heterogeneous data.

For election control, Linear Threshold Ranking extends the Linear Threshold Model and uses submodularity for approximation guarantees in both constructive and destructive control. These problems involve scoring-rule voting, including plurality and Borda count. Probability of Victory evaluates constructive success, while Margin of Victory evaluates destructive control. The Negativity-Aware Diffusion Model extends the Linear Threshold Model to negative influence and defines a monotone submodular influence function. Submodularity also supports efficient fairness-aware algorithms, with surrogate objectives enforcing fairness during propagation. Social influence additionally raises privacy-leakage risks for highly influential nodes.

S3CA addresses cross-modal event retrieval by using deep neural networks, correlation alignment, and a shared semantic space to learn multimodal representations. The Wiki-Flickr Event dataset contains paired image and text samples for evaluation.

1c8a72be7a7c55f3d5808b6baf7b75e582198ce9.text:
### Weighted Networks, Survey Bias, and Citation Uncertainty

This community examines weighted heterogeneous networks, offline social networks, and uncertainty in normalized citation indicators.

A minimal generative model produces inhomogeneous weighted networks, with edge-weight updating informing weight evolution. The extended corona product constructs the model from two weighted graphs. These networks support analytical results for degree and strength distributions, clustering coefficients, and weighted spanning-tree counts. Their transition probability matrices define random walks, whose spectra yield mean hitting times and whose dynamics quantify network structure.

For offline social networks, strong ties represent close friends and family, while weak ties represent difficult-to-enumerate acquaintances. Fixed-choice surveys limit reported weak ties and produce crude observed networks that omit many connections. Consequently, direct estimates of degree distributions and clustering can be biased. The method of moments estimates network characteristics and network size from such data; simulated data assess estimator performance, and jackknife procedures estimate variance.

A second theme concerns citation impact. Field normalisation produces MNCS and MNLCS, reducing disciplinary and temporal effects. Bootstrapping and formula-based methods construct confidence intervals. Bootstrap intervals for MNLCS are generally accurate but may be unsafe for small samples; MNCS accuracy improves with sample size, while formula-based MNLCS intervals are generally safe and conservative for large groups.

083e6d56145fad58adcfbcd702fb6b1e8eb0303d.text:
## Information Spreading, Influence, and Network Analysis

This community centers on how information and influence move through social, mobile, academic, and online networks. Information spreading is examined in mobile networks, emergency events, citation cascades, event cascades, and social ties, using gossip mechanisms, random spreading, epidemic and self-exciting processes, infection kernels, and large-scale simulation. Flooding time and mobile conductance measure spreading performance.

A major theme is influence maximization and seed selection. Basic-Selector, Fast-Selector, sequential seeding, sequential seeding with buffering, and online influence maximization with persistence select influential vertices to maximize coverage, while static and temporal approaches use network structure and time-dependent measures such as outdegree. Competitive influence maximization accounts for opponents, and the Social Item Maximization Problem incorporates item inference.

The community also studies detecting genuine influence through probabilistic causal analysis, minimal causal topologies, propagation traces, and discriminative influence detection. Social influence is linked to topical diversity, focused messengers, Tencent Weibo activity, and event attendance.

Additional work analyzes geographic distance and academic relationships, city-based mobility, sampling efficiency, and network complexity. Applications include WebAPIRec for project-oriented API recommendation, table-question answering, visual spam detection, and election control through constructive or destructive influence.

8ba4a4b05873325908a152b20edd61f6c541af15.text:
## GraphRAG Community Report: Network Dismantling, Relational Learning, and Fair Recommendations

This community spans three connected research areas.

**Network robustness and dismantling:** Generalized network dismantling seeks cost-aware node removals that fragment networks into subcritical components, supporting analyses of vulnerability, misinformation spread, and epidemic containment. The spectral dismantling method uses the node-weighted Laplacian and combines spectral optimization with a weighted-vertex-cover fine-tuning mechanism. Robustness in complex systems is related to graph spectral properties, network vulnerability, and the lifetime of the network core. An optimal cost level maximizes both network robustness and core lifetime.

**Relational learning and answer selection:** Learning models over relational data support classification and regression using relational databases. Feature-extraction queries, batch aggregates, query compilation, factorized computation, semiring structure, and hypertree width provide computational and structural foundations. Training datasets feed classification, regression, and neural answer-selection models; high-quality labels are costly, and fractional subsets train collections of answer-selection models.

**Social networks and recommender systems:** Reciprocity contributes to core–periphery structure and user benefits, while equitable core–periphery graphs specialize equitable random graph structures. Agent-based models study online-social-network costs, benefits, reputation, and long-term average benefit. Fairness-aware recommender systems address fairness, balance, reciprocity, and profitability—dimensions typical recommender metrics may not capture. Motif-based features can outperform node centrality for predicting edge cardinality during diffusion inhibition.

7925734c0d71d85f9f15bcda12708d381485117d.text:
## Database-Centric Learning, Prediction, and Network Systems

This community connects machine learning with database execution, predictive indexing, transaction processing, and network analysis.

**LMFAO** learns ridge linear regression, regression trees, and classification trees over databases, optimizes group-by aggregates and data cubes, and supports Bayesian-network structure learning using Chow–Liu trees. It outperforms TensorFlow, AC/DC, and MonetDB in reported benchmarks. **SQL4ML** expresses machine-learning algorithms in SQL and translates SQL into training representations for TensorFlow.

For query optimization, **query selectivity estimation** uses Chow–Liu trees and Bayesian networks to model attribute-value distributions. It improves selectivity accuracy while maintaining time and space efficiency, influencing query execution plans and cost models. Evaluation uses TPC-DS.

**TSPDB** and the **prediction index** support predictive queries over time-series data. TSPDB uses incremental prediction; prediction indexes provide bounded predictive-query latency and support forecasting, imputation, and faster updates.

For transaction systems, intelligent scheduling uses supervised and unsupervised learning to estimate transaction conflicts, balance concurrency, reduce abort rates, and increase throughput over random scheduling. **ChainifyDB** adds a permissioned blockchain layer to existing systems, provides recovery, supports heterogeneous processing through Whatever-LedgerConsensus, and reports up to six-times Fabric throughput.

Network research uses network portraits, portrait divergence, graphlet analysis, and multilayer or multilevel network structures for comparison and structural analysis. Evaluation spans synthetic, protein-interaction, neuroscience, and computational-social-science networks.

624df9d9fa25efc7a8af812fff18f7dae6e3cb46.text:
# Graph-Based Recommendation, Data Integration, and Network Analysis

This community spans graph methods for recommendation, semantic data management, clustering, migration, and distributed computation.

Link recommendation includes learning- and proximity-based approaches grounded in social interaction theory. Utility-based link recommendation combines linkage likelihood, link value, and cost; Bayesian networks model dependencies among these variables and the recommendation decision. Google+ provides a prominent system context, including “You May Know,” image posts, places-lived data, and brand-marketing messages. Graph optimization addresses recommendation through partitioning algorithms and bipartite matching, with evaluation on production data.

Semantic integration connects Web data, extraction systems, heterogeneous sources, and cleaner integrated datasets. Direct qualification models semantic relationships among documents and named graphs, using applied analytics in an event-based prototype. Bayesian networks also represent term relationships in document collections and support thesaurus construction. Stack-based DAG pattern matching proposes PathStackD, TwigStackD, and DAGStackD, extending holistic twig joins.

Network analysis covers spectral clustering and AMOS, which automates model-order selection and evaluates clustering reliability; word-collocation networks represent words as vertices and collocations as edges. Migration-cluster models analyze country triads using bilateral flows, shared language, and colonial ties. FVSS applies verifiable secret sharing to cloud warehouses to enforce data integrity, while parsimonious flooding in geometric mobile ad hoc networks is equivalent to an SIR infection process.

55261efb2a03f2275da2dc9479bce2499629642f.text:
## Semantic Web Graph Data and Querying

This community centers on RDF-based Semantic Web data management, Linked Data, and ontology-driven integration. RDF represents subject–predicate–object triples and is a W3C-standard graph model supporting heterogeneous data integration, open-data publishing, bibliographic data, nanopublications, and micropublications. RDF graphs underpin Linked Data, Linked Open Data, semantic search, and semantic layers.

SPARQL is the principal W3C graph query language for RDF, executed through SPARQL endpoints and studied through query processing, basic graph patterns, set operations, joins, multiset semantics, and real-world query corpora. Extensions and related approaches include ontology-mediated query answering, nSPARQL, CPSPARQL, and geospatial variants. Gremlin and Cypher represent complementary graph-query and traversal technologies; Gremlinator translates SPARQL queries.

Ontologies, represented with OWL and supported by RDFS, provide conceptual structure, reasoning, semantic annotation, and interoperability. SKOS and Shape Expressions (ShEx) support knowledge organization and RDF validation, while ontology matching addresses cross-source interoperability. Provenance, provenance graphs, and nanopublications capture the origin and context of data.

The community also addresses scalable and evolving graph management through incremental view maintenance, incremental evaluation, distributed RDF management, trie-based indexes, source selection, relational join algorithms, and systems including Sage, Waterfowl, TriéJax, and SystemDS.

a66c5517d86377cbed4360f8b2d17961e5785e34.text:
## Airbnb, Crowdsourced Data, and Budgeted Selection

This community covers Airbnb spatial analysis, crowdsourced data refinement, and budget-constrained selection problems.

Airbnb is studied as a peer-to-peer marketplace and accommodation model within collaborative consumption and peer-to-peer marketplaces. In Barcelona, Airbnb listings and hotel patterns are compared using bivariate spatial autocorrelation and multiple regression analysis. They exhibit a centre–periphery relationship, while Airbnb benefits more from proximity to major tourist attractions and contributes to tourism pressure. The Airbnb dataset supports evaluation of frequent item-based count techniques.

Gain maximization over flexible attributes (GMFA) selects attributes under a limited budget by maximizing a gain function. Monotonic gain functions, the exact GMFA algorithm, and frequent item-based count support gain computation. GMFA is NP-hard; approximation algorithms, preprocessing, and pruning strategies address efficiency, while a constant-ratio approximation is considered unlikely.

Budgeted item recommendation selects items for accurate profile learning, particularly for cold-start users. Its least-square-error objective is neither submodular nor supermodular, and the problem is NP-hard with hardness-of-approximation results. Scalable heuristics are proposed.

CrowdFusion performs data fusion over Web data by selecting crowdsourcing tasks, accounting for data confidence, correlations, and potentially incorrect crowd answers. Its approximation solutions use preprocessing and are evaluated on a real crowdsourcing platform.

371477515ba928d0be48015bd82221672c1488fb.text:
## Graph-Based Recommendations, Semantics, and Network Analytics

This community centers on methods for analyzing and enriching graph-structured data.

**Link recommendation** combines learning- and proximity-based methods with social interaction theory. Utility-based link recommendation extends linkage likelihood with link value, cost, and operator utility, modeled through a Bayesian network and evaluated on a major U.S. online social-network dataset. Google+ provides related systems and datasets, including *You May Know*, image posts, places-lived information, and brand-marketing messages.

For graph mining, stack-based algorithms—**PathStackD, TwigStackD, and DAGStackD**—perform pattern matching on directed acyclic graphs and analyze correctness assumptions. **AMOS** automates model-order selection for spectral graph clustering, using random interconnection models and clustering reliability guarantees. Word collocation networks represent words as vertices and collocations as edges; documents can be converted into these networks and grouped by genre.

Semantic data management includes direct qualification, which models relationships among documents, named graphs, and concepts using applied analytics in an event-based system. Web data supports knowledge-driven tasks, extraction, integration, migration analysis, and probabilistic cleaning.

Other themes include migration-cluster prevalence from country triads, shared language, and colonial ties; FVSS for verifiable secret sharing in cloud data warehouses; and cost-aware task assignment, parallelization, and computation contracts.

57eb2bdffe30ea96e845f2085e31ac4a5b0f3f1e.text:
## Transfer, Integration, and Visual Task Understanding

This community connects deep transfer learning, recommendation, entity resolution, data integration, and visual task understanding.

**CoNet** performs cross-domain recommendation using neural networks, multi-layer feedforward networks, cross mappings between two base networks, dual knowledge transfer, joint loss functions, and efficient back-propagation. Transfer learning, fine-tuning, and visual embeddings support content-based and artwork image recommendation. NASNet and ResNet are pretrained on ImageNet and evaluated for artwork recommendation; ImageNet is associated with the ILSVRC challenge.

For **entity resolution**, distributed representations encode tuples into a standard feature space to address noisy joins in data integration. Machine-learning classifiers, transfer learning, crowdsourcing, and human–machine cooperation contribute to resolution, with entity-resolution datasets used for experiments.

The **task understanding framework** combines convolutional neural networks, external hierarchical task ontologies, and task descriptions to understand real-world tasks in images. It generates descriptions and can support image alt-text generation, while visual task understanding and image captioning address scene interpretation, though captions may not identify the exact task.

The **programmable architecture** provides a declarative language for view update strategies, data access control, general integration, and decentralized-data management. It supports both GAV and LAV mappings, integrated-data analysis and updates, and is demonstrated by a privacy-preserving ride-sharing alliance system.

bd21ed5411d472c04c23fa59aaa399d3112f5406.text:
## Community Report: Data Fusion, Networks, XML, and Online Communities

This community centers on methods for learning from imperfect, heterogeneous, and privacy-sensitive data. Synthetic data complements real and real-world data, preserves aggregated distributions, and provides alternatives when access to real data is limited by privacy concerns. It is widely used to evaluate probabilistic learning, clustering, truth discovery, reputation ranking, transfer entropy, and network models, often alongside real-world validation.

Network reconstruction is another major theme. Stochastic block models provide parametric reconstruction models, while point-process approaches—including multivariate spatiotemporal Hawkes processes and latent self-exciting point-process models—address temporal or incomplete network information. The methods are evaluated on empirical, artificial, social-media, and crime-related networks, with attention to heterogeneous errors and reconstruction accuracy.

Data fusion and truth discovery use probabilistic graphical models, source accuracy, reputation algorithms, posterior sampling, and domain knowledge. Logical or statistical constraints can detect inconsistent records and improve fusion accuracy.

XML research includes schema inference, deterministic regular expressions, XPath satisfiability, and query evaluation. VIP2P distributes XML documents using a DHT overlay and distributed materialized XML views, supporting structured queries in snapshot and subscription modes.

Finally, community question answering examines question–answerer matching, knowledge circulation, and how national culture shapes questioning, answering, and contribution behavior.

cd07335f7977437a92d853b4cd707cb380752107.text:
## Community Report: Data Fusion, Interactive Exploration, and Applied Learning

This community centers on methods for resolving, evaluating, and exploring complex data, with strong connections to synthetic and real-world datasets.

**Truth finding and data fusion** address conflicting values and source reliability. Probabilistic graphical models infer true records and source quality, while sampling-based inference improves scalability. SlimFast provides a data-fusion framework, and product synthesis incorporates fusion into an end-to-end solution. Truth-discovery methods are evaluated on synthetic and real-world data.

**Interactive analysis** combines multiple-hypothesis testing with false-discovery-rate control. Smart Drill Down supports exploration through rule lists, interesting-group discovery, and dynamic sampling, and is implemented as an evaluated prototype.

**Specialized systems and applications** include VIP2P, which combines a structured DHT, distributed materialized XML views, and an expressive XML query language, supporting snapshot and subscription modes. Fashionista performs visually aware fashion recommendation using binary feedback, learned visual spaces, trend evolution, and clothing-accessory data.

**Modeling and evaluation** span latent self-exciting point processes for spatial-temporal interactions and prediction, mixed-membership blockmodels, reputation-ranking methods, transfer entropy, RTED, and probabilistic learning. Synthetic data complements real data, supports privacy when access is limited, and is used extensively to validate these techniques.

d6ef4143133bcb5027b796a171985256dd328cc9.text:
## Community Report: Cross-Domain Representation, Recommendation, and Prediction

This community centers on unsupervised and cross-domain representation learning for social networks, recommendation, text analysis, and cyberattack prediction.

**Factoid embedding** represents user information as factoids and learns latent user embeddings across networks with differing profile attributes, content types, and links. It supports unsupervised user identity linkage by matching users close in embedding space, avoiding the labeled data typically required by supervised linkage.

**CDNR** transfers random-walk knowledge from a structurally rich domain to a structurally scarce domain through cross-domain two-layer random-walk learning, node-scale balancing, and knowledge transfer.

For recommendation, **VB-CAR** combines Bayesian skip-gram co-occurrence modeling, Bayesian behavior, amortized variational inference, and basket context to learn user/item representations for grocery recommendation. Multitask learning supports cold-start playlist recommendation for cold users, songs, and playlists using curated playlists, classification loss, and bipartite ranking loss.

Text-focused work includes emotionized representations built with emotion-intensity lexicons for fake-news identification, and topical stance prediction that estimates political leaning among Twitter users and online media using Media Bias Fact Check gold labels and manual analysis. Comparative summarisation formulates extractive selection across document groups using maximum mean discrepancy and gradient-based optimization, evaluated by crowdsourcing on controversial-news datasets.

Finally, a darkweb framework predicts enterprise attacks using reply-network structure, random-walk transitions, and forum statistics from 53 forums over 17 months.

ae78df16f1f6e1ffba5c594ce1d3cbed8beb43fd.text:
### Graph Analytics, Databases, and Scalable Search

This community focuses on graph databases and scalable graph analysis. Graph databases store large sparse relational datasets, support property-graph structures, and enable graph algorithms, although they generally lack a standard algebra. Algebraic property graphs provide a mathematically rigorous bridge between graph data models and graph algebra.

Graph analysis uses graph algorithms, graph algebra, and foundational single-source distance and shortest-path queries. Applications include breach detection from simulated and real-world log data, provenance analytics, and analysis of massive social graphs. Systems such as SNAP, STINGER, TableMult, GraphBLAS, and Apache Spark support large-scale graph computation and graph-algorithm execution.

Graph generators learn models from source graphs to reproduce linking properties and create data for data-intensive tasks, while raising concerns about implicit and explicit bias. Synthetic provenance graphs provide testbeds for provenance algorithms.

Similarity search spans graph and time-series databases, knowledge networks, and high-dimensional spaces. Methods include approximate search, text hashing, query relaxation, result diversification, and Forward Backward Similarity; representation independence addresses robustness across database representations.

Apache Accumulo supports distributed NoSQL storage, real-time ingest, scalable warehousing, D4M 2.0 schemas, and server-side sparse matrix multiplication. Temporally biased sampling— including T-TBS and reservoir-based R-TBS—uses decay functions for evolving streams and robust supervised learning.

5eb75896c3377dddf8a78e49f4fab81c1b1a8f4d.text:
## Graph Analytics, App Feature Extraction, and Verification

This community covers graph analysis, evolving networks, app-review mining, and natural-language verification.

**GSANA** is an iterative graph-alignment system designed for large graphs. It uses global graph structure and vertex and edge attributes to improve alignment accuracy. Graph alignment is also a first step in graph merging, a common model for heterogeneous data integration.

**VERSE** provides graph embeddings calibrated to preserve vertex-to-vertex similarity distributions. It has both full and sampling-based variants; the sampling-based implementation trains a single-layer neural network using graph sampling and achieves results as good as the full variant while improving time efficiency. VERSE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in precision and recall.

A size-agnostic change-point detection framework detects structural changes in temporal evolving networks. It is evaluated on synthetic dynamic-model data, the Enron email exchange, and the Ask Ubuntu forum, with successful precision and recall performance.

The app feature extraction model automatically extracts developer-useful features from app reviews. It is trained using supervised machine learning and annotated data guided by annotation guidelines. An augmented training set incorporating product reviews improves recall but reduces precision.

**AggChecker** is a natural-language query interface for verifying text-summary claims against relational datasets. It translates claims into SQL queries, uses query merging and result caching, and achieved higher precision and recall than baselines when tested on public articles.

62b25bba53440277d08c4696faf532ee50ea120d.text:
## Research on Retrieval, Annotation, Security, and Crisis Support

This community spans information retrieval, ranking, annotation, software security, social-media analysis, and emergency response.

**Ripex** identifies IP addresses in security forums and classifies them as malicious or benign, using cross-forum learning to transfer knowledge. Evaluated on five forums (31K users, 542K posts), it achieves over 93% recall and 95% precision for identification, and 78% recall and 88% precision for malicious-IP classification. Textual retrieval also maps vulnerability information to software weaknesses using the Snyk database and four repositories; keyword search is more consistent than regular-expression search and exploits explicit vulnerability and weakness identifiers.

**DALPHI**, an annotation framework, provides annotation assistance and pre-annotations for named-entity annotation, improving annotation quantity, quality, and annotator efficiency. Proposed models support early follower-loss detection from post-derived features and outperform a baseline.

Other work addresses top-k route search over points of interest, rated features, and feature spaces under travel-cost budgets, using indices, heuristics, and submodular personalized diversity. Pareto-optimal ranking manages user attention and workload.

Automated census construction uses topical crawling of faculty directories to produce the 2017 census, enabling turnover and retention analysis, including female faculty, relative to 2011. Finally, HomeGuard extracts victim situations in Bangladesh domestic-violence cases, using NGO case studies to support help provision and emergency response; alert ranking is evaluated with crisis-event data for emergency operation centers.

a28d4c751f82e01a8bd52074fdd1cf86aca09dc6.text:
## Open, Reproducible Research and Data Discovery

This community connects open science, computational documentation, reproducibility, and data reuse. **Jupyter Notebook**, originally designed as a free version of Mathematica notebooks, supports scientific and data-intensive research by combining computation with documentation and enabling code sharing. It contributes to open science and helps make research processes and results more reproducible. Open research data likewise supports data reuse and is associated with increasing reproducibility.

A second focus is recommender-system research. **LensKit** supports a wide range of research experiments, offline evaluation, educational experiences, and algorithmic backends for user-facing recommendation services. **LKPY** provides flexible, open-ended experiment designs, leverages the PyData stack, integrates smoothly with Keras, and enables new offline evaluations while maintaining the reproducibility of LensKit experiments.

The community also examines **data search** and **data discovery systems**. Data seekers engage in search to locate data for reuse, while a socio-technical perspective informs understanding and improved design of discovery systems. A **bibliometric study** examines academic discourse around data search, and **interviews** investigate data seekers’ practices and behavior.

210be461530af7bb830dd068456fa1ff7ca4516d.text:
## Distributed Graph Analytics, Sampling, and Network Dynamics

This community centers on scalable graph and data processing, evolving networks, and network-based inference.

**Apache Spark** is a major platform: it enables large-scale processing, hosts parallel MLPCD, Infe rSpark, Portal, statistical and inference libraries, and supports distributed evolving-graph analysis. **Portal** provides declarative querying, temporal selection, exploratory analysis, multiple physical representations, and partitioning strategies. **BigDatalog** supports graph analytics on Spark and reportedly outperforms GraphX for such workloads. Apache Accumulo, a distributed NoSQL database modeled on Google BigTable, supports scalable warehousing, real-time ingest, and graph-data persistence; the D4M 2.0 schema provides unique-string indexing and rapid queries across cyber, bioinformatics, and citation data.

Temporal methods include temporally biased sampling—simple and reservoir-based variants—which use decay functions to retain older stream data and improve robustness of supervised models under evolving data. Graph-query research studies projected, full conjunctive, acyclic, cyclic, beta-acyclic, beta-cyclic, triangle, and join-aggregation queries using worst-case-optimal, Yannakakis, output-sensitive MPC, and matrix-multiplication methods.

MLPCD detects protein communities using weighted PPI and gene-expression data, evaluated by modularity and functional cohesion. Optimal-control methods use Pontryagin’s principle and forward-backward sweeps to control diffusion, opinions, and neural dynamics on complex networks.

2ddbb33d7c9634d4abdc3791e3e27884cf82d419.text:
## Community Report: Structured Data, Diversity, and Graph Dynamics

This community connects XML query processing, graph analysis, technological diversity, and human or social dynamics.

A major strand centers on XPath over grammar-compressed trees. Automaton-based execution supports downward navigation, node counting, subtree serialization, and PTIME evaluation, while grammar repetitions avoid materialization. The XML grammar index accelerates structural XPath count queries, arbitrary tree algorithms, and XML result serialization. Type-based document projection prunes documents using query types, predicates, backward axes, and multiple-query optimization. XTPATH extends XPath with recursive tree matching, DOM context, annotation extraction, and informed search; on 117,422 pages across 75 websites, it outperforms XPath and a commercial wrapper system.

Another strand studies diversity and heterogeneity. Rao-Stirling diversity combines variety, balance, and disparity, while new, DIV, and relative-variety indicators measure related dimensions. These concepts connect to technological life cycles, inventor counts, and the 3V paradigm of volume, velocity, and variety, with variability and veracity as extensions. Heterogeneity is examined using Shannon entropy and power-law exponents.

Graph methods support tag recommendation, folksonomy analysis, community detection, target-set selection, and butterfly counting. Folkrank uses multi-hop graph relations, content data, and weight spreading to address new items. Other work models researcher migration, citation distributions, attention dynamics, and degree patterns through log-normal, power-law, and exponential-cutoff distributions.

a9d003346f6780a2ff6216d01469b56ff979c381.text:
## Graph-Structured Methods for XML, Networks, and Knowledge Analysis

This community centers on scalable querying, graph analysis, and heterogeneous data systems.

For XML, XPath queries support downward navigation, node counting, subtree serialization, and pre-order materialization. XPath can be translated into automata and executed in PTIME over grammar-compressed trees. The XML grammar index supports arbitrary tree algorithms, structural count queries, and XML result serialization without materialization. Type-based document projection prunes documents for multiple queries, predicates, and backward axes, with XMark and XPathMark evaluations. XTPath combines recursive tree matching, DOM context, annotation extraction, and informed search; it outperforms XPath and a commercial wrapper on its evaluation dataset.

Graph methods model networked information spaces through metric spaces, metric distance, link probability, and spatial preferred attachment models. Metric-space community detection uses graph-to-metric transformations and pairwise metrics. FolkRank and tag recommenders apply graph-based ranking, weight spreading, and feature or content data to tag recommendation and the new-item problem.

The community also examines heterogeneity through Shannon entropy and power-law exponents, alongside the 3V paradigm of volume, velocity, and variety, with variability and veracity extensions. Power-law, log-normal, and gamma distributions describe growth and attention. Rao–Stirling diversity connects variety, disparity, patent classifications, and technological life cycles.

8f9a402474565bf71c186031a6d17df54b96916f.text:
## Community Report: Clustering, Search, and Urban-Topic Modeling

This community connects methods for clustering, information retrieval, user behavior, and urban analysis.

**Clustering and graphs:** Hierarchical clustering addresses core community detection, producing compact communities and connected-core solutions. It uses LexDFS, node dissimilarity, and linear-time algorithms, and applies to moving points, brain structural connectivity networks, and urban-district classification. Admissible clustering methods are constrained by value and transformation axioms and bounded by universal upper and lower bounds. Active clustering incorporates user-desired dimensions, feature spaces, similarity metric learning, and limited human feedback, with evaluation on sentiment datasets.

**Search systems:** Search indices support top-k route search over route spaces, points of interest, travel costs, and cost budgets. User-profile embedding places users in topical-interest spaces and improves commercial web search. Context-aware search is studied through an Android app, diary studies, task-based user studies, collected search data, and quantitative log analysis. EGSE-A and EGSE-B are epsilon-greedy methods with theoretical search-performance results.

**Predicate evaluation:** ShallowFish optimizes column-store evaluation for shallow expressions, while DeepFish approximates deeper expressions; ShallowFish is optimal up to depth two and DeepFish targets depth three or greater.

**Topics and urban data:** Topical generalization and Wikipedia category graphs support topic clustering and topical user profiles. Heterogeneous topic modeling builds hierarchical models and outperforms concatenation baselines. Attraction profiles identify urban attractors; POI patterns and cell-phone-derived origin-destination matrices inform trip distribution models.

f86bdc4f102e7b50b7fae91025ce85ef7ce984be.text:
## Human-Centered Computation, Search, and Participation

This community studies how human participation and computational methods jointly support search, crowdsourcing, data integration, and online services. Human computation uses crowdsourcing platforms and machine computation for tasks such as quality assurance, content generation, and stream processing. AIDR classifies crisis-related social-media messages, achieving higher accuracy and lower manual effort than corresponding pure approaches; the CSP design framework supports its analysis.

Worker preferences—including required skills and payment—influence task completion, motivating preference elicitation and worker models. Participation is also shaped by gamification, reward mechanisms, and marginal quality incentives. In mobile crowd sensing, these mechanisms encourage timely, high-quality reporting and maximize expected user profits. Linear AoI-based rewards provide asymptotically optimal information freshness in deterministic settings, while selfish users can degrade performance, characterized through the price of anarchy.

Search research connects context of use, topical user profiles, human judgments, and search performance. Android-app and diary studies capture search context, while topical generalization uses the Wikipedia category graph to create broader profile labels. Semantic layouts and user-profile embeddings are evaluated through task-based studies. Top-k route search uses indices to retrieve routes visiting points of interest under travel-cost budgets.

Additional themes include interaction-decay prediction, citizen-science participation, computational politics, ranking, topic modeling, and semantic data integration in knowledge ecosystems.

0fab26205cdcaf02e6143d22eeddc336af68b3cb.text:
## Community Report: Social Question Answering, Ranking, and Behavioral Analytics

This community centers on community question answering, user expertise, question routing, and answerer matching. Systems such as Yahoo Answers and Stack Overflow support knowledge circulation, while QDEE estimates question difficulty and user expertise using competition graphs and social agony, then routes questions to appropriate users. Related tasks include duplicate and off-topic question detection, question refinement, answer retrieval, and answer-quality prediction. National culture influences questioning, answering, and contribution behavior across platforms.

A second major theme is ranking and reputation. Ranking algorithms use interaction patterns, semantic features, familiarity, and temporal changes to rank files, media, candidates, or cascade sources. Reputation ranking, correlation-based reputation, diversification, and discriminative influence detection address user evaluation, influence, anomalous behavior, reputation attacks, and sybil campaigns.

The community also studies online reviews and sentiment. Heterogeneous and homogeneous graphs capture local and global review context, while rule-based NLP processes customer feedback and detects opinion spamming. Sentiment analysis measures engagement and links nature contact and urban park visits—especially regional parks—with improved mood.

Synthetic, curated, and real datasets enable evaluation of these frameworks, including spectral partitioning, network recovery, rendering, and utility estimation, while addressing privacy concerns when real-data access is limited.

43586dd2c2fa53260e205fe569674962a97f7ebf.text:
## Privacy, Wikipedia Contributions, and Social-Media User Profiling

This community covers two connected research themes: anonymous contributions to user-generated-content platforms and profiling users from multimodal social-media data.

Wikipedia, a major user-generated-content site, has attempted since at least 2005 to block contributions from users connecting through Tor, a privacy-enhancing proxy used by anonymity seekers. The motivation includes concerns about spam, abuse, and vandalism. Although thousands of Tor-based editing attempts have succeeded despite blocking, Tor contributions are more likely to be reverted. Their overall quality is otherwise similar to contributions by unregistered users and to initial contributions by registered users. Contribution blocking is therefore related both to vandalism prevention and to contribution-quality assessment.

The second theme uses social-media networks as diverse data sources. Status updates, profile pictures, and Facebook page likes provide textual, visual, and relational user-generated content. Social-media data supports user profiling and personalized recommendation, while multimodal data trains machine-learning models. Profiling infers characteristics such as age, gender, and personality traits, using hinge-loss Markov random fields as a statistical relational learning framework. Model performance varies by network and depends critically on data-source selection.

20971b4cdaefd2c00fcab32bc9f12275c506a214.text:
## Community Report: Search, Summarization, Networks, and Privacy

This community spans information retrieval, recommendation, summarization, graph analysis, and privacy-preserving data systems.

**Retrieval and ranking.** LRSE supports lightweight multi-keyword and top-*k* ranked search over encrypted cloud data, using secure kNN, local/global representations, and a known background model while achieving state-of-the-art search quality and low system cost. A multilingual retrieval system, trained on English collections, evaluates Arabic, Chinese Mandarin, and Spanish retrieval and can benefit from target-language examples. Ranking algorithms generate objective item-quality rankings under fairness constraints. TIB ArXiv extends arXiv Sanity Preserver with text search, ranking, visualization, a unified backend, and a user interface. Paper Evolution Graph uses author information for one- and two-paper queries.

**Summarization and analytics.** Multi-document summarization includes extractive, hierarchical, and multilayered-graph approaches. Content-Based Weighted Consensus Summarization combines ensemble and consensus methods, estimating system performance from pseudo-relevant summaries and producing improved aggregate rankings, evaluated on DUC 2003/2004. AOMG uses workload-driven approximation, temporal-window quantiles, and frequency-based summaries, retaining tail values with under 5% relative value error.

**Graphs and recommendations.** Ego networks support social-circle detection, local-to-global structure estimation, and PCMA community reconstruction. Friend recommendation studies randomization, friend-of-friend methods, interestingness, and temporal behavior.

**Privacy and bioinformatics.** Randomization protects sensitive data and mitigates bias while supporting micro and aggregate reconstruction; the encrypted E-FM index enables exact pattern search over FASTA nucleotide collections.

8f896d466ebe2e1c5fcfa0dd4124531a816354ba.text:
## Differentially Private Spatial and Federated Data Analysis

This community centers on applying differential privacy to spatial data mining, hierarchical estimation, and private SQL query processing.

**Hierarchical group size estimation** estimates household counts by size across a geographical hierarchy, including national, state, and county levels. Differentially private estimation provides privacy while maintaining **hierarchical consistency**; error metrics assess accuracy. Group size is linked to a hierarchical attribute, and the household size distribution is a key target.

For spatial analysis, **differentially private counting** supports range queries over planar spatial regions. The Euler characteristic prevents duplicate counting when regions span multiple data-structure cells. Bounded user region size calibrates noise, while constrained inference—using robust least absolute deviations—imposes consistency and reduces noise. Concentration bounds support high-probability utility guarantees, with evaluation on real-world spatial datasets.

For federated SQL query processing, **private data federation** uses secure multiparty computation and traditionally relies on oblivious query processing, which pads intermediate results to hide operator cardinalities. **Shrinkwrap** instead uses computational differential privacy to minimize padding, improving query performance by up to 35× while trading result accuracy against performance.

b6f764e856a722bc7c466809b58eb5519f14d82c.text:
## Social Media Intelligence, Research Migration, and Data Extraction

This community spans three themes: social-media applications, international researcher migration, and web data collection.

Social media supplies user-generated text and multimedia for natural-disaster detection, disaster analysis, and response. Text-based detection and satellite imagery support natural-disaster detection, while visual content analysis examines disaster-related multimedia. Social-media utility for disaster response is assessed using measures such as post frequency. A literature survey reviews detection and disaster-analysis approaches.

Social platforms also support word-of-mouth and direct marketing. Reinforced WOM marketing jointly uses authoritative users to improve product promotion. In cryptocurrency promotion, social media and Telegram can spread false hype, enabling pump-and-dump scams that manipulate perceived cryptocurrency value. Bot activity increases during pump attempts, while a computational approach detects scams as they unfold.

A scientific migration network models countries as nodes and researcher movements as temporal, directed, weighted links, using 2.8 million ORCID public profiles. Weighted HITS identifies hubs (researcher-supplying countries) and authorities (researcher-attracting countries), including countries serving both roles. Ego networks and network visualization show their temporal evolution.

Finally, site-agnostic social-data collection, automatic pagination navigation, browser emulation, and dynamic data collection expose user-generated content for knowledge management, data-value extraction, and analytical applications. An internet-sites testbed benchmarks these methods against existing data-extraction techniques.

9853b8b5e4e3ad2d238c22c5ff065fe49a66e06f.text:
## Graph Learning, Signals, Diffusion, and Scholarly Analysis

This community links graph-based learning and querying with information diffusion, social behavior, and research evaluation.

**Graph methods and systems.** GraphSAGE performs inductive representation learning by sampling and aggregating local node features, supporting classification of unseen nodes and graphs using Reddit and protein-interaction data. A unified framework supports transductive learning, attributed multiplex heterogeneous-network embeddings, and efficient shortest-distance queries, while reachability indices, landmark covers, graph partitions, and distance landmarks address exact and approximate distance and reachability tasks.

**Graph and temporal signals.** Graph signals are modeled as network-process outputs or filtered white noise, enabling covariance analysis, blind centrality ranking, localized spectral analysis, sampling, and recovery. ARMA graph filters support distributed filtering and time-varying signals. Temporal signals—such as sharing duration, inter-copying time, and speed—combine with lexical evidence in search and ranking architectures.

**Diffusion and agents.** Agents exchange information, update beliefs about a true state, and make decisions under noisy or private observations. Evolutionary and global-game models examine participation, regimes, and information sharing. Social signals affect information-spread likelihood and speed, with Pinterest data measuring originality, retention, and production.

**Scholarly evaluation.** Citation matching addresses reference inaccuracies using reference strings, segments, and segmentation probabilities. Breakthrough detection uses micro-clusters, citation filtering, CSS rankings, and knowledge diffusion. Rao–Stirling and newer indicators study variety, balance, disparity, and technological life cycles.

ad4b4605883ca944c7312a1698a94f6dbd8def9e.text:
### Multi-Level Architecture for Named Entity Recognition

This community centers on a **multi level architecture** for **named entity recognition (NER)**, framed as a subtask of **information extraction**. The architecture combines **image features** and **text features** while avoiding dependence on **hand crafted features**. It also does not rely on specific **linguistic resources**.

NER performance is evaluated on the **Ritter dataset**, where it achieves an **F-measure of 0.59**. Overall, the reported work links multimodal feature extraction—using both visual and textual information—to an NER system designed to reduce reliance on manually engineered features and resource-specific linguistic knowledge.

0b290f0d9583eaca7aebec42b00c33a87a8ada75.text:
## Community Report: Folksonomies, Linked Data, and Networked Knowledge

This community centers on **folksonomies** and the Folksodriven framework, which represent tags, sources, and time as weighted networks. These structures support tag suggestion, serendipitous content discovery, ontology mapping, and evolving ontology environments. Tagging is highly uneven: “supertaggers” generate most annotations and differ in expertise, motivation, and behavior. Tag changes produce **structural plasticity** in network connectivity.

Network analysis is also supported by the **generalized stochastic block model**, which infers hidden group memberships, positive and negative connection patterns, mesoscopic and overlapping structures, structural patterns, and bridge vertices.

A second major theme is semantic infrastructure. RDF stores, SPARQL endpoints, D2R Server, and federation frameworks support query evaluation, joins, updates, entailment, and federated access to distributed Linked Open Data. Triple Pattern Fragments and binding-restricted fragments address query execution and join performance.

**Wiktionary** provides machine-readable definitions and translations through automatic extraction, prescribed entry structures, and SPARQL access; its data supports multilingual ontology matching.

The community further connects networks to scientific and cultural analysis: Scopus-based methods identify field-specific excellence and city-level centers of excellence; international mobility links early-career researchers to transnational networks; and city networks model musical preferences and leader–follower relationships.

f214e30211d7064cee89300be802645761cb70e4.text:
## Community Report: Information Extraction, Relational Learning, and Data Processing

This community centers on information extraction, its formal languages, and database-oriented learning and querying.

**Information extraction** includes relation extraction and systems such as information extractors and QA4IE. It draws on ontologies and ontology enrichment to improve extraction from technical data sheets, and is benchmarked using IE Benchmark. **Document spanners** provide a formal framework for extraction languages: regex formulas extract relations from text documents using capture variables, can be compiled into automata, and are extended to handle incomplete information. Sequential variable-set automata describe spanner extraction tasks, while regular spanners combine regular expressions with relational algebra. Recursive Datalog captures polynomial-time document spanners.

**Relational algebra** manipulates regex-extracted relations and can include black-box extractors. It also formalizes graph queries and simulates MATLANG using arithmetic, grouping, and summation. Joins are relevant to S3 Select, where they may be pushed down or require reimplementation.

A second theme is learning over databases. **AC/DC** supports factorization-machine and principal-component-analysis training, uses sparse representations, and decomposes optimization over database joins; it is benchmarked against R, LibFM, and TensorFlow. Factorization machines model knowledge tracing and exploit LOD-enabled features. Text categorization uses TCMS, relation extraction, similarity search, and KNN, with categorization performance as an evaluation metric.

d1812bf91ceb68dcd6c906acceb6cfa2cdbaac74.text:
## Ranked Enumeration, Spanners, and Approximate Dependencies

This community connects ranked query evaluation, information extraction, and dependency-based data cleaning.

**Ranked enumeration** orders answers to full conjunctive queries by a ranking function, including cyclic queries. Extending ideas from **k-shortest paths** in weighted graphs, it achieves asymptotically optimal top-result time, enumeration delay, and total enumeration time, outperforming batch algorithms that generate and sort all results. It also provides a framework for ranking dynamic-programming problems and studies annotated answers from **weighted vset automata**, whose transitions carry elements of commutative semirings.

For information extraction, **document spanners** are defined through regular expressions with capture variables and relational algebra. Their expressive power is captured by **vset automata**, while **annotators** extend them with auxiliary annotations such as confidence and support. Provenance semirings annotate extracted tuples, and annotators are investigated for closure under positive relational algebra.

A second theme is **approximate band conditional order dependencies**, a new integrity-constraint type extending band order dependencies with approximate satisfaction, exceptions, and conditional subsets. Automatic discovery is formulated as constraint optimization and improved by a pieces-based algorithm that greedily processes contiguous tuple sequences. Dynamic programming finds an optimal solution in polynomial time, while longest monotonic bands identify qualifying tuple subsequences. These dependencies support dependency-based data cleaning.

48d9888d40412b48b450df79c6da025e5a2dfc41.text:
## Semantic Querying and Knowledge Organization in Linked Data

This community connects Semantic Web technologies, knowledge organization systems (KOS), and advanced user-query analysis. Linked Data and SKOS support representing KOS—including thesauri, subject-heading systems, and classification schemes—in a machine-readable environment. SKOS assigns each concept a URI, while an RDF literal provides its lexical representation; URIs act as surrogates for KOS concepts. The work also examines the relationship between a KOS concept’s ontological substance and its linguistic form.

The LD SDS system fuses Semantic Web and spoken-dialogue-system technologies. It leverages Linked Data, identifies and links entities in data and user input, performs entity disambiguation, and expands conventional slot-filling dialogue models. Its semantic query-answering services use reasoning over data semantics and support exploratory search.

Information extraction automates user-query analysis by using knowledge bases and authority files to identify entities, including person and place names. Linked Data helps characterize queries. Web analytics captures queries, while the BelgaPress query dataset—generated by the BelgaPress historical-newspaper platform—supports automated analysis. The Royal Library of Belgium conducted the case study.

8758c3e8cfb0cfe1e6cadb134d7906afa550c456.text:
### Social Media Sentiment and #MeToo Research

This community focuses on sentiment analysis of social-media content concerning college sexual harassment, the #MeToo trend, and sexual misconduct in academia. Sentiment analysis, a branch of affective computing, uses social-media data to determine user attitudes and is commonly treated as a binary-classification task. Text may be represented with a vector space model, while deep semantic meaning representations are used to discover sentiments in #MeToo tweets.

The research examines tweet sentiments in relation to different types of college sexual harassment and studies how the #MeToo trend influences reporting and discussion. Social-media data complement survey-based studies, and the prevalence of the trend significantly correlates with official reports in several geographic regions. Analysis of the trend also aims to raise awareness of sexual misconduct in academia.

The community additionally addresses social-media polarization and proposed polarization-reduction solutions. Social bots operate as automated social-media accounts, and credulous accounts have a high percentage of social bots among their followees. The #MeToo trend emerged and spread through social media, connecting computational sentiment methods with harassment research, awareness efforts, and discussions of polarization.

e36816042478a97e1a440f8ee4cf9e088237f9d1.text:
**Community Report: Social Graphs, Context, and Recommendation**

This community centers on using social graphs, contextual information, and user representations to improve recommendation, retrieval, and social-media analysis. Social graphs encode user connections in social networking services, commerce networks, and peer-to-peer settings; they support social recommendation, collaborative retrieval, consumer-choice analysis, and socially informed routing. Methods and systems include Serec, DiffNet, DiffNet++, DASO, DSCF, LLGR, LCGR, heterogeneous graph propagation, social regularization, and neural social collaborative ranking. These approaches exploit social diffusion, graph structure, neighbors’ opinions, and heterogeneous user representations.

Collaborative retrieval addresses sparse query–user–item interactions through latent collaborative retrieval, social collaborative retrieval, ILCR, and query-user-item tensors. Contextual information varies by user, time, and location and is used in CA-RNN, context-aware genre prediction, hybrid filtering, fusion graphs, and Twitter sentiment classification. Social context also frames behavior, engagements, and structures.

The community covers retweeting activity classification using information-theoretic classification and user entropy; sentiment classification on Amazon reviews and labelled tweets; and textual reply generation through Soc2Seq, which incorporates content preferences, conversational style, and social-graph structure.

A parallel service-oriented theme represents, discovers, recommends, composes, and integrates web services, including QoS prediction and service stitching.

b65db0133ee4e3cf8e384a3e269de072586a68bf.text:
## Community Report: Summarization, Retrieval, Fair Ranking, and Networked Recommendations

This community centers on document summarization, privacy-preserving retrieval, multilingual search, and fair ranking. Multi-document summarization extends single-document methods and includes extractive, hierarchical, ensemble, consensus, and graph-based approaches.
