The multi-layered graph model captures sub-sentence-, sentence-, and document-level relations. Content-based weighted consensus summarization combines system performance and content, using pseudo-relevant summaries and aggregate ranking; it is evaluated on DUC 2003 and DUC 2004. Privacy-preserving summarization uses secure binary embeddings and achieves results similar to non-private systems on standard evaluation datasets.

Secure binary embeddings convert bag-of-words or key-phrase representations into bit strings supporting approximate distances. Privacy-preserving passage retrieval uses secure document representations and performs similarly to non-private retrieval on clean and speech-recognized text. Multilingual retrieval evaluates Arabic, Chinese Mandarin, and Spanish, with English collections and occasional benefit from target-language examples.

Ranking research addresses item quality and fairness through exposure allocation, disparate-treatment, and disparate-impact constraints. Concept-driven probabilistic search uses cluster-based language modeling, concept extraction, and cluster popularity, outperforming plain search.

Other themes include Text2Vis for textual-to-visual mapping, artwork recommendation, and image search; PathWalk for graph-based short-text modeling; migration networks; and influence-based base-station localization in wireless networks.

12c8f12d39f53900ec55900617bf217adb3f584d.text:
## Affect, Political Discourse, and Recommendation Systems

This community covers three themes: urban greenspace and mental affect, political communication on Twitter, and movie recommendation.

Studies associate nature exposure with improved affect and mental-health benefits. Park visits correspond to higher affect during and after visits. Regional parks, with greater vegetative cover and greenery, produce larger affect increases than civic plazas and squares. Urban parks also provide potential mental-health benefits and are associated with decreased use of negation words in tweets.

Political discourse research uses sentiment analysis, toxicity analysis, media-bias analysis, retweet analysis, and social-graph analysis. Political parties operate party accounts, while media houses contribute to and exhibit bias within political discourse. Retweet analysis estimates information diffusion power; this metric is more informative than follower count alone. Party accounts reach users with limited diversity and deliver information to only a few politically detached users. Low user diversity is associated with users sharing similar values.

A hybrid recommendation system combines content-based filtering with sentiment analysis of movie tweets to implement movie recommendation. Movie tweets, collected from microblogging websites, provide tweet sentiment, estimates of mental affect, and information about current movie trends. The system is evaluated using a public database.

4932ae620c94df90729638f854f6aaa2875dd68f.text:
## Search, Ranking, Privacy, and Graph-Based Research

This community centers on information retrieval, ranking, and recommendation. Ranking functions order results by relevance, often through weighted sums in a multidimensional weight space, and support vertical, image, and video search. Ranked enumeration produces top-*k* answers with guarantees for top-result time, enumeration delay, and total enumeration time, including outputs from weighted VSET automata.

Sponsored and personalized ad retrieval is another major theme. Multi-stage architectures, cost-sensitive weighting, EENMF, and hierarchical signal-key ad networks address ad matching and pre-ranking. Click models incorporate externalities, fatigue, and both pre- and post-click relevance.

Similarity and representation methods include cosine similarity, textual spatial cosine similarity, word mover’s distance variants, and secure binary embeddings, which convert document or key-phrase representations into bit strings. Privacy is further addressed through differentially private search-log sanitization and privacy-preserving retrieval and summarization.

TIMEMACHINE generates timelines using relevance, temporal and content diversity, web co-occurrence statistics, and submodular optimization. Omicron supports Android mobile-information-retrieval studies and collects query and interaction data. CyberChair applies pattern-language concepts to conference reviewing. Graph research examines edge attributes, reciprocal edges, anomalies, and parallel adjacency lists, while incremental view maintenance and dependency discovery address dynamic databases.

36da153459461177189c0c4002c143c5a9bee076.text:
## Social Media Mining, Domain Adaptation, and Graph-Based Analysis

This community centers on NLP analysis of social-media and conversational data. Topic modeling and extraction use LDA and PLSA, with Gibbs sampling, entropy-based feature selection, and feature expansion. LDA and PLSA support semantic mining and recommendation systems but are limited by sparse word co-occurrence in short texts; long-text topic modeling addresses this limitation.

Twitter datasets—including the 2016 election and 2018 U.S. midterm-election data—support topic, sentiment, emotion, discourse, and text classification. Analysis of alt-right supporters identified racist, anti-immigration, alternative-media, and white-supremacist themes, while community finding examined supporter organization. Geocoding and transportation-data analysis also use public Twitter data.

Health-oriented studies apply correlation, co-occurrence, and behavior-pattern analysis to opioid use disorder, emotion, addiction recovery, and relapse prevention. Abusive-language detection combines textual content features with graph-based features from conversational graphs; fusion methods improved abusive-message classification, achieving a reported F-measure of 93.26%.

A domain-adaptation layer combines generic and domain-specific word embeddings for encoder-classifier frameworks, particularly on modest-sized datasets. Recommendation systems use content-based features, LDA, and personalized PageRank in online communities. Personalized PageRank and random walks operate on edge-weighted graphs, using Monte Carlo approximation, short-walk precomputation, walk-count optimization, and distributed or parallel computing frameworks to reduce runtime and memory.

a764e0b5f98ad1a86690c3a2f8ec6817f3be5390.text:
## Community Report: Privacy-Aware Cleaning, Dynamic Graphs, and Topic Visualization

This community brings together three themes: data cleaning, dynamic graph analysis, and document/topic representation.

**Data cleaning and privacy:** DPClean enables engineers to tune cleaning workflows involving matching, blocking, and edit similarity joins. Its privacy engine translates queries into differentially private mechanisms, returns answers within specified error tolerance, and tracks overall privacy loss while maintaining high cleaning quality.

**Similarity joins:** Edit similarity join finds string pairs within an edit-distance threshold and supports data cleaning, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. EmbedJoin uses metric embeddings of edit distance and is evaluated on real-world DNA sequences.

**Dynamic graph analysis:** Random walk with restart (RWR) supports node-similarity tracking in dynamic graphs with node and edge updates. OSP uses offset score propagation to update RWR scores after graph changes, with exactness and convergence/update-efficiency guarantees. OSP-T trades time for accuracy, with guarantees parameterized by restart probability and improved L1-norm and rank error.

**Document representation and visualization:** Distributed document representation depends on model parameters and can be evaluated through topic quality. Topic clouds visualize topics using pie-chart slices and word importance, which controls font sizes; they complement traditional word clouds and support qualitative comparison by NLP practitioners.

de1fe087195b34750311eb76a72f75dbc1aa8110.text:
## Graph-Based Knowledge Discovery in Technical and Biomedical Texts

This community centers on knowledge graphs, semantic networks, and natural language processing for discovery, retrieval, and design support.

**TechNet** is a large-scale technology semantic network constructed by mining the complete U.S. patent database from 1976 onward. Natural language processing extracts patent terms, while word embeddings vectorize them and establish semantic relationships. TechNet evaluates pairwise relevance and supports engineering knowledge discovery, technology search and retrieval, engineering design and innovation, technical text summarization, relational knowledge discovery, and design ideation.

A second strand is a biomedical **knowledge graph** derived from the entirety of PubMed and SCAIView data. Implemented as a labeled property graph and based on polyglot persistence systems, it stores contextual information for querying and discovery. It supports context mining and graph querying and is enriched with domain-specific language data using BEL.

Across both strands, context is central: it influences the exact meaning of natural language and is explicitly stored in the biomedical graph. Together, these systems connect text-derived representations, semantic relations, and graph-based querying for technical and biomedical knowledge discovery.

9eed4544d7671d7533c13df10a55dd7adac8f3cc.text:
## Community Report: Embeddings, Authorship Verification, and Stock Prediction

This community connects graph representation learning, natural language processing (NLP), digital text forensics, and financial forecasting.

For graphs, graph clustering jointly learns node representations while integrating both node contents and link structures. Deep embedding, motivated by neural-network representation learning, learns intrinsic node representations. Network embeddings support node classification and edge prediction. Sub2vec extends embeddings from nodes to arbitrary subgraphs, learning subgraph representations while preserving local proximity.

In authorship verification, compression-based authorship verification is an intrinsically one-class classification method. It uses a compressing algorithm, a dissimilarity measure, and a decision threshold to accept or reject authorship, and is evaluated on publicly available authorship-verification datasets. Compression models are adapted for authorship verification, while neural networks provide a comparison. Authorship verification is positioned within digital text forensics; notably, this approach does not use NLP.

For financial applications, hybrid attention networks predict stock trends from sequences of recent related online news, capturing sequential content dependencies and diverse influences. Self-paced learning supports effective and efficient training, evaluated using real-world stock-market data. The stock market contains news related to trends and volatility, while NLP enables online-news analysis and includes morphosyntactic analysis.

c735a79a080dafd3d1588d002acc2b15f26c7ad4.text:
## Community Report: NLP for Abuse, News, Tables, and Software Adoption

This community centers on natural language processing (NLP) and its applications to cyber-related discourse, online abuse, news analysis, tabular data, and software engineering.

A cyber lexicon is developed from cyberwar news and Stack Overflow data. Candidate terms are scored with APMIS, FDR, and TF-IDF, supporting cyber-related discussion detection on online social platforms. NLP also supports abuse and hate speech detection. Abuse detection should address both subtle and serious abuse, while proactive abuse prevention aims to inhibit online abuse before harm occurs. Transfer learning with deep neural networks enables shared hate representations across datasets and produces the Map of Hate, which visualizes different hate-speech types. A justice framework promotes healthy communities; victims seek validation and solutions.

Newsdeps combines NLP and plagiarism-detection methods to measure article similarity, analyze information provenance, identify primary sources, and improve news-consumption transparency. It uses temporal force-directed graphs, where news articles are chronological nodes and similarity is encoded by edge width.

Table2vec applies neural language modeling to captions, column headings, and cells, producing word and entity embeddings for tabular data; semantic annotation improves tabular-data understanding.

Finally, GitHub commit-log analysis studies team learning through software-library adoption. Library first use, code additions/deletions, team size, popularity, Stack Overflow prevalence, and adoption speed are related measures.

094aaf329682523f69451dc5566f0dbbfc98f154.text:
## Spectral Analysis, Parallel Graph Algorithms, and Synthetic Networks

This community spans spectral graph analysis, scalable graph processing, and graph-generation and learning systems.

**Spectral methods.** Network Density of States computes and estimates spectral densities for large real-world graphs, borrowing tools from condensed matter physics. Spectral density captures graph-motif signatures and provides structural information beyond extremal eigenpairs. Spectral graph theory connects eigenvalue distributions, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors to graph structure and spectral geometry.

**Parallel labeling and matching.** VC-PLL implements pruned landmark labeling (PLL) with vertex-centric computation, while BVC-PLL reduces VC-PLL’s computational inefficiency through batch execution. On a SIMD multicore architecture, BVC-PLL uses hierarchical parallelism, achieving parallel efficiency and scalability, with lower computational and memory-access costs than PLL under a stated assumption. It can also support weighted graphs. GSI solves subgraph isomorphism, using the PCSR representation and the Prealloc Combine strategy in GPU architectures that provide massive parallelism and memory hierarchy support; it is evaluated on real and synthetic graphs.

**Generation and learning.** Diverse synthetic graph generation creates varied graphs intended to imitate real-world networks, supports supervised subset selection, and applies to power-network synthesis. Graph representation ensemble learning is tested on four real-world graphs, improving macro-F1 by up to 8% and underrepresented-class performance by up to 12%.

8bfc8ebf5aab0f308ee36a20fef95b14d663147f.text:
# Signed Graphs and Balanced Subgraph Detection

This community centers on graph balance in signed networks. Signed graph theory provides the framework for studying signed networks, with graph balance as a key concept. Graph balance is also useful for modeling polarized communities.

A central task is large balanced subgraph detection, which seeks subgraphs satisfying graph balance. The proposed efficient balanced subgraph algorithm addresses this task by relying on signed spectral theory and using a novel laplacian perturbation bound.

The graph Laplacian is directly connected to this perturbation bound, which concerns how the Laplacian behaves under perturbations. Together, signed spectral theory and the Laplacian perturbation bound support the algorithmic approach to finding large balanced subgraphs.

14a2aac2237f2ba35db0804fbb4470a2c0cb315d.text:
## Distributed Graph, Trajectory, and Tag Recommendation Systems

This community covers distributed big-data processing, partitioned graph querying, trajectory management, and e-book tag recommendation.

**Graph and big-data processing:** Graph partitioning uses divide-and-conquer to produce partitioned graphs for query evaluation. Graph querying systems evaluate partitions independently, often with multiple processors, while partition-loading heuristics use partition characteristics to reduce response time. MapReduce supports multiprocessor graph-query evaluation and batch processing on Hadoop. Hadoop and Spark provide large-scale processing platforms, with Spark also supporting stream processing. However, both systems’ locally distributed computation models limit geographically distributed data processing.

**Trajectory data management:** Distributed subtrajectory join is a major trajectory-management operation. DTJb provides a basic solution, DTJr uses data repartitioning, and DTJi adds an indexing scheme. On a maritime trajectory dataset, DTJi achieves up to 16× speedup over DTJb, 10× over DTJr, and 3× over the closest related algorithm.

**Tag recommendation:** A hybrid system combines Amazon user search terms, e-book metadata, and publisher/editor-assigned tags. Evaluated on Amazon e-book reviews, it improves tag recommendation accuracy and diversity. Semantic similarity, including skip-gram word embeddings for identifying semantically similar hashtags, is proposed for evaluating recommendation algorithms.

2525301baa9b61c2dc61dfdce8bf85f41d6cbd9c.text:
## Signed Networks, Balance, and Graph Learning

This community centers on structural balance in signed networks, where positive and negative ties represent friendship and antagonism. Balance theory explains favored configurations, while the frustration index and partial balance quantify departure from balance; graph optimization and binary linear programming compute these measures, accelerated by prioritized branching, valid inequalities, and heuristic or approximation algorithms.

Signed clustering partitions networks so positive links remain within groups and negative links cross groups. An MBO scheme, adapted from Merriman–Bence–Osher and derived from the Ginzburg–Landau functional through a graph-based diffuse-interface model, supports semi-supervised clustering and scales to sparse networks. It is evaluated on stochastic block models and financial correlation matrices.

Graph neural methods include signed graph attention networks, which generalize graph attention networks, incorporate graph motifs, and outperform signed graph convolutional networks on real-world signed datasets. Hypergraph learning uses hypergraph Laplacians, adjacency matrices, and conjugate-gradient optimization to model high-order relations on social media sharing platforms; randomized SVD supports large-matrix approximation and low-rank factorization.

Structural balance visualization combines signed-Laplacian spectra, edge coloring and bundling, and Cartesian layouts, with validation on synthetic networks and political debates. Structural-balance dynamics and sociality transitions describe mixed hostile-faction and harmonious single-faction states. Opinion dynamics further addresses polarization, boomerang effects, and persistent fluctuations in signed social networks.

f041a433877c630982179d8fd43d600e24928460.text:
## Disinformation, Controversy, and Information Disorder

This community focuses on disinformation as a form of information disorder, including its relationship to fake news. Social media enables users and bots to propagate fake news and spread disinformation, while user engagement contributes to the dissemination of information disorder.

Key tasks include disinformation detection, characterization, and attribution to sources or actors. Fact-checking helps assess and combat disinformation, and weak supervision supports disinformation detection when labeled data are limited.

The community also addresses controversy detection. Vocabulary-based controversy detection uses community jargon and social-media vocabulary to detect controversial topics without requiring domain-specific knowledge. It relies on a vocabulary-based measure that quantifies controversy and outperforms measures based only on community graph structure. Controversy detection can support approaches aimed at avoiding information segregation.

Together, these entities connect the spread and assessment of disinformation with methods for identifying controversial topics and understanding how community language and structure shape information environments.

3983ffb8792c4fbfce69dfa1bb33027e48fa1480.text:
## Reliability, Influence, Polarization, and Network Structure

This community centers on reliability maximization in uncertain graphs, where edges have existence probabilities and reliability is the reachability probability between source and target nodes. Budgeted and multiple-source/multiple-target variants add limited edges, with applications to sensor networks and social influence maximization. These problems are NP-hard and have studied approximation hardness, reduction rules, data reduction, and scalable algorithms.

A second theme is influence maximization in social networks: influence spread is optimized through node selection, while deactivation reduces spread. Competitive leader–follower models and adaptive strategies include adaptive RMKCG, formulated as stochastic optimization with a bilevel model. Sample Average Approximation, complete enumeration for small instances, and matheuristics for large instances are used; adaptive RMKCG is adaptive monotone but generally not adaptive submodular, and is NP-hard. Revenue maximization under a k-hop collaborate game extends RMKCG through adaptive initiator selection.

Network dismantling seeks minimal-cost node removal to enforce a target component size, including generalized dismantling via spectral approximation and ensemble methods using power iteration. Minimum hitting set and its reduction rules are affected by instance locality and heterogeneity.

Finally, social polarization studies two-state opinions and zealots under varying initial conditions and zealot fractions, including real-world social networks linked to meetings, identified users, and G1 cryptocurrency transaction records.

993d979bd85c315d53b2f2d10ea0899bb0f2c1da.text:
## Social-Media Dynamics and Scholarly Impact

This community connects bibliometrics, altmetrics, social-media analysis, and temporal machine learning.

**PlumX**, an EBSCO bibliometric suite, assesses the multidimensional impact of books and monographs. It accepts ISBNs, analyzes a collection of more than 200,000 books, and provides measures including catalogue and library holdings, citations, views, usage counts, downloads, reviews, and social-media indicators. Academic-book impact is not fully captured by citation indicators: library holdings are identified as especially promising, usage counts are quantitatively predominant, and books generally show a long impact half-life, unlike views and social-media measures.

Altmetrics complement citation indicators through tweets, Facebook posts, Mendeley readership, blog mentions, and policy-citation prediction. Document characteristics are examined as factors associated with these signals and with citations. Research papers may also receive public-policy citations.

Social-media studies address popularity prediction, controversy identification, pharmacovigilance, and B2B entrepreneurial behavior. **Deep Temporal Context Networks (DTCN)** combine joint embeddings, temporal-context learning, and temporal attention to model sequential, multimodal user-post data; they improve popularity prediction on approximately 600,000 Flickr photos using Spearman ranking correlation. Motif-based controversy detection enables language-independent, fine-grained discussion-evolution analysis and improves over baseline network features.

Recurrent neural networks, including LSTMs, support ADR mention extraction and recommendation, though supervised methods face labeled-data scarcity.

591858b74ae50a3c69313df98fb867009b926f1c.text:
### Database Systems, Relational Learning, and Scholarly Data

This community spans relational database theory, query processing, data integration, and scholarly-data analysis.

Key database methods include classical join algorithms and worst-case-optimal approaches for multiway equijoins. Degree information, fractional hypertreewidth, and matrix-multiplication bounds characterize query complexity and enable subquadratic processing. Hidden-database crawling algorithms provide upper and lower bounds and achieve asymptotic query efficiency.

Theoretical work studies database instances, GLAV mappings, keys, and independence atoms. Finite and general implication problems arise for keys and independence constraints. The DB category connects database semantics with the power-view monad, Kleisli and Set categories, universal algebra, and functorial semantics.

Relational learning includes schema-independent, sample-based, and query-based learning, as well as relational learners and classifiers for networked data. Data curation uses spreadsheets, Jupyter, Vizier, and singleton operations.

Systems apply these ideas to practice: SkyQuery performs parallel astronomical cross-identification over catalogs using extended SQL and commodity clusters; cohort-query systems use alternative evaluation schemes and columnar databases; relational notebooks integrate notebooks with database processing; and database mapping systems support separation.

A further strand analyzes arXiv and scholarly repositories, including announcement-position effects, author identifiers, citation impact, peer review, and long-term web-resource availability.

869c00927f59f47aaa44476bd305972efece7988.text:
## Recommendation, Visual Features, and Streaming Graph Methods

This community centers on recommender systems, sequential recommendation, visual artwork recommendation, and scalable graph similarity.

**Telepath**, deployed in JD’s recommender and advertising systems, uses deep neural networks and a recurrent neural network to model user interests from browsed items. It improved gross merchandise value and return on investment. Sequential matrix completion addresses user-product recommendation with a gamma process factor model and posterior-focused bandit policies, including Information-Directed Sampling and Thompson Sampling; recommendations target reward, while finite-horizon regret remains challenging.

A second cluster develops unbiased similarity estimation for streaming bipartite graphs. Reservoir and weighted sampling, common-neighbor counts, and stream aggregators produce fixed-size estimates of similarity matrices and projected graphs. Arriving edges generate similarity updates, supporting neighborhood-based and item-based recommendation.

Artwork recommendation compares explicit visual features—such as attractiveness, brightness, and texture—with features from pretrained deep neural networks. Using UGallery transactional data, DNN visual features outperform explicit features for recommendation performance and support digital and physical artwork recommendation. Visual descriptor recommendation is an item-based method and produced highly diverse objects, complementing attribute-based recommendation based on person attributes.

Finally, recommender methods support photo lineup assembling for eyewitness identification, where lineup fairness is important. Deep neural networks also support short-text matching, while forensic technicians provided evaluations of visual and attribute-based recommendation methods.

d2bfcb32303cc5997c9c6e56865fd20ab7169027.text:
## Community Report: Relational Data, Learning, and Scholarly Infrastructure

This community centers on relational database systems, their theory, and applications to data quality, learning, and scientific communication. Database instances are modeled as relations, with keys and independence atoms supporting integrity and improved data quality. Join processing is a major systems theme: classical block nested-loop, hash, grace, and sort-merge joins are complemented by worst-case-optimal algorithms for multiway equijoins, using degree information to improve running times. Cohort query processing, feature-extraction queries, batch aggregates, B-tree indexes, columnar evaluation, and relational notebooks extend practical database analysis.

Relational learning studies schema-independent, sample-based, and query-based learners that define new relations, while relational classifiers and collective inference address networked data. The DB category provides formal semantics through database instances, GLAV mappings, the power-view monad, and functorial semantics.

Data curation connects spreadsheets, Jupyter, repair techniques, and singleton operations; collaborative patching enhances Web-of-Data quality. Applications include SkyQuery for astronomical cross-identification, stream LSH for quality-aware search over endless streams, and database-backed cohort and churn analysis.

A parallel scholarly-infrastructure theme concerns arXiv as a preprint and research-communication platform, linked to author identifiers, peer review, citation and URL-availability analysis, and proposed modernization.

25721e06606871824d59d4669a034ff2816f48f9.text:
## Privacy, Surprise, and Explainable Recommendation Systems

This community focuses on recommender systems, emphasizing accuracy, diversity, privacy, explainability, and surprising recommendations. A theory-guided recommender system, inspired by human memory theory and activation process modeling, produces recommendations evaluated by surprise, recommendation accuracy, and diversity. Normalised surprise uses maximum and minimum potential surprise—estimated with a greedy algorithm—and shows consistent behavior across distance functions, recommendation algorithms, and data representations. It is analyzed using the MovieLens dataset.

Selective Privacy Preserving SP2 separates public and private ratings. Public ratings build an initial recommendation model, while private ratings remain on the user’s device and fine-tune personalized models. SP2 aims to improve accuracy and is evaluated through a user survey concerning willingness to share ratings under user-controlled privacy.

Another theme is category-based recommendation. Hierarchical latent tree analysis and HLTA forests learn hierarchical item categories from implicit feedback data, enabling efficient browsing, category-based recommendations, recommendation explainability, and automatic item-taxonomy skeleton creation. These recommendations preserve accuracy with little compromise, increase diversity, and help mitigate choice overload.

The Hikester event-management application integrates a recommender system, spam recognition service, parameters optimizer, and project architecture for event creation and invitation. Related applications include tag recommendation. Research is associated with Graz University of Technology’s Institute of Interactive Systems and Data Science.

970dd0478de1c4243216fb9c4196d533945bff02.text:
## Signed Networks, Opinion Dynamics, and Research Diversity

This community centers on signed social networks and opinion dynamics. DeGroot-type averaging and consensus models describe opinion formation, while negative links, biased assimilation, heterogeneous communication, and personal thresholds explain divergence, persistent disagreement, polarization, and opinion neutralization. Structural balance connects signed-graph structure to polarized or clustered beliefs; the frustration index measures distance from balance and partial balance.

A major methodological focus is exact frustration-index computation. Quadratic and linear binary programming, binary linear programming models, valid inequalities, global optimization, and local-search heuristics address this task, which is related to MAXCUT and other NP-hard graph problems. These methods are evaluated on random and real signed networks.

The community also studies edge-sign inference in signed directed networks. Structural balance theory, social status theory, node types, triadic features, and edge-content distributions support signed social network induction, including social-function and relationship-formality induction and address-term clustering.

Phase-transition analysis characterizes changes in convergence, divergence, community detectability, and asymptotic detection accuracy. Thresholds depend on inter- and within-community connection probabilities and community size.

Finally, research profiles and publication portfolios are mapped with customized science maps. Stirling and modified Stirling indices measure knowledge diversification and research-performance diversity, including organizational units and university comparisons. Recommender algorithms, refugee-crisis discussions, and online collective behaviour provide applied settings.

154fe572bbf3f204bd511431abca754c25dd2f48.text:
## Signed Networks, Opinion Dynamics, and Polarization

This community centers on opinion formation and evolution in signed social networks, where friendly and antagonistic relationships shape convergence, divergence, polarization, and neutralization. Structural balance theory links signed-graph structure to polarized opinions, belief-boundary clustering, and persistent fluctuations when balance is absent. The frustration index measures distance from balance, with exact computation formulated through binary or quadratic binary programming, valid inequalities, prioritized branching, local search, MaxCut, and integer-programming optimization; Gurobi supports these computations.

DeGroot averaging provides a baseline for opinion dynamics and opinion formation, while negative links, biased assimilation, boomerang effects, heterogeneous thresholds, cognitive mechanisms, and repulsive interactions extend the modeling framework. Convergence is studied in expectation, mean-square, and almost-sure senses, including phase transitions governed by graph structure and model parameters.

A signed social network induction model infers edge signs from exchanged content, using edge-content distributions, triadic features, and address-term clustering to infer social functions and relation formality. The community also connects polarization with recommender algorithms, random walks, collective identities, and common vocabulary. Modified Stirling indices assess research-profile polarization, publication portfolios, diversity, and interdisciplinarity, while community-detectability phase transitions and signed-network datasets support empirical analysis.

2b6d1403fe9ad39ad749b553eaa677bd51cbd39e.text:
## Indexing, Approximate Search, and Data-Intensive Analytics

This community centers on efficient indexing, approximate search, and scalable query processing. Locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) supports approximate nearest-neighbor and *r*-near-neighbor reporting with sublinear query complexity, while tunable and improved variants address real-time processing. It is applied to earthquake detection, support-data similarity search, community-core discovery, and real-time graph systems.

Inverted indexes represent sparse term-document matrices through postings lists and support ranked top-*k* retrieval, copy detection, and product search. Their high memory requirements motivate collection partitioning, factorization-based lossless compression, and learned index structures. Learned indexes use models to predict record positions and are evaluated as alternatives to B-trees, hash indexes, bitmap indexes, and other traditional structures.

Bitmap indexes, compressed bitmaps, roaring bitmaps, run-length encoding, and variable-byte encoding target compact representation and fast logical operations. Systems such as PRETTI, Lucene, Anserini, and HDIdx support retrieval and indexing workloads.

The community also addresses correctness and approximate analytics: false positives and negatives arise in metagenomic algorithms and detection tasks, with multiple-testing, permutation, and holdout corrections providing control. iCam combines sampling, neural-network selection, and learning-based planning for bounded-error object counting on embedded hardware. ArrayBridge provides scalable, version-deduplicated array access across scientific formats and HPC workflows.

6bbb59f41e8095cff8357391a8fcc80941f3621b.text:
## Influence Maximization and Network Diffusion

This community centers on **influence maximization**, which selects seed nodes or users to maximize expected influence spread in network diffusion, especially for viral marketing. It is studied under the **independent cascade**, **linear threshold**, triggering, awareness, and two-phase diffusion models, with spread sometimes represented by a discrete-time Markov chain. Extensions address time-critical deadlines, targeted propagation, multiple products or behaviors, adaptive seeding, network uncertainty, intrinsic nodal activation, audience or seed diversification, influence limitation, and fairness-related disparity.

Because the task is generally NP-hard, **submodularity**, monotonicity, and budget constraints support greedy and approximate solutions with approximation ratios or guarantees. Key methods include adaptive greedy, greedy approximation, stochastic optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, reverse influence sampling, hybrid sampling, and scalable algorithms such as **TIM**, **IMM**, **SSA**, **IRIE**, and **QuickIM**. Comparative independent cascade and weighted cascade variants model interacting or valued influence.

Related applications include coupon and profit maximization, opinion maximization, multi-winner contests, and influence estimation. **Networkit** provides high-performance network analysis, while real-world social networks and real and synthetic datasets support evaluation. Metrics include influence spread, approximation factor, centrality indices, balanced index, and group performance index.

d5afeabd9e72e495ac9f9fc6c6913574f1272eca.text:
## Network Spreading, Reliability, and Inference

This community centers on spreading processes in contact, temporal, uncertain, and social networks. Epidemic thresholds characterize stability: they depend on network structure, degree–degree correlation, contact adaptation, and non-backtracking eigenvalues, while aggregated static networks provide approximations whose accuracy improves with reduced temporal volatility. Multiplex spreading may occur even when every layer is below its individual threshold. Applications include influenza, pathogen diffusion, epidemic detection, causative-network identification, vaccination, and targeted or node immunization. Spectral-radius reduction supports epidemic-spread control; GreedyWalk and primal-dual algorithms provide approximation guarantees, while local subgraphs support spectral-radius bounds.

A second focus is reliability maximization through edge addition, including budgeted, multiple-source/multiple-target, and sensor-network settings. Uncertain graphs model probabilistic edge existence and source–target reachability, linking reliability to social influence maximization and social-graph anonymization.

Link prediction spans static, dynamic, and add/remove settings, evaluated by link-prediction accuracy. Network-based inference supports personal recommendation, with global ranking corresponding to its infinite-iteration limit; reference-based ground truth is constructed from computer-science publication data. Theoretical analysis connects inference and ranking, calculates outbreak size, and is supported by experimental validation. Other themes include k-truss minimization, communicability, political classification, and network stability.

f222bc07a2c55a3e379a3b8673787982d71e10fe.text:
## Network Diffusion, Epidemics, and Scalable Graph Analytics

This community centers on modeling, controlling, and inferring spreading processes on networks. SIR, SIRS, SIS, and compartmental models represent disease, information, adoption, and interacting epidemic processes; awareness can reduce total infections and eradication time, while network segregation, finite memory, attention, and user types shape hoax spread. The protection resource allocation framework distributes preventive and corrective resources under budget constraints, using dynamic systems theory and extending to generalized epidemics and uncertain contact networks.

Influence analysis includes VoteRank, Clusterrank, hill climbing, and degree discount for selecting decentralized spreaders. Spectral radius and normalized Laplacian properties support containment: GreedyWalk and primal-dual methods reduce spectral radius with approximation guarantees.

Source localization uses infection timestamps, partial observations, candidate selection, and infection source estimators. OJC finds a minimum-radius Jordan cover for heterogeneous SIR diffusion, while minimum-distance centrality provides a baseline.

The community also covers scalable graph structure and prediction. I/O-efficient and semi-external core decomposition methods target web-scale graphs, and peeling algorithms discover dense bipartite subgraphs using butterfly motifs. Nameling derives name relations from co-occurrence graphs and query logs, measuring structural similarity. Link prediction, dynamic graph updates, deep hashing, and layered networks address prediction accuracy, user-product networks, and social-web applications.

0ab44dbfd01f835f063273da371378dba88114d7.text:
## Epidemic Diffusion, Source Localization, and Graph Analytics

This community centers on modeling, controlling, and analyzing spreading processes in networks. SIS, SIR, and SIRS models describe infection diffusion, infectious recovery, and interacting epidemic processes. Awareness models, represented by discrete-time Markov chains and mean-field approximations, reduce total infections and eradication time and can exhibit metastable states. Compartmental models incorporate network segregation, finite memory, attention limitations, and gullible or skeptic users in hoax spreading.

Protection resource allocation frameworks distribute preventive resources to reduce spreading rates and corrective resources to increase recovery, using SIS models and extending to generalized epidemic models and uncertain contact networks. Spectral radius provides epidemic thresholds and supports graph-intervention methods such as GreedyWalk, edge removal, and primal-dual algorithms.

Another major focus is infection source identification under partial observations. OJC uses candidate selection and minimum-radius Jordan covers, while infection source estimators and minimum distance centrality provide alternative approaches.

Graph mining includes dense subgraph discovery using butterfly motifs and peeling algorithms, core and k-shell decomposition, and I/O-efficient methods for web-scale graphs. Nameling uses co-occurrence graphs of given and city names, structural graph similarity, and query logs. Additional topics include link prediction, synchronization over SO(2) and Z2, layered-network prediction, and infectious-recovery modeling of user adoption and abandonment.

125d4d71366534932bcbc7367890465b4513f904.text:
## Query Evaluation for Temporal Video Analysis

This community focuses on evaluating temporal queries over video feeds using computer-vision-based object detection and tracking. Streaming frames provide the input from which detected objects, classes, and tracked identifiers are extracted.

Intermediate data generation organizes these detections into structured intermediate data for query evaluation. The MFS and SSG methods organize detected objects within this layer and reduce the number of objects and frames considered during evaluation. State traversal further prunes irrelevant objects and frames while maintaining query-evaluation states; SSG processes incoming frames against the SSG structure.

Temporal queries identify temporal segments and object patterns in video feeds. They can express requirements involving the joint appearance of objects, including object co-occurrence, and incorporate physical effects of object occlusion during video capture. Overall, object detection and tracking supplies the data, intermediate data generation structures it, and MFS, SSG, and state traversal improve the efficiency of query evaluation.

48147766ffe06ee400a9a335aea2c9f6d028fafd.text:
## Graph Partitioning and Graph Similarity Methods

This community covers two related areas: network community detection through minimum-conductance graph partitioning, and graph similarity search in graph databases.

Minimum conductance graph partitioning is formulated as a pseudo-Boolean optimization problem and is NP-hard. It optimizes conductance and is closely related to community detection. A memetic algorithm solves this problem using local search to generate initial solutions, a steady-state evolutionary phase, and two intensification subroutines. It outperforms multi-start local search and compared genetic algorithms; both are used as comparison targets.

For graph similarity search, graph edit distance is a common similarity measure and an NP-hard computation. Graph branch distance compares branches between graphs and can be computed in polynomial time, providing a basis for efficiently estimating graph edit distance. The probabilistic GED estimation method models branch variations caused by graph edit operations and estimates graph edit distance from graph branch distance. It is evaluated on real and synthetic datasets.

Graph branch distance supports graph similarity search, which is identified as a fundamental operation in graph databases.

410116e1d01e9846de8edb3e81f9ee8cc212ccbe.text:
## Community Report: Motifs, Feature Learning, and Recommendation Systems

This community links graph motifs, time-series analysis, predictive rule mining, and recommender systems.

**Network motifs** represent graph-topology patterns, particularly in scale-free networks whose degree distributions follow a power law. Their counts and fluctuations are asymptotically characterized, while a variational principle formulates dominant-motif identification as an optimization problem. Higher-order motif features capture detailed topology around node pairs and outperform prior feature-learning methods. Feature selection identifies motifs characteristic of spam campaigns. Experiments use Weibo cascades and Flixster movie ratings.

For time series, **catch22** reduces the 4,791-feature hctsa library to 22 interpretable properties. It is evaluated on 93 classification datasets, scales near-linearly with series length, and reduces computation time by about 1,000-fold, with an approximately 7% average reduction in classification accuracy.

In recommendation, **FLEN** uses field-wise bi-interaction pooling and incorporates DiceFactor. Deployed in Meitu’s commercial recommender system, it targets CTR prediction, improving CTR by 5.19% over NFM while reducing computation time and memory usage. A two-stage session-based method uses Candidate Rank Embedding to rerank candidates, integrates attention-based global preference and current interest, and improves Recall@20, MRR@20, and online CTR on Fashion-Similar, extending STAMP and NARM.

Finally, FP-Growth supports fuzzy association-rule mining for dengue prediction, outperforming Apriori in execution time and memory usage.

e115347c81a844cccc3d89560cfaad8ed0b8bef9.text:
## Summarization, Fairness, and Neural Conversation Systems

This community covers text summarization, conversational response modeling, and evaluation. Text summarization includes extractive methods, which select source units such as microblogs, and abstractive methods, which fuse source content. A joint extractive-compressive summarization model first extracts sentences, uses summary-state representations, and compresses them. It avoids difficulties of abstractive methods, produces more concise summaries than extractive approaches, and achieves state-of-the-art results on CNN/DailyMail and Newsroom. Human evaluation finds its summaries concise and informative; ROUGE is a traditional automatic metric. Oracle compressive summaries are derived from CNN/DailyMail reference summaries.

Fairness-preserving summarization addresses the tendency of summarization algorithms to represent groups differently from their input distributions. It compares group representation in summaries with group distributions in microblog datasets, considering socially salient user groups and their exposure or visibility while maintaining summary quality.

For multi-turn conversation, the hybrid neural conversation model combines retrieval-based response selection with generation-based response production. Retrieval performance is limited by the response repository, while generation is compared with knowledge-grounded neural conversation. The model is evaluated through automatic metrics and human evaluation, including on Foursquare data. Intelligent personal assistant systems are identified as supporting multi-turn conversations with users.

ce7f19600de92f402a9a625670e8ad2c5085839b.text:
## Community Report: Spatial, Social, Political, and Biomedical Graph Mining

This community connects methods for analyzing spatial behavior, online communities, political organizations, healthcare, and biomedical knowledge.

For location-based social networks such as Foursquare, **GeoSAGE** supports spatial item recommendation by modeling personal interests and regional crowd preferences, using spatial item co-occurrence, content, and a spatial pyramid. Related systems address check-in prediction and social, time-aware spatial keyword queries through Netr trees and scores for geography, keywords, visiting time, and social relationships. Accessibility computation uses quad-trees to evaluate origins, destinations, and public transport access.

Online-community research studies antisocial behavior, trolling, banned users, sockpuppetry, and early antisocial-user identification. User contributions, badge systems, community feedback, and tolerance connect participation incentives with community health.

Political-network work analyzes Italian Senate and Brazilian roll-call data. Mixture models, EM optimization, and the Political DNA metric characterize voting, party affinity, fragmentation, discipline, coalitions, isolation, and partisan polarization. Arrange seeks balanced party configurations while preserving discipline.

Biomedical and healthcare topics include Kinderminer for transcription-factor discovery and drug repositioning, nanopublications involving genes, proteins, and pathways, and collaboration structures related to care quality and cost. Other methods include knowledge-graph embeddings, latent-state models, sentiment analysis, and recommendation systems.

5cc8a10883080a1b1c3c8396d6666a40fd04d4ae.text:
## Graph Analytics, Crowdsourcing, and Evolving Networks

This community spans scalable graph analysis, dynamic indexing, cohesive subgraphs, crowdsourcing, and citation-network modeling.

**Graph structure and algorithms:** k-truss and k-core decomposition identify cohesive subgraphs; incremental computation, update algorithms, and maintenance support changing networks. Network sparsification uses algebraic distance, multilevel control, and matrix–vector multiplication to filter local or global edges. Paired threshold graphs are characterized by vertex-weight inequalities and forbidden induced subgraphs, with polynomial-time recognition. Graph coloring, graph edit distance, similarity search, and probabilistic GED estimation address structural comparison and reconstruction.

**Systems and scalability:** Networkit provides high-performance network analysis through C++ kernels, a Python front end, shared-memory parallelism, efficient data structures, and centrality analytics. LIAH adaptively builds HDFS-block indexes during MapReduce jobs, reducing indexing overhead and improving workloads as indexes converge.

**Crowdsourcing and human computation:** Task assignment, batching, selection, verification, and specialty-aware or multi-skill team formation support spatial and knowledge-intensive crowdsourcing. SmartCrowd, hyperlocal spatial crowdsourcing, online heuristics, and human-assisted graph search address practical workflows, although many associated optimization problems are NP-hard.

**Pattern and network mining:** USPT and HUSP-ULL mine high-utility sequential patterns using individualized thresholds, utility bounds, trees, and pruning. ReforCite models citation copying and bibliographic-network densification, matching observed diameter and directed-triangle behavior.

ee379bad108a1f73bbfc00acaec32ce2ff2b43ea.text:
## Community Report: Entity Understanding, Question Routing, and Crowdsourced Tasks

This community connects book-impact analysis, entity retrieval, community question answering, and crowdsourcing optimization.

**Pangloss** is a production entity-disambiguation and linking system for noisy, loosely structured text. It combines probabilistic linear-time key-phrase identification, a semantic similarity engine based on context-dependent document embeddings, and a tiered local embedded database. It supports streaming disambiguation and improves F1 by more than 5% over comparison systems. Contextual Named Entity Retrieval similarly uses free-text context, entity profiles, and term relevance feedback weighted by importance; it is related to entity disambiguation and list question answering.

**QDEE** estimates question difficulty and user expertise for community question answering, using competition graphs and social agony to support question routing. It is evaluated on Yahoo! Answers and Stack Overflow, where user feedback also contributes to profiles.

The crowdsourcing cluster includes Amazon Mechanical Turk and CrowdFlower. Specialty-aware task assignment in spatial crowdsourcing matches workers’ skills to requirements and budgets, models fine-grained skill charges, and maximizes completed tasks, though it is NP-hard. In-Route Task Selection chooses tasks along a worker’s preferred path under a travel budget; skyline methods yield exact non-dominated solutions.

Finally, Altmetric.com and PlumX analyze book social attention, using sources such as Google Books, Wikipedia, DOI identifiers, and library datasets for bibliometric analysis.

7673c0406d6b201e7ea0cbb3737fb38945ed9899.text:
## Graph Data Systems, Analytics, and Streaming Methods

This community centers on graph data management, analysis, generation, and search. Graph databases store complex and large sparse relational datasets, support property-graph data models, and enable topology analysis and common graph algorithms. Algebraic property graphs provide a mathematically rigorous bridge where graph databases generally lack a standard algebra. Neo4j, SNAP, STINGER, and other execution or programming systems support graph processing; SNAP provides more than 140 graph algorithms.

Graph analysis includes single-source distance and shortest-path queries, graph algebra, provenance analytics, breach detection, and analysis of massive social graphs. Graph generators learn from source graphs and compare generated and original graphs through graph properties, while addressing implicit and explicit modeling bias. Kronecker product graph models and graphlet estimation support synthetic or sampled graph evaluation.

A second major theme is data streams. Count-min sketch, count-min log sketch, Bloom filters, stable and biased sampling-based Bloom filters, and approximate counters provide sublinear-space frequency estimation, deduplication, and approximate duplicate detection, with false-positive/negative rates and relative error as key metrics. Variance and quantile sketching support approximate query processing.

Additional topics include time-varying and temporal interaction networks, random walks, flow computation, frequent pattern and subgraph mining, query suggestion, task representation, and interactive information retrieval.

cb9b9b763270d90fb1538ae9e42958d486de050e.text:
## Query Processing, Graph Matching, and Incremental Analytics

This community centers on efficient query processing, graph pattern matching, and ranking over graph, relational, XML, and text data.

Graph pattern matching includes subgraph isomorphism, graph simulation, dual simulation, and triple simulation. Investigative simulation adds categorical node labels, partial-match pruning and completion, and top-*k* prioritization. Graph queries use parallel adjacency lists, while GraphChi and GraphChi DB support graph storage and fast insertion. Graph database views store precalculated matches and improve query performance.

Incremental view maintenance addresses changing materialized and graph database views. LinView, delta-query derivation, matrix factorizations, and incremental graph pattern matching reduce the cost of re-evaluation. IncNRC+ and NC0 concern incremental maintenance for positive nested relational calculus.

Query performance is also linked to join-order selection, optimization heuristics, secondary indexing, in-memory compression, multicore parallelism, and tuple compaction. Apache AsterixDB, HadoopDB, RDF stores, and LSM-tree systems provide evaluation contexts.

A second theme is retrieval and interpretability: document ranking uses term proximity, proximity-based ranking, neural and context-aware models, and query features. LIME and retrieval-model interpretability explain rankings, while DeepBase queries hidden units to analyze neural-network behavior. Graph streams are summarized using sketches, sampling, and hashing for query processing.

54699a994fc462a6a3343007192107c9201b0f8b.text:
## Community Report: Sequential Recommendation and Polarized Networks

This community covers two themes: personalized recommendation systems and analysis of polarized information networks.

**HierTCN** performs dynamic next-item recommendation using temporal convolutional networks. It models within-session interactions and sequential behavior across sessions, supported by a data-caching scheme and a queue-based mini-batch generator for efficient single-GPU training. It is evaluated on Pinterest and XING. **AttList** targets user-generated list recommendation on platforms such as YouTube, Spotify, Pinterest, and Goodreads. It hierarchically aggregates items into lists and lists into user preferences, using self-attentive aggregation to capture item and list consistency. AttList improves NDCG, Recall@k, and Precision@k; nDCG also underlies an explainability metric.

The **Vevo network**, constructed from YouTube music videos, contains 60,740 videos and associated viewing dynamics. It examines attention flow estimation, attention allocation, recommendation links, and bow-tie structure.

The second theme concerns vaccine discourse. A repeated mutual interaction network distinguishes pro- and anti-vaccine profiles. Anti-vaccine profiles primarily link to alternative health product sites, while YouTube links are characteristic of these profiles. Network polarization is assessed with assortativity coefficients of 0.8 and 0.813, and media PCA scores computed by principal component analysis; Fox News appears in the largest right community.

bcd0aa0333d9005f4147228feb673ff364da7ca3.text:
## Community Report: Incremental Graphs, Querying, and Stream Summarization

This community connects efficient query processing, graph analytics, dynamic data management, and spatiotemporal discovery.

Incremental view maintenance updates materialized and graph database views using delta query derivation, incremental graph pattern matching, and generalized discrimination networks. Linview and incNRC+ support efficient maintenance for positive nested relational calculus; matrix factorizations can reduce maintenance cost relative to full re-evaluation.

Graph querying includes graph pattern matching, subgraph isomorphism, dual simulation, and investigative simulation. The latter uses categorical node labels, partial-match pruning and completion, and top-k ranking. GraphChi and GraphChi DB use parallel adjacency lists for compact storage, fast insertion, vertex attributes, online queries, and scalable analytical graph computation.

For graph streams, gLava provides a probabilistic graph model and graph sketch with theoretical error bounds. gSketch combines data-stream synopses with sketch partitioning for query estimation. Hash- and sampling-based summarization, including gLava, target linear construction time and constant update cost.

Query performance is addressed through speed partitioning, partitioned indexing, in-memory compression, multicore parallelism, and SPARQL optimization heuristics informed by semantics and evaluation complexity. Other topics include proximity-based document ranking, XML redistribution over P2P networks, and convoy discovery over trajectory data using filter refinement and distance bounds for planning and carpooling.

604fcaa8b741b902228076570938f6c8241f4c78.text:
## Community Report: Entity, Hashtag, and Sequential Social-Media Retrieval

This community centers on retrieval and analysis of entities, relationships, hashtags, and emerging social-media activity.

**Entity-relationship retrieval** uses the *early fusion* design pattern to build extensible entity and relationship representations and support multi-relationship queries. Wikipedia supplies entity representations, while ClueWeb-09-B provides documents and FACC1 entity linking for extracting relationships. The approach is evaluated with a collection of 469 E-R queries.

**MixedTrails** analyzes heterogeneous sequential traces using a generative mixed transition Markov chain. It applies Bayesian hypothesis comparison, with Bayesian priors encoding hypotheses and Bayes factors calculated from marginal likelihoods. Wikipedia and Flickr provide empirical evaluation data; Wikipedia also represents collective memory and the incorporation of entities after public emergence.

**Hashtag-centric immersive search** integrates information across online social networks, using hashtags to aggregate and organize multimodal items from systems such as Flickr and YouTube. Its pipeline includes hashtag representation, hashtag clustering, and hashtag demonstration, displayed through a cluster-hashtag-item hierarchy. Trending event queries support quantitative and qualitative validation; YouTube contributes a 5.3-million-video dataset.

The community also addresses entity emergence analysis and tracking, including bursty and delayed emergence, plus spatial visual search evaluated with Flickr, Google Street View, and GeoUGV datasets.

57bcc8637d4337ff00b9c69177d445ed04402311.text:
## Recommendation in Spatial, Trust, and Fashion Domains

This community centers on personalized recommendation under sparse data, heterogeneous relations, and cold-start conditions. In location-based social networks, POI recommendation uses user check-in data to infer preferences and rank top-k points of interest. The spatiotemporal-aware representation (STA) generalizes knowledge-graph embedding by translating user embeddings toward POI embeddings while modeling spatial and temporal information. It improves robustness to sparse data, handles cold-start problems, and achieves state-of-the-art recommendation accuracy.

For top-N recommendation, the trust-aware collaborative denoising autoencoder learns representations from sparse rating and trust data. Its weighted hidden layer balances representation importance, while correlative regularization bridges user preferences from different perspectives and improves recommendations for cold users.

A second thread addresses heterogeneous networks. Weighted random-walk sampling, applied to weighted heterogeneous networks, improves model-generation efficiency and recommendation accuracy. It generates weighted and extended meta-paths that capture additional user and item information for multi-relational factorization and hybrid recommender models.

The community also covers online fashion recommendation. The LSTM customer model uses recurrent and feedforward networks: article embeddings in a learned fashion space support prediction of client style vectors from purchase sequences. The fashion sales dataset from Zalando’s 100k frequent shoppers supports backtesting, with popularity ranking as a baseline.

265f3555b8b84c17dbdf2c1ada71e8fea2ecc49f.text:
## Graph Clustering, Network Distance, and Efficient Graph Analytics

This community centers on methods for understanding network structure, clustering, distance, and query processing.

**Hierarchical clustering** supports core community detection, compact communities, and moving-point clustering across snapshots. LexDFS-based and agglomerative variants include admissible methods governed by value and transformation axioms, with universal upper and lower bounds. HAMUHI performs multi-scale hierarchical community detection, checks parameterized community definitions, and is evaluated on real and synthetic benchmark networks.

**Network distance** is studied through graph distance, length spectra, non-backtracking cycles, and degrees of separation. Facebook-network analyses examine distance distributions and large-scale graph-distance computation; an average distance of 3.74 is reported in one analysis, while another reports 4.74. Randomized shortest-path frameworks connect shortest-path, random-walk, and current-flow methods through Boltzmann path distributions.

**Graphlets** characterize local and global topology, support network characterization, and provide sufficient statistics for exponential-family random graph models. Graphlet decomposition and parallel/global counting are implemented alongside the ERGM and `ergm.graphlets` R packages.

The community also covers efficient analytics: GSketch estimates graph-stream queries using partitioned sketches; ShallowFish and DeepFish process predicate expressions; PRAO answers travel-time path queries using indexing and pruning; and column-oriented datastores support ad hoc queries and interactive web interfaces. Coarse-grained state detection combines graph distance and clustering for social-temporal and functional-connectivity data.

6fd36fda48c4e519ecf2dca69d2570700b8bc2a1.text:
# Community Report: Context-Aware Personalization, Search, and Auction Forecasting

This community centers on modeling context, user interests, and market behavior with neural and statistical methods.

**Personalization and recommendation:** HCRNN is a recurrent neural network evaluated on MovieLens, LastFM, and CiteULike. It models interest drift using hierarchical context containing global, local, and temporary interests, complemented by bi-channel attention. Personalization uses purchase histories, query characteristics, and product-search sessions to determine when user-query pairs benefit from personalization. The zero attention model, evaluated on commercial product search logs, uses a novel attention mechanism and outperforms personalized product retrieval models.

**Search and extreme classification:** CARL encodes context with a recurrent neural network, attention, module embeddings, and auxiliary self-supervision for aggregated search. It supports selecting heterogeneous modules such as news, images, and videos alongside blue links. AttentionXML and HAXMLNet apply multi-label attention to extreme multi-label text classification; HAXMLNet also uses hierarchical structure and hyperbolic embeddings.

**Product analysis:** Rule-based natural language processing extracts product affordances from Amazon Kindle e-reader reviews and timestamps. Conjoint analysis, inspired by the Kano model, compares changing user expectations and supports product improvement strategies.

**Advertising:** Deep Landscape Forecasting predicts market price distributions in real-time bidding using recurrent networks, the probability chain rule, negative likelihood losses, and survival analysis for censorship caused by second-price auctions.

8da97f8f7b0c093d44c359df25234b9b5df524a2.text:
## Community Report: Search Interaction, Neural Ranking, and Weak Supervision

This community spans search interaction modeling, user-response prediction, query suggestion, weakly supervised text classification, and early Parkinson’s disease detection.

The Click Sequence Model (CSM) uses an encoder–decoder architecture with attention to compute contextual embeddings and predict clicked-result positions, click sequences, click counts, and interaction order on search engine results pages. It is optimized by maximum likelihood estimation and achieves state-of-the-art unordered click prediction.

For user response prediction on multi-field categorical data, Product-based Neural Network (PNN) models feature interactions using one-hot encoded inputs. Product Network in Network (PIN) generalizes PNN through a kernel-product, net-in-net architecture, improving AUC and online CTR in A/B testing.

Weakly supervised neural text classification combines deep neural networks with a pseudo-document generator and self-training. Seed information produces pseudo-labeled documents for model pre-training, while self-training bootstraps from unlabeled data.

In health applications, mouse-tracking data supports Parkinson’s disease detection. Random forests combine expert-generated and unsupervised learned features, achieving an AUC of 0.92 and supporting early-stage detection.

Finally, candidate generation forms the first stage of a two-stage pipeline, producing query-suggestion candidates from information sources and test collections. Query suggestion generation supports task-based search and can be performed without relying on a search engine.

2af6a25375f0a14b3a509c606cfaff59059edab5.text:
## Personalized Recommendation and eCommerce Search

This community centers on recommendation, personalized product search, and industrial eCommerce systems. Recommender pipelines commonly use successive matching and ranking stages: matching retrieves candidate items relevant to user interests, while ranking orders them. Multi-interest representations encode different aspects of users’ interests for matching.

MIND models diverse interests with multiple user vectors, using a multi-interest extractor, label-aware attention, and capsule routing. It was evaluated on the Tmall dataset and deployed on major Mobile Tmall App homepage traffic. NRPA is another neural recommendation approach, using personalized attention in review and user/item encoders to learn personalized user and item representations; it was evaluated on five recommendation datasets.

A PGNN addresses personalized session-based recommendation and next-click prediction from sequential behavior. It models user- and item-specific transition relationships, uses dot-product attention to incorporate historical sessions, and is associated with a bipartite user–repository network also modeled for GitHub.

Other recommendation approaches include embedding MLPs, memory-based nearest neighbors, similarity measures, and dissimilarity-enhanced computation. The ECOM’19 eCommerce workshop covered product search, data challenges, and related applications; its challenge used real-world eCommerce data and accepted 24 of 38 submissions (63%). Personalized product search applies personalization directly to eCommerce product search.

30e004298fe80fb9ab99dfc8684bea68a675b8ea.text:
## Community Report: Polarization, Participation, and Recommendation Systems

This community links research on Reddit behavior, online polarization, knowledge markets, and personalized recommendation.

Reddit datasets from 2008, 2014–2015, and a 60K-plus article Reddit News collection support behavioral pattern analysis, statistical post analysis, user-interaction modeling, and studies of social-media evolution. The Reddit policy banning r/fatpeoplehate, identified as a hateful subreddit, produced sustained reductions in affected users’ interactions and measurable post-banning behavior. Forum banning is associated with reducing hateful content.

Polarization research models the emergence of polarized communities through bounded-confidence and opinion-dynamics models. Engagement, trust in information broadcasters, selective exposure, initial conditions, majority rule, and conflicting ideas shape opinion formation and polarization; configuration-model analysis reproduces splits observed in karate and dolphins networks. Polarized communities may also facilitate misinformation. Polarization rank measures community polarization across countries.

Knowledge markets, including StackExchange, are analyzed with interpretable economic production models. Cobb–Douglas models explain content generation, whose output shows diminishing returns and constant elasticity; participant growth can produce diseconomies of scale.

Recommendation research combines deep neural, sequence-based, and hybrid item-representation models using content and user-engagement features. Multi-armed-bandit reranking optimizes engagement, while cumulative long-term reward can represent click-through rate, satisfaction, and revenue. Production performance is evaluated through online experiments, including FINN.no marketplace recommendations and temporal generalization across periods.

ac3b337da6d4b2294b0c6f2c0e65add76564eaa2.text:
## Recommendation Systems, CTR Prediction, and Digital Libraries

This community links personalized recommendation, research-article discovery, and advertising systems through effectiveness measurement.

**Dionysius** is a personalized recommendation system deployed as part of a job recommendation engine. It uses a hierarchical graphical model, incorporates user–item interaction signals, and learns a hidden-fields vector for each user. This vector replaces a user profile vector in a user-profile content-based model, while content-based features leverage existing infrastructure. Dionysius was evaluated through offline experiments and validated with online A/B testing.

For research articles, recommender systems are built for digital libraries and reference managers. **Mr DLib**, a recommendation-as-a-service provider, delivers related-article recommendations in **Sowiport**, the digital library operated or provided by **GESIS**. Choice overload is associated with displaying larger numbers of recommendations; prior work also examines recommendation counts for media recommendations.

The community also covers **CTR prediction** for sponsored search advertising and promoted listings, including Etsy’s seller advertising campaigns. Ensemble learning combines historical and behavioral signals for older listings and content-based features for new listings. Click-through rate measures recommendation effectiveness: Mr DLib achieved an average rate of **0.12%**, based on interactions from **3–4 million delivered recommendations**.

43a0eef677bf5ab84d7e4c9c36dbf88ac11d3052.text:
## Semantic Indexing and Scientific Recommendation Systems

This community connects content-based quality estimation, semantic annotation, digital libraries, and scientific recommendation delivery.

Content-based quality estimation assesses automatic subject indexing using a deep multi-layered regression architecture that incorporates content-based indicators. It was evaluated on law and economics text collections, including very short texts, and identifies data subsets with improved document-level recall. The resulting filtering supports operative information retrieval systems.

Automatic subject indexing produces semantic annotations through multi-label classification, assigning subject annotations with confidence scores. These annotations support useful digital library resources. Digital libraries, reference managers, and other academic products are related application contexts; recommendations-as-a-service APIs can integrate with academic products.

Mr. DLib implements a scientific recommender system and generates recommendations for research articles. It provides a recommendations-as-a-service API, uses GESIS Sowiport and JabRef, and is released as open source. Over two years, it delivered 94 million recommendations, achieving an average click-through rate of 0.12%.

e65a00bde0c43d1e0d3390fc1d976665d1646417.text:
## Personalization, Advertising, and Content Intelligence

This community connects real-time news personalization, advertising optimization, content-quality analysis, and user-data valuation.

Immediate personalized news recommendation is a news-personalization task requiring **immediacy**. A decay score accounts for elapsed time and changing interests, while system architecture supports deployment in a production environment, with commercial news delivery data used for offline evaluation. A/B testing and click-through rate evaluate online effectiveness.

**Zorro** operationalizes the Value of Data for targeted advertising, using matrix estimation and extending to explicit user intent. It prices personal data, enables payment for data sharing, and is evaluated on a large ad-click dataset. Dynamic user profiling improves targeting.

Algorithmic ad rewriting uses a sequence-to-sequence neural network trained on more than 114,000 Microsoft Advertising ads. In medical-symptoms and preventative-healthcare advertising, generated ads achieve higher predicted click-through rates for many ads, with increased valence, arousal, and calls to action.

Multimodal quality recognition applies image and text feature extractors within a Siamese network, optimized with rank loss, to produce quality scores for graphic content. This supports content-quality analysis, identifying high-quality content and potentially improving reading-time estimates.

Other forecasting and profiling methods include autoregressive models, linear extrapolation, and article-mention prediction. A hybrid LSTM model recognizes offline activity from tweet data, uses contextual features, supports dynamic profiles, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods with orthogonal validation.

7fc86d79383ff6148feac05af26040ee28ed08a9.text:
## Crowdsourced Entity Resolution and Literature Screening

This community focuses on entity resolution using human judgments and machine-learning methods, with clustering of images as an example task. An uncertain graph model represents uncertain relationships between records, while a possible-worlds model captures independence across different crowdsourcing tasks. Entity resolution can also be formulated as maximum-likelihood clustering.

**HUMO** provides a human-machine framework that allocates entity-resolution work to reduce human cost. Its HUMO optimization problem minimizes human cost subject to quality requirements, aiming for reasonable return on investment.

**PERC** performs probabilistic entity resolution under imperfect crowd judgments. It improves quality and reduces crowdsourcing cost, and provides parameter-free algorithms for selecting the next crowdsourcing question. This “next crowdsourcing” step chooses the record pair expected to most improve the reliability of maximum-likelihood clustering.

The community also applies crowdsourcing to systematic literature reviews, particularly the paper-screening phase. **Phased crowdsourcing** divides the process into phases and is used to improve screening results. Screening design includes test size and labels per paper, while classification functions support screening decisions. **CrowdFlower** is identified as a public crowdsourcing platform facilitating this work.

4f2cfe5e70a3bd364bdbd84e01e1c88ef37eb307.text:
## Community Report: Recommendation, Geo-Experimentation, and Content Intelligence

This community centers on online recommendation, advertising, and experimentation, alongside systems for organizing and interpreting content.

**Recommendation and engagement:** Immediate personalized news recommendation emphasizes immediacy and uses decay scores, system architecture, and commercial news-delivery data for evaluation. Two-stage session-based recommendation applies candidate-rank embeddings and reranking, improving Recall@20, MRR@20, and click-through rate (CTR) over baseline systems such as STAMP and NARM. Contextual rankers, matrix estimation, and Zorro address CTR prediction; CTR-Norepeat reduces click overestimation.
