Algorithmic ad rewriting seeks higher CTR, including in medical-symptom and preventative-healthcare advertising. SAEC compresses embedding matrices through feature clustering and is evaluated on Numerous and QQ Mobile Browser data.

**Experimentation and geography:** A/B testing evaluates recommendation frameworks in production, including under interference, with equality-of-means power analysis. Geocuts supports geo-based experimentation by clustering anonymized mobile-user movement graphs into geographically coherent, balanced regions while minimizing inter-cluster movement; its performance is comparable to designated marketing areas and hand-crafted geo-regions. Geographical regions also capture shared social identity, cohesiveness, and intra-/inter-regional communication.

**Content intelligence:** Story Forest incrementally clusters streaming Chinese news, identifies events, and builds evolving story trees. A hierarchical attention network classifies song lyrics using word-to-song structure and visualizes important words and lines.

c8e34494b2d4efec356678f012ad806138dd4844.text:
## Social Networks: Influence, Privacy, and Structural Algorithms

This community covers social-network influence, link formation, privacy, and network optimization. The DeGroot opinion formation model defines an asymptotic consensus value, computed using eigenvector centrality. External influence, including online news articles, can alter consensus; DIVER counters this by strategically adding a limited number of edges. Perturbation analysis and Markov-chain theory support DIVER, while mean first passage times enable its pseudo-linear-time heuristic.

Influence estimation methods infer peer and external influence from voting times. A Facebook application collected friendship relationships, votes, voting times, and demographics for an opinion poll concerning the 2013 Croatian marriage referendum; methods were validated on simulated and actual data.

Link recommendation and formation use common-neighbor predictors, Adamic-Adar, and local degree. Transitivity explains common-neighbor performance, while global and local degree affect new links and recommendation accuracy, including in two-hop egocentric networks centered on ego nodes.

Other work addresses community search and team formation, extending both to low-tension communities and evaluating community-and-team algorithms. Social-network de-anonymization links anonymous nodes to identities using background or auxiliary information; synthetic and real network data support evaluation. Although more auxiliary information need not increase de-anonymization gain, publishing network data creates privacy risk.

41b89e25971d771d62da3d2520817f990e998fcc.text:
## Recommendation, Ranking, and Algorithm Selection

This community centers on recommender systems, learning-to-rank, and meta-learning.

Collaborative filtering uses implicit feedback for rating prediction and user–entity affinity modeling, while hybrid recommendation and hybrid recommender systems improve predictive accuracy and address item cold start. A Wasserstein autoencoder for collaborative filtering adds mutual-information loss and L1 regularization; it is evaluated on ML-20M, Netflix, and Last.fm, outperforming comparisons on Recall@1, Recall@5, and NDCG@10. Attribute-driven active learning uses item attributes and user rating histories to select users and address item cold start.

A major ranking thread tackles presentation bias in implicit feedback. Counterfactual learning-to-rank motivates SVM PropRank, SVM PropDCG, and Deep PropDCG. These methods use propensity weighting for unbiased training, optimize DCG and other additive ranking metrics, and employ convex-concave optimization or deep networks.

Algorithm-selection research applies metalearning and graph-based metafeatures to characterize collaborative-filtering problems. Comprehensive metafeatures use feature selection, while multicriteria metatargets and Pareto-efficient rankings compare algorithms across evaluation measures.

Applications include patient–doctor matchmaking in primary care, where hybrid recommendation models patient trust and temporal dynamics using consultation histories, and spoken-dialog personalization. User-affinity models use play duration, binarized into implicit labels, and convex weighting functions, evaluated with Spearman correlation on Alexa music-service records.

7f6db4dc66cf487aacd1e82589a51d5fc8c92626.text:
## Recommendation, Retrieval, and Information-Sharing Analysis

This community covers recommender systems, retrieval for disaster relief, and Pinterest sharing and popularity analysis.

**MARS** models users’ diverse interests through a memory component and novel attentional mechanism, learning adaptive user representations with end-to-end training. It provides interpretable recommendation explanations and outperforms competing methods in mean average precision.

**DeepICF** is a deep variant of item-based collaborative filtering and is evaluated on Pinterest and MovieLens. It uses nonlinear neural networks to model higher-order relationships among item pairs, while an attention network improves fine-grained second-order interaction modeling. Item similarity underlies item-based collaborative filtering and item-based recommender systems.

For disaster response, **emergency aid identification and ranking** performs categorical information retrieval over short, multilingual tweets in the Nepal earthquake dataset. A weighted ranking key algorithm ranks classified tweets using weighted top terms, including “need and availability” categories. Non-governmental organizations use the retrieved disaster-relief information; mean average precision is reported as 6.81%.

Pinterest fashion boards support **board popularity prediction** using image and temporal signals. Social signals characterize sharing and borrowing through originality, retention, and production coefficients; temporal signals include inter-copying time, duration of sharing, and speed coefficients. Retention coefficients are among the most discriminatory popularity features.

eea589b1803b0ee6eb4b31d3681e1b8561c61b3f.text:
## Italian Disinformation and Fact-Checking Resources

This community concerns Italian disinformation, its forms, and resources for studying and countering it. Italian disinformation websites produce low-credibility disinformation content, including hoaxes, clickbait, false news, and hyper-partisan stories.

The **HoaxItaly** dataset includes titles and bodies for approximately 37,000 news articles. These articles are published by both Italian disinformation websites and Italian fact-checking websites. A related **tweets** dataset contains over one million tweets, which contain links to news articles and are associated with HoaxItaly.

**Fact-checking** is the key method in this community: it helps assess and combat disinformation. Italian fact-checking websites perform this work by debunking and verifying claims. Together, the datasets connect social-media activity and article content with the organizations producing disinformation and those evaluating it.

0289067fe4052e4d16530256e373fc1dc0235017.text:
### Community Question Answering, Recommendation, and Social Systems

This community centers on community question answering (CQA), including Stack Overflow, Yahoo Answers, and question-and-answer websites. Key tasks include question–answerer matching, expert recommendation, question routing, answer retrieval, answer-quality prediction, duplicate-question detection, and question refinement. QDEE estimates question difficulty and user expertise, using competition graphs and social agony, while expertise is also inferred from domains and historical performance.

Recommendation research addresses products, blogs, and experts. UCB-RS applies an enhanced upper-confidence-bound approach to non-stationary, large-state recommendation and outperforms epsilon-greedy, UCB1, and EXP3. Latent-factor systems account for user expertise, tastes, and readiness; scalable product recommendation learns similarity metrics from content.

Dialogue and language methods include QRFA, which models request–answer information-seeking flows and uses conformance analysis, and word reranking based on standard-deviation weighting or chi-square selection.

The community also studies participation and social dynamics. Gamification and incentive mechanisms support sustained service quality and timely, high-quality crowd sensing by mobile users. Event-based sentiment detection identifies event-related tweets and influential users. Interaction-decay prediction uses network attributes and supervised classification, while mobile social-network studies examine centrality and indirect relations. National culture shapes questioning, answering, and contribution behavior across platforms.

86c60c48bec63b5fa9415b4307d99d8ea83ca121.text:
## Twitter Knowledge Graphs and Evolving Data Integration

This community links **tweetskb**, a corpus of more than 1.5 billion tweets, with data-integration methods and analysis of Kavanaugh supporters and opponents. TweetsKB exposes tweet annotations through established RDF/S vocabularies, including metadata, extracted entities, hashtags, user mentions, and sentiment information. It facilitates data-integration use cases.

The **big data integration ontology** governs integration across evolving sources. Its query rewriting algorithm converts ontology-mediated queries into source queries, while its ontology adaptation algorithm semi-automatically adapts the ontology after new source releases. The ontology also annotates source schemas to manage schema evolution. REST APIs provide continuously evolving data sources; ontology-mediated queries retrieve data from the most recent source schema and support correctness for both current and historical queries. Functional and performance evaluation validates this ontology-based approach on real-world APIs.

The Twitter analysis distinguishes Kavanaugh supporters and opponents through divergent hashtags, retweeted Twitter accounts, and shared websites. These relationships connect social-media behavior—including retweeting and extracted metadata—to integrated, queryable knowledge.

b9aade93cafe9d2e2e2ae4f0410df4b5a9e1247e.text:
## Social Bots, Misinformation, and Detection

This community examines how social bots and fake news contribute to online misinformation, influence campaigns, and deception campaigns. Social bots—including impersonation bots and chatterbots—can display human-like behavior, target influential users, and operate in coordinated campaigns. They are especially active during the early diffusion of viral claims; humans may also retweet false news. Misinformation-spreading accounts are more likely to be bots.

Research distinguishes fake news from real news using article style and language features, title structure, and proper nouns in titles. Fake news is more similar to satire than real news, and uses persuasion and mental associations to shape beliefs. Its dissemination was studied in relation to the 2016 US presidential elections.

Countermeasures include bot detection, fact checking, Curb, and crowd powered misinformation reduction. Fact checking evaluates claims but can lag sharing by 10–20 hours; crowd-based systems select sufficiently flagged stories. Curb uses stochastic optimal control, formulated with stochastic differential equations with jumps, and is evaluated on Twitter and Weibo datasets.

Detection frameworks and tools use user metadata, content, sentiment, network patterns, activity time series, tweet metadata, and behavioral metrics. Twitter datasets include human annotations, popularity groups, and bot/human ground truth; Stweeler and publicly annotated Twitter-user datasets support bot research.

a9ae47d4ce2cc501c17528f30a56c38af9083935.text:
## NoSQL Selection and Resume Parsing Systems

This community covers graph data management, NoSQL storage infrastructure, and resume-parsing applications. NoSQL is presented as another name for graph data management and as a technology for big-data storage infrastructure. Graph data management includes RDF and property graphs as graph data models, while storage infrastructure is a fundamental component of big data systems.

The **NoSQL solutions dataset** contains 80 solutions. Feature analysis examines criteria for choosing among them, and bivariate analysis studies relationships among nine solution features. Cluster analysis groups the solutions into statistically supported categories. NoSQL solutions are reviewed and classified by application areas, recognizing that different areas have data characteristics suited to different data models. A decision tree prediction model predicts the suitability of a NoSQL solution for an application area, while random forest classification identifies the most relevant application features. The decision tree was implemented and deployed as a web application.

A separate resume-parsing task uses a resume parser to process LinkedIn and non-LinkedIn resumes. The resume parser is also made available through a web application.

833f5ae00a7ae89115384fd8f8c77fe3a4f31382.text:
## Graph Pattern Matching, Alignment, and Property-Graph Systems

This community centers on graph pattern matching, network alignment, and graph data management. Pattern matching is commonly formulated as subgraph isomorphism, while graph simulation and triple simulation reduce complexity; triple simulation supports polynomial-time matching and incorporates label-repetition constraints over pattern graphs and data graphs. Gremlin traversals, Gremlinator, and SPARQL support querying, with Gremlinator translating SPARQL into Gremlin and evaluated on Neo4j, Sparksee, and Apache TinkerGraph. SPARQL performance is compared on OpenLink Virtuoso, 4Store, and JenaTDB.

Property graphs manage vertices and edges with labels and property maps. Gremlin is their traversal language, while type systems and data definition languages define schemas. Schema-less methodologies avoid schema requirements but suffer data dependency and weaker compression; schema-based approaches address these limitations. RDF uses SPARQL, and schema.org provides RDF-like vocabulary subsets.

Network alignment includes REGAL, xNetMF, landmark-based node matching, and discrete Ollivier Ricci flow. REGAL uses automatically learned node representations, including xNetMF, and supports multi-network problems; it is reported up to 30 times faster than comparable representation-learning methods. Ricci flow metrics derive from Ollivier Ricci curvature and are evaluated on email, Internet, and protein-interaction networks.

Pattern matching also supports top-k team formation, including dynamic settings handled incrementally, with collaboration compatibility, structural constraints, and capacity bounds. Synthetic data supports evaluation.

62787ede7dd2245e788bf10e16d1715b8f18fe3c.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Publishing and Document Revision Detection

This community covers two related areas: differential-privacy mechanisms for social-media publishing and scalable document-revision detection.

Differential privacy provides statistical guarantees for releasing sensitive information, especially answers to count queries over groups of individuals, while protecting user privacy. The privacy-preserving publishing framework uses differential privacy and ε-text indistinguishability to publish perturbed social-media datasets and counter text-based user-linkage attacks, which can identify users behind anonymous IDs. Its goal is high data utility. Simulated datasets and social-media datasets support evaluation.

The privacy-mechanism work compares candidate mechanisms on real and synthetic data. The truncated geometric mechanism is a well-known optimal option, while a novel optimal mechanism is newly introduced. Privacy parameters influence which mechanism is preferable in practice.

The second area models document revision detection as a minimum-cost branching problem based on document distances. Word-vector-based dynamic time warping (WDTW) and word-vector-based tree edit distance (WTED) provide these distances. The document revision detection system is implemented in Apache Spark and evaluated on simulated datasets and Wikipedia revision dumps, achieving more precise detection than state-of-the-art methods.

9b9679d14dc18063b7fc7d3253f3714fcd28ebea.text:
## Social Networks, Diffusion, and Network Inference

This community centers on **social networks**: their topology, communities, temporal structure, user profiles, and social cohesion. It covers information spread, information cascades, product diffusion, app adoption, and infectious-disease processes, including **SAIS**, **SIS**, susceptible-infected-susceptible, and adaptive epidemic models. Critical thresholds, infection times, indirect transmission, and epidemic control connect diffusion analysis to resource allocation.

Opinion and influence dynamics are represented by the **DeGroot–Friedkin model**, French DeGroot opinion dynamics, social power, and non-Bayesian social learning. Community discovery uses **label propagation**, semi-synchronous label propagation, overlapping communities, 2-clubs, and close-community structure. **Team formation** seeks connected groups with required skills.

Network inference and identity tasks include topology discovery, graph-structure recovery, diffusion-network inference, multiplex-network inference, profile matching, and cross-network identity resolution. Methods include network vectors, matrix decomposition, Bayesian inference, maximum-likelihood estimation, spectral analysis, and greedy expectation maximization.

Optimization themes include convex and linear programming, cost-optimal resource allocation, protection-resource allocation, influence maximization, and ranking. Systems and data include **SnapVX**, **Finding Nemo**, **TrendNets**, **HRLHG**, **PhD Store**, **Expert Recommendation System**, **LDBC SNB**, **PeerJ referral data**, Wi-Fi access logs, and cascade data.

a5207d485262b9bc83d1a074bac10c9dd5ac6b82.text:
## Process Mining, Data Analytics, and Graph Inference

This community centers on process mining and event-log analytics. Process mining supports process discovery, variant and exception analysis, and machine learning on event data; process models are evaluated by fitness and may overgeneralize when events are too low-level. Local process model mining discovers frequent behavioral patterns and structured fragments, while unsupervised event abstraction lifts logs to higher-level representations. ProM provides an open-source process-mining framework, and CSM Miner explores artifact interactions through visualization and quantification, evaluated on personal-loan and overdraft processes.

A second theme is scalable workflow and log infrastructure. Loginson centralizes logs and provides analytics for large IT infrastructures, exploiting vertical scalability. Cloud infrastructure supports scientific workflows, cloud-aware provenance, virtual-machine configuration, and resource re-provisioning. User sessions and session sequences support two-level analytics and online web recommendation.

The community also addresses probabilistic graph inference. OJC performs source localization under partial observations using candidate selection and minimum-radius Jordan covers for heterogeneous SIR diffusion. Cascade reconstruction estimates infection probabilities using directed-Steiner-tree sampling, with guarantees and evaluations on synthetic and real cascades.

Additional topics include entropy-based similarity and coherence measures, synchronization via eigenvector methods, and the complexity and approximation of counting completions or valuations in incomplete databases.

d892ff0f3d2975b28b421b0baa13fb6d1af2740d.text:
## Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Selection

This community centers on reinforcement-learning approaches to selecting useful information under computational constraints. In e-commerce search ranking, Taobao.com operates a large-scale commodity search system where **contextual factor selection** chooses effective factor subsets for each search instance. The **RankCFS** method formulates this selection as a combinatorial optimization problem and uses reinforcement learning to reduce response latency while balancing ranking effectiveness and efficiency.

The same sequential decision perspective models sequential user–system interactions as a **Markov decision process**. Reinforcement learning also designs an **instance selector** for sentence-level relation classification from noisy data. The selector chooses high-quality sentences and feeds them to a **relation classifier**, which makes sentence-level predictions. Rewards provide feedback to the instance selector, guiding selection quality.

Thus, the community links reinforcement learning, contextual and instance selection, and sequential decision processes across two applications: accelerating online search ranking and improving relation classification through more effective data selection.

eb71c3a322ab06e1fb683e81bb2410e62e433a98.text:
# Graph-Based Recommendation, Search, and Big-Data Analytics

This community connects graph methods for recommendation, search, and statistical analysis. Personalized PageRank supports recommendation systems and local graph clustering; mean-field analysis on Erdős–Rényi graphs studies value concentration, damping-factor optimization, and limitations for clustering. It also extends to the edge space of simplicial complexes and is evaluated on book co-purchasing data, including graphs with planted denser subgraphs.

Recommendation research addresses sparse data, latent-factor models, neighborhood-based collaborative filtering, and result diversification. Collaborative memory networks combine global latent structure with local neighborhoods, using user and item memory modules plus neural attention to produce ranking scores. Diversification frameworks define set diversity, support numerical and string data, and provide probability-of-success guarantees for web search and query processing.

For large-scale search, online k-nearest-neighbor graph construction incrementally builds graphs through sequential searches, supports dynamic updates, and accommodates various distance measures. These graphs enable k-nearest-neighbor search and general nearest-neighbor retrieval.

Big-data analytics emphasizes query processing, statistical accuracy, and consistency. A general statistical framework, algorithmic principle, and partition-repetition approach address practical analytic problems while requiring revised statistical theory and tools. Higher-order interactions are represented by simplicial complexes, though sparse data limits their support.

8e4fd6a8e9720785a3f56954ca4e02045bf09198.text:
## Community Report: Provenance, Document Understanding, and Network Inference

This community links scientific data management with scalable document processing, OCR, table recognition, and network analysis.

Scientific datasets are generated by scientific codes and large-scale simulations. Integrated metadata management, permissions, read-only formats, Fluidinfo, and data annotation support dataset publication, governance, usage, and provenance. Data provenance records identity and lineage, while workflow engines, visualization interaction, and fine-grained provenance connect outputs to their origins. Lineage can be queried through dependency annotations and represented using OBDDs or d-DNNFs on bounded-treewidth instances.

Document infrastructure focuses on ingestion, parsing, annotation, and conversion of PDF, bitmap, and complex-table content. The corpus conversion service uses scalable asynchronous microservices and machine-learning classification, reporting approximately 99% precision and recall. OCR systems and mixed models use diplomatic transcriptions as ground truth; semi-automatic improvement reduces manual labeling, with character accuracy above 90%. Table structure recognition addresses spanning cells in PDF and ASCII text, including the SciTSR dataset and GraphTSR method.

Network and behavioral methods include HypTrails, which uses Markov chains, Dirichlet priors, and Bayes factors, and MixedTrails, which models heterogeneous sequences with generative mixed transition Markov chains. Proximity graphs and authenticated co-location edges support detection of Sybil devices and virtual vehicles, defending against traffic-rerouting attacks. Spam-tweet detection applies classification algorithms to hand-labeled datasets.

5ad7237a7acb7c78f154bbe196ee9805c36dfcbe.text:
## Networks, Diffusion, and Social Inference

This community centers on computational analysis of evolving social, document, and behavioral networks. Temporal methods include longitudinal analysis, temporal point-process models, and multidimensional marked Hawkes processes. These model product adoption and recurrent usage, competing products, cascade diffusion, and latent diffusion networks, evaluated on URL-shortening and music-streaming datasets.

Social structure is inferred from RFID tracking, mobile-phone communication, purchasing habits, and displacement or proximity data among rhesus macaques. Related work studies cooperation, competition, intergroup ties, socioeconomic stratification, opinion evolution, and networked agents. Genealogical networks are computationally inferred from historical records for digital demography, genetics, and long-term mating-pattern analysis.

A second focus is information and idea diffusion. Document corpora support pairwise co-occurrence and prevalence-correlation analysis, while event-evolution tracking identifies event birth, death, growth, decay, merging, and splitting in social-post streams. Coordinated word storms and legal-document classification use automated classification, including Bi-LSTM methods.

Image virality is modeled through visual and relative attributes, virality scores, and state-of-the-art image features; machine-learning systems predict viral events and relative virality, sometimes exceeding human performance. Other methods address relationship inference, opponent-action anticipation, trolling prediction, ranking analysis, and community-structure change through scaled inclusivity. Systems such as hierarchy graph, sketch graph, correlation network, GreyCat, and parallel-worlds exploration support network representation, risk propagation, and prescriptive analytics.

bbf3b719f5b5d6c92e975984e741178858264586.text:
## Telegram and News Diffusion Datasets for Disinformation Research

This community centers on datasets and data-collection resources for studying disinformation, online social movements, protests, and political extremism.

The **Pushshift Telegram dataset** was collected from **Telegram** and contains **317 million messages** across more than **27.8K channels**, covering **2.2 million unique users**. Its release includes the **source code** used for collection, enabling researchers to run their own data-collection instance. The dataset supports research on online social movements, protests, political extremism, and disinformation.

The **Twitter diffusion network dataset** represents the spread of articles through diffusion networks, including both **mainstream news** and **misleading news**. Mainstream news and misleading news form the two classes distinguished by a classifier, while misleading news is connected to the broader concept of disinformation.

Together, these resources support analysis of messages, channels, and users on Telegram, as well as the diffusion of different types of news on Twitter.

468457aa55438fa7371ab4d2e442b2f4c36e08ff.text:
## Ensembles for Recommendations, Triple Scoring, and Data Cleaning

This community centers on ensemble-based methods for recommendation hybridization, knowledge-base triple scoring, and data-error management.

**Genetic algorithm inspired hybridization** combines unscored recommendations into a single ensemble by repeatedly selecting items. Inspired by genetic algorithms and compared with weighted voting, it is evaluated on movie- and name-recommendation datasets. It improves recommendation quality over the weighted method and reduces overall execution time.

**Team Radicchio triple scorer**, developed by Team Radicchio for the WSDM Cup 2017 triple-scoring task, assesses the relevance of knowledge-base triples. It combines explicit features with latent features, using Word2Vec representations for person entities and GloVe representations for profession and nationality values, through an ensemble approach.

**BoostClean** automates error detection and repair, targeting inconsistencies such as domain value violations. It selects detection-and-repair combinations using statistical boosting and evaluates them with clean test labels across 12 datasets. Its ensemble incorporates a Word2Vec-based detector and achieves end-to-end speedups through parallelism, materialization, and indexing.

04bc6bde202f53583f60696b0f3c46c0511c94e4.text:
## Community Report: Topic Models, Semantic Hashing, and Predictive Applications

This community links advances in topic modeling, representation learning, hashing, and applied prediction systems.

For topic modeling, Embedded Topic Model (ETM) integrates word embeddings, represents topics with embeddings, handles large heavy-tailed vocabularies, and discovers interpretable topics using amortized variational inference. It is evaluated by topic quality and predictive performance and outperforms LDA. LDA uses a collapsed Gibbs sampler to discover topic patterns. The Full Dependence Mixture models second moments, is fitted directly to co-occurrence data with stochastic optimization, and is evaluated on the SOTU and NeurIPS papers corpora. The coefficient of determination \(R\) is proposed as a cross-context evaluation and goodness-of-fit metric for probabilistic topic models.

Hashing methods learn compact binary codes and semantic structure. Deep Collaborative Discrete Hashing uses visual features and semantic labels to construct a common discrete space and semantic-invariant structure. SHREWD performs weakly supervised hashing using semantic distance, KL-divergence loss, and hierarchical retrieval scores.

In computational advertising, hybrid models combine shallow and deep embeddings with gradient boosting trees to predict booking probability from sparse session logs; one is deployed in a production system. Deep Personalized Retargeting addresses booking probability and booking value prediction for a vacation rental marketplace. Other applications include CAD search, product-name detection with an LSTM tagger, and webpage-quality analysis.

944569be79938f44e43565166f4919b4550a40be.text:
### AGL for Scalable Graph Neural Network Processing

This community centers on **AGL**, a system for scalable **graph neural network (GNN) training and inference**. GNNs use **message passing** as their underlying computational scheme, and a **graph attention network** is a type of GNN. AGL bases its system design on message passing and supports both GNN training and GNN inference.

For training, AGL uses a **parameter server** because of data independency. It uses **MapReduce** for neighborhood generation and inference, generating information-complete **k-hop neighborhoods**. At billion-node scale, AGL achieves a reported **14-hour training time** and **1.2-hour inference time**, highlighting its focus on scalable execution.

9428bdc939cac9c714a56a499ea4b03c9016e1ea.text:
## Graph Learning, Sampling, and Computational Provenance

This community connects graph-based learning, network generation, distributed computation, and reproducible research objects.

Graph representation learning uses graph neural networks (GNNs), with feature propagation as an inference process that spreads features across graph neighborhoods. Structure2vec is linked to feature propagation, while edge2vec extends it from nodes to edges and supports fraud transaction detection. Graphs are limited to pairwise relationships, whereas hypergraphs model co-occurrence networks and support multi-adic relationships. Co-occurrence networks contain links among dataset instances and metadata references, enabling knowledge discovery from datasets.

Convergence is studied for feature propagation, dynamic average diffusion, interaction coordination, and connected random graph generation. Dynamic average diffusion uses randomized coordinate-descent updates for online distributed average tracking over time-varying distributed signals. Interaction coordination requires convergence and avoidance of bias.

Graph sampling includes Metropolis-Hastings methods for sampling from graph distributions and generating connected spatially embedded random graphs, including Waxman networks. Property-conditioned sampling enforces connectedness or another desired property.

Computational provenance organizes research objects, including datasets and software, around computational experiments. Provenance summarization uses process views and summary graphs that resemble application workflows. Provenance supports reference execution, partial reuse, and modified reuse of research contents.

de4097893e5acd24670db5eb5721259dc38e0f64.text:
## Graph Robustness, Trust, Privacy, and Adversarial Networks

This community covers attacks, defenses, and optimization in social and collaborative networks. For dynamic network link prediction, **time-aware gradient attacks** use gradients from deep dynamic network embedding across network snapshots to rewire a small number of target links. Traversal (TGA-TRA) and greedy (TGA-GRE) searches implement these attacks. **Robust active attacks** formulate attacks as optimization problems and remain resilient to graph perturbations, while active attacks target naively anonymized social network graphs and can re-identify sybils and other users.

Privacy research connects **graph anonymisation** and privacy-preserving social graph publication with the challenge of re-identification. **Unattack** and data poisoning attacks inject well-designed fake users into neighborhood-based recommender systems, targeting items and transferring to Bayesian Personalized Ranking Matrix Factorization and Neural Collaborative Filtering. These systems may use Euclidean-distance similarity, and effectiveness is evaluated on recommender-system datasets.

Community detection uses **variational community partition**, graph clustering, affinity matrices, and network centrality measures derived from network structure information. Convex optimization and a primal-dual variational perspective support its iterative formulation and evaluation on artificial and real-world datasets.

Trust research combines direct and indirect trust through trust aggregation and decentralized trust management, with formal effectiveness and robustness analysis under threats. Resource allocation supports containment, reducing accumulated infections. Generalized stable marriage extends stable matching to unequal groups and active messengers; simulations examine group homogeneity, active messenger percentages, and social optimality.

657566b925c44b9519562b00d94065e221fc6dc0.text:
## Opinion Dynamics, Equilibria, and Stubborn-Agent Placement

This community studies opinion dynamics among agents on directed social networks, including settings with switching structures and immutable (stubborn) agents. The Friedkin–Johnsen model uses susceptibility weights to represent interpersonal influence, analyzes asymptotic behavior, and can converge to quasi-consensus with an achieved consensus value under suitable assumptions. It is contrasted with the DeGroot model, a baseline opinion-update model generalized to signed networks.

Individual bias and state-dependent edge weights extend social opinion dynamics beyond classical models, producing highly nonlinear network dynamics. Bias can attract polarized initial opinions toward interval boundaries and alter the location and stability of social equilibria. Stability analysis identifies the interval centroid as an interior equilibrium but proves it unstable regardless of bias level and topology.

Opinion equilibria are determined by a linear system and admit an electrical-network interpretation. Harmonic influence centrality uses these equilibria to quantify nodes’ effects on mean opinion.

A further focus is stubborn-agent placement: selecting nodes to maximize population influence through a monotone submodular utility. Greedy algorithms apply when the objective is submodular, while they cannot be directly used for non-submodular utilities. The placement problem is evaluated on simulated networks.

92f94c4785ee66064e1bdbc9451236b18019611e.text:
## Retrieval, Ranking, and Semantic Network Analysis

This community centers on retrieval and ranking, including similar-question retrieval, gist detection, and learning-to-rank. End-to-end continuous retrieval relies on distances between learned embeddings and approximate nearest-neighbor search, replacing a discrete inverted index. Its retrieval architecture is evaluated on similar-question tasks and improves over a discrete baseline by 8% and 26%, with mean average precision (MAP) as a measure.

Learning-to-rank constructs relevance-ranking functions and can use implicit feedback, although position bias makes observed clicks dependent on result position and can produce biased training data. Counterfactual learning-to-rank addresses this bias and is generalized to additive rank metrics, including DCG and Precision@k. SVM PropDCG optimizes an unbiased DCG estimate using a convex-concave procedure and generalizes SVM PropRank; Deep PropDCG uses deep networks for nonlinear ranking functions.

Gist detection is framed as concept ranking, using semantic relatedness, entity linking, subgraph selection, and automatically generated captions or image tags. The Gist dataset provides annotated image-caption pairs, and reported MAP is 0.69.

A bibliometric strand introduces citation-context keyword co-occurrence networks. Networks based on Eugene Garfield’s papers and papers citing them are compared with title-and-abstract keyword networks using semantic relatedness.

c9caef96ace7b1b0694140145bce808f3af63ead.text:
## Community Report: Web Archives, Automated Discovery, and Research Evaluation

This community centers on web archiving, temporal access, and automated crawling. The Wayback Machine models archived-page access through Dip, Slide, Dive, and Skim patterns, while humans account for most accesses. Memento, MediaWiki extensions, web-archive APIs, and ArcLink support datetime negotiation, revision retrieval, URI lookup, metadata, links, and temporal web-graph construction. Archival quality, temporal drift, inconsistency windows, and embedded resources evaluate archive behavior. Blockchain-based timestamping services provide trusted timestamps using cryptographic or referenced data.

Crawling research compares Heritrix, wget, PhantomJS, and EPOW. Deferred-representation discovery uses classifiers, headless browsing, and a Hypercube model, discovering more URIs but at substantially lower crawl rates. EPOW emphasizes scheduling, parallelization, throughput, and crash robustness; two-tiered and sliding or sticky target policies address crawling and temporal consistency.

Other topics apply automated methods to research and content. Moliere generates biomedical hypotheses and candidate genes from historical biomedical data, evaluated through candidate ranking and numerical validation frameworks. PICO span annotation supports medical-literature filtering, with standard and relaxed agreement measures. Candidate ranking also supports job matching and web-page recommendation. Food-image collection combines crawling, crowdsourcing, human ground-truth labeling, and automatic detection. Finally, Arabic-bot characterization examines detection features, religious hatred, and sectarian rhetoric, noting weaker performance of English bot tools.

6eb199975861f69529729a12a04dda7c1c57b215.text:
## Graph Methods, Fair Search, and Team Formation

This community spans graph representation, network analysis, search, and collaborative team design.

**Unsupervised network embedding** uses unsupervised neural networks to learn graph representations for graph collections. It is evaluated for graph clustering, classification, and visualization, achieves high runtime efficiency, and outperforms graph distances and graph kernels on clustering and classification tasks. **graspy**, a Python library distributed through the Python Package Index under the Apache 2.0 license, supports graph-population analysis, visualization, statistical inference, and random-graph analysis through a scikit-learn-compatible API.

**Graph coarsening** uses spectral graph theory to create coarse graphs for large-scale graphs. Coarsening algorithms are assessed on graph classification and block recovery, with spectral distance measuring structural differences and preservation of spectral properties.

For search, **fairsearch** provides fair-ranking notions and APIs, implementing FA*IR and DELTR through Python and Java libraries. Elasticsearch, based on Apache Lucene, exposes these capabilities through plugins. **FENSHSES** enables exact Hamming-space neighbor search using binary codes, bit operations, substring filtering, and permutation preprocessing, achieving speedups over term matching.

Team research addresses guided and automated team formation, optimizing centroids toward target vectors and minimizing faultlines that affect cohesion and performance. Multilayer-network work covers Boolean layer combinations, decomposition, adaptive contact neighborhoods, and reduced computation time.

0ff255705f11072d3fcce8eb6a00054a54402cef.text:
## Community Report: Neural Retrieval, Recommendation, and Controversy Detection

This community links neural methods for search, recommendation, and web-content analysis. **Controversy detection** is studied on general web pages and formulated through Wikipedia linking and exact lexical matching. Neural classifiers and semantic approaches provide robust detection, evaluated by annotator congruence, cross-temporal performance, and cross-topic performance. Word embeddings support neural processing of text.

For **recommendation**, neural networks enable effective models, while joint modeling simultaneously learns retrieval and recommendation models using a joint loss function, demonstrated on product data. The heterogeneous-item framework combines mixture-of-experts and knowledge-graph-embedding ideas to represent multiple relationship modalities, model user susceptibility over time, and provide recommendation explanations. **COSRA+T** integrates social trust relations into network diffusion and resource redistribution, using a scaling parameter for resources received by trusted users; it improves recommendation accuracy and is evaluated on Epinions and FriendFeed.

For **sponsored search**, CLSM is a neural retrieval approach trained on click-through data, generating tri-letter embeddings and approximating query-ad categorical similarity. It improves offline AUC ROC by 5.23% and relevance by 8.2% in A/B testing. Cached query categories have limited tail-query coverage, while tri-letter representations address tail queries. Retrieval models perform search ranking, complementing navigation.

7b1cf7bd3fdb1c093faea53ba95c5a2a0c69304a.text:
## Sampling and Sketching for Approximate Query Processing

This community focuses on estimating query results efficiently in data warehouses and large-scale systems, especially for group-by queries and complex filters involving correlated subqueries, self-joins, or user-defined functions.

**Learning to Sample** uses samples to train a probabilistic classifier, which guides final stratified sampling. It is designed for complex query count estimation, seeks meaningful confidence intervals, and is compared with quantification learning and weighted sampling. Stratified sampling is further connected to optimal stratification, CVOpt, and the production of pivots with quality guarantees.

**CVOpt** is a sampling framework for group-by queries. It can be tuned using partial query-workload information and evaluates sample quality through the coefficient of variation. It achieves lower relative errors than competing approaches. Random sampling is also widely used for approximate query processing and group-by queries.

For quantile sketching, **DDSketch** provides formal relative-error guarantees, is fully mergeable, and is used at wide scale by Datadog. Mergeability enables combining summaries from distributed data streams. Quantile sketches approximately summarize sample quantiles and are commonly evaluated by rank error, although rank error does not preclude arbitrarily large relative error.

fdb4531b92f838b397b617b2f14fa6d8952055b4.text:
## Community Report: Topics, Data Repair, and Social Discovery

This community connects three major themes: topic modeling, data quality, and social-network search.

Topic modeling represents queries and elements in a topic space. LDA, DocNADE, and iDocNADE are modeling methods, while separable non-negative matrix factorization supports topic recovery through anchor-word selection. Anchor selection uses word similarity graphs, minimum-edge-weight anchor cliques, and similarity information; it improves topic quality. SATO applies contextual signals and structured prediction to semantic type detection for relational-table columns, supporting schema matching, semantic search, data cleaning, and data discovery.

Data repairing addresses dirty data using repairing rules, data dependencies, and external verified data sources. Weighted matching rectifying rules use similarity matching; WMRR Discovery derives such rules from dirty data, resolves rule inconsistencies, and WMRR-DR performs automatic repair.

Social search uses direct links, weak ties, and the small-world phenomenon to reach distant networks. A recursive incentive scheme motivates participants, illustrated by a referral contest in MIT Climate CoLab: referred participants were more likely to submit proposals and high-quality proposals, particularly when connected through distant networks. For social streams, K-SIR queries maximize representativeness using semantic and influence scores. Multi-topic ThresholdStream and ThresholdDescend approximate real-time processing using per-topic ranked lists and sliding windows.

f44618a7da417e8be92525069a30c7a132127f6a.text:
## Probabilistic Recommendation, SQL Synthesis, and Program Analysis

This community connects three themes: recommendation from implicit feedback, structured analysis of mathematical language, and natural-language-to-SQL/program synthesis.

For recommendation, Poisson factorization models users and items from implicit consumer data. Recurrent Poisson factorization extends it with a Poisson process for time-varying feedback, supporting time-sensitive recommendation. Its variants model dynamic preferences and item specifications, social product adoption, and consumption heterogeneity. Variational inference provides approximate posterior inference, while amortized variational inference uses neural networks for scalable learned posteriors. Evaluation includes synthetic data, music-streaming logs, M-Commerce interactions, and MovieLens 1M ratings.

The community also covers matched bipartite block models for bipartite networks. These support matched communities and node covariates containing matching information; degree-corrected extensions address degree variation, with a fast fitting algorithm and evaluation on real data.

In language and synthesis, semantic parsing converts natural language into query sketches, which guide type-directed program synthesis using database-schema type information. SQLizer generates SQL queries and iteratively maximizes confidence scores, using database contents and top-five candidate ranking for evaluation. Query sketches also support fault localization and automated program repair. Mathematical language is distinguished from natural language, while Symbol2Vec learns vector representations of formula symbols.

bb62fb34906c987dc13f09161d367283b1d7bef4.text:
## Hybrid Deep Embedding for Explainable Recommendation

This community focuses on aspect-based explainable recommendation, rating prediction, and personalized preference learning from review data and implicit feedback. The central method, **hybrid deep embedding**, is proposed for aspect-based explainable recommendation and fuses implicit feedback with attentive user–item interactions.

The method learns **dynamic user and item embeddings**, supporting rating prediction. It also learns **dynamic latent aspect preference and quality** for explanation generation. These latent aspects capture aspects not mentioned in review data, complementing the aspects available in textual reviews. The resulting representations generate **dynamic aspect-level explanations**, which are supported by the learned dynamic latent preferences and qualities.

Overall, the work connects behavioral signals extracted as implicit feedback with review data, attentive user–item interactions, dynamic embeddings, and latent aspect modeling. This combination addresses the challenge of personalized preference learning while producing explanations that vary dynamically across aspects, users, and items.

7fc16eae44ecb96ba2dc428adfcdd6495399b589.text:
## Community Report: Scientific Production, Open Data, and Real-Time Analysis

This community connects research on scientific specialisms, open data, and scalable analysis. The rural–urban analogy models urban specialisms as having stronger collaboration, productivity, resource competition, and citation recognition, while rural specialisms are fragmented into smaller topics with greater author mobility and lower collaboration and productivity. Specialism operationalization applies these ideas empirically to computer science, history, biology, literature, and astronomy. It also examines unequal representation in computing and questions citation-based indicators for humanities specialisms.

Open science includes open data and open peer review. Scalable data publishing addresses dynamic and newly arriving data, but may produce network latency, server capacity overload, or unwanted knowledge disclosure. Context-dependent publication heuristics, informed by domain knowledge, support scalable publishing and improve publication performance.

The **aserv** system processes newly arriving data and supports low-latency, real-time scientific event analysis in cloud environments. Its domain-aware filtering, accuracy-aware partitioning, efficient indexing, statistical data design, and performance modeling optimize processing and resource selection.

**EmbNum** uses deep metric learning to represent numerical attributes without prior distributional assumptions, supporting semantic labeling through value distributions. It is evaluated on city data and open data. **CSIndexBR** provides transparent open data on Brazilian scientific production, collecting full papers from selected conferences for scientific production analysis.

0c17b02b75be00db2308246866659cabd43f5818.text:
## Community Report: Neural Querying, Video Analytics, and Accessible Databases

This community connects approximate data exploration, video analytics, handwritten-record retrieval, and natural-language database interaction.

**NeuralCubes** provides a neural approximation of data-cube functionality for large multidimensional datasets. It predicts aggregate-query results, enabling real-time exploration and low-memory aggregation, including client-side evaluation in a web browser and new visualization and interaction types. Neural networks learn its query-result prediction functions.

**BlazeIt** supports video analytics through **FrameQL**, a declarative extension of SQL. It optimizes queries over spatiotemporal video-object information, including approximate aggregation and cardinality-limited queries. Neural networks provide video-object annotations, while control variates enable fast approximate aggregation with error bounds; a search algorithm addresses cardinality-limited queries.

The **CITlab Recognition and Retrieval Engine**, developed for the ICDAR2017 competition, processes line images from historical handwritten records, including marriage records. It uses neural networks for its optical model, regular expressions to define feasible word sequences, and infers person names; it outperforms a baseline.

**Cyrus** is an iOS voice-query interface for arbitrary relational databases. It supports SQL learners in tutoring and formative assessment, using cooperative error reporting. More broadly, SQL supports keyword-based querying and natural-language database programming, linking database access with natural-language voice interaction.

51ed1d21d6fbe8c5103b8e3c08e3dc2d7343d210.text:
## Learned Data Systems, Answer Selection, and Infection Estimation

This community connects learned indexing, answer selection, and infection-probability estimation.

**Learned indexes** replace core components of data management systems, including B-tree, hash, and bitmap indexes, with deep learning models and neural networks. They learn key order to predict record positions in sorted arrays (B-trees) or unsorted arrays (hash indexes), and predict record existence for bitmap indexes. These systems can outperform cache-optimized B-trees by up to 70% in speed and reduce memory usage by an order of magnitude.

For **answer selection**, neural networks provide state-of-the-art learning-to-rank models. Methods combine pretrained word embeddings with traditional learning-to-rank techniques, while term frequency supports traditional baseline approaches. These methods are evaluated on answer selection datasets.

For **edge infection probability estimation**, the task is formulated as a general optimization problem. A generalized estimation framework handles an arbitrary number of infection process observations, works with widely used infection and diffusion models, and is evaluated on realistic infection scenarios and computational speed. A particle swarm heuristic is proposed to solve the optimization task.

7bc365e732b7e911891e6fd0c97f84b02bc176d0.text:
## Heterogeneous Graph Search, Recommendation, and Streaming Analytics

This community focuses on learning, querying, and ranking over heterogeneous networks containing multiple node and relation types, as well as associated unstructured semantic content. **CARL** jointly learns heterogeneous SkipGram and deep semantic encodings, combines review- and interaction-based features, models context for aggregated search, and supports online updates for incoming nodes. **HeteSim** measures relatedness between same- or different-type objects using path-constrained measures and efficient computation strategies, supporting relevance search and data-mining tasks.

Search research includes diversified top-*k* processing, with **Div-A\***, **Div-DP**, and **Div-Cut**, and relevance search in heterogeneous networks. **Regrank** performs reliable graph-based collaborative ranking through semantically aligned recommendation paths. Recommendation methods also include **Caser**, which uses convolutional filters for local sequential features, and probabilistic neighborhood-based approaches.

Streaming work addresses similarity self-joins over unbounded streams using time-dependent similarity, minibatches, streaming algorithms, and an L2 index. Other graph-analytics topics include typed graphlet counting, graph stream summarization, homophily estimation, infection-source identification, and approximate dependency discovery.

The community also covers review and data practices: **CyberChair** supports conference reviewing and conflict resolution, while datasheets for datasets promote accountability for datasets, commercial APIs, and pretrained models.

ba825b3e48dc582af23d97433019559c92e8a697.text:
## Human–Machine Methods for Data, Knowledge, and Prediction

This community centers on **entity resolution**, which identifies and merges records for the same real-world entity. Methods include blocking schemes, weighted bipartite or maximum-weight matching, maximum-likelihood clustering, collective and query-driven resolution, and progressive entity resolution. **MinoanER**, **PERC**, and **HUMO** support machine-based, probabilistic, or human–machine resolution; HUMO addresses consistent solutions, while PERC handles imperfect crowd judgments. **Skyblocking** uses active learning to identify preferred blocking schemes and scheme skylines.

**Crowdsourcing** supplies human cognitive labor for entity resolution, data mining, paper screening, research contribution descriptions, and multimodal knowledge acquisition. Amazon Mechanical Turk, social machines, QurK, and human–machine networks exemplify this integration, with fault tolerance and quality control needed for noisy worker input.

**Active learning** supports annotation assistance, predictive coding, multilingual tweet datasets, and on-the-fly model learning through uncertainty sampling, bootstrapping, and continuous active-learning methods such as AutoTAR and Cormack–Grossman CAL.

Predictive models use social, network, behavioral, and early-spreading patterns for tasks including student support, rankings, purchase prediction, meme success, game outcomes, and sports betting. Folksonomy work connects tags, sources, and time through the Folksodriven structure and related networks.

ae2808abd20f792c706c45a0098e3773a041e251.text:
### Ranking, Retrieval, and Adaptive Learning Systems

This community centers on **learning to rank** for search, answer selection, biomedical literature retrieval, personalized search, notable-news and gist detection. Rankers combine relevance, popularity, user/query context, structured triples, word/entity interactions, pre-trained embeddings, and latent vector-space features. Methods include pointwise, pairwise, and listwise learning (including **ListNet**), tree-based models, neural networks, and **counterfactual risk minimization** from partial click feedback. **Termpicker** applies learning to rank and is evaluated with mean average precision; **CascadeLSB** addresses online ranking from partial clicks.

**Reinforcement learning** supports dynamic search, factor selection (**RankCFS**), instance selection, and long-term engagement optimization in **FeedRec**, while addressing exploration–exploitation trade-offs through dueling bandits, Thompson sampling, and related strategies.

Classifiers handle product relevance, migrant churn, censorship detection, bursty tokens, and labeled or unlabeled documents. Neural networks support ranking, regression, answer selection, metadata classification, relevance estimation, and individual representations. **Convolutional neural networks** generate visual embeddings and deep features for video retrieval, analytics, and task understanding.

Graph-oriented systems and representations complement these approaches, including Graphene, graph-based video indexes, affiliation and auxiliary graphs, and graph-augmented document representation learning.

195a73b45c580a6b30336e214acc0ad4b7269fad.text:
## Network Sampling, Popularity Bias, and Dynamic Diffusion

This community covers two connected research themes: efficient network estimation and dynamic contact modeling.

For degree distribution estimation in undirected networks, **friendship paradox sampling** exploits the friendship paradox to sample the tail of power-law degree distributions more efficiently than uniform node sampling. Its maximum-likelihood estimator has lower variance and a smaller Cramér–Rao lower bound than the uniform-sampling baseline; log-log linear regression provides another approach.

In directed networks, the friendship paradox explains why people are less popular than their friends or followers on average, creating perception bias. The **polling algorithm** uses this bias to estimate global topic prevalence and popularity, which may differ substantially from topic frequencies perceived in users’ social feeds. Synthetic polling experiments using Twitter data evaluate its efficiency.

The **SPDT graph model** extends activity-driven time-varying network modeling by representing multiple concurrently active copies of nodes. Fitted by maximum likelihood to a city-scale location-update dataset from a social networking app, it generates dynamic contact networks containing direct and indirect links. Indirect links represent transmission between nodes visiting the same place at different times. The model is evaluated through SPDT diffusion simulations and its ability to reproduce empirical network properties, including variation by time of day and communication channel.

8611dc600fafd4eb99fbce0f190471e51b462ea7.text:
## Community Report: Learning, Retrieval, and Resilient Networks

This community connects machine learning systems for multimedia retrieval, recommendation, question answering, and network analysis.

Video analytics is a major theme. Convolutional neural networks produce visual embeddings and deep feature representations for video retrieval and task understanding. Cloud camera query systems use multi-pass processing on low-cost hardware and achieve over 100× video real time. VStore manages video ingestion and storage, selecting formats and operators through backward configuration derivation to optimize resources and meet target accuracy. Graph-based and semantic video indexing support spatial and temporal search.

Recommendation research focuses on compatibility and heterogeneous relationships. Monomer learns compatibility from textual embeddings while relaxing nearest-neighbor and metricity assumptions. Related systems address clothing, artwork, image, citation, and subject-label recommendation, using logged recommendation data and Pinterest collections.

Question-answering work applies neural networks and CNNs to answer selection, evaluated on TRECQA against IDF-weighted word overlap and user assessment. Other methods include compression-based authorship verification, domain adaptation, and real-time user-type classification.

A further cluster studies communication, organizational, cyber, physical, and smart-grid networks. Network resilience is measured with an invulnerability index under attacks, failures, and node heterogeneity; smart grids use decentralized control and demand response. Organizational communication is analyzed through information synthesis, network coding, and interaction data.

4e14e305d502407ff2f94993d955413546b82c49.text:
## Evolving Networks, Citation Growth, and Novelty Measurement

This community studies temporal network growth, citation dynamics, and prediction of emerging or high-impact content. In evolving networks, preferential attachment models rich-get-richer link acquisition and is associated with power-law in-degree distributions. The American Physical Society journal citation network instead exhibits a log-normal citation distribution, motivating the preferential-attachment paradox and investigation of alternative attachment mechanisms.

Measurement procedures distinguish preferential attachment from competing mechanisms; a recognized design flaw caused systematic error, while a corrected procedure resolves the paradox. Related evolving-network methods include link copying, aging and frugal aging models, relay linking models, triangle-completion-based link formation, and temporal graph sketches for summarizing and characterizing temporal dynamics.

Recent behavior dominance models use recent behavior with dominant or equal importance relative to total behavior to predict novelty and emerging nodes. They are evaluated on MovieLens, Netflix, and the arXiv high-energy-physics citation dataset using novelty, Kendall rank correlation, and AUC/ROC analysis.

A second theme evaluates altmetric and bibliometric indices. Altmetric indices, including Altmetric.com data from Scopus-indexed publications, are assessed for correlations using Spearman correlation and for discrimination of highly cited publications using AUC.

3ed91e543204fe68ba6607ee5a7a33a5727a86c2.text:
## Community Report: Local Community Detection and Ambiguity-Aware Ranking

This community covers two methodological themes: local graph community detection and list-wise learning to rank.

LOSP uses sampling around labeled seed members and defines a family of local spectral subspaces. It seeks a sparse indicator for a target community, obtained through one-norm minimization. Its theoretical analysis uses the Rayleigh quotient, while its local spectral subspace is based on a Krylov subspace. LOSP also has variants based on random walks, including regular and inverse random walks.

The second theme addresses ambiguity in relevance labels: multiple documents may receive the same relevance label for a query. List-wise learning to rank uses these labels to learn document rankings, while existing list-wise methods are described as ignoring such ambiguity. The proposed sampling technique models this ambiguity and computes a corresponding list-wise loss. Its loss is compared with ListNet and ListMLE. A three-layer deep neural network is trained using the sampling technique, which outperforms competing methods on both validation and test sets.

3f72194e59254c0021c6be66e954851a24ff420f.text:
## Learning, Interaction, and Explanation in Search

This community covers document and passage retrieval, learning to rank, interactive search, and probabilistic inference. Learning-to-rank methods—including point-wise and pair-wise approaches—support document and passage ranking, traditionally using explicit relevance judgments such as TREC assessments or PubMed article judgments. Document ranking can use document–query features, while the best described method uses features from the highest-ranked passage. Passage-based retrieval derives document-ranking information from passages and may use passage–query similarity.

Counterfactual risk minimization learns ranking models from logged contextual bandit feedback without manually aggregated relevance judgments. Evaluated on the Commercial dataset of add-to-basket clicks and orders, it outperforms λ-MART and full-information-loss approaches, including across deep neural network models. Cross entropy is an example of full-information loss.

Seeker is an alternative to conventional representation-based search: it lets users interactively refine rankings, adapts results in real time, and is evaluated through human-in-the-loop experiments. Representation-based search queries items in an embedding space, while user likes, dislikes, sequential feedback, clicks, and orders inform ranking.

A separate line performs probabilistic inference on graphical models, using simple subgraphs as faithful approximations. Constrained cross-entropy minimization searches these subgraphs and is formulated for inference explanation.

6bf7ff55a2eee986a75887551ffbcba1ae2abd52.text:
## Scholarly Communication, Recommendation, and Evaluation Systems

This community links scholarly repositories and research communication with search, recommendation, review, and assessment. arXiv is presented as a preprint and subject repository that supports research communication, programming interfaces, author identifiers, post-publication discussion, and access before formal peer review. Its citation, affiliation, and co-authorship structure forms a natural graph; referenced-URL availability and compliance with the HEFCE open access policy are also examined. A proposed “modern arXiv” would substantially differ from today’s platform.

Recommendation research spans research articles, fashion, news, and cross-modality retrieval. Research article recommendation ranks source papers relative to webpages using canonical correlation analysis (CCA), baseline ranking methods, and accuracy measures. Fashionista learns low-dimensional visual spaces and fashion trends from binary feedback, while SAERS combines a Semantic Extraction Network with fine-grained preference attention to explain clothing recommendations. CCA also learns joint query–item embeddings and can be implemented as a neural layer for text–image and audio–sheet-music retrieval. G-BBAN represents user-dependent interaction graphs, concentration features, graph convolution, and attention-based LSTMs for interactive news recommendation.

Online-review studies use Amazon and Kindle data, rule-based NLP, timestamps, and customer feedback to investigate opinion spamming and reputation attacks. Finally, departmental h-index metrics support research assessment and REF 2014 prediction, but poorly predict overall outcomes and ranking movements.

283d0175ea59959c5c6911f4d0c00e7ca3336126.text:
## Diffusion Networks for Misleading Information Analysis

This community focuses on using diffusion networks to classify news articles and identify misleading information. Diffusion networks exhibit systematic structural differences when associated with misleading information, providing a basis for distinguishing reliable and unreliable content.

Topological network analysis examines diffusion-network topology, while alignment-free network analysis compares diffusion networks without requiring network alignment. It uses basic network properties, network distances, and distributions of centrality measures to characterize and compare these networks.

A related task estimates the percentage of bot-followees among human-operated accounts. This estimation can help identify users more exposed to misleading or unreliable content. A regression model performs the estimation, with the best reported model achieving a Root Mean Squared Error of 5.96% and a Mean Absolute Error of 3.62%.

Overall, the community connects structural network analysis with news article classification and user-level bot-followee estimation to study the detection and exposure pathways of misleading information.

2c655da4e495f664b10e609b56c542a77610e9e7.text:
## Diffusion Network Recovery and Cascade Prediction

This community studies continuous-time diffusion models for recovering hidden network structures and predicting cascading processes. **Diffusion network structure recovery** uses observed **cascades**, with an \(l_1\)-regularized likelihood maximization framework and an efficient soft-thresholding inference algorithm. Correct recovery depends on an incoherence condition in the cascade sampling process and requires \(O(d^3 \log N)\) cascades with high probability; the cubic factor is controlled by the maximum parent degree.

A second theme is **cascading process prediction**, including cascade size prediction and outbreak time prediction. Cascades provide early observations for predicting cumulative cascade size at later times, while outbreak time prediction estimates when a cascade reaches a specified threshold. A scalable cascading-process approximation offers a theoretical guarantee and is evaluated on a large-scale social network dataset.

**Behavioral dynamics** describe how a node’s neighbors become infected after that node is infected. Networked Weibull regression models these dynamics in a data-driven manner and, together with cascading process aggregation, predicts overall cascades. This approach outperforms baselines for both cascade size and outbreak time prediction. One-hop subcascades supply the local behavioral information used in this aggregation.

3a264cb8a16719e34db2c5d5ef01a669e238f5c7.text:
## Echo Chambers, Polarization, and Online Political Discourse

This community examines whether echo chambers explain political polarization and radicalization. Echo chambers are theorized as ideologically homogeneous discussions shaped by opposing viewpoints and cognitive dissonance theory; in radical online discussions, opposing viewpoints may be undermined or marginalized. An online white nationalist website provides a setting for studying such an ideological echo chamber using observational trace data.

Research uses both macro-level studies and micro-level experiments. Macro-level studies question whether individual preferences generate echo chambers and suggest that cross-cutting exposure is common in digital life. Conversely, micro-level experiments find that individuals may favor belief-consistent information over cross-cutting exposure.

The Kavanaugh nomination is a case for studying polarization between Republican and Democratic senators, who generally supported and opposed the nomination, respectively. Twitter users are classified by stance toward the nomination using supervised and semi-supervised classification. Polarization quantification measures assess differences between user groups through hashtag usage and whom users retweet. Overall, the entities connect theories of ideological homogeneity and radicalization with computational analysis of online political discussions and engagement.

1f1a5890f075c5dd566729c42689131d04036578.text:
## Graph Learning and Processing in Attributed Networks

This community covers graph processing, semi-supervised learning, and change detection in evolving attributed networks. Graph software supports graph computations on real-world graphs, with applications including recommendations, fraud detection, and data integration. An online survey examines how users perform graph processing, including the computations they run; visualization remains a major challenge.

Higher order label spreading extends traditional label spreading, which relies on edges, by incorporating higher-order structures such as triangles. It operates on graphs and supports semi-supervised learning, reducing to standard label spreading in the base case. Semi-supervised learning is applied to fraud detection and protein identification. Graph software also supports fraud detection and recommendation applications.

Change detection in dynamic attributed networks represents evolving relationships as time sequences of attributed graphs. Attributes may be attached to vertices and edges. The task can identify changes at vertex, edge, subgraph, or community levels, supporting cyber intrusion detection, health care monitoring, and fraud detection.

a173378eb1e03cbc74fa34e8eafaf4fb48c5057a.text:
## Community Report: Accelerated Data, Verification, and Interactive Workflows

This community centers on systems that accelerate data-intensive computation, verification, retrieval, and iterative machine-learning workflows.

For data access, **SCOUT** performs structure-aware spatial prefetching using an approximate graph model, achieving 71–92% prefetching accuracy on neuroscience, medicine, and biology datasets. **SpeedReader** applies document-tree translation before rendering, predicts reader-mode suitability, removes trackers, and provides up to 27× speedup and 84% bandwidth reduction. **TSDS** supports time-series subsetting, uniform gridding, constraint queries, spectrogram data, and locally cached access through DAP and NcML.

Verification systems include **Verifas**, which uses symbolic representation and optimized Karp–Miller algorithms to verify LTL-FO properties and hierarchical workflow artifacts, outperforming Spin Verifier on a broader artifact class. Artifact verification also incorporates richer artifact data, task hierarchies, dependencies, arithmetic constraints, and vector addition systems. **TARS** combines static and dynamic analysis with coarse-grained command logging for parallel recovery in main-memory databases, reducing recovery latency and improving recovery rate.

Similarity and retrieval methods include **BayesLSH**, its lighter variant, adaptive candidate pruning, hash sketches, and Dice-coefficient estimation; **FENSHSES** combines bit operations, substring filtering, and permutation preprocessing. GPU and parallel implementations accelerate joins and analytics, while **Helix** reuses intermediates across ML iterations, achieving up to 19× runtime reduction and supporting rapid, responsive experimentation.

db5946068e7b316bf11ad1f61b9f88efc227f794.text:
## Community Report: Topic Mining, Political Networks, and Social-Data Analysis

This community links topic modelling and classification with political, public-health, advertising, and network-analysis applications. LDA supports unsupervised topic modelling, topic extraction, semantic mining, and analysis of CFPB consumer complaints, while topic models derive themes from question-answer pairs and policy records. Policy records reveal societal needs and can be compared with scientific outputs for research-society alignment. For short texts, LDA is limited by sparse word co-occurrence; entropy-based feature selection and feature expansion support topic extraction from tweets.

Political analysis includes stance classification for the Kavanaugh nomination, party-affiliation prediction for Republican and Democratic users, and polarization measurement. Multiple partitioning uses layer-wise partitioning and partition-similarity grouping on multiplex signed graphs to identify antagonistic parliamentary voter groups, including European Parliament data. Graph and network comparison is also relevant to systems biology and pattern recognition.

Other applications include hybrid LSTM offline-activity recognition from tweeting behavior, dynamic user profiling, and disease-spread prediction from geo-tagged Twitter and partial epidemiological data. Social-media image analysis addresses public health, smoking, and geo-tagged images. Privacy inference attacks expose personal information in Google profiles, motivating privacy-aware advertising. Finally, FNC-1 evaluation metrics and feature-rich stacked LSTM systems concern stance-classification performance, while discourse analysis examines alt-right racist, anti-immigration, and white-supremacist themes.

dabc0d2748e5904eb728852d09d1d94a6d6aef1e.text:
### Community Report: Multilayer Networks, Robustness, and Spreading

This community centers on multilayer and multiplex networks, where nodes may share multiple edge types and heterogeneous relationships. Graphlet analysis, similarity rates, clique percolation, motif clustering, persistent homology, and high-order network distances support structural comparison, mesoscale analysis, and essential-relationship discovery. Multilayer modularity and vectorial representations further analyze network organization.

A major theme is robustness. Robustness metrics, robustness surfaces, core lifetime, and optimal cost levels assess network disruption and network-core persistence. Layer-node random and targeted attacks expose multiplex vulnerability, while sequential defense mechanisms and targeted immunization improve resilience.

The community also studies spreading processes, including pathogen diffusion, epidemic spreading, awareness diffusion, and SIS/SIR models, across contact, physical, virtual, temporal, and multilayer networks. Epidemic thresholds are derived theoretically and through nonlinear Perron–Frobenius analysis; they depend on network structure, degree correlations, contact adaptation, transmission probability, and awareness diffusion. Aggregated static networks approximate thresholds when temporal volatility is reduced.

Generative model frameworks construct benchmark and weighted pairwise networks. Contact-network methods address influenza, epidemic detection, causative-network identification, and disease games. Recommendation research uses MONOMER, textual embeddings, and visual or compatibility representations to model heterogeneous relationships beyond simple similarity.

748212a0b0682b164df04a2c5dd5c7c45b5c502e.text:
