## Dynamic Search and Open Data Ecosystems

This community connects dynamic search, AI agents, and open data infrastructure.

Dynamic Search models human interaction with a search engine agent; AI agents interact with and assist humans in this setting. Early Dynamic Search agents used reinforcement learning. The Corpus-Level End-to-End Exploration (CE3) method is proposed to address limitations in Dynamic Search agents. CE3 compresses an entire text corpus into a global representation and introduces a retrieval function whose linear approximation enables document manipulation. It is evaluated on the TREC Dynamic Domain Track and outperforms state-of-the-art Dynamic Search systems.

A parallel theme concerns open data ecosystems. Artificial intelligence and data science aim to democratize these ecosystems, while AI and data science drive data-related assets. Data infrastructure enables the open data ecosystem, supports fine-grained asset exchange, and combines with scalable systems operation. Fine-grained asset exchange helps overcome lock-in effects, and the ecosystem aims to remove entry barriers. Agora presents a vision for an open data ecosystem.

Together, the entities describe methods and systems for scalable search-agent interaction alongside infrastructure and exchange mechanisms intended to make data-related assets more accessible.

4abd248a65970e23c0de67c811e61151e6358870.text:
## Multilayer Networks, Spreading, Robustness, and Recommendation

This community centers on **multiplex and multilayer networks**, which represent multiple edge types and heterogeneous relationships, including physical and virtual contact layers. It studies **network robustness** through robustness metrics and robustness surfaces, especially under layer-node random or targeted attacks. A sequential defense mechanism performs attack inference and vulnerability assessment to reduce network disruption, validated on canonical models and real-world topologies.

A major theme is **spreading processes**—including epidemic spreading, pathogen diffusion, and awareness diffusion—on time-varying, multilayer, and contact networks. Epidemic thresholds characterize spreading stability; theoretical analysis connects them to network structure, transmission probability, degree-degree correlation, and awareness diffusion. SIS and SIR models, multilayer spreading models, stochastic network disease games, and microscopic Markov-chain approaches support analysis of influenza and other disease-spread scenarios. Contact networks also enable epidemic detection, causative network identification, targeted immunization, and prediction using hybrid rooted PageRank.

The community further addresses **high-order network analysis**, representing tuple relationships with weighted hypergraphs and simplicial-complex filtrations, using persistent homology and network-distance metrics. Finally, **ReCoN** supports scalable network generation, while **Monomer** learns compatibility from textual embeddings and heterogeneous relationships for item recommendation beyond simple similarity.

4fef01802d10f920b743d442871e8027ccdd4fb1.text:
### Community Report: Graph Embeddings, Paper Evolution, and Trustworthy Content

This community links graph-based representation learning with academic retrieval, user trust prediction, and misinformation detection.

**Paper evolution and retrieval:** The *paper evolution graph* uses author, citation, and content information to uncover relationships, construct evolution chains, and support keyword, single-paper, and two-paper queries. Topic distributions group papers by topical aspects, while metagraph factorization soft-clusters papers into paper communities and obtains these distributions.

**Graph embedding and trust:** GEM-D provides a unifying framework for graph embedding algorithms, decomposing and unifying DeepWalk, node2vec, and LapEigs. It uses a node proximity function, loss function, and an empirically optimal exponential warping function. UltimateWalk is proposed from GEM-D analysis and outperforms DeepWalk and node2vec. Simultaneous user representation and trust inference learns user embeddings and trust prediction from limited binary user-user trust relations, outperforming classifier-based approaches using DeepWalk or LINE features. Trust prediction achieves a 92.65% F-score on approximately 356,000 user pairs.

**Clickbait and fake news:** The clickbait detector uses primarily text-based features extracted from post text and target article titles, with two-level classification combining 65 first-level classifiers. It was evaluated in the Clickbait Challenge 2017, achieving F-scores of 0.63 in blind tests and 0.43 in final evaluation. A related clickbait detection model uses distributed sub-word embeddings and achieves 98.3% accuracy. These methods support fake news detection and content-accuracy assessment on the BuzzFeed fake news dataset.

56617103fefc972968fb1ad1a2cfcb988ede7506.text:
## Community Report: Value-Aware Retrieval, Extraction, and Recommendation

This community connects information extraction and semantic retrieval with economically optimized recommendation.

For product data, sentence ranking uses product titles, descriptions, bullets, and search click-through logs. Attribute extraction supports ontology development and semantic search, while named entity recognition extracts attributes. An unsupervised NER model avoids annotated lexicons or corpora by combining pre-trained word embeddings, a Gaussian hidden Markov model for entity-span detection, and a deep autoencoding Gaussian mixture model for entity-type prediction. It is evaluated on CoNLL benchmark datasets. Semantic search expands queries through spreading activation over an ontology and retrieves documents in a text document retrieval system, including queries containing entities and explicit relations.

The recommendation methods emphasize list-level and business-aware optimization. Value-aware recommendation applies microeconomic concepts and reinforcement learning to e-commerce systems, directly optimizing profit and improving top-k ranking. User actions are mapped to economic value, with action conversion rate generalizing click conversion rate; aggregated value becomes the reward for a recommendation list. Personalized re-ranking follows a ranking algorithm, using transformer self-attention and pre-trained embeddings to model users and global item relationships, and is tested offline and in online e-commerce systems.

FeedRec is a reinforcement-learning framework for long-term engagement. Its Q-Network uses hierarchical LSTM behavior modeling, while its S-Network simulates the environment; off-policy learning remains a challenge.

5c4a8973159bd51d103b9474999ecc6562e7a39a.text:
## Indexing, Compression, Ranking, and Adaptive Query Systems

This community centers on efficient data indexing and query processing. Inverted indexes support scalable copy detection, semantic knowledge graphs, ranked top-k retrieval, and shared-value lookup; PRETTI uses one for its right-hand collection. Factorization-based compression, variable-byte encoding, partitioned representations, and collection partitioning reduce index size and memory requirements, while learned index structures use models to predict record positions and potentially replace B-trees, hash, bitmap, and traditional indexes.

Bitmap indexes emphasize compression and fast logical operations. Run-length encoding, WAH, CONCISE, Word-Aligned Hybrid compression, lexicographical sorting, row reordering, and 64-bit variants trade space for query speed. Root-split coding and other encodings further reduce size.

Rank-aware databases extend the Codd model with rank annotations, ranked relations, relational calculus, and ordinal transformations. Top-k queries address scoring, uncertain membership probabilities, and dynamic updates.

Join and set-processing methods include Join-Agg for memory-efficient aggregation over arbitrary acyclic multi-way joins without intermediate materialization, and temporal-probabilistic set operations using LAWAs. Semantic knowledge graphs dynamically materialize nodes and edges from corpus statistics.

Finally, iCam combines sampling, neural-network selection, and a learning-based planner to provide bounded-error approximate camera analytics on embedded hardware.

5f4b291084408b031e5cf936713e57ebae162a3c.text:
## Interdependent Cyber-Physical Network Resilience

This community focuses on failure propagation and self-healing in interdependent cyber-physical networks. These systems contain an overlay cyber network and an underlying physical network; the cyber network can heal failures in the physical network.

A factor graph represents the interdependent cyber-physical system, with factor nodes modeling node functionalities. A message passing algorithm operates on this representation. It studies the dynamics of failure propagation initiated by initial disruptions, as well as healing dynamics associated with self-healing.

Fixed point analysis is used to analyze the fixed points of the message passing algorithm. Together, the factor graph and message passing framework connect node functionalities to the evolution of failures and recovery across the cyber and physical networks.

897e7514d1da0b17a6e1ca72c30908d3a1177b1a.text:
## Community Report: Ranking, Recommendation, and Marketplace Search

This community covers neural ranking and optimization across recommender systems, information retrieval, and multimedia search.

**Recommendation:** SDM is deployed in Taobao’s large-scale online recommender system. It models multiple interest tendencies with multi-head self-attention, combines short-term sessions and relevant long-term behaviors through long-short-term gated fusion, matches sequential user-behavior vectors with item embeddings, and captures dynamic preferences while improving commercial metrics. Taobao is also associated with a Transformer-based Behavior Sequence Transformer for sequential user signals.

**Set ranking and retrieval:** SetRank learns permutation-invariant ranking functions over document sets using stacked induced multi-head self-attention and permutation-equivariant document representations. It models cross-document interactions and local query context, outperforming traditional learning-to-rank and neural IR baselines.

**Video retrieval:** A Cross Modal Interaction Network addresses query-based moment retrieval. Its multi-stage cross-modal interaction relates natural-language queries to video context, while syntactic GCN learns fine-grained query representations from syntactic structure; self-attention captures long-range video dependencies.

**Marketplace optimization:** Search experience optimization in two-sided marketplaces—including Taobao, eBay, and Etsy—jointly optimizes group- and market-level metrics under business constraints. Evolutionary Strategies act as policy learners, jointly optimizing these metrics and avoiding traditional cascading methods, with evaluation on Etsy data.

581cde8583ee9d2e87064a63b844fd531605718a.text:
## Open Research, Citation Infrastructure, and Scalable Visual Analytics

This community connects open science infrastructure with research software, citation analysis, and interactive data exploration. **OpenCitations** publishes open citation data, including the **COCI** DOI-to-DOI index, OpenCitations Corpus, indexes, and Open Citation Identifiers. These resources support citation-content analysis, quality control, coverage-gap analysis, and research on Russian papers. **Crossref** contributes source citation data.

Software citation and credit are linked to software authorship, publishing, open peer review, and research-software quality. The **Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS)** publishes research-software articles under a Creative Commons license and is sponsored by NumFOCUS and affiliated with the Open Source Initiative. INRIA, WSSSPE, and related efforts develop citation guidance and software-credit practices.

A second focus is scalable visualization and graph analytics. **NeuralCubes** approximates data-cube functionality for real-time aggregation over large multidimensional datasets, using low-memory and client-side evaluation. **Diel** compiles declarative specifications into relational queries and scales visualizations through back-end services and transparent autoscaling. **Network Repository**, **Zenvisage**, and **WebSMATCH** support graph analysis, dataset exploration, public-data integration, metadata extraction, and visualization.

Additional applications include **Progmosis**, which estimates individual contagion risk from mobility and regional infection rates, and regulatory impact analysis, which evaluates how scientific evidence informs economically significant regulations.

83fb7d0d5694c321403b991f9eae67d4b0f80004.text:
## Graph-Based Retrieval, Estimation, and Adaptive Search

This community connects graph sampling, classification, retrieval, and real-time information systems.

For graph analysis, **AdjustedWalk** learns classifiers during graph walks and applies post-hoc adjustment to estimate group properties, including minority proportions overall and among high-degree nodes. Sampling methods divide edges into training and probe sets, affecting prediction performance and missing-link results. Target, auxiliary, and affiliation graphs support sampling in hybrid social affiliation networks. Classifiers also predict migrant churn, crowdsourced decisions, and censorship.

Search research emphasizes adaptive and real-time systems. **Seeker** adapts results in real time, while user feedback supports interactive and human-in-the-loop retrieval, training-set refinement, entity profiles, and ranking adaptation. Dynamic postings allocation manages in-memory postings lists, balancing query speed and memory utilization through the “Goldilocks” trade-off. Pangloss performs streaming entity disambiguation in noisy text using key-phrase identification, semantic similarity, and a local embedded database.

Multimedia retrieval includes content-based image retrieval, dominant-color descriptors, texture features, and linear-time approximate Earth Mover’s Distance. Pareto depth combines Pareto fronts with manifold ranking for multiple-query image retrieval. Approximate filters evaluate spatial predicates.

Additional applications include Laburst for burst and sports-event detection, supervised keyword extraction, open knowledge bases based on an OpenStreetMap semantic network, flood-impact analysis, and toxic-behavior detection.

f3184288a42ef5fc8a9685759ab3382a30d6916d.text:
## Community Report: Opinion Dynamics, Online Communities, and Knowledge Accumulation

This community connects spatial opinion dynamics, computational community detection, and the study of knowledge accumulation in analytic philosophy.

Spatial opinion dynamics models spatially situated opinions with varying conviction using a fully spatial model without mixing. It produces clustering, polarization, and deadlock patterns. Mean field differential equations provide comparison-based insight for selected parameter regimes. Mixing mechanisms—including spatial relocation and the non-local interaction method telephoning—can break up deadlock and polarization; telephoning also hastens consensus.

NeuroCom profiles communities in online groups by inferring neural representations from published user content. It uses word and message embeddings to identify nuanced discussion topics and finds communities in a latent space. Its clustering improves on common unsupervised approaches. Online communities generate the user-authored content that supports this analysis.

The knowledge-accumulation strand examines analytic philosophy as a case study in para-scientific areas. Analytic philosophy began accumulating knowledge after the Second World War and is analyzed through Kuhn’s theory of normal science, qualitative citation context analysis, and temporal citation context analysis. Analytic philosophy papers from 1950–2009 form the sample, with citations classified by epistemological function. Subfield fragmentation is proposed to explain knowledge accumulation without a corresponding rise in consensus.

ee9bdfe9d6728b1afa70f37731241b21f3bd9ac1.text:
## Diversity-Aware Ranking and Network Centrality

This community covers two related themes: ranking design ideas for diversity and quality, and optimizing network centrality through network modifications.

For design idea ranking, diversity and quality are evaluated with rank metrics that extend set-based measures to ranked-list permutations. Determinantal point processes support diversity modeling and selection across bundles and are reported as suitable for ranking text-expressed items. Additive submodular functions provide an alternative diversity measure. A greedy algorithm diversifies rankings with theoretical guarantees and empirical performance, demonstrated on OpenIDEO, an online design community.

For networks, coverage centrality counts node pairs whose shortest path passes through a node set. Coverage centrality maximization seeks to maximize this metric, while network design frames centrality control as a network modification problem, including adding edges. Network updates control node centrality through such modifications. Greedy and sampling algorithms provide scalable approaches, with approximation guarantees yielding almost-optimal solutions under realistic constraints. However, inapproximability results establish strong limits on efficient approximation for coverage centrality maximization.

bfc24ee9fdacfd780a317fd1c149925a04113204.text:
## Community Report: Verification, Data Systems, and Intelligent Querying

This community centers on verification, data integrity, and systems that make data-driven workflows reliable. **Artifact verification** extends the Guard-Stage-Milestone artifact model and supports richer artifact data, database dependencies, arithmetic constraints, and task hierarchies. **Verifas** efficiently verifies LTL-FO properties of hierarchical workflows using symbolic representations, Karp–Miller optimizations, and evaluations on real and synthetic workflows; it outperforms Spin Verifier. Verification also addresses temporal properties and first-order μ-calculus variants.

Data integrity is connected to AI training data, data-dependent programs, and formal integrity guarantees. **FVSS** secures cloud data warehouses through verifiable secret sharing, while advanced secret-sharing schemes support encrypted computation and are assessed by querying power, access, and cost. **CLX** supports data transformation through pattern clustering and regular-expression replacement, improving users’ verification success and limiting verification-time growth relative to data size.

The community also covers recovery and querying. **TARS** combines static and dynamic analysis with coarse-grained command logging to reduce recovery latency and improve recovery rate in main-memory databases. **Duoquest** performs dual-specification query synthesis using guided partial enumeration, outperforming natural-language interfaces on query construction and top-1 accuracy. **SetRank** learns permutation-invariant entity-set rankings with induced multi-head self-attention, modeling entity relationships and types. **NLI GIBIR** provides natural-language bibliographic retrieval and answers 39 of 40 example queries.

58a2a03ebee414a656ae37af057917ee4e60ff45.text:
## Reddit Activity and Controversy Analysis

This community centers on **Reddit**, a community-driven discussion platform, and the analysis of activity within it. Reddit contains behavioral data from the **Reddit activity data** dataset, which supports research on **post activity** and controversies in posts.

**Statistical analysis** is applied to Reddit activity data to analyze patterns in post activity. The **controversy detection** task studies controversies in posts using the same data. **User interaction modeling** models user interactions around posts, providing a method for examining participation and engagement.

The concept of **mayfly buzz** describes short-lived but extremely active posts on Reddit and characterizes corresponding post activity. **Limelight hogging activity** likewise describes activity around highly active posts. Together, these concepts and methods connect Reddit’s behavioral data with the study of unusually intense, short-lived, and potentially controversial discussions.

99aa89aed4c7aff6ce2f6c63efa4238cd94832a6.text:
## Neural, Query-Aware, and Quantum-Inspired Information Retrieval

This community covers document ranking and unsupervised information retrieval across news, web, email, and session search.

The **neural vector space model** learns low-dimensional word and document representations using gradient descent, learning term specificity and regularities related to Luhn significance directly from document collections. It ranks documents by query–document similarity, improves on latent semantic vector space methods and mixtures containing a baseline vector space model, and provides a complementary relevance signal to lexical language models.

**Query-aware neural ranking** incorporates query types into ranking models. Hierarchical query clustering uses truncated SVD and varimax rotation to produce coarse-to-fine query types, while query cluster prediction serves as an auxiliary task. Multi-task neural ranking simultaneously ranks documents and predicts query types, significantly outperforming baseline neural ranking models; it is proposed for email search ranking and evaluated on real-world email search queries.

The **quantum-inspired geometric model**, based on quantum theory, ranks documents for subsequent queries using estimated relevance weights. Dynamic relevance weights capture users’ changing importance across relevance dimensions, informed by relevance feedback and evolving during a user session. The model is tested with web search engine data and evaluated on the TREC Session Track.

cdd9b66d3f21a19fb1800db0d3453955f78e7fea.text:
## Graph Learning for Classification, Recommendation, and Music

This community centers on graph neural networks (GNNs), whose core operation is graph convolution, usually approximated through message passing. General spectral graph convolution unifies convolution- and sampling-based GNNs, while graph diffusion convolution replaces direct-neighbor propagation with generalized graph diffusion, including personalized PageRank and heat-kernel approaches. It can combine with graph-based models, spectral clustering, and supervised learning.

GNN research targets semi-supervised node classification, graph classification, and low-data learning. Benchmarks examine high- and low-dimensional signals, showing that simple, regularized architectures can be near-optimal with little data, whereas complex architectures perform better with more features and training data. MuchGCN uses layer-specific graph convolutions, graph channels, convolutional-neural-network-inspired multi-channel encoding, and iterative pooling for hierarchical graph structures.

Recommendation work addresses sparse user–item interaction graphs. AGNN exploits attribute graphs, uses an extended variational autoencoder and Gated-GNN, and learns preference embeddings for cold-start users and items. S²-Meta combines few-shot, scenario-specific, and sequential meta-learning to initialize and adapt models for online recommendation, including Mobile Taobao’s Guess You Like session.

Music applications combine timbral, harmonic, and rhythmic frame-level features with similarity network fusion, affinity matrices, and spectral clustering for hierarchical repeated-section discovery and music structure analysis. GNNs are also studied under black-box and white-box attacks.

8c166222fbcb0c1eee470746649fe60042499df3.text:
## Opinion Dynamics and Optimal Influence

This community studies **opinion dynamics**: how opinions evolve in societies modeled by the **voter model**, its **generalized voter model**, and the **discrete-time Friedkin–Johnsen model**. The generalized model represents heterogeneous populations containing strong-willed individuals, conformists, and rebels, while voter-model extensions account for stubborn agents with immutable opinions.

A central task is **opinion shaping**, in which external inputs continuously influence selected agents. Related **influencing strategies**, including those motivated by political campaigns, are optimized over a finite time horizon. Strategies tend to be applied near the end in predominantly strong-willed or rebel societies, and near the beginning in predominantly conformist societies.

The control objectives TF, GF, and MF formalize different goals: minimizing control cost while raising all opinions above a threshold (TF), raising a scalar function of the opinion vector (GF), or maximizing the minimum scalar opinion value under a cost constraint (MF). **Optimal control** and the **Pontryagin maximum principle** provide optimality systems and control functions, including nonsmooth numerical methods for MF. TF and GF exhibit a **turnpike property**, maintaining controls and states near equilibrium for much of the horizon; this property also guides controllable-node selection. Opinion dynamics can additionally be formulated as a **stochastic shortest path** problem solved using **value iteration**.

cca63ff5811d0aa3f0b546e816f1f500f2f5979b.text:
## Regret Queries and Tractable Graph-Database Reasoning

This community covers two themes: utility-aware database retrieval and the expressiveness and complexity of query languages.

**k-regret queries** return a size-\(k\) subset of a database while minimizing the maximum **regret ratio** across utility functions. Additive utility functions have been the primary focus, while multiplicative utility functions provide a proposed variant and more expressive modeling of diminishing marginal rates of substitution. Cobb–Douglas and constant-elasticity-of-substitution functions are related multiplicative families frequently used in microeconomics. A bounded regret query algorithm guarantees regret-ratio bounds, whereas a heuristic algorithm reduces regret empirically. Unlike top-\(k\) queries, which optimize a specific utility function, k-regret queries address the worst case across functions.

The second theme concerns query determinacy and reasoning over graph data. **Regular path queries** are a paradigmatic query language for graph databases, but query determinacy—whether views suffice to compute a target query—is undecidable for them. **Warded TGDs**, a restricted fragment of tuple-generating dependencies and the logical core of Vadalog, support tractable data-complexity reasoning. Piece-wise linear recursion can otherwise cause undecidability; wardedness restricts recursion and, combined with it, is proposed for space-efficient reasoning.

25099c663458d8aa9b920c1d3e03872af3e30ee2.text:
## Community Report: Semantic Recommendation and Ranking Systems

This community centers on recommendation, question-answer retrieval, and semantic similarity across text, visual, and multimodal data.

A production hybrid recommender at FINN.no combines marketplace text, images, metadata, and user behaviors such as page views and messages. It uses deep learning, attention mechanisms, transfer learning for unbalanced data, and staged training, with user behavior serving as noisy labels for embeddings.

Visual and multimodal style recommenders support assortment generation, curating living-room furniture around seed products and optimizing visual compatibility. The multimodal system combines product text and visual data, uses transfer learning and polylingual topic modeling to infer style, and has been evaluated through large-scale online A/B tests at Overstock. A related multimodal recommender performs large-scale complementary assortment generation.

HyperQA addresses efficient question-answer ranking and retrieval using a pairwise ranking objective. Question and answer embeddings are represented in hyperbolic rather than Euclidean space, enabling latent hierarchy discovery. It outperforms Attentive Pooling BiLSTMs and Multi-Perspective CNNs on QA benchmarks without complicated attention mechanisms.

Story recommendation ranks stories by shared literary themes using knowledge-based filtering, set-based similarity, and hierarchical semantic similarity. The Star Trek episode dataset, theme ontology, topic modeling, StorySet benchmarks, and an R Shiny application support annotation, evaluation, and public use.

78f3e0898ff8c7ecf42683c79b98f0c0ba380d83.text:
### Social Behavior, Mobility, and Predictive Research

This community combines demographic inference, social-network analysis, human mobility, data compression, and scientific-impact modeling.

Gender, age, race, ethnicity, nationality, and occupation are used to characterize users and relationships. Demographic inference and automatic demographic identification predict gender and age from profile images, while mobile-phone communication patterns support age and relationship characterization. Call frequency and daily regularity vary by gender and age: opposite-gender intimate pairs are highest on both measures, whereas older pairs communicate less frequently and regularly. These analyses use mobile-phone users, Mexican mobile-phone users, and the European FetLife member network.

Human mobility is studied through location-based social media, cellular-phone mobility data, trajectories, and transportation networks. It informs epidemic modeling, pandemic-spread analysis, traffic prediction, opportunistic routing, and information-diffusion protocols. Aggregate distance-decay patterns may produce ecological fallacy for individual movements.

Twitter, Facebook, Weibo, Google+, election, and candidate datasets support studies of personality, emojis, campaigns, identity, and prediction. AUC and ROC curves evaluate credit scoring, drug-recall prediction, conversion prediction, platform identification, multimodal attacks, and altmetric indices.

Compression research evaluates SIMD algorithms on Twitter, TREC, and Wikipedia data, emphasizing encoding and decoding speed. Citation profiles are categorized by peak patterns; a dynamic growth model reproduces observed profiles where preferential attachment fails.

69a232b79a852dc45962cae4c8b5b5260161dfcd.text:
## Community Report: News Sharing, Manipulation, and Community Identity

This community studies news engagement and popularity on social platforms, especially Reddit and Twitter. Research on clickbait compares it with news tabloidization, examining sensational article titles, social sharing patterns, organic reach, and the behavior of news consumers. Non-clickbait tweets provide a comparison.

On Reddit, news aggregation and popularity prediction use content and sentiment features; posts with user-changed article titles tend to be more popular than posts retaining original titles, while title changes can alter perceived engagement. These studies consider crowd and platform manipulation.

A second theme is the early detection of promoted campaigns. A supervised learning framework, trained and evaluated on trending hashtag tweets, distinguishes artificially promoted trends from organic trends. It exploits hundreds of time-varying features, including changing content, sentiment, timing, and user metadata. Content features remain consistently useful, while user features are more informative before or at trending time and timing features become more useful after additional activity.

Finally, a language-based identity typology maps nearly 300 Reddit communities by identity distinctiveness and temporal dynamism. Both are associated with larger acculturation gaps between existing users and newcomers; these gaps may hinder community integration. Distinctive and highly dynamic identities are also associated with higher user retention, while community identity shapes engagement among new and existing users.

dc7f4afd899a3e6cf2de7a89a27ec530d130a375.text:
## Community Report: Constrained Mining, Prediction, and Network Optimization

This community spans sequential pattern mining, financial prediction, language analysis, graph algorithms, and epidemic/network modeling.

Sequential pattern mining extracts frequent subsequences from sequence databases for web-user and DNA analysis. Constraint programming, global constraints, generic solvers, and methods such as PrefixSpan and CSPADE support mining, regular-expression mining, and index deployment ordering. Parallel approaches include partition-, Apriori-, pattern-growth-, and hybrid PSPM for stream data.

Financial work combines stock-market data, online news, semantic sentiment analysis, and hybrid attention networks to capture sequential content dependencies and diverse influences. Adaptive trading algorithms select financial instruments using sentiment and historical values, while stock-trend prediction is evaluated on real-world market data and supported by self-paced learning.

Optimization research includes stochastic and mixed-integer programming, bilevel models, sample-average approximation, and network design for disagreement minimization and centrality control. Bregman hyperlink regression predicts tuple hyperlink weights in hyper-relational data using Bregman divergence. Randomized optimal transport replaces traditional cost minimization with free-energy minimization over hitting and non-hitting paths.

Graph methods address flow and maximum-flow computation, graph simplification through gate graphs, and path-based probabilistic models. Epidemic studies use SI/SIS dynamics, bounded susceptibility, and disease-resistant networks to analyze spreading, extinction, and network structure. Clinical data management, decision support, and bipolar-disorder recognition apply linguistic features including morpheme collocations, syntactic patterns, gender differences, and LIWC.

1206390a4f3f6f85f2884d6ef5e99927ad078398.text:
## Probabilistic Data Engineering and AI-Assisted Peer Review

This community connects large-scale data processing, probabilistic programming, featurization, and editorial strategy. Apache Spark enables fast large-scale data processing, provides statistical models and inference algorithms, and underlies InferSpark. InferSpark promotes probabilistic programming in data engineering, leverages Spark’s distributed main-memory processing, provides a programmable framework for big data analysis, and supports efficient statistical inference. Probabilistic programming enables succinct development of statistical models and can automatically generate inference algorithms.

Featurization includes feature creation, feature selection, and feature extraction. Columnar databases efficiently calculate featurization operations, while augmented dictionary values reduce data movement and duplication to improve efficiency. An integrated columnar database and AI architecture connects database processing with AI analysis and supports iterative feedback across extraction, featurization, and analysis.

The community also applies evolutionary computation to social systems and peer review. Cartesian genetic programming evolves editorial strategies, reduces journal editors’ workload, and is reported to reduce peer-review duration by 30% without increasing the reviewer pool. Peer review uses artificial intelligence to support faster editorial strategies, which publishing houses may treat as trade secrets.

cb8ba94f14fb0f2d05f310190ee0cc10fce91d07.text:
## Query Enrichment, Neural Inspection, and Expert Answering

This community connects data-centric query processing, neural-network analysis, and community question answering.

**PIQUE** integrates into query processing as an operator, prioritizing enrichment functions and supporting progressive data enrichment. Because enrichment may not be completed during ingestion preprocessing, progressive enrichment enables interactive exploratory analysis. PIQUE improves answer quality faster than baseline approaches, while enrichment is needed before data can be effectively queried.

**DeepBase** provides a query-based interface for neural network behavior inspection. It identifies individual or groups of hidden units through their statistical dependencies with desired hypotheses, and evaluates hypothesis functions that transform datasets into time-series signals. Applied to a neural translation model, DeepBase analyzes different model portions and shows that the model learns syntactic structure while performing language translation. Its optimizations speed existing analysis approaches by up to 413×.

In **community question answering**, expert recommendation addresses question–answerer matching by directing questions to suitable answerers. This supports knowledge acquisition and knowledge circulation, aims to improve answer quality, and reduces response time. Requesters ask questions, and answerers provide responses.

7a53e55287ccd45d579edbcbe287886a7143c6ce.text:
## University Ranking Systems and Their Comparability

This community focuses on the **i UGR Rankings**, a national ranking system for the Spanish university system. It ranks Spanish universities by fields and subfields, emphasizing disciplinary profiles.

The i UGR Rankings are compared with the **Shanghai**, **QS**, **NTU**, and **Leiden** rankings. Shanghai and QS are also associated with the **university ranking comparison** method, which is used to compare ranking results.

The community distinguishes between **international rankings** and **national rankings**. International rankings are described as unable to accurately represent national university systems and as often inadequately representing universities’ disciplinary profiles. National rankings are therefore proposed as complements to international rankings.

Overall, the entities connect ranking systems through comparative evaluation while highlighting the role of national, field-based approaches—particularly the i UGR Rankings—in representing the Spanish university system.

fcd2bd59a89f38ffa2cba2095788c923b9b1ed45.text:
## Cross-Domain Ideas, Consumer Protection, and MOOC Learning

This community connects three applications of text and topic analysis.

For creative ideation, **topic modeling**, implemented with **LDA**, extracts latent topics from unstructured **OpenIDEO ideas**. These topics support a **bisociative information network** that represents conceptual similarity and helps users find cross-domain links and bridges. Such **cross-domain inspiration** stimulates idea generation and design inspiration; the resulting connections are perceived as more novel.

For consumer protection, LDA analyzes **CFPB Consumer Complaints** and extracts latent topics from complaint narratives. **Trend analysis** tracks these topics over time and evaluates the effectiveness of CFPB regulations. A **decision support system** can automate emerging-topic detection for the CFPB, supporting more efficient investigations into unfair, deceptive, or abusive practices. Financial institutions are expected to prioritize consumer protection.

For MOOC social learning, a **probabilistic point process model** represents learner posts in discussion forums, integrates topic modeling of post text, infers learner topic interests, and recommends discussion threads. It models the decay of post activity, varies excitation according to thread structure, and provides topic-category timescales. The approach is evaluated on three MOOC datasets, with thread recommendation performance assessed using MOOC forum data.

f5c9a691086601921b46da45b17ddef84cc19766.text:
## Image Virality, Visual Attributes, and Prediction

This community examines image virality through virality dynamics, visual characteristics, and prediction tasks. Virality is measured by a virality score, while post reactions exhibit dynamics associated with post virality. Visual characteristics are analyzed as factors associated with image virality; image orientation and mean saturation are examples. Five key visual attributes correlate with image virality, and relative attributes encode semantic information relevant to virality.

The work addresses individual image virality prediction, viral image topic prediction, and relative virality prediction. Classifiers using state-of-the-art image features predict the virality of individual images, the dominant topic of viral images, and relative virality between image pairs. The SVM+deep relative attributes method achieves 68.10% accuracy on relative virality prediction, outperforming human performance, while humans achieve 60.12% accuracy. Human predictions vary across viewing contexts, highlighting the role of context in assessing image virality.

1415fafa034901ceb12d4a796cdf9a5adbae599a.text:
### Diel: Scalable Interactive Visualization and Event Modeling

This community centers on **Diel**, a system for interactive visualizations over large datasets. Diel treats UI events as a data stream and captures them in an **event history** that represents interaction state. It provides a simple **declarative interface**, compiling declarative specifications into **relational queries** that query event history and visualization data.

Diel scales visualizations to use **back-end services** and provides cross-layer **transparent autoscaling**. Large datasets enable visualization scaling as data size increases, while **caching** supports cross-layer performance optimization.

The community also connects event histories to **temporal point processes**, which conventionally represent event history as a vector and model sequential event propagation over time. However, these conventional models do not explicitly model **latent graph structure**. Thus, relational querying and event-history representations support Diel’s interactive visualization workflow, while temporal point processes provide a related approach to modeling sequential events.

11a404ee558ee2a80b1d8017aec94aae2da80d4e.text:
## Scalable Persistent-Memory Hashing

This community centers on **DASH**, a system for scalable dynamic hash tables on **persistent memory**. DASH provides a holistic design for dynamic hash tables and adapts both **extendible hashing** and **linear hashing**. It supports load factors above 90%, emphasizing high space utilization.

DASH also provides **instant recovery** for hash tables. This capability is associated with a demonstrated **57 ms recovery time**, highlighting rapid restoration after interruption.

The system is evaluated using real persistent-memory hardware, specifically **Intel Optane DCPMM**, on a **24-core machine**. Thus, the community connects hash-table design methods, high-load operation, persistent-memory systems, and recovery performance in one evaluation setting.

4df9e5ad8ee3937362ea2685c3f02397f0ce25fb.text:
## Community Report: Social Learning, Scalable Analytics, and Event Modeling

This community connects social learning, database tuning, visualization, and temporal event analysis.

Social-learning research models interactions among individual agents estimating an underlying state of nature and transmitting rating actions. Local non-Bayesian social learning, the Chinese restaurant game, and simulation examine learning under network effects, including negative network externality, herding, and data incest. Applications include online reputation systems, analytical reasoning, human society, and MOOC discussion forums.

Database-system research focuses on index tuning for workloads. RITA uses a binary integer program to generate divergent index designs for replicated databases, monitors online workload changes, and supports elastic reconfiguration and replica failure. Cophy is another index-tuning approach.

Visualization systems address large and multidimensional datasets. NeuralCubes provides low-memory neural approximations to data cubes for real-time aggregation and client-side evaluation. Zenvisage uses ZQL for visual queries, while DIEL offers a declarative interface that compiles specifications into relational queries and provides transparent autoscaling for visualization back ends.

Temporal point-process methods model event histories, sequential propagation, and latent dynamics. NESTPP represents online discussion forums through main-thread and reply streams, using intensity functions for information-cascade modeling. A probabilistic point-process model infers learner topic interests and recommends MOOC threads. Progmosis estimates individual contagion risk from cellular-network movement and regional infection rates.

54070079dbdd413f24028c5e1dfaf73791358a80.text:
## HashGNN for Scalable Graph Hashing

This community centers on **HashGNN**, a graph neural network system for hashing in industry-scale applications. HashGNN contains a **GNN encoder** that learns continuous node representations from a **user–item interaction network**, followed by a **hash layer** that converts these representations into discrete hash codes.

Training optimizes both a **reconstruction loss**, which reconstructs observed links in the interaction network, and a **ranking loss**, which preserves the relative ordering of hash codes. A guided **straight-through estimator** supports discrete optimization and provides guidance to reduce gradient magnification.

The broader graph neural network context includes link prediction with few or no node features and improvements for industry-scale applications. HashGNN applies these graph neural network capabilities to hashing, and is evaluated on real-world **Alibaba datasets**.

7d7607139a3a07da720143d87fbecc14cfc1f4b0.text:
## Influence, Profit, and Scalable Seed Selection

This community focuses on viral marketing in online social networks (OSNs), especially profit maximization and threshold activation. Advertisers hire OSN providers to run campaigns, while user activity creates diffusion costs for providers. The profit metric accounts for these costs and, under diffusion models, is expressed as the difference between two submodular functions.

A two-phase framework selects a seed set for profit maximization. A seed set may also address the threshold activation problem by achieving a target expected activation with minimum size. The framework is evaluated on real OSN datasets.

The scalable bicriteria TAP algorithm solves the threshold activation problem with approximation guarantees under the general triggering model, which represents internal influence within the network. It exploits bicriteria optimization to trade solution quality against computational cost; the parameter alpha controls the running-time versus accuracy tradeoff. Its scalable running-time bound depends on network size, alpha, and solution size.

The algorithm also incorporates external influence when a seed-selection cost-effectivity condition is satisfied. Thus, the framework and algorithm connect seed selection, expected activation, influence diffusion, provider costs, and efficient approximation.

8997814152422e3b44c728b3a38eb5264d043409.text:
## Merchant Incentive Optimization in Mobile Payment

This community focuses on optimizing merchant incentives in mobile payment marketing. **Alipay** provides the mobile payment platform, while mobile payment marketing promotes its use and includes merchant incentive optimization.

The optimization task uses **merchant representations** to model how merchants respond, with **incentive sensitivity** guiding allocation of **incentives**. Optimization is constrained by the **marketing budget** and aims to maximize a **commercial objective**. The **transaction network** describes similarities in merchant responses to incentives, supporting this optimization.

A key method is **graph representation learning**, which learns merchant representations from the transaction network and applies them to **node classification**. **Online experiments** evaluate the effectiveness of this approach. Overall, the community connects transaction-network-based representation learning with budget-constrained incentive allocation for mobile payment marketing.

a1ae82dad23fccc59a21fde5fb272c01abbab182.text:
## Spatial Indexing and Spatial Frequent-Pattern Mining

This community covers spatial search, adaptive indexing, and the analysis of spatial social data. Nearest-neighbor search uses spatial indexes to filter unnecessary computations, with kd-trees, R-trees, Vor-trees, and other tree-like spatial indexes serving as baselines. K-nearest-neighbor search generalizes this task. Multi-layer Voronoi diagrams provide a non-tree spatial index, support both nearest- and k-nearest-neighbor queries with logarithmic time complexity, and achieve higher search efficiency than compared indexes. They are constructed from multiple Voronoi-diagram layers.

Flood is a multi-dimensional in-memory index that optimizes predicate-based range scans, adapts automatically to workloads and datasets, and contributes toward end-to-end learned database systems. R-trees and z-ordering represent alternative approaches to multi-dimensional indexing.

A second theme is spatial frequent-pattern mining from spatial social data. The spatial social data model defines spatial support, spatial frequent patterns, spatial partitioning, and spatial clustering. SFP-growth explores these patterns using an SFP-tree, which maintains frequent words and frequent spatial cells. Spatial partitioning commonly supports hierarchical, tree-like spatial index construction.

5a1c2993a089446bfe6866c00bd0c801f46e03be.text:
## Characterizing WhatsApp Groups and News Media

This community covers two related research areas: political discussion in WhatsApp public groups and source-level characterization of news media.

The **public WhatsApp group dataset** contains public group data collected through a defined data collection methodology, supporting social science research and statistical exploration. Political discussion analysis operates at three levels: the **message layer** (individual messages and user posts), **user layer** (actions during interactions), and **group layer** (aggregate message patterns). Groups are classified as political or non-political using associated keywords. Political groups use more text messages and exhibit a Zipf-like distribution of user messages; their content distributions are represented through input data distributions. Messages may combine audio, images, and video.

The **group behavior characterization framework**, applicable to systems such as WhatsApp, introduces communication group metrics for characterizing behavior.

A second strand addresses **factuality prediction** and **news media bias prediction** for entire news media sources. News websites and news articles provide evaluated sources and content-derived media features. Wikipedia, URL structure, and web traffic provide additional source, structural, audience, and reach features. Both tasks improve over baselines and provide information relevant to fact-checking systems.

53be4f016e65929dd1cc024d7f7bd78534943520.text:
## Community Report: User Concepts, Advertising, and Social-Behavior Modeling

This community covers three related areas: user-centered concept mining, distributed advertising prediction, and online-behavior classification.

A system deployed in Tencent QQ Browser mines user queries and interactive search click logs, discovers user-centered concepts, constructs a topic–concept–instance taxonomy, and tags documents. These concepts improve search and news-feed recommendation, increasing Impression Efficiency by 6.01%.

SAEC is a similarity-aware embedding matrix compression method implemented and evaluated on Tencent’s Numerous production distributed machine-learning system. It clusters similar features within each field, using feature frequency for faster optimization, and is evaluated on 10 days of QQ Mobile Browser feature data. For conversion prediction, SAEC matches the uncompressed system on AUC and log loss. Conversion prediction uses online activity trails and supports B2B ad targeting for B2B products and advertisers; Yahoo Gemini provides evaluation data.

Other work detects abusive behavior, including cyberbullying and cyberaggression, using text, user, and network attributes. Gamergate is associated with both phenomena. Verification-status prediction uses profile metadata and tweet/content features through verification classifiers, evaluated with AUC.

Finally, distributed activity representations build seed lists to identify relevant users for B2B advertisers. Traditional recommendation methods also incorporate content features.

0f10af6c0b32b9712666fd97b133c4b934d83be9.text:
## Mapping Innovation, Knowledge Translation, and Scientific Dynamics

This community focuses on how research knowledge moves through innovation processes, from basic science and technological development to preclinical, translational, and clinical applications. Knowledge translation is examined in drug discovery, molecular entities, nanomaterials, cervical cancer, Ebola hemorrhagic fever, and biomedical innovation, with demand and supply perspectives complemented by technological capabilities and selection mechanisms.

Bibliometric and scientometric mapping provide the main analytical toolkit. Multidimensional scaling, VOS, spring-embedded algorithms, overlay mapping, literature network analysis, controlled-vocabulary embeddings, panel data analysis, and topic-evolution analysis map innovation patterns, research fronts, semantic change, and emerging technologies. MeSH and MEDLINE support document matrices, vocabulary-based embeddings, and citation-data normalization, while Web of Science categories provide a comparison.

Patents and patent families extend publication-based analysis to RNA interference, Ebola-virus targets, inventor communities, and first-citation timing. Algorithmic historiography and HistCite reconstruct intellectual lineages and intellectual history. Bifold visualizes bipartite datasets and structures in voting, cuisine, and other datasets.

Systems such as CASCON, VxM, GoPubMed, Network of Excellence, Translational Axis, and Innovation Opportunities Explorer connect mapping with knowledge dissemination, communication, strategic intelligence, and practical use. Dental materials, HPV, MRI, and RNA interference serve as innovation case studies.

59c19864d1c492aaae974023b173aa803a6bb471.text:
## Query Pushdown into S3 Select

This community centers on query pushdown for database management systems (DBMSs) using Amazon Web Services’ S3 Select. Query pushdown moves DBMS query operations into S3 Select, potentially reducing cost.

PushdownDB is a DBMS developed to evaluate S3 computation and implements query pushdown into S3 Select. It was reported to be 30% cheaper than a baseline without S3 Select.

Several operations can be pushed into S3 Select cost-effectively, including filtering, projection, and aggregation. Group-by operations and joins may also be pushed down, but they require reimplementation to use S3 Select. The community therefore connects S3 Select, query pushdown, and operation-specific methods with cost considerations for DBMS execution.

8c789c084b93d6401882397c52dc8727bcde6e87.text:
### Homophily Estimation and Relational Prediction

This community focuses on **homophily estimation**, **node attribute prediction**, and **dyadic prediction** in networks. Homophily estimation commonly relies on predicted node attributes, such as ethnicity or gender, which are generated through **node-level classification**. However, classification performance does not reliably indicate homophily estimation accuracy, and node-level classification can introduce bias.

Homophily estimation may also be formulated directly as a dyadic prediction problem. For both node-level and dyad-level prediction, **ego-alter modeling** outperforms standard classification or dyadic prediction strategies. These results highlight the importance of modeling relationships between an ego and its alters rather than relying solely on independent node or dyad predictions.

The community further connects estimation quality to **dyad-level residuals**, **error autocorrelation**, and **relational measures**. Homophily estimates are unbiased when dyad-level residuals sum to zero, while error autocorrelation along dyads causes bias. The estimation results generalize to other relational measures aggregated over network dyads.

4fbc0a930e1200b0b8dd097c19dccd302e0ee9b7.text:
## Private Blockchains and Spreadsheet Data Management

This community connects benchmarking of private blockchains with database-backed spreadsheet systems.

**BlockBench** provides a framework for analyzing and comparing private blockchains, evaluating **Parity**, **Ethereum**, and **Hyperledger Fabric**. It benchmarks workloads based on real and synthetic **smart contracts** and measures **throughput**, **latency**, and **fault tolerance**. Ethereum provides a Turing-complete smart contract machine, while smart contracts support applications and workloads implemented on private blockchains. These blockchain platforms are positioned as alternatives to traditional **database systems** for distributed data processing.

The spreadsheet-focused systems include **DataSpread**, which uses spreadsheets as a front-end interface and databases as a back-end datastore. It implements **presentational data management**, supported by the **PDM storage engine**. Database systems represent spreadsheet data, linking database technology with spreadsheet software.

Research on **spreadsheet data representation** addresses **optimal representation selection**, an NP-hard problem. Representations support positional access and modification, and are evaluated using a **typical spreadsheet workload**. The approach achieves up to 20% storage reduction and reduces formula evaluation time by up to 50%.

ff37c638e0f10662ff0a23ac132a64fd9dc72a59.text:
### Spatiotemporal Hotspot Detection Through Computational Stigmergy

This community focuses on detecting and interpreting spatiotemporal patterns in collective social activity, mobility behavior, and transaction data. The credit card transaction dataset provides transaction data for analyzing spatiotemporal patterns and supports the study of individual mobility behavior.

Computational stigmergy is applied to the dataset to enable hotspot detection, identifying high-density areas. It associates each sample position with a digital pheromone deposit, which is aggregated according to spatiotemporal proximity. A hotspot represents a high-density spatiotemporal pattern and may be permanent, occurring throughout the observation period, or intermittent, occurring only at certain times and days.

Intermittent hotspots are associated with community-level occurrence, for which nightlife is an example. The community also connects collective social activity with spatiotemporal patterns: related posts from nearby locations and times generate distinctive patterns. Overall, the entities describe a framework linking transaction-based mobility analysis, pheromone-inspired computation, spatiotemporal proximity, and the identification of persistent or time-specific social activity hotspots.

698f224c1cf07ee0a82e40765a2c9ab3f622fdb8.text:
### NEW for Tie Strength and Weight Prediction

This community centers on **neighborhood estimating weight new (NEW)**, a computational framework for **tie strength prediction**, also referred to as **weight prediction**. NEW uses **connection inclination** to generate representative network features and capture the distribution of tie strength for prediction.

The method is driven solely by basic **network structure information**. It incorporates a **parameterized regression model** to optimize prediction results. The model has approximately linear time complexity and can therefore be extended to **large-scale networks**.

NEW was experimentally evaluated on **six real-world networks**, providing the dataset context for assessing its prediction performance. Overall, the entities describe a structure-based approach that connects connection inclination, regression modeling, and scalable network analysis for predicting tie or edge weights.

7cc03ef1e858233acc7203240e50ff4c7801028d.text:
## Sampling Methods for Betweenness Centrality Approximation

This community focuses on **betweenness centrality (BC) approximation**, a task addressed through sampling-based methods.

The **Bader algorithm** performs a sampling-based approximation of BC. The **non-adaptive BC approximation** method uses **shortest path sampling**, while the **adaptive BC approximation** method uses **vertex sampling** and extends the non-adaptive sampling approach. Thus, adaptive approximation represents an adaptive alternative to the non-adaptive method.

The **Riondato method** proposes a method for non-adaptive BC approximation. Together, these methods connect BC approximation with two sampling concepts—shortest paths and vertices—and distinguish adaptive from non-adaptive sampling strategies.

010d0d730fc712849ed3e4100976915a0366e1a2.text:
## Relational Methods for Social-Network Spam Classification

The community focuses on **social network spam classification**, especially methods that exploit relationships among users and messages. **EGGS** is described as a general-purpose method that uses relational structure to group related spam messages for classification. It combines with **stacked graphical learning** and **probabilistic graphical models**.

Several approaches model related spam labels through probabilistic or sequential inference. Probabilistic graphical models use probabilistic inference to represent related spam labels, while stacked graphical learning uses sequential classifier predictions for the same purpose. Probabilistic graphical models can be implemented using **probabilistic soft logic** and **Markov logic networks**.

EGGS outperforms an **independent model** when relational message information is used, highlighting the value of modeling dependencies rather than treating messages independently.

142fce6840d8aadd9598b23fbc75909e5ca5d9a9.text:
### Bibliometric Metrics, Publishing Effects, and Resource Allocation

This community examines the role and limitations of bibliometric indicators in academic publishing and the broader scientific ecosystem. The Journal Impact Factor is a widely discussed indicator that has transformed the publishing industry, shaped hiring practices and resource allocation, and reoriented research and dissemination practices. Its validity is challenged by skewed citation distributions, an insufficient citation window, and increasing publication volumes. Publication count likewise becomes less useful as output rises and author lists grow.

The literature analyzes publishing and citation patterns using over 120 million papers across more than 2,600 research fields, including citation-based metrics for comparing researchers within and across fields. Alternative journal indicators are presented as other forms of bibliometric measurement, alongside calls for responsible application.

Publishing success metrics can become targets, illustrating Goodhart’s Law. Resource allocation is formulated as a convex-programming problem subject to a budget constraint and designed to achieve specified control performance. This framework supports performance measures represented by posynomials with nonnegative exponents.

cfa4d7419b3473fc50e194603333157ce765c4f1.text:
## Network Spreading, Reliability, and Inference

This community centers on network science for epidemics, influence, reliability, and recommendation. Epidemic thresholds characterize spreading-process stability in contact, time-varying, multilayer, and SIS networks. They can be estimated through aggregated static networks or non-backtracking eigenvalues, and derived via theoretical analysis and nonlinear Perron–Frobenius problems. Thresholds depend on network structure, degree correlation, temporal volatility, and contact adaptation; multiplex epidemics may occur even when individual layers remain below threshold. These ideas support pathogen diffusion, epidemic detection, causative-network identification, outbreak-size analysis, and targeted or community-based immunization. X-degree, X-non-backtracking centrality, global centrality, and local random walks provide immunization strategies.

A second theme is reliability maximization in uncertain graphs, where edge-existence probabilities define reachability and network reliability. Budgeted and multiple-source/multiple-target variants address sensor networks and social influence, while approximation hardness and scalable algorithms characterize computational limits and solutions. Uncertain-graph semantics also support social-graph anonymization.

For representation and inference, NetSMF uses sparse matrix factorization and spectral sparsification to efficiently embed large academic collaboration networks with bounded spectral error. Network-based inference connects iterative recommendation with global ranking and personal recommendation. Affinity methods construct similarity networks from messaging and senator Twitter histories, including privacy-preserving similarity. Epidemic and recommendation studies also use influenza, social-media, and other observational data under incomplete or limited ground truth.

33a3d80af00c6b1e155985a171ccafdef93abc15.text:
## Scientific Concept Extraction and Categorization

This community focuses on extracting and categorizing scientific concepts from research text, particularly scientific article titles and multi-domain corpora.

The **two phase algorithm** performs scientific concept extraction. Its first phase uses **phrasetype**, which learns from multi-domain corpora, segments text snippets into **aspect typed phrases**, and identifies these phrases across academic domains. Its second phase uses **adaptor grammars**, which extract concepts from aspect typed phrases and identify **fine grained concept mentions**.

Scientific concept extraction extracts scientific concepts from **scientific article titles** and supports construction of an **academic knowledgebase**. Separately, **concept categorization** categorizes concepts in scientific article titles. The community therefore links phrase segmentation, domain-aware processing, grammar-based extraction, fine-grained mention identification, and concept categorization in support of academic knowledge representation.

33b4407513e64c866587c421b55ab1eb30cc888c.text:
## Community Report: Intent-Aware Search, Recommendation, and Ranking

This community centers on personalized retrieval and recommendation driven by user intent, interaction, and feedback. In conversational systems, intent is inferred through follow-up questions, on-the-fly query decomposition, variable-length interpretations, and open-intent discovery. A two-stage approach first detects intent presence and then tags intents, supporting robustness to computer transcription errors.

Ranking research includes dynamic and two-level ranking: first-level results capture interactions and infer intent, while second-level ranking returns results relevant to that intent. Mobile search emphasizes on-the-go tasks, information cards, and alternatives to “ten blue links.” Conversational product search uses negative and fine-grained feedback, including aspect-value likelihood modeling; DEERS incorporates both positive and negative feedback for e-commerce recommendation.

Recommendation applications include automatic playlist continuation using user-playlist-song and song-song similarity models, unified modeling, memory metric-based attention, and adversarial personalized ranking. Job recommendation uses embedding-based methods and joint tripartite representations across job, skill, and job-job graphs.

Learning-to-rank methods include ListNet, Stochastic ListNet, ListMLE, list-wise loss, and sampling strategies addressing relevance-label ambiguity. Pretrained sequence-to-sequence models derive relevance probabilities and support zero-shot transfer, particularly in data-poor MS MARCO passage ranking. Graph methods include LOSP, graph symmetrization, and undirected graph embeddings.

1108b29021651bd35f7f6599cb97c2ab651ba79f.text:
## Evaluating Scientific Excellence and Referee Competence in Italy

This community examines how scientific excellence and referee competence are measured to support research policies and competitive research funding. A bibliometric methodology analyzes scientific research categories, beginning with assessments of individual researchers’ excellence and scientific performance. It is also used to identify centers of excellence from the excellence of affiliated researchers within Italian public research organizations.

The study focuses on the hard sciences, covering 109 scientific research categories, and compares the scientific performance of referees listed in expert registers. These registers support referee selection for research proposal evaluation, where referee competence is essential to producing trustworthy judgments. Their register coverage is evaluated against the evaluation competency spectrum required for proposal assessment.

The broader system connects competitive research funding with public research programs. Research proposal evaluation operates within these competitive schemes, while excellence measurement and evaluation remains challenging because scientific excellence is multidimensional. In this setting, bibliometric evidence and expert-register analysis provide complementary approaches: the former measures performance and identifies excellence, while the latter supports the selection and assessment of competent evaluators in Italy.

0be8db29a63064061d62b1bb4071373936580d5a.text:
### Editorial Networks and Research Perspectives in LIS/MIS

This community examines information science and library science journals, spanning two major research-oriented subfields: library and information science (LIS) and management information systems (MIS). Links between the LIS and MIS journal subsets are weak, while professional journals form relatively isolated groups and are characterized more by subject matter than by a focus on information flows.

The central system is an editorial board network, generated from the editorial activities of board members. Interlocking editorship—scholars serving on multiple editorial boards—links journals into an interlocking editorship network and serves as a proxy for similarity in editorial policies. This network contains multiple compact components, whose fragmented configuration may reflect the field’s lack of consensus about research aims, methods, and instruments.

The components are interpreted as representing different theoretical perspectives on economic research. These perspectives concern appropriate methods for investigating problems and constructing theories in economics.

993027ec8fedd0a53be21231b650146aac6c49a1.text:
## Community Report: Sybil Resilience, Dynamic Graph Privacy, and Transaction Networks

This community centers on securing and analyzing evolving social, trust, and transaction graphs. Sybil identities and Byzantine actors threaten e-communities, consensus protocols, democratic governance, and social-choice systems. **SybilFence** strengthens social-graph-based Sybil defenses by discounting edges associated with negative feedback and resisting continuous connection-solicitation attacks. Sybil-resilient conductance-based community expansion uses trust-graph conductance to support safe community growth while limiting Sybil penetration; Byzantine agreement and resilient parameter updates rely on a Byzantine fraction below one third.

A second theme is graph privacy and adversarial re-identification. Graph anonymisation and privacy-preserving publication address re-identification in static and dynamic social graphs. Active, robust active, static, and periodic active re-identification attacks exploit structural and temporal patterns; robust attacks are formulated through optimisation and withstand graph perturbations. Time-aware gradient attacks use deep dynamic network embeddings, network snapshots, and link rewiring to hide target links, with traversal and greedy implementations.

The community also covers transaction analytics. **Trans2vec** embeds transaction networks using address features and transaction amounts, supporting one-class SVM classification; Ethereum records reconstruct transaction networks, which can form multilayer networks with joint patent and other transaction data. Merchant incentive optimisation models merchant responses, incentive sensitivity, budgets, and commercial objectives. Community genealogy graphs characterize parent connections, parent counts, and maximum parent weights, while sentiment detection and phishing-address detection represent additional graph-based tasks.

1d613ff05347d85b7ea55b27972fd98cdeb0be00.text:
## Community Report: Trust, Explainability, and Data-Driven Systems

This community connects trust-aware recommendation, explainable AI, rumor analysis, open-access publishing, and scalable data processing.

Trust networks model explicit trust scores, implicit relationships, reciprocation, and rating profiles. In recommender systems, the multi-faceted trust model incorporates social links and public anonymous feedback; LOCABAL+ extends LOCABAL and is evaluated on item-review datasets. Trust-aware and hybrid trust-aware neighbourhoods use trust information to improve recommendations, with the latter doubling rating coverage and supporting budget-constrained cloud deployment. EverQuest2 provides chat and trade networks for studying reciprocation, which decreases as barrier level rises.

Explainable question answering promotes transparency by exposing computational models, information context, and interpretation, with XQA evaluation assessing such systems. It is also proposed to reduce information pollution. Datasheets for datasets similarly support transparency, accountability, consent documentation, and dataset documentation for commercial APIs, pretrained models, and example datasets.

Rumor dissemination is modeled through agents’ desires, rumor features, society homogeneity, and trust networks. Homogeneity is necessary for rumor convergence, for which a convergence theorem provides a theoretical result.

Other work addresses mobile multimedia overload in smart communities through context-aware, proactive, and sensor-based recommendation. ASERV enables real-time scientific analysis of large, newly arriving data in cloud environments, while web-based business intelligence and in-memory processing support SMEs. An analysis framework examines open-access journals, article processing charges, activity metrics, and predatory publishing.

d18323a68f440671d9d48372285637d0f919bd63.text:
## Graph Signal Processing, Networks, and Social Inference

This community centers on **graph signal processing**, which models graph-indexed observations as outputs of network processes. Core methods include graph shift operators, normalized Laplacians, spectral representations, convolution, z-transforms, graph-filter design, and discrete signal processing on graphs. The **z-Laplacian** provides a unifying framework for graph shift operators, continuous-time dynamical processes, nonnegative filters, wireless networks, and structural brain networks.

Graph filters—including FIR and ARMA filters—support distributed filtering, signal percolation, filtered-white-noise modeling, and processing of time-varying signals. Successive local aggregations enable single-node sampling, Vandermonde-structured recovery, and signal interpolation. Related tasks include topology inference, localized spectral analysis, sparse-frequency representation, graph signal sampling, and network-agnostic regression.

Applications span weather-station compression, blog classification, customer-behavior and traffic forecasting, performance-rating prediction, and structural brain-network analysis. Consensus-based prediction and diffusion models connect ratings to peer interactions and graph topology.

A second theme concerns **social and temporal signals**: sharing duration, copying intervals, propagation speed, retention, production, and originality characterize information diffusion on Pinterest and real social networks. Temporal and lexical evidence supports social-media stream search and end-to-end ranking.

Finally, editorial-board networks study interlocking editorship, policy similarity, and LIS/MIS journal structure, while paper-to-reviewer matching uses suitability scores, learning, integer programming, and matching frameworks for reviewer assignment.

03cd414eb11120714afb154fddc0049c716f0088.text:
## Urban Lifestyle and Citywide Shopping Analysis

This community studies urban lifestyle analysis through multiple behavioral views, including mobility patterns, work–rest patterns, and shopping patterns. Mobility data encode where people go, while shopping records provide sparse observations for citywide shopping pattern prediction. Social media data support large-scale, low-cost lifestyle analysis as an alternative to traditional surveys.

Matrix factor analysis provides an unsupervised method for extracting salient mobility, lifestyle, and work–rest patterns. Mobility and shopping patterns are complementary views of urban lifestyle and help infer what people buy. Collective matrix factorization (CMF) fuses multiple lifestyle data sources and is extended with interaction regularization, incorporating regional relational structure from spatial interactions.

Spatial interactions between urban regions are affected by distance decay and can be modeled using a gravity model. These methods support prediction of shopping patterns and analysis of divergent regional demands across urban regions.

The study compares the Greater New York City area, representing big cities, with the Greater Rochester area, representing small cities. This comparison quantitatively examines behavioral differences and reveals functional characteristics of urban lifestyles.

81c43e5b427b867090c11b4c79e943f9cba2906e.text:
## Bursty Twitter Botnets and Detection

This community focuses on discovering, retrieving, and analyzing Twitter botnets, with implications for spam and public opinion manipulation. Twitter bots can send spam tweets, manipulate public opinion, and are targets of bot detection systems designed to detect and remove them.

The **Star Wars botnet** provides ground truth for Twitter bot research. It consists of more than 350,000 bots that tweet random quotations from *Star Wars* novels. Its analysis revealed bursty bot creation: bots are created in batches, tweet only during their first few minutes, and post uniformly from locations within two rectangular geographic zones. The botnet was discovered, retrieved, and studied to understand its design and behavior.

The related **bursty botnet** system is characterized by burst-based creation and short-lived activity. It was discovered through unusual tweeting behavior and was directly responsible for a large-scale online spamming attack in 2012.

**Bot detection algorithms** commonly assume bots share common features, but can also identify them through distinctive or unusual tweeting behavior. Together, these entities connect botnet discovery and analysis with Twitter bot detection, spam attacks, and the potential manipulation of public opinion.

7a7860d1ef707f539a4331f32fe22d2b3d305b10.text:
## Social Bots, Political Leaning, and Influence
