This community examines how social bots interact with humans and disseminate misleading or fake information. Bots may amplify fake information, while credulous users—who have a high percentage of bots among their followings—may unknowingly spread misleading information by retweeting them.

Key methods include classifying bots by political leaning, analyzing their strategies, measuring social network embeddedness, and evaluating bot influence effectiveness on humans. Bot detection features support differentiation between bots and humans.

The analysis distinguishes conservative and liberal bots. Conservative bots generally align their discussion topics with human counterparts, are more deeply embedded in the network, and are more effective at influencing humans. Liberal bots show less topic overlap with humans and adopt a more inflammatory attitude. Thus, conservative bot strategies emphasize topic alignment, whereas liberal strategies involve lower overlap and greater inflammatory behavior.

f544a63777080ef672232efd0430c51c5a73cae0.text:
## Semantic Integration and Join Estimation

This community connects semantic integration for clinical data with efficient query processing. EHR systems can be mapped to RDF data, which preserves source semantics before conversion to harmonized domain semantics. RDF is represented both as a directed labelled graph and a 3-way Boolean tensor, creating demands for triple indexing and join-size estimation.

Semantic data virtualization builds layers over heterogeneous EHR systems and supports clinical research through on-demand semantic data generation. N3 rules explicitly represent ontology and semantic conversions, while EYE executes these rules and can generate proofs for conversions. Local ontologies are mapped to reusable domain ontologies; clinical terminologies further support harmonization and help bridge the semantic gap in clinical information systems. i2b2 and OMOP are clinical research databases supporting research settings.

The computational focus is join size estimation, including relational joins, similarity self-joins, d-ary inputs, and streaming settings. Estimates support query handling and query-plan generation, including database query optimizers and potentially more efficient SPARQL query processors. Clinical research is also associated with higher citation variance and a lower likelihood of producing highly cited “hit” works.

5501fca108d4434759dd8d80ec50f40a5607f4e8.text:
## Semantic Virtualization and Querying of Clinical RDF Data

This community focuses on bridging the semantic gap in clinical information systems and heterogeneous EHR systems. Semantic data virtualization builds layers over EHR systems and supports clinical research through on-demand semantic data generation.

EHR data can be mapped to RDF, initially preserving source semantics and then converted into harmonized domain semantics. Domain ontologies support this harmonization and reuse, while local ontologies are mapped to domain ontologies through N3 rules that explicitly state ontology mappings. Clinical terminologies also contribute to harmonized semantics. The EYE system executes N3 rules and can generate proofs of conversions used in clinical research data processing.

Clinical research settings include the i2b2 and OMOP clinical research databases. RDF data may be represented as a directed labelled graph or interpreted as a 3-way Boolean tensor. The tensor representation supports join size estimation, which is valuable for query handling and may enable more efficient SPARQL query processor implementations.

51a2e5aa6d3d011ce236645cacc85f2eecf699c8.text:
## Innovation, Knowledge Translation, and Scholarly Networks

This community centers on innovation processes and knowledge translation in biomedical and technological development. Medical innovation is analyzed through demand, supply, and technological-capability perspectives, represented by medical-subject-heading categories and illustrated by human papillomavirus, RNA interference, and magnetic-resonance-imaging cases. Knowledge translation connects molecular entities, nanomaterials, drug discovery, biomedical innovation, and preclinical, translational, and clinical development. Doxil/liposomal doxorubicin exemplifies an approved nanodrug, while dental materials research distinguishes titanium implants, ceramics, composites, and mineral trioxide aggregates as competing or disruptive technologies.

Scientometric overlay and base mapping, literature-network analysis, topic-evolution analysis, and computer-assisted content analysis study innovation, technological emergence, strategic intelligence, and emerging research fronts. Patent data, patent families, co-inventor networks, and first-citation measures extend this analysis; Ebola proteins glycoprotein, VP40, and VP35 form therapeutic patent targets.

A second theme concerns scholarly and online communication. CASCON supports knowledge mobilization and R&D-topic evolution; conference categorization and stability distinguish top-tier and non-top-tier venues. IRC, Ubuntu, VXM, and adaptive-contact-network studies examine participation, embeddedness, influence, knowledge dissemination, and online mobilization using social-network metrics and inter-event patterns. Finally, two-layer representations link social and publication layers in INSPIRE-HEP and physics-journal data.

4efb80129ddb7bfb84967f74453228d23d78113b.text:
## Spotify Charts and Sequential Skip Prediction

This community centers on Spotify music data, especially the **Spotify Top 200**, which Spotify publishes as a daily chart ranking its 200 most-streamed songs. The dataset contains **daily streaming counts** for ranked songs. Exploratory data analysis examines song **popularity**, **rarity**, and **longevity** on the chart.

A **stochastic process model** represents daily streaming counts using **stochastic intensity point processes** and **marked point processes**. Estimated model parameters feed a **clustering algorithm** that groups songs with similar features and performance. **Acoustic features** are associated with tracks and support analysis of song characteristics.

A second focus is the **Spotify Sequential Skip Prediction Challenge**, organized by Spotify. It addresses **skip prediction**: whether tracks in listening sessions are skipped. The **aferraro** system, submitted by the **Music Technology Group**, combines predictions from multiple **boosting tree** models trained on features extracted from sessions and tracks. It achieves an **MAA score of 0.554**.

c5201fd34764005a9426e93afd36c6ab44fdcdb7.text:
## Sockpuppetry Detection and Graph-Based Social Analysis

This community examines sockpuppetry in online discussion communities, studying it across nine communities and aiming to automatically detect deceptive behavior. Sockpuppets differ from ordinary users in posting behavior, linguistic traits, and social network structure: they tend to start fewer discussions, write shorter posts, use more personal pronouns such as “I,” and exhibit more clustered ego-networks and social networks. Their deceptiveness and supportiveness may vary, including whether they impersonate another user or support arguments from sockpuppets controlled by the same person. Sockpuppetry also motivates a broader deceptive behavior taxonomy.

A related line of work addresses social circle prediction. An ego network organizes an individual’s alters into social circles, and prediction benefits from both global and local features. Global feature learning encodes global network structure, while local feature learning captures neighborhood structure and features hidden from global representations.

The community also develops generalized degree, a parametric family of centrality measures that generalizes and improves on degree, accounts for global network structure, has a graph interpretation, and can be computed iteratively. It supports key node identification and has a sufficient condition for rank monotonicity.

2e6bfda6f963c33e76a4d473ac6f5b68cf62a42d.text:
## Image Retrieval and Human-Assisted Graph Reasoning

This community connects content-based image retrieval with crowdsourced graph search and relation inference. Image retrieval systems use color descriptors, dominant color descriptors, texture features, and image semantics to address the semantic gap, including searches over hyperspectral and real-world image databases. Dominant colors are quantized and compared using Earth Mover’s Distance, optimal color composition distance, or the linear-time approximate EMD, which uses a space-filling curve in multidimensional color space.

Texture retrieval and classification use scattering transforms, filterbanks, and subband histograms, with Bhattacharyya kernels for similarity. Scattering representations are stable to spatial deformations; Weibull distributions model descendant-layer subbands, while generalized Gaussian distributions are unsuitable for most subbands. Multiple-query retrieval uses Pareto depth, combining Pareto fronts and manifold ranking; its performance is linked to Pareto-front concavity.

Interactive retrieval includes Seeker and multinomial or Bayesian relevance feedback, modeled with Dirichlet and beta distributions. A second theme concerns human-assisted graph search, using reachability queries and human-computation optimization for hierarchy curation, workflow debugging, segmentation, categorization, and filter synthesis. Crowdsourced join queries combine machine-generated candidate pairs with parallel human labeling. Transitive relations enable inferred matches, while optimal or heuristic labeling orders reduce labeling cost on platforms such as Mechanical Turk.

bfd56724fc3f4963ebf66d1c1634a669a524003a.text:
## Fusion Research and Blockchain Incentive Systems

This community links two themes: international nuclear fusion research and blockchain incentive design.

In fusion research, a dynamic topic model identifies material, plasma, device, diagnostics, and simulation clusters. A normalized revealed comparative advantage metric uses these clusters to measure national research capability and topic-specific comparative advantage. A gravity model analyzes international collaboration in nuclear fusion and finds that countries collaborate less on plasma, device, and diagnostics research when their comparative advantages differ. Nuclear fusion is framed as “big science,” requiring substantial national investment; tokamaks are major facilities and research systems within this field.

The second theme concerns token engineering and Insolar. Token engineering combines systems modeling with cryptocurrency expertise, while simulation and systems modeling evaluate incentive mechanisms. Token economics studies the design and operationalization of these mechanisms. Insolar applies token economics and token engineering to its blockchain incentives and develops the Insolar MainNet public network. Incentive mechanisms and subsidy pools encourage participation, adoption, and application-developer support for MainNet.

Simulation also detects a simulation topic cluster and extends opacity findings to a probabilistic SI model, connecting methodological analysis across the community.

d9522d9315c7ebcdd32148a4f4087762f01b7a5e.text:
## Framework for Analyzing Open Access Journals

The community centers on an **analysis framework** for **open access publishing** and **systematic journal analysis**. The framework supports systematic analysis through **18 core attributes**, including **activity metrics** and examination of **predatory publishing** issues.

A key analytical dimension is **article processing charges**: journals are compared based on whether they charge publication fees. These charges also relate to **open access adoption**, since high or poorly justified fees may discourage authors from choosing open access.

**Transparency** is an associated concern. High article processing charges are reported as insufficiently justified and lacking transparency. Predatory publishing is likewise identified as an issue affecting open access publishing and is incorporated into the framework’s analysis areas.

92725203904416c8e526628b59bd72198b521a2b.text:
## Governance and Success in Online Communities

This community examines **community success** in self-governing online communities, using a systematic study of **5,000 sovereign, resource-constrained online communities**. Success is measured through **member growth, member retention, community survival,** and **activity volume**; correlation analysis assesses relationships among these measures.

The **success prediction** task uses early information about **community properties** and **community behaviors** to predict outcomes. A central finding is that greater **governance complexity** predicts increased success. Complexity is indicated by more numerous and broader **governance rules**, and its positive effect increases with **population size**. Successful large communities rely more on rules that concentrate power in **administrators**.

The community also frames governance as a response to **resource management problems**. Larger populations exacerbate interdependent problems, which can drive the emergence of **integrated governance systems** that organize collective responses. Finally, **selection pressures** favor better-managed and better-populated servers, linking governance and population to long-term community success.

f114d7fd9e475dbf9da146c87f06d26668641911.text:
## Nonlinear Optimization and Modularity Methods

This community centers on a proposed **nonlinear optimization** approach. The method is inspired by **nonlinear modularity eigenvector** methods and uses a fast **first-order method** for optimization.

The first-order method incorporates a tailored **active-set strategy**, linking efficient optimization with active-set techniques. The proposed approach is evaluated numerically against standard **matrix-based approaches** and the **Generalized Ratio DCA** approach.

Overall, the community connects nonlinear optimization, modularity eigenvector methods, first-order algorithms, and active-set strategies, while emphasizing numerical comparison with matrix-based and Generalized Ratio DCA methods.

902dca7cc546740f30c30a5a02bbb77da6ed239a.text:
## Algorithmic Frameworks for Exact 4- and 5-Vertex Pattern Counting

This community focuses on efficient, exact counting of 4- and 5-vertex subgraph patterns. An algorithmic counting framework targets all 5-vertex patterns and uses pattern decomposition: larger patterns are derived from counts of smaller subgraphs. The framework therefore supports exact subgraph counts across the 5-vertex patterns.

Degree orientation is another key method, used to accelerate 5-vertex pattern counting and reduce subgraph-counting runtime. The 4-vertex counting method serves as a stepping stone toward counting 5-vertex patterns and is reported to be faster than prior methods. Together, these methods connect foundational 4-vertex counting with broader 5-vertex enumeration, emphasizing both exactness and improved counting runtime.

038b3d823f23b26da3d0e1d5336e6d97af5dde1c.text:
## SourceCR: Joint Credibility and Source Detection

This community centers on **SourceCR**, a system for jointly performing the **source detection** task and assessing credibility. SourceCR includes two iterative modules: **credibility reliability training** and **division querying**.

Credibility reliability training uses **expectation maximization** for simultaneous estimation of **claim credibility** and **user reliability**. Division querying then uses claim credibility to divide the network into subnetworks and performs source detection through **budgeted user querying**. Together, these modules support iterative interaction between credibility estimation, network division, and source identification.

SourceCR improves both **credibility accuracy** and **source detection rate** compared with separate methods.

366dcd3a0433dfd3f4b44a569fd2b3defaf0afe2.text:
## Image Retrieval and Human-Assisted Search

This community centers on content-based image retrieval, texture analysis, and crowdsourced graph and join labeling.

Content-based image retrieval uses color descriptors, dominant color descriptors, and linear-time approximate earth mover’s distance for efficient search in large and hyperspectral image databases. Dominant colors are obtained through color quantization; earth mover’s distance and optimal color composition distance measure image dissimilarity, with space-filling curves organizing multidimensional color spaces. Multiple-query image retrieval addresses queries with different image semantics. Pareto depth combines Pareto fronts and efficient manifold ranking, improves retrieval on real-world image databases, and is linked to Pareto-front concavity. Image retrieval systems also use interactive search and multinomial or Bayesian relevance feedback, modeled with Dirichlet and beta distributions, to help bridge the semantic gap.

Texture retrieval and classification use scattering transforms, filterbanks, and subband histograms, compared with a Bhattacharyya kernel. Scattering representations are stable to spatial deformations; Weibull distributions model descendant-layer subbands, while generalized Gaussian distributions are unsuitable for most subbands.

Human-assisted graph search uses reachability questions and human-computation optimization for interactive search, hierarchy curation, workflow debugging, segmentation, categorization, and filter synthesis. Crowdsourced joins combine machine-generated candidate pairs with human labeling, exploiting transitive relations, optimized labeling orders, parallel algorithms, and platforms such as Mechanical Turk to reduce labeling cost.

ef33863c67b96b7f12a982d978b32d605884b902.text:
### Graph-Based User Group Discovery in a Push Service Platform

The **push service platform**, operating in the **Huawei application store**, performs automatic **user group discovery** for targeted delivery. The discovery task uses **web-scale user operation logs** together with a small set of **labeled apps**.

Its graph-based algorithm is **A-PARW**, an approximate version of the **partially absorbing random walk** method. A-PARW is used in the platform’s application layer to support user group discovery. The platform also includes a **distributed storage layer**, providing an infrastructure component alongside the application-layer discovery method.

f28925599254c3cd7c43f32f9e6f947bdcb5235c.text:
## Curing Epidemics Under Information Constraints

This community studies curing epidemics in an SI process, where infection spreads over a known graph and infected nodes are cured under a limited curing budget.

Under perfect information, the required curing budget is determined precisely by the graph’s cutwidth. With this knowledge, some infections can be cured in sublinear time. The budget must also grow at least logarithmically with the number of nodes, while cutwidth may increase only sublinearly with network size.

Observation uncertainty represents degradation from perfect knowledge of infection states. The necessary curing budget is characterized as a function of per-node observation uncertainty. Even minor uncertainty can fundamentally worsen performance, making curing require exponential time, contrasting with the sublinear-time possibility under perfect information.

Larger curing budgets reduce the expected extinction time to order \(n/r\), and under the stated budget conditions, expected extinction time is sublinear in the number of nodes. Overall, the community connects epidemic-control performance to graph structure, network size, curing resources, and the accuracy of infection-state observations.

7c31f5270aea4d4ab2ab5c258fb030cb8b56a79c.text:
### Multi-Feature Rumor Blocking on Multi-Layer Networks

This community centers on **multi-feature rumor blocking**, formulated over a **multi-layer network**. Its foundation is the **multi-feature diffusion model**, which represents influence spread across multiple feature layers and provides the basis for the rumor-blocking formulation.

Two key methods address this task. **Multi-Sampling** is designed to solve multi-feature rumor blocking and is applicable to multi-layer network structures. **Revised-IMM** returns an approximate solution to the same problem. Revised-IMM is inspired by **martingale analysis**, linking the algorithm to this analytical method.

Overall, the entities describe a framework in which multi-feature diffusion is modeled across layered networks, then addressed through specialized sampling and approximate-solution methods.

92718d4ee7f371d4b70fbe1be6226cc4329c9350.text:
## Entity Clustering for Two-Fold Entity Retrieval

This community focuses on entity clustering and its role in improving entity retrieval. **Entity clustering** is used during offline preprocessing, where **x means** clusters entities. These precomputed clusters support an **optimized retrieval model**, which uses the clustering results to improve retrieval.

The same clustering process serves as the offline preprocessing step for **two fold entity retrieval**. This retrieval method incorporates the optimized retrieval model as its second step, linking clustering-based preprocessing with subsequent retrieval optimization. Two fold entity retrieval is experimentally evaluated on the **BTC12 dataset**.

Overall, the methods form a pipeline: x means performs clustering, entity clustering supplies precomputed groupings, the optimized retrieval model uses those groupings, and two fold entity retrieval combines the clustering stage with the optimized retrieval stage and evaluates the resulting approach on BTC12.

5d635483671a6bb6fe86d2188bda448374d1c654.text:
### Archive Search and Temporal Information Needs

This community focuses on archive search and the investigation of user search behavior. Search tasks are designed for archive-search settings, vary in complexity, and are assessed through pre- and post-task evaluation mechanisms. A pilot study informed the creation and refinement of these tasks and used a temporal search engine.

The document collections searched in archive search are longitudinal corpora. User search behavior is strongly influenced by temporal information needs, while analysis of search strategy provides insight into how users search. Findings about user behavior can guide improved interface design and system design.

Overall, the community connects task design and evaluation with the study of search behavior in archives. It links temporal information needs, search strategies, and task complexity to the design of temporal search systems and interfaces.

1488eae851337452addf0b44751eec9b28f93630.text:
## Approximate Analytics, Sensor Networks, and Query Optimization

This community connects sensor-data management, approximate analytics, causal event prediction, and scalable query optimization.

**Plato** and **PlatODB** compress time series and support approximate query answering or analytics over multiple sensor datasets. Plato provides deterministic, potentially amplitude-independent error guarantees, while PlatODB builds hierarchical summaries for efficient queries. Fixed- and variable-length segmentation, wavelet histograms, and linear-algebra operators support compact summaries and cross-correlation analysis. Deterministic guarantees complement probabilistic error bounds and are derived from hierarchical data structures and function families.

For sensor networks and environmental monitoring, multi-resolution cube hierarchies summarize data through distributed construction and in-network processing. They improve spatial aggregate queries by optimizing query plans and minimizing data requests. Heterogeneous sensors provide environmental properties, while semantic integration middleware combines sensor data with indigenous knowledge for drought forecasting and supports ad hoc business queries over integrated business and manufacturing-simulation data.

Multi-query optimization reduces cost by sharing common subexpressions and work. Cache-based methods add in-memory caching under memory constraints and target data-intensive frameworks. Polynomial-time planning, linear cost transformations, and reduced search address scalability; reduced search cuts runtime relative to exhaustive exploration.

Finally, event precedence models use absorbing Markov chains over event streams for top-k predictive and causal queries. Exhaustive and reduced searches identify likely effects, while runtime causal inference removes noncausal precedence relationships and learns causal relationships dynamically.

cd6322617c74c00caecb024359fa2fb49ab0b3f7.text:
### Validating Facebook Archives with Survey Data

This community focuses on comparing Facebook data archives with survey data, particularly for studying digitally expressed and self-reported music interest. Music interest is positioned as a key indicator in cultural sociology.

The central approach is **parallel data collection**, which collects personal Facebook data archives alongside survey responses and combines social media data collection with a **face-to-face survey**. **Cross-validation** operates in both directions: survey data are used to validate Facebook data, while Facebook data are used to validate survey data.

Both datasets are evaluated for **data validity**. Facebook data archives also address **social media data leanness** by providing fuller user data, and they capture digitally expressed music interest. In contrast, survey data capture respondents’ self-reported music interest. Together, these methods and datasets support validity assessment and comparison between social media-based and survey-based measures in cultural sociology.

a71c90cf8e2fe9b6c36989b2d999c05419370b96.text:
### Streaming Analytics, Causal Inference, and Sensor Data

This community centers on processing sensor and event-stream data for Industry 4.0 and spatial-temporal analytics. Sensor data represents environmental properties, follows smooth underlying phenomena, and is produced by manufacturing simulations; semantic representations and semantic data integration middleware support its integration. PlatoDB compresses and processes sensor data, while sensor networks support spatial aggregate queries.

Multi-query optimization minimizes cost by sharing work and computing common subexpressions once, although conventional query optimizers generally do not exploit them. Cache-based multi-query optimization extends this approach through caching. Exhaustive search explores the \(O(n^n)\) plan space, whereas reduced search lowers runtime by 25–80% with a small accuracy reduction. Related polynomial-time methods include query-plan optimization and data-request minimization; linear cost transformation converts cost minimization into linear maximization.

Multi-resolution cube hierarchies summarize sensor data, are constructed distributively, and can be maintained in-network. They improve spatial aggregate queries by minimizing data requests and enabling query plans over summaries.

For event streams, event precedence models use temporal precedence relationships and first-order absorbing Markov chains to identify likely effects. Reduced search accelerates this process. Runtime causal inference removes non-causal precedence links and learns causal relationships during query processing. Top-k predictive query processing predicts likely next events, evaluated on cascading-blackout and web-page-view datasets. Industry 4.0 adoption is enabled by stream-processing systems and technologies but faces implementation obstacles.

ab79a0a73c877cc1d4f55cad2a8d35839e4767f7.text:
## Science, Collaboration, Citations, and Complex Governance

This community links research impact, international collaboration, citation dynamics, and governance in complex communities. Scientific influence is measured using 161-country panel data, with globalization, population size, and international research collaboration included as control variables. Higher democracy is associated with greater scientific influence and higher-impact science; these findings may inform research policy and management and broader policy implications.

International research collaboration is represented as a global research collaboration network, commonly explained through socio-economic factors. African countries exhibit distinctive patterns involving external collaboration links, highlighting the need for collaboration analysis in policy and management.

Citation dynamics provide measures of scientific influence. Citation histories from American Physical Society journal articles are analyzed over time and compared with technology-disaggregated patent cohorts. A mechanistic citation model, derived from citation histories, characterizes a universal temporal pattern by collapsing citation histories into a common form.

A second focus concerns integrated governance systems. Interdependent resource management problems, exacerbated by larger populations, drive collective responses. Five thousand sovereign, resource-constrained online communities provide evidence for studying how such systems emerge. Governance complexity is indicated by more numerous and broader governance rules, while successful large communities rely more on rules concentrating power in administrators.

3cc110ade3b211d1696692ec862d242fd268e5c2.text:
### Causal Prediction and Distributed Query Optimization

This community covers predictive querying over event streams, causal inference, and efficient query processing over spatial and sensor data.

An event precedence model incrementally constructed from event streams represents temporal precedence relationships as edges and constructs a first-order absorbing Markov chain. It supports causal prediction queries, including top-k prediction of events likely to occur next in real time. Exhaustive search identifies likely effect events, while reduced search uses early termination and lowers runtime by 25–80% with a small accuracy reduction. Runtime causal inference dynamically learns causal relationships and removes precedence relationships that do not exhibit causality; temporal precedence is a necessary condition for causality. Cascading blackouts and web page views provide evaluation datasets.

Multi-query optimization addresses spatial aggregate queries by reusing common subexpressions and minimizing cost, with polynomial-time formulations; conventional query optimizers generally do not exploit such sharing. Its plan search may involve an O(n^n) space.

For sensor networks, multi-resolution cube hierarchies summarize sensor data, are constructed distributively, and maintained through in-network processing. Query-plan optimization over cube summaries improves spatial aggregate queries, while data-request minimization selects the fewest requests and has a polynomial-time algorithm. Cost functions can be transformed into linear maximization formulations.

350bf35d223c1f2a2840e799437acdfd522d603d.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Analysis of Sensitive Social Networks

This community focuses on privacy preserving social network analysis for distributed sensitive social networks. The networks include enmity, financial transaction, supply chain, and sexual relationship networks, each identified as an example of such distributed sensitive data.

Key methods include secure multiparty computation and data oblivious algorithms. Secure multiparty computation is used in privacy preserving social network analysis and provides the basis for secure computation protocols. Data oblivious algorithms can be translated into these secure computation protocols.

The analytical measures and techniques addressed are k shell decomposition and pagerank centrality. Both are computed over distributed sensitive social networks, and data oblivious algorithms compute both k shell decomposition and pagerank centrality. Overall, the relationships connect privacy-protecting computation systems with network-analytic methods for studying sensitive, distributed network structures.

ebc5d6779bef1101ed476644d3233e19c5aefbad.text:
### Structural Diversity in Clustered Networks

This community focuses on an evolutionary framework for mapping structural diversity among networks with controlled properties. Structural diversity manifests in higher-order network structure and affects the behavior of a complex contagion model.

The framework uses subgraph-based encoding as a core feature, providing greater confidence when assessing higher-order structural diversity. It also applies exact mutations based on systems of Diophantine equations. A diversity-driven mechanism changes the resolution of MapElite, supporting exploration of diverse network structures.

The framework is compared with state-of-the-art clustered network generation methods, which generate networks with a specified global clustering level. It uncovers diverse networks without computationally infeasible mixing times, linking network generation and evaluation to the mixing-times metric.

db73a7268359d1df5c1744f5cefbcc93f21f1a02.text:
## SQL Workload Management, Query Labeling, and Ontology Analysis

This community centers on machine-learning-driven SQL workload analysis, labeling, sampling, and management. SQL workload analysis is modeled as a set of query-labeling variations, with applications including security audits, workload analytics, and index recommendation. Learned SQL query embeddings replace application-specific syntactic feature engineering, support representative workload sampling, and enable user labeling for security audits. These representations can be integrated into a workload management and analytics service supporting multiple database backends.

Machine learning algorithms enable automatic query labeling, query generation, and topic discovery. Hierarchical k-means performs topic discovery and constructs a topic hierarchy, extending standard k-means clustering; generated queries can represent discovered topics. A database-agnostic workload-management system supports generalized SQL workload analysis and targets multi-tenant platforms.

A second theme concerns biomedical ontology query processing. MedTQ uses a predicate-neighborhood-pattern-based approach to analyze ontology predicates, computing similarity through a predicate similarity metric. It was evaluated with the DrugBank ontology, while the biomedical ontology entity supports analysis and query processing over biomedical ontologies. Overall, the community links learned representations and clustering with practical workload services, and connects predicate similarity methods with ontology-oriented systems.

7bde12e06f1577c2a8ec76e6b0a57369ecea7d5f.text:
## Multiplex Link Persistence and Hyperbolic Correlations

This community focuses on modeling and embedding multiplex networks across layers, particularly through link persistence and correlations in hyperbolic node coordinates.

**Link persistence**—the recurrence of links across layers—explains high **edge overlap** between multiplex layers. It occurs irrespective of **hyperbolic distances**, but accounting for it improves **trans-layer link prediction**. The **geometric multiplex model** is extended to represent link persistence across layers, and multiplex embedding methods should likewise incorporate it.

A complementary theme is **coordinate correlations**: correlations measured across **hyperbolic node coordinates** in different layers. These correlations facilitate both trans-layer link prediction and **mutual navigation** across layers. Consequently, multiplex embedding methods should account for coordinate correlations as well as link persistence.

Together, the concepts and methods connect geometric structure, cross-layer link recurrence, and navigation or prediction tasks in multiplex networks.

12da7a7f2ad95e5562d404759950b86ce79b4680.text:
## Collective Dynamics and Job-Related Social Media

This community covers collective interaction effects, social counters, and job-related social media discourse.

A **collective state model** describes revert behavior: a revert action establishes the point from which non-revert actions are counted, while each non-revert action increments the collective social counter. The probability of a revert declines as the square root of the number of non-revert actions since the previous revert. The model uses an effectively **unbounded resource** in its collective-state description. The social counter emerges from collective interaction effects and is attributed to those effects rather than to individual-user properties.

A second topic concerns individual users and commercial accounts producing job-related social media discourse. Researchers analyze linguistic differences and job-related tweet volume patterns, including monthly, daily, and hourly variation. Job-related tweet volume patterns also show distinct diurnal rhythms associated with job-related moods.

bfca6adbfbcd0d4025f85f0d400bc5e895b9bb35.text:
### Dublin Meetup Co-Membership Network

This community concerns the organization and analysis of Meetup communities in Dublin. **Meetup.com** facilitates the organization of **meetup groups**, which users may attend in multiple groups. These shared memberships form a **co-membership network**: meetup groups are represented as nodes, and common meetup users create connections between groups.

The **Dublin Meetup Network** is a location-specific instance of this co-membership network. It maps meetup communities located in **Dublin**, linking the structure of local groups to their participating users. Together, the entities describe how Meetup groups, users, and communities are organized and modeled through shared membership.

6b8d90d6f83eb2dee5cd9da80ab075617003e5df.text:
## Audio-Based Semantic Modeling for Music Clips

This community focuses on audio-based distributional semantic models for representing and comparing music clips. These models enable computation in a **joint acoustic semantic space**, where both audio representations and lexical representations are represented.

A key task is **automatic tag generation**: the models produce predicted tags, which are combined with acoustic representations to construct **acoustic semantic clip embeddings**. These embeddings are evaluated for **music clip similarity measurement**, which measures similarity between music clips.

The community thus connects audio representations, lexical representations, predicted tags, and semantic embeddings into a unified approach to music understanding. Its reported performance is notable because audio-based distributional semantic models **outperform the state of the art on music clip similarity measurement**.

3e86c2099d05468a5e36a7b9869c4384a7678409.text:
## Tensor-Based Analysis of Human Migration

This community focuses on global migration analysis and the extraction of migration patterns from data. Human migration is modeled as a three-mode tensor whose dimensions represent origin, destination, and time. The geocoded Twitter dataset provides data for studying migration patterns and supports their extraction.

Tensor decomposition methods are applied to this three-mode migration tensor. In particular, CP decomposition decomposes the tensor and extracts meaningful low-dimensional factors. These factors represent meaningful migration patterns, providing a compact representation of migration behavior. Together, the dataset, tensor model, and decomposition methods connect observed geocoded Twitter data to low-dimensional analyses of human migration trends.

97c7f264949d23b526c5a718a34aeeafa5231e49.text:
## Traffic Networks, Ride Sharing, and Infrastructure Vulnerability

This community examines traffic networks as critical infrastructure, linking mobility optimization, ride-sharing, and behavioral threats. Ride sharing can reduce traffic congestion and emissions, support smart-city development, and provide a ride-sharing utilization metric. Utilization is modeled and forecast a few hours ahead through a network-centric approach and a dynamic travel network that represents traffic using topological network features. Aggregated New York City taxi-trip data supports construction of this network.

A second focus is target selection optimization: choosing streets in a traffic network to maximize disruption and congestion. Exact optimization is computationally intractable, so a suboptimal heuristic is analyzed and evaluated on the Chicago traffic network. Concentrating targets in Chicago’s business district produces more far-reaching disruption.

The community also connects congestion and communication conditions: congestion affects vehicle–infrastructure communication, while traffic density influences communication speed and quality. Behavioral manipulation is an infrastructure vulnerability. Fake information can manipulate driver decision making, creating congestion; such disinformation attacks may target critical infrastructure. Thus, the same traffic systems studied for efficient ride-sharing and smart-city benefits are also examined as vulnerable networks where manipulated decisions and strategically selected targets can disrupt mobility and communications.

9cd3d1dfc4c66e117269f999f44de36201fb7b47.text:
## Dynamic Modeling of Interbank Trading Networks

This community focuses on link forecasting and the time-varying topology of the interbank market, represented by the e-MID interbank network dataset.

The central method is a dynamic network model that forecasts future link presence. It models link probabilities through persistent links—whether links existed previously—and node-specific dynamic fitnesses that capture changing propensities to form links. The model assumes Markov dynamics for both link persistence and node fitnesses and is applied to the e-MID interbank network, which represents trading relationships in the interbank market.

The associated concepts concern preferential trading and preferential lending. Persistent links are connected with preferential trading in network formation, while dynamic fitnesses capture trading driven by node-specific characteristics. The evidence supports preferential lending behavior. However, ignoring changes in network topology tends to overestimate preferential lending, highlighting the importance of modeling time-varying network structure.

74512709af1c61503fc355e424f5f9c9a55541ef.text:
## Joint Stock Market Prediction with Heterogeneous Information

This community focuses on **stock market prediction**, particularly predicting multiple correlated stocks jointly. The central method is **coupled matrix and tensor factorization**, which constructs and factorizes a tensor while incorporating a stock quantitative feature matrix and a stock correlation matrix to assist tensor decomposition.

The approach implements **heterogeneous information fusion** by combining quantitative stock information with information extracted from **web news**. News provides **stock events**, which serve as predictive indicators, affect stock price movements, and encode shared event effects among correlated stocks through the stock correlation matrix. **Investor sentiment** is another predictive indicator and influences stock price movements.

The method is evaluated using **China A-share stock data** and **HK stock data**. Overall, the relationships connect news-derived events, sentiment, stock correlations, and quantitative features within a coupled matrix–tensor framework for modeling stock price movements and predicting market behavior.

abd307c7da0e472613da585d1890f7120893c596.text:
### Non-Adaptive Ranking from Noisy Comparisons

This community concerns **object ranking** using noisy **pairwise comparisons**, with comparisons supplied by **crowd workers**. Objects are ranked according to their **intrinsic qualities**, while the **preference difference model** assumes that preference probabilities depend on differences in these qualities.

Key methods include **non-adaptive ranking algorithms**, which solve the ranking task using a **least-squares criterion** to estimate object qualities. Their performance is comparable to that of a **maximum likelihood algorithm**. The methods are evaluated through a **PAC guarantee**: they achieve an \((\epsilon,\delta)\)-PAC ranking guarantee.

The associated **sample complexity** is \(O(N/\epsilon^2 \log(N/\delta))\) comparisons, specifying the comparison requirement for the PAC guarantee. Overall, the relationships connect crowd-sourced pairwise data, quality estimation by least squares, and provable non-adaptive ranking performance.

4dfbc26edcc656ad8618cdeaba24fbffa0417ceb.text:
## Web Search–Based Antimicrobial Consumption Surveillance

This community centers on predicting **antimicrobial drug consumption**, which is linked to **antimicrobial resistance** and monitored through **surveillance systems**. The prediction task uses **web search data** supplied by **Google Health Trends**, with **web search query selection** identifying queries related to diseases, drugs, and descriptions associated with antimicrobial drugs.

Predictions are compared against **historical antimicrobial purchase data**. Combining web search data with purchase data produces the best predictions. Two modeling approaches are highlighted: **Elastic Net** as a linear prediction model and **Gaussian Processes** as a nonlinear prediction model. **Mean absolute error** evaluates weekly consumption predictions.

Overall, the relationships describe a surveillance-oriented framework in which selected Google Health Trends queries provide predictive signals for antimicrobial consumption, while historical purchase records support comparison and improved prediction. Web search data may therefore improve systems for monitoring antimicrobial drug consumption.

ffe2d8bb92aa37a95ad7619cf2ae49c4b24440db.text:
### Directed Coauthorship and Scholarly Collaboration

This community focuses on modeling coauthorship as a structured, directed relationship rather than relying solely on traditional undirected network analysis. The **coauthorship credit allocation model**, proposed by the **Kim–Diesner model** in 2014, conceptualizes coauthoring as a **directed, weighted, self-looped network**. It uses **coauthor ordering** to assign differing levels of contribution credit and is adopted by the **directed network approach** to represent coauthor relationships.

The directed network approach complements conventional undirected-network measures while revealing the **hierarchy of collaboration among scholars**. It was tested and validated using a sample of **861 Psychometrika authors** and can detect prominent **Psychometric Society** scholars affiliated with *Psychometrika*. The author sample contains authors affiliated with the Psychometric Society, linking the methodological framework to an empirical scholarly community.

6a461b0007358b13fe285318d62a64f562815dd6.text:
## Interpretable Fashion Matching and Compatibility Learning

This community focuses on clothing matching, especially compatibility across fashion categories. **Cross-category compatibility learning** uses a semi-supervised approach to map fashion items from different categories into a shared **latent style space**, where compatible items are positioned close together.

**Distribution alignment** improves this space by bringing category distributions closer. It uses **unsupervised adversarial learning** to minimize distances between distributions, while **annotated compatible items** provide anchor points. **Semantic attributes** define dimensions of a **fine-grained interpretable semantic space**.

The **SAERS** system extracts semantic information with a **Semantic Extraction Network** and models fine-grained user preferences through **Fine-grained Preferences Attention**. Both item information and user preferences are projected into the interpretable semantic space. SAERS models user preferences for clothing attributes and explains recommendations using personalized **visual attribute semantic highlights**. It is evaluated on **real-world fashion datasets**.

Overall, the community connects semantic extraction, preference modeling, distribution alignment, and semi-supervised compatibility learning. Fashion items are represented through semantic attributes and latent style structure, while annotated compatible items support learning across fashion categories.

46ab6449783a6d1b104305bc0fa5b04efd79c016.text:
## Predicting Institutional Research Assessment Outcomes

This community focuses on bibliometric prediction of institutional research performance, assessment outcomes, and institutional ranking movements. The central metric is the **departmental h index**, used to predict REF 2014 results and estimate relative institutional performance. It was also evaluated against the **normalised citation based indicator**, a competing bibliometric estimate.

The **Research Assessment Exercise** provides the broader assessment context, with **RAE 2008** serving as a reference point for measuring subsequent institutional ranking movements. **REF 2014**, an instance of the **Research Excellence Framework**, produces overall REF outcomes used for comparison.

The task of **predicting REF outcomes** aimed to anticipate both overall outcomes and changes in institutional rankings. Although the departmental h index correlated better with the Research Assessment Exercise’s actual results than the competing normalised citation based indicator, the reported abstract states that it did not accurately predict overall REF outcomes or institutional ranking movements. Ranking movements were defined relative to positions in RAE 2008, while institutional rankings represent the changing positions being measured.

e988768c29344a4605f6cc6a678282ef770b56bc.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Clickstreams for Recommendation

This community focuses on generating privacy-conscious clickstream data for recommender systems. A **memory biased random walk** performs the **synthetic clickstream generation** task: it is based on a **clickstream graph** and generates **synthetic clickstreams**.

The synthetic clickstreams are designed to conform to the statistical properties of **real clickstream data**. They adhere to **privacy protection policies** and provide **de minimization guarantees**, addressing the restricted public availability of **personal usage data**. This makes them a potential alternative resource for developing and evaluating recommendation models.

Synthetic clickstreams are used to learn a **recommender system model**, whose quality is evaluated by **recommender performance**. The model also achieves performance on real clickstream data, linking synthetic-data training with real-data recommendation outcomes. Separately, a **personalized recommender system** relies on personal usage data, highlighting the tension between personalization requirements and privacy restrictions.

cf505760c14ba6e622c8f6f90857eca443a28c11.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Synthetic Clickstreams for Recommendation

This community focuses on generating privacy-preserving synthetic clickstreams for recommender-system research. A **memory biased random walk**, based on a **clickstream graph**, performs the synthetic clickstream generation task and generates **synthetic clickstreams**. These synthetic data conform to the statistical properties of **real clickstream data**, adhere to **privacy protection policies**, and provide **de minimization guarantees**.

Synthetic clickstreams are used to learn a **recommender system model**. The model is evaluated by **recommender performance**, while real clickstream data also achieves performance on the model, linking synthetic-data quality to recommendation evaluation.

The community also includes a **personalized recommender system** that relies on **personal usage data** and supports **Walmart’s e-commerce platform**. It ranks recommendations using a **ranking criterion** based on product and customer embeddings. Public availability of personal usage data is restricted by privacy protection policies, motivating the use of synthetic alternatives.

cad983ef77a53c8bb15801df880059c37aa997fa.text:
## Supporting Formal Mathematical Knowledge

This community focuses on the formalization of mathematical content: converting informal mathematical knowledge into machine-oriented representations. It connects this task with mathematical knowledge management, which studies how to support formalization, and with software support, which can make the process more efficient.

An integrated development environment (IDE) provides support for formalization and motivates best practices for implementation. The Semantic TeX IDE is a specialized system that supports the formalization process; its development is guided by software requirements. It supports Semantic TeX, a format for editing knowledge in the context of large mathematical corpora.

The community also relates mathematical formalization to object-oriented languages: IDEs use approaches associated with these languages to address similar time-consuming tasks. Together, Semantic TeX, its IDE, software support, and general IDE practices form a tool-oriented infrastructure for managing and formalizing mathematical knowledge.

7d6b26f4f68b36fd87ac0da452e2aa6c900b2a22.text:
### Hodge-Based Analysis of Simplicial and Trajectory Data

This community centers on the Hodge Laplacian, simplicial complex topology, and methods for analyzing edge-based structure. The **normalized Hodge 1 Laplacian** provides an appropriate normalization of the Hodge Laplacian and defines a relationship with **edge random walks**. These random walks are connected to the topology of the underlying simplicial complex.

**Spectral embeddings**, derived using the normalized Hodge 1 Laplacian, provide another key method in the community. They are applied to **ocean drifter trajectories near Madagascar**, linking Hodge-based spectral analysis with real-world trajectory data. Overall, the entities connect normalized Hodge operators, topology-aware random walks, and spectral representations for studying structured data.

add6d7edf5877b84c16ef295f3f65c16b3603290.text:
## Mizar, Formal Dependencies, and Smart Re-verification

This community centers on the Mizar system and its large corpus of formalised mathematical knowledge. Mizar uses a sound translation from the Mizar language, integrates automated theorem proving and presentation tools, supports proof finding with first-order ATP systems, and helps users explore the Mizar library and prepare new articles. Its mathematical library, MML, and Mizar articles are constructed and maintained by the Mizar community.

A major theme is formal dependency extraction. The approach extracts dependencies from both Mizar and Coq, while alternative dependency extraction methods are motivated by different dependency types and compared for detailed dependency analysis. Such analysis concerns formal dependencies in formal mathematics and supports mathematical dependency tracking.

Smart re-verification is based on precise dependency tracking. It is proposed for re-verifying both the MML library and the CoRN library. Coq is associated with the Coq repository at Nijmegen, while Coq and CoRN are added to the systems handled by the wiki. First-order ATP systems are applied to large theories containing many facts.

The copyright and license policy clarifies the legal status of MML authors and maintainers, governs the Mizar Mathematical Library, and offers an experience for other formalised mathematics libraries.

bd88ec6d4140882354fba974bfc7bc00601183a2.text:
## Learning Graph Orderings with DON-RL

This community centers on **graph ordering** and its close relationship to **edge partitioning**. It features the **Deep Order Network (DON)**, a method that learns to solve graph-ordering tasks. DON is trained from sampled **partial vertex orders** and captures hidden **locality structure**.

DON integrates with both a **policy network** and the **DON-RL** system. The policy network improves DON’s training efficiency and adjusts sampling probabilities for partial vertex orders. DON-RL integrates DON and the policy network, and is evaluated in the context of edge partitioning. Together, these methods connect learned graph ordering, adaptive sampling, hidden locality, and edge-partitioning evaluation.

045a732e923224c9f04a2fb4cd02b6ebb770dde2.text:
## Treatment Effects on Ratings

This community examines how positive and negative treatments affect evaluation outcomes, using a control group for comparison.

- **Positive treatment** was compared with the **control group** and improved the **final rating** by an average of **11.02%**.
- It also increased the probability of achieving a **high rating** by **24.6%**.
- **Negative treatment**, likewise compared with the control group, reduced the **final rating** by an average of **5.15%**.

The entities form a comparative framework linking treatment methods to rating metrics. Positive treatment is associated with higher final and high-rating outcomes, whereas negative treatment is associated with a lower final rating.

9fca2e72c07b435c65240a81dc95b8249cf53f7e.text:
## Distributed Subgraph Matching Strategies

This community focuses on distributed subgraph matching and the evaluation of alternative matching strategies. Distributed subgraph matching is studied in two experimental settings: unlabelled matching and labelled matching. Its performance is analyzed under various settings through a dedicated performance analysis method.

The matching strategy concept represents an algorithmic approach for distributed subgraph matching. Strategies are compared at the strategy level, with general purpose optimization incorporated into this comparison. General purpose optimization is also described as an optimization target or concern for matching strategies.

Timely dataflow serves as the common implementation system for the strategy-level comparison, providing a shared basis for evaluating the alternatives. Overall, the community connects the matching task, optimization-oriented strategy design, comparative evaluation, and performance analysis across both labelled and unlabelled matching settings.

af170daa3853f7e67b4ca761c71587081242a706.text:
### Functional Complexity in Telecommunication Networks

This community focuses on understanding and designing telecommunication networks through a **functional complexity framework**. The framework enables **functional analysis** of telecommunication networks by isolating and analyzing individual **network functions as complex systems**.

**Functional topology** visualizes relationships between entities in telecommunication networks and represents the functional structure and interactions underlying a network function. Together, these concepts connect network-level analysis with the internal organization and interactions of specific functions.

The key relationship is a progression from the functional complexity framework to functional analysis, from functional analysis to network functions, and from network functions to their functional topology. This provides a structured approach for studying how network functions are organized and how they interact within telecommunication networks.

fe0fb4050162458cac2f662d792803510149b7dd.text:
### Hierarchical Consolidation of Noisy Information

This community focuses on prediction and label aggregation when information is noisy, conflicting, or drawn from multiple sources. Its central method, **multi-source hierarchical prediction consolidation**, addresses the broader task of **prediction consolidation** by combining predictions from multiple information sources and resolving conflicts from imperfect inputs. It uses **label hierarchies** to constrain consolidation results and infers **hierarchical instance similarity** through an unsupervised, iterative process.

A related task, **crowdsourced label aggregation**, handles noisy and conflicting labels provided by human workers. When labels have structured relationships, it requires hierarchical aggregation based on a label hierarchy.

The **label hierarchy** concept also represents structured relationships in application domains, including **protein functionality interactions** and **disease relationships**. Thus, the community links hierarchical representations with methods for consolidating predictions and aggregating human annotations, emphasizing structured relationships and robustness to unreliable information.

4f9bc502dbffa0cb51ed2e833e73698c0570f8e1.text:
## Binomial Ordering and Global Structure

This community centers on **binomial ordering**, the study of how two-word expressions appear in established or variable orders. It distinguishes **frozen binomials**, which occur in only one established order, from **non-frozen binomials**, which occur in multiple orders and exhibit ordering variation.

The analysis extends beyond individual expressions to the **global binomial structure**. This structure is modeled and analyzed separately for both frozen and non-frozen binomials, connecting local ordering behavior with broader structural patterns.

The community also tests whether binomial-ordering analyses extend to **trinomials**, or lists of three words. Finally, binomial ordering is related to **language conventions**, reflecting conventions in written language.

4074297883e48f76d60b065774f20510fa5c4545.text:
## Deterministic Modeling of Media Effects on Influenza

This community focuses on influenza transmission modeling that incorporates mass media effects. The central **influenza dynamics model** is a deterministic model designed to explain the dynamics of historical influenza outbreaks.

An **online influenza message dataset** measures population engagement with mass media through shared influenza-related messages and provides media-engagement data for formulating the model. **Traditional influenza surveillance data** supplies epidemiological data used to formulate and evaluate the model, including measurements of **influenza activity**.

The model represents media influence through a **media function**, which captures the functional relationship between media engagement and influenza transmission. This function is linked to historical influenza outbreaks and fits their data better than previously proposed media functions. Overall, the community connects online message activity, surveillance measurements, and historical outbreak data in a deterministic framework for assessing how mass media affects influenza dynamics.

4eb65ce91fc1f988e848bb5fbc43c422afbb2480.text:
## Mutual Information Metrics and Clustering Evaluation

This community focuses on normalized mutual information (NMI) and proposed alternatives for evaluating clustering. NMI is reported to exaggerate performance for the leximin method and on weak communities. Leximin, in turn, finds the trivial singleton clustering, linking NMI’s evaluation behavior to singleton clustering as a concept.

Several metrics are presented as improvements to NMI: adjusted mutual information (AMI), revised normalized mutual information (rrNMI), and corrected normalized mutual information (cNMI). Together, these relationships highlight concerns about NMI’s assessment of clustering quality, particularly for weak communities and solutions such as leximin’s singleton clustering.

5984b4970455d60ad18f954c24b9092e324f4cfc.text:
## Online Visual Analytics for Evolving Topics

This community focuses on analyzing **streaming text data** and understanding how topics change over time. **Online visual analytics** supports the analysis of high-volume text streams and helps users explore and understand **hierarchical topic evolution**.

A key method is **sedimentation based visualization**, which is incorporated into online visual analytics for analyzing evolving topics. Applied to streaming text data, it enables interactive analysis that moves from global patterns to local details. The incoming documents are also used to identify **representative topics**, connecting the underlying text stream with topic-level summaries.

Together, these methods and concepts support interactive exploration of evolving, hierarchical topic structures in continuously arriving text.

4ee173f625926a278972d049b9d2b673e820f184.text:
## Entity Metrics and Biological Citation Networks

This community focuses on **entitymetrics**, a method for measuring the impact of knowledge units and constructing an **entity-entity citation network**. **Metformin**, a drug used for diabetes, serves as the example entity around which the network is formed.

The community also concerns ranking and validating biological entities. **Centrality ranks** rank biological entities by their network centrality and are compared with results from the **Comparative Toxicogenomics Database**. This database contains **manually curated interactions**, while entitymetrics detects many of these curated interactions.

Together, the entities connect network-based impact measurement, entity-entity citation analysis, biological-entity centrality, and comparison against a database of curated biological interactions.

b57fd1bf7feb9d746f8b0329379b99b9e807b8c3.text:
## Hierarchical Backbone Extraction in Networks

This community centers on **hierarchical backbone extraction**, a method for identifying hierarchical structure in networks. It leverages **conditional probability asymmetry**, which manifests a hierarchical relationship between nodes, to estimate both the **importance** and **direction** of hierarchical relationships.

The method is evaluated using **semi-synthetic benchmarks**, including networks with a **planted hierarchy**, where it identifies the embedded hierarchical structure. It is also applied to the **skills individuals network** and the **gene products–gene ontology terms network**.

Beyond hierarchy identification, hierarchical backbone extraction supports **ontology extraction**, including the automatic extraction or augmentation of ontologies. Overall, the community connects conditional probability asymmetry with tasks involving hierarchy identification, relationship importance estimation, direction estimation, and ontology extraction.

fcb8c8ced24d04d81dfc51092115727cf87f205d.text:
### Thread Reconstruction in Discussion Forums

This community centers on **thread reconstruction**, a task performed on **conversational data**. Its goal is to identify the underlying thread structure in **discussion forums**, where **forum discussion** is contained.

The key method is a **neural coherence model**. This model computes a **coherence score**, which is used to evaluate candidate reconstructions. Thread reconstruction selects the reconstruction with the highest coherence score, linking the task’s structural inference directly to the model’s scoring mechanism.

Overall, the community describes a framework for recovering coherent discussion threads from conversational data in forums using neural modeling and coherence-based selection.

d4ce603d10d0df8a6adf9f01398d1c3452b0eb03.text:
## Constrained Frequent Sequence Mining

This community focuses on controlling **frequent sequence mining** through general **subsequence constraints**. Constraint types include **length**, **gap**, **span**, **regular expression**, and **hierarchy constraints**, providing different ways to specify which subsequences should be mined.

**Pattern expressions** describe these general subsequence constraints and are used by frequent sequence mining algorithms to specify mining requirements. The computational model for constrained mining is based on **compressed finite state transducers**: algorithms translate pattern expressions into these compressed transducers.

The **desq** system unifies diverse subsequence constraints within a single framework. Overall, the entities connect constraint specification, computational representation, and mining execution: subsequence constraints guide the frequent sequence mining task; pattern expressions express the constraints; compressed finite state transducers provide the computational model; and mining algorithms perform the translation and constrained mining.

8075a93b4c99add000e38603a10f6491834d685c.text:
## Bag-of-Paths Criticality and Spectral Graph Properties

This community connects network-disconnection criticality with spectral methods for graph analysis. **Exact BoP criticality** is a Bag-of-Paths-based measure evaluated under simulated network disconnections on Erdős–Rényi and Albert–Barabási graph samples. **Approximate BoP criticality** approximates the exact measure, is also evaluated through disconnection simulations, and uses a Sherman–Morrison rank-one matrix update.

A second theme concerns adjacency-matrix constructions and Ramanujan-type spectra. **Neighborhood expansion** constructs a **modified adjacency matrix** that counts self-avoiding paths of a specified length between node pairs. Leading eigenvectors are computed from this matrix, which satisfies a **weak Ramanujan property** separating the two leading eigenvalues from the remaining spectrum.

The **Ramanujan property** requires the second eigenvalue magnitude to be at most \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) for \(d\)-regular graphs. Neighborhood expansion can regularize an original adjacency matrix to recover a weak Ramanujan form. Random regular graphs are almost Ramanujan because their second eigenvalue approaches this bound, as described by the **Kesten–McKay law**. Erdős–Rényi graphs satisfy a weaker spectral bound at logarithmic average degree.

0c5402a1cff5e4efcfe722abd25d5aecfa966887.text:
## Dense Datasets for Preference Research

This community centers on **dense recommender datasets** and their collection through a **preference elicitation interface**. The interface enables quick **preference elicitation**, collecting users’ preferences for **visual stimuli**, and is intended to produce dense datasets that complement existing **sparse industry-scale datasets**.

These datasets support integration with **social and behavioral sciences** research and enable analysis of human preference patterns. Specifically, they facilitate measurement of **preference diversity**, **preference consistency**, and **scale acuity**, as well as assessment of **anchoring biases**. They also facilitate evaluation in **counterfactual learning** experiments.

Overall, the relationships connect an efficient elicitation system and visual-preference task to a dataset resource designed for broader empirical analysis, measurement of preference characteristics, bias investigation, and counterfactual-learning evaluation.

596973560f0005055aef6a50fd37af331456a958.text:
**PAC Learnability in Diffusion Models**

This community focuses on proper and improper PAC learnability for network diffusion systems.

Proper PAC learnability is established for the discrete-time linear threshold model and the discrete-time independent cascade model. It also addresses incomplete observations by reducing them to complete observations using a modified graph.

Improper PAC learnability applies to the discrete-time linear threshold model, the discrete-time independent cascade model, and the continuous-time independent cascade model.

Together, these entities connect PAC-learning tasks with several standard diffusion models, while highlighting a modified-graph method for handling incomplete observational data.

3018b3648141361a4330c386289ee99316568499.text:
## Temporal Graph Prediction with TNA

The community focuses on temporal graph prediction, particularly **future link prediction**, **next graph state prediction**, and **temporal edge prediction**. Temporal edge prediction is presented as a form of future link prediction involving newly formed temporal edges.

The central method is **Temporal Neighbourhood Aggregation (TNA)**. TNA captures changes in temporal neighbourhoods and is optimized to predict the next graph in a sequence, supporting future link prediction. Its architecture uses **recurrent variational graph convolution**, with **hierarchical recurrence** applied at different graph depths. TNA creates final vertex representations through **variational sampling**.

The method is evaluated on **synthetic benchmark datasets**. Its performance is also considered in relation to **model parameter count**: TNA achieves competitive performance while using fewer model parameters.

cca122db1150e07eea5d78a6d6c893cf663aacd9.text:
### Joint Modeling for Real-Time Dengue Surveillance

This community centers on real-time dengue surveillance and dengue case count prediction using reported cases and disease-related Twitter posts. The latent shared component generative model models fluctuations in both dengue reported cases and Twitter activity, jointly driven by a hidden Markov process. It predicts disease counts for upcoming weeks by combining reported disease cases with Twitter posts as predictive signals.

The model is developed for timely monitoring of dengue epidemics and is empirically evaluated using data from large Brazilian towns. The disease-related Twitter posts dataset includes a stable random tweet source, representing tweets posted when no disease cases are recorded. Together, these datasets support a framework that connects observed dengue reports and social-media activity for near-term prediction and surveillance.

4359e68810ff876b48cd6c6ca05744407f21b07a.text:
## Ranking National Football Teams from World Cup Matches

This community focuses on ranking national football teams using a **world cup match graph** built from the **football world cup** dataset. The graph represents matches between teams, with **link weighting metrics** assigning weights to graph links. These metrics combine **matches won** and **goals scored**.

**PageRank with restarts** is applied to the world cup match graph and supports the task of ranking national football teams. The resulting rankings are comparable to the **FIFA all-time ranking**, which is published by **FIFA**. Thus, the community connects World Cup match data, weighted graph construction, and a PageRank-based ranking method with an official FIFA ranking for comparison.

abba1705833e2daa5b28da0a76a3444ed73905e7.text:
## Vertex Orbit and Subgraph Counting

This community centers on **vertex orbit counting**, which computes **vertex orbit counts** by measuring vertex participation in **5-vertex pattern subgraphs**. These counts provide a fine-grained view of structure compared with **total subgraph counting**, which aggregates subgraph occurrences.

The main method is **EVOKE**, a scalable algorithm for vertex orbit counting. EVOKE also addresses total subgraph counting and incurs only a small constant-factor overhead relative to the best 5-vertex counter. Methodologically, EVOKE generalizes the **graph cutting framework**.

The graph cutting framework generates **polynomial equations**. These equations relate counts of larger and smaller subgraphs, supporting the connection between subgraph-counting tasks and vertex-level structural metrics. Together, the methods and concepts describe a progression from total subgraph counts to more detailed vertex orbit measurements, with polynomial equations providing a mechanism for relating counts across subgraph sizes.

595b7921b57c5b82c036af8a8d358217e9f4ebc9.text:
## Filtering Free-Rider Episodes in Frequent Episode Mining

Frequent episode mining can discover free-rider episodes, which are redundant patterns consisting of a real pattern combined with additional noise events. Episode filtering addresses these redundant episodes.

EDP is a partition model for free-rider episode filtering. It uses a dual partition strategy that divides an episode into consecutive subepisodes, representing an underlying real pattern and potential noise events. EDP defines and estimates the expected support of free-rider episodes. This estimate assumes that the partitioned subepisodes occur independently.

Expected support is compared with observed support to assess an episode’s interestingness. Through this comparison, EDP performs free-rider episode filtering and helps identify episodes whose observed support may reflect redundancy rather than an underlying meaningful pattern.

7179ec41379e3440bc779a558301cce2fe840723.text:
## Tweet Feature Mining and Effectiveness

This community focuses on mining tweet features to understand and predict tweet effectiveness. The analysis draws on **2.5 million original tweets** and **122 million associated engagements**, using engagement outcomes as the primary measure of effectiveness.

Key feature categories include **tweet time**, **tweet entities**, **tweet composition**, and **user account features**. These factors are studied for their relationships with tweet effectiveness, with timing, content entities, composition, and account characteristics treated as potentially informative signals.

The resulting methods support several applications. Tweet-feature analysis is used for **advertising campaign analysis** and **user engagement prediction**, linking tweet characteristics to expected audience response. It also provides tweet-derived signals for **automated trading**. Overall, the community connects large-scale tweet feature mining with engagement-based effectiveness measurement and downstream prediction and analysis tasks.

4c05fd66bd4386f94c96abc008d4025680539d79.text:
## Multilayer Stream Graphs and Layer Importance

This community focuses on analyzing temporal, multilayer interactions and assessing the importance of individual layers. **Multilayer stream graphs** represent interactions using a multilayer structure while modeling interactions occurring over time. They provide **layer centralities**, which support the **layer importance assessment** task by quantifying the importance of layers.

Layer centralities are evaluated on two datasets: an **individual interaction dataset**, containing interactions involving individuals, and a **flight interaction dataset**, containing interactions involving flights. These datasets also support the study of **behavior patterns**. In turn, layer centralities help explain subtle behavior patterns observed in the interaction data.

Overall, the community connects a method for representing temporal multilayer systems with centrality-based analysis, layer assessment, and empirical investigation of behavior patterns across individual and flight interactions.

de3c55f9c8feec89597196d939f023cb7766723e.text:
## K-VCC Enumeration for Cohesive Subgraphs

This community centers on **k-vcc**, a cohesive subgraph model used in **cohesive subgraph detection**. Cohesive subgraph detection is applied to both **social community detection** and **network topology analysis**. The k-vcc model effectively eliminates the **free rider effect**, while **k-vcc enumeration** is designed to enumerate all k-vcc instances.

The enumeration method uses **recursive graph partitioning**, dividing the graph into overlapping subgraphs. It also incorporates **neighbor sweep** and **group sweep** as optimization strategies. Both sweep methods reduce the number of **local connectivity testing** operations, improving the enumeration process.

The method is evaluated on **seven large real datasets**, connecting its algorithmic design to large-scale empirical analysis. Overall, the community links a cohesive connectivity model with efficient enumeration techniques and applications in social and network-structure analysis.
